The auction will be conducted on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system on October 19, 2026 (Monday). The Government Stock up to ten per cent of the notified amount of the sale of each stock will be allotted to eligible individuals and institutions, subject to a maximum limit of one per cent of its notified amount for a single bid per stock as per the ‘Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility’. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).
Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system on October 19, 2026 (Monday). The competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:30 A.M. and non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:00 A.M.
In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team may be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
For other auction related difficulties, IDMD Auction Team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Only in the event of system failure, physical bids would be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form obtainable from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
The yield per cent per annum or the price as the case may be, expected by the bidder should be expressed up to two decimal points. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid at same/different rates of yield or prices in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system. However, the aggregate amount of bids submitted by a bidder should not exceed the notified amount for each State.
The Reserve Bank of India will determine the maximum yield / minimum price at which bids will be accepted. Stock will be issued for a minimum nominal amount of ₹10,000.00 and in multiples of ₹10,000.00 thereafter.
The results of the auction will be announced on October 19, 2026 (Monday) and payment by successful bidders will be made during banking hours on October 21, 2026 (Wednesday) at Mumbai and at respective Regional Offices of RBI.
The new State Government Stocks will bear interest at the rates determined by RBI at the auctions. For the new stock, interest will be paid half yearly on April 21 and October 21 of each year till maturity. For the re-issued Government Stock, interest will be paid at the rate as determined on the date of original issue of Government Stock and will be paid on half yearly basis till maturity. The Stocks will be governed by the provisions of the Government Securities Act, 2006 and the Government Securities Regulations, 2007.
The investment in State Government Stocks will be reckoned as an eligible investment in Government Securities by banks for the purpose of Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. The stocks will qualify for the ready forward facility.

items.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has directed the State Public Works Corporation (LSPWC) to commence immediate road reconstruction and rehabilitation across the state, taking advantage of the dry season to address deteriorating infrastructure.
The General Manager of LSPWC, Engr. Tokunbo Ajanaku, disclosed this on Thursday during an inspection tour of ongoing projects, assuring residents of improved road networks as weather conditions become more favourable for construction work.
Ajanaku said Oshodi-Isolo Local Government Area was a major focus of the exercise, with reconstruction underway on Godwin Omonuwa Road, Taiwo Street, Salamotu Street, Peter Agah Street and Ibeh Street.
He said the projects were undertaken at the governor’s direction to address infrastructure deficits and improve connectivity within communities.
“These roads are important links within the Oshodi-Isolo axis, serving residents, traders, business owners and other road users daily.
“Their reconstruction will not only improve mobility but also reduce transportation costs, enhance road safety, boost commercial activities and create a more conducive environment for businesses and residents,” Ajanaku said.
He added that the inspection covered other ongoing rehabilitation projects across the state, including Ogunnusi Road in Ojodu Local Council Development Area (LCDA), Awolowo Way in Ikeja Local Government Area, Lanre Awolokun Road and Idowu Olaitan Street in Shomolu, as well as Idimu-Ikotun Road in Alimosho.
According to him, heavy rainfall often limits asphalt laying, but the corporation maintained emergency palliative interventions during the rainy season to keep critical roads motorable.
He said the agency was now shifting towards more comprehensive and durable repairs with the return of dry weather.
Ajanaku added that much of the maintenance and asphalt-laying work was being carried out at night, under appropriate safety measures, to minimise traffic congestion across the metropolis.
He appealed to residents to be patient, explaining that road repairs were prioritised based on road conditions, traffic volume and the urgency of intervention.
The general manager said the corporation would progressively extend its operations to other parts of the state.
He also urged residents to protect public infrastructure by avoiding practices that contribute to road deterioration, including dumping refuse in drainage channels, spilling petroleum products and discharging wastewater onto roads.
“Our roads are our collective heritage. Government has the responsibility to provide and maintain them, but citizens also have a duty to protect them. Road preservation must therefore be a shared responsibility,” Ajanaku said.

By Vincent Ujumadu
The Tinubu Support Group (TSG) in the Southeast, led by former All Progressives Congress (APC) National Auditor, Sir Paul Chukwuma, on Thursday held a rally in Awka, Anambra State, to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.
At the rally, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, urged voters in the zone to support APC candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections.
Chukwuma, a former governorship candidate in Anambra State, and the APC senatorial candidate for Anambra Central, Uche Ekwunife, also urged voters to support Tinubu and other candidates of the party.
They expressed confidence that the APC would secure substantial votes across the five Southeast states, arguing that Tinubu’s actions and policies had earned him support in the region.
However, some APC leaders in Anambra State reportedly expressed dissatisfaction with what they described as the party’s national leadership relying on the strength of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) to secure votes for Tinubu in the state.
The APC state secretary, Sir Obiora Okpala, said the party should be adequately recognised in political arrangements in Anambra, given its status as the ruling party at the national level and a major political stakeholder in the state.
He argued that the APC should be carried along in the process, rather than APGA being given what he described as undue advantage over the party in Anambra.
The post APC group rallies Southeast support for Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Chioma Obinna
The Coalition of Civil Society Action for Education for All (CSACEFA), Lagos State Chapter, has called for increased investment in girls’ education, stronger child protection measures and coordinated efforts to end child marriage and ensure that girls have access to quality education.
The coalition made the call at its Lagos Education Summit and International Day of the Girl Child 2026, held at the State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB) Hall, Maryland, Lagos, with the theme, “End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights.”
Speaking at the event, CSACEFA Lagos Coordinator, Stella Olubunmi Francis, said every child deserved access to quality education, irrespective of gender or personal circumstances.
Francis expressed concern over the stigma and discrimination faced by pregnant schoolgirls, urging stakeholders to create opportunities for them to continue their education.
“There is a lot of stigma and shame, but these children should not be denied education because of their pregnancies. We need to create more opportunities for them to continue their education,” she said.
Representing the Executive Chairman of SUBEB, Dr Akeem Babatunde Shittu, the Board Secretary, Lamidi Akeem, reaffirmed the Lagos State Government’s commitment to children’s rights and basic education.
“The Lagos State Government has already domesticated the Child Rights Act. Every government agency saddled with responsibilities concerning children, particularly SUBEB, has a role to play,” Akeem said.
He acknowledged the contribution of civil society organisations and development partners to efforts aimed at bringing out-of-school children back into the education system.
In her keynote address, a lawyer and member of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) Nigeria, Mrs Olubola Afolabi, called for stronger child protection mechanisms, legal accountability and improved access to education to tackle child marriage.
“Why does child marriage happen? What happens to the girls? These are the questions I want us to ask ourselves,” Afolabi said, urging stakeholders to confront the factors responsible for the practice and its consequences for girls.
CSACEFA Lagos Provost and Founder of LEADIN AFRICA, Margaret ChiChi Nkire, said the summit was organised to strengthen gender-responsive education financing and inclusive budgeting in Lagos State and Nigeria.
During a panel session she moderated, participants called for rights-based education policies, the removal of hidden charges that undermine free education and improved support for pregnant, married and parenting girls to remain in school or return without discrimination.
“We hope that beyond this summit, we will have better coordination among stakeholders. We have Plan International, Save the Children, the British Council, SUBEB, the National Human Rights Commission and other stakeholders here today,” Nkire said.
Representing Plan International Nigeria, Aishatu Usman Bukar stressed the need for adequate and sustainable education funding, gender-responsive budgeting and measures to remove financial barriers facing girls and vulnerable households.
A student participant, Esther Matthew, said the summit had broadened her understanding of the opportunities available to girls beyond marriage.
“I have learnt that being a girl child is not only about marriage. A girl can stand on her own, become a business owner and achieve whatever she wants in the future,” Matthew said.
She also pledged to act on the message, “See Something, Say Something,” by intervening where possible when she encountered situations threatening children’s safety and reporting cases beyond her capacity to a teacher or another trusted adult.
The summit featured discussions on child marriage, inclusive education and sustainable financing, alongside cultural dance and spoken-word performances celebrating the girl child.
Other participants included representatives of Save the Children International Nigeria, the National Association of Proprietors of Private Schools, Child Protection Network Lagos, the National Youth Council of Nigeria, mothers’ associations and School-Based Management Committees.
The stakeholders called for stronger collaboration among government agencies, civil society organisations, development partners, schools and communities to protect girls’ rights and ensure that poverty, pregnancy, early marriage and discrimination do not deprive them of education.
The post CSACEFA seeks end to child marriage, demands more investment in girls’ education appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said on Thursday that the Federal Government (FG) had no plan to increase electricity tariffs.
Tegbe said this in Ibadan while flagging off the 17.7MW hybrid solar mini-grid project, with a 17.74MW Battery Energy Storage System for communities in Oyo State.
The minister described reports of a planned tariff hike circulating on social media as misinformation and urged Nigerians to disregard it.
“I want to say this clearly and without ambiguity: there is no plan to increase electricity tariffs.
“What we are planning is a power sector that works round the clock,” he said.
He said the FG’s commitment to regular power supply starts with having three Energy Zones: the Lagos-Ogun corridor, Abuja-Kaduna-Kano corridor, and the Benin-Enugu-Port Harcourt corridor.
He explained that the 17.7MW project would serve communities across Akinyele, Ido, Ibadan North, Egbeda and Lagelu Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Oyo State.
According to him, the interconnected mini-grid would improve supply to homes and businesses, reduce dependence on generators and create better conditions for investment and jobs in the beneficiary communities.
Tegbe commended President Bola Tinubu for his leadership under the Renewed Hope Agenda and appreciated the Olubadan of Ibadanland for his support.
He also thanked the Rural Electrification Agency (REA), Paras Energy, the World Bank, Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company (IBEDC) and the Oyo State Government for their contributions.
He said the FG plans to build and improve the national grid across the eastern, western and central corridors to ensure stability and extend the 24/7 power vision to every part of Nigeria.
Mr Deolu Ijose, the Managing Director (MD)/Chief Executive Officer (CEO), IBEDC, said the new mini-grid project would provide electricity to 22,597 customers across five communities.
Ijose said the project, developed by Paras Energy and Natural Resources Development Limited, would provide 17.7MWp solar PV generation with battery storage to Bola, Jiboye, Molade-Adelubi, Ogo-Oluwa, and Sooko-Elega clusters.
According to him, IBEDC’s existing distribution infrastructure will be used to integrate and deliver electricity generated by Paras Energy.
He said that this model would show how DisCos and private developers could collaborate to improve access.
Ijose added that the project builds on IBEDC’s previous innovative interventions such as the Mokoloki Mini-Grid in Ogun and the recently commissioned Oke-Oyi mini-grid in Kwara.
He then urged the host communities to protect the infrastructure.
The MD/CEO of REA, Abba Abubakar-Aliyu, said the project details are: 1.8 megawatts in Bola, Akinyele LGA and 3.5 megawatts in Jiboye, Ido LGA.
Others are 6.9 megawatts in Molade, Ibadan North LGA; 3.6 megawatts in Ogo Oluwa, Egbeda LGA, and 1.9 megawatts in Sooko, Lagelu LGA.
Earlier, the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, lauded the minister for including rural and underserved communities in various power reform projects.
He urged the Oyo State Government to speed up work and complete its ongoing hybrid power project before 2027 for residents to start enjoying regular power supply.
Earlier, Gov. Seyi Makinde, represented by the state Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Prof. Dahud Shangodoyin, said the government would continue to pursue practical electricity interventions across the state.
He noted that the state government’s Hybrid Independent Power Project, meant to serve the state’s secretariat and other strategic public facilities, has a plant capacity of 11 MW.
He recalled that the 5 MW phase was commissioned in 2024.
“Our wide agenda includes solar power for public facilities, rural electrification, mini-grids, as well as private sector-led generation and distribution.
“Therefore, no single technology can meet every need,” said Makinde.
He charged the developer and implementing institutions to maintain clear construction and commissioning mindsets, and comply with applicable licenses and technical standards. (NAN)

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman
Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has rejected suggestions that the arrest of politician Alhaji Wakiil Goni Mama, popularly known as Mai Salati, was politically motivated, insisting that the military has nothing to do with politics.
Buni spoke on Thursday during the swearing-in of commissioners and chairmen of the 17 local government areas in Damaturu, where he disclosed that he had directed the chairman of Geidam Local Government Area to follow up on the case with military authorities and community elders.
The governor’s remarks come amid allegations in some quarters that he was behind Mai Salati’s arrest and had used the military to target the politician over political differences.
Dismissing the insinuations, Buni said he has no history of opposition bullying, insisting that threatening political opponents was inconsistent with his principles.
“I reached out to the Geidam chairman, instructed him to follow up on the case with the military commander and other elders on the case and report back to me,” the governor said.
“It is not in my principle to threaten opposition,” he added.
Buni also maintained that the military should not be drawn into partisan political disputes, insisting that Mai Salati’s case was not political.
It could be recalled that troops of the Nigerian Army’s Operation Hadin Kai reportedly arrested Mai Salati in early October over allegations of providing logistics support to suspected members of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), a faction of the Boko Haram insurgency operating in the North-East.
Reports published by TheCable and other media organisations on October 8 and 9 said the arrest followed an alleged attempt by the politician to bribe soldiers to secure the release of suspects arrested in Kanamma, Yobe State, over suspected terrorist logistics activities.
According to the reports, the suspects were being processed for further investigation when Mai Salati allegedly intervened to secure their release by offering money to military personnel.
The soldiers reportedly rejected the alleged inducement and arrested him instead, with security sources saying he and other suspects were subsequently moved from Damaturu to Maiduguri for further investigation.
The arrest generated political controversy, with reports highlighting speculation that it might be connected to Mai Salati’s reported defection from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to the African Democratic Congress (ADC).
Security sources cited in the initial reports rejected the suggestion that the operation was politically motivated, maintaining that it concerned allegations of terrorism-related logistics and an attempt to interfere with the detention of suspects.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
A shooting has left “multiple victims” at an elementary school in the northwestern US state of Oregon, police said Thursday, adding that the shooter is dead.
“We don’t have confirmation yet who shot the suspect. It may have been a bystander. At this time, we have multiple victims,” said Sheila Miller, a spokesperson at the Bend Police Department, in a press conference.
The Bend-La Pine School District said in a statement on social media that the Silver Rail Elementary School was under lockdown.
An updated post later said law enforcement was escorting students in buses to a separate location, where families could reunite with their children.
Miller said that officers were alerted to respond to a critical scene at 1:00 pm local time, and that police were on the scene approximately two minutes later.
“Seconds later, we received word over the radio that the suspect in this incident was down,” she said.
Miller said medics had taken at least two people to a local hospital, adding that “we do not know their status.”
The school is more than 100 miles (160 kilometers) southeast of the city Portland. It serves primary-age students in kindergarten through fifth grade.
The United States, where firearms are readily available, is a frequent scene of gun violence, with thousands of people killed every year. It has the highest rate of gun-related deaths among all developed nations.
The deadliest school shooting in US history took place at Virginia Tech on April 16, 2007, when South Korean student Seung-Hui Cho killed 32 people and wounded 17 others before taking his own life.
There have been more than 360 mass shootings in the United States so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as four or more people shot.
AFP

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Meta on Thursday launched a new open-weight AI model which it claims rivals, and in some cases outperforms, similar products from leading Chinese developers.
Muse Spark Open “is the most capable US open-weight model to date,” Meta’s chief of AI Alexandr Wang wrote on X.
Unlike with so-called closed models — such as Anthropic’s Claude or OpenAI’s ChatGPT — developers can download the parameters, or weights, of an open-weight model and then customize it.
Chinese developers have emerged as dominant players in the open-weight market for AI models over the past couple of years.
Alibaba’s Qwen, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 and Z.ai’s GLM models have been considered open-weight frontrunners globally, but Meta claims its new open model now competes on a similar level.
“Built for coding and agentic work,” Muse Spark Open “excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning,” Meta said in a blogpost, adding that “strong safeguards” have been integrated into the new model.
Muse Spark Open is also “optimized” to run on Apple’s advanced M5 Ultra chips, Meta said, signaling an unusual partnership between the two tech giants.
Meta boss Mark Zuckerberg wrote on X that the new model “runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work” with Apple and its new CEO John Ternus.
Ternus, who took over as Apple’s chief from Tim Cook in September, responded that it is “amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open’s caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!”
Muse Spark Open still requires significant computing power, though.
Users can run the model on two Mac Studios with M5 Ultra chips to create a “supercomputer” on their own desktop, Meta said.
The launch comes just days after Meta announced its newest closed model.
On Monday, the company unveiled two new “frontier” models called Wonder and Wonder Full, which the company claimed rival the most advanced versions of ChatGPT and Claude.
Meta’s AI efforts were initially focused on open models, but more recently Zuckerberg has pushed the company to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic.
Meta launched its Spark model in April, marking a departure from its open-source model known as Llama, which lagged behind the rest of the industry.
AFP

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
Viral footage circulating online appears to show sealed iPhone boxes and luxury perfume packs floating in the Strait of Hormuz after a container ship was struck, caught fire and sank this week, turning a shipping attack into an unlikely consumer-tech story.
The Singapore-flagged vessel GFS Pride went down near Oman’s Musandam peninsula after what Singapore’s Maritime and Port Authority described as an unknown projectile strike that damaged the ship and started a fire. All 21 crew members were evacuated and no injuries were reported.
&&&&&&&
Clips shared widely on social media appear to show Apple iPhone boxes and perfume packs bobbing in the water, with small boats moving among scattered containers. Major outlets that carried the footage, including India Today, said they could not independently verify where or when the clips were filmed, or confirm that the phones were part of the ship’s cargo. AI-generated images claiming to show thousands of iPhones in the water were also shared around the same time.
What Officials Say Happened
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said a ship hit a naval mine while using what it called an unauthorised route through the strait. Singapore and other maritime reports said the vessel was hit by an unidentified projectile. A second Singapore-flagged ship, GFS Giselle, was also hit around the same period, suffered hull damage, and reached a safe anchorage with its crew.
Pakistan’s Hydrographer warned mariners that GFS Pride had sunk about four nautical miles north-west of Ras al-Sheikh Masud. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported multiple projectile strikes on commercial vessels in the strait this week.
Why The Strait Matters
The Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for global oil and gas trade. Shipping there has faced repeated attacks since the wider Iran conflict began earlier this year, and the waterway has at times been effectively closed or tightly restricted. The viral iPhone clips do not change the maritime facts: a freighter sank, its crew survived, and commercial traffic through one of the world’s most important sea lanes remains under threat.
Source: BBC (Singapore Maritime and Port Authority)

items.content:
By Adeola Badru
The Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has urged the people of Oyo State to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election bid, arguing that the President deserves another four-year term to consolidate his reforms.
Tompolo, who described Tinubu as a son of Oyo State, made the call while donating 32 vehicles to the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in the state to strengthen its grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general election.
He spoke through his representative, the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Chief Kestin Pondi, at the inauguration of the movement’s Oyo State structure at the Liberty Stadium, Ibadan, on Thursday.
The vehicles, according to him, were donated to support the movement’s campaign for Tinubu’s re-election and the election of other candidates contesting under the All Progressives Congress (APC).
Tompolo urged the people of Oyo State to support the President’s return to office, arguing that his re-election would enable him to complete the South’s two-term presidential tenure.
He also commended Tinubu for what he described as far-reaching reforms across critical sectors of the economy, particularly those that had increased the resources available to state governments to pay salaries and pensions and execute major development projects.
He charged members of the movement to take the message of the President’s re-election to every part of Oyo State, insisting that the state should be among those supporting Tinubu’s bid for another four years.
“We are here today to tell you that we are coming to join you to canvass for votes across the country for your son, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. What Tompolo is preaching is that Tinubu is doing very well.“
“Tinubu’s reform policies are fantastic. We want you to support President Tinubu’s re-election for him to continue with the good work he is doing,” he said.
Also speaking at the rally, the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli, assured the gathering that the party would deploy all available resources to secure victory in the state.
Alli said Oyo State had remained disconnected from the centre for too long, expressing the party’s determination to return to power.
He thanked Tompolo for the donation of the 32 vehicles and his support for Tinubu, urging party members and supporters to ensure that the vehicles were effectively deployed across the state during the campaign.
“We are very grateful. I want to assure you that we are going to make judicious use of all these vehicles and all other items that you may want to give us or from any other support group.“
“As far as we are concerned in Oyo, we have stayed out of government for too long and we are sincerely working assiduously to ensure that we take over the mantle of leadership in Oyo State,” Alli said.
Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Mr Sunday Asuku, urged the people of Oyo State, particularly the youth, to support Tinubu’s re-election bid.
Asuku described the President’s reforms as necessary for Nigeria’s economic growth and sustained development, citing the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as one of the administration’s people-oriented policies that had made a positive impact.
He urged members of the movement to intensify their grassroots mobilisation efforts and take the campaign for Tinubu’s second term to every nook and cranny of the state.
Calling on the electorate to turn out in large numbers during the election, Asuku said: “Oyo State, come out massively in January 2027 to vote massively for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu for President and vote Senator Sharafadeen Alli for Governor of Oyo State.
“Listen to me, Oyo State, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu has done a lot. He has done a lot in the past three years and a half. We want to give him four more years to consolidate on what he has started.
“Listen to me, a vote for Asiwaju is a vote for progressive Nigeria. A vote for Asiwaju is a vote for development.”

The Executive Director of the Youths and Environmental Advocacy Centre (YEAC-Nigeria), Dr Fyneface Dumnamene Fyneface, confirmed the incident in a statement on Thursday evening, saying the organisation had deployed volunteers to the area to assist with rescue efforts and independently verify the incident.
“The Youths and Environmental Advocacy Centre (YEAC-Nigeria) can now independently confirm an explosion at Aleto in Eleme Local Government Area of Rivers State,” he said.

Fyneface said volunteers who visited the scene confirmed the presence of officials of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).
He added that the cause of the incident remained unclear, although preliminary reports had attributed it to a pipeline rupture allegedly caused by equipment failure at a facility said to belong to NNPC Ltd.
YEAC-Nigeria called on the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) to identify the operator of the affected facility and conduct a Joint Investigation Visit (JIV) to establish the cause of the incident.
The organisation also urged the agency to invoke relevant provisions of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021, where applicable.
When contacted, the Rivers State Police Command spokesperson, ASP Agabe Blessing Kaborlo, said she was not aware of the incident but requested a text message to enable her to make enquiries and respond.
She had yet to provide an update as of the time of filing this report.
Similarly, the NSCDC spokesperson, Mr Ihemnacho Umeado, said he would make enquiries and get back to our correspondent but had not done so as of the time of filing this report.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% jump in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in the fiscal year 2025-26 (FY26), up from ₹1.23 Lakh Cr in the year ago fiscal.
Meanwhile, its consolidated net loss narrowed marginally by 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹8,646 Cr in FY25.
The numbers reflect the performance of the Flipkart Group as a whole, rather than the standalone financials of the Flipkart ecommerce marketplace. The financial results come after the Walmart-backed ecommerce giant completed its reverse flip from Singapore to India in March 2026.
The restructuring brought the group’s holding structure back to India, ahead of a potential domestic public listing. The consolidated entity includes businesses such as Myntra and Cleartrip, alongside logistics, platform services and other specialised operations.
“As part of its re-domiciliation to India, (the) Flipkart Group is publishing consolidated financial results under Flipkart Internet Private Limited. The results reflect the group’s performance over the reporting period for the year ended March 2026 and provide a historical view of the business rather than a current trading update,” said the ecommerce giant in a blog post.
On the operational front, the company said that its gross margins rose 23% YoY in FY26, while adjusted EBITDA improved by around ₹1,500 Cr during the fiscal. “Adjusted operating margin improved by 230 basis points, from -7.7% to -5.4%, supported by higher gross margins and lower overheads,” added the ecommerce major.
Flipkart also noted its adjusted operating business losses, before finance costs, tax, other income and exceptional items, narrowed by 17%, or around ₹1,600 Cr, during the fiscal under review.
However, this improvement in operating losses translated into only a marginal reduction in net losses. Flipkart attributed the higher net losses to higher finance costs, the derecognition of deferred tax assets recognised in earlier periods and certain exceptional items.
How Did Flipkart’s B2C Arm Perform?
Meanwhile, the ecommerce major’s B2C arm, Flipkart Internet Private Limited, reported a 19.3% YoY decline in revenue from operations to ₹16,295 Cr in FY26 compared with ₹20,202 Cr in the year-ago fiscal.
Including other income of ₹744 Cr (down from ₹947 Cr in FY25), the B2C vertical’s total income stood at ₹17,039 Cr in FY26, 19.4% lower than ₹21,149 Cr in the previous fiscal.
On the expenses front, Flipkart Internet Pvt Ltd’s total expenses fell 3.6% to ₹22,522 Cr from ₹23,361 Cr in FY25.
Overall, the B2C business’ net loss rose to ₹5,498 Cr in FY26 from ₹1,694 Cr a year earlier. Notably, the FY25 figures were restated to account for the business combination.
Where Did Flipkart Group Spend In FY26?
Despite the growing top line and narrowing losses, Flipkart Group’s total expenses rose 16% to ₹1.54 Lakh Cr in FY26 as against ₹1.33 Lakh Cr in the year-ago period.
Purchase Of Traded Goods: This was the biggest cost-centre for the company. Expenses under this head climbed 17.4% YoY to ₹1.17 Lakh Cr in the fiscal under review.
Employee Benefit Expenses: The group’s employee benefit costs remained relatively flat at ₹8,376 Cr compared with ₹8,268 Cr in FY25.
Finance Costs: Expenditure under this bucket nearly doubled to ₹1,209 Cr from ₹649 Cr in FY25.
Logistics & Storage Service Charges: Expenses under this header stood at ₹15,154 Cr in FY26, up 28.9% from ₹11,759 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. The expense accounted for nearly 54% of the group’s total other expenses of ₹28,277 Cr in FY26, highlighting the cost of running its logistics, warehousing and delivery operations.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
The Senate has ordered an investigation into the death of a National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) member, Etimbuk Daniel, at the Enugu State orientation camp, amid concerns over medical facilities and emergency response services in camps nationwide.
The resolution, adopted on Thursday, followed a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Senator Aniekan Bassey, who called for an urgent review of healthcare services available to corps members across the country.
The investigation will be conducted by the Senate Committees on Police Affairs, Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, Ethics, Code of Conduct and Public Petitions, Youth Development and Health, in conjunction with the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services.
The probe is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding Daniel’s death and determine whether any lapses occurred in the provision of medical care at the camp.
Bassey expressed concern over “the sudden and untimely passing of the corps member, describing him as a vibrant, patriotic young Nigerian and a shining light of his community who had only set out to serve the country.”
He said the incident raised broader questions about the adequacy of medical services available to corps members participating in the mandatory national service programme.
“The incident is not isolated, but highlights a recurring pattern of systemic negligence, poor medical infrastructure, and absence of qualified emergency personnel and rapid referral protocols across NYSC camps, underlining that the government owes a duty of care to young graduates mobilized away from their homes to serve the nation.”
The senator said Daniel had embarked on national service with hopes of contributing to Nigeria’s development before his death.
He called for urgent legislative scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly allegations of medical negligence, inadequate healthcare infrastructure and ineffective emergency response and referral systems at orientation camps.
Citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, Bassey said the security and welfare of the people remained the primary purpose of government.
He argued that the government and relevant authorities had a responsibility to protect corps members and ensure they received timely and adequate medical care throughout their service year.
Bassey added that Daniel’s death had thrown his family, associates, the student community and the people of Akwa Ibom State into mourning, stressing the need for a thorough investigation.
The Senate Chief Whip, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, representing Borno North, seconded the motion.
Contributing to the debate, Senator Abdul Ningi, representing Bauchi Central, expressed condolences to Daniel’s family, Bassey and the people of Akwa Ibom State and Nigeria.
Ningi urged the relevant committees to make concrete recommendations and identify measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.
The Senate subsequently observed a minute of silence in honour of the deceased.
Daniel, the immediate past Students’ Union Government president of Akwa Ibom State University, reportedly died at the NYSC orientation camp in Enugu State following allegations that he was given fake medication and did not receive timely medical attention.
Reports indicated that Daniel complained of a headache at the camp and was given medication, but his condition allegedly deteriorated afterwards.

By Davies Iheamnachor
About 20 people have been injured and over 50 houses burnt down following the explosion of a gas pipeline in Aleto community, Eleme Local Government Area of Rivers State.

Chuma, who visited the scene of the explosion, said: “There was a leakage on another section of the Nigeria Gas Company. We wrote to them, and we did a petition to NOSDRA and Rivers State Ministry of Environment and copied the Police for urgent intervention.
“We asked for a joint investigation. We don’t know what they did before they left. Today we were called to an explosion at the same pipeline of the Nigeria Gas Company that has destroyed over 50 houses, cars, and many casualties. People have been rushed to the hospital.
“Before now, everyone scampered for safety. The few that came, we asked them to stay far away to avoid any further incident.”

Fyneface said: “We are using this medium to call on the relevant authorities, the Rivers State government, Ministry of Environment, NOSDRA, the Rivers State, the Federal Government, and all the bodies involved in checking oil spill and explosion to come to the aid of Aleto people. This is a serious incident.
“As of the time of this statement, YEAC-Nigeria has not independently confirmed any fatalities.
“Members of the Advocacy Centre’s volunteers who visited the scene for independent verification confirmed the presence of officials of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on ground. The cause of the incident is yet to be independently verified.
“YEAC-Nigeria calls on the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) to identify the facility operator and conduct a Joint Investigation Visit to the site, and to invoke relevant provisions of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021 as appropriate,” he added.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
President Bola Tinubu has directed heads of security agencies to ensure a safe and secure environment for Nigerians to vote freely in the elections scheduled for January, Minister of Defence General Christopher Musa (retd) has said.
The minister disclosed this while briefing State House correspondents after a security meeting presided over by the President at Aso Villa, Abuja.
He said the session was convened to update Tinubu on the security situation across the country ahead of the polls.
“Today’s meeting was to brief Mr. President on the security situation within the country. You know, the elections coming in January, and it’s important that we keep him abreast of what is ongoing,” the minister said.
Gen. Musa said all heads of security agencies attended the “intensive discussion,” during which the President made clear his expectation for the electoral process.
“Mr. President made it very clear he wants a free, fair, and credible election. We must do everything possible to ensure that the country is safe and secure for the citizens to go out and vote,” Musa stated.
The minister assured Nigerians that the security forces would remain neutral and would not allow intimidation of voters or political actors.
“We are going to ensure that we give everybody opportunity to go and serve, so they have nothing to worry about, nothing to be afraid of, and that nobody is going to intimidate them for whatever reasons,” he said.
“It is important for all other political parties to ensure to understand that the security forces are going to be neutral.”
The Defence Minister also dismissed suggestions that underage persons were being recruited into the armed forces, saying the concern related to terrorists’ use of children.
According to him, “There is nobody that is underage that is being brought here. I think the discussion that was made was that the accusation was on the terrorists using underage.
“Well, we know that we don’t have control over what they do, and that’s why it’s important for us to understand that we must not allow them remain wherever they are.”
He said the President had ordered security agencies to intensify operations to locate abducted persons and dismantle terrorist and bandit enclaves.
“The directive from the president is: all of us must go all out to fish out and rescue all those that have been abducted, kidnapped wherever they are. There shouldn’t be any camp of any terrorists or bandits anywhere in Nigeria,” Musa declared.
On measures to improve security capacity, the minister cited increased recruitment, training, and procurement.
He said the President would soon commission “almost about 10” newly acquired aircraft and helicopters.
“Mr. President is coming to commission a set of new aircrafts and helicopters that have been bought. I think almost about 10 of them in number, and to show Nigerians that despite the economic issue, the issue of security is in the front burner of Mr. President’s view,” he said.
The minister also pointed to the recent salary increment for members of the armed forces, adding that improvements for the police, other agencies, and pensioners were being addressed.
“I’m sure very soon the police and all others is being been addressed, including those of the pensioners. Nobody is going to be left behind,” he said.
The minister urged citizens to support security agencies by reporting wrongdoing, including misconduct by security personnel.
“Security is everybody’s responsibility. It’s not only for members of security forces. Everyone has a role to play,” he said.
“Whatever you see that is going wrong, even with our members that are not doing what is right, please don’t hesitate to report. Action will be taken.”
The high-level meeting was attended by the National Security Adviser, NSA, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu; Minister of Police Affairs, Senator Ibrahim Gaidam; Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle; and Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, Major General Adeyinka Famadewa (rtd.).
Also in attendance were the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu; Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abbas; Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke; and Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lieutenant General Emmanuel Undiandeye.
Other security chiefs at the meeting included the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu; Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency (NIA), Ambassador Mohammed Mohammed; and Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi.

The Senator representing Bauchi Central, Abdul Ningi, has recounted the circumstances surrounding the death of his late colleague, Bello Mandiya, who reportedly slipped and hit his head in his bathroom, with his body discovered about 72 hours later at his Abuja residence.
Ningi narrated the incident during Senate plenary on Tuesday, October 13, 2026.
A video of his account went viral on Thursday.
According to Ningi, Mandiya lived alone, and his absence went unnoticed for days until the chief imam of Apo became concerned that the former lawmaker had missed prayers for three consecutive days.
Ningi said he was in Saudi Arabia when his son called to inform him of Mandiya’s death. His son was among those who discovered the former senator’s body on September 7, 2026.
Recounting the events leading to the discovery, Ningi said Mandiya was last seen by a colleague at about 11 am on Friday, September 4, after returning home to prepare for the congregational prayer.
“He brought out his cap, his phones, and put them on the bed, and went into the bathroom to take his bath.
“After taking his bath, when he was out of the bathroom, then he slipped and knocked his head in the bathroom,” Ningi said.
The senator explained that the incident remained unknown until a foul smell began emanating from Mandiya’s apartment, raising concerns among residents.
“For 72 hours, Mr President, nobody knew where Bello Mandiya was,” he said.
Ningi said those who went to the residence eventually forced the door open and found the former lawmaker dead in the bathroom.
“And there lies Bello Mandiya in the bathroom, lifeless. Seventy-two hours, and that’s a simple tragedy,” he said.
Reflecting on the incident, Ningi said Mandiya’s death underscored the uncertainty of life, stressing that political positions and material wealth offered no guarantee against tragedy.
“There is nothing permanent about anything. Nothing permanent about our position, nothing permanent about our wealth,” Ningi said.
The senator, who said he had known Mandiya since 2002, offered prayers for the deceased and extended his condolences to his family, the people of Katsina State and his former constituents.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Emerging out of stealth mode, robotics startup Origin has raised $20 Mn (around ₹189 Cr) in a funding round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures.
The round also saw participation from Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures and Z21. Angel investors from Anduril, Skild AI, 1X and Tesla also participated in the fundraise. As part of the investment, Zacua Ventures’ founding partner Vivin Hegde has also joined the startup’s board as a director.
The startup said that the fresh capital will primarily be utilised to deploy its flagship OG-1 robot and build a fleet of construction robots. A chunk of the capital will also be used to support “large-scale” pilots with customers in the US and Europe and explore new use cases for bots.
“We think of Origin as a time machine for construction, helping crews complete work faster while moving the industry toward autonomous job sites. Wall finishing and painting are only our starting trades; our ambition is to automate the full range of interior trades so contractors can build faster with consistent quality,” said Origin cofounder and CEO Yogesh Ghaturle.
Founded in 2025 by Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, the US-headquartered startup develops autonomous robotics for construction work. It aims to address widespread labour shortages in the construction sector and claims that its robots can work 3X faster than a human.
Its flagship robot, OG-1, is currently capable of automatically completing wall-finishing tasks such as applying compound, sanding, and priming. The startup claims to have already deployed its robots at construction sites in New York, adding that its bots are also being deployed across commercial spaces, apartments, data centers, hotels and warehouses.
Under the hood, OG-1 is powered by a proprietary foundation model that the startup calls a construction action model. The model integrates a reasoning system to plan complex sub-tasks, an action policy to help it navigate autonomously and a controller for feedback-driven movement.
Going forward, the startup plans to deploy 150 robots by the end of 2027. It is also exploring additional pilots for its offerings in countries like Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia. Origin also noted that incoming investor Zacua will support its expansion plans through its network of contractors, developers and manufacturers.
With the latest fundraise, Origin is eyeing a piece of the global construction robotics sector, which is projected to become a $12 Bn opportunity by 2036. Back home in India, startups like Pace Robotics and Flo Mobility are also raising big bucks to take a lead in the burgeoning space.

items.content:
Ligue 1 club Lyon held off Crystal Palace 3-2 in the Europa League on Thursday, while Sunderland made a late comeback to break the hearts of Portuguese second-division side Torreense.
Bayer Leverkusen went top of the table with a 4-0 win, while AC Milan strolled to victory by the same scoreline.
It was a painful return to his old home for Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage as the UEFA Conference League champions fell to their fourth defeat of the season in all competitions.
Lyon took the lead inside the opening 10 minutes when Corentin Tolisso was quickest to react to the dropping ball at a corner to prod the hosts in front.
Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage two minutes into first-half injury time as he tucked home Keito Nakamura’s cross at the end of a slick move.
A clever set-piece routine allowed Yeremy Pino to halve the deficit for Palace early in the second period.
A clever close-range flick by Pavel Sulc then restored the two-goal buffer for Paulo Fonseca’s charges just inside the final quarter hour.
Kamada smashed home a second for Palace with nine minutes on the clock but the home side held out to make it two wins from two to start the league phase.
In the Estadio Municipal de Leiria, Portuguese Cup winners Torreense looked set to hold their Premier League opponents to a draw until Noah Sadiki’s 93rd-minute strike made it 2-1 for the visitors.
The 15th-placed side in Portugal’s second division stunned Sunderland in the 37th minute as centre-half Volnei Feltes cut past a flimsy challenge and unleashed a piledriver 30 yards from goal, which left Robin Roefs rooted to the spot.
Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris sent on first-team regulars Granit Xhaka and Enzo Le Fee just shy of the hour and the move paid dividends as Jules Ahoka struck shortly afterwards to level the scores.
After a lengthy VAR check decided against awarding Sunderland a late penalty, Torreense must have thought they had done enough to earn a famous point until Sadiki popped up at the death to thrash in the winner.
– Cisse on fire –
Bayer Leverkusen sit pretty at the top of the standings as they followed up their opening 2-0 win with a 4-0 success at Polish side Lech Poznan.
Czech striker Patrik Schick was on target twice from the penalty spot in the first half, either side of a Malik Tillman goal, to ensure the points were wrapped up for Carles Martinez’s side before the interval. Ibrahim Maza added a late fourth.
AC Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory at Red Bull Salzburg, courtesy of a hat-trick scored by Italian teenager Alphadjo Cisse.
Club-record signing Goncalo Ramos made it four on 72 minutes before a red card for Filippo Terracciano took some of the sheen off the win for Ruben Amorim’s men.
La Liga’s Real Sociedad followed up their matchday one loss at home to Bournemouth with a 1-1 draw at Union Saint-Gilloise.
Later, Celtic travel to Lisbon to take on Benfica and Celta Vigo host Italian giants Juventus.
Bournemouth’s Vitality Stadium will welcome European football for the first time in the Premier League outfit’s history as they welcome Austrians Sturm Graz.
AFP

By Adegboyega Adeleye
Former Deputy Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Hon. Kolawole Taiwo, has attributed the state’s growing population and pressure on public infrastructure to its perceived success, saying people continue to move to Lagos because “things are working.”
Taiwo, who represented Ajeromi-Ifelodun Constituency and served as Majority Leader in the Assembly, said this on Vanguard’s Politics Hub, where he discussed why the All Progressives Congress (APC) has continued to govern Lagos since 1999 despite persistent challenges.
Explaining why Lagos continues to experience population growth and infrastructure pressure, the former lawmaker said the situation partly reflects the state’s success, which has continued to attract people from different parts of the country.
“The problem in Lagos is a result of the success, and when you are successful, there are some things that will happen to you that, if you are not careful, it would look like it is consuming you,” Taiwo said.
He further argued that the state’s growing population had increased the pressure on infrastructure and public services, noting that Lagos had grown from about six million people in 1999 to an estimated 20 million today.
“What was the population of Lagos in 1999 compared to the population of Lagos now? 20 million. What was the population of Lagos then? It was around than 6 million,” he said.
Taiwo argued that people naturally move to places where they believe opportunities and public services are better, adding that Lagos’ appeal had contributed to the pressure on its infrastructure.
“Anywhere there is a good thing, people will move there, and that is what is happening; people are moving towards Lagos because things are working,” the former lawmaker added.
“We need a place to put our heads, and there is no government in Lagos that did not do one housing project or the other.”
The former Deputy Speaker maintained that successive administrations in the state had undertaken housing projects, insisting that Lagos was making progress despite residents’ concerns aboutits development challenges. “Lagos is improving,” he noted.
Taiwo also addressed complaints about refuse collection and waste management, arguing that the increased attention being paid to the problem reflected a change in residents’ awareness and willingness to speak up when public services fell short.
“The reason why people are complaining more about refuse now is that their consciousness is very high,” he added.
“In those days, the refuse situation was worse than this but nobody sees it. But now, if you ever see a small thing that is not working well, you will see somebody who will say something.”

items.title: Top 5 oldest countries in the world
items.summary:

However, ranking the oldest countries in the world depends on whether age is measured by the emergence of ancient civilisation, the formation of a unified state or continuous sovereignty. Egypt, Iran, China, India and Greece are among the countries with some of the world’s oldest historical roots.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Some of the world’s oldest countries have histories stretching back thousands of years, with ancient civilisations that developed early systems of government, writing, trade, religion and law.
However, ranking the oldest countries in the world depends on whether age is measured by the emergence of ancient civilisation, the formation of a unified state or continuous sovereignty. Egypt, Iran, China, India and Greece are among the countries with some of the world’s oldest historical roots.
Here are five of the oldest countries in the world based on the history of their ancient civilisations and early states.
1. Egypt
Egypt is home to one of the world’s oldest civilisations, with the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt traditionally dated to around 3100 BC.
Ancient Egyptian civilisation flourished along the River Nile, producing monumental pyramids, hieroglyphic writing and sophisticated systems of administration. Despite centuries of foreign rule, Egypt has retained a strong connection to its ancient heritage.
Its capital is Cairo, and the country remains an important cultural and political centre in North Africa and the Middle East.
2. Iran
Iran, historically known as Persia, has roots in ancient civilisations dating back thousands of years. The region was home to Elamite societies, with organised political centres emerging during the third millennium BC.
The Achaemenid Persian Empire, founded by Cyrus the Great around 550 BC, later became one of the largest empires of the ancient world.
Although Iran’s political systems have changed considerably over the centuries, the country has maintained a distinctive Persian cultural and historical identity. Its capital is Tehran.
3. China
China has one of the world’s longest recorded histories, with early civilisations developing thousands of years ago.
The Xia dynasty is traditionally dated to around 2070 BC, although details of its history remain debated. The Shang dynasty, which emerged around 1600 BC, is supported by archaeological evidence, including inscriptions on oracle bones.
China subsequently developed powerful dynasties, extensive administrative systems and influential philosophical traditions. Despite major political changes, its cultural and written historical heritage spans several millennia.
Beijing is the country’s capital.
4. India
India’s historical roots extend to the Indus Valley Civilisation, which flourished in parts of present-day India and Pakistan more than 4,000 years ago.
Major urban centres such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro featured organised settlements, drainage systems and extensive trading networks. Later societies developed influential religious, philosophical and political traditions across the Indian subcontinent.
India’s modern republic was established in 1950, following independence from British rule in 1947. Its ancient civilisation, however, predates the modern state by thousands of years.
New Delhi is India’s capital.
5. Greece
Greece has a rich history associated with the Minoan and Mycenaean civilisations, which flourished in the Aegean region during the second millennium BC.
Ancient Greece later became known for its contributions to philosophy, mathematics, politics, drama and science. Its influence helped shape many aspects of modern Western thought and institutions.
However, the modern Greek state was established in the nineteenth century after a war of independence against Ottoman rule. Greece’s ancient civilisation and the modern country’s founding date therefore represent different historical milestones.
Athens is the country’s capital.
Vanguard News

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez apologised on Thursday for publicly criticising the club’s board for a lack of investment in the transfer market following their defeat by Atletico Madrid.
The English giants lost 2-0 to Atletico in Spain on Tuesday in the Champions League. They are also off to their worst start to a Premier League season for 40 years.
Martinez took aim at technical director Jason Wilcox, saying he “100 percent” expected more investment in the squad during the transfer window after United finished third in the Premier League last season to return to Europe’s top competition.
United signed three midfielders — Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos — for around £150 million ($198 million), but their spending fell far short of some of their Premier League rivals.
In a social media post earlier Thursday, Martinez said he had spoken “out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted”, but stopped short of apologising.
But having faced criticism for piling pressure on under-fire manager Michael Carrick following United’s poor start to the season, Martinez met with club officials.
– ‘Passionate’ –
Afterwards, Martinez issued a fresh statement saying: “Today (Thursday) I met with the club’s leadership and the manager.
“It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday’s game.
“Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.
“The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.”
The Argentina international’s post-match comments were backed by some fans.
But Martinez has been criticised for his own part in United’s sluggish start to the season.
He scored an own goal in a 1-1 draw at bottom-of-the-table Fulham last month and was outmuscled by Dominic Solanke as 10-man Tottenham salvaged a point at Old Trafford last weekend.
“When I talk about wanting more, I’m talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level,” said Martinez.
“These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.
“I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.”
Pressure is increasing on Carrick just months after he was appointed manager on a permanent basis.
Carrick’s men travel to historic rivals Leeds on Sunday before another Champions League trip, to Italian side Como, on Wednesday.
AFP

items.author: Rameez Khan
items.content:
With the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) now ready to take a back seat, Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Aain-e-Pakistan (TTAP) will establish its own political arm and develop a formal organisational structure at the provincial level, a TTAP leader has revealed.
The leader also said an All Parties Conference (APC) was expected to be held on October 25, give or take a few days.
TTAP, which drew much of its strength from PTI, was now in dire need of its own dedicated support base, the leader said. Given the government's strong-arm tactics, PTI could no longer flex its muscles as it had in the past.
With PTI's support virtually unavailable for the time being, TTAP leadership felt the multiparty opposition alliance needed to build its own support base to organise events and get its message across.
The leader said the alliance had asked its provincial chapters to develop organisational structures and establish working groups and research groups.
Asked why TTAP was pursuing the initiative again despite having announced it several times in the past, the leader said the biggest hurdle had been PTI itself, despite TTAP's desire to establish its own organisational structure.
He said PTI had initially viewed the move as an attempt to establish a parallel power centre, leading to heated discussions between the two sides. However, recent developments had made PTI realise the benefits of such an arrangement.
He said regional parties could offer only limited street power because of their relatively small support bases, adding that PTI had therefore remained TTAP's main source of strength.
Now that PTI chairman had agreed to and fully endorsed the initiative, TTAP had once again embarked on the mission, he said.
The move would allow TTAP to generate political pressure independently of PTI and enable it to challenge what it considers government injustices against the party, the leader added.

items.author: Baba Martins
items.content:
The Allied Peoples Movement (APM) and the Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has asked President Bola Tinubu to either face Nigerians in all the states or drop his reelection ambition.
During the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council on Wednesday, Tinubu had stated that he would skip some campaign rallies.
The President, who hinged his decision on the fact that he did not want governance to suffer, however, promised to find out time to speak with Nigerians.
But reacting in a statement on Thursday, Richard Ihediwa, Director of Strategic Communications of the
MDPCO, said the APM campaign considers Tinubu’s decision not to accompany the Campaign Council to every state of the federation as a “desperate attempt to evade public resentment, knowing that his government has hopelessly renewed the anger of Nigerians, rather than their hope in the past three and half years.”
Ihediwa said the decision not only constitutes a serious “affront” to the Nigerian electorate, but also makes a caricature of democratic ethos”.
“Besides, Mr. President’s decision and his confabulatory statement further confirm fears by Nigerians that he is not fit to face the rigours of governing a nation like Nigeria.”
“The decision not to campaign across the country also reinforces public apprehension that the All Progressives Congress (APC) is not ready for a free, fair and credible election but “plotting to circumvent and compromise the process against the Will of the people.
“A president who believes he has performed well should be confident to defend his record before the people. However, having failed in all of his promises and having no meaningful achievements to boast of, President Tinubu is now fishing for excuses not to face the people.
“If governance was truly his priority, as he claimed, President Tinubu would not have been globe-trothing and staying away from the theater of governance. In fact, he should be eager to use the opportunity of the campaign to face Nigerians and take responsibly for his failures.
“Mr. President is reminded that he told Nigerians not to vote for him in 2027 if he fails to fix electricity in the country. Today, electricity has become more epileptic and Nigerians pay 10 times higher the amount they paid on tariff before this administration.”
APM said the “reckless removal of petrol subsidy, poorly executed floatation of the Naira and other policies without adequate protection for vulnerable citizens has plunged millions of households into punishing hardship”.
The party said Tinubu could not continue to demand another mandate without coming out to campaign and account for the conditions under which Nigerians currently live.
“If President Tinubu is so fatigued, that he cannot go round the country to canvass for votes, then he should withdraw from the race as Nigerians are not ready to continue with an absentee and lethargic president that lacks the capacity and capability to lead from the front.
“Nigerians at this moment earnestly desire a youthful, energetic and active President with stamina for leadership. This is why they are clamouring for the Presidential Candidate of the APM, Seyi Makinde, whose Reset Nigeria Agenda offers solutions for the security, economic and social challenges confronting our nation.”

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan has secured agreement from the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC) to renegotiate the pricing and volume of its remaining financing tranche, with technical teams set to explore adjustments that align borrowing costs with the country's improved market conditions, according to statements issued by the Ministry of Finance on Thursday.
The understanding was reached at a meeting between Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb and ITFC Chief Executive Officer Adeeb Y Al Aama on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. Both sides agreed to find a mutually acceptable solution, as Pakistan seeks to replace costly short-term borrowing with longer-maturity financing without increasing external debt.
Separately, discussions with the OPEC Fund for International Development covered M6 motorway financing, including the approved first tranche, the pending loan agreement and subsequent tranches. Fund President Dr Abdulhamid Alkhalifa invited the minister to visit and sign the project agreement, with ML-1 railway modernisation and power transmission infrastructure identified as priorities.
With Chinese Finance Minister Lan Fo'an, the minister reviewed Pakistan's inaugural Panda Bond issuance, including regulatory support, credit enhancement from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), a 2.5% coupon and strong investor demand. He reiterated Pakistan's intention to be a repeat sovereign issuer in the Chinese capital market, and discussions covered Pakistan's return to the Eurobond market after four years and further Panda Bond issuances under the approved RMB 7.2 billion programme.
Both discussed Pakistan's Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) chairmanship, including the forthcoming summit and the preceding SCO Finance Ministers' Meeting in Islamabad, which Lan said he would attend. They exchanged views on the proposed SCO Development Bank, with China seeking Pakistan's active participation in consultations and support for consensus. Infrastructure cooperation covered progress towards consensus on proposed changes to the route of a China-Pakistan highway project.
In an interview with Channel News Asia, the minister said Pakistan is shifting from aid to trade and investment across bilateral partnerships, acknowledging support from longstanding partners, particularly Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. Remittances reached $41.6 billion last year and are expected to rise to $44 billion this year. He said CPEC Phase II focuses on monetising existing infrastructure through business-to-business collaboration, joint ventures and export-oriented production. Pakistan seeks stronger ties with both China and the United States under an "and-and" approach, while expanding engagement with GCC countries, Central Asian republics and ASEAN to unlock regional trade.
In a meeting with Moody's, the minister welcomed the recent rating upgrade and improved fiscal and external indicators, highlighting renewed access to international capital markets, rising foreign exchange reserves and reduced State Bank forward liabilities. He sought the rating agency's views on achieving a stronger rating and striking the right balance between political risk and economic performance.
At the JP Morgan Investment Seminar, titled "Pakistan: The Road to Resilience in a Turbulent Global Economy Landscape", the minister highlighted fiscal consolidation, revenue mobilisation and sustained primary surpluses, alongside strong remittances and a contained current account deficit. Discussions also covered federal-provincial fiscal coordination.
At the Bank of America Small Talks Symposium, he outlined tax administration reforms, broadening the tax base and privatisation, alongside tariff reforms, competitive inputs and targeted financing to promote export-led growth. Discussions covered managing regional conflict, energy-price pressures and climate-related shocks.
With United Nations (UN) Deputy Secretary-General Amina J Mohammed, the minister discussed development financing, debt sustainability and climate resilience. He emphasised a stronger Global South voice, simpler access to climate finance, local currency financing and strengthening the Borrowers' Forum through peer learning and an effective virtual Secretariat. He thanked her for appreciating Pakistan's mediation in the recent US-Iran crisis.
With Alibaba International Digital Commerce (AIDC) leadership, discussions covered digital payments, a cashless economy and social protection payments. Both sides discussed rationalising e-commerce taxation, accelerating the Pakistan Single Window platform, tracking cross-border payments, and cooperation on cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI) and tax administration. They explored modernising Pakistan Post's sorting systems and expanding agricultural exports to China through Alibaba's retail network.
With International Organization for Migration (IOM) Deputy Director-General SungAh Lee, discussions covered climate mobility, early warning systems, skills training aligned with labour-market demand and safe migration pathways.
With Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas, the two discussed increasing bilateral trade, cultural ties, two-way tourism and resuming high-level exchanges.
In the Atlantic Council conversation, the minister said tax revenues rose 40% over two fiscal years, with the tax-to-GDP ratio at approximately 10.3%, supported by digitalisation and structural reforms. Privatisation of power distribution companies and airport outsourcing are advancing, alongside growing private-sector and foreign investor interest. Rs838 billion has been allocated to the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP). He said Pakistan is moving towards investment- and export-led growth rather than consumption-driven expansion, and will assume the G-24 chairmanship on November 1 while chairing the Borrowers' Platform Governing Council.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan has sought expanded private-sector lending from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and faster processing of the ML-1 Railway Upgradation Project, with ADB President Masato Kanda committing to fast-track the bank's institutional processes for the flagship scheme.
Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Pakistan's Governor to the ADB Ahad Khan Cheema raised the requests at a meeting with Kanda on the sidelines of the 2026 Annual Meetings in Bangkok, according to a statement issued on Thursday. Cheema congratulated Kanda on his re-election for a second term and welcomed approval of the ADB Country Partnership Strategy (CPS) 2026-2030. Emphasising private sector-led growth, he called for expanding ADB's non-sovereign operations in Pakistan and a stronger permanent on-ground presence to facilitate investment transactions and develop a pipeline of public-private partnership projects.
The delegation highlighted the importance of affordable development financing, greater flexibility in ADB's lending framework, expanded private-sector operations and sustained support for Pakistan's priorities. Cheema appreciated ADB's lead role on ML-1 and underlined the need for early completion of the feasibility study and commencement of procurement.
In a separate meeting with Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) Group Chairman Dr Muhammad Sulaiman Al Jasser, Cheema discussed accelerating cooperation under Pakistan's Member Country Partnership Strategy (MCPS) 2026-2030, which envisages $5.6 billion in indicative IsDB Group financing.
He stressed translating the envelope into a concrete pipeline of well-prepared projects with clear timelines for approvals, disbursements and implementation. He appreciated IsDB's $475 million financing for the M-6 Sukkur-Hyderabad Motorway and welcomed continued support for polio eradication, including recent approval of $100 million for Phase V. Seeking enhanced IsDB support for ML-1, he urged close coordination with ADB and other co-financiers. He called for a whole-of-Group approach involving IsDB, the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC), the Islamic Corporation for the Development of the Private Sector (ICD), the Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit (ICIEC) and the IsDB Institute to expand export finance, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), infrastructure, public-private partnerships and energy transition.
Cheema highlighted mobilisation of over $1 billion in trade financing through ITFC during FY2025-26. He sought more competitive terms, reflecting Pakistan's improving macroeconomic and credit profile.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) has averted a potential Rs5-6 per unit hike in the September 2026 Fuel Price Adjustment (FPA), limiting the projected adjustment to Rs2.56 per unit despite rising international fuel prices and constraints on liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies.
The division said targeted load management for approximately two to two-and-a-half hours during September helped reduce reliance on costly alternative fuels, including furnace oil and high-speed diesel, saving consumers from an additional burden of up to Rs3.44 per unit. It added that the provision of imported re-gasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) for power generation at domestic gas prices eased the burden by a further 83 paisa per unit.
Consequently, the September FPA is expected to be Rs1.45 per unit higher than August, with an estimated financial impact of Rs32.7 billion on consumers' electricity bills in November 2026.
The Power Division said international fuel prices rose sharply amid regional conflict and disruptions following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude prices surged beyond $120 per barrel against the benchmark of around $70 assumed during determination of the base tariff.
Despite Qatar's force majeure declaration, Pakistan met its RLNG requirements through contracted supplies and additional spot cargoes.
The statement said the combined impact of fuel price and quarterly tariff adjustments during January-August 2026 was limited to 65 paisa per unit, an increase of only 1.9% over the base tariff. It attributed this partly to tariff rationalisation measures and an additional consumption package for industrial and agricultural consumers.
