items.content: San Francisco: The Federal Reserve will probably need to increase short-term interest rates further to rein in too-high inflation, San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly said on Wednesday, but she also signaled there's no need to do so at the US central bank's October 27-28 meeting."We are more likely than not to need additional adjustments, but the timing of those adjustments to me is something we're still deliberating," Daly told Reuters in an interview. "I don't feel urgent that we have to decide with a limited set of information. I think we have the time that we need."Also Read: US inflation worsened last month to 3.7% in sign that prices remain elevated as midterm elections nearSeveral of Daly's colleagues have also signaled in recent weeks that the Fed is unlikely to raise rates this month. The Fed's policy rate is in the 3.75%-4.00% range, and longer-term borrowing costs are even higher, with some -- like 7.5% mortgage rates -- putting an increasingly obvious damper on demand in some parts of the economy.Daly said she feels financial markets understand the Fed's "reaction function," pointing to how traders responded to data earlier on Wednesday that showed consumer price inflation accelerated to 3.7% in the 12 months through September, a bit faster than economists had anticipated. The Fed targets 2% inflation by a different, but related, measure.Though the initial reaction was "robust," she said -- rate futures traders quickly piled into bets on an October Fed rate hike -- investors "calmed" after parsing through the data. Higher gasoline prices drove the overall increase, and underlying inflation, while still sticky, did not take a sharp turn upward."Definitely this data point suggests that the risk to inflation remains elevated," Daly said. "The risk to inflation has gone up more, but risks are not realities, and reacting on risk when you have time to make a good decision, to me, feels imprudent."Also Read: More expensive gas, semiconductors likely pushed up inflation in US last monthDaly said that the labor market's continued stability gives the Fed room to focus on price stability.But, she said, "why force urgency when you don't need to have urgency? Why not take the time to be thoughtful and deliberate? And we have more meetings ahead of us."Financial market pricing now puts about a 40% chance of a second straight Fed rate hike at the central bank's next meeting, up from before the data but no longer seeing an increase as the most likely outcome.

items.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri
As the number of death row inmates in the country continues to swell, stakeholders in the justice sector and concerned foreign missions have nonetheless commended Nigeria for going ten consecutive years without a state execution.
The Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) recently disclosed that 4,329 persons are currently awaiting execution in various custodial facilities across the federation.
Of this number, more than 82 are women.
In its presentation at an event commemorating the 2026 World Day Against the Death Penalty, the NCoS acknowledged the need for national action on capital punishment, a process it said would ultimately require a constitutional amendment.
“Everybody in our custody has a story, and the way we treat those stories says a lot about our society,” the Comptroller-General of the NCoS, Mr. Sylvester Nwakuche, stated.
The World Day Against the Death Penalty is observed every year on October 10.
This year’s event was jointly organised by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and Avocats Sans Frontières France (also known as Lawyers Without Borders), with support from the Australian High Commission in Nigeria, the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany, and the Embassy of Spain.
A key outcome of the programme was participants’ unanimous call for a moratorium on executions and for the commutation of existing death sentences to life imprisonment.
The last execution in Nigeria took place on December 23, 2016, when three death row inmates were put to death in Benin, Edo State.
Unsurprisingly, the executions drew varied reactions, with Amnesty International condemning them in strong terms.
It noted that they were carried out even though one of the inmates, Apostle Igene, was sentenced to death in 1997 by a military tribunal and was never afforded the opportunity to appeal the verdict.
The Executive Secretary of the NHRC, Dr. Tony Ojukwu, SAN, observed that, under Nigerian law, capital punishment presents a constitutional duality.
He stated that whereas Section 33(1) of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) protects the right to life, it also contains an explicit exception for court-ordered executions.
On the other hand, Section 34(1)(a) guarantees the right to human dignity and protection against inhuman or degrading treatment.
According to Ojukwu, the Supreme Court affirmed the constitutional validity of capital punishment in Onuoha Kalu v. The State (1998) 13 NWLR (Pt. 583) 531, reaffirmed in Joseph Amoshima v. The State (2011) 14 NWLR (Pt. 1268) 547.
“However, the constitutionality of the penalty does not dilute the non-negotiable requirement of fair trial guarantees under Section 36.
Systemic issues, such as inadequate pro bono defence, forced confessions, and pre-trial delays, undermine procedural justice,” he added.
Ojukwu, SAN, argued that Nigeria, having achieved 10 consecutive years without a state execution, has satisfied the international standard for a de facto moratorium.
“Yet, mandatory death sentencing continues, leaving over 3,000 individuals on prolonged death row detention.
“To resolve this limbo, statutory and executive mechanisms exist. Section 12(2)(c) of the Nigerian Correctional Service Act, 2019 authorises the commutation of death sentences for inmates who have exhausted appeals and remain unexecuted after a specified period.
“Furthermore, State Governors possess explicit constitutional powers of prerogative of mercy under Section 212 (and the President under Section 175) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.
“Pursuant to Section 5 of the NHRC (Amendment) Act 2010, the Commission calls for three immediate policy steps:
Transition Nigeria’s 10-year pause into an official executive moratorium on executions.
“Urge State Governors to systematically invoke Section 212 of the Constitution and Section 12(2)(c) of the NCoS Act to commute death sentences to life imprisonment.
“Re-evaluate mandatory death penalty statutes to allow judges to weigh mitigating circumstances and systemic vulnerabilities during sentencing,” he added.
Prior to 1990, only one country in Africa, Cape Verde, had abolished the death penalty.
However, of the 55 African Union member-states, 28 have now abolished it in law, with Zimbabwe the latest to join the list.
While 20 countries apply a long-term moratorium on executions, seven nations, including Nigeria, still retain and use capital punishment.
German Ambassador to Nigeria, H.E. Stefan Rössel, said that although the death penalty remains part of Nigerian law, the 10-year mark since the last execution is an important milestone that deserves to be celebrated.
Drawing on his country’s experience, the Ambassador said: “Germany opposes the death penalty unconditionally. Working towards its permanent abolition is a pillar of our human rights policy.
“We believe that the right to life is universal, as laid out in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and must not be denied by law.
“The last execution on German soil took place in 1981. Today, Article 102 of the German constitution states simply: ‘Capital punishment is abolished.'”
He said the death penalty raises important questions about justice, human dignity and the protection of human life.
“We recognise the deep suffering caused by serious crimes. The grief of victims and their families must be acknowledged, and their need for justice, truth and support deserves our continued attention.
“At the same time, every justice system must protect human rights and guard against the possibility of error. A death sentence is irreversible. If a conviction is later found to be wrong, the consequences cannot be undone.
“We must also not forget that those sentenced to death often spend years, sometimes decades, behind bars before being executed. At the same time, our understanding of crimes and justice continuously evolves.
“For instance, we have gained a much more nuanced understanding of mental illness in recent decades, and how that might affect the way we judge the circumstances of a crime committed many years ago.
“Ultimately, we need to ask ourselves: do we want to live in a society in which the state is tasked to take a human life?” he queried.
The German Ambassador concluded by recognising that the issue of the death penalty is complex, involving legal questions, public concerns and the needs of victims and their families.
“We hope that Nigeria’s approaching 10-year milestone can be a source of pride. We believe: not using this ultimate form of punishment is a sign of strength, not weakness,” he added.
Likewise, the Australian High Commissioner to Nigeria, H.E. Ms. Leilani Bin-Juda, PSM, described the 10-year non-execution achieved by Nigeria as “a significant milestone that calls for a reflection of how far Nigeria has come and the next step to be taken.”
She urged the country to build on the achievement and chart a way forward, insisting that capital punishment is a cruel, inhumane and degrading punishment that has no place in any modern justice system.
For his part, the Ambassador of Spain to Nigeria, H.E. Félix Costales Artieda, categorically opposed the use of the death penalty “under any circumstance and for any crime.”
He insisted that life is an inalienable fundamental right that no state has the right to take, stressing that there is no evidence that capital punishment has helped to reduce crime anywhere in the world.
The Ambassador noted that in the United States alone, 130 persons sentenced to death have been found innocent and released from death row since 1973.
He urged Nigeria to take appropriate measures to commute the sentences of those already facing the death penalty.
The Country Head of ASF France, Angela Uwandu Uzoma-Iwuchukwu, said the organisation, on the basis of its conviction that the right to life is sacrosanct, had embarked on a series of projects aimed at highlighting the need for Nigeria to do away with capital punishment.
She said it has since represented over 1,000 persons through its Right To Life project.
Referencing the case of Arthur Angel, who spent 16 years in prison, 10 of them on death row at Enugu Prison, before his release in 2000, she argued that lapses in a justice system run by humans cannot be overlooked.
“Arthur Angel spent 16 years in jail for a crime he did not commit,” she noted, insisting the death penalty is “discriminatory as it targets the weakest in the society.
“There are people who cannot afford the services of good lawyers. We all know that the quality of defence provided for a defendant matters so much.
“A lot of those on death row in Nigeria were represented by inexperienced lawyers, some of whom were National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members.
“A mistake made at the trial stage may not be corrected at the appeal stage,” the ASF Country Head added.
She also referenced a recent case involving a poor farmer, Sunday Jackson, who was sentenced to death for self-defence but later pardoned by the Adamawa State Government.
For now, Nigeria’s position is a contradiction: a death penalty on the books, thousands waiting under sentence, and no one carrying it out.
Hopes are high that the 10-year milestone will become a step towards the abolition of capital punishment in the country.
The post Death penalty: Foreign missions applaud Nigeria’s abolitionist shift appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Real Madrid scored three late goals to overturn a two-goal deficit and secure a dramatic 4-3 victory over Roma in the UEFA Champions League on Jose Mourinho’s return to the Stadio Olimpico.
Madrid appeared destined for defeat after Roma took a 3-1 lead in the 83rd minute, but substitutes Carlos Espi and Endrick inspired a stunning comeback before Antonio Rudiger struck the decisive goal in the 90th minute.
The victory extended Real Madrid’s perfect start to their Champions League campaign, having won both matches, while Roma were left with one point from their opening two games.
Mourinho, who previously led Roma to the Europa Conference League title in 2021-22 and the Europa League final the following season, received a warm reception from the home supporters, who displayed banners celebrating his time at the Italian club.
Roma made a strong start and took the lead in the 20th minute when Marten de Roon fired a first-time effort from the edge of the box after being set up by Matias Soule.
Real Madrid responded five minutes later through Kylian Mbappe, whose effort took a deflection off Gianluca Mancini before looping over goalkeeper Pierluigi Gollini.
The goal was Mbappe’s 72nd in the Champions League, moving him ahead of Real Madrid legend Raul, who finished his career in the competition with 71 goals. The appearance also marked the French forward’s 100th match in the tournament.
Roma regained control after the break, with Donyell Malen scoring twice in a six-minute spell to put the hosts in a commanding position.
Malen made it 2-1 after capitalising on a mistake by Vinicius Junior, whose attempted flick gave away possession. The striker’s shot took a deflection off Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde before finding the net.
The Dutch forward struck again soon afterwards, finishing calmly to extend Roma’s advantage to 3-1. Although the goal was initially ruled out for offside, a video assistant referee review confirmed that Valverde had kept Malen onside.
Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini introduced several defensive substitutes as he attempted to protect the lead, but Real Madrid’s late attacking changes proved decisive.
Espi pulled one back five minutes after coming on, converting the rebound after Gollini had parried Endrick’s header.
Endrick then levelled the contest by heading home from an Arda Guler corner, leaving Roma struggling to contain Madrid’s set-piece threat.
The visitors completed the turnaround in the 90th minute when Rudiger volleyed home from close range following another Guler delivery to seal a remarkable 4-3 win.
The result provides a boost for Real Madrid as they continue their Champions League campaign, while Roma will need to improve after failing to hold on to their advantage on home soil.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the expanded presidential campaign council of the All Progressives Congress (APC) as a “confession of fear”, accusing President Bola Tinubu of prioritising political alliances over Nigeria’s economic hardship and insecurity.
Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), said the expansion of the council for the 2027 general election reflected the president’s concern about his political standing rather than the challenges facing Nigerians.
In a statement issued on Wednesday by Phrank Shaibu, director of strategic communication of the ADC presidential campaign council, Atiku argued that the inclusion of more political figures would not address hunger, violence, kidnappings and the rising cost of living.
“Only a man afraid of his record would think he could bury it under hundreds of names,” the statement reads.
“Tinubu can gather every governor, minister and political defector in Nigeria. None of them can erase the hunger in people’s homes, bring back those killed by violence or free Nigerians still held captive. Their families are waiting for answers, not another campaign list.”
The APC initially released its presidential campaign council list on August 22, naming Abdulaziz Yari, former governor of Zamfara State, as director-general. The expanded council includes Nyesom Wike, minister of the Federal Capital Territory;
Ademola Adeleke, governor of Osun State; and Chukwuma Soludo, governor of Anambra State.
Atiku also accused Tinubu of maintaining an extensive political structure while Nigerians grapple with the consequences of rising prices and declining purchasing power.
“Tinubu has room for an army of ministers and a stadium full of campaign officials, but no room in his plans for Nigerians crushed by the cost of living. He feeds his political machine and tells hungry families to sacrifice,” he said.
The former vice-president maintained that adding more names to the campaign council would not change Nigerians’ experiences under the current administration.
He also faulted the decision to inaugurate the APC campaign council at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, describing the venue as public property that should not be used for partisan political activities.
“The Presidential Villa belongs to the Nigerian people. It is not a campaign venue or the private property of any political party. Using it for an APC political event is a gross breach of public trust and a troubling abuse of public office,” he said.
Questioning the choice of venue, Atiku argued that Abuja had sufficient alternative locations for the event.
“Abuja has no shortage of halls and public spaces large enough to host a campaign gathering. Why, then, did Bola Tinubu choose to inaugurate his campaign council at night, behind the gates of the Presidential Villa?” he asked.
He said the decision raised questions about the president’s confidence in his performance, adding that Nigerians should assess his
administration based on their experiences.
“Nigerians may draw their own conclusions. But a president confident in his record should be willing to face the public in daylight and ask for another mandate,” he said.
Atiku further described the expanded council as an attempt to shield Tinubu from public criticism by recruiting more political figures, including members of other parties.
“When the first list drew criticism, Tinubu had a chance to show that he understood the country’s anger. Instead, he returned with an even longer list, reaching into other parties for more names. He is collecting politicians like shields against public judgment,” he said.
The ADC presidential candidate also cited a claim that 17.9 million more Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty, linking the figure to the economic and security challenges confronting the country.
He argued that the enlarged campaign structure would do little to make food affordable or improve the purchasing power of workers and other citizens.
“No campaign council, however crowded, can make food affordable, restore a worker’s purchasing power or explain why the sacrifices demanded of ordinary Nigerians never seem to reach Tinubu’s own political circle,” he said.
Atiku said the ADC had assembled its own campaign team to offer Nigerians an alternative, insisting that voters would ultimately judge the president by their living conditions rather than the number of political figures backing his re-election bid.
“On January 16, the ballot will contain no column for the size of a campaign council. Nigerians will judge Tinubu by the lives they have lived under his government,” he added.

Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, for 2027, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to go home and let Nigeria breathe.
Adebayo said this in a statement, in Abuja, on Wednesday.
He was responding to the President’s plan to excuse himself from the rigors of physical campaigns in some states ahead of the presidential polls.
Tinubu spoke at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, where he urged members to take the party’s message to Nigerians across the states and local government areas while he continues to attend to matters of governance.
In response, Adebayo said if Tinubu is too tired to campaign, he is too weak to govern.
In a statement signed by his Presidential Campaign’s Chief Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, the SDP candidate described Tinubu as a “president in absentia” at a time Nigeria needs hands-on leadership.
Adebayo said, “Nigeria is too complex, too dynamic, and currently too distressed to be governed by remote control.”
He cited what he called repeated instances of the President governing from a distance, including prolonged medical vacations disguised as working visits, absence during national emergencies and reliance on proxies to announce state policies.
The SDP candidate further said, “We have seen repeated instances where the President is visibly missing when the country needs reassurance.
“From unannounced foreign trips during critical economic decisions to his complete silence during widespread regional protests, he has consistently acted like a president in absentia. If you are too tired to campaign, you are too weak to govern.”
Adebayo alleged that the decision to stay off the campaign trail was not about strategy but fear.
“The excuse of bowing out of the 2027 campaign is a cowardly smokescreen. The truth is that the President is terrified of the Nigerian people,” he argued.
According to him, the administration’s economic policies – fuel subsidy removal fallout, skyrocketing inflation and currency instability -have made the President unpopular.
“He knows the pain his bad policies have inflicted on families. He is hiding because he cannot face public anger, and he knows any appearance on a campaign trail will be met with collective booing of a betrayed populace.”
Adebayo also said, “It is time to face reality: step aside, go home, and let this country breathe.”
He called on the administration to prioritise national interest over political survival and be transparent about the President’s capacity to lead for the remainder of his term.

By Dickson Omobola
National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Felix Muoka, has insisted that Nigeria and Nigerians are better off than ever before, saying the party will win the 2027 presidential election based on its positive records.
Muoka said the APC was working hard to secure voters’ support, adding that the party would not take Nigerians’ votes for granted.
Speaking on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, Thursday, he said the party’s preparations and campaign efforts were aimed at securing as many votes as possible in the next general elections.
He said: “Qualitatively speaking, our country is better. Nigerians are better today than they have ever been. Is there a country that has transited from this depressed economy, like we have had for decades, to that level of prosperity that didn’t go through these stages?
“Nigerians also understand that. So what the president has done is to give this country a fighting chance, not just at recovery, but at building the prospects for sustainable prosperity.”
On the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, he said: “What you saw today and what we’ve been up to is really taking ourselves seriously. If we thought this was all said and done, we wouldn’t put in this level of energy and work in an effort to really get to the last vote within the electorate. We are not taking this for granted. We’re taking it very seriously. I’m sure that if our party was docile and we were doing nothing to campaign or put out our information, you would also bring me here to say that we had been very docile. We’re a political party.
“We are a party for a reason. We are in this to compete with other political parties and to win the support of Nigerians. Since 2023, there’s a reason that our party has been very successful. Since the last general elections, we’ve won fantastically all elections in which we have contested. There’s a reason for that. It’s because we prepare. We do our homework.
“Nigerians bought in and voted for our party massively in 2023. We won that election, even though there are elements who want to claim that they won without evidence. But we won that election without question. As I said a few minutes ago, in every other
election that has been called since then, Nigerians voted, not Indians. Nigerians voted in all the other elections since 2023. We won by upwards of 90 per cent.
“Let me remind you that the APC is the governing party in this country, put in office by Nigerians. Already, the answer to your question has been codified in an election in which the APC is governing, not just at the centre, but in so many states in our country.”
On the APC’s chances in 2027, he said: “We will win the election. We are working hard to win the election. I think that Nigerians are going to stand tall, shoulder to shoulder with the APC to win the next election.”

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
By Joseph Erunke
The Federal Government has proposed a new examination timetable that will see candidates sitting the 2027 West African Examinations Council (WAEC), National Examinations Council (NECO) and other major external examinations receive their results by August, ahead of the September admission process into tertiary institutions.
Under the proposed schedule, the government is seeking to end delays in the release of examination results that could disrupt candidates’ transition from secondary schools to universities, polytechnics and colleges of education.
A statement on Wednesday night by the Director, Press and Public Relations of the Federal Ministry of Education, Boriowo Folasade, said the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’id Ahmad, disclosed the plan during a meeting with heads and representatives of examination bodies at the Federal Ministry of Education headquarters in Abuja.
“The meeting focused on harmonising examination schedules, preventing clashes among major examinations and ensuring that results are processed and released within agreed timelines, “the statement said.
According to the proposed timetable, the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) will conduct the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) from March 15 to 25, with results expected in the same month.
NECO’s Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) is scheduled to hold from April 1 to May 14, while WAEC’s West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) will run from May 11 to June 18.
Both NECO and WAEC are expected to release their results in August 2027.
The National Business and Technical Examinations Board (NABTEB) examination is proposed for June 1 to July 5, while the National Board for Arabic and Islamic Studies (NBAIS) examination will hold from June 10 to July 9. Results from both examinations are also expected in August.
The proposed schedule places the examination bodies under pressure to complete their respective processes in time to meet the government’s August results-release target.
The Federal Ministry of Education said the initiative was part of the education reform agenda of the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Tunji Alausa, under the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI), which seeks to improve efficiency, coordination and educational outcomes.
It added that engagement with examination bodies would continue to ensure compliance with the proposed timelines, strengthen accountability and align the release of results with tertiary admission schedules.
The government, under President Bola Tinubu, said it remained committed to reforms that would improve the efficiency of the education system and expand timely access to tertiary education.
However, the timetable remains proposed, with the success of the plan depending on effective coordination among the
examination bodies and their ability to meet the agreed deadlines.
If implemented as planned, the initiative could give candidates and their parents greater certainty over the transition from secondary school examinations to tertiary admissions, while reducing disruptions caused by late results.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Pope Leo XIV is out of bed, walking and eating after doctors removed a cancerous tumour from his lung, while post-surgery tests show his progress is “normal”, his doctors said Wednesday.
Part of the pope’s right lung was removed in Tuesday’s operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital and the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics is now awaiting the results of a biopsy to determine if the cancer has spread.
Blood tests and a chest X-ray meanwhile “confirm a normal post-operative course”, doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora said in a statement released by the Vatican.
“The values are within the expected range for the type of procedure performed,” they said.
The discovery on Tuesday that a nodule detected in Leo’s lung was cancerous has plunged the Catholic Church into a period of uncertainty.
“It’s a shock for everyone. We’re in ‘wait-and-see’ mode,” a Vatican source told AFP.
Doctors said his recovery was “proceeding as expected” and the pontiff had eaten both breakfast and lunch, been walking about his room, and had done some respiratory physiotherapy.
Another Vatican source said the pope had even celebrated a mass on Wednesday in a specially prepared room on the 10th floor of the hospital, where is staying.
The papal suite on the same floor is where popes are usually treated. It has a private chapel but is currently being refurbished.
– ‘Show my spiritual support’ –
The sporty 71-year-old, elected as the first pope from the United States only last year, made the surprise announcement that he would be undergoing surgery after Sunday prayers.
Messages of support flooded in from around the world, including from Britain’s King Charles III, who is also being treated for an undisclosed cancer.
A banner flying outside the hospital read “Long live the pope!” and a handful of people recited prayers for the hospitalised pontiff.
Nearby, nun Angele Bilegue said she had come to pray for Leo.
“I’m not worried. I came to express my closeness, to show my spiritual support, because I also came for Pope Francis,” she told AFP.
Leo’s predecessor, the Argentine Francis, spent five weeks last year being treated for double pneumonia at the same hospital, before his death at the Vatican on April 21, 2025.
Experts said much would depend on how advanced Leo’s cancer was, and whether it had spread, but the Vatican has said it had been detected early and was localised.
Before the operation, the Vatican said the pope’s recovery should take around a week. All his audiences have been cancelled until October 20.
“If we are dealing with stage I or II disease, and recovery is good… the patient can resume a normal life and usual activities within a few weeks,” Alain Gelibter, an oncologist at Rome’s Policlinico Umberto I hospital, told AFP.
The Chicago-born Leo had entered the hospital smiling and waving on Tuesday.
In the hospital chapel, dozens of faithful prayed for the pope’s health during the operation.
– New uncertainty –
The shock news of the tennis-playing pope’s illness has rattled the Catholic Church.
Expert Marco Politi, who has spent decades covering the Vatican, told AFP: “The Church is now in a state of uncertainty. When Leo was elected everyone foresaw a long papacy.”
Hendro Munsterman, a theologian and expert for Dutch newspaper Nederlands Dagblad, told AFP “we have a pope whom everyone described as young, active and athletic. Now, we have a pope who also has his own vulnerabilities, which will change his image.”
His health issues may prompt him to speed up personnel appointments, Munsterman said.
Politi said Leo had been working on “repairing” rifts between various wings of the Church, and many will want him “to continue with this important mission as soon as possible”.
Filipino Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, newly nominated to the influential role of dean of the College of Cardinals, celebrated mass on St Peter’s Square on Wednesday instead of Leo.
The surgery has raised questions about whether Leo will go ahead with a lengthy visit next month to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he worked as a missionary for two decades.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Bradley Barcola silenced his critics as the Liverpool forward ended his goal drought with a hat-trick in a chaotic 6-3 win against LASK in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Barcola had come under fire for some lacklustre performances since his blockbuster £123 million ($161 million) move from Paris Saint-Germain in August.
But the France forward finally started to live up to his hefty price tag with his first goals for Liverpool in his seventh appearance.
Barcola struck twice before the interval at the Raiffeisen Arena after Ronald Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the first half with his maiden goal for the club.
Jeremie Frimpong netted the fourth after the break against the Austrian champions before Barcola completed his treble.
There was still time for Lewis Koumas to score his first Champions League goal as Liverpool maintained their 100 percent record in this season’s tournament after beating Atletico Madrid in their opening game.
It was a welcome boost for Iraola following his first defeat in eight games as Liverpool manager when Premier League leaders Manchester City won 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday.
Iraola this week said he has “100 per cent” trust in Barcola and Florian Wirtz, who has struggled mightily since joining from Bayer Leverkusen last year.
Injuries to Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, who all missed the trip to Austria, increased the pressure on Wirtz and Barcola to carry the Liverpool attack.
The pair repaid Iraola’s faith with a much-needed display of their undoubted qualities.
Now Iraola will demand they produce that level of intensity and quality on a regular basis.
The trip to Linz was the second of six games in 18 days for Liverpool, forcing Iraola to make changes in a bid to save his players from burnout.
Reds captain Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister and Victor Munoz were all rested as Frimpong, Kostas Tsimikas, Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha came in.
– Clinical Barcola –
After some disjointed displays at the start of Iraola’s reign, this was an indication of what they can become under the former Bournemouth boss, although he will still be concerned about their defensive issues.
Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the 22nd minute, rising highest to meet Tsimikas’s corner with a thumping header past LASK keeper Lukas Jungwirth.
The on-loan Barcelona defender’s goal was swiftly followed by one for Barcola 96 seconds later.
Ngumoha was the catalyst with an incisive run into the LASK area and Barcola applied the finishing touch as he guided a clinical finish beyond Jungwirth.
Iraola’s men were running riot and Barcola scored their third in the 37th minute.
It was a riposte to the criticism of Wirtz and Barcola as the pair combined to cut through the LASK defence.
Barcola picked out Wirtz and the German played a pinpoint return pass that allowed the 24-year-old to fire past Jungwirth.
Frimpong has also frustrated Liverpool fans since signing last year, making his goal in the 51st minute a welcome tonic for the Dutch right-back.
Tsimikas got to the byline and lofted a cross towards Frimpong, who belied his diminutive stature with a towering header into the bottom corner.
Robert Ljubicic reduced the deficit in the 63rd minute with a composed finish from Yvan Dibango’s pass.
But Barcola sealed his treble with a nimble finish from Frimpong’s pass in the 66th minute.
Teed up by Frimpong, Koumas hit Liverpool’s sixth with a searing strike in the 72nd minute.
Despite the introduction of Van Dijk and fellow defender Joe Gomez, Liverpool lost control in the closing stages.
Florian Flecker’s diving header two minutes later punished slack Liverpool defending.
Flecker struck again with a close-range finish in the 77th minute, but nothing could spoil Barcola’s big night.

items.content:
Manchester United are reportedly considering Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler, former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte as potential replacements for Michael Carrick if the club decides to part ways with its current manager.
According to talkSPORT, the three managers have attracted interest from different figures within the Old Trafford hierarchy as pressure mounts on Carrick following a difficult run of results.
United’s reported interest comes after their 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, which extended their winless run to five matches across all competitions.
The result also followed a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur, a run of form that has raised concerns about the team’s performances and Carrick’s tactical decisions.
The defeat to Atletico also prompted defender Lisandro Martinez to criticise technical director Jason Wilcox over what he reportedly viewed as insufficient squad strengthening.
United will look to end their poor run when they face historic rivals Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday.
Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, the station’s chief live football anchor, Adrian Durham, suggested Carrick’s position could become increasingly difficult if the team fails to improve.
“Does it feel like an inevitability? Absolutely, that Michael Carrick will go,” Durham said.
He added that Carrick would need to turn around the team’s results to improve his chances of remaining in the job.
Durham also expressed concerns about Carrick’s tactical decisions in the Atletico Madrid match, arguing that some of the changes made during the game contributed to United’s defeat.
Among the three reported candidates, Nagelsmann and Conte are said to be available for an immediate appointment.
Conte left Napoli by mutual consent in May, while Nagelsmann reportedly departed his position as Germany coach following the country’s elimination by Paraguay in the round of 32 at the World Cup.
The report said United’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, was advocating for Nagelsmann internally as a potential successor should the club decide to dismiss Carrick.
Hurzeler, meanwhile, remains under contract with Brighton until 2029 after signing an extension in May.
The German coach is reportedly favoured by Wilcox and has overseen a strong start to the Premier League season, with Brighton winning four of their opening six matches to sit third in the standings.
Hurzeler has also guided Brighton to victory over Manchester United in the third round of the EFL Cup in September, adding to his credentials as a potential candidate.
However, Manchester United have not been reported to have made a formal appointment decision, and Carrick’s immediate future could depend on the team’s results in the coming matches.

items.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye
Vice-President Kashim Shettima has criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar over what he described as disrespectful comments about President Bola Tinubu, saying anyone seeking the presidency must show discipline and respect for public institutions.
Shettima spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 election.
In his remarks, Shettima said Atiku’s repeated presidential bids and recent policy proposals did not, in his view, excuse language he considered disrespectful toward the sitting president. He also questioned how Atiku’s proposed production subsidies would be funded.
“Those who want equity must come with clean hands. You can call him Bola. If you like, you can call him Adekunle. But the truth is that he is the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.
“Your Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, Atiku Abubakar. I will still respect him and call him his former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar.
“I will not follow suit with the maverick Babachir Lawal and call him Kachalla, no. But believe me, Atiku Abubakar, who has contested for the presidency of this country for the eighth time, is no Abraham Lincoln. He is more of Oginga Odinga.”
Shettima framed his criticism as an argument about the conduct expected of presidential contenders, saying the higher the office sought, the greater the responsibility candidates bear in their words and dealings with public institutions.
“The presidency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is not an ordinary political prize. It is the highest expression of constitutional authority in our country. And those who aspire to occupy it must demonstrate, even before they get there, the qualities they will expect of themselves, if entrusted with the responsibility of leading more than 200 million Nigerians.
“Political ambition is not merely the desire to occupy public office. It is a test of character, cerebral strength, intellectual maturity, and responsibility. The higher the office a person seeks, the greater the discipline expected in his words, conduct, and relationship with public institutions,” he added.
Turning to Atiku’s proposal on production subsidies, Shettima questioned the cost and the competing priorities that might be affected.
“Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, this political season has become a masterclass in cinematic comedy. Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal for production subsidies raises questions that some changes cannot answer. Who pays? Who benefits? And which competing priorities must surrender their funding? A change in ideological wardrobe cannot balance a national budget.”
The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council inauguration, held at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa in Abuja, formally brought the expanded campaign structure into focus as the ruling party prepared for the 2027 general election.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja
The House of Representatives Committee on Public Petitions has ordered a halt to further development on a disputed parcel of land in Umundoche community, Ngor Okpala Local Government Area of Imo State, pending the resolution of a petition alleging illegal land acquisition and intimidation of residents.
The committee also directed that armed men allegedly operating in the community be disarmed following claims that villagers had been threatened with firearms amid the dispute.
The directives were issued on Wednesday during a hearing on Petition No. 901 of 2026, filed by J.U. Okoye Chambers against Prince Charles Amadi, also known as Chavon; Chikadibia Anyanwu; and Chidubem Nwosu.
The petition alleges the illegal acquisition of more than 2,500 hectares of land, shooting and attempted murder of villagers, the invasion of the community by armed men, desecration of a corpse, abuse of police powers and breach of a memorandum of understanding.
The petition also names HRH Eze Lambert Unuoha, traditional ruler of Nma 1 of Obioma Autonomous Community in Ngor Okpala, as a respondent.
Addressing the parties, the committee chairman, who was represented by his deputy, Rep. Matthew Nwogu, directed that no further activity should take place on the disputed land until the matter was resolved through the committee or other appropriate means.
“There are orders that no more actions on this land until this matter is resolved,” the chairman said.
“Either through this place, or through which other means you want to resolve it. That’s the first order. No more putting up caterpillars or bulldozers in that land.”
He said the committee had contacted the Department of State Services (DSS) and the police, which, according to him, denied supplying firearms to the men allegedly operating in the community.
“All the boys that are armed in that village should be disarmed. Because we have made contact with the DSS. They said they didn’t give them the gun. The police said they didn’t,” he said.
The chairman said the directives were intended to prevent further escalation while the committee examined the allegations.
The hearing featured disagreements among lawyers representing the parties over the status of a pending court case and whether the committee should continue considering the petition.
Counsel to Charles Farms Limited, identified during the proceedings as one of the parties involved in the dispute, told the committee that his clients had legally acquired the land and paid the relevant parties.
He rejected the allegations in the petition and disclosed that his clients had instituted legal proceedings against the petitioners.
According to him, he wrote to the committee on September 28, 2026, explaining his clients’ position and providing details of the court proceedings.
He, however, acknowledged that he had not brought the supporting court documents to the hearing.
The committee chairman said a letter and oral explanations were insufficient, demanding certified documentary evidence to establish the status of the case.
The lawyer subsequently undertook to organise the documents he had received, certify the necessary papers and submit them to the committee.
A committee member, intervening in the exchange, cautioned against allowing the existence of a court case to automatically terminate the legislative investigation.
He said the committee had a constitutional responsibility to consider petitions submitted to it, adding that the scope of the court proceedings would have to be examined before determining whether they covered all the issues raised in the petition.
“That a matter is in court does not immediately stop us from doing our duty. This is a constitutional committee. One of the very few committees written into the Nigerian constitution,” the lawmaker said.
He urged the parties to respect the committee’s procedures and allow the petitioners an opportunity to present their grievances.
“Tomorrow he might be the one petitioning this National Assembly over an issue. So let us respect processes, respect our constitution. And then respect the will of the people who have come here to seek justice,” he added.
The lawmaker also urged the committee to give the respondents time to file formal responses, noting that the proceedings would benefit from documentary evidence from both sides.
Petitioners allege intimidation of villagers
Counsel to the petitioners, Dr Julius Onyemi, told the committee that efforts had been made to resolve the dispute before the matter was brought before the House.
He said the first petition was submitted on July 17, 2026, followed by another on August 14 and a subsequent petition later that month.
Onyemi alleged that he had made several attempts to contact the respondents to resolve the dispute with the community but was unsuccessful.
He further alleged that the court action was initiated after the petitions had been submitted to the House and suggested that it was intended to frustrate the committee’s proceedings.
The lawyer also accused the respondents of using security personnel and armed men to intimidate residents and prevent them from accessing their community.
He urged the committee to ensure that the alleged intimidation stopped while the petition was being considered.
Onyemi questioned the circumstances surrounding the land acquisition and called on the parties to demonstrate compliance with customary land acquisition procedures.
He also raised concerns about the environmental implications of the proposed development, asking whether an environmental impact assessment had been conducted and made available to the community.
The lawyer argued that residents had a right to be consulted over activities that could affect their land and environment.
The respondents’ representatives disputed the allegations, maintaining that the land had been legally acquired. The claims remain subject to the committee’s investigation.
Committee demands video evidence
During the hearing, one of the respondents’ representatives challenged claims that armed men had visited the community and threatened residents.
He said he had been in the area since Monday and disputed claims that he was present at the location where the alleged incident occurred.
He offered to provide his flight itinerary and hotel booking details to support his account.
The chairman subsequently asked the parties to provide any available video or photographic evidence to establish what happened.
He said the committee was interested in examining the available evidence rather than relying solely on conflicting oral accounts.
The chairman reiterated that further development on the disputed land must stop and that armed men allegedly involved in intimidating residents must be disarmed.
The committee adjourned the matter until November 2026 to allow the respondents to study the petition, prepare their formal responses and submit the necessary documentary evidence.
The hearing formed part of the committee’s consideration of the petition seeking intervention over the disputed land in Umundoche community, Imo State.
The allegations have not been established as findings of fact. The respondents maintain that the land was legally acquired, while the committee is yet to conclude its investigation.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…Says Nigerians, not AI, will determine election outcomes
By Omeiza Ajayi
ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has assured Nigerians that voter accreditation and result collation will not be fully automated in the 2027 general elections, insisting that citizens, not Artificial Intelligence AI, will determine the outcome.
Chairman of the Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN said on Wednesday that “Algorithms will not, and must never, decide the 2027 vote.”
INEC in its Wednesday Bulletin said Amupitan spoke in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the Artificial Intelligence and Democracy Forum 2026, held in collaboration with Yiaga Africa.
Amupitan said, as a foundational policy, no critical electoral decision, result collation, voter accreditation or candidate qualification would ever be fully automated or delegated to an autonomous system.
“Human accountability, statutory oversight and judicial review will remain paramount at every stage of the electoral chain,” he said.
Responding to the forum’s opening question, “Will Algorithms Decide the 2027 Vote?”, he said the answer was an unequivocal no. According to him, the choice of who leads Nigeria belongs exclusively to the Nigerian people.
The chairman said the forum was taking place 92 days before the general elections, in a digital landscape that had shifted significantly since 2023.
He warned that the Commission was no longer dealing only with the “analogue” challenges of logistics but with a world in which AI can influence what a voter sees, how the voter thinks and how the voter trusts.
“The greatest threat we face is not the hacking of a ballot box, but the hacking of the voter’s mind,” Amupitan stated.
He said generative AI had reduced to near zero the cost of producing convincing deepfakes, including videos of candidates saying things they never said and of INEC officials giving false instructions.
“If a voter cannot distinguish between truth and a synthetic lie, the foundation of informed consent crumbles,” he said.
The INEC chairman warned that a well-timed deepfake video or cloned audio recording of a candidate, an election official or a security chief could announce a false candidate withdrawal, a postponement of the election or inflammatory ethnoreligious statements, and spread virally within minutes.
He added that malicious actors could also impersonate the INEC Chairman, Resident Electoral Commissioners RECs and other officials to issue fake guidelines, declare unauthorised results or instruct voters to stay home.
On the Commission’s response, Amupitan disclosed that INEC had created an AI Unit within its Information and Communication Technology ICT Directorate, equipped with real-time digital monitoring tools, deepfake detection software and data analytics expertise.
He said any AI tool or automated system deployed by the Commission for logistics, database management or operational support must undergo rigorous audits to guarantee explainability, fairness and security before deployment.
The Commission, he added, was working on a Digital Strategy to audit the information environment and partnering with technology platforms for the rapid debunking and labelling of AI-generated content touching on electoral processes.
Amupitan called on technology companies, including Meta, X, Google, TikTok and Telegram, to rapidly restrict unlabelled synthetic media impersonating election officials, candidates or security personnel.
He also asked them to enforce disclaimers on political advertisements and restrict micro-targeting based on ethnicity, religion or local origin.
He urged political parties and candidates to sign an Ethical AI Code of Conduct, committing to refrain from deploying deepfakes, synthetic impersonation, dark ads or automated botnets.
The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission does not view AI only through the prism of risk. He described it as a powerful force multiplier for administrative precision, predictive planning and institutional integrity.
He said while human collation remained the statutory standard for declaring results, AI could run parallel statistical audits on polling unit result sheets uploaded through the eEC8A, flagging mathematical inconsistencies, atypical entry patterns and image quality defects for administrative review.
On logistics, he said AI-driven geospatial analytics could help INEC deploy ad-hoc staff, vehicles, boats and sensitive materials to 176,846 polling units before 7:30 a.m. on election day.
Amupitan said the 2027 General Election would be the largest democratic exercise on the African continent, involving over 103 million registered voters across 774 Local Government Areas LGAs. He said 10 of the 14 major operational milestones under the Electoral Act 2026 had been successfully executed.
The two-day forum was attended by the Chairperson of the Economic Community of West African States Network of Electoral Commissions ECONEC and Chairman of the Senegal Electoral Commission, Mr Abdoulaye Sylla, along with National Commissioners, RECs, political party leaders, civil society organisations, security agencies, technology firms and the media.
Amupitan said algorithms had no moral compass, no civic duty and no constitutional oath. “They do not have a conscience, they do not have a country, and they do not have a vote. INEC’s job is to ensure that the voice of the people is heard clearly, above the noise of the machines.
“On election day in 2027, it will be the thumbprint of the Nigerian citizen, guided by their own will and their own hopes, that decides our future,” Amupitan said.

items.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of coercing opposition governors into its presidential campaign council, alleging that the ruling party is undermining Nigeria’s multiparty democracy ahead of the 2027 general election.
The ADC Presidential Campaign Council’s Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, made the allegation in a statement reacting to the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on Wednesday.
Ologbondiyan accused the ruling party of using state power to pressure opposition governors into its fold or include them in its campaign structure despite their continued membership of other political parties.
“What we are witnessing is not politics but political abduction. You cannot claim to be a democrat while using state power to force opposition governors into your party and then drafting them into your campaign council. This is political banditry,” he said.
The ADC spokesman also alleged that the APC was pursuing a political agenda aimed at concentrating power in the hands of one individual, claiming that national institutions, security agencies and the judiciary were being deployed to weaken opposition forces.
He urged Nigerians to resist what he described as an attempt to establish an immoral political order driven by the desire to retain power at the expense of citizens’ welfare.
Ologbondiyan further accused the ruling party of neglecting the economic hardship, hunger and insecurity confronting Nigerians while focusing on its political interests.
“These particular sets of leaders don’t care about the current conditions of the people but how best to remain in power at a time when average Nigerians find it difficult to eat and be secure,” he said.
He also alleged that the country’s democratic space was shrinking, citing what he described as the suppression of dissenting voices, harassment of opposition figures and the weakening of democratic institutions for partisan purposes.
“Never in our democratic journey have we witnessed this level of intolerance and desperation. The APC government has weaponised poverty, hunger and insecurity to subjugate Nigerians and cripple the opposition,” Ologbondiyan said.
He added that the situation was inconsistent with the democratic ideals for which late politician Moshood Abiola and other pro-democracy figures fought.
The ADC spokesman also promoted the party’s presidential ticket of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi, describing them as having the experience and democratic credentials to address the country’s challenges.
“Atiku Abubakar is a democrat to the core. He has the national spread, the capacity and the will to reunite Nigeria and restore our battered democracy,” he said.
The ADC Presidential Campaign Council called on Nigerians, media organisations, civil society groups and the international community to oppose what it described as the APC’s anti-democratic agenda and support efforts to protect multiparty democracy.

items.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu
The Senate has urged the Federal Road Maintenance Agency (FERMA) to undertake emergency repairs on failed sections of the Onitsha–Ogbaru–Ndoni–Rivers Federal Highway pending its comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction.
The Senate said the immediate intervention would reduce the hardship faced by motorists and communities along the route.
Following a motion sponsored by Senator Tony Nwoye, representing Anambra North, the Senate also proposed that the Federal Government mandate the South East Development Commission (SEDC) or the Federal Ministry of Works to carry out the remedial work.
The Senate recommended that the comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction be executed through a special intervention programme or another appropriate funding arrangement, given the road’s strategic importance as a major link between the South-East and South-South geopolitical zones.
It mandated the Senate Committee on Works to conduct an on-the-spot assessment of the highway, engage relevant stakeholders and report back within four weeks with appropriate recommendations.
It also urged the Senate committees on Works and Appropriations to ensure adequate budgetary provision for the road’s comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction.
The Senate noted that the highway was partially constructed in the late 1980s but had suffered decades of neglect without any major rehabilitation.
It said the prolonged abandonment, ageing infrastructure, increasing traffic volume and lack of routine maintenance had left the road in a deplorable condition, characterised by extensive pavement failures, deep potholes and severe erosion.
According to the Senate, the condition of the highway posed a serious threat to the lives and property of commuters and other road users.
It further observed that the deterioration had significantly increased travel time, with a journey of approximately 70 kilometres from Onitsha through Ogbaru to Ndoni, which would ordinarily take about one hour, now taking nearly two hours.
The Senate said the situation had resulted in higher transportation costs, loss of productive man-hours and disruption of commercial activities.
It added that the failed sections frequently caused vehicles to break down and remain stranded for extended periods, exposing commuters to road accidents and heightened security risks.
The Senate also noted that the highway served as a vital economic corridor, supporting significant oil and gas exploration and production activities in the Ogbaru oil belt and contributing to Nigeria’s economy.
It expressed concern that continued neglect of the federal highway had affected interstate commerce, agricultural value chains, regional integration and investment, undermining efforts to promote economic development, national connectivity and safe transportation.
The Senate warned that without urgent intervention, further deterioration would endanger lives and property, impede economic activities, increase transportation costs and affect oil exploration and production along the Ogbaru corridor.
It added that the situation would worsen the hardship faced by residents of Anambra and Rivers states and negatively affect businesses that depend on the transport corridor.

items.content:
The Nigerian Football Federation (NFF) will receive $175,000 more in its annual subvention from the Confederation of African Football (CAF).
CAF President, Patrice Motsepe, announced the 33% increase in federation subvention on Wednesday, with its members to receive $700,000 annually going forward.
The African football governing body revealed that the latest increase in the third since 2021, the year Motsepe took over.
The South African football administrator has overseen a 250% increase in subvention since then, jolting the amount from $200,000 to the $525,000 currently being received by Federations.
Other subventions to regional and club football association bodies were also increased by the president and the executive committee, with zonal unions to receive $900,000 from $750,000, while the African Clubs Association will also get a $500,000 subvention from the current $400,000.
In the press release, CAF stated that the latest subvention increments shows its commitment to ensure football in its 54 member associations is world class and self-sustaining.
CAF reiterated that the increased financial support should be channeled towards multiple projects related to football in their respective countries including human development, women and youth football, and improved administration.
“The announcement represents another significant increase in CAF’s financial support for its Member Associations under the leadership of CAF President Dr Motsepe and the CAF Executive Committee, as part of his commitment to making football in each of Africa’s 54 Member Associations world-class and self-sustaining.
“The latest allocation represents a 250% increase compared with 2021, underlining CAF’s continued commitment to investing in football development and strengthening the capacity of its Member Associations.”
“The additional financial support is intended to assist CAF Member Associations in strengthening football development structures, investing in youth and women’s football, improving administration and governance, and building sustainable programmes that create opportunities for players, coaches, referees and other football stakeholders.”

By Emma Nndozie
The Chairman of the Forum of Former Members of the Enugu State House of Assembly, Denge Josef Onoh, has urged Nigerians to elect leaders with proven competence in the 2027 general elections to address the country’s economic challenges and rising poverty.
Onoh made the call on Tuesday while addressing traders, importers and business communities from the South-East, South-South and Middle Belt regions in Apapa, Lagos.
He said the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians required a deliberate shift towards leadership focused on economic recovery, human development, fiscal accountability and inclusive governance.
Citing figures he attributed to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) and the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index, Onoh argued that the economic reforms introduced since May 2023 had significantly worsened living conditions for many Nigerians.
“The facts before us are stark, painful, and undeniable,” he said, attributing the rising cost of living and growing poverty to the combined effects of fuel subsidy removal and foreign exchange reforms.
Onoh claimed that national poverty had risen from 56 per cent to an estimated 63 per cent, leaving more than 140 million Nigerians below the poverty line. He also cited a figure of 17.9 million Nigerians falling into multidimensional poverty over a three-year period.
He further expressed concern over inflation, rising food prices, higher petrol costs and the depreciation of the naira, saying the developments had severely weakened household purchasing power.
According to him, petrol prices had risen from about ₦185 per litre to more than ₦1,000, while the exchange rate had moved from about ₦460 to over ₦1,500 to the dollar.
“This is no longer just a statistical debate; it is a lived, daily crisis of survival in households across every state of our federation,” he said.
Questions APC campaign strategy
Onoh also criticised what he described as the political class’s preoccupation with retaining power ahead of the 2027 elections, instead of addressing the economic difficulties facing citizens.
He cited the inclusion of opposition figures in the revised Presidential Campaign Council of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), including Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, a member of the Peoples Democratic Party; Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance; and Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party.
He argued that the arrangement had raised questions about party loyalty and the priorities of political leaders.
“While some political actors defend these moves as a practical ‘rainbow coalition’ necessary for electoral survival, it sends a dangerous signal to the electorate,” Onoh said.
He added that Nigerians should look beyond political alliances and assess candidates on their capacity to address the country’s economic and governance challenges.
According to him, the 2027 elections present an opportunity for voters to demand a different standard of public service and elect leaders with credible plans for economic recovery.
Outlines priorities for next government
Onoh identified four priorities he said should guide the choice of leaders in 2027: proven economic competence, investment in human development, fiscal accountability and inclusive governance.
On economic competence, he called for leaders with practical, evidence-based plans to stimulate production, control inflation and promote sustainable industrialisation.
He said investment in education, infrastructure and healthcare should take precedence over short-term relief measures, while public officials should ensure transparent management of public resources and eliminate waste.
Onoh also stressed the need for inclusive governance, arguing that sustainable economic growth would remain difficult if large sections of the population continued to experience poverty and deprivation.
“The year 2027 is not just another standard election cycle; it is our collective opportunity for structural liberation,” he said.
“We must use our constitutional power to vote for vision, competence, and character. We owe it to the present generation and those to come to elect leaders who will systematically lift Nigerians out of poverty and safeguard our economy.”

By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR
The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) may suspend the posting of corps members to Cross River State after its Director-General expressed dissatisfaction with the dilapidated state of the scheme’s permanent orientation camp in Obubra.
A source within the scheme, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak publicly on the matter, told our correspondent that the decision followed a recent inspection of the camp by the Director-General.
According to the source, the Director-General was concerned that the facilities had become outdated and no longer met the required standards for hosting corps members.
NYSC Director General during inspection
He said the proposed directive would take effect after the ongoing 2026 Batch C, Stream One orientation exercise, effectively ruling out postings to the state for Stream Two, pending further notice.
“After going through the camp facilities, we discovered that the facilities are old and no longer meet the required standards.
“As a result, the Director-General said there would be no further posting of corps members to Cross River until further notice.
“In fact, he is saying that the state needs a brand-new camp,” the source said.
He added that the scheme was seeking the intervention of the Cross River Government to address the situation.
Findings indicate that the condition of the camp has reportedly reduced the number of corps members accommodated in the state.
The facility, which previously hosted about 2,500 corps members per stream, now accommodates slightly more than 1,000, while more than 700 corps members are reportedly processing relocation to other states.
This represents a sharp decline from the approximately 6,000 corps members the state was expected to receive annually.
The orientation camp, located in Obubra Local Government Area, occupies the premises of the former Government Science School and is said to have operated for more than two decades without any major renovation.
The Cross River Coordinator of the NYSC, Mrs Mojisola Oyenuga, declined to comment on the matter.
The state Commissioner for Youth Development, Mr Ijom Ukam, had not responded to inquiries on the proposed suspension as of press time.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
Manufacturer Aamir Allawala told a government-sponsored seminar on Thursday that authorities used a wrong figure of 18.5% for the National Tariff Policy (NTP) to make a case for a 52% cut by claiming Pakistan had the highest tariffs in South Asia.
Allawala disclosed that the government included customs duty, additional customs duty (ACD) and regulatory duty (RD) to show Pakistan's tariff in 2023 was 18.54%, but said comparative tariffs of India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and other regional economies were based only on customs duty. He used World Trade Organisation (WTO) data to prove his point and shared the link to the source.
He said that against the claimed tariff figure of 18.54%, Pakistan's tariff was 10.3%, which was not only lower than the regional average but also far lower than India and Bangladesh.
Interestingly, the commerce ministry had last year shared similar figures on its website as part of the tariff policy but subsequently removed those slides.
When contacted, the commerce ministry spokesperson said the WTO "has not clarified about the inclusion or exclusion of para-tariffs of any country including the countries located in South Asia, however, WTO does not include para tariffs in the calculation of simple average in their tariff profile report," according to the commerce ministry.
It was responding to a question about the tariff rates given in the NTP for regional countries that were inclusive of para-tariffs, as was in the case of Pakistan.
The World Bank, which provided technical support for the preparation of the tariff policy, did not respond to a set of questions about using any wrong numbers for making a case for tariff cuts.
The commerce ministry said para-tariff, as per the WTO, means border charges, fees or levies imposed on foreign trade transactions that function like a tariff but are not included in a country's official customs tariff schedule. It added that the WTO calculates countries' tariffs based on the information provided by the respective countries.
Allawala shared these startling details at the 39th International Conference and Annual General Meeting of the Pakistan Society of Development Economists (PSDE). The conference was organised by the Pakistan Institute of Development Economics under the banner of the Ministry of Planning.
The drafters of the policy, currently in its second year of implementation, challenged the statement, which if proven correct can open a Pandora's Box for the World Bank, the Prime Minister's Office, the commerce ministry and the National Tariff Commission.
According to Allawala, the NTP inflated Pakistan's tariff to make it look like the highest. It added Pakistan's extra import duties to Pakistan's number only, turning the WTO's 10.3% into 18.5%, and compared that with every other country's customs duty alone. It did the same in its trade-weighted chart: 10.36% shown in the NTP, against the WTO's 7.6%, according to Allawala.
The basic premise used for the NTP that Pakistan's tariffs were the highest in South Asia is not correct and an apple had been compared with an orange to prove that, he said. The NTP should be reopened and the error rectified, he added.
To a question whether the Prime Minister's Office, the World Bank and the commerce ministry misled the nation, Allawala said he would not judge intentions, as it was a complex matter and there was a possibility that the Prime Minister's Office might not have been properly briefed.
To a question whether the prime minister should order an investigation to ascertain the facts, Dr Rubina Athar, a strong proponent of trade liberalisation, said the figures were misleading, as those used for the NTP were also often quoted by the World Bank in different studies.
The session was moderated by senior customs official Mukaram Jah Ansari.
It is correct that Bangladesh's and India's tariffs comprise customs duty but Pakistan's tariff by definition is inclusive of customs duty, ACD and RD, said former National Tariff Commission chairperson Dr Rubina Athar, a core member of the NTP team.
She said the para-tariffs are other taxes at import stage like sales tax and withholding taxes, which have not been included in Pakistan's 18.5% tariff in the base year. Tariff Policy Board member Dr Manzoor Ahmed, also part of the NTP core team, said the figures quoted by Allawala and Dr Rubina were correct in their own rights.
The commerce ministry spokesperson said the figure of 18.54% represents Pakistan's overall average tariffs, including 10.3% customs duty, 3.65% ACD and 4.57% RD.
Under the policy, Pakistan has decided to cut import duties from 20.1% to 9.7% by 2030 - a reduction of 52% in protection that has panicked many industries.
To a question whether it was correct that based on 2023 data, after excluding para-tariffs, Pakistan's simple weighted average most-favoured-nation (MFN) applied tariffs was 10.3% compared to India's 17% and Bangladesh's 14.1%, the commerce ministry spokesperson said the definition used by the WTO for para-tariffs is different from what is being assumed in the question.
According to the WTO Tariff Profiles 2024, Pakistan's simple average MFN applied tariff rate of 10.3% combined with 3.65% ACD and 4.57% RD makes it the highest in South Asia. India's was 17%, Bangladesh's 14.1%, and Nepal's 12.7%.
Allawala said Bangladesh has regulatory duty and supplementary duty. Sri Lanka charges Ports and Airports Development Levy, CESS and Social Security Contribution Levy. Türkiye has additional customs duties and additional financial liabilities, all of which are para-tariffs. However, the NTP added para-tariffs only for Pakistan and not for any other country.
The government and proponents of the NTP, aimed at demolishing half of the protection wall, argued that due to high import tariffs Pakistan's exports were not increasing.
But Allawala argued that Pakistan's low exports are not because of high tariffs. They are because of the geopolitical security situation, Pakistan's lack of intelligent strategic FTAs that practically close off African, Central Asian and South American markets for Pakistani exports, and a systemic cost disadvantage with the highest electricity tariffs, interest rates and taxation in the region.
