items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Panic has gripped the American Business Forum (ABF), the Overseas Investors Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OICCI) and the Collect and Recycle (CoRe) Alliance after the federal authorities suddenly decided to ban the use of recyclable bottles by the beverages sector in breach of international and local regulations.
The move to suddenly ban the use of 100% recyclable polyethene terephthalate (PET) in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) has sent shockwaves, mostly among multinational companies, which were already complying with the international and local environmental standards. ABF requested the withdrawal of the proposed ban on PET bottles and the effective enforcement of the ICT Single-Use Plastics Regulations, 2023, in an appeal to the minister for interior.
Separately, the OICCI and the CoRe Alliance approached the minister for finance, minister for investment and minister for climate change to review the proposed ban, which was also threatening foreign investment and the circular economy.
"The CoRe Alliance seeks your office's intervention to withdraw the proposed ban on PET bottles, ensure effective enforcement of the ICT Single-Use Plastics Regulations, 2023, and support the government's broader efforts to promote ease of doing business, attract and retain foreign investment, and maintain a predictable, investment-friendly regulatory environment," read a letter sent to the investment minister.
The alliance ensured its commitment to advancing circular economy solutions in Pakistan. The multinational companies and their advocacy groups in Pakistan stated that the leading international regulatory frameworks, including the European Union's Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR), prioritise packaging recyclability, effective collection and recycling systems, and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), rather than imposing blanket bans on recyclable PET beverage packaging.
They panicked after the Islamabad Capital Administration started raiding shops for using PET bottles without realising that these bottles were already in compliance with the regulations. The alliance said that there was also no notification issued by the CDA or the Ministry of Interior for banning PET and its removal from trade. They said that the PET bottles were fully compliant with the Pak EPA Single-Use Plastics Regulations of 2023. PET is on the positive list of plastic packaging.
The alliance, the OICCI and the American Business Forum said that reportedly, on the instructions of the Office of the Chief Commissioner, and chairman Capital Development Authority (CDA), retailers and Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) companies in ICT were advised to discontinue the sale of products packaged in polyethene terephthalate bottles across various categories.
The CoRe Alliance believes that such a ban would be scientifically unjustified, environmentally counterproductive, inconsistent with international circular economy best practices, and detrimental to businesses operating in the country, it added. Furthermore, the proposed ban contradicts the spirit of the ICT Single-Use Plastics (Prohibition) Regulations, 2023.
PET is a lightweight, food-grade, 100% recyclable polymer with an established collection and recycling value chain. Unlike some plastics, post-consumer PET bottles are commercially valuable and sought after for recycling into fibres, packaging and new bottles, supporting economic activity and livelihoods across collection, sorting and recycling.
A ban could undermine this circular economy value chain. Scientific life-cycle assessments evaluate packaging impacts from raw material extraction and manufacturing to transportation, collection and end-of-life management, according to CoRe. Replacing PET with glass, aluminium or other single-use alternatives may not improve environmental outcomes, as heavier materials can increase transportation emissions while others require more energy and resources for production, it added.
The priority should therefore be to strengthen existing PET waste collection, segregation and recycling systems to prevent environmental leakage, rather than banning a valuable and recyclable material, according to these representative bodies.
Similarly, the ICT Single-Use Plastics (Prohibition) Regulations, 2023, notified under the Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997, already provides a regulatory foundation for addressing plastic pollution. Rather than pursuing a blanket PET ban, the government should strengthen implementation through mandatory producer-funded collection and recycling systems, measurable recovery targets, waste segregation and investment in recycling infrastructure, it added.
Various reports indicated that local administrative authorities commenced enforcement actions, which included the sealing of several retail outlets across the city. Industry experts and business leaders have warned against such coercive measures.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The government has decided to conduct a study to restructure regulatory bodies as some organisations exercise regulatory powers from within ministries, raising questions about their independence.
The government has described some as "blurred ministry and regulator roles". It feels that they are under the influence of some ministries and the regulatory bodies are exercising regulatory powers from within the ministries, which raise questions about the independence of regulators. The proposed focus of the study will be on making the federal regulators effective and accountable without eroding the independence credible regulation depends on.
Owing to this, the government is of the view that the situation requires a review. The role of regulators is to safeguard the interests of consumers but they are working under complete control of the ministries while ignoring the welfare of consumers.
Moreover, rapid expansion has taken place since 2024 and new authorities for virtual assets, seeds and food safety have come on stream. This also underscores the need for a review of the regulators to ensure their independence.
The government is working on autonomy versus accountability of the regulators. Recurring tariff, licensing and enforcement questions have been raised. In the energy sector, two regulators are functioning, whose decisions have a direct impact on consumers. These include the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) and the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra).
These regulatory bodies come under the administrative control of the cabinet but are following directives from the Ministry of Energy. Hardly, they are said to have taken decisions that shield the interests of consumers.
In the power sector, Nepra has allowed companies to set up power plants by giving the incentive of capacity charges, which put a burden of over Rs2 trillion on consumers every year. In a recent case, the regulator increased the multi-year tariff of K-Electric but reversed the decision following a motion filed by the Power Division. Such decisions are alleged to have caused controversies.
Earlier, in the rental power case, the Supreme Court ruled that Nepra should not follow the "manipulated" decisions of the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC).
Similarly, Ogra has been locked in controversies as in the past it granted licences to oil marketing companies despite not meeting the requirement of building storages. It also issued licences to LPG marketing companies in bulk, though only a few had LPG supplies.
Sources were of the view that the federal bodies with regulatory powers had been developed over seven decades, which now require a review under the present circumstances. The study will address three questions – how they were designed, how well they functioned and whether statutory aims were met.
It will also examine the purpose of the law and the failures each law fixes, whether it still holds and whether regulation is still the right tool. The study will propose key recommendations relating to legal, institutional, financial, capacity and system gaps.
The federal bodies have been divided into three groups. First is related to sector and independent regulators, which include Nepra, Ogra, the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority, State Bank of Pakistan, Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, Competition Commission of Pakistan, Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan and Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority.
The other category comprises technical, safety and professional services, which include Pak-Environmental Protection Agency, Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority, Pakistan Engineering Council, PNDC and quarantine departments. The third category has hybrid and borderline bodies including the Higher Education Commission, HRSA, Public Procurement Regulatory Authority, Alternative Energy Development Board, PDA and Special Technology Zones Authority.

Minister of State and Chairman, Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, Bilal Bin Saqib, holds high-level meetings with senior leadership of the World Bank Group, IFC, Treasury, Digital & AI and Controllers during the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group in Bangkok, Thailand. The discussions revolved around modernising Pakistan's financial infrastructure and mobilising international capital.
The engagements focused on positioning Pakistan to benefit from the next generation of global financial innovation, including asset tokenisation, digital capital markets, artificial intelligence, cross-border payments and technology-enabled regulatory supervision.
In a meeting with Imad N Fakhoury, Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Central Asia at the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the World Bank Group's private-sector development arm, discussions explored potential collaboration on tokenised bonds and sukuk, digital financial infrastructure, cross-border payments and mobilisation of international private capital.
The engagement examined how emerging financial technologies could help Pakistan attract investment, deepen its capital markets and create new financing opportunities for the public and private sectors.
Chairman PVARA also met Jorge Familiar, Vice President and Treasurer of the World Bank Group, to explore potential cooperation on digital bond issuance, asset tokenisation and AI-enabled financial operations.
Discussions included opportunities for knowledge exchange, institutional capacity building and the application of emerging technologies.

items.content:
Speciality chemical manufacturing startup Scimplify has raised $25 Mn (around ₹238 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by Hitachi Ventures, the venture capital arm of Japan’s Hitachi Group.
The round also saw participation from existing backers such as Accel, Bertelsmann India Investments, 3one4 Capital and Omnivore. New investors including Teknor Apex, Henkel and an undisclosed Japanese chemical company also joined the round.
The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its research, processing and manufacturing capabilities across rare earth and critical metals purification. The funds will also go towards scaling its semiconductor chemicals and battery chemicals businesses.
A chunk of the capital will also be used to strengthen SciNode, Scimplify’s agentic AI platform that connects research, process development, control and physical manufacturing.
Founded in 2023 by Sachin Santhosh, Salil Srivastava, Dheeraj Dhingra and Hersh Manek, Scimplify is a B2B platform that specialises in end-to-end sourcing and manufacturing of speciality chemicals. It also offers contract research and commercial chemical manufacturing for agro-chemicals, active pharmaceutical ingredients and fragrances.
The startup currently operates R&D facilities in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, with its SciNode software platform supporting its manufacturing operations. Its network comprises more than 500 manufacturing partners and thousands of scientists and technical partners.
Prior to this, Scimplify had secured $40 Mn in its Series B funding round, co-led by Accel and Bertelsmann Investments, in March last year.
“In the 18 months since our initial investment, Scimplify has grown from serving 600+ customers across 16 countries to building a global platform with 1,000+ customers across 40+ countries,” Accel partner Rachit Parekh said.
Scimplify’s customers include Henkel, Coromandel, Dr Reddy’s, Coherent, Holcim, BASF, Sanyo, Marubeni, among others. The startup claims to operate across five countries and serves more than 1,000 customers across over 40 countries.
Going forward, Scimplify plans to expand its presence in the US, initially focusing on sectors where domestic processing capabilities remain limited. These will include rare earth and critical metals purification and processing as well as high-purity semiconductor and battery chemicals.
Scimplify’s latest fundraise comes as India looks to strengthen its position in the global chemicals value chain. Earlier this week, Bengaluru-based speciality chemicals startup NuSynth Technologies raised ₹36.5 Cr in a seed round co-led by Avaana Capital and Shastra VC.
Scimplify operates in the broader Indian deeptech sector, which continues to draw investor attention on the back of regulatory push, subsidies, innovative local solutions, a thriving talent pool and growing local demand.
Overall, Indian deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals in Q3 2026, a 176% increase from $105 Mn across 29 deals in the year-ago period. The sector outpaced the broader Indian startup ecosystem, where funding grew 5% to $2.2 Bn.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
A 66-year-old scientific study predicted that the world’s population would reach an extreme mathematical limit on November 13, 2026.
The Doomsday: Friday, 13 November, A.D. 2026 study was published in the journal Science in 1960 by physicist Heinz von Foerster and his colleagues at the University of Illinois.
The researchers examined historical population growth and developed a mathematical model suggesting that, if the existing trend continued unchecked, the global population would approach infinity on November 13, 2026.
The paper warned that accelerating population growth could eventually put enormous pressure on the resources and living space available to humanity.
However, the study did not predict that Earth would explode, humanity would suddenly disappear, or a natural disaster would destroy the world on that date. Its doomsday reference described the mathematical consequences of assuming that population growth would continue accelerating indefinitely.
Why Did Scientists Predict Doomsday in 2026?
The researchers based their calculations on historical population trends. Their model suggested that population growth was accelerating so rapidly that it would eventually reach an impossible mathematical limit.
The November 13 date represented the point at which the model broke down under its assumptions.
Population growth has since changed, with falling birth rates in many countries slowing the global growth rate.
What Do Current Population Projections Say?
The United Nations expects the world’s population to continue growing for several decades, reaching approximately 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s before declining slightly.
The 1960 paper does not provide evidence that humanity faces an imminent end.
Therefore, there is no credible scientific or anthropological evidence that Earth or humanity will come to an end on November 13, 2026.

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
German police have seized a humanoid robot after it allegedly touched a teenage girl inappropriately and made sexually suggestive movements toward her in Cologne.
Investigators are now trying to determine whether two young men deliberately controlled the robot during the incident. Police also believe the pair may have livestreamed the encounter on social media.
The incident took place shortly before midnight on October 10 near a fast-food restaurant in a busy nightlife area of Cologne.
Videos shared online appear to show the teenager standing with two friends, aged 17 and 18, when a red-and-gold humanoid robot approached her from behind.
According to police, the robot then touched the girl’s buttocks. It also repeatedly made thrusting movements toward her.
Two Young Men Allegedly Livestreamed the Incident
Police said the robot belonged to a 16-year-old boy. He was with a 19-year-old companion at the time.
Authorities allege that the two young men recorded and livestreamed the incident themselves. They also reportedly commented on the situation live on social media.
Police officers responded shortly after the incident was reported and found the two suspects nearby.
By that time, the robot had already been placed inside the trunk of a Volkswagen.
Officers seized the humanoid robot along with both suspects’ smartphones as evidence.
German media identified the machine as a commercially available humanoid robot worth around €5,000, or approximately $5,600.
Suspect Claims Contact Was Accidental
One of the people involved later claimed on TikTok that the robot accidentally collided with a woman while trying to avoid another pedestrian.
However, longer videos circulating online appear to show the robot making sexually suggestive movements after the contact with the 16-year-old.
Investigators are now reviewing surveillance footage and videos posted online to establish exactly what happened.
Police also want to determine whether someone remotely controlled the robot, whether certain actions were programmed in advance, or whether the machine performed the movements independently.
Case Raises New Legal Questions
The unusual case has also raised questions over how existing criminal laws apply when a robot is used in potentially abusive conduct.
Under German law, the offense of sexual harassment generally requires direct physical contact between people.
Legal experts told German broadcaster RTL that this could make it more difficult to prosecute the robot’s owners under existing sexual harassment laws.
Instead, police are investigating the incident on suspicion of a sexually motivated insult.
Authorities may also examine possible violations linked to the unauthorized publication of images or videos.
So far, police have not filed charges against either suspect.
The case highlights a growing challenge for law enforcement as humanoid robots become more advanced and increasingly available to private users.
It also raises wider questions about legal responsibility when a person uses a machine to carry out actions that could otherwise be considered criminal.

items.content:
Telecom giant Jio Platforms has set a price band of ₹1,065-₹1,119 per share for its IPO, which is set to open for public subscription next week.
The company is seeking to raise ₹30,213 Cr at the upper end of the price band, overtaking Hyundai Motor’s ₹27,870 Cr IPO in 2024 to become the largest public offering to hit the Indian equities market till date.
At the upper end of the IPO, RIL’s telecom arm is seeking a valuation of ₹10.3 Lakh Cr for the IPO.
Jio filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) earlier today for its IPO comprising a fresh issue of up to 27 Cr equity shares. Post anchor bidding on October 19 (Monday), the IPO will open for public subscription on October 21 and close on October 23.
The telco has reserved ₹500 Cr worth shares for eligible employees, who can avail a discount of ₹54 per share. Additionally, up to ₹2,500 Cr will be reserved for eligible shareholders of RIL.
The company intends to utilise ₹27,500 Cr of the fresh capital raised via the IPO for prepayment, in full or in part, of certain outstanding borrowings availed by its material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm (RJIL).
The remaining proceeds, ₹2,713 Cr to be precise, will be allocated for general corporate purposes may fund strategic initiatives, growth opportunities, capital expenditure, working capital, marketing and other business requirements.
The issue has no OFS component, meaning existing shareholders will not sell shares through the IPO. RIL currently holds a 66.43% stake in Jio Platforms, while Meta and Google own 9.98% and 7.73%, respectively.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
WhatsApp is officially rolling out guest calls, allowing people to join a WhatsApp call even if they do not have an account.
Guests can join directly from a web browser without downloading the app or creating an account. WhatsApp says the calls are free, have no time limit, and remain protected with end-to-end encryption.
How Guest Calls Work
Only users with a WhatsApp account can create a call link. To do this, users can open the Calls tab, tap the “+” button, and create a call link. That link can then be shared with anyone.
A guest simply opens the link in a browser, enters their name, and joins a waiting room. The host must manually approve every guest before they can enter the call.
Guest calls support both individual and group calls with up to 32 participants.
Guests Get Most Calling Features
Guests can use several of the same features available during normal WhatsApp calls.
They can share their screen, react with emojis, and raise their hand during a call.
However, guests cannot see other participants’ phone numbers, send messages during the call or invite additional people.
The host can remove guests at any time or end the call for everyone.
Calls Remain End-to-End Encrypted
WhatsApp says guest calls still support end-to-end encryption.
The web client creates a unique identifier used to encrypt the call, allowing guests to participate without having a normal WhatsApp account.
Calendar Integration Is Coming
WhatsApp is also working on integrations with Google Calendar and Outlook.
Users will eventually be able to add WhatsApp call links directly to calendar invitations through a plugin.
People receiving those invitations will be able to join the meeting even if they do not have a WhatsApp account. WhatsApp says this feature is expected later this year.
Gradual Rollout
Guest calls are rolling out to users on the latest versions of WhatsApp for Android and iOS.
The rollout is gradual, so the option may not appear for everyone immediately.
WhatsApp has not provided a date for when the feature will be available to all users.

MLB The Show 26 Is Close Behind

Interestingly, 48% of its revenue came from Xbox, despite the smaller Xbox console install base compared with PlayStation.

However, Alinea estimates the game currently has around 50,000 daily users across all platforms.

items.author: Arsalan Khattak
items.content:
The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) has outlined the requirements for Pakistani citizens aged 18 and above who want to apply for their first Computerized National Identity Card (CNIC).
Applicants whose parents or siblings are registered with NADRA must prepare the required documents before submitting their applications.
They must provide the CNIC number of a parent or blood relative, along with the Child Registration Certificate (B-Form) number or the Computerized Birth Registration Certificate’s CRMS number.
Applicants can have their application forms verified through biometric authentication by a parent or a sibling aged 18 or above. If biometric verification is not possible, a gazetted officer or public representative can verify the application form.
For applicants born abroad, NADRA requires a foreign birth certificate, an S1 form, or a citizenship or naturalization certificate. Applicants can visit their nearest NADRA Registration Center to submit their applications.

items.author: Munawwar Khan
items.content:
The bodies of an elderly couple, who had returned from Canada a few months ago, were found at their house in North Karachi, with the cause of death yet to be ascertained, police said.
According to a statement issued by the District Central police spokesperson, the bodies were found at house R-93 in Sector 11-C of North Karachi, opposite B Amma Park, within the jurisdiction of the Sir Syed police station.
The deceased were identified as 70-year-old Muhammad Yameen, son of Khuda Bakhsh, and his 65-year-old wife, Nafis Akhtar. The couple had returned from Canada some time ago and were living at the house, the police said.
Read: Five members of a family found dead inside home in Karachi's Malir
Their bodies were taken to Abbasi Shaheed Hospital for medico-legal formalities. An initial examination found no marks of injuries caused by a sharp-edged weapon on either body, contrary to earlier reports that the couple had been found with their throats slit, the police spokesperson said.
However, blood had flowed from their noses and ears and dried on the floor. Police suspected that excessive bleeding might have caused their deaths, while the possibility that they had been given a poisonous substance was also being investigated.
Sir Syed Station House Officer (SHO) Irfan Asif said the cause of death could not be immediately established. He added that poisoning was one possibility, but it was too early to reach a conclusion and the post-mortem report would be needed to determine the cause of death.
The incident came to light when a close relative of Yameen visited the couple but received no response from inside the house. The police were subsequently informed.
Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Fareed Khan said the bodies appeared to be more than 18 hours old. Police were obtaining footage from closed-circuit television cameras installed in the area to gather further information about the incident.
Also Read: Mother, three children brutally murdered
Investigators were also told that workers had been visiting the house for repair work. The couple had last been seen outside the house on Tuesday evening, according to information gathered by the police.
The house, a ground-plus-one structure with a shop, had reportedly been owned by the couple for several years. They planned to sell it and return to Canada to join their three children. The house had recently been vacated by a tenant, and repair work was under way. There was little furniture or other household material inside.
Police recovered mobile phones from the house but found no evidence of robbery, the report said.
Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar took notice of the incident and sought details from the senior superintendent of police for District Central.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
IT advisory firm Infotech has acquired Bengaluru-based SaaS startup Zluri to add the latter’s application discovery, identity governance and administration capabilities to its offerings stack. The terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
Following the acquisition, Zluri will operate as a standalone division within Infotech, retaining its product development and core engineering teams in Bengaluru.
It will also contribute to Infotech’s newly launched CIO Analytics platform, an API-driven advisory model that combines operational IT data with AI-assisted services and analyst expertise.
For Zluri, the acquisition would open a pathway to expand its reach among enterprise customers by tapping into Infotech’s global community of more than 30,000 IT leaders.
Founded in 2020 by Ritish Reddy, Chaithanya Yambari and Sethu Meenakshisundaram, Zluri offers businesses a software that helps them track and manage all the digital tools their employees use.
These include work apps (Asana, Slack, etc), cloud software as well as AI tools. Its platform also helps companies control who can access what tools, identify unused subscriptions, reduce software costs and protect sensitive company data by removing unnecessary or unauthorised access.
Zluri caters to over 250 enterprise clients globally, including Monday.com, Tipalti, Whoop, Catapult Sports, Razorpay, Smartnews, Amagi, Daxko, and Traveloka, and earns over 60% of its total revenue from Europe and North America. It will continue serving existing customers post acquisition.
“We started Zluri to give IT and security teams visibility and control over every application and identity in their organisation. Joining Infotech lets us put that data at the heart of how IT leaders make decisions, and we’re excited to build together,” said Zluri’s cofounder and CEO Ritish Reddy.
The startup has raised over $32 Mn in funding from marquee backers like Lightspeed, MassMutual Ventures, Endiya Partners, and Kalaari Capital – most recently bagging a $20 Mn Series B fundraise in 2023.
Meanwhile, Infotech (erstwhile Info-Tech Research Group) is an Ontario-based IT research and advisory firm that helps organisations improve their tech operations by developing IT strategies with key focus areas like cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, data and AI.
As of now, the firm is seeking to expand beyond its traditional research and advisory business. It claims to have grown by more than 340% over the past seven years and crossed $300 Mn in annual revenue.
The deal is in line with an emerging trend of global companies acquiring Indian SaaS startups to expand their capabilities.
Most recently, Nasdaq-listed SaaS major Freshworks recently acquired US-based Torii to expand its AI and software spend governance capabilities as well. Besides, software giant Adobe also acquired Peak XV Partners-backed Rilo back in September to build broader marketing workflows for its customers and integrate Rilo’s agentic capabilities into its enterprise suite.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Reliance Industries Ltd’s (RIL’s) technology arm Jio Platforms has filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) with SEBI for its IPO which will open for public subscription on October 21 and close on October 23. Anchor bidding for the issue will take place on October 19 (Monday).
The company has retained its IPO size as outlined in its draft IPO papers. The IPO will comprise a fresh issue of up to 27 Cr equity shares. As per earlier reports, Jio’s IPO size was expected to be over ₹30,000 Cr.
In its RHP, the company outlined that ₹27,500 Cr of the fresh capital raised via the IPO will be uitilised for prepayment, in full or in part, of certain outstanding borrowings availed by its material subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm (RJIL).
The repayment will help it reduce RJIL’s net debt and interest costs, improve leverage as well as strengthen its financial position and preserve its ability to invest in strategic priorities such as 5G network expansion, fixed broadband, AI and cloud services, enterprise digital services and international technology partnerships.
The proposed prepayment covers three external commercial borrowing (ECB) term loan facilities availed by the company totaling over ₹29,971 Cr. The loans were sanctioned by a consortium of international and Indian lenders including the likes of SBI, Bank of America, First Abu Dhabi Bank, among others and are due for repayment within 2028.
The loans were originally raised to fund capital expenditure towards 5G infrastructure deployment and spectrum acquisition. Their scheduled repayment dates fall between March and June 2028. Interest rates on these borrowings range from 1.40% to 5.13% per annum.
The remaining proceeds allocated for general corporate purposes may fund strategic initiatives, growth opportunities, capital expenditure, working capital, marketing and other business requirements.
The company has outlined the following competitive strengths in the RHP:
Technology and innovation: Jio claims proprietary capabilities across network infrastructure, devices, software, operating systems and applications. As of June 30, 2026, it had filed 7,220 patent applications. It also operates an end-to-end indigenous 5G standalone technology stack at a nationwide scale.
Scale of digital services: RJIL had 533.3 Mn customers, including 284.9 Mn 5G subscribers, as of June 2026. It had 28.6 Mn JioFiber and JioAirFiber subscribers and held a 61.73% share of net fixed broadband customer additions in the June quarter. Its MyJio app recorded 227.6 Mn average monthly active users during the quarter.
Technology-led operations: Jio uses AI-powered network automation, digital twins and its JioBrain platform to optimise network capacity, predict faults and improve service delivery. It said 84% of customer service requests were handled through self-service or AI-assisted workflows in the June quarter.
Network infrastructure: The company had access to 3.61 Lakh network towers, over 1 Mn route kilometres of fibre and 26,800.8 MHz of spectrum. Its wireless broadband network covered over 99% of India’s population.
The Buzz Around Jio’s IPO
The proposed IPO could be among the largest public issues in India. Jio filed its DRHP in June and received an observation letter from SEBI in August.
The IPO has also been highly anticipated by investors of RIL. The oil-to-telecom conglomerate said that the IPO will have ₹500 Cr portion reserved for eligible employees and up to ₹2,500 Cr for eligible shareholders of RIL.
Earlier, reports said the company has already received more than $20 Bn in bids ahead of the issue, while existing investors, including Meta and Google, are said to be looking to increase their stakes rather than exit.
However, the buzz around Jio’s IPO extends to a more fundamental question: can Reliance Industries turn Jio’s telecom dominance into a broader digital technology business that commands a premium valuation?
As per Inc42’s analysis in June, Jio’s next phase of growth will depend less on subscriber additions and more on monetisation. With 524.4 Mn subscribers as of March 2026, even a modest increase in average revenue per user (ARPU) could significantly influence earnings.
The telecom giant has also displayed robust financial growth ahead of its listing. In the quarter ending June (Q1 FY27), Jio Platforms reported a consolidated net profit of ₹7,764 Cr, up 9.2% from ₹7,110 Cr. Operating revenue rose 11.8% YoY and 2.4% QoQ to ₹39,173 Cr. Meanwhile, gross revenue jumped 12% YoY to ₹45,961 Cr.
Beyond telecom, Jio is expanding into AI, cloud computing, data centres, enterprise software, and satellite connectivity. Turning these initiatives into meaningful earnings will be key to establishing itself as a broader digital technology business.
The post Jio Platforms IPO To Open For Subscription On October 21 appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.title: Government Rules Out Further Tax Relief on Imported Mobile Phones
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.

Government Rules Out Further Tax Relief on Imported Mobile Phones

He added that income tax and sales tax rates on digitally acquired services and supplies had already been capped at a maximum of two per cent under the Finance Act, 2025-26.
The government maintained that all measures discussed during the 2026-27 budget proceedings had been implemented, leaving no further mobile phone tax adjustments planned at present.
The issue of taxation on imported mobile phones has remained a concern for consumers and the technology sector, as duties and taxes increase the cost of legally imported handsets. Lower taxation could improve affordability and access to digital services, while further changes would have implications for government revenue.

Netflix is laying off 6% of its workforce, or roughly 1,000 employees, in its biggest cuts since ​2022, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters, as the streaming pioneer ‌faces tough competition for viewers from legacy rivals and YouTube.
The bulk of the job cuts would be in Netflix's product, tech, legal and human-resources teams, the email Co-CEOs Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos sent to ​employees on Wednesday showed.
"Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on ​it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritise our people ⁠and resources," they said in the memo.
Exclusive: Netflix is cutting about 1,000 jobs, its biggest round of layoffs in years as it struggles with slowing growth and customer engagement https://t.co/4kLKUmxN40
— The Wall Street Journal (@WSJ) October 14, 2026
"Our business is strong and growing, and we remain ​on track to deliver our full-year forecast."
Netflix shares, down around 25% so far this year, rose ​0.7% on Wednesday. The company had about 16,000 employees at the end of last year.
Read: Netflix faces new round of layoffs amid PR reorganisation, impacting series and film publicity
This year, the streaming giant has faced doubts about its ability to sustain the growth that disrupted the US media industry by putting ​pressure on cable TV businesses.
Engagement, or the amount of time users spend on Netflix, has ​become a key concern for investors as platforms such as YouTube and TikTok attract viewers with free-to-watch, ‌user-generated content ⁠that gives them a cost advantage over Netflix.
A failed pursuit of Warner Bros Discovery's streaming and studio assets earlier this year deepened doubts about Netflix's strategy. Paramount completed its $110-billion Warner Bros acquisition earlier this month to form Skydance.
"They haven't been able to find like another line ​of major revenue," said ​Ross Benes, senior ⁠analyst at eMarketer, adding the company remains reliant on a subscription business that could be approaching a ceiling.
"Eventually, because they've kind of nearing a ​ceiling with that, they'll need another revenue stream to diversify, and that's ​where it's ⁠been more of a struggle."
Netflix has been trying to expand beyond its subscription business by investing in an ad tier, live programming and gaming.
Its last major round of layoffs came in 2022, ⁠when it ​cut about 450 jobs in two rounds after losing ​subscribers for the first time in more than a decade.
The Wall Street Journal first reported on Wednesday's memo.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Google’s philanthropic arm Google.org has committed $15 Mn in funding to nonprofit organisation The/Nudge (formerly The/Nudge Institute) to support the growth and digital enablement of Indian MSMEs (micro, small and medium enterprises).
The initiative aims to develop scalable AI tools that can help small businesses improve access to formal credit, discover new markets and navigate compliance requirements.
Besides, an open call for proposals to identify innovative solutions addressing challenges faced by MSMEs is also on the cards. The initiative also includes a multilingual AI platform to train talent in Tier III and Tier IV towns in job-ready skills and connect them with small businesses.
“By partnering with The/Nudge, we are putting open digital tools directly into the hands of small business owners, ensuring that India’s economic backbone is equipped to lead this technology shift,” Preeti Lobana, VP and country manager at Google India, said.
The initiative also aims to establish open standards that can help Indian MSMEs become more competitive, creditworthy and visible in global markets.
The funding comes amid growing efforts to leverage AI for improving productivity and expanding access to digital services among small businesses. For MSMEs, AI-powered tools could help simplify operational processes, improve access to information and address some of the barriers that limit their ability to scale.
India’s MSME sector continues to face structural challenges in accessing formal finance, expanding market reach and navigating compliance requirements. For smaller enterprises, limited access to business information and digital tools can further complicate these processes.
A World Economic Forum report published in October 2025 estimated that AI adoption could unlock $490-685 Bn in economic value for India’s MSME sector.
Amid this, digital lenders have increased focus on MSMEs, which often have difficulty in raising formal credit despite being the country’s second largest employer. New-age NBFCs like Indifi Capital, Techfino, Lendingkart, FlexiLoans, Aye Finance, among others, are leveraging tech to address this issue and provide credit to MSMEs.
Prior to this, Google.org announced a $1 Mn grant to help improve news literacy in India and fight back against misinformation and fake news, in 2020. It has also given a grant of $3 Mn to non-profit organisations in India in 2018, to provide quality education in India through elearning.

items.content:
The federal government on Wednesday increased the price of petrol by Rs1.2 per litre, while decreasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 17 paisas per litre for October 15.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs393.86 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs396.65 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.71 and 3 paisas per litre, respectively, for October 14.
The government has revised the prices of petroleum products for Thursday@Official_PetDiv #RadioPakistan #News https://t.co/bsKRhWfzBM pic.twitter.com/cudBQVtC4Y
— Radio Pakistan (@RadioPakistan) October 14, 2026
Read: Govt cuts petrol by Rs2.71, diesel by 3 paisas for Oct 14
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices steadied on Wednesday after rising on an attack, opens new tab on the ​headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company and Iranian comments about new tactics deployed to target ships and keep oil prices ‌high to influence US midterm elections.
Brent crude futures were up 13 cents at $105.56 a barrel by 1325 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained $1.25, or 1.33%, to $95.39 for a more than two-week high.
"Attacks on ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz and military strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis are supporting prices as market participants remain concerned ​about lower oil exports from the region," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo, adding that exports have held up so far.

The document, filed on Tuesday, is part of an ongoing trade secret dispute filed by Apple ‌earlier ⁠this year in which it alleged employees of the iPhone maker left and took confidential information to OpenAI's hardware division. OpenAI has denied those allegations.
Earlier this week, US District Court Judge Edward Davila granted part of Apple's request to get early access ​to digital files from ​OpenAI in the ⁠suit.
Davila said Apple could gather data from some of its former employees' devices and sit three of them for depositions on ​a sped-up schedule, including the two defendants in the case — ​Chang Liu, ⁠a former senior system electrical engineer, and Tang Yew Tan, a former vice president of product design for iPhone and Apple Watch.
The case is likely to go to trial ⁠in ​October 2027, though OpenAI has said in court ​filings that it could be ready for trial as soon as June 2027.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Enterprise AI startup Parallel Loop has raised $6.6 Mn (about ₹63.1 Cr) in a seed funding round led by 3one4 Capital, with participation from Picus Capital, Flourish Ventures, and Economic Development Innovations Singapore.
Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma, CRED founder Kunal Shah, and former Singapore Economic Development Board chairman Philip Yeo also participated in the round, among others.
The startup plans to use the capital to strengthen its go-to-market strategy, expand its team, and scale operations, with a focus on Western markets, cofounder Prateek Jogani told Inc42.
Founded in June this year by Jogani and Yujun Chean, Parallel Loop helps mid-market and large enterprises integrate AI into their existing technology systems, processes, and workflows.
The US-headquartered startup has an entity in Bengaluru, with 85-90% of its workforce based in India, Jogani said. It has a team of 30 across Singapore, Bengaluru, Bangkok, London, and Dubai, and works with more than 12 enterprises globally. Its clients include Licious and Havells in India, and Tokio Marine Safety Insurance in Thailand.
Jogani and Chean previously cofounded FairDee, a Thailand-based insurtech startup acquired by Qoala. At Qoala, Jogani served as group chief technology officer, while Chean was group chief operating officer. They helped scale the business across five Southeast Asian markets.
Parallel Loop’s Enterprise AI Play
Parallel Loop combines its AI platform with engineering teams that work alongside clients to identify use cases, integrate AI into existing systems, and build customised workflows and applications. It describes this combination of software infrastructure and engineering support as an “AI operating partner” model.
Its offerings span AI enablement, an AI stack, and a software factory. The AI enablement service helps leadership teams identify use cases and develop adoption roadmaps, while the AI stack connects existing systems and organisational data to power dashboards and automated workflows. The software factory focuses on modernising legacy systems and building new applications.
Enterprises can deploy the platform in their own cloud environment or on-premises, retaining control over data access and residency. It supports multiple AI model providers, including open-weight models.
Within these deployments, Jogani said the startup focuses on deterministic workflows in which steps follow pre-defined rules, rather than autonomous AI agents that execute tasks independently. It uses AI to develop workflows but codifies most steps, reserving AI-based decisions for tasks requiring classification or judgement. Such tasks account for around 10% of a workflow, he said.
At Havells, several hundred employees already use the platform for workflows, automations, and dashboards, according to the startup. Parallel Loop is also working with the electrical equipment maker to improve coordination among sales teams, channel partners, and influencers through AI-powered insights.
Parallel Loop’s fundraise comes amid investor interest in startups applying AI to enterprise workflows. Yesterday, Clueso raised $10 Mn in a Series A round led by Dharana Capital to expand its platform for creating and updating business videos using AI agents.
The opportunity extends across enterprise functions as businesses move beyond AI pilots to production deployments. According to Google and Inc42’s ’Bharat AI Startups Report 2026’, India’s enterprise AI market is projected to grow to $71 Bn by 2030.

items.author: Anirudh Trivedi
items.content:
For as long as Anshita Mehrotra can remember, conversations at her home were all about cosmetic formulations, ingredients, and consumer behaviour. For Mehrotras, beauty wasn’t just another industry but a family business.
Her mother, Shailey Malhotra, had built Fixderma into one of India’s trusted skincare brands, serving millions of consumers. And the obvious path for Anshita was to step into an already successful business.
Instead, she chose a road less trodden.
After graduating in Canada and returning to India in 2018, Mehrotra began exploring a gap in the beauty market that’s worth tapping into. And it didn’t take long to find one. Like millions of Indians with naturally curly hair, she knew the daily struggle of keeping her textured hair hydrated.
The products available in the market largely revolved around oils, which moisturised but often left hair greasy and difficult to manage. There was little available that could hydrate curls, style them, be used daily, and still feel light and smell good. The market was dominated by expensive salon-grade products that were not suitable for daily use.
“There was no curl cream or shampoo for hair like mine. The market simply didn’t exist, and there was a huge unmet need staring us in the face, and I knew I could build in that space,” Anshita Mehrotra, founder of Fix My Curls, told Inc42.
Having grown up around the beauty industry, she understood the product development process, knew the experts she needed to work with, and had access to manufacturing capabilities.
After almost eight months working with hair care specialists, she developed what she says was the category’s first leave-in curl cream and hair gel specifically for the Indian market. The products were free from sulfates, silicones, parabens, mineral oils, and drying alcohols, and promised an everyday styling routine.
In 2019, Mehrotra launched Fix My Curls through its own website, followed by an Amazon listing. But just as the business was finding its footing, the pandemic brought the industry, like much of the world, to a standstill.
“It was a difficult year for sales. But with everyone spending more time on their phones, I realised that if I couldn’t get the product into their hands, I could at least help them understand why they needed it,” Mehrotra said, sharing that within the first lockdown, her educational content led the brand to gain over 12,000 active followers on Instagram.
After 2021, Fix My Curls began operating independently of Fixderma and expanded its presence across beauty-focussed marketplaces such as Nykaa, Vanity Wagon, and Sublime Life. According to Mehrotra, that was when the brand found its first real product-market fit. And the next chapter of growth began with a bet on quick commerce.
Fix My Curls first entered quick commerce in the second half of 2023 with a limited rollout across a handful of Blinkit pin codes. We were trying to reach out to a new customer base that ordered more frequently.
“We were among the first personal care brands to bet on quick commerce. It was challenging because neither Blinkit nor we had a playbook. We were figuring out purchase orders and operations as we went,” Mehrotra told Inc42.
The breakthrough came in January 2024, when Blinkit expanded the brand’s presence nationwide. And by then, Mehrotra’s years of educating consumers online had created a loyal audience that was ready to buy.
Today, quick commerce is among the largest contributors to Fix My Curls’ total sales. Marketplaces and quick commerce account for nearly 70% of the brand’s total sales, while its D2C website contributes around 25%. The remaining 5% comes from exports to markets including Nepal, Switzerland, Malaysia and Romania.
While Fix My Curls reported revenue of over ₹21.42 Cr in FY25, it is yet to turn profitable. According to Mehrotra, the company expects to achieve EBITDA profitability of 2-5% in FY27.
As it works toward that goal, quick commerce is increasingly emerging as a profitable channel, and during our conversation, Mehrotra shared the lessons she learned over the last three years of building in quick commerce that helped the brand crack the channel.
Overcoming Q-Comm Challenges
According to Mehrotra, the initial few months in 2023 were challenging. The team was trying to identify the right hero product, determine its pricing, and decide which cities to launch in first.
Because the category was new to the platform, Blinkit had no historical data to show which products would sell, how often they would need replenishment, or what consumer behaviour to expect.
But now that the company is three years into quick-commerce operations, it has a clear list of dos and don’ts.
Building For Q-Comm Cart Behaviour
Without a proven framework, Fix My Curls leaned back on its most trusted signal: customer data. Fix My Curls used performance metrics from its hero SKUs on Amazon and its website to decide which products to list first on Blinkit. It also ran self-funded Meta campaigns to spread awareness that they were now available on Q-comm, too.
“We would make ads just to tell people that our products were available on Blinkit. Nobody asked us to do it. We did it because we knew we needed to increase awareness,” Mehrotra said.
But the brand soon realised that the channel was highly price sensitive. Blinkit users weren’t necessarily willing to spend ₹700-₹800 on haircare while ordering groceries. Cart context and purchase intent were fundamentally different.
“We realised that if somebody is adding groceries worth ₹1,000 to ₹1,500, our product needs to feel like an easy addition to that cart,” Mehrotra explained.
In response, Fix My Curls designed smaller trial and travel packs priced between ₹150 and ₹300, which helped the brand sell quickly and maintain smaller but frequent POs.
Catching Replenishment Rhythm
For Fix My Curls, Q-comm widened execution challenges that didn’t exist in traditional ecommerce. Mehrotra noted that, unlike ecommerce channels, where inventory cycles are relatively predictable, quick commerce operates on tight replenishment windows of just four to seven days.
“The biggest thing we struggled with was that we just weren’t able to fulfil purchase orders fast enough,” Mehrotra said.
To deal with this, Mehrotra built a dedicated quick commerce function. One team member was assigned exclusively to the channel and is responsible for tracking SKU-level demand daily and maintaining inventory buffers above projected needs. The brand also began closely monitoring daily run rates and planning inventory 15% to 20% above forecasts.
However, according to Mehrotra, inventory planning continues to be tested during new product launches, when demand can far exceed projections. She recalled that the quick commerce version of the Milky Leave-In Serum sold out almost immediately after launch, forcing the company to place “three separate purchase orders in quick succession” to keep up with demand.
Mehrotra also shared that getting POs delivered on time to fulfilment centres was another critical factor, as larger logistics partners, she found, were often too stretched across clients to handle Fix My Curls’ tight replenishment cycles.
Smaller logistics partners, however, proved more responsive and reliable. “The biggest thing is that you cannot miss your purchase order, and to make sure you don’t, you have to find the right logistics partner,” she added.
Building For Q-Comm’s Search Intent
Eventually, Mehrotra also realised that quick commerce shoppers were fundamentally different in their shopping habits. Unlike Instagram or a brand website, where consumers often come with a specific intent, quick commerce is driven largely by searching for a specific product.
“People were not searching for Fix My Curls. They were searching for products like shampoo, gel or dry shampoo,” she said.
To accommodate that insight into the product, Fix My Curls worked with quick commerce partners to shape the final form of their dry shampoo. The data showed that customers on the channel wanted travel-friendly haircare, so the brand launched a version that was compact, competitively priced, and under 100 ml.
According to the founder, these minor product changes drastically impacted sales, and the company now works closely with quick commerce platforms while developing new products.
Fix My Curls’ experience reflects a wider discovery challenge for haircare brands on quick commerce. Being available on a platform is only the first step. How consistently products remain in stock, where they appear in search results, how much shelf visibility they receive and how their prices compare with competitors can also influence their chances of discovery.
Future Growth For Fix My Curls’ Q-Comm Journey
For Mehrotra, the biggest takeaway from Fix My Curls’ quick commerce journey is that the channel is far more than a convenience-led delivery mechanism. It is increasingly becoming a discovery engine.
“Quick commerce has helped us reach cities that I genuinely have never targeted. To be honest, I’ve not even heard about some of these cities. Reaching tier-III markets at this scale is remarkable because, in our category, achieving such deep penetration used to be nearly impossible,” said Mehrotra.
In many ways, quick commerce has helped Fix My Curls solve the same challenge it faced when it first launched in 2019: making an underserved category more accessible.
As the company works towards EBITDA profitability and its next phase of product-market fit, Mehrotra believes the opportunity in quick commerce remains significant. However, she is equally convinced that the channel will not be able to accommodate every brand that enters it.
“I think the next two years will be a boom, but there’s going to be a clean-out after that. In every category, only the players who can move products, replenish inventory and build genuine demand will survive,” she said.
For Fix My Curls, the focus now is on ensuring it remains one of those players. After spending its early years building a category from scratch and its recent years building a quick commerce playbook, the brand is now entering a new chapter centred on scale, profitability and deeper penetration across India.
The post How Fix My Curls Built Its Quick Commerce Engine From Scratch appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
A new leak has revealed possible specs for an upcoming Realme smartphone that could share hardware with the OnePlus 16R. The realme phone may feature a 200MP main camera, a high-refresh-rate OLED display, a Snapdragon 8-series chipset, and a large 8,700mAh battery.
However, the latest information contradicts an earlier camera leak that suggested the Realme phone and OnePlus 16R would feature three 50MP rear cameras. The conflicting reports leave questions about the final camera setup.
Realme Phone Leaks With OnePlus 16R-Like Specs and 200MP Camera
According to a new tip, the upcoming Realme phone could feature a 200MP main camera paired with a 50MP telephoto camera. The telephoto sensor may support 3.5x optical zoom. Interestingly, the device reportedly lacks an ultrawide camera.
These details resemble previous leaks about the OnePlus Ace 7, which is also expected to feature a 200MP main camera and a 3.5x periscope telephoto lens.
The camera module could also look similar to the one on the Realme 16 Pro+. However, the exact identity of the upcoming device remains unclear, as the tipster suggests it could be a Realme smartphone or the OnePlus 16R intended for the Indian market.
High-Refresh-Rate OLED Display and Snapdragon Chipset
The leaked specifications suggest that the phone could offer a 1.5K flat OLED display. The screen may support refresh rates of up to 185Hz in certain games, while the system interface could operate at up to 165Hz.
These high refresh rates could provide smoother animations and more responsive gameplay. The phone may also use a Snapdragon 8-series chipset, although the leak does not identify the exact processor.
According to the tipster, the device could run Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) at 120 frames per second and Call of Duty at 165fps. These figures suggest that Realme may be targeting users who want a smartphone designed for demanding mobile games.
Large Battery and Built-In Cooling Fan
Battery capacity could be another major highlight. The phone reportedly packs an 8,700mAh battery, which could provide extended usage and longer gaming sessions between charges. However, the leak does not reveal charging speeds or expected battery life.
The device may also include a built-in cooling fan to help control temperatures during intensive gaming. A circular RGB light could add to its gaming-focused design.
Other reported design features include a metal frame and a flat glass back. If these details prove accurate, the phone could combine premium materials with features aimed at mobile gamers.
OnePlus 16R and Realme Phone Could Share Hardware
Realme and OnePlus both operate under Oppo’s corporate umbrella, making hardware sharing between the two brands a possibility. The leaked specifications could therefore belong to different versions of a similar device, although this remains unconfirmed.
For now, the conflicting camera reports make it difficult to determine which specifications are accurate. An earlier leak pointed to three 50MP rear cameras, while the latest information describes a 200MP main sensor and a 50MP telephoto camera without an ultrawide lens.
Neither brand has officially confirmed the phone’s specifications or identity. More leaks will likely be needed to clarify whether this is an upcoming Realme gaming phone, the OnePlus 16R, or a device that shares hardware with both.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
D2C supplement brand The Stack has raised ₹21.5 Cr ($2.2 Mn) in fresh capital to bolster its R&D and expand its product portfolio. The round was co-led by Sauce.vc, OTP Ventures and Huddle Ventures, and also saw participation from AYRA Ventures.
The funding comes months after the startup raised its first institutional round of ₹5.5 Cr. It claims to have grown 5X since then and is now targeting 6-7X growth in FY27 compared with FY26.
Founded by Shreya Jain and Kshitij Rihal in 2024, Bengaluru-based The Stack sells supplements to support sleep, recovery and gut health. The formulations of its five supplements that combine magnesium bisglycinate, glycine, prebiotics and probiotics.
The startup claims that one in three customers places a second order within six months, while several opt for subscriptions spanning six to twelve months. Its top 10% of customers account for 30% of revenue, with referrals and word of mouth driving new customer acquisition.
“We’d rather have five products people keep coming back to than fifty they try once. We’re playing a long game, and our customers are rewarding that patience,” said Rihal, cofounder of The Stack.
The startup aims to become one of India’s most trusted supplements brands over the next three years, with a focus on transparent formulations, clinically studied ingredients and a quality-first approach to product development.
The Stack competes with brands such as Wellbeing Nutrition, Supply6 and Trunativ in India’s health and wellness supplements market.
The funding comes amid growing demand for dietary supplements in India, driven by rising awareness of preventive healthcare, the increasing availability of global brands and the use of supplements to support the management of chronic conditions.
India’s dietary supplements market was valued at $5.8 Bn in 2025 and is projected to grow to $6.6 Bn in 2026 and $12.4 Bn by 2033, at a CAGR of 9.5% from 2026 to 2033, according to Grand View Research.
Investor interest appetite for the segment is also growing in tandem with the growing market size. In July, D2C nutrition and wellness startup Supply6 raised about $5 Mn in a funding round led by Unilever Ventures, with participation from existing investor Zeropearl VC. Before that , nutrition-focused brand TruNativ raised $30 Mn in a Series B round from US-based investor OrbiMed.

items.content:
The Centre is preparing a policy for data centres, minister of state for IT Jitin Prasada said, amid concerns about the sector’s growing electricity demand and its potential impact on consumers’ power bills.
Prasada made the announcement at the Central Electricity Authority’s brainstorming conclave on ‘Making Indian Power Sector AI Enabled’. He did not disclose the policy’s scope or a timeline for its rollout.
At the conclave, he said the policy is needed “because we believe India is a very fertile ground for hyperscaler data centres”.
According to Reuters, Prasada also said data centres in some countries are diverting power from consumers, leaving them paying higher electricity bills — a situation the government wants to avoid.
His comments follow his remarks last month about balancing data centre expansion with environmental safeguards. Speaking at the inauguration of Microsoft’s data centre infrastructure, Prasada had said India has the land, talent, and other requirements to attract investments, while the government is working to ease the process of setting up operations.
He also said expansion must not come at the cost of environmental sustainability or excessive water consumption, pointing to efforts to increase green power generation and technologies that recirculate water in closed loops.
These concerns have already triggered opposition to some large projects. In Maharashtra’s Thane, residents have protested against Amazon’s proposed data centre, which is expected to consume 422 MW of power, citing concerns about electricity and water demand, noise from backup diesel generators, and tree felling.
Meanwhile, Google began construction of its AI hub in Visakhapatnam in April as part of its planned $15 Bn investment in India between 2026 and 2030. The project has also faced opposition from residents and civil society organisations over land use, water demand, and energy consumption.
Google and Amazon have denied wrongdoing and said their facilities use advanced technologies to minimise resource consumption, according to Reuters.
The push for safeguards comes alongside efforts to attract more data centre investments. The Union Budget 2026-27 proposed a tax holiday until 2047 for eligible foreign companies providing cloud services globally through India-based data centres.
These policy efforts accompany a wider push by global technology companies, including OpenAI, Microsoft, and Meta, to expand their data centre presence in India.
Domestic players are also expanding, with CtrlS Datacenters announcing yesterday that it has signed a letter of intent with the Bihar government to invest ₹10,000 Cr in a 150 MW hyperscale AI factory in Bodh Gaya, alongside inaugurating a ₹400 Cr data centre in Patna.

items.content:
Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected, and ​he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday, after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being ‌treated for lung cancer.
World leaders, Catholics across the globe and senior cardinals at the Vatican have offered prayers for Leo after he had part of his right lung removed in an operation on Tuesday.
Blood tests and a chest X-ray carried out on Wednesday showed normal post-operative results, the Vatican said, adding that the pontiff had undergone respiratory physiotherapy.
JUST IN: Pope Leo is back on his feet after surgery as doctors confirm his recovery is progressing as expected.
The Holy Father has begun walking around his room, resumed eating regular meals, and undergone respiratory physiotherapy following his lung procedure.
Dr. Luigi… pic.twitter.com/a94O8Gvlo3
— Fox News (@FoxNews) October 14, 2026
Read: Pope Leo admitted to Rome hospital for lung surgery
The cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic ​and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy as he deals with the illness.
Leo normally ​follows a very busy schedule. He is due to make a tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17 ⁠, and the Vatican press office said on Wednesday that "nothing has changed" regarding the planned trip.
However, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori said on Wednesday that the dates could change because of the ​amount of time his recovery would take.
The pope is the ultimate earthly authority for the world's 1.4 billion Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when ​he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval.
Prayers for Leo
A prayer was recited for Leo to have a good convalescence and complete healing during an open-air Mass in St Peter's Square on Wednesday following the surgery.
The pope has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of ​lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung during Tuesday's operation in an effort to eliminate all cancerous tissue.
Human lungs have five lobes — three ​in the right lung and two in the left.
The operation lasted about 90 minutes and was completed without complications, the pope's lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, and his personal physician, Dr Luigi Carbone, said ‌late on ⁠Tuesday.
Pope Leo XIV underwent thoracic surgery at Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, as planned, according to a statement from Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora released by the Holy See Press Office.
The surgeons removed the lower lobe of the Pope’s right lung,… pic.twitter.com/QAShHu1eG6
— Vatican News (@VaticanNews) October 13, 2026
The Vatican has not disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis.
Read More: Pope Leo diagnosed with cancer
Dr Serena Ricciardi, a lung cancer specialist at Rome's San Camillo Forlanini Hospital, said that if the cancer had not spread to Leo's lymph nodes, the surgery may have been sufficient for treatment.
"If there are no further issues or lymph node involvement, we could consider the surgery curative," she told Reuters. "The disease has been completely removed."
Leo is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys ​sports, including tennis, and is not known ​to be a smoker or to have ⁠had recent health issues.
Engagements cancelled until next week
The Vatican said this week that the pope was expected to remain in hospital for about a week and that all his public engagements had been cancelled until October 20.
The Mass on Wednesday was the closing act ​of an assembly of bishops called by Leo to discuss the Church's family life teachings, the largest gathering of Church leaders ​so far during this ⁠papacy.
Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle led the service in place of Leo. The pope last week approved Tagle as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role.
Pope Leo calls on us to take to heart the riches of ‘Amoris laetitia’
In a homily read by Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, Pope Leo XIV called on the Church to put the Apostolic Exhortation's pastoral guidance into practice in the heart of families.
The homily was delivered at the… pic.twitter.com/XCa1Gsl97l
— Vatican News (@VaticanNews) October 14, 2026
Political leaders offered messages of support.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he and his wife Jeanette were praying for the pope, an American who was born ⁠in Chicago.
"May the ​Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy ​Father," he said on X. Rubio met Leo at the Vatican in May.
Jeanette and I are united in prayer for @PONTIFEX’s health following his recent diagnosis.
May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father. https://t.co/KPVoGrnKUW
— Secretary Marco Rubio (@SecRubio) October 13, 2026
There was no immediate response on social media from US President Donald Trump, who has criticised the pope, or from Vice President JD Vance, who ​is a Catholic.
