items.title: ‘You’re not alone, the truth will come out’: Nobel winner Navi Pillay on global support for Palestinians
items.summary:
Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navi Pillay said Palestinians seeking justice are not alone, and the truth will emerge, urging the international community to draw lessons from the collective action and economic sanctions that helped end apartheid in her native South Africa.
In an exclusive interview on Wednesday, Pillay, judge at the International Court of Justice and a former UN human rights chief, reflected on her experience fighting apartheid and the importance of international support for Palestinians amid continuing concerns over accountability for violations in the Gaza Strip.
"I imagine I'm correct in saying that even though Palestinians are struggling for their freedom for more than 90 years now, attention by the international community and support by the international community would be of great significance for them," she told Anadolu.
"The message being, you're not alone. That with information and correct information, the truth will come out."
EXCLUSIVE &ndash
items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navi Pillay said Palestinians seeking justice are not alone, and the truth will emerge, urging the international community to draw lessons from the collective action and economic sanctions that helped end apartheid in her native South Africa.
In an exclusive interview on Wednesday, Pillay, judge at the International Court of Justice and a former UN human rights chief, reflected on her experience fighting apartheid and the importance of international support for Palestinians amid continuing concerns over accountability for violations in the Gaza Strip.
"I imagine I'm correct in saying that even though Palestinians are struggling for their freedom for more than 90 years now, attention by the international community and support by the international community would be of great significance for them," she told Anadolu.
"The message being, you're not alone. That with information and correct information, the truth will come out."
EXCLUSIVE – Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay on Gaza genocide, international law and accountability
🇵🇸 Message to Palestinians: Pillay says international support tells Palestinians that “you’re not alone” and the “truth will come out”
✊ Collective action: Pillay says… pic.twitter.com/sY2g81CTf7
— Anadolu English (@anadoluagency) October 14, 2026
Pillay, 85, who was awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize for her contributions to international justice, chaired a UN commission of inquiry, which concluded last year that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.
Recalling her experience under apartheid, she said South African lawyers fought a lonely struggle with little international attention. "We really had very little relief. And honestly, the rest of the world didn't pay attention to us," she said.
The rights lawyer said a UN commission gathering evidence and presenting its findings internationally would have greatly helped Black South Africans at that time.
Palestine needs same level of economic sanctions, collective action that helped end apartheid
Pillay stressed the importance of identifying the root causes of Palestinian suffering, and reiterated her commission's finding that Israel's unlawful occupation was the root cause of the longstanding conflict.
She criticised governments for increasingly prioritising their political and regional interests over their responsibilities to maintain international peace and justice.
She said the UN Security Council already possessed mechanisms to respond to violations, including peacekeeping operations, investigative commissions, mediation and economic sanctions.
"The principal tool they have is to impose sanctions, economic sanctions against governments that are violating international human rights law, international humanitarian law; they've used this before," she said.
Questioning the international community's response to Gaza, Pillay said: "So, the question that civil society is asking: 'Why are you sitting back and doing nothing in the face of huge violations that we, the people, can see daily? We can see genocide being committed on our television screens'."
"And I am as unhappy as most people that there has been so little action," she added.
Drawing on South Africa's experience, where apartheid ended in 1994, Pillay emphasised the decisive role of international economic pressure.
Read: Navi Pillay: Nobel laureate who led UN inquiry that found genocide in Gaza
"Apartheid came to an end mainly because of the economic sanctions imposed by the Security Council, by the United Nations against the apartheid government," she said.
"I never thought apartheid will end in my lifetime, but it's this collective action by governments, by businesses, and civil society all over the world that brought an end to apartheid."
Pillay said she had been hoping for similar international cooperation in response to the situation in Gaza.
"I've been hopefully looking for and calling for that level of cooperation, that level of condemnation of the huge violations and killings of Palestinians," she said.
Doing nothing 'unacceptable'
Asked whether Israel's growing international isolation and sanctions targeting settlers in the occupied West Bank could help end its impunity, Pillay said such developments could contribute to broader collective action.
"The one thing we cannot accept is doing nothing," she said.
Recalling Nelson Mandela's position that South Africans could not fully enjoy freedom while Palestinians remained oppressed and occupied, she said Palestinians were seeking measures similar to those used against apartheid.
"Palestinians are calling for the kind of action that was taken to end apartheid. They see the value of economic boycotts," she said.
Read More: Genocide in Palestine
She also referred to protests by Israelis against efforts to weaken the country's Supreme Court, urging governments to respect civilians' right to protest and cooperate with international criminal investigations.
She stressed that international legal principles must be applied consistently, without selectivity or bias, particularly when civilians are suffering.
States have a duty to prevent genocide
Pillay emphasised that governments, rather than international organisations alone, bear responsibility for preventing genocide.
"The Genocide Convention is very clear. The duty is on every state to prevent genocide," she said. "That's a purpose; it's not to react to genocide and to punish the alleged perpetrators. The main reason is to prevent, because it's an intolerable crime when a whole group is being destroyed in whole or in part."
About the potential legal responsibility of governments supplying weapons, intelligence or political support despite warnings of serious violations, Pillay said the states themselves established international conventions and treaties.
"They set the standards. Now they must implement them without selection," she said, arguing that governments were failing to apply their own commitments because of political interests.
Pillay recalled that her UN commission had urged the General Assembly to seek an advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice (ICJ) concerning Israel's occupation of Palestinian territory.
She welcomed the court's opinion in 2024, which found Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territory unlawful, and outlined obligations concerning Palestinian rights.
She, however, acknowledged that legal proceedings offered limited immediate relief to people suffering on the ground.
"I agree; they're not very helpful to relieve their immediate dire situation," she said. "Let's use international law to assert and realise the rights of people who are oppressed everywhere in the world."
UN system 'very skewed'
On shortcomings of the international system and its eroding credibility, Pillay pointed to the dominance of governments within the UN and the shrinking space for civil society.
"Certainly, the system is very skewed. Who controls the United Nations? It's member states, it's governments," she said, urging UN members to conduct their affairs in closer cooperation with civil society organisations.
Global opposition to US sanctions on ICC a must
Turning to Washington's measures against the International Criminal Court (ICC), Pillay called on governments, including those outside the Rome Statute, to oppose the campaign.
"I would like to see states of the world, the member states, whether they're parties to the Rome Statute or not, to condemn the unlawful measures and sanctions that the United States is imposing on this court," she said.
Also Read: US imposes sweeping sanctions on ICC
"We should say roundly that it's unacceptable, and then we all have the responsibility to help the court to overcome these obstacles."
The former ICC judge expressed confidence that the court's staff would continue their work despite mounting political pressure.
"They're not going to stop doing what they are doing because they are working out of commitment. They believe that it is possible to realise justice for all," she said.
Nobel Prize a 'wonderful surprise'
Reflecting on receiving the Nobel, Pillay described the recognition as unexpected and deeply meaningful. "This award was a huge surprise to me, but a wonderful surprise," she said.
She expressed gratitude that the Nobel Committee had recognised different aspects of her decades-long career, from challenging apartheid to advancing international justice.
"You don't win a case all the time. You win some. You lose many, especially under apartheid South Africa," she said.
Pillay described the committee's recognition of her work as a "memorable moment," saying she appreciated its efforts to examine her contributions to international peace and justice.

The White House has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as U.S. ambassador to Greece, after The Wall Street Journal reported that she had solicited $100,000 from a Trump donor in the run-up to her confirmation hearing last year.
🔗 Read more: https://t.co/JzxVmmD2xc pic.twitter.com/Lrpbj0uO5H
— The Wall Street Journal (@WSJ) October 13, 2026
In a post on X, Guilfoyle repeated denials of wrongdoing and said her gratitude and ​respect for Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio remained "unwavering".
"While my time as ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the ​America First movement, and the country I love will never end," she wrote. "These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity."
Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime. I will forever be grateful to President Donald J. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio for entrusting me with the extraordinary privilege of representing the greatest country in the history of…
— Kimberly Guilfoyle (@kimguilfoyle) October 13, 2026
One of the reports published by the Journal described Guilfoyle's close relationship with a lobbyist for a Greek energy company and her promotion of that firm, while another cited audio recordings of ​Guilfoyle bragging about her ties to wealthy Greek businessmen as she sought an invitation to a Davos dinner honouring another of Trump's sons, Eric.
US businessman ​Eric Deters also told the newspaper that Guilfoyle, a former San Francisco prosecutor, had offered access to Trump administration officials for money, at one point asking him to pay ‌her $100,000 credit ⁠card bill. Britain's Daily Mail reported last week that the State Department's internal watchdog was looking into complaints of inappropriate behaviour from staff at the Athens embassy.
Read More: Kimberly Guilfoyle 'still very fond' of Donald Trump Jr. at inauguration event
The Greek government has not commented on the allegations involving her tenure as ambassador.
Neither the State Department nor Washington's embassy in Athens responded to requests for comment.
Deals and diplomatic waves
Greece has been an important NATO ally of the United States, offering key military facilities to safeguard security in the Eastern Mediterranean, and it leads an ​EU maritime mission to protect commercial ​shipping in the Red Sea.
During a ⁠visit to Athens last week, Rubio said Greece and the US were launching new counterterrorism information sharing between their law enforcement agencies.
Guilfoyle's tenure in Athens was high-profile from the start as she appeared on the cover of Vogue ​Greece and attended late-night parties with Greek celebrities.
She aggressively touted American interests, including signing deals for the import of ​US liquefied natural ⁠gas and drilling deals involving companies including Exxon Mobil.
But she also created diplomatic waves. In her first interview with local media after arriving last November, she said China should sell its 67% stake in the port of Piraeus, which has become a cornerstone of Beijing's Belt and Road Initiative. China’s ambassador to Greece, Fang Qiu, responded ⁠by accusing the ​US of having "an outdated and a harmful mentality" and "a hegemonic mindset".
Dimitris Mantzos, foreign affairs spokesperson ​for Greece’s opposition PASOK party, said Guilfoyle’s firing raised serious issues and unanswered questions. Would Greek officials demand an explanation, he said, or "content themselves with watching the country serve as a 'theatre'" for ​outside interests.

items.content:
Comedian Russell Brand was a "sexual predator" who was "ruthless, calculated and manipulative" when targeting women for sex, a British prosecutor told a UK jury Wednesday at the start of his rape and sexual assault trial.
The one-time left-wing personality, 51, who shot to fame as a television and radio presenter, faces seven sexual offence charges involving six women. He denies all the alleged offences.
Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones said the alleged offences took place between 1999 and 2009, when Brand's career was beginning to flourish.
Addressing the jury, she gave graphic details of accusations by women, saying the youngest was 21 at the time of the alleged offences.
They came forward to police after seeing media coverage about Brand in 2023 and after he was initially charged in 2025, the court heard.
Brand was "not deterred" when some of the women said no, she said, adding his desire for sexual contact was "indiscriminate and voracious".
He used charm and comic talents when he wanted something but would then be "demanding and entitled... childlike in his expectation that his every desire should be met," Karmy-Jones told the jury of eight men and four women.
Bragging
"He was ruthless, calculated and manipulative, and the prosecution say -- a sexual predator," she added.
The identities of the women will not be revealed during the trial.
Brand, dressed in a dark suit, black-and-white striped shirt and long white tie, arrived for the start of the case at London's Southwark Crown Court in a black Mercedes-Benz van accompanied by his wife Laura.
In each woman's case, Brand responded to police with a prepared statement saying he did not remember the women and any sexual activity was consensual.
Karmy-Jones said Brand's acquaintances recalled him bragging that he wanted to "bed 5,000 women in his lifetime", adding, "you have to tell them what they need to hear".
It was a clear indication of "how manipulative the defendant could be," she said.
Brand has in recent years reinvented himself as a conservative and faith-based guru for millions of social media followers.
He has pleaded not guilty to all seven of the charges -- three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one charge of indecent assault.
The first woman met Brand when he was performing at a Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in southern England in 1999.
She invited him to her hotel room where he pushed her onto the bed before raping her without using a condom, the prosecutor said.
Brand has denied seven charges of rape and sexual assault against six women between 1999 and 2009. PHOTO: AFP
One woman said Brand in 2001 tried to drag her into a toilet cubicle at MTV's office, but she resisted.
Another woman met Brand at a London bar in 2004 and said he grabbed her breasts and pulled her into a toilet cubicle, orally raping her, after telling her not to be a "spoilsport".
Yet another woman said Brand visited the radio station where she worked in 2004 or 2005, and kissed her "very aggressively" then grabbed her breasts and bottom.
One woman, who was 21 at the time, said she had consensual oral and then vaginal sex with Brand in 2009 at his house but he then forced her into anal sex without her consent "with full force" without a condom, the prosecutor said.
Massage
In the final charge, a woman employed by Channel 4 television said she was working with Brand in a record studio in 2009.
Members of his production team told her she must give him a massage and he then pressed his face into her groin.
The trial at London's Southwark Crown Court should last around six weeks but could stretch into December.
The trial is attracting intense media scrutiny, with numerous British outlets launching dedicated podcasts and US channels reporting from outside the court.
Born to working-class parents in Essex in eastern England, Brand launched a successful stand-up comedy career as a teenager.
He became a household name as a television presenter on MTV, Channel 4 and the BBC, also penning newspaper columns and two autobiographies.
He then made a foray into Hollywood, starring in several hit films, and was in a brief but high-profile marriage to US pop star Katy Perry.
Now remarried and living in Florida with his young family, he has gained a new following as an influencer, with six million subscribers on YouTube, 10.1 million on X and 4.9 million on Instagram.

items.content:
Pakistan on Wednesday launched Pakistan Hockey League (PHL) at a ceremony in Islamabad in a bid to revive the country’s national sport.
Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) said that it is a joint initiative of the federation and Media Cast, designed to bring together international players, Pakistani talent, corporate sponsors and team owners under a professional competition structure.
Rana Mashhood Ahmed Khan, chairman of the Prime Minister's Youth Programme and chief guest at the launch ceremony, reaffirmed the government's commitment to supporting hockey's revival and encouraging investment in the sport.
He welcomed efforts to bring the government, private sector and hockey community together, expressing confidence that the league and other development initiatives would help restore Pakistan's standing in international hockey.
Khan said the government would continue to support initiatives aimed at developing the sport, nurturing young talent and creating new opportunities for Pakistani players.
PHF President Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani said the federation was committed to sustained reforms, investment and institutional development to strengthen the sport's foundations.
He said priorities included improving playing standards, upgrading infrastructure, attracting corporate investment, expanding facilities and providing players with better incentives and opportunities.
Wani stressed that restoring Pakistan hockey would require professional management, long-term planning and stronger partnerships between the government and private sector.
"Our commitment is to bring investment into hockey, improve infrastructure, provide better incentives for our players and create an environment in which Pakistan hockey can once again progress and succeed," he said.
Salman Danish, owner of Media Cast and a partner in the league, said the company would work with the PHF to organise the competition professionally, attract corporate partners and sponsors, and develop a sustainable commercial model for the sport.
Organisers said the league would seek to increase commercial interest in hockey, raise competitive standards and create sustainable investment opportunities. It is also intended to reconnect younger generations with Pakistan's rich hockey history and traditions.
Pakistan, a former powerhouse in international hockey, has struggled to maintain its position among the sport's leading nations. The league's success will depend on attracting investment, establishing a competitive structure and translating commercial interest into long-term development opportunities for players.

Mumbai-based customised haircare startup Traya is in talks to raise around ₹300 Cr (about $31 Mn) from Belgium-based investment firm Verlinvest, sources told Inc42.
The proposed round would value the startup at ₹2,500 Cr (about $262 Mn) to ₹3,000 Cr (about $315 Mn) and include both primary and secondary components, the sources said.
The round is not finalised yet and the funding amount can go up, the sources added.
Questions sent to Traya and Verlinvest remained unanswered till the time of publication.
The funding talks come amid what sources described as strong growth in recent months, with Traya currently clocking an annualised revenue rate of ₹900 Cr to ₹1,000 Cr.
The funding talks follow Traya’s ₹75 Cr investment from Xponentia Capital in April 2024. At the time, the startup claimed to have served more than 10 Lakh customers through its app, website, and ecommerce platforms Amazon and Flipkart.
Alongside its online business, Traya has been expanding its offline presence. It currently has more than 20 centres across Pune, Mumbai, Nagpur, and Hyderabad.
Founded in 2019 by Saloni Anand and Altaf Saiyed, Traya offers customised haircare solutions, using technology to identify customers’ specific hair loss triggers.
The startup says it combines hair assessment, recommendation algorithm, and doctor approval to develop personalised treatment plans.
Besides Xponentia Capital, Traya counts Kae Capital, Fireside Ventures, and Whiteboard Capital among its investors.
Traya is yet to file its FY26 financial statements with MCA. Its operating revenue rose 43% to ₹338.4 Cr in FY25 from ₹236 Cr in FY24. However, it slipped into a net loss of ₹22.5 Cr from a profit of ₹8.8 Cr as total expenses climbed 60% YoY to ₹365.5 Cr.
The startup competes with brands such as Vedix, Evoke, SkinKraft, and Ravel Care in the broader haircare and personalised beauty market.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Indian stockbrokers’ combined active client base on the NSE rose by about 1.6 Lakh to 4.61 Cr in September, despite benchmark indices recording their steepest monthly decline in six months.
Market leader Groww continued to widen its lead in India’s stockbroking market over the previous month, adding 1.01 Lakh active users even as benchmark indices recorded their steepest monthly decline in six months.
Meanwhile, Angel One managed to narrow its gap with Zerodha, as the latter saw a marginal decline in its active client base, while Dhan continued to add clients, according to NSE data. Dale Vaz-led Sahi emerged as the fastest-growing broker, with its user base rising about 11% to 2.53 Lakh.
The expansion came amid a selloff in Indian equities, driven by foreign investor outflows, elevated crude oil prices, and inflation concerns. Despite the market weakness, domestic investors continued to invest in equity mutual funds.
Groww Leads As Zerodha, Upstox Lose Clients
Groww’s active client base increased to 1.34 Cr in September from 1.33 Cr in August, taking its market share to 29.16%. However, its net additions slowed to 1.01 Lakh from 2.2 Lakh in August.
Second-largest broker Zerodha lost 5,313 active clients during the month, taking its base to 67.92 Lakh. Angel One added 36,956 active clients to reach 67.56 Lakh, narrowing the gap with Zerodha to around 35,830 clients. The two brokers had 67.97 Lakh and 67.19 Lakh active clients, respectively, in August.
Zerodha’s market share stood at 14.73%, marginally ahead of Angel One’s 14.65%. The gap between the two brokers has narrowed as Angel One continued to add clients while Zerodha’s base contracted in September.
Angel One’s September business update, however, pointed to a mixed picture, with client growth accompanied by weaker activity in some segments. Its client base rose 1.1% MoM to about 4 Cr, while gross client acquisitions fell 19.6% to 4.5 Lakh.
The number of orders increased 11.7% to 12.2 Cr, taking average daily orders to 58.2 Lakh from 52.1 Lakh in August.
“While cash market share moderated in September 2026, exit trends improved, with sequential growth in average daily orders and turnover market share across overall equities and equity derivatives,” the company said in its monthly disclosures earlier.
Further, fintech unicorn Dhan, operated by Raise Securities, continued to gain ground. With the addition of 13,624 active clients in the month, Dhan’s user base expanded to 11.21 Lakh. Its client base rose from 11.07 lakh in August, when it added 19,818 clients.
Despite the slower pace of additions, Dhan maintained its position as the eighth-largest broker by active clients.
Among other leading platforms, ICICI Securities added 4,410 active clients to reach 21.61 lakh, while HDFC Securities added 2,532 to reach 13.54 lakh. Upstox lost 10,343 active clients, taking its base to 18.54 lakh from 18.65 lakh in August.
The biggest dent in the active user base was incurred by SBI Securities. The retail stockbroking subsidiary of SBI Capital Markets lost 22,525 active users to end September with 10.21 Lakh, compared with 10.44 Lakh a month earlier.
Indian Equities Fall Amid FII Outflows
The Nifty 50 declined 6.1% in September to close at 22,620.45, while the BSE Sensex fell 5.8% to 72,480.29. This marked the benchmarks’ second consecutive monthly decline and their steepest correction since March.
Alongside foreign investor selling, geopolitical uncertainty and elevated crude oil prices weighed on markets. Higher oil prices fuelled concerns about India’s import bill, inflation, and currency stability, while a weaker rupee added to the pressure.
According to JM Financial Institutional Securities’ September flow tracker, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) recorded net equity outflows of ₹39,660 Cr ($4.1 Bn), while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) were net buyers of around $8 Bn.
FIIs invested a net ₹9,300 Cr in the primary market but withdrew a net ₹49,000 Cr from the secondary market. Their ownership of Indian equities fell to 13.8% in September 2026 from 19.9% in September 2016.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
The co-founders of Nigerian on-demand commerce startup Chowdeck have been selected to join Endeavor’s global network of high-impact entrepreneurs.
Founded in October 2021, Chowdeck brings together smart logistics, seamless payments, inventory management, and real-time performance tools. Combining reliable infrastructure with strong merchant partnerships, Chowdeck enables thousands of businesses to run more efficiently while delivering excellent experiences to millions of customers every day.
The startup operates in 14 cities across Nigeria and Ghana, serving more than 800,000 active customers, nearly 9,000 vendors and around 8,000 riders, and processing approximately 1.2 million orders each month. It raised a US$9 million Series A round in 2025 to scale expansion.
Founders Femi Aluko, Olumide Ojo and Lanre Yusuf have now been chosen by Endeavor Nigeria to join the organisation’s global network after completing a multi-stage selection process. As part of the network, the Chowdeck founders will gain access to Endeavor’s global community of entrepreneurs, mentors and investors. Endeavor Nigeria, launched in 2018, now supports 39 entrepreneurs leading 21 companies in sectors including fintech, mobility, logistics, healthcare and agriculture.
“The most valuable thing for a founder at this stage is being able to talk to someone who has already solved the problem in front of you,” said Aluko, Chowdeck’s CEO.
“Someone who has expanded into a market they didn’t understand, hired their first set of senior leaders, or managed growth across currencies and regulators. Endeavor gives us access to exactly those people, across Africa and around the world.”

Update | Oct 13, 14:29 IST
Almost two months after Inc42 had exclusively reported about former Dyson India MD Ankit Jain raising capital from BEENEXT for his new venture, the startup officially announced the development today. Foundry has raised ₹12 Cr in funding from BEENEXT and Kettleborough VC, with participation from Rishubh Satiya of Plix, Anindita Sampath of Yogabar, and Anita Pramoda of Owned Outcomes.
The funding will support technology development and product engineering as Foundry prepares its first product range of kitchen appliances for launch in H2 2027.
Original | Aug 13, 15:29 IST
Former Dyson India MD Ankit Jain is working on a startup focused on building premium consumer appliances, sources told Inc42.
The startup, which is currently operating in stealth, has raised pre-seed funding from Singapore-headquartered BEENEXT, the sources added. The amount raised could not be ascertained.
While queries sent to BEENEXT did not elicit a response, Jain declined to comment.
An ISB alumnus, Jain worked with Nestle India, Walmart, and 21st Century Fox before joining UK-based technology company Dyson in 2017. He was elevated as MD of Dyson India in 2021 to oversee the company’s expansion in the country.
Last year, he was appointed MD of Dyson’s Middle East and Africa operations. He stepped down from the company in February this year.
“Over these years, I built Hong Kong and Taiwan into a top 10 market, returned to India and turned around the business, and strengthened the Dyson into a brand that every customer aspired to own, and every business desired to build,” Jain said in a LinkedIn post announcing his exit from Dyson yesterday.
In the same post, he added, “Time to build something new. More soon.”
Jain’s startup will enter a segment that includes new-age brands such as Nester, Nuuk, Atomberg, Geek Technology, and Wonderchef. These brands are focusing on product innovation and newer designs to compete with legacy players such as Havells and Usha.
Earlier this year, Nester raised around ₹19 Cr to expand its product portfolio, while Nuuk raised $4.5 Mn last year.
Mumbai-based Atomberg has raised about $126.5 Mn to date from investors such as Inflexor Ventures, Trifecta Capital, Steadview Capital, and Temasek. It is now looking to raise ₹1,500 Cr to ₹2,000 Cr through an IPO.
India’s household appliances market is expanding on the back of rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, growing adoption of smart appliances, and the expansion of ecommerce and retail infrastructure.
The market, estimated at $22.45 Bn in 2024, is projected to reach $33.63 Bn by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 7.2% between 2025 and 2030.

items.author: Fact Check By iVerify
items.content:
Several users, the majority of whom appear to be pro-Yemeni accounts based on their past posts, have been sharing an image of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and an alleged royal family member on social media platforms X and Facebook since October 12, 2026, claiming that Saudi authorities busted an assassination plot involving them. However, nothing of the sort has occurred.
Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis are at war again. The latest Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia came amid a renewed escalation in the conflict in Yemen. Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched a military campaign to push Houthi forces away from the strategically important Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key maritime route connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
The Houthis responded with missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi territory, including airports, military installations and oil infrastructure. The renewed fighting has intensified after years of intermittent conflict and a period of relative calm following a truce in 2022.
On October 8, Yemen’s Houthi movement claimed that it had launched a ballistic missile towards King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, saying it had struck its intended target and disrupted air traffic. Saudi Arabia’s Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles, including two heading towards Riyadh and another directed towards Khamis Mushait. Subsequent attacks on Saudi airports have killed civilians.
How it started
On Oct 12, a user who appears to share anti-Saudi content based on their past posts shared an image on X, claiming that it shows an alleged assassin and a royal family member of the crown prince.
The caption of the post said: “Attempted coup inside led by Sheikh Mubarak bin Nuwaf Al-Duaisi Al Saud. It appears there are deep and significant disagreements within the ruling family that may lead to the assassination of bin Salman and end his rule.”
It gained 587,500 views.
Another user shared the same visuals with the following caption: “Urgent! Right now in Saudi Arabia. Saudi intelligence announces the arrest of the owner of His Highness the Amir Mubarak bin Nawaf Al-Duaisi Al Saud and a number of officers and affiliates following an attempt to assassinate His Highness the Amir Mohammed bin Salman. And thus a military coup attempt that was supported by the Houthis has failed.”
The post racked up 1.9 million views.
The same visuals were shared by another user, accumulating 1m views.
A pro-Yemeni account, based on its past posts, shared the same image with a similar caption, gaining 290,400 views.
The image with a similar claim was further shared by several other users on social media platforms Facebook and X, as can be seen here, here, here, here, here, here, here, here, here, here, and here; collectively accumulating 108,300 views.
Methodology
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in developments related to Saudi Arabia amid the conflict in the Middle East.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible Saudi or international media outlets had reported any alleged assassination attempt or the involvement of any such royal family member. However, no credible reports confirming the incident were found.
Further keyword searches for “Amir Mubarak bin Nawaf Al-Duaysi Al Saud” in both English and Arabic yielded no results on any such individual in the Saudi royal family.
A reverse image search was subsequently conducted to trace the origin of the face shown in the viral image and led to the account of Iraqi YouTuber Ali Adel, who has no known connection to the Saudi royal family.
The image was then examined using Google Gemini’s SynthID detector, which identified a digital watermark indicating that the image had been generated or edited using Google AI.
A comparison of the circulated portrait and a screenshot of Adel taken from one of his YouTube videos was subsequently conducted using Quantilence, an AI-based facial-similarity analysis tool. The tool found a 93.7 per cent facial similarity between the two images, further supporting the finding that the portrait uses Adel’s picture rather than depicting a member of the Saudi royal family.
The image was also analysed using AI detection tools and Sightengine flagged the image as 73 per cent AI-generated.
Similarly, another AI detection tool, TruthScan, flagged the image as 99pc AI-generated.
Undetectable AI also flagged the image as 99pc AI-generated.
Further keyword searches revealed that the same claim had circulated on social media in March 2026, without any evidence at that time as well.
Fact-check status: False
The viral claim of Saudi authorities busting an assassination plot involving the crown prince and an alleged royal family member is false.
No such incident has occurred, and the alleged royal family member does not exist.
This fact check was originally published by iVerify Pakistan — a project of CEJ-IBA and UNDP.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Pakistan reaffirmed its resolve to deepen longstanding relations with Russia and expand practical cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly security, as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir met Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev on Wednesday.
According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the meeting at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi focused on matters of mutual interest and the regional security environment, with particular emphasis on strengthening bilateral security cooperation.
“They underscored the importance of closer institutional linkages and improved coordination between the security institutions of Pakistan and Russia,” the statement outlined further.
Read: Pakistan, Russia agree to sign MoU to combat organised crime, finalise prisoner transfer agreement
CDF Munir reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its longstanding ties with Moscow and translating bilateral relations into tangible cooperation in areas of shared interest, particularly in the security domain.
The Russian interior minister, meanwhile, appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability and acknowledged the professionalism and sacrifices of the Pakistan Armed Forces in the fight against terrorism.
CDF Munir’s meeting with Minister Kolokoltsev comes amid expanding Pakistan–Russia engagement on counterterrorism, law enforcement, military training and broader bilateral relations.
In February, Russian President Vladimir Putin reaffirmed Moscow’s readiness to strengthen counterterrorism cooperation with Pakistan following a suicide attack on an Islamabad imambargah that killed at least 31 people. In letters of condolence to President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Putin expressed solidarity with Pakistan and reiterated Russia’s willingness to work with Islamabad in combating terrorism.
Then, in May, Pakistani and Russian officials held the 16th meeting of the Russia-Pakistan Consultative Group on Strategic Stability in Moscow, where they discussed international security, global stability, arms control, disarmament and non-proliferation. The Foreign Office said both sides found their approaches “aligned” on most of the issues discussed and agreed to continue coordination at relevant international forums. The next meeting was scheduled to take place in Islamabad in 2027.
A month after that, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Kolokoltsev, signed agreements to enhance cooperation on illegal immigration, the repatriation of illegally residing citizens and counter-narcotics efforts. Their discussions also highlighted regional security concerns linked to terrorist camps and drug production in Afghanistan. The agreements provided a practical framework for expanding cooperation between the two countries’ interior ministries and law enforcement agencies.
Read more: Russian interior minister arrives in Pakistan on maiden visit
On August 18, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met Russian Ambassador to Pakistan Albert Khorev in Islamabad and welcomed what he described as positive momentum in bilateral relations. Dar stressed the need for continued collaboration in key areas and sustained high-level exchanges to further strengthen ties.
Towards the end of September, the Pakistan Army and Russian Army participated in the ninth edition of their joint military exercise, Druzhba-IX, at Cherat and the National Counter Terrorism Centre in Pabbi. The two-week exercise focused on sharing operational experience, refining counterterrorism drills and procedures, and enhancing interoperability between the forces.
Finally, a couple of days ago, Kolokoltsev arrived in Pakistan on a four-day visit at the invitation of Naqvi, marking the first visit to Pakistan by a Russian interior minister.

items.title: Fact check: Viral K-P Home Department notification ordering arrests of PTI workers is fake
items.author: Fact Check By iVerify
items.content:
Several people, the majority of whom appear to be Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) supporters based on their past posts, have been sharing an alleged notification on social media platforms since October 13, 2026, from the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Home Department ordering the identification and arrest of PTI workers across the province. However, the notification is AI-generated.
The federal government imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on October 11 following the president’s approval of the recommendations by the federal cabinet. The measures were approved under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution.
The decision came during an emergency meeting of the federal cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, where he was briefed on the security situation in K-P. Cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”, according to the Prime Minister’s Office.
Read: Govt was left with 'no option' but emergency, governor rule: PM Shehbaz
A couple of hours after the imposition of emergency was announced, K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan, who had been accompanying now-dysfunctional K-P chief minister Sohail Afridi on PTI’s long march, claimed that Afridi had been taken into custody.
Later, PTI issued a statement condemning the “arrest” of Afridi and others, describing it as an act of “political victimisation and an attempt to weaken the province’s elected leadership and democratic institutions”.
Communication and internet services have also been disrupted in the province. Several PTI leaders and workers were also arrested in the lead-up to the imposition of governor’s rule.
How it started
On October 13, YouTuber and self-described journalist Measum Abbas shared a post on X containing a purported notification from the K-P Home Department.
The document bore the name and alleged signature of the additional chief secretary of the province’s Home Department. Its subject read: “Arrest of PTI workers – submission of names from your respective areas.”
It directed deputy commissioners across K-P to identify, verify and arrest PTI workers and submit their names, addresses, CNIC numbers and other details within seven days.
The post gained 17,000 views.
Another X account that appeared to support PTI, based on its past posts, shared the same notification with the following caption: “Order to arrest PTI workers, notification issued.”
The post gained 81,300 views.
Another apparent PTI supporter shared the same image with the following caption: “A display of shamelessness and lack of honour. They’ve made an illegitimate grab in the name of counter-terrorism, and instead of targeting the terrorists, these shameless people are demanding names to crack down on PTI.”
The post gained 17,200 views.
Other pro-PTI accounts on X also shared the same notification, as can be seen here, here, here, here, here and here; collectively gaining 14,000 views.
Methodology
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its virality and keen public interest in the arrest of PTI workers in K-P following up to and after the implementation of governor’s rule.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible Pakistani or local news outlets had reported on the alleged K-P Home Department notification ordering the arrest of PTI workers across the province, but nothing was found to corroborate it.
While news reports were plenty about PTI supporters being detained and arrested, none mentioned any such order from the K-P Home Department.
A visual and textual examination of the alleged document revealed discrepancies in its letterhead, which names the issuing authority as “Government of Pakistan, Home Department, Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.”
Whereas the official X account of the Home & Tribal Affairs Department, Government of K-P, shared a notification on April 6, 2023, along with an authentic letter, which identifies the issuing authority as “Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Home & Tribal Affairs Department.”
The viral notification features Pakistan’s national emblem at the top, whereas the authentic notification carries the provincial government’s emblem.
Furthermore, the alleged notification identified Muhammad Iqbal Khan as the additional chief secretary of the Home Department. However, a keyword search yielded an Oct 13, 2026, Dawn news report titled “Massive reshuffle in K-P bureaucracy under governor’s rule”, which said Amjad Ali Khan, the industries secretary, was transferred and posted as the home and tribal affairs secretary.
Other reports by Dawn and The Express Tribune also identified him as the additional chief secretary, instead of any Muhammad Iqbal Khan.
The notification image was subsequently analysed using OpenAI’s tool to detect the SynthID watermark, which identified a SynthID signal, indicating that the image was likely generated or edited using OpenAI tools.
SynthID works by embedding an invisible digital watermark directly into AI-generated media content. Unlike normal metadata, the watermark forms part of the content itself and is designed to remain detectable even after the media is doctored, such as cropping, applying filters or lossy compression.
The image was also analysed using other AI-detection tools. Undetectable AI flagged the visual as 99 per cent doctored, while Fake Image Detector flagged it as 71pc AI-generated.
Meanwhile, Truthscan flagged the image as 99pc AI-generated, and Sightengine labelled it as 72pc doctored.
iVerify also reached out to Express Tribune K-P bureau chief Shahid Hamid, who confirmed that the Home Department had been contacted to verify the alleged notification and that it was found to be fake.
Furthermore, Dawn correspondent Zahid Imdad said that a deputy inspector general of police posted in K-P had also confirmed the notification was fake and that nothing of the sort had been issued.
The official fact-check account of the K-P government also issued a statement on X dated Oct 13, 2026, saying the viral notification was fake.
The statement read, “A fake notification is currently being circulated on social media, falsely claiming that the K-P Home Department has directed the identification and arrest of PTI workers across the province.”

فیک نیوز الرٹ‼️
سوشل میڈیا پر خیبر پختونخوا کے محکمہ داخلہ کی جانب سے پی ٹی آئی کارکنوں کی شناخت، فہرستوں کی تیاری اور گرفتاریوں سے متعلق ایک جعلی نوٹیفکیشن گردش کر رہا ہے۔
یہ جعلی نوٹیفکیشن عوام میں گمراہ کن تاثر پیدا کرنے کی کوشش ہے۔ نوٹیفکیشن پر درج چیف… pic.twitter.com/tSMPYbx5YB
— Fact Check - KP Govt (@factcheckkpgovt) October 13, 2026
It continued, “The fabricated notification also bears the fake name of the chief secretary/official signatory, misleading the public and creating a false impression of politically motivated state action. The public is advised to verify official notifications through authentic government channels and refrain from sharing unverified information.”
Fact-check status: False
The claim that a viral notification from the K-P Home Department ordered the identification and arrest of PTI workers across the province is false.
The notification is fake and AI-generated.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Anthropic has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) systems could self-replicate on smart devices within the coming months. Such a development could allow AI-powered malware to spread through smart home appliances and other connected equipment without relying on centralized data centers.
The company described the potential threat as “AI worms,” referring to autonomous systems that could exploit security weaknesses, spread across networks, and avoid detection. Devices such as smart ovens, refrigerators, televisions, security cameras and robotic vacuum cleaners could become potential targets if these capabilities emerge.
Anthropic Warns AI Could Self-Replicate on Smart Devices Within Months
In a research report published on Monday, Anthropic’s researchers warned that self-replicating AI systems could become difficult to control once they spread across multiple devices. Unlike conventional systems that depend on a central server, these replicators could operate across distributed networks, making them harder to shut down.
AI Worms Could Spread Across Smart Devices
Anthropic’s frontier red team, which tests the capabilities and security risks of advanced AI systems, investigated how AI agents might exploit internet-connected devices.
During their research, the team prompted an AI agent to attempt to hack connected devices. The researchers explored whether an AI system could use such access to replicate itself and spread to other vulnerable machines.
According to the report, smaller AI models could be more suitable for this type of activity. Homes and small businesses could face particular risks because they often use multiple connected devices with limited built-in computing resources and varying levels of security.
Potentially vulnerable products include smart ovens, smart TVs, automatic lawnmowers, security cameras and video-conferencing equipment. These devices may contain small AI chips that support certain computing tasks.
However, Anthropic’s warning describes a potential security threat rather than confirming that widespread, self-replicating AI malware has already emerged.
Why Self-Replicating AI Could Be Difficult to Stop
Traditional malware can spread between computers and connected systems by exploiting software vulnerabilities. AI-powered malware could potentially take this threat further by using autonomous agents to identify weaknesses, adapt their actions, and search for additional devices.
If an AI system could copy itself onto other machines and continue operating independently, security teams might struggle to contain it. Shutting down one server or blocking a single connection might not stop a threat that had already spread across multiple devices.
Anthropic warned that different AI worms could potentially coordinate their activities and target computer hardware. Such a scenario could increase the scale and complexity of cyberattacks.
The company said security experts should strengthen existing systems to prevent these replicators from spreading. It also called for preparations to manage the risks if such threats become a reality.
Growing Concerns Over AI Safety
The warning comes amid increasing concerns about the cybersecurity risks associated with advanced AI systems. Technology companies have reported improvements in AI agents’ ability to perform tasks independently, including identifying vulnerabilities and carrying out complex operations.
These capabilities could help security researchers detect weaknesses more quickly. However, they could also give malicious actors new ways to automate cyberattacks.
Anthropic and other AI developers face growing pressure from researchers, lawmakers, and technology executives to introduce stronger safeguards as their models become more capable.
Despite these concerns, companies continue to develop and release increasingly advanced AI systems. This has intensified discussions about how developers can balance innovation with the need to prevent potentially dangerous uses of the technology.
See Also: NCCIA Arrests Man Over Alleged Use of Claude AI to Plan Ex-Girlfriend’s Murder
Stronger Security Measures May Become Necessary
Anthropic’s findings highlight the importance of securing internet-connected devices before AI-powered threats become more advanced.
Manufacturers may need to improve software updates, strengthen device authentication, fix vulnerabilities more quickly and limit the actions that connected devices can perform. Network monitoring and stronger isolation between devices could also help reduce the risk of malware spreading throughout homes and businesses.
Consumers can also reduce their exposure by installing security updates, replacing devices that no longer receive support, changing default passwords, and disabling unnecessary remote-access features.
Although the prospect of self-replicating AI presents serious security concerns, the timeline remains uncertain. Anthropic’s estimate that these capabilities could emerge within months is a warning about a possible future threat, not a confirmed deadline.
The report underscores the need for AI developers, device manufacturers, and cybersecurity experts to prepare for threats that could become more autonomous and difficult to contain as AI technology advances.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Oppo has announced the global rollout schedule for ColorOS 17, its latest Android-based operating system. The update will begin with newer flagship smartphones before reaching older Find series devices, Reno smartphones, F and K series models, and selected Oppo tablets.
ColorOS 17 debuted in China alongside the Find X10 Pro Max series. Oppo will launch the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max globally on October 21, 2026, with both smartphones running the new software out of the box.
The company will begin updating eligible older devices on October 29. The rollout will continue through November and extend into the first three months of 2027.
ColorOS 17 Global Rollout Starts Next Week: Full Update Schedule Revealed
Oppo will initially focus on its flagship Find series and foldable smartphones. The Reno lineup will also receive the update, followed by more devices from other series.
October 29, 2026
The first wave of updates for existing devices will include the following smartphones:
Oppo Find N6
Oppo Find X9 Ultra
Oppo Find X9s
Oppo Find X9 Pro
Oppo Find X9
October 30, 2026
Oppo will expand the rollout to older flagship phones and the Reno 16 series. The eligible devices scheduled for this date include:
Oppo Find N5
Oppo Find X8 Pro
Oppo Find X8
Oppo Reno16 Pro
Oppo Reno16
Oppo Reno16c
Oppo Reno16 F
Oppo Reno16 FS
November 2026 Onward
In November, Oppo will focus on the Reno 15 and Reno 14 series while expanding ColorOS 17 to more F and K series smartphones.
The company will add further Reno and K series devices to the rollout in the following months. Selected Oppo tablets will also receive the update.
Oppo plans to continue distributing ColorOS 17 through January, February and March 2027. However, users should check the official schedule for their specific device, as eligibility and rollout timing may vary by model and market.
ColorOS 17 Introduces Living Flow Design
ColorOS 17 brings visual changes and performance improvements to Oppo smartphones. The new version introduces Living Flow Design, which builds on the animation improvements introduced in ColorOS 15 and ColorOS 16.
The updated interface uses translucent visual elements and more responsive animations. Interactive elements can stretch, compress, or bounce when users touch them, giving the interface a more dynamic feel.
Oppo has also introduced a Unified Rendering Architecture to improve how the system handles graphical tasks. According to the company, this change reduces rendering workload by 25% and RAM usage by 30%.
These improvements could help compatible devices deliver smoother animations while using fewer system resources.
Performance Improvements and Faster Apps
ColorOS 17 also upgrades Oppo’s Laminar Flow Engine, which manages several aspects of system performance.
Oppo claims the updated engine allows smartphones to keep 25% more apps running in the background. This could help users switch between applications without frequently reloading them.
The company also says the Gallery app loads thumbnails 50% faster when launched from a cold start. App launch stability has improved by 55%, according to Oppo.
These figures represent the company’s reported results. Actual performance may vary depending on the device, hardware and applications being used.
New AI Features in ColorOS 17
Artificial intelligence is another major focus of ColorOS 17. Oppo has expanded AI Mind Pilot and AI Mind Space with features designed to simplify everyday tasks.
AI Mind Pilot’s Agent Mode can organize and rename photos and files based on their content and dates. It can also handle multiple steps in a single task.
For example, users can organize pictures from a trip into albums. The system can also help turn those photos into a vlog, reducing the amount of manual work required.
AI Mind Space receives new tools for learning and planning. Users can add documents and video links, which the feature converts into structured and searchable information.
The same feature can help with travel planning by combining saved information with destination maps to create personalized itineraries.
Privacy and Security Enhancements
With more AI features processing personal information, Oppo has also highlighted privacy and security improvements.
ColorOS 17 introduces Private Computing Cloud, which uses end-to-end encryption and a secure processing environment to protect user data. Oppo says the system is designed so that even the company cannot access the protected information.
The update also adds post-quantum security capabilities to strengthen data transmission against emerging security threats.
Another addition is AI Call Guard, which can detect potential AI-generated face swaps and synthetic voices. The feature processes detection tasks directly on the device, according to Oppo.
These tools aim to improve protection against scams and emerging forms of digital fraud.
When Will Your Oppo Phone Get ColorOS 17?
Oppo will begin the global rollout with its latest flagship devices before expanding support to older smartphones and tablets. The initial update wave starts on October 29, followed by another group of devices on October 30.
The company will gradually expand the rollout through March 2027, bringing the redesigned interface, performance improvements, AI tools, and security features to more eligible devices.
Users should remember that the announced dates represent the rollout schedule, not a guarantee that every device will receive the update immediately. Availability may depend on the phone model, region, and software distribution process.
The post ColorOS 17 Global Rollout Starts Next Week: Full Update Schedule Revealed appeared first on PhoneWorld.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Huawei has shipped more than 100 million Kirin-powered devices since 2023, marking a major milestone in its efforts to rebuild its semiconductor business despite US sanctions. The Chinese technology giant is also developing new processors and expanding its ambitions in artificial intelligence (AI) hardware.
Huawei announced the achievement on October 13, highlighting the progress of its in-house chip development. The company has faced restrictions on accessing advanced semiconductor technology and key components from international suppliers, forcing it to strengthen its domestic supply chain.
Huawei Ships Over 100 Million Kirin-Powered Devices Despite US Sanctions
Kirin processors have become an important part of Huawei’s strategy to reduce its reliance on foreign chip suppliers. The company has focused on developing its own processors and working with Chinese manufacturing partners to improve its smartphone technology.
The shipment milestone shows that Huawei has continued to expand its Kirin-powered device lineup despite the challenges created by US export restrictions. However, the company has not shared a detailed breakdown of the 100 million devices by model or processor generation.
Huawei has also introduced details about its latest Kirin 9050 series, which it describes as the first mass-produced processor to use its proprietary LogicFolding architecture. The technology was developed under a framework known as the Tau Scaling Law.
The company aims to improve chip performance and manufacturing efficiency through these new designs. Its progress also highlights China’s efforts to develop domestic semiconductor capabilities despite restrictions on access to advanced manufacturing equipment.
Kirin 9050 Brings New Chip Technology
The Kirin 9050 series represents another step in Huawei’s processor development. According to the company, the new chip uses more than 50 million hybrid bonds and delivers a 53.5% improvement in transistor density.
Transistor density refers to the number of transistors that manufacturers can fit into a specific area of a chip. Higher density can help pack more computing components into a smaller space. However, overall performance also depends on chip architecture, power consumption, cooling, and manufacturing quality.
Hybrid bonding connects components within semiconductor packages. This approach can support compact chip designs and improve communication between components.
Huawei said the Kirin 9050 series had entered mass production with support from China’s domestic electronics supply chain. The development is significant because US restrictions have limited Huawei’s access to certain advanced semiconductor technologies and manufacturing tools.
By investing in chip architecture, packaging methods, and domestic production, Huawei is trying to overcome some of these limitations.
However, the company has not provided independent benchmark results comparing the Kirin 9050 with leading processors from competitors. Independent testing will be necessary to determine its actual performance, energy efficiency, and AI computing capabilities.
Huawei Tests Next-Generation Kirin Processor
Huawei is also working on its next-generation Kirin 2027 processor. A report published by Chinese financial news outlet Yicai on October 13 said the chip had entered testing and achieved its initial performance targets.
The report cited Xu Songyu, a director responsible for wireless device chips within Huawei’s semiconductor business. However, the company has not disclosed detailed specifications, a confirmed launch date or a production schedule for the upcoming processor.
The Kirin 2027 forms part of Huawei’s longer-term efforts to improve its semiconductor technology. Its development could help the company maintain progress in smartphone processors while working on future chip designs.
Huawei Expands Its AI Chip Ambitions
Huawei’s semiconductor strategy now extends beyond smartphones. The company is also working to strengthen its position in China’s artificial intelligence chip market.
AI processors support demanding tasks such as training machine-learning models, running AI applications and powering cloud computing services. These chips are becoming increasingly important as businesses and technology companies expand their use of artificial intelligence.
Developing competitive AI hardware could help Huawei reduce its dependence on overseas suppliers and expand into new areas of the technology industry.
However, significant challenges remain. Advanced chip manufacturing requires specialized equipment, efficient production processes and high manufacturing yields. Software support and compatibility also play important roles in determining whether processors can compete successfully in the market.
Huawei’s latest milestone demonstrates progress in its efforts to rebuild its chip business despite US sanctions. With more than 100 million Kirin-powered devices shipped since 2023, the company is continuing to develop new processors and strengthen its domestic supply chain.
The next challenge will be to turn these advances into commercially competitive products while expanding its presence in the global smartphone and AI hardware markets.

items.content:
UK-based clean energy firm Octopus Energy has opened applications for the second edition of its Africa Energy Entrepreneurship Award, which offers grant funding, mentorship and support to early-stage startups expanding clean power access across the continent.
Run in partnership with the Sustainable Markets Initiative (SMI), and this year also supported by Nigerian solar company Salpha Energy, the Africa Energy Entrepreneurship Award will select three winners to receive a grant to scale product development and deployment, as well as access to a mentorship programme and resources and visibility aimed at helping them unlock follow-on funding.
The programme is open to startups based in Sub-Saharan Africa that are no more than five years old and have fewer than 20 full-time employees. Applications will be assessed on the uniqueness of the innovation, how it improves energy access, scalability, community impact, and the strength of the founding team. A panel of CEOs, founders and C-suite executives with experience in Africa’s energy transition will judge entries.
Last year’s winners were Nigeria’s Nimsy Agro Solar, which provides solar-powered irrigation pumps to smallholder farmers; PAM AI, which uses technology to optimise mini-grid energy; and KAMIM Technologies, which builds solar-powered cooling systems for farmers.
“With last year’s grant funding, we developed and piloted a first-of-its-kind solar irrigation reservoir in Giwa LGA in the Kaduna State in Nigeria,” said Onimisi Charles Atere, founder of Nimsy Agro Solar Concept. “The award has opened up new opportunities and networks, positioning us for greater impact and scale.”
Zoisa North-Bond, CEO of Octopus Energy Generation, said the company was proud to back early-stage startups delivering change through energy.
“We can’t wait to see this year’s applicants and hope this award continues to provide a launchpad for trailblazers to take their ideas to the next level,” she said.
Applications close on December 11.

China’s Shengtang Group Eyes $10 Million Investment in Pakistan’s EV and Energy Sectors
During the meeting, Haroon Akhtar Khan said the government was working to turn Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s vision of stronger relations with China into practical economic benefits. He added that the government was facilitating Chinese investors and taking steps to improve the business environment.
The adviser highlighted ongoing regulatory reforms aimed at attracting foreign investment and supporting industrial growth. He also identified the land-lease model as an important way to help investors establish businesses and develop industrial projects in Pakistan.
Haroon invited Chinese companies to explore Pakistan’s investment potential. He said the country had demonstrated resilience and reliability internationally and offered promising opportunities for foreign investors.
He also emphasized the longstanding relationship between Pakistan and China, describing their friendship as “thicker than blood.”
Investment Could Support Industrial Growth
Haroon Akhtar Khan noted that around 40% of the joint ventures and memorandums of understanding signed between Pakistan and China had reportedly moved into the implementation phase.
He said greater Chinese investment could help expand Pakistan’s industrial sector, introduce new technologies and create employment opportunities. It could also increase economic activity and strengthen cooperation between businesses in both countries.
The adviser stressed that cooperation with Chinese companies could play an important role in developing local industries and improving Pakistan’s industrial capabilities.
Electric Vehicles Among Key Investment Areas
Electric vehicles emerged as one of the promising areas for future cooperation. Haroon said partnerships with Chinese companies could help Pakistan advance EV technology and strengthen its position in the electric mobility sector.
China has a major presence in the global electric vehicle industry, and closer cooperation could provide Pakistan with opportunities to access technology, develop industrial expertise and support the growth of related businesses.
The proposed investment also covers energy, railways, infrastructure, tourism and urban development, potentially opening doors for cooperation across several parts of Pakistan’s economy.
Haroon assured the visiting delegation of the government’s full support in facilitating investment. He also presented a commemorative souvenir to the Chinese representatives.
Additional Secretary Humaira Zia Mufti, Joint Secretary Freedoon Akram Sheikh and Joint Secretary Amir Aqiq attended the meeting.
While the proposed $10 million investment signals Shengtang Group’s interest in Pakistan, the available information does not confirm that the investment has been finalized or that specific projects have entered the implementation stage.

items.content:
Pre-owned goods marketplace Circle has raised ₹25 Cr (about $2.6 Mn) in a seed funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors Titan Capital and Myntra cofounder Raveen Sastry. Delhivery COO Ajith Pai also joined the round as an angel investor.

Founded in 2025 by Chirag Kataruka and Ankit Misra, Circle operates a managed marketplace for pre-owned goods, handling product verification, payments and logistics for transactions between individual buyers and sellers without owning inventory.
Its platform combines AI-powered tools with human verification, with products ranging from smartphones, gaming consoles, and cameras to furniture, watches, handbags, and sneakers. Circle handles listing, pickup, and seller payouts, while offering buyers product verification and a three-day guarantee.
The Bengaluru-based startup claims to have facilitated around ₹25 Cr in pre-owned goods sales within a year of launch, attracting over 1 Mn visitors and generating 1 Lakh listings in the city. It said sellers typically find buyers within three days, compared with weeks or months on classifieds platforms.
The startup previously raised ₹3.4 Cr in a pre-seed round led by Titan Capital in November last year, with participation from Sastry.
Circle operates in a pre-owned goods market that includes classifieds platforms OLX India and Quikr, electronics-focused Cashify, and community resale platform FreeUp. These players overlap with Circle across different categories and services, rather than following an identical operating model.
Circle’s approach centres on managing transactions to address the verification, payment, and logistics challenges associated with buying and selling used goods.
According to ResearchAndMarkets, India’s recommerce market is projected to reach $5.91 Bn in 2026 and $8.61 Bn by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 9.8% over 2026-2030.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Merchants accepting electronic payments grew fourfold last fiscal year under the Prime Minister’s Cashless Pakistan initiative. The government’s next step is less about growth than about counting: it wants to tighten what qualifies as an active user, an active merchant and a unique digital payment user.
Minister of State for Railways and Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani chaired the meeting at the Finance Division. It brought together public officials and private payment companies to review this year’s Cashless Pakistan dashboard and plan the next phase.
Three numbers under review
The discussion centred on three indicators: the number of active and unique users of digital channels, the number of digital transactions in a year, and the number of active merchants accepting digital payments.
Participants questioned whether each indicator is valid and relevant to the initiative. They also weighed different definitions of usage, activity and uniqueness. The committee decided to review and set definitions for active app users, active merchants and unique digital payment users.
Indicator
Question the committee is addressing
Active and unique users of digital channels
What counts as “active”? What makes a user “unique”?
Digital transactions per year
Is this a valid measure for Cashless Pakistan?
Active merchants accepting digital payments
What level of use qualifies a merchant as active?
The Minister of State stressed that the dashboard needs accurate, validated and non-duplicated data so progress is measured credibly and transparently.
What the government reports so far
Beyond the fourfold rise in merchants, officials cited progress inside the public sector. NADRA has digitised 99 percent of payments at its service centres nationwide, and passport centres can now accept digital payments.
The government also reports about 75 percent digital payment acceptance across Centralised Entities and Self-Accounting Entities, two categories of government bodies.
The release gives no absolute figures. It does not say how many merchants accept electronic payments, how many users are active or how many transactions took place. The fourfold growth cannot be judged without the starting number.
Tax policy comes next
The Minister of State asked the private sector members of the committee to compile recommendations on enabling Cashless Pakistan through tax policy reforms. These will be reviewed by the government.
No specific taxes were named. The request suggests officials see tax treatment as a factor in whether merchants and consumers move to digital channels, but the release does not say which measures are under consideration.
The Minister of State described the aims as public convenience, transparency and faster documentation of the economy. He also reiterated that the government would work with regulators, financial institutions, fintech firms and the wider private sector on digital payments and financial inclusion.
Attendees came from the Finance Division, State Bank of Pakistan, Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication, NADRA and the Pakistan Digital Authority.
The private sector side included the Chairman of the Pakistan Banking Association, the President of Easypaisa Digital Bank, the Chairman of JazzCash, and the President and CEO of Bank Alfalah. Senior officials of JS Bank, Karandaaz Pakistan and other payments companies also took part.
The Minister of State directed that coordination between public and private stakeholders be strengthened.
Bottom Line
Most digital payment targets fail quietly at the definition stage. If one transaction a year makes a user “active”, the dashboard will look healthy while habits stay unchanged. If duplicate accounts count as separate users, the same person can be counted three times across three apps.
Tighter definitions will probably make the headline numbers smaller and more honest. That is a risk for a government that has just reported a fourfold rise, but it is also the only way later figures will mean anything.
The tax question is the harder one. Digital payments leave a record, and that record is the point of a documentation drive. Merchants who have stayed out of the tax net may see acceptance as a cost, not a convenience. How the private sector’s recommendations address that will show whether the government plans incentives, relief or both.
The next test is publication. If the revised definitions and the absolute numbers behind the fourfold claim appear on the dashboard, readers will be able to check the progress for themselves.
