Meanwhile, CaratLane founder Mithun Sacheti, who joined the board as an additional director earlier this year, has been elevated to an executive whole-time director role for a period of five years. Sacheti will now assume a new position to oversee strategic initiatives and take on some operational responsibilities.
“He understands the consumer business space, digital consumer ecosystems … He brings extensive entrepreneurial,consumer and brand building experience,” the gaming major said in its disclosures to the bourses earlier today.
Besides, the board also noted the resignation of Rohit Sharma as Whole-time Director, effective from January 1, 2027, onwards, as he decided to pursue entrepreneurial opportunities. Sharma joined the company’s board as an advisor in January 2025 and was later roped in as executive director in August.
Additionally, Nazara’s CFO Rakesh Shah has also resigned to pursue external opportunities and will be replaced by Arun Agrawal, former global CFO at Ness Digital Engineering. Shah, who has been with the gaming major since 2010, will exit the company on October 15 though he will assist with transition duties for 90 days.
The change at the top of Nazara’s hierarchy comes shortly after Mittersain exited as CEO amid a turning point in the listed company’s journey.
Back in March, Nazara acquired a 50% stake in Spanish casual gaming studio Bluetile Games and its associate BestPlay Systems for a deal worth $100.3 Mn at base value, with performance-linked earn-outs of up to $98.2 Mn.
However, the terms of the deal were later restructured such that Nazara acquired 100% of Bluetile and BestPlay for a fixed cash consideration of $303 Mn, shelling out $89 Mn upfront and committing to pay the remainder in agreed tranches by April 1, 2027.
Besides, the gaming giant also approved a ₹733.5 Cr fundraise via preferential issue of equity shares to the founders and senior leadership team of Bluetile and BestPlay, including Bluetile’s founder and CEO Raymond Stauffer, who also took over from Mittersain as CEO on September 1.
Notably, Bluetile and BestPlay together generated nearly ₹1,400 Cr in revenue in calendar year 2025. Yet, Bluetile’s EBITDA remained flat in the quarter despite a 54% revenue jump as the company faced climbing user acquisition costs.
Besides all this, the company also faced de-subsidiarisation of its gaming and esports media arm NODWIN Gaming this year. Nazara opted not to participate in a $100 Mn external funding round raised by NODWIN, resulting in its shareholding slipping below 51%. NODWIN is also seeking to list independently on the bourses in the near future.
On the financial front, Nazara reported a net loss of ₹82.5 Cr on operating revenue of ₹428.8 Cr in Q1 FY27. The gaming major’s operating revenue also declined 14% YoY to ₹428.8 Cr.

items.content:
Bengaluru-based Whizzo is in talks to raise around $26 Mn in its Series B funding round which could be co-led by Aavishkaar Capital and Bertelsmann Investments (BI), Inc42 learnt.
As per sources, existing backers Fundamentum, Lightspeed Ventures, among others, are also likely to participate in the round.
Questions sent to Whizzo didn’t elicit any response at the time of publication of the story. The article will be updated based on their responses.
The fresh round of funding comes almost six months after the startup raised around $15 Mn in its Series A funding round led by Fundamentum, with participation from Korean investor LB Investment Fund, and Lightspeed. Back then, the startup said it would utilise the funds for strengthening research and development of in-house IP for materials science innovation. Prior to this, Lightspeed Ventures led Whizzo’s seed round in 2025.
The Bengaluru-based startup raised its maiden institutional funding round in January 2025 to develop its advanced R&D capabilities, creation of a design lab for fashion-engineered textiles and the expansion of its supply chain.
Founded in 2024 by Shrestha Kukreja, Whizzo is a CDMO (contract development and manufacturing organisation) that offers textile design services and textile research & development services to clients across India, Vietnam, China and Bangladesh.
The startup integrates R&D, formulation, prototyping, process engineering, and commercial-scale manufacturing under one roof.
Whizzo works with B2B manufacturers and produces a wide range of materials for applications across geotextiles, agriculture textiles, protective and flame-retardant materials, specialty yarns, engineered apparel textiles, and industrial composites. It claims to combine sustainability with advanced materials science, offering proprietary textile blends.
The potential fundraise comes amid continued investor interest in tech-led textile manufacturing and fabric innovation, as startups look to improve product development and manufacturing processes through proprietary materials and R&D capabilities.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Sony dikabarkan mengalihkan ratusan paten terkait teknologi extended reality (XR) kepada Meta. Informasi yang beredar menyebutkan, proses pengalihan mencakup puluhan paten di Amerika Serikat yang berkaitan dengan perangkat virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), dan mixed reality (MR). Langkah ini memunculkan pertanyaan mengenai arah pengembangan teknologi XR Sony ke depannya.
Dalam laporan ZDNet Korea, mereka disebut telah mengalihkan 43 paten yang terdaftar di Amerika Serikat kepada Meta melalui proses yang berlangsung antara Juni hingga September 2026. Paten-paten itu mencakup teknologi layar yang dipasang di kepala atau head-mounted display, kacamata XR, serta berbagai teknologi yang dikembangkan Sony sejak 2010 hingga 2022.
Pengalihan tersebut diklaim mencakup total 419 paten secara global. Dari jumlah itu, sekitar 180 paten terdaftar di Amerika Serikat, sedangkan 239 lainnya berasal dari berbagai negara, termasuk Jepang, China, Korea Selatan, dan sejumlah wilayah Eropa. Meski demikian, informasi ini belum cukup untuk memastikan bahwa Sony sepenuhnya meninggalkan pengembangan perangkat XR.
Baca Juga: Sony Patenkan AI yang Bisa Membuat NPC dan Boss Beradaptasi dengan Gaya Bermain
Masa Depan Headset VR Sony Jadi Tanda Tanya
Saat ini memiliki PlayStation VR2 (PSVR 2), headset VR yang dirilis pada 2023 untuk digunakan bersama PlayStation 5. Perangkat tersebut awalnya berfokus pada ekosistem konsol PlayStation, sebelum Sony menghadirkan adaptor yang memungkinkan headset digunakan pada PC. Kehadiran dukungan PC memperluas penggunaan PSVR 2, meski perangkat ini tetap berkaitan erat dengan ekosistem gaming.
Pengalihan paten tersebut memunculkan spekulasi bahwa peluang hadirnya penerus PSVR 2 dalam waktu dekat semakin kecil. Namun, kepemilikan paten yang dialihkan tidak otomatis berarti Sony menghentikan seluruh riset XR atau membatalkan produk generasi berikutnya. Tanpa pernyataan resmi mengenai strategi produknya, arah pengembangan headset VR Sony masih belum dapat dipastikan.
Meta Berpotensi Memperkuat Teknologi Headset XR
Bagi Meta, akuisisi hak kekayaan intelektual tersebut berpotensi memperluas portofolio teknologi yang dapat dimanfaatkan untuk mengembangkan perangkat XR. Pengalaman dalam merancang perangkat VR untuk kebutuhan gaming bisa menjadi referensi yang relevan bagi Meta, terutama jika perusahaan ingin memperkuat kemampuan headset-nya di luar penggunaan umum.
Meski begitu, pengalihan paten tidak menjamin teknologi tersebut akan langsung digunakan dalam produk Meta berikutnya. Pemanfaatannya bergantung pada strategi pengembangan, kebutuhan teknis, dan keputusan bisnis perusahaan. Untuk saat ini, langkah tersebut lebih tepat dilihat sebagai potensi penguatan aset teknologi Meta, sekaligus perkembangan yang membuat masa depan bisnis XR menarik untuk diamati.

items.author: Amiya Johar
items.content:
Elon Musk pledged to make Starlink affordable in India as he renewed his attack on billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s (pictured) telecoms dominance, days before Jio Platforms launches a record-breaking IPO.
In a series of posts on social media platform X, the SpaceX chief argued that competition from Starlink would benefit Indian consumers by expanding connectivity options. “The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does,” he explained, adding, “Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business”.
Musk also dismissed claims that Starlink would struggle to compete with Jio’s low-cost data plans while also posing a threat to the incumbent operator. “This is absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole,” he said.
His comments come as Jio Platforms targets a valuation of around $106 billion, according to Reuters, in a planned IPO that could become India’s largest-ever listing. The business includes telecoms operation Reliance Jio, which reported 524.4 million subscribers at the end of March, including 268.5 million 5G customers.
“Prime Minister Ambani“
Musk has escalated his criticism of India’s regulatory process in recent days, accusing authorities and “certain oligarchs” of delaying Starlink’s entry into the country to maintain a “monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people”.
In a separate post on Friday (9 October), he sarcastically addressed the Jio Platforms-owner as “Prime Minister Ambani” and asked whether he would “consider allowing Starlink to compete”.
He argued satellite connectivity could bring internet access to underserved communities, improve educational opportunities and enable small businesses to reach international markets.
“Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India,” he wrote, adding “Starlink would change their lives for the better”.
India’s Ministry of Communications has rejected allegations of discriminatory treatment, stating that Starlink and incumbents Bharti Airtel and Reliance Jio were at broadly the same stage of the regulatory process. All three have secured initial approvals but remain subject to outstanding security clearances before they can obtain spectrum access.

items.author: Fiaz Mahmood
items.content:
An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Monday directed jail authorities to facilitate meetings between lawyer Imaan Mazari, her husband Hadi Ali Chattha and their legal team, which had been unable to meet them in connection with a case involving the removal of barriers.
ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra issued the directions during the hearing, which was attended by former human rights minister Shireen Mazari and lawyers Riasat Ali Azad and Aimal Khan. During the proceedings, Azad argued that the case could not proceed without allowing the legal team, comprising Azad, Zainab Janjua and Aimal Khan, to meet their clients.
The judge observed that anti-terrorism law required trials to be conducted on a daily basis and asked the prosecution how many witnesses it intended to produce. The prosecutor said there were nine witnesses. The judge subsequently directed the prosecutor to ensure that the accused were given access to their lawyers.
Also Read: Barricade removal case: ATC rejects plea to drop terrorism charges against Imaan, Hadi
Chattha questioned why he and Imaan were not being brought before the court, arguing that their continued absence undermined the requirements of a fair trial. He said they had been in jail for eight months and questioned how they could defend themselves and proceed with the case under such circumstances.
He also raised concerns about the confidentiality of meetings between lawyers and their clients, pointing out that cameras had been installed in the areas where meetings were held inside the jail. “The court has to decide our fate. Please summon us to court,” Chattha said, adding that it was for the court to determine whether he and Imaan were terrorists.
The court adjourned further proceedings until October 14.
Case background
Imaan and her husband Chattha were rearrested on September 17, shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.
Read More: SC suspends trial court order, grants bail to Imaan Mazari, Hadi Ali Chattha
On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Chattha signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29, the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.
On October 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Chattha in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
PharmEasy parent API Holdings narrowed its consolidated net loss by 67% to ₹520 Cr in the fiscal year ended March 2026 (FY26) from ₹1,572 Cr in the previous fiscal, with its operating revenue growing 12.7% YoY to ₹6,618.5 Cr.
The company attributed the improvement to its focus on customer experience, higher-value profitable segments, capacity utilisation, increasing wallet share and leveraging digital capabilities.
In its FY26 annual report, API Holdings said it improved margins by focusing on higher-margin products, particularly its private label brands, and optimising discounts in its B2R business.
Including other income of ₹70.8 Cr, the company’s total revenue stood at ₹6,689.2 Cr for FY26. However, it continued to report a loss before tax of ₹456.1 Cr.
In the first quarter of FY27, API Holdings reported a 10% YoY increase in revenue to ₹1,754 Cr while EBITDA rose to ₹39.3 Cr. Gross margin improved to 21.4% from 19.9% in FY26, and EBITDA margin reached 2.2%. Its B2B business grew 8.2% YoY to ₹1,006 Cr revenue and turned EBITDA-positive at ₹70 lakh.
The company said that PharmEasy’s B2C business posted ₹348 Cr revenue, with EBITDA losses narrowing to ₹17 Cr. Thyrocare reported 24% YoY revenue growth to ₹240 Cr, processed 5.4 Mn patients and conducted 55.2 Mn tests.
Where Did API Holdings Spend In FY26?
API Holdings’ consolidated expenses declined marginally by 0.9% to ₹7,146.7 Cr in FY26 from ₹7,208.6 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Purchases of stock-in-trade remained its largest expense, while lower employee benefit costs contributed to the overall reduction.
Purchases Of Stock-In-Trade: The expense rose 10.9% to ₹5,244.8 Cr from ₹4,729.6 Cr, accounting for about 73% of total expenses. The increase came as the company’s operating revenue expanded during the year.
Employee Benefit Expense: Employee costs fell 47.5% to ₹476.9 Cr from ₹908.4 Cr in FY25. A substantial part of the decline came from lower employee share-based payment expenses, which dropped to ₹62 Cr from ₹482.2 Cr in FY25.
Other Expenses: This category increased 7.5% YoY to ₹656.7 Cr from ₹610.7 Cr. Major components included ₹111.8 Cr of contractual payments to delivery associates, ₹73.4 Cr of sales promotion and marketing, ₹72.6 Cr of manpower charges, and ₹63.4 Cr of legal and professional fees.
API Holdings also reported a tax expense of ₹64.2 Cr, comprising ₹68 Cr in current tax, offset by a deferred tax credit of ₹4.2 Cr, and a prior-period charge of ₹0.4 Cr.
Products Account For 86% Of Revenue
API Holdings generates revenue from the sale of products and services. Product sales contributed ₹5,670 Cr, or 85.7% of revenue, in FY26. These include pharmaceutical, over-the-counter (OTC), surgical, consumable and private label products.
The company sources products from manufacturers and wholesalers and supplies them to local chemists, large pharmacies, doctors, clinics, online retailers on the PharmEasy platform and hospitals.
A significant part of this business flows through its chemist-focused distribution operations, while Aknamed supplies hospitals. The group also generates product revenue through collection kits sold by Thyrocare.
Services contributed ₹941.3 Cr, or 14.2% of revenue, in FY26. This includes diagnostics, teleconsulting, licensing and technology services.
Thyrocare’s diagnostic operations account for a substantial part of this stream, serving franchise partners, consumers, hospitals, diagnostic companies and independent phlebotomists. API Holdings also earns service revenue from diagnostic tests sold through the PharmEasy marketplace, fulfilment services and technology platforms, including Retailio, which connects pharmaceutical wholesalers and pharmacies.
How API Holdings’ Subsidiaries Contribute
Although API Holdings has six direct subsidiaries and 18 step-down subsidiaries, four businesses account for much of its activity across B2B distribution, diagnostics and consumer healthcare.
B2B: Ascent Wellness And Pharma Solutions, Aknamed
Ascent Wellness and Pharma Solutions supplies pharmaceutical products to chemists and institutions, sourcing directly from pharmaceutical companies and enabling retailers to place orders through a platform. Aknamed supplies hospitals with pharmaceutical products, consumables and surgical products sourced from pharmaceutical companies and distributors.
Together, the B2B businesses generated ₹4,082.4 Cr in revenue in FY26, with an EBITDA loss of ₹3.6 Cr. In Q1 FY27, they recorded combined revenue of ₹1,005.6 Cr and EBITDA of ₹70 Lakh.
Diagnostics: Thyrocare Technologies
Thyrocare, API Holdings’ listed diagnostics arm, is a key contributor to the group’s profitability. In FY26, it operated 41 laboratories, offered 1,275 tests, processed about 21 Cr tests and had more than 10,800 franchisees.
Its revenue grew 24% YoY to ₹240 Cr in Q1 FY27.
B2C: PharmEasy
PharmEasy operates the group’s consumer-facing healthcare marketplace. In FY26, the segment generated ₹1,334.5 Cr in revenue and reported an EBITDA loss of ₹44.1 Cr.
In Q1 FY27, it recorded revenue of ₹347.9 Cr, alongside an EBITDA loss of ₹17 Cr.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Monday that last month’s alleged terror plot targeting a British air base was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), as he announced fresh sanctions against two Iranian men.
However, Iran on Monday denied any involvement in an incident at Britain's RAF Fairford airbase, which has been used by the United States in its war with the Islamic republic.
"The Iranian ambassador in London, Ali Moussavi, has again categorically rejected the accusations concerning Tehran's role in the incident at the Fairford military base," state news agency IRNA reported, adding that he "called on the British government to present evidence supporting its allegations if it possesses any".
Addressing Parliament, Burnham said the UK assessment was that the alleged plot, which led to five arrests on suspicion of terror offenses, was highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran.
“I can confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard,” he told MPs.
“We will not tolerate these threats on our soil. We will crack down on Iran’s use of criminal networks, using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams.
“And we will bring further sanctions to restrict the capacity of Iran and the IRGC to do us harm.”
In late September, a major security incident occurred at RAF Fairford, a Gloucestershire airbase used by the US Air Force. The incident triggered a large-scale counter-terrorism investigation.
Separately, the UK government also announced that it summoned Iran’s ambassador for ongoing "malign activity."
Read More: US removes B-1 bombers from UK base amid security concerns
“Iran’s continued attempts to undermine the security of the United Kingdom and international partners through its criminal networks, proxy groups and state-backed malign activity is unacceptable," Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said in a statement.
"This Government will never waiver in our commitment to tacking Iran’s unacceptable actions and protecting our national security. We have already designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) under our new state threats powers," he added.
Britain has also imposed sanctions on two Iranian men, including an asset freeze and a ban on entering the UK.
'We stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis'
Burnham also addressed the escalating situation involving Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, saying he had discussed the issue with US President Donald Trump last month on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
“In my meeting with President Trump, we discussed the situation in the Middle East. I confirmed Britain's decision to send air defense and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia to provide air-to-air refueling support," he said.
"I can confirm today it has already completed 14 operational missions. This support is needed to protect civilians. I condemn the appalling attacks on the King Khalid International Airport. We will continue to stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis,” he added.
No reopening 2016 Brexit referendum
Burnham also ruled out reopening the Brexit referendum or revising his government's manifesto commitments on relations with the EU, while advocating closer cooperation with the bloc to boost economic growth and address migration.
He also said he respected the result of the 2016 referendum, in which Britain voted to leave the EU, but argued that pragmatic cooperation with European partners could serve the country's interests.
"I am not reopening the referendum. I respect the referendum result," he said.
Also Read: UK examines foreign state involvement in airbase plot
Burnham said his government would pursue opportunities to strengthen the British economy and improve cooperation to tackle migrant boat crossings in the English Channel.
"The deal that I've inherited coming into office represents an opportunity to secure progress on both of those things," he said, adding that rejecting such opportunities would be "a dereliction of duty from any member of this House," he noted.
‘It’s a conversation we must have’
Ahead of next month's UK-EU summit, Burnham called for discussions on the future relationship between Britain and the bloc, saying closer ties could help promote growth, control migration, and strengthen security.
"If we are serious about promoting growth, controlling migration, upholding our values and our security, it is a conversation we must have," he said.
However, Burnham ruled out rejoining the EU single market or customs union or restoring freedom of movement, citing commitments in Labour's 2024 general election manifesto.
Mentioning what he “can’t do” to improve growth in the UK, he said: “I also want to maintain trust in politics. And I'm afraid I'm not prepared to revisit the red lines in our manifesto.”
The manifesto pledged to keep Britain outside the EU while seeking to reset relations and deepen ties with European partners.
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch accused Burnham of attempting to distract the public by raising claims of Russian interference in the 2016 referendum.
She questioned whether he considered the referendum result legitimate and called on Burnham to publish evidence if he believes Russia influenced the outcome.
"This is lazy thinking from people who don't have solutions to the real problems we face," Badenoch said.
But Burnham accused the Conservatives of being "in denial about, and not open to seeing, how we can move forward to a better position for the country."
He said public opinion in Britain has shifted in favor of a different approach to relations with the EU, while insisting that his government would respect its existing commitments.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
“Have you ever clicked your mouse HERE? You will.”
That was the text accompanying the first banner ad on the internet, launched by telecommunications company AT&T on HotWired.com in 1994. The ad reportedly clocked a 44% click-through rate in its first four months, a figure that would be extraordinary by the standards of almost any digital marketing channel today.
Over three decades, online advertising has evolved from banner ads to search, social media, programmatic buying, influencer marketing and performance marketing.
Then, with the emergence of search engine optimisation (SEO) practices, brands started optimising websites, building backlinks, targeting keywords and creating content to improve their visibility. Over time, SEO grew into a $90 Bn industry.
But the search box is now changing again.
Today, a growing number of consumers are turning to AI assistants instead of typing keywords into Google and opening a dozen links. Whether they are looking for accounting software, a nearby restaurant or the best smartphone under ₹50,000, they can simply ask an AI assistant for recommendations.
Their interaction with AI is no longer limited to a query or a list of results. Users/consumers ask follow-up questions, compare options, refine their requirements, and direct AI to recommend what they should buy.
This is where answer engine optimisation (AEO) and generative engine optimisation (GEO) have emerged as a new trend. But there is no single platform to optimise for, no standard ranking system and no clear way to measure success.
Much like what the SEO function was in its early days, marketers are still figuring out what works. Agencies are experimenting with how brands appear in answers generated by ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google’s AI-powered search products. They are tracking brand mentions, citations and recommendations, while trying to understand why one company gets surfaced over another.
But as brands scramble to show up in AI-generated answers, a bigger question is emerging: How can they ensure they are not just recommended by AI, but show up at the right moment?
The Missing Link In AI Marketing
Currently, for brands, the challenge is not how to appear in AI answers but figure out whether that visibility brings more visitors, customers or sales.
Google historically gave marketers detailed visibility through tools such as Search Console and keyword-level paid search data. This model is considerably harder to replicate when consumers interact with AI through multi-step conversations.
AI platforms currently offer limited visibility into the prompts driving discovery. A user may start with a broad question, ask several follow-ups, compare products, and only then arrive at a purchase decision. For marketers, identifying which interaction influenced that journey is harder than attributing a click to a specific search query.
Organic visibility is also inconsistent across platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity. For queries around the “best” or “top” products and services, AI models may rely heavily on third-party publishers, reviews and user-generated content rather than brand websites.
As a result, brands need to build a consistent information ecosystem across websites, ads, influencers and third-party platforms.
“So, eventually, for optimising, it becomes a lot more important to produce content in the broader ecosystem. We often ask brands to be consistent with their communication,” said Rishabh Mahendru, senior vice president of client success and growth at AdLift.
Marketers are also grappling with how much control they have over their brands’ visibility in AI-driven discovery. AI platforms can answer users’ questions without sending them to an external website. These zero-click answers may be convenient for consumers, but they can reduce traffic to publisher and brand websites.
Even when AI search leads to a sale, tracing that purchase back to a specific interaction can be difficult. A consumer may discover a brand through an AI assistant, research it elsewhere and make a purchase days later. Traditional last-click attribution models may fail to capture the role AI played in that journey.
There is also less certainty around where and how brands appear. AI platforms determine which ads match a user’s intent, while changes in how models cite sources can make organic visibility unpredictable. Brands also risk appearing alongside misinformation, hate speech or polarising content in AI-generated responses. To address these, OpenAI is exploring geo-based ad experiments and brand-suitability pilots to give advertisers more insight into where their ads appear and how they perform.
Overall, with its ChatGPT Ads in India, OpenAI is bringing sponsored messages into conversations on the AI chatbot in one of its largest markets. Ads have been rolled out to users on Free and Go tiers, while Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Education users get an ad-free experience. More than 50 brands were planned to go live during the initial rollout, with WPP and Omnicom as OpenAI’s first agency partners in India. Businesses can access ChatGPT’s self-serve Ads Manager, with daily budgets starting at ₹725.
The Next Frontier Of Brand Visibility
With no standard way to measure AI search visibility or predict which brands will surface in AI-generated answers, startups are building tools to help businesses navigate the new landscape.
Antler-incubated RankinLLM, for instance, is building a GEO and AI search visibility platform. “We operate across three layers: an observability layer to track LLM activity, an intelligence layer to extract meaningful signals from noisy data, and an optimisation layer to fix identified gaps. Optimiser agents create a closed loop, while KPIs such as brand mentions, share of voice, citations and sentiment measure the impact,” said cofounder and CEO Kartik Sharma.
Bengaluru-based TruCommerce has taken a different approach. It initially built a tool to track how often brands appeared in AI-generated answers. But it found that much of the traffic coming from AI platforms was being wrongly counted as direct website visits. This led the startup to shift its focus to helping brands sell directly through AI platforms.
TruCommerce now connects brands’ product catalogues and inventory with AI assistants. This helps businesses track visitors coming from AI, make product information easier for AI tools to understand, and enable customers to buy products without leaving the conversation.
Meanwhile, Lightspeed-backed Gushwork helps small and medium-sized businesses attract potential customers through traditional search engines and AI tools. Its AI agents create content designed to appear in search results, while its platform tracks the enquiries this content generates.
Other startups, including Nexad, Parsnip and AdCreative AI, are also building tools to help brands advertise and improve their visibility across AI platforms.
For marketers, however, this shift is still in its early stages. Traditional SEO took decades to develop its tools, metrics and best practices. AI is at the same crossroads.

India’s deeptech startups raised substantially more capital in Q3 2026, even as the number of deals edged lower.
As per Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026’, deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals, compared with $105 Mn across 29 deals in Q3 2025. The 176% YoY increase outpaced the broader startup ecosystem, where funding grew 5% to $2.2 Bn.
For context, deeptech startups are the ones that develop advanced technologies and hardware and include innovations across sub-segments like spacetech, robotics, defence technology and semiconductors.
Large Spacetech Rounds Drive Deeptech Funding Surge
The sharp rise in funding, despite a marginal decline in deal count, points to a concentration of capital in a smaller pool of startups.
In this, large spacetech rounds accounted for a significant share of the funding deployed during the quarter, with the startups in the sector netting $130 Mn, accounting for about 45% of deeptech funding in Q3. Six-year-old spacetech startup Pixxel’s $100 Mn round was one of four mega funding rounds recorded during the quarter. The round accounted for over three-fourths of the segment’s total.
Sustaining this momentum will require capital to reach beyond a select group of companies. As per a recent report by the Indian Venture and Alternate Capital Association (IVCA), deeptech startups continue to face a funding gap at the Series B and C stages, with few funds equipped to write the larger cheques needed to take technologies from development to commercial scale.
IVCA President Rajat Tandon said bridging this gap, deepening domestic limited partner participation, and improving exit pathways will be critical to building globally competitive deeptech companies.
“India’s deeptech opportunity is moving from promise to more investible commitments, with an increasingly institutionalised ecosystem play. The growth in capital flowing into deeptech over the past decade reflects the confidence investors have in India’s scientific and technological capabilities. However, taking deeptech startups and entrepreneurs from the laboratory to global scale will require capital that is patient, appropriately structured, and available across the entire growth journey,” he said.
Government Push Adds To Deeptech Funding Momentum
Bharat Innovation Fund cofounder and partner Ashwin Raguraman attributed some of the recent momentum to the government’s ₹1 Lakh Cr Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund and its wider push to support technology-led businesses.
“I attribute (growth in deeptech funding) this quarter and maybe even last quarter predominantly due to the announcement on the government’s deeptech-focused ₹1 Lakh Cr RDI Fund and a fairly solid government push, which is making capital available to VC funds,” Raguraman told Inc42.
The RDI Fund aims to catalyse private investment in research-intensive businesses. Its framework includes eligibility requirements for R&D-intensive technologies at technology readiness level (TRL) 4 or above, indicating that they have progressed beyond basic laboratory validation.
New investment vehicles also emerged during the quarter. Asiana Fund and JC Capital jointly launched a ₹1,000 Cr deeptech fund, while Transition VC and Accel launched funds to back technology-led businesses.
Access Free Report
RDI Fund Faces Questions Over Governance
However, the extent to which the RDI Fund has influenced investor sentiment remains uncertain. In August, The Indian Express reported that nearly two-thirds of the more than ₹2,000 Cr allocated to deeptech companies under the scheme had gone to firms with links to members of the panel involved in selecting beneficiaries, raising concerns over potential conflicts of interest.
Inc42’s Q3 2026 Indian Investor Ranking & Sentiment Survey, which covered 85 institutional investors, found that 52% considered disclosure and recusal safeguards adequate but said visibility remained limited.
Another 25% viewed the issue as a governance failure requiring independent oversight, while 14% said such investment ties could be managed through disclosure and recusal. The remaining 9% said it was not a concern, arguing that the focus should remain on company selection.
The findings suggest that the availability of government-backed capital is only part of the equation. Transparency in its allocation and the availability of patient capital across funding stages will also shape the sector’s ability to turn promising technologies into globally competitive businesses.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Steam dilaporkan mencatat rekor baru dengan mencapai 43,5 juta pengguna yang online secara bersamaan pada Minggu, 11 Oktober 2026. Berdasarkan laporan yang beredar, angka tersebut tercapai pada pukul 14.00 UTC atau 21.00 WIB. Pencapaian ini kembali menunjukkan besarnya aktivitas pengguna di platform distribusi game milik Valve tersebut.
Meski demikian, tidak semua pengguna yang online sedang memainkan game. Dari total 43,5 juta pengguna tersebut, sekitar 14,46 juta tercatat sedang bermain. Sisanya kemungkinan menggunakan Steam untuk aktivitas lain, seperti mengobrol dengan teman, menjelajahi katalog game, atau mencari judul yang ingin dibeli. Dengan begitu, jumlah pengguna bersamaan tidak bisa disamakan dengan jumlah pemain aktif di dalam game.
Rekor ini juga menarik karena terjadi di luar periode liburan akhir tahun, yang biasanya memberi banyak orang waktu luang untuk bermain. Ada sejumlah kemungkinan yang dapat mendorong peningkatan aktivitas, mulai dari pengguna mencoba perangkat baru hingga berburu diskon dan mencari game menarik. Namun, faktor-faktor tersebut masih berupa dugaan dan belum dapat dipastikan sebagai penyebab langsung tercapainya rekor.
Baca Juga: Game Indonesia KuloNiku: Bowl Up! Raih Rating Overwhelmingly Positive di Steam
Jumlah Pengguna Steam Terus Meningkat
Nah, mereka telah menjadi salah satu platform utama untuk membeli dan memainkan game PC, dengan katalog yang mencakup berbagai genre serta judul dari pengembang independen hingga studio besar. Kehadiran banyak game baru, termasuk rilisan AAA, berpotensi menarik lebih banyak pengguna untuk mengakses platform tersebut. Meski begitu, data pengguna bersamaan saja belum cukup untuk menjelaskan seberapa besar kontribusi masing-masing game terhadap rekor terbaru.
Perlu dibedakan pula antara jumlah pengguna yang online dan jumlah orang yang benar-benar bermain. Angka 14,46 juta pemain aktif menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar pengguna yang tercatat online saat itu tidak sedang bermain game. Mereka bisa saja sedang membuka toko, mengobrol, atau melakukan aktivitas lain di Steam. Karena itu, rekor ini lebih tepat dipahami sebagai gambaran aktivitas keseluruhan platform, bukan semata-mata lonjakan jumlah pemain.
Perangkat dan Ekosistem Game Ikut Berkembang
Pertumbuhan aktivitas Steam juga berlangsung ketika ekosistem gaming PC semakin beragam. Perangkat seperti Steam Deck memungkinkan pengguna memainkan game PC dalam format portabel, sementara perangkat lain yang dapat menjalankan Steam membuka lebih banyak pilihan untuk mengakses koleksi game. Steam Frame, perangkat VR yang disebut dalam laporan sumber, juga berpotensi memperluas ekosistem tersebut jika benar-benar menarik minat pengguna.
Meski begitu, belum ada bukti bahwa perangkat tertentu menjadi penyebab utama rekor 43,5 juta pengguna ini. Angka tersebut tetap menjadi pencapaian besar bagi Steam, tetapi tren berikutnya akan lebih menarik untuk diamati: apakah jumlah pengguna bersamaan terus meningkat atau rekor ini hanya mencerminkan lonjakan aktivitas pada akhir pekan.

A delegation of China’s Shengtang Group called on Adviser to the Prime Minister on Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan to explore investment opportunities in Pakistan and discuss potential cooperation in key sectors of the economy.
The Chinese delegation expressed interest in signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) worth *US$10 million* and exploring investment opportunities in industrial development, infrastructure, tourism, electric vehicles (EVs), railways, energy and urban development.
During the meeting, Haroon Akhtar Khan said that Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif’s vision of enhanced cooperation with China was being translated into practical outcomes. He emphasised that the Prime Minister had issued clear directions to facilitate Chinese investors, improve the business environment and ensure ease of doing business in Pakistan.
He said that business-friendly regulatory reforms were being introduced in line with the Prime Minister’s directives. He also highlighted the land-lease model available to investors as an important facilitation mechanism for promoting investment and industrial development.
“The time is right for investors to explore opportunities in Pakistan. The country has demonstrated its reliability and resilience at the international level,” Haroon Akhtar Khan said, inviting Chinese investors to benefit from emerging opportunities in Pakistan’s industrial and economic landscape.
Highlighting the longstanding relationship between Pakistan and China, the Adviser remarked that the two countries enjoyed ties “thicker than blood.” He said that numerous joint ventures and MoUs had been signed between the two countries, with approximately 40 per cent of these joint initiatives reportedly having entered the implementation phase.
He observed that further Chinese investment would contribute to industrial expansion, economic activity, technology transfer and employment generation in Pakistan.
Speaking about emerging investment opportunities, Haroon Akhtar Khan identified electric vehicles as an important area for the next phase of investment and industrial cooperation. He said Pakistan was progressing towards EV technology and that collaboration with Chinese companies could support technological advancement and strengthen the country’s industrial base.
The Adviser assured the delegation of the government’s full support and commitment to facilitating investment. He also presented a commemorative souvenir to the Chinese delegation.
Additional Secretary Humaira Zia Mufti, Joint Secretary Freedoon Akram Sheikh and Joint Secretary Amir Aqiq were also present at the meeting.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Hackers forced the temperature of fridges ​and freezers in many French supermarket fridges up to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, causing fires and spoiling food at several hundred ‌stores in a major cyberattack.
The Paris prosecutor's office said a "large-scale" attack was "affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France", leading to food losses and fires.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has instructed France's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) to investigate, a person in his office said.
France was coordinating with European counterparts because other countries could also be affected, the person said, adding that authorities were assessing whether ​other French companies were at risk.
Felix Aime, a senior cyber threat intelligence analyst at Sekoia Threat Detection and Research, said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and ​Belgium had also been affected.
Carrefour said 80 of its supermarkets had been hit, while Monoprix said 5% of its stores were affected.
Les ⁠Mousquetaires, owner of retailer Intermarche, said fridges at around 150 of its stores were heated up to 50 degrees Celsius for six hours overnight. A spokesperson said ​all affected food had been discarded to eliminate health risks.
Paris resident Geert de Clercq witnessed staff at an Intermarche in central Paris throwing cartfuls of defrosted frozen foods into ​a giant trash container, with molten ice cream sloshing out of broken tubs on the street.
Cooperative U CEO Dominique Schelcher said his supermarket group had also been targeted.
Read More: Thousands of cyberattacks blocked every month
"Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented," he wrote on X.
E.Leclerc and Auchan did not respond to requests for ​comment.
There was no immediate estimate of industry-wide losses.
"Retail and wholesale play an essential role in keeping Europe supplied with the goods people rely on every day," said Christel ​Delberghe, director general at European retail association Eurocommerce. "This incident underlines the importance of resilience across the entire supply chain."
Cold aisles controlled over internet
Supermarket cold aisles are typically run by control panels ‌that manage ⁠an entire store's fridges and freezers and can be accessed over the internet, which lets maintenance companies adjust them from anywhere.
The source close to Lecornu said ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by Danish company Danfoss.
Danfoss said it was "aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems".
The affected units "were running outdated firmware", Danfoss said, adding that it had "long advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions".
On August 9, cybersecurity ​firm Claroty's Team82 published research detailing vulnerabilities ​in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A controller. ⁠According to the report, software updates issued by Danfoss addressed issues that could have allowed attackers to bypass authentication controls and execute code on compromised devices.
The attacks resemble disruptions reported at about a dozen US military commissaries in late August that led ​to food losses after fridges were affected.
Dutch security issue
Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize, which operates the Netherlands' largest supermarket chain Albert Heijn ​and has major operations ⁠in the US, said it was dealing with a "security issue" on its network and had taken several systems offline as a precaution.
A message on the retailer's smartphone app said it was unable to deliver groceries because of a "cybersecurity incident".
Online orders account for about 10% of Albert Heijn sales. Physical stores remained open, while Dutch news agency ANP reported that ⁠rival retailers had ​seen a surge in delivery orders.
Ahold Delhaize said there was no reason to see a link ​between the incidents in France and its supermarkets.
Ahold is the fourth-largest grocery retailer in the US. Websites for its Stop & Shop, Giant, Hannaford and Food Lion chains displayed notices saying "site temporarily down".
It was unclear whether ​other operations had been affected.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Phone slogans usually don’t mean much. “Beauty and Beast” is different, because it tells you exactly what TECNO is going for. It is the theme for the POVA Curve 2 5G, the phone leading POVA’s return to Pakistan on October 15. And it is aimed squarely at a choice local buyers know too well: the phone that looks good, or the phone that lasts.
The Beauty: Slim, Curved and Hard to Ignore
Start with the looks. The POVA Curve 2 5G goes slim and curved, with flowing lines and a clean, modern finish. TECNO is positioning it as the slimmest phone in its segment, which is a big call for POVA, a line that built its name on big batteries.
That matters, by the way. Performance phones in this bracket tend to be chunky, and POVA has always put power first. The POVA Curve 2 5G is one you can slide into a pocket, hold through a long gaming session and still want to show off on the table.
The Beast: Built to Outlast Your Day
Now for the part POVA fans actually came for. TECNO is promising a massive battery inside that slim body, and that pairing is the whole point of the POVA Curve 2 5G. Battery life is one of the biggest complaints among smartphone users in Pakistan, and slim phones are usually the worst offenders.
The POVA Curve 2 5G is meant to break that pattern: light in the hand, but still going after a full day of calls, scrolling, streaming and gaming. And the Beast is not only about stamina. It is also about the 5G processor driving the phone, built to keep everything running fast and smooth when the day gets demanding. TECNO says the phone is built tough enough for real life too, drops and rough weather included.
Two Promises, One Phone
Neither idea is new on its own. Slim phones exist. Big-battery phones exist. Getting both in one body, without the usual compromise, is the rare part, and that is the gap the POVA Curve 2 5G is going after.
For buyers, it could make things a lot simpler. Nobody enjoys asking “do I want the good-looking one or the one that lasts?” The POVA Curve 2 5G wants to make that question disappear.
What TECNO Isn’t Telling Us Yet
Here is the catch. TECNO is holding back the details for Pakistan, including the final specifications and pricing, until the launch, though the estimated price is around PKR 110,000 to 120,000. So, for now there is no way to tell whether “Beauty and Beast” is a real shift for POVA or just a very good tagline.
The launch will settle it. Until then, the pitch is simple enough: a slim phone should be able to go the distance. Stick around, because the POVA Curve 2 5G is not far off.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MoIB) on Monday called out the Afghan Taliban for resorting to “rhetoric and diversion” to deflect attention from terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory and launching attacks against Pakistan.
In a post on X, the ministry said the Afghan Taliban regime’s spokesperson had once again resorted to rhetoric instead of addressing what it described as a well-documented terrorist threat emanating from Afghanistan.
It added that attempts to shift attention towards Pakistan’s internal affairs could not conceal the Afghan Taliban’s failure to prevent terrorist groups from using Afghan territory to plan and launch attacks against Pakistan.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MoIB) on Monday called out the Afghan Taliban for resorting to “rhetoric and diversion” to deflect attention from terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory and launching attacks against Pakistan.
In a post on X, the ministry said the Afghan Taliban regime’s spokesperson had once again resorted to rhetoric instead of addressing what it described as a well-documented terrorist threat emanating from Afghanistan.
It added that attempts to shift attention towards Pakistan’s internal affairs could not conceal the Afghan Taliban’s failure to prevent terrorist groups from using Afghan territory to plan and launch attacks against Pakistan.
The Afghan Taliban regime’s spokesperson has once again resorted to rhetoric and diversion instead of addressing the well-documented terrorist threat emanating from Afghan territory. Attempts to shift attention towards Pakistan’s internal affairs cannot conceal the regime’s…
— Ministry of Information & Broadcasting (@MoIB_Official) October 12, 2026
Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Afghan Taliban regime of failing to act against militant sanctuaries despite being provided with information about their locations and activities.
Citing the Sixteenth Report (S/2025/796) of the UN Security Council’s Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team, the ministry said the report estimated that approximately 6,000 Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) fighters were present in Afghanistan and documented Taliban support for the group.
“These findings cannot credibly be dismissed as Pakistani propaganda. The regime must address this documented threat through concrete action rather than denial,” the ministry said.
Also Read: ‘Irrefutable evidence’ links Afghan soil to terror attacks in Pakistan
It also criticised the Afghan Taliban regime’s record on governance and citizens’ rights, saying its attempts to lecture others on these issues rang hollow in light of its continued restrictions on girls’ education and violations of fundamental human rights.
The ministry reiterated that Pakistan remained committed to dialogue, but said meaningful progress required the Afghan Taliban regime to honour its counterterrorism commitments and take verifiable action against terrorist sanctuaries and support networks.
“Pakistan will take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law, to protect its citizens, defend its sovereignty and safeguard its territorial integrity. The responsibility to end the use of Afghan territory for attacks against Pakistan rests squarely with the regime,” it concluded.
Terrorism emanating from Afghanistan
Islamabad has rejected Taliban assurances that Afghan territory would not be used against neighbouring countries, arguing that the ground situation and documented militant activity tell a different story.
Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.
Security officials estimate that up to 70 per cent of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.
The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan.
In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.
Read More: Pakistan warns Afghanistan after Kohat attack, says it can eliminate terror threats ‘wherever they are’
Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.
UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM) and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.
Pakistani officials say the continued presence of these groups, combined with training facilities, cross-border infiltration and access to sophisticated weapons, demonstrates that Afghanistan remains an important base for terrorist activity affecting Pakistan.
Pakistan's position, according to officials, remains that Kabul must take concrete steps to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries, eliminate training infrastructure, prevent cross-border infiltration and ensure that Afghan territory is not used for attacks against Pakistan.
The government has maintained that the issue was fundamentally one of Pakistan's national security and that continued attacks from Afghan soil cannot be addressed through denials alone.
Pakistan says it expected the Taliban regime to fulfil its commitments by taking verifiable action against terrorist groups operating from its territory rather than defending or denying their presence.

items.title: China's $7.5b EU hybrid boom faces new curbs under China-EU deal
items.summary:

items.content:
China's deal to curb hybrid vehicle exports to the European Union is set to deal a fresh blow to electric vehicle makers that ramped up hybrid ​shipments exempt from the bloc's tariffs on Chinese-made EVs as sales growth slows at home.
Beijing's exports of hybrids to the EU's 27 member states tripled to $7.5 billion ‌in the first half of this year from $2.5 billion a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data. The figure was nearly nine times the $845 million exported in all of 2021.
Since the EU imposed additional tariffs on Chinese-made EVs in 2024, automakers have increasingly turned to plug-in hybrids, which are exempt from the extra duties. Weak charging infrastructure in parts of Europe has also supported demand for plug-in hybrids, which are marketed for their long range and strong ​fuel economy.
SAIC, BYD and Chery accounted for more than 90% of Chinese hybrid sales volume in the EU, while hybrids represented more than half of their European sales, according ​to Jefferies.
"It's making life a bit more difficult for the Chinese, but...that's not going to stop them as it happened to the electric cars," said ⁠Felipe Munoz of Car Industry Analysis.
"Europe is going to a point where they will need to decide whether they're doing what the US is doing or just let the whole industry be ​bought by the Chinese."
Speaking to reporters at the Paris auto show on Monday, Changan president Zhao Fei said he was "not that concerned" by the deal, which he viewed as a preamble to 'Made in ​Europe' local content rules that could be dealt with by setting up production in the region.
"This actually provides opportunities for Chinese companies like Changan to enter the European market," he said, adding that the company is planning to produce its first cars in the region early next year.
Chinese brands captured a record 15% share of Europe's EV market in the second quarter, up from 9.5% in the first quarter of 2024, while Chinese plug-in hybrids accounted for ​more than a quarter of the segment, rising sharply from just 1.7% at the beginning of 2024, according to Schmidt Automotive Research.
‘Tariff risk off, quota risk on’
While European Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic ​said on Friday the agreement would cut the imports of "several million cars over four years," Brussels and Beijing have yet to disclose how the arrangement will be implemented.
Read More: Scientific expedition warns of accelerated glacier melting in NW China's Xinjiang
China's Commerce Ministry said on Monday that the arrangement would ‌allow continued export ⁠growth and guarantee China a quota no smaller than that granted to any other source of imports.
Renault CEO Francois Provost said on Monday the surge in Chinese hybrid imports was unsustainable for Europe, but added the agreement was preferable to a trade war and underscored the need to manage trade relations "sensibly".
Investors largely viewed the agreement as a de-escalation of trade tensions and a sign that tariffs on Chinese hybrids may be off the table for now. Shares in BYD fell 1.8%, while Chery and SAIC rose 1.4% and 0.5%, respectively.
"Overall, we believe it is a risk-relief rally story...as the implementation rules, ​volume caps, price floors, carve-outs are still pending technical ​negotiation," Citi analysts said.
The rapid growth of ⁠Chinese hybrid sales has increasingly challenged European manufacturers, including Volkswagen, long the region's leading plug-in hybrid seller, said Li Yanwei, an analyst at the China Automobile Dealers Association.
BYD, China's largest hybrid vehicle exporter to Europe, sold more plug-in hybrids than fully electric models in the first eight months of ​the year, with its Seal U SUV its best-selling model, according to data compiled by Li.
Together with Chery, SAIC and Geely, the company has ​narrowed the gap with ⁠Volkswagen, which still commanded a 31.8% share of the EU plug-in hybrid market.
"Let's see if China honours the agreement or finds workarounds, or temporary tariff exemptions," said Michael Dunne, a consultant who closely follows the Chinese automotive industry.
Analysts said the deal could ultimately accelerate Chinese automakers' push to build vehicles in Europe, even if some manufacturers attempt to frontload exports before any quota system takes effect.
"I would expect this to strengthen ⁠the incentive ​for Chinese automakers to manufacture in Europe," said Bill Russo, founder of Shanghai-based consultancy Automobility.
"If access through imports becomes more ​constrained, investing closer to the customer becomes more attractive. But localisation requires capital...smaller players may reconsider their European ambitions."
Jefferies analysts said the deal signalled "tariff risk off, quota risk on," potentially pushing Chinese automakers towards higher-priced models, increasing pressure on German ​premium brands and accelerating plans to build more vehicles in Europe.

The federal government on Monday decreased the price of petrol by Rs2.93 per litre, while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 61 paisas per litre for October 13.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs395.37 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs396.85 per litre on Tuesday.
The latest revision comes after the government decreased the price of petrol by 66 paisas per litre, while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 52 paisas per litre from October 10 to October 12.
Read: Govt cuts petrol by 66 paisas, increases diesel by 52 paisas till Oct 12
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
Since daily pricing began on July 21, petrol prices had been raised 35 times and cut 22 times, while diesel had seen 34 increases and 23 reductions, leaving consumers grappling with persistent price volatility.
Read More: Fuel costs keep squeezing household budgets
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices were up 2% at near two-week ​highs on Monday as attacks on Saudi Arabia overshadowed the prospect of increased supplies after US President Donald Trump hailed ‌fresh Russian diesel exports and a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire on energy targets.
Rebounding from earlier losses, Brent crude futures were up $2.04, or 2%, to $106.76 a barrel at 11:07 am EDT (1507 GMT), their highest since September 29. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $93.69 a barrel, up $1.84, or 2%.
"The sense of some kind of normality of exports from the Strait of Hormuz was shattered last week. Fresh ​attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia added to this and helped to lift prices," said SEB commodities analyst Bjarne Schieldrop.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
D2C fitness and sportswear brand Boldfit has raised around ₹400 Cr (about $41.8 Mn) from Bharat Value Fund as part of its Series B funding round.
The fund is a Category II AIF managed by The Wealth Company Alternates, part of Pantomath Group.
Boldfit said the investment would support nationwide retail expansion, product innovation, and manufacturing. It also plans to pursue selective acquisitions to strengthen its presence and capabilities across categories.
Founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani, Bengaluru-based Boldfit sells performance sportswear, athletic footwear, sports equipment, and fitness essentials. The startup claims to serve more than 2 Cr customers annually across India.
“We’re building a deeply integrated sports business, investing in product innovation, manufacturing excellence and nationwide retail to create the scale and capabilities required to serve India’s sporting ambitions,” Bihani said.
The retail push builds on plans outlined during its ₹110 Cr funding round from Bessemer Venture Partners in November 2024, when Boldfit said it intended to open offline stores over the following 12-18 months.
Following the latest round, Boldfit’s total funding to date has risen to over ₹510 Cr. The startup also counts cricketer KL Rahul and former tennis player Sania Mirza among its investors.
India’s fitness and sports goods market is estimated to be worth $16 Bn and is projected to reach $35 Bn by FY31, driven by rising disposable incomes, growing health awareness, and wider access through ecommerce, organised retail, and quick commerce channels.
As a result, Indian sportswear and athleisure startups are seeing a lot of investor interest. In June, sportswear startup Agilitas raised ₹225 Cr funding round from Nexus Venture Partners and Rainmatter, with Nexus investing ₹200 Cr and Rainmatter contributing ₹25 Cr.
In January, D2C athleisure brand CAVA announced a ₹40 Cr Series A round led by Sharrp Ventures, with participation from V3 Ventures and existing investor Spring Marketing Capital.

items.title: NVIDIA Dikabarkan Hentikan RTX 5090, Pasokan Chip GB202 Dialihkan ke RTX PRO
items.summary:
NVIDIA dikabarkan menghentikan alokasi chip grafis GB202 untuk GeForce RTX 5090 dan mengalihkan pasokan berikutnya ke lini kartu grafis workstation RTX PRO. Informasi ini berasal dari leaker MEGAsizeGPU melalui X, yang menyebut seluruh pasokan GB202 mendatang akan diprioritaskan untuk produk RTX PRO. Hingga artikel ini ditulis, NVIDIA belum memberikan konfirmasi resmi mengenai kabar tersebut.
GB202 merupakan chip grafis terbesar dalam keluarga Blackwell. Selain digunakan pada RTX 5090, chip ini juga menjadi basis RTX PRO 6000 dengan memori 96 GB dan 24.064 CUDA core, serta RTX PRO 5500 yang memiliki 21.760 CUDA core dan memori 84 GB. Kapasitas memori kedua kartu workstation tersebut jauh lebih besar dibandingkan RTX 5090, sehingga dapat memenuhi kebutuhan profesional yang berbeda dari pasar gaming.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
NVIDIA dikabarkan menghentikan alokasi chip grafis GB202 untuk GeForce RTX 5090 dan mengalihkan pasokan berikutnya ke lini kartu grafis workstation RTX PRO. Informasi ini berasal dari leaker MEGAsizeGPU melalui X, yang menyebut seluruh pasokan GB202 mendatang akan diprioritaskan untuk produk RTX PRO. Hingga artikel ini ditulis, NVIDIA belum memberikan konfirmasi resmi mengenai kabar tersebut.
GB202 merupakan chip grafis terbesar dalam keluarga Blackwell. Selain digunakan pada RTX 5090, chip ini juga menjadi basis RTX PRO 6000 dengan memori 96 GB dan 24.064 CUDA core, serta RTX PRO 5500 yang memiliki 21.760 CUDA core dan memori 84 GB. Kapasitas memori kedua kartu workstation tersebut jauh lebih besar dibandingkan RTX 5090, sehingga dapat memenuhi kebutuhan profesional yang berbeda dari pasar gaming.
All future GB202 supplies are RTX Pro exclusive https://t.co/eZPZW3HdXU— MEGAsizeGPU (@Zed__Wang) October 10, 2026
Kabar penghentian pasokan ini muncul ketika harga RTX 5090 sudah meningkat jauh di atas harga peluncurannya. Kartu tersebut pertama kali dijual pada Januari 2025 dengan harga US$1.999. Pada September 2026, sejumlah listing di Eropa dilaporkan melampaui €5.000, sementara Walmart sempat menjualnya seharga US$4.299 sebelum kehabisan stok. Kondisi ini memunculkan kekhawatiran bahwa pengurangan pasokan dapat semakin menekan ketersediaan kartu tersebut.
Baca Juga: Kingston Pertahankan Posisi Pemasok Modul DRAM Terbesar Dunia
RTX 5090 Berpotensi Berhenti Diproduksi
Leaker lain, hongxing2020, turut mengunggah informasi yang mengklaim NVIDIA akan menghentikan penjualan seluruh model RTX 5090, termasuk varian D untuk pasar China. Unggahan tersebut juga menyebut RTX 5080 24 GB akan menjadi kartu GeForce kelas atas yang diproduksi, sedangkan versi RTX 5080 dengan memori 16 GB akan dihentikan.
Informasi itu mengarah pada kemungkinan hadirnya RTX 5080 SUPER dengan memori GDDR7 24 GB, yang sebelumnya sempat dirumorkan. Namun, belum jelas apakah model yang disebut dalam laporan tersebut memang merupakan RTX 5080 SUPER. Kabar bahwa NVIDIA mengakhiri produksi RTX 5090 juga masih belum terverifikasi, sehingga belum bisa dianggap sebagai keputusan resmi perusahaan.
RTX 5080 24 GB Bisa Jadi Andalan Berikutnya
Jika informasi tersebut benar, pengalihan chip GB202 ke lini RTX PRO kemungkinan berkaitan dengan prioritas produk workstation yang memiliki harga jual lebih tinggi. Namun, alasan tersebut masih berupa dugaan, bukan penjelasan resmi NVIDIA. Stok RTX 5090 yang sudah berada di tangan mitra produsen juga berpotensi tetap beredar untuk sementara waktu sebelum benar-benar habis.
Di sisi lain, RTX 5080 24 GB berpeluang mengisi posisi kartu GeForce teratas apabila RTX 5090 tak lagi diproduksi. Situasi ini dapat menjadi kabar baik bagi pengguna yang membutuhkan kapasitas memori lebih besar, tetapi belum tentu menyelesaikan masalah harga dan ketersediaan. Terlebih, generasi GeForce RTX 60 dikabarkan baru meluncur pada 2028, meski jadwal tersebut juga masih sebatas rumor.

items.content:
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari said on Monday that Punjab Police had not arrested journalist Iqrarul Hassan, adding that investigations into the matter were underway and his family would be informed as soon as verified information about his whereabouts became available.
In a statement posted on X, Bokhari said the police had not taken Hassan into custody and that the matter was being investigated.
پنجاب پولیس نے اقرار الحسن کو گرفتار نہیں کیا،اس معاملے کی تحقیقات کی جا رہی ہیں، ان کے بارے میں جیسے ہی کوئی مصدقہ اطلاعات موصول ہوں گی ان کے اہل خانہ کو آگاہ کر دیا جائے گا۔
— Azma Zahid Bokhari (@AzmaBokhariPMLN) October 12, 2026
Earlier, journalist Iqrarul Hassan’s wife, Farah Iqrar, told The Express Tribune that a group of unidentified individuals posing as officials of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) had allegedly taken him away from their residence in Lahore’s Defence C area.
According to Farah, between five and seven people, including women, arrived at the house late on Sunday night, during the intervening hours of Sunday and Monday, and demanded that Hassan come outside.
She alleged that the individuals threatened to break down the door if he was not handed over. They subsequently entered the house, forcibly took the journalist from a room and took him away.
Farah said she contacted the relevant agency’s office to inquire about her husband’s whereabouts but received no response. She added that an application regarding Hassan’s alleged abduction was submitted to the Defence C police station at around 6am, after which the police issued a diary number.
She further said she later contacted the relevant authorities to register a computerised first information report online but was told that the network was down.
Farah appealed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz to take notice of the incident and ensure her husband’s recovery. She said Hassan had served the country through his journalistic work and exposed various mafias.

items.author: Inc42 Staff
items.content:
For decades, names like Bose, Marshall, Bang & Olufsen and KEF have shaped how the world listens to music. Their dominance was built on one simple premise: better sound came from bigger hardware, larger cabinets, larger drivers and speakers designed to be seen and admired.
But that premise is increasingly getting at odds with how modern spaces are being designed today. Architects and homeowners are favouring clean walls, minimal interiors and technology that fits seamlessly into the room instead of dominating it.
The shift has put one of consumer electronics’ oldest categories in a difficult spot: speakers. Good quality speakers need physical space to deliver the depth, power and clarity that listeners expect. Manufacturers have tried to shrink the hardware, but making it smaller meant compromising on sound quality that made the product desirable in the first place — a trade-off the industry has largely lived with rather than solved.
For Utkarsh Hora, the cofounder of Canadian architectural audio startup XSCACE, audio was part of his family history. His grandfather, Bansi Lal Hora, had worked with Philips in Thailand before returning to India, where he began repairing high-end audio equipment. His father, Manoj Hora, carried that experience forward, building a business around premium audio installations. For Utkarsh, speakers and audio systems were therefore less a hobby than a part of everyday life.
During his time at the University of Toronto, he began wondering whether high-performance audio really needed to take up so much space. The question eventually became the starting point for XSCACE, which Utkarsh founded in 2022. He set out to build speakers that could deliver high-quality sound without taking over a room or compromising its design.
The challenge, however, was rooted in a fundamental constraint of speaker design known as Hoffman’s Iron Law. According to the law, a designer can optimise for only two of three things at once: deep bass, a small enclosure and high efficiency. XSCACE’s challenge was to push the boundaries of that trade-off without compromising the quality of sound.
After two years of development and testing, XSCACE made its first commercial sale in January 2024. Today, the brand has a range of ultra-compact speakers built around six proprietary technologies. It is expanding its distribution across international markets.
 
How XSCACE Is Reinventing The Wheel
When Utkarsh started his entrepreneurial journey, he observed that modern luxury spaces were becoming increasingly minimal. Architects and interior designers wanted clean walls, hidden wiring and fewer visible fixtures.
Speakers, however, remained stubbornly hard to hide. In-wall and in-ceiling speakers existed, but they often came with a compromise. Products that blended into the architecture could fall short on sound, while speakers built for stronger performance typically needed more space.
The fundamental challenge stemmed from a long-standing principle of speaker design known as Hoffman’s Iron Law. It describes the trade-off between a speaker’s size, bass response and efficiency. Improving one typically means giving up something elsewhere.
Rather than accept the rules as they were, the founder began by rethinking what sat at the speaker’s centre: the driver. In a sense, Utkarsh was trying to reinvent the wheel.
Instead of optimising individual components in isolation, XSCACE approached the speaker as one interconnected system. Driver geometry, motor design, cone materials, crossover architecture, cabinet construction and thermal management were developed together, with each element designed to work within the constraints of the others.
“We didn’t eliminate the trade-off altogether but became far more intentional about where it exists,” the founder said.
This paved the way for the foundation of six proprietary technologies, each tackling a different part of the performance equation. These are as follows:
Nano Resonance: To focus on ultra-compact driver performance
PowerDense Dynamics: Extracts higher output from miniature motors
AeroFrame Chassis: Reduces resonance
PrecisionXover Array: Solves for seamless driver integration
XS-Flow: For Airflow and bass response
PsySculpt: Creates a more convincing spatial experience through psychoacoustic tuning
“Among these, Nano Resonance was one of the hardest pieces to develop,” the founder said, adding that the challenge was to get deep bass, high output and low distortion from a miniature driver while maintaining long-term reliability.
From Prototype To Production
A prototype that performs exceptionally in controlled conditions does not automatically translate into a product that can be manufactured consistently. So the next big task was to turn that engineering into a product that could be manufactured consistently without losing performance.
The founder had to revisit parts of the product with manufacturability and repeatability in mind.
“It’s one thing to build a prototype and altogether a different ball game to build the exact same product at scale,” he said.
While spending on simulation, prototyping, testing and refinement across acoustics, mechanical design, materials and manufacturing, the founder had to build a multidisciplinary team and invest in engineering capabilities.
After rigorous experimentation, testing and improving the designs, the founder was finally able to turn its two products, Bonsai and Cane, from early experimental concepts into actual products that were ready to be manufactured and sold.
Bonsai: An ultra-slim, compact speaker that is just 12 mm deep and delivers 40W. It is designed to be mounted discreetly on walls or installed in walls or ceilings.
Cane: A slightly larger 23 mm-thin slim-array speaker with 50W output, designed for spaces where you want more output while keeping the speaker visually unobtrusive.
Building More Than Speakers
Utkarsh’s quest didn’t end with making speakers compact and minimal. From the outset, he saw software as an extension of his product lineup.
“I did not want our products to depend entirely on third-party software,” he said.
Therefore, he started developing an in-house software ecosystem. Today, the brand offers an AI Configurator to help architects, designers and integrators plan and configure audio systems, alongside a companion app for users and the Xylem DSP Controller, which lets installers fine-tune sound based on a room’s acoustics.
Over time, the AI Configurator is expected to become more than a planning tool. Utkarsh sees it evolving into a broader platform that can support installation, calibration, optimisation and ongoing system management. The software strategy also reflects where he wants to take XSCACE as a business.
“Our five-year vision is to establish XSCACE as a global reference in premium architectural audio,” he said, adding that broader plans include expanding beyond loudspeakers into software, DSP, amplification and complementary products, while strengthening its presence in India and expanding across the US, Europe and the Middle East.
For him, growth is not just about revenue or entering more markets. He measures the brand’s progress through its engineering, intellectual property, product consistency and the trust it builds with architects, integrators and customers.
In many ways, that brings XSCACE back to the problem that started it.
The brand did not set out simply to build smaller speakers. It wanted to challenge the assumption that high-performance audio had to remain visible.
Now, as XSCACE moves from compact architectural speakers towards a broader audio ecosystem, the original idea remains at the centre of the brand: build small, think big and make every inch punch above its weight.
