items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Microsoft announced the next generation of its custom AI chip on Monday and said it plans to deploy potentially more than a million of them next year to back its internal AI services.
The Maia 300, ​as the chip is called, is the third generation of the company's custom chips ​designed to handle AI data crunching such as coding and carrying out complex business ⁠tasks on a user's behalf. Its predecessor is already running Microsoft's in-house AI models, as ​well as models from OpenAI delivered on Microsoft's Azure cloud computing service.
The new version comes amid ​a flurry of custom chips from both cloud computing rivals and AI firms such as OpenAI aimed at loosening the hold of Nvidia on the AI computing market.
To construct the chip, Microsoft took a different technical path from Nvidia ​whose AI accelerators use one massive computing chip surrounded by high-bandwidth memory chips.
The central computing processor ​in Microsoft's Maia 300 silicon is composed of "chiplets" — typically specialized chips bonded together — that use 2-nanometer technology from Taiwan Semiconductor ‌Manufacturing ⁠Co for key computing functions.
Read More: Microsoft president says milk faces more regulation than AI
Other chiplets included in the design use cheaper 3-nanometer tech for functions such as moving data off the processor and elsewhere inside the system.
The Maia 300 processors will go into racks that contain 96 chips and use about 167 kilowatts of power, compared with the ​142 kilowatts used by Nvidia's ​most recent GB300 ⁠AI server racks with 72 of its graphics processing units (GPUs).
Microsoft said the Maia 300 chips will get about 40% more useful computing done per ​megawatt than "leading GPU-based systems," though it did not name the systems it ​used for ⁠a comparison.
"It's basically delivering more intelligence for every watt, every dollar, and every byte of memory by optimizing across the entire system," Rani Borkar, president of Azure hardware systems and infrastructure at Microsoft, ⁠told Reuters ​in an interview.
Microsoft said it plans to roll out "multi-gigawatt deployments" ​of the Maia 300 chip starting next year. Microsoft has said it expects to spend more than $175 billion in capital expenditures ​this calendar year.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Belakangan ini, ArtCraft, perusahaan pengembang software asal Atlanta, Georgia, AS mencuri perhatian banyak pengguna PC dan Mac dengan meluncurkan sejumlah aplikasi gratis menyerupai fungsi Adobe.
Tak ingin berhenti di Adobe, perusahaan yang dibentuk dirikan oleh Brandon Thomas ini sudah memperluas proyek software gratisnya tersebut dengan memperkenalkan aplikasi alternatif untuk Microsoft Office.
Baca Juga: OPPO Reno X Dirumorkan Usung Layar 16:9, Lebar Bodi Capai 85 mm
Adapun aplikasi tersebut adalah WordCraft, GridCraft, dan DeckCraft, di mana masing-masing software menawarkan alternatif untuk Microsoft Word, Excel, dan PowerPoint, sebagaimana dikutip dari Tom’s Hardware, Senin (12/10/2026).
Saat ini, ketiga aplikasi tersebut sudah tersedia sebagai proyek open-source melalui GitHub dan dirancang untuk berjalan di Windows, macOS, serta Linux. 
ArtCraft menawarkan pengalaman penggunaan familier bagi pengguna Office, meski kemampuan aplikasinya belum sepenuhnya setara dengan software milik Microsoft tersebut.
ArtCraft Juga Buat Alternatif Adobe
ArtCraft menjadi sorotan pengguna PC dan Mac lewat sejumlah aplikasi gratis menyerupai software kreatif Adobe, yang masing-masing adalah PhotoCraft sebagai alternatif Photoshop, VectorCraft untuk Illustrator, dan FilmCraft yang dikembangkan dengan pendekatan serupa Premiere Pro.
Tak hanya itu, perusahaan juga mengambangkan LightCraft yang berfungsi sebagai software pengolah foto seperti Lightroom, EffectCraft untuk motion graphics, serta DesignCraft untuk pekerjaan tata letak publikasi.
ArtCraft menyebut pendekatan pengembangannya sebagai clean-room reimplementation, yakni membangun kembali fungsi software berdasarkan spesifikasi publik dan pengamatan, tanpa menyalin kode sumber aplikasi aslinya.
Proyek ini juga menggunakan lisensi open-source MIT atau Apache 2.0. Dengan demikian, kode sumbernya dapat diperiksa dan dikembangkan lebih lanjut sesuai ketentuan lisensi.
Masih Tahap Alpha, Belum Siap Gantikan Microsoft Office
WordCraft, alternatif Microsoft Word gratif buatan ArtCraft. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson)
ArtCraft sendiri mengakui WordCraft, GridCraft, dan DeckCraft masih berada dalam tahap alpha. Pengembang terus menambahkan fitur sekaligus memperbaiki stabilitas dan kompatibilitas file.
Berdasarkan dokumentasi proyeknya, WordCraft baru mencapai sekitar 60 persen kesiapan untuk menggantikan seluruh kebutuhan Microsoft Word dalam pekerjaan nyata. Sedangkan GridCraft diperkirakan berada di kisaran 50 persen, sementara DeckCraft sekitar 55 persen.
Salah satu tantangan terbesarnya adalah kompatibilitas file. Dokumen Word, spreadsheet Excel, dan presentasi PowerPoint tidak selalu berisi teks atau angka sederhana. Ada berbagai elemen seperti grafik, objek tertanam, formula, animasi, dan pengaturan layout yang perlu dipertahankan saat file dibuka atau disimpan melalui aplikasi lain.
Dalam pengujian awal dilaporkan The Register, WordCraft dapat dijalankan pada perangkat Microsoft Surface berbasis Arm dan memberikan kesan awal baik. Namun, media tersebut tetap menyarankan agar aplikasi itu belum digunakan untuk pekerjaan produksi.
Dikembangkan dengan Bantuan AI Claude
Hal menarik dari ArtCraft adalah penggunaan AI dalam proses pengembangan software. Proyek ini memanfaatkan Claude untuk membantu pekerjaan pemrograman, sehingga pengembangan berbagai aplikasi dengan fungsi berbeda dapat dilakukan secara lebih cepat.
Pendekatan tersebut memperlihatkan bagaimana AI coding tools membuka peluang bagi pengembang independen untuk membangun software yang sebelumnya membutuhkan sumber daya lebih besar.
Namun, kecepatan menulis kode tidak otomatis menghasilkan aplikasi matang. Software produktivitas membutuhkan pengujian menyeluruh, termasuk kompatibilitas dokumen, stabilitas, performa, dan penanganan kesalahan saat digunakan.
ArtCraft juga bukan satu-satunya penyedia alternatif Microsoft Office gratis. Sebelumnya, pengguna juga sudah memiliki pilihan seperti LibreOffice dan ONLYOFFICE yang lebih lama dikembangkan.
Saat ini, WordCraft, GridCraft, dan DeckCraft lebih tepat dilihat sebagai proyek open-source yang menarik untuk diikuti atau dicoba, terutama bagi pengguna yang ingin bereksperimen dengan alternatif software berbayar.
Ketiganya bisa diakses melalui repositori resmi ArtCraft di GitHub. Namun, pengguna sebaiknya tetap membuat salinan cadangan dokumen sebelum mencoba aplikasi tersebut untuk membuka atau mengedit file penting.
Adobe Resmi Integrasikan Photoshop, Express, dan Acrobat ke ChatGPT
Di sisi lain, Adobe mengumumkan bahwa Photoshop, Express, dan Acrobat kini bisa digunakan langsung di dalam ChatGPT. Alih-alih membuka aplikasi terpisah, pengguna cukup memberi instruksi melalui percakapan, lalu ChatGPT akan mengeksekusi tugas tersebut menggunakan alat resmi Adobe. Pendekatan ini membuka peluang baru bagi pengguna kasual maupun profesional yang ingin mempercepat alur kerja kreatif tanpa berpindah aplikasi.
Fitur ini dihadirkan secara native, artinya pengguna bisa langsung meminta ChatGPT mengedit foto, membuat desain visual, atau memodifikasi PDF hanya dengan memberikan perintah bahasa natural. Adobe dan OpenAI mengklaim bahwa integrasi ini tetap mempertahankan kualitas output dari masing-masing produk Adobe, sehingga tidak sekadar menjadi shortcut, tetapi benar-benar menghadirkan kemampuan penuh dalam format percakapan.
Meski menjanjikan efisiensi tinggi, integrasi ini tetap menyisakan beberapa pertanyaan. Salah satunya soal batasan kemampuan dibandingkan aplikasi penuh, khususnya bagi desainer profesional yang selama ini bergantung pada kontrol granular. Selain itu, isu privasi dan keamanan dokumen juga akan menjadi sorotan mengingat file diproses dalam lingkungan AI yang terhubung ke cloud.

items.title: Jepang Tetapkan Status Darurat Siber, Serangan ke Perusahaan Kian Meluas
items.summary:
Jepang menetapkan situasi keamanan sibernya sebagai kondisi darurat setelah serangkaian serangan digital menargetkan perusahaan-perusahaan besar dalam beberapa pekan terakhir. Lebih dari 20 perusahaan dilaporkan terdampak, termasuk jaringan minimarket Lawson dan operator penyewaan mobil Times Car. Serangan tersebut memicu kekhawatiran karena menyebabkan kebocoran data pelanggan dalam jumlah besar.
Salah satu insiden yang mencuat melibatkan JR East, operator kereta api terbesar di Jepang. Sistem pemesanan perusahaan tersebut dilaporkan mengalami kebocoran sekitar 1,67 juta alamat email pelanggan. Secara keseluruhan, berbagai insiden yang terjadi disebut telah mengakibatkan hilangnya puluhan juta data pelanggan, meskipun rincian dampak dari setiap serangan berbeda-beda.
Menteri Keamanan Siber Jepang, Toshiharu Furukawa, menyebut situasi tersebut “sangat kritis” dalam pertemuan di National Cybersecurity Strategy Headquarters (NCSH). Sementara itu, Masaaki Taira, kepala NCSH, menggambarkan

Sistem pemesanan perusahaan tersebut dilaporkan mengalami kebocoran sekitar 1,67 juta alamat email pelanggan. Secara keseluruhan, berbagai insiden yang terjadi disebut telah mengakibatkan hilangnya puluhan juta data pelanggan, meskipun rincian dampak dari setiap serangan berbeda-beda.
Menteri Keamanan Siber Jepang, Toshiharu Furukawa, menyebut situasi tersebut “sangat kritis” dalam pertemuan di National Cybersecurity Strategy Headquarters (NCSH). Sementara itu, Masaaki Taira, kepala NCSH, menggambarkan kondisi tersebut sebagai keadaan darurat di dunia maya. Sejumlah pakar keamanan siber menilai perkembangan teknologi AI berpotensi ikut memperbesar ancaman, meski belum ada konfirmasi bahwa seluruh serangan terbaru menggunakan AI.
Baca Juga: CEO Microsoft Satya Nadella Ingin Model AI Punya Rem Darurat, Mengapa?
AI Diduga Mempermudah Serangan Siber
Masaki Hiraoka, direktur pelaksana Blackpanda untuk kawasan Asia Timur Laut, mengatakan kepada Financial Times Bahwa AI dapat membantu pelaku kejahatan siber melakukan serangan yang sebelumnya membutuhkan penyelidikan panjang. Teknologi ini berpotensi mempercepat proses pencarian target dan persiapan serangan, termasuk terhadap perusahaan yang sebelumnya dianggap kurang menarik bagi peretas.
Menurut Hiraoka, layanan berskala lebih kecil kini berpotensi menjadi sasaran karena hambatan untuk melancarkan serangan semakin rendah. Namun, dugaan pemanfaatan AI dalam serangkaian insiden tersebut belum membuktikan bahwa teknologi itu menjadi penyebab langsung kebocoran data yang terjadi.
Nobuo Miwa, presiden perusahaan keamanan siber asal Tokyo, S&J Corp, menggambarkan pola serangan terbaru seperti “pengeboman karpet” atau serangan yang dilakukan secara luas terhadap banyak target. Dalam pernyataannya kepada Reuters, Miwa juga menilai AI dapat membantu peretas asing mengatasi hambatan bahasa saat menargetkan perusahaan Jepang.
Insiden Siber Jepang Melampaui Catatan Tahun Lalu
Data TrendAI yang dibagikan kepada Reuters menunjukkan bahwa jumlah insiden keamanan siber di Jepang selama sembilan bulan pertama 2026 telah melampaui total sepanjang 2025. Angka tersebut mengindikasikan bahwa ancaman siber terus meningkat dan tidak hanya terbatas pada satu atau dua perusahaan.
Meski AI berpotensi membuat serangan lebih mudah dilakukan, penyebab setiap insiden tetap perlu ditelusuri secara terpisah. Bagi perusahaan, situasi ini menegaskan pentingnya perlindungan data dan kesiapan menghadapi serangan, sementara kaitan langsung antara AI dan gelombang serangan terbaru masih membutuhkan bukti lebih lanjut.

items.title: The cyber-fueled cult of Ibrahim Traoré
items.author: Olatunji Olaigbe
items.content:
Thomas Sankara had a signature look: a natty red beret, worn with military fatigues. A striking figure, Sankara was a military officer and the radical, anti-imperialist prime minister of the Republic of Upper Volta. His arrest in 1983 led to demonstrations, followed by a coup, after which Sankara was released and installed as president. By the following year Sankara had given the country he now led its new name — Burkina Faso. He fashioned a Burkinabè identity in his own anti-imperialist image, eschewing French for local languages, promoting economic self-reliance and national pride. 
In 1986, he famously took the then French president François Mitterrand to task in a fiery speech broadcast both in Burkina Faso and France. Sankara’s dashing uniform played an outsized role in how his words were interpreted. Here was Africa’s own Che Guevara. But by October 1987, Sankara was dead, killed during a military coup led by his former friend and ally Blaise Compaoré.
France, the old colonial power, backed Compaoré. Soon after the coup, French officials once again flocked to Ouagadougou, helping to prop up Compaoré for decades. 
Burkinabè children wearing false kepis during the military parade in Ouagadougou to commemorate the second anniversary of the revolution of the Burkina Faso. August 4, 1985. Daniel LAINE / AFP via Getty Images.
This potted history is important to understanding the phenomenon of Ibrahim Traoré, Burkina Faso’s current president, an authoritarian head of state who in his charisma and self-presentation so deliberately echoes Sankara.
On September 30, thousands of Burkinabè gathered in Ouagadougou’s Place de la Révolution to hail Traoré on the fourth anniversary of the coup that brought him to power. As the second coming of Sankara, Traoré — whatever their entirely different political ideologies – is arguably the face of contemporary African anti-imperialism. It is a meticulously cultivated image that has almost nothing to do with Traoré’s actual record, or his achievements in Burkina Faso. 
Traoré is a pan-African leader for a digital age, an autocrat who has suspended his country’s constitution, dismantled its admittedly fledgling democratic institutions and been accused of crimes against humanity, but who has used artificial intelligence, particularly deepfakes, to bury that record beneath a highly effective cyber cult of personality.
How do Burkinabè reconcile the man with the persona? And is Traoré a triumph of the algorithm, the kind of politician increasingly familiar from Ouagadougou to Delhi, Berlin, Buenos Aires, and of course Washington, DC?
Left: Burkina Faso President Thomas Sankara during a speech on October 5, 1983, in Paris, France. Alain MINGAM/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images. Right: New coup leader Captain Ibrahim Traoré at a news conference on October 2, 2022 in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. Stringer/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images.
The man, the myth, the algorithm 
Ibrahim Traoré came to power in September 2022. In his own telling, while Sankara was installed as president, Traoré led the putsch himself. By January 2023, Burkina Faso terminated its military accord with France, giving French special forces one month to leave the country. In June this year, Burkina Faso ended all diplomatic relations with France. 
As Traoré turned away from France, he strengthened relations with Moscow. It’s in keeping with the pattern across the countries of the Sahel — Burkina Faso and its neighbours Mali and Niger — as the region’s colonial history with France has been swept clean by a broom held first by the mercenaries of the Wagner Group and latterly the Russian state itself, represented by the Africa Corps. 
But in April and May 2026, Africa Corps forces were dealt a humiliating defeat in northern Mali by a combination of Tuareg separatists and allegedly Al-Qaeda linked Islamists. The Malian defence minister was assassinated in a suicide bombing at his home near the capital Bamako. With Russia so involved militarily in the Sahel countries, Ukraine has admitted to assisting rebel forces. Both Mali and Niger have cut diplomatic ties with Kyiv. And Burkina Faso has described Kyiv as a destabilising force in the region, making the Sahel effectively a front in Russia’s war with Ukraine. As recently as September, Traoré named Ukraine as a part of Burkina Faso’s “map of enemies” for which, he added menacingly, “we need to prepare.”
Russia, as Coda Story has reported for years, has used everything from weapons sales to mercenaries to paying African influencers to both spread Russian narratives and hold Moscow up as the alternative to continuing to rely on exploitative economic relationships with the West, particularly erstwhile European colonialists.
Despite the extent of Russian attempts to influence the Sahel, it’s not Moscow that is signing the most consequential deals with the military juntas it helps prop up. It’s Beijing. And the deals being signed with China to mine the region’s extensive mineral wealth — the lithium, gold, copper, zinc, bauxite and uranium — have served as a reminder to the United States that it too should resume stalled relationships in the Sahel. Early in 2026, Burkina Faso signed a near $150 million healthcare deal with the U.S. in exchange, it appeared, for favourable access to minerals. Both Zambia and Zimbabwe backed away from similar deals, expressing concern about U.S. demands for data and minerals that amounted to an infringement of sovereignty. 
Burkina Faso's President Ibrahim Traoré arrives in Moscow, Russia on May 8, 2025. Grigory Sysoev / RIA Novosti/Anadolu via Getty Images.
The deals with China and the United States are being negotiated alongside a drive to reduce reliance on foreign loans and grants and ramp up domestic production, particularly of gold. Traoré claims his economic policies emphasise nationalisation and self-reliance. His government has taken over major mining operations and increased state stakes in other industries. In early 2024, his administration suspended export permits for small-scale gold production to crack down on smuggling and keep mineral wealth inside the country. Last month, he inaugurated Burkina Faso’s first gold refinery. 
Some of this has had positive economic effects. The World Bank, in a June 2026 update, said the country had an estimated 5.3% growth in 2025, up from 4.8% in 2024, and its fiscal deficit narrowed from 5.8% of GDP to 1.8%. Inflation was also negative, 0.5%, compared to 4.2% in 2024. Reports by the World Bank and IMF have ascribed these growth to external factors such as the gold rally, climate-driven increase in agricultural outputs, and reduction in energy prices. 
Economic growth, though, is part of a larger story that includes a crackdown on the press, particularly critical coverage of alleged human rights violations. Human Rights Watch documented 1,840 civilian deaths between January 2023 and April 2025, over 1,200 of which were directly attributed to government forces. Even as the report acknowledged widespread violations by Islamist groups, the actions of the Burkina Faso military, it said, “amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity.” At the same time, Traoré has clamped down on Burkinabè civil society, banning over 100 human rights organizations and dissolving all political parties.
None of it appears to have affected his carefully-honed image in certain online spaces.
Street of Ouagadougou shows a poster celebrating former President Thomas Sankara, known as "Africa's Che Guevara" and the portrait of the Argentine-born guerrilla leader Ernesto Che Guevara. Ahmed Ouobaa/AFP via Getty Images.
Streets of Accra, Ghana, May 9, 2026. Olatunji Olaigbe.
A graffiti portrait of the president of Burkina Faso Ibrahim Traoré. Boniface Muthoni/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images.
A pan-African hero 
Traoré is everywhere. In Accra, the capital of Ghana, his image is pasted onto buses and in parks. In January 2025, at the swearing-in of the Ghanaian president John Mahama, it was Traoré who the crowd responded to, cheering for a rockstar rather than a head of state. Even Mahama joked that Traoré had stolen the show. Artwork celebrating Traoré is frequently posted online. The commentary that accompanies the art is gushing. “Through this artwork,” reads one Facebook tribute, “I celebrate the spirit of a man who stands for sovereignty, truth, and the rise of a self-determined Africa.”
Meanwhile, the Ivory Coast government has granted refugee status to at least 69,000 Burkinabè fleeing Burkina Faso.
In May, when I travelled to Ghana and Ivory Coast to talk to people displaced from Burkina Faso, at least five sources decided they no longer wanted to speak. Guaranteeing anonymity didn’t seem to matter. A Burkinabè journalist who was helping me find people to speak to, stopped responding to my messages the day after I arrived in Accra. Those who did speak to me refused to be quoted for fear that harm would come to family and friends left behind in Burkina Faso.
Reporters have been intimidated into silence. “Today, any journalist living in the country is forced to practice self-censorship to avoid being arrested,” says Harouna Simbo Drabo, disinformation analyst and Director of Programs & Partnerships of Faso Check. “Burkinabé journalists have two options,” he told me, “either practice self-censorship or go into exile.” After threats to his life, Drabo has left Burkina Faso.
He’s one of the luckier journalists. Since 2022, at least seven Burkinabè reporters have been forcibly conscripted into the army after criticizing the Traoré junta's crackdown on the press. Guezouma Sanogo, Boukari Ouoba, and Luc Pagbelguem were abducted days after their union denounced state media as "instruments of propaganda." Atiana Serge Oulon, editor-in-chief of L'Événement, is among the disappeared. Many, like Drabo, have either left Burkina Faso or quit their jobs. 
As conditions deteriorate, what information is becoming available is government propaganda amplified by social media linked to Russian misinformation. In the absence of accurate, verified information, there is inevitably only disinformation. For instance, one of the most persistent pieces of disinformation is the story that Traoré — a supposedly avowed anti-imperialist despite his kowtowing to Moscow, Beijing and Washington — rejected billions of dollars in International Monetary Fund handouts because he believes, à la Thomas Sankara, in economic self-reliance. It is a story that has been debunked but was repeatedly told to me by Traoré supporters, including at least one journalist.
The claim was cited more than 700 times in a single three-day window in January 2025 alone, racking up millions of views across Facebook, X, and TikTok. Dubawa fact-checked the story and found that rather than rejecting money from the IMF, the Burkina Faso government had negotiated a 48-month IMF loan program in September 2023 and drew on World Bank financing in 2024. 
By mid-2025. Code for Africa's analysis found social media in sub-Saharan Africa flooded with AI-generated videos casting Traoré alongside Beyoncé, Rihanna, and, in one particularly unhinged iteration, Pope Leo XIV, all of whom supposedly endorsed him as a Pan-African hero holding the line against the West. After US AFRICOM commander Michael Langley criticized Traoré's handling of Burkina Faso’s gold reserves in a Senate hearing, a network of 165 Facebook accounts began posting identical language claiming Putin had deployed special forces to protect Traoré from an American assasination plot. In ten days it pulled 10.9 million views. 
In Accra, I caught a bus with a picture of Traoré emblazoned on the side. The driver, who only identified himself as Kofi, insisted that before we spoke I should tell him what I thought of Traoré. I say I am not Burkinabè, that I have not visited Burkina Faso but that I have spoken to many people whose lives have been upended by Traoré’s strongman politics. I told him about Burkinabè journalists in exile, forced to join the army, or even disappeared. I told him that when asked about a transition to democracy, Traoré said it was important for Burkinabè to “forget” about democracy. “We have to tell the truth,” Traoré said, “democracy isn’t for us.” I told him about the Burkinabè refugees I met in Treichville, a district in Abidjan, the Ivory Coast capital.
Kofi listened and then told me that “good things take sacrifice,” including the death of a free press. When I asked what he meant by good things, he showed me AI-generated videos of a smart city Traoré had supposedly built.
African identity is tightly wound around the belief that the continent has more potential than it has achieved. The deficit can be attributed to a lot of issues, but chiefly to Western exploitation and the complicity of African leaders. “African countries have also fallen into autocratic democracy,” Sanusi Sanusi, Research Analyst at the Digital Tech, AI & Information Disorder Analysis Centre, DAIDAC, tells me. “There is an election every couple of years but it isn't free or fair.”
Supporters of Traoré wave Burkina Faso and Russian flags during a rally at Place de la Nation Ouagadougou on April 30, 2025. AFP via Getty Images.
Neil Postman, in Amusing Ourselves to Death, writes that “disinformation does not mean false information. It means misleading information — misplaced, irrelevant, fragmented or superficial information — information that creates the illusion of knowing something but which in fact leads one away from knowing.”
Many Traoré supporters I spoke with, most of whom were men, were convinced they knew things I did not. They told me to educate myself more on Western hypocrisy in Africa. They said they did not have faith in those who appointed themselves arbiters of what was fact and what was disinformation. In Lagos I met Lemi Ghariokwu, who designed album covers for the iconic Nigerian musician Fela Kuti, a revolutionary figure. Ghariokwu, who has a portrait of Ibrahim Traoré hanging in his studio, told me that “Western education and propaganda has made our elite class toothless bulldogs.” Listening to them, it seemed as if a successful Africa needed strongmen, needed autocrats.
In Abidjan, the last person I spoke to about Traoré was Oumar, a Burkinabè taxi driver who had moved to the Ivorian capital in 2021. He told me he “supports Traoré with all my heart.” But as we talked, he admitted he had not been back home because “things are only getting worse.” Three Burkinabè refugees I spoke to told me they thought I might be a government agent planted among them to find out what they really thought about Traoré and that I would then report those thoughts back to Ouagadougou.
Many of the Traoré supporters I spoke with thought I was brainwashed by Western media or, worse, too docile to participate in an African revolution. For my part, I thought they were ill-informed and unable or, worse, unwilling to see through propaganda.
The fundamental curse of the age of information and connection is that we rarely confront how the mediums meant to unite us have fractured us. An unprecedented flood of data has shattered shared reality into millions of customized, mutually hostile subcultures.
With the help of AI and social media, Traoré has managed to decouple national and anti-imperial pride from government performance. By the middle of next year, Burkina Faso will no longer be part of the International Criminal Court, denounced by Traoré as an “instrument of neocolonial oppression”, and thus no longer accountable in any international forum. His government has said it is “decolonizing” the school curriculum. Cheered on by social media, Traoré has used anti-imperial grievances and resentments to argue that authoritarian military rule is the only safeguard for sovereignty.
As some Burkinabè exiles told me ironically, they thought both I, so sceptical of Traoré, and the Traoré die-hards in the African diaspora could use a few months living in Burkina Faso. We should, they said, experience the country Traoré has made IRL. See past the carefully curated myth of the man himself, the largely online fantasy of the pan-African, anti-imperial revolutionary who needs to break a few eggs to make the omelet, and assess the country he runs unchallenged.

The visit comes in the backdrop of the Moscow Format's eighth meeting held on October 5, which brought together senior representatives from Russia, Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Iran, India and Central Asian states to discuss Afghanistan's political, security and economic situation, including counterterrorism and regional connectivity.
Russia's special presidential envoy for Afghanistan, Zamir Kabulov, confirmed that the dispute between the Pakistani and Afghan delegations prevented the participants from adopting the final document.
The failure to forge a regional consensus was accompanied by unusually strong Russian support for the Taliban government. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, who opened the meeting, praised the Taliban's performance since its return to power in 2021 and described it as a "national government".
Read More: Pakistan, Taliban clash at Moscow talks
Russia has already gone further than other major powers in its engagement with Kabul. Moscow formally recognised the Taliban administration in 2025, making it the first country to do so.
The Russian position at the Moscow meeting therefore stood in marked contrast to Pakistan's emphasis on the Taliban's links with terrorist groups operating against Pakistan.
On August 18, Deputy Prime Minister (DPM) and Foreign Minister (FM) Ishaq Dar met with Russian Ambassador to Pakistan Albert Khorev in Islamabad and welcomed the positive momentum in Islamabad-Moscow relations.
On June 9, Energy Minister Awais Ahmed Khan Leghari confirmed that Pakistan and Russia had agreed to sign an Economic Cooperation Programme extending through 2030. Leghari also stated that a recently signed “readmission agreement” was expected to facilitate improved visa arrangements and strengthen people-to-people contacts.

items.title: Vivo X500 E Surfaces on Bluetooth SIG, Google Play Console Ahead of Anticipated Launch
items.summary: Vivo’s upcoming X500 E smartphone has surfaced on two certification platforms, with its Google Play Console listing revealing the model number V2656 and device code V2648. The latter matches the Vivo V80 5G, fuelling speculation that the two phones could share a hardware platform. Bluetooth SIG has also listed the X500 E under the same model number but has not disclosed its specifications. Rumours point to a Dimensity 9500 chipset, a 64-megapixel periscope camera and a 7,500mAh battery.

items.title: Info ministry rejects social media claims of unrest in K-P as misleading
items.summary:
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MoIB) on Monday rejected misleading claims of unrest in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), accusing social media accounts of circulating AI-generated visuals, old footage and unrelated videos to portray a situation of chaos in the province.
In a fact-check posted on X, the ministry shared examples of previously circulated material that it said was being misrepresented as evidence of unrest in K-P.
The ministry said accounts linked to the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) were sharing “AI-generated visuals, old footage and unrelated videos” as evidence of conflict in the province.
“The circulated material includes factory fires, protests over load shedding and footage from Syria, etc; all mis-captioned to manufacture an impression of chaos,” it added.
The ministry also stated that Afghan and Indian social media accounts were amplifying the claims alongside accounts associated with domestic political interests.

President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday signed off on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's recommendation of imposing emergency rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) amid a deteriorating security situation and the provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism. The move was supported by Articles 232 (Proclamation of emergency on account of war, internal disturbance, etc) and 234 (Power to issue Proclamation in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a Province) of the Constitution of Pakistan.
The move came forth as PTI pushed the federal government to give into its demands that included to press for the release of party founder Imran Khan, accelerate hearings in cases against him and his wife Bushra Bibi, address concerns over his medical treatment and seek an end to restrictions on meetings with him.
The party initially planned to launch the march on September 27, but on September 26 CM Afridi rescheduled the protest to take place on October 4, amid extensive security and traffic restrictions and continuing efforts to negotiate with the federal government. items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
OPPO dikabarkan tengah mengembangkan smartphone flagship dengan desain layar lebar yang berbeda dari kebanyakan ponsel modern. Perangkat yang dirumorkan bernama OPPO Reno X ini kembali menjadi sorotan setelah tipster Digital Chat Station membagikan informasi terbaru mengenai rasio layar dan dimensi bodinya. Jika rumor tersebut akurat, OPPO berpotensi menghadirkan pendekatan desain yang mengutamakan layar lebih lebar dibandingkan smartphone pada umumnya.
Digital Chat Station menyebut OPPO Reno X akan menggunakan layar dengan rasio aspek 16:9. Rasio ini dahulu cukup umum digunakan pada smartphone, tetapi kini sebagian besar perangkat beralih ke layar memanjang dengan rasio sekitar 19,5:9 atau 20:9. Perubahan tersebut membuat desain ponsel modern lebih mudah digenggam secara vertikal, meski pengalaman saat menikmati konten tertentu bisa berbeda.
Bocoran terbaru juga menyebut bezel di keempat sisi layar memiliki ketebalan sekitar 1 mm. Lebar area layar diperkirakan mencapai 81 mm, sedangkan keseluruhan bodi ponsel berada di kisaran 85 mm. Ukuran tersebut mengindikasikan Reno X akan memiliki bentuk yang relatif lebar dibandingkan smartphone konvensional, tetapi spesifikasi ini masih sebatas informasi dari tipster dan belum dikonfirmasi OPPO.
Baca Juga: Oppo A7 Pro dan A7 Pro Max Resmi di Indonesia, Apa Bedanya Selain Baterai?
Layar 16:9 dan Dimensi Lebar Jadi Pembeda
Dalam bocoran sebelumnya, Digital Chat Station sempat menyebut perangkat ini akan memakai layar berukuran 6,3 hingga 6,4 inci dengan rasio 16:10. Namun, informasi terbaru mengarah pada kemungkinan penggunaan layar 6,5 inci dengan rasio 16:9. Perbedaan informasi tersebut menunjukkan bahwa spesifikasi perangkat masih dapat berubah selama proses pengembangan.
Layar dengan rasio lebih lebar berpotensi memberikan pengalaman berbeda saat menonton video atau menggunakan aplikasi tertentu. Namun, ukuran bodi yang mencapai sekitar 85 mm juga dapat membuat ponsel lebih sulit digenggam dengan satu tangan, terutama bagi pengguna dengan tangan kecil. Karena itu, desain ini belum tentu lebih praktis dibandingkan bentuk smartphone yang lebih memanjang.
OPPO Reno X Dibandingkan Huawei Pura X View
Sebagai pembanding, Huawei Pura X View saat ini disebut sebagai satu-satunya smartphone non-lipat dengan desain layar lebar di pasaran. Perangkat tersebut menggunakan rasio layar 5:3 dan memiliki lebar bodi sekitar 87 mm. Berdasarkan angka yang beredar, OPPO Reno X berpotensi memiliki bodi sedikit lebih sempit, tetapi dengan bentuk yang berbeda.
Meski begitu, belum tersedia informasi lengkap mengenai spesifikasi lain OPPO Reno X, termasuk chipset, kamera, kapasitas baterai, harga, maupun jadwal peluncurannya. Sampai OPPO memberikan konfirmasi resmi, rasio layar dan dimensi perangkat ini masih perlu dipandang sebagai rumor. Kehadirannya tetap menarik untuk dinantikan, terutama jika Oppo benar-benar ingin menawarkan alternatif dari desain smartphone yang semakin memanjang.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Hero Electronix-owned Tessolve Semiconductor raised $75 Mn (₹718 Cr) in a funding round led by Vector Line Capital, with additional participation from existing backers TPG and Novo Tellus Capital Partners.
The fresh capital will support acquisitions that complement its existing capabilities, broaden its service offerings and strengthen its international business.
The company is already in advanced discussions to close multiple acquisitions over the next couple of quarters. It last acquired Germany’s Dream Chip Technologies GmbH (DCT) in a ₹400 Cr deal back in November 2024.
“This investment will support acquisitions that further strengthen our offerings, and Vector Line’s focus on the sector and their relationships will add significant value,” Tessolve cofounder and chief executive Srini Chinamilli said.
Founded in 2004 by Chinamilli, P Raja Manickam and Veerappan V, Tessolve provides end-to-end semiconductor engineering services, spanning chip architecture and design, validation, testing and embedded systems.
The company is designing AI and HPC chips by leveraging its in-house pre-engineered semiconductor platforms and design flows to shorten development cycles, alongside a global lab infrastructure and partnerships with leading foundries, IP, EDA and test equipment companies.
Tessolve claims to have worked with leading hyperscalers and 18 of the world’s top 20 semiconductor companies.
Hero Electronix, the electronics and tech arm of Hero Group, acquired a controlling stake in the semiconductor company in 2016, with plans to complete a phased acquisition of a significant majority holding by the end of that year.
“Two decades ago we started with silicon test engineering. Today we are designing and productising complete chips for the companies building AI infrastructure,” Chinamilli said.
Tessolve last raised $150 Mn in a fresh round in 2025, led by TPG Growth. With the latest infusion, the startup’s cumulative funding stands at $265 Mn.
The development comes amid broader momentum in India’s deeptech sector, where semiconductor and chip design startups have drawn rising investor interest.
This increasing investor interest is also supported by the government’s ₹1.25 Lakh Cr India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, which was launched with an aim to build the country’s chip design and manufacturing ecosystem.
Some examples of this include AI-native semiconductor verification startup VerifAIX’s $5 Mn seed funding round in September, HrdWyr $13 Mn Series A funding round, among others.
Broader investor interest for advanced hardware and tech startups in India, which includes robotics, semiconductors and aerial vehicles, rose 176% YoY to $290 Mn, as per Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan could generate between $60 billion and $80 billion in economic benefits over the next five years through digital transformation, according to a briefing presented by the Pakistan Digital Authority (PDA) to the National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunication.
The projections highlight the potential of digital technologies to improve economic productivity, attract investment, and strengthen public service delivery. However, the authority has warned that disconnected government systems and weak coordination between institutions remain significant obstacles.
According to the PDA’s assessment, digital transformation could generate more than $9 billion in economic benefits for agriculture by 2030, while digital reforms in healthcare could deliver savings exceeding $450 million.
The real estate sector could attract an additional $15 billion in investment through digitalisation, while small and medium-sized enterprises, commerce, and retail could generate an estimated $6 billion in additional revenue.
Over 100 Digital Platforms, but Integration Remains a Challenge
Pakistan has already established more than 100 digital platforms across different government departments and public services. However, many of these systems operate independently, limiting their ability to exchange information and provide integrated services to citizens.
The PDA has proposed a comprehensive National Digital Masterplan to address these challenges and develop a coordinated digital framework across federal and provincial governments.
Under the proposed framework, the Pakistan Digital Stack would connect digital identity, payment systems, and secure data-sharing infrastructure, allowing government institutions to exchange information more efficiently.
The authority also plans to establish common digital standards, strengthen data governance, and improve oversight of artificial intelligence applications.
The initiative is consistent with the government’s broader Digital Nation Pakistan program, which focuses on modernizing public services, strengthening digital infrastructure, and expanding the digital economy.
Can Pakistan Achieve the $80 Billion Target?
While the projected benefits are substantial, achieving them will depend on effective implementation, institutional coordination, and the integration of existing digital platforms.
The government will need to address administrative inefficiencies, eliminate duplication between departments, and ensure secure data-sharing mechanisms across federal and provincial institutions.
The PDA’s proposed framework seeks to improve these areas while supporting digital investment and technology adoption in key economic sectors.
Importantly, the $60 billion to $80 billion figure represents projected economic benefits rather than confirmed investment or revenue.
If implemented successfully, the reforms could improve business efficiency, reduce administrative costs, and make public services more accessible. However, the scale of the eventual gains will depend on how quickly Pakistan translates its digital transformation plans into measurable outcomes.

items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
Pakistani actor Hiba Bukhari has urged her fans to treat others with respect after coming across what she described as “really disrespectful” comments on social media.
In an Instagram Story, Bukhari clarified that her intention behind an earlier post was to understand the situation rather than encourage hostility among her followers.
“Okay. So I am posting this after reading comments and some really disrespectful things which I don’t appreciate in any way,” Bukhari wrote.
The actor emphasised that while she valued her fans, she did not want their support to come at the expense of respect for others, particularly her fellow actors.
“I love my fans and I know for a fact my fandom can not disrespect anyone,” she stated. “I respect my co actors and that is exactly what I expect from you all,” she added.
Screengrab: ihibaqadir/Instagram
Bukhari also clarified the purpose of her earlier interaction, explaining that she had been seeking an understanding of the situation rather than attempting to fuel disagreements. “The story was to inquire what is happening,” she wrote.
Concluding her message, the actor appealed to her followers to remain considerate towards one another, expressing disappointment at the hurtful remarks she had encountered. “It’s a request to you all please be respectful towards each other! And it’s actually hurtful to see such things. Lots of love from your Hiba Bukhari,” she said.
Bukhari’s message highlights the challenges public figures can face as their fan communities extend beyond television screens into highly active online spaces. While passionate supporters can play an important role in celebrating actors and their work, disagreements between fans can also spill over into personal attacks and hostility.
The actor’s comments come amid continued public interest in her television projects and on-screen pairings. She starred opposite Danish Taimoor in Humrahi, which became a subject of online discussion following its release. She is also set to appear in Rutba, an upcoming drama featuring Mehwish Hayat and Haseeb Hassan.

items.content:
Matt Renshaw continued his prolific batting form before Australia declared on 314-6 at tea on the fourth day of the first Test on Monday, setting South Africa a daunting victory target of 421.
Australia held a 106-run first-innings lead after Renshaw scored 190, and the 30-year-old Queenslander again dominated the home bowlers at Kingsmead before a controversial caught-and-bowled dismissal by Keshav Maharaj ended his innings.
Renshaw looked disgusted after Maharaj appeared to juggle the catch before claiming it, with a television review confirming the dismissal.
Australia, who resumed on 33 without loss, scored 141 runs in a fast-moving morning session for the loss of four wickets and added another 140 in the afternoon as they sought to give themselves enough time to take the 10 wickets required for victory.
Opener Nic Maddinson, playing his first Test in a decade after scoring a duck in the first innings, struck 48 before being bowled by Anrich Nortje. Beau Webster remained unbeaten on 39, while captain Pat Cummins smashed four sixes in a whirlwind 32 off 12 balls.
Travis Head managed 11 and Marnus Labuschagne scored 37, but Labuschagne's 53-run partnership with Steve Smith, who made 27, helped Australia accelerate.
Smith was struck on the helmet by a Nortje bouncer while batting and underwent a lengthy on-field assessment before continuing his innings. He was later caught on the boundary off spinner Simon Harmer and did not take the field at the start of South Africa's second innings.
An Australian team spokesman said Smith was "undergoing further assessment", with an update expected later on Monday or on Tuesday. A concussion diagnosis could put him in doubt for the second Test in Gqeberha, which starts on Sunday.
South Africa were 60-1 at the time of filing, with Aiden Markram on 22 and David Bedingham unbeaten on 35. Josh Hazlewood dismissed Ryan Rickelton for two.
The hosts need a determined batting performance to avoid defeat and preserve captain Temba Bavuma's unbeaten record in 12 Tests as skipper.
Bad light curtailed play on each of the first three days and was again expected to threaten an early finish on Monday.

vivo X500E Dirumorkan Bawa Dimensity 9500
Menurut rumor yang beredar, vivo X500E akan menggunakan chipset MediaTek Dimensity 9500. Perangkat ini juga disebut bakal memiliki layar berukuran 6,59 inci. Namun, belum ada informasi lebih lanjut mengenai jenis panel, resolusi, maupun refresh rate yang akan digunakan.

Similarly, the iPad Mini (2026) might sport a relocated FaceTime camera and an upgraded speaker setup.

items.title: Rumor Terbaru iPhone Air 2, Lebih Tipis dengan Baterai Lebih Besar
items.summary:
Setelah resmi memperkenalkan iPhone seri Pro dan Duo beberapa pekan kemarin, Apple siap merilis sejumlah produk lainnya sepanjang akhir tahun hingga awal 2027 mendatang. Salah satunya adalah generasi berikutnya dari lini smartphone Apple tertipis, yakni iPhone Air 2, yang dikabarkan siap diluncurkan bersamaan dengan iPhone 18 standar. Kini dikabarkan bakal hadir dalam dimensi yang lebih tipis lagi.
Ya, saat pertama kali debut September 2025 lalu, iPhone Air hadir sebagai smartphone Apple tertipis, bahkan lebih tipis dari lini produk lainnya termasuk iPod, dengan ketebalan hanya 5,6mm (terkecuali bagian modul kamera atau yang Apple sebut dengan “plateau” untuk menyimpan sejumlah komponen penting seperti kamera, speaker, dan chipset).
Tentunya smartphone ini menjadi opsi baru bagi para konsumen yang mungkin lebih ingin mengutamakan gaya, sembari tetap membawa performa andal, namun tidak membutuhkan sejumlah fitur ekstra seperti sensor kamera telefoto khusus maupun ukuran layar lebih lega
items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
Setelah resmi memperkenalkan iPhone seri Pro dan Duo beberapa pekan kemarin, Apple siap merilis sejumlah produk lainnya sepanjang akhir tahun hingga awal 2027 mendatang. Salah satunya adalah generasi berikutnya dari lini smartphone Apple tertipis, yakni iPhone Air 2, yang dikabarkan siap diluncurkan bersamaan dengan iPhone 18 standar. Kini dikabarkan bakal hadir dalam dimensi yang lebih tipis lagi.
Ya, saat pertama kali debut September 2025 lalu, iPhone Air hadir sebagai smartphone Apple tertipis, bahkan lebih tipis dari lini produk lainnya termasuk iPod, dengan ketebalan hanya 5,6mm (terkecuali bagian modul kamera atau yang Apple sebut dengan “plateau” untuk menyimpan sejumlah komponen penting seperti kamera, speaker, dan chipset).
Tentunya smartphone ini menjadi opsi baru bagi para konsumen yang mungkin lebih ingin mengutamakan gaya, sembari tetap membawa performa andal, namun tidak membutuhkan sejumlah fitur ekstra seperti sensor kamera telefoto khusus maupun ukuran layar lebih lega. Dan lewat iPhone Air 2, Apple siap menjawab sejumlah keluhan dari generasi pertama lewat sejumlah penyempurnaan.
Baca juga: iPhone 18 Pro Lesu? Pesanan Komponen Dikabarkan Turun 15 hingga 20 Persen
Baterai iPhone Air 2 Siap Dibuat Lebih Besar
Render iPhone Air 2
Dikutip dari MacRumors, bocoran terbaru dari iPhone Air 2 menyebutkan dua peningkatan yang tentunya bakal sangat menarik bila benar-benar berhasil terealisasi saat diluncurkan awal tahun depan. Masing-masing ada pada sektor desain serta kapasitas daya baterai—yang seperti kita tahu, menjadi salah satu nilai jual utama sekaligus nilai konsiderasi utama konsumen ketika membeli iPhone Air.
Kalau yang sebelumnya sudah sangat tipis, disebutkan bila desain iPhone Air 2 bakal dibuat lebih tipis dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya, hingga 0,4mm lebih tipis. Artinya, profil bodi keseluruhan hanya 5,2mm, alias setara dengan ketebalan iPhone Duo saat terbuka. Benar-benar sangat tipis bila memang benar adanya.
Peningkatan berikutnya ada pada sektor baterai, di mana meski bodi dibuat lebih tipis, kapasitas baterai iPhone Air 2 akan dibuat meningkat, setidaknya mencapai 3,500 mAh. Dengan begitu, naik sekitar 11% dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya yang hanya 3,149 mAh. Tentunya aspek ini akan memberikan pengalaman penggunaan yang lebih positif.
Besar kemungkinan bila Apple bisa sematkan baterai dengan densitas energi lebih tinggi, sehingga kapasitasnya bisa naik, seperti yang mereka terapkan pada iPhone 18 Pro Series. Dipadukan dengan cip yang juga lebih efisien daya, tentunya bisa membuat iPhone Air 2 lebih pas untuk menemani hari yang lebih produktif sekalipun. Kita nantikan saja perkembangan rumornya dalam beberapa pekan ke depan ya.
Sejalan dengan Bocoran yang Pernah Muncul Sebelumnya
Render iPhone Air 2
Sebelumnya, Mark Gurman dari Bloomberg sudah menyebutkan bila Apple siap meluncurkan iPhone Air 2 bersama dengan iPhone 18 standar, dan iPhone 18e pada awal tahun 2027. Sementara di akhir tahun, bakal ada tiga jenis iPhone berbeda, yakni iPhone Duo generasi kedua, iPhone 20 Pro Series, dan iPhone edisi spesial untuk merayakan edisi tahun ke-20.
Dan pada bulan Juni kemarin, Mark juga menambahkan bila iPhone Air 2 siap mengusung sensor kamera tambahan, yakni 48MP ultra-wide, untuk menemani sensor 48MP tunggal yang sebelumnya ada di iPhone Air generasi pertama. Bisa dibilang, membuat iPhone Air 2 memiliki setup kamera setara dengan iPhone Duo.
Tidak hanya itu, Mark juga mengonfirmasi usaha Apple untuk membuat daya tahan baterai iPhone Air 2 lebih lama, termasuk dengan penggunaan cip generasi terbaru. Rumor ini kemudian menjadi sah-sah saja bila benar terjadi, mengingat Apple sematkan cip A20 Pro berfabrikasi 2nm pada iPhone 18 Pro, dengan poin efisiensi andal. Memberikan iPhone 18 Pro Series masa pakai baterai yang jauh lebih awet dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya.

The Alfa Mall listing displays a PTA approval service price of Rs 249,999, with payment options ranging from 3 to 36 months. The shortest plans are advertised at 0% markup, although processing fees and Federal Excise Duty (FED) are still applicable.

As stated on the Alfa Mall installment interface, credit cards issued within the previous three months or cards without sufficient available limit are not eligible for the facility. Eligibility and final terms remain subject to the bank’s conditions.
For iPhone 18 Pro Max owners who need PTA registration, paying in installments may make the upfront expense easier to manage. However, the longer-term plans add markup, so users should compare the full cost rather than choosing solely on the basis of the lowest monthly installment.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
vivo appears to be preparing another addition to its V80 smartphone lineup, as the upcoming vivo V80 FE has surfaced on Indonesia’s SDPPI certification database. The development suggests that the company is moving closer to introducing a more affordable alternative to its standard V80 model.
According to the certification listing, the smartphone carries model number V2624, confirming its product name. However, the database does not reveal its hardware specifications, design, or official launch date.
The new model is expected to succeed the vivo V70 FE, which arrived in Pakistan earlier this year with a 200MP camera, a large AMOLED display, and a 7,000mAh battery. Given the popularity of camera-focused smartphones in Pakistan’s upper mid-range segment, the V80 FE could become another interesting option for local buyers.
vivo V80 FE Expected Specifications
Although vivo has yet to disclose the specifications, its predecessor provides an indication of what the upcoming handset could offer.
The vivo V70 FE featured a 6.83-inch AMOLED display with 1.5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate. It was powered by MediaTek’s Dimensity 7360 Turbo processor, paired with 8GB or 12GB RAM and 256GB storage.
Photography was one of its major selling points, with a 200MP primary camera featuring optical image stabilisation (OIS), accompanied by an 8MP ultrawide sensor and a 32MP front-facing camera in Pakistan.
The device also offered a 7,000 mAh battery with 90 W fast charging, making battery endurance another key attraction.
The upcoming V80 FE could retain a similar display and camera configuration while introducing improvements to its processor, imaging capabilities, or battery efficiency. However, reports suggesting a larger battery remain speculative, and no reliable specifications have emerged from the certification listing.
Expected vivo V80 FE Price in Pakistan
The vivo V70 FE officially launched in Pakistan in April 2026 at Rs. 124,999 for the 8GB/256GB variant and Rs. 139,999 for the 12GB/256GB model. The device subsequently became available through the company’s authorised retail network.
Considering the predecessor’s launch pricing and the expected positioning of the new model, the vivo V80 FE could arrive in Pakistan within the following estimated price range:
Expected variant
Estimated Pakistan price
8GB + 256GB
Rs. 130,000–140,000
12GB + 256GB
Rs. 145,000–155,000
These estimates assume that vivo maintains a similar pricing strategy and introduces relatively modest hardware upgrades. Actual prices will depend on the final specifications, exchange rates, applicable taxes and the company’s local pricing decisions.
vivo has not announced any official Pakistan pricing for the V80 FE.
Expected Launch Timeline in Pakistan
The appearance of the vivo V80 FE on Indonesia’s certification database indicates that preparations for its regional launch may be progressing. However, certification does not necessarily mean an immediate commercial release.
The previous-generation vivo V70 FE officially launched in Pakistan on April 27, 2026, with nationwide sales beginning on May 5. This suggests that Pakistan remains an established market for vivo’s FE-series smartphones.
If vivo follows a similar regional rollout strategy, the V80 FE could reach Pakistan during the fourth quarter of 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, following its introduction in other Asian markets.
This remains a tentative estimate rather than a confirmed launch window. The company has not announced whether the smartphone will be released in Pakistan.
The V80 FE could face competition from Samsung’s Galaxy A-series, OPPO’s Reno lineup and other premium mid-range smartphones, particularly if its price approaches Rs. 150,000.
For now, the SDPPI listing provides the first concrete indication of the handset’s existence. Further certifications, benchmark appearances, and official announcements should offer a clearer picture of its specifications and availability in the coming weeks.

items.author: Maksuda Akter
items.content:
Repeated disruptions raise concerns over recruitment transparency and migrant workers’ protection from exploitation.
Originally published on Global Voices
On Saturday, October 5, 2024, a Memorandum of Collaboration (MOC) was signed in Dhaka between the Wage Earners Welfare Board and Malaysia's PERKESO, regarding the expansion of the labor market in Malaysia. Image via Wikipedia by Press Information Department of Bangladesh. Public Domain.
Officials in both Bangladesh and Malaysia’s have made repeated attempts to reform the countries’ labour migration relationship, leading to numerous suspensions and reopenings over more than three decades.
However, on August 30, 2026, Bangladesh’s State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives, Mir Shahe Alam, announced that Malaysia would recruit around 200,000 Bangladeshi workers over six months, with departures expected to begin in late September. He also referred to a plan to send 10,000 workers without requiring them to bear migration costs.
Two days later, however, Malaysia’s government spokesperson Fahmi Fadzil clarified that the figure of 200,000 workers did not represent an official government position. The clarification introduced fresh uncertainty over the scale and timing of the recruitment drive.
The mixed signals came as the two countries were trying to reset a labour migration corridor that has faced repeated allegations of excessive recruitment fees, syndication and worker exploitation.
Repeated reopenings, repeated suspensions
Bangladesh first entered into an agreement with Malaysia for the systematic transfer of labour in 1992, followed by another agreement in 1994 that provided for the recruitment of 50,000 workers annually, mainly for the construction sector. Between 1992 and 1998, around 307,000 Bangladeshi workers were issued permits to work in Malaysia. But recruitment was halted in 1997 amid a rise in unauthorised migration. During that period, local brokers could charge workers between USD 2,000 (approximately BDT 245,700) and USD 3,000 (approximately BDT 368,600) for authorised migration.
In an effort to reduce recruitment malpractice and costs, the two governments turned to a government-to-government model (G2G model) in 2012. The programme initially aimed to recruit around 30,000 Bangladeshi workers for Malaysia’s palm-oil sector. More than 1.4 million people registered and workers were selected through a lottery system. The G2G arrangement substantially reduced migration costs, but it struggled to meet its recruitment targets.
The system was later replaced by the G2G Plus arrangement. Under the model introduced in 2016, Malaysia selected only 10 Bangladeshi recruiting agencies. Although the agreed migration cost was around BDT 37,000-40,000 (approximately USD 300 to USD 325), later reports put the amount actually paid by workers at an average of around BDT 300,000 to 400,000 (approximately USD 2,450 to USD 3,260). Allegations of syndication, high costs and other irregularities eventually led Malaysia to suspend recruitment again in 2018.
Recruitment resumed following a new memorandum of understanding signed in December 2021. Between 2022 and 2024, 476,672 Bangladeshi workers were sent to Malaysia through 101 recruiting agencies. But by June 2024, the labour market had again closed to new Bangladeshi recruits amid concerns over high migration costs and worker exploitation.
Against this history of repeated closed and reopened borders, the latest attempt to reset recruitment has revived a familiar question: whether the new arrangement can reduce the financial burden on workers and prevent the problems that undermined earlier recruitment systems.
The latest debacle
On August 28, 2026, Bangladesh’s Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment outlined a broader recruitment arrangement involving 338 entities. Malaysia had directly selected 25 recruiting agencies, while 312 others were approved to work as associates. The state-run Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited, or BOESL, was also included.
Under the same arrangement, Malaysia had agreed in principle to take 10,000 workers on a zero-cost basis. Prospective migrants were also warned not to make payments, undergo medical examinations or hand over their passports until formal instructions were issued.
That warning stands out against the record of the previous recruitment cycle.
In July 2026, Bangladesh revoked the licences of 49 recruiting agencies over alleged syndication and irregularities linked to Malaysia-bound recruitment. The Anti-Corruption Commission alleged that agencies under investigation had sent 267,276 workers to Malaysia and collected more than BDT 45.45 billion (approximately USD 370 million) in excess fees. The government-approved recruitment cost was BDT 78,990 (approximately USD 645), yet investigators alleged that some workers were charged as much as five times that amount. Concerns over high recruitment costs have continued into the new cycle, with industry sources warning that migration expenses could exceed BDT 600,000 (approximately USD 4,900).
The financial burden is not limited to the Malaysia corridor. Bangladesh’s Labour Force Survey 2024 found that migrant workers spent an average of BDT 463,000 (approximately USD 3,778 ) on recruitment. With average monthly earnings of BDT 42,599 (approximately USD 348), recovering that expense took about 10.9 months on average.
For some families, however, the financial loss begins even before a worker leaves Bangladesh.
Paying for a journey that never happened
For a 22-year-old worker originally from Sherpur, Bangladesh, the financial loss began with a job abroad that he never reached.
Speaking to Global Voices by phone and asking to remain anonymous, he said he began preparing to migrate to Malaysia around 2024 after hearing about work opportunities through a local intermediary. By the time the process stalled, his family had spent around BDT 500,000 (approximately USD 4,079). The money came from their savings, the sale of land and loans — around BDT 220,000 (approximately USD 1,795) of which were borrowed at interest.
The payments were made in stages for visa processing, medical costs and other expenses. Much of the process was handled through a local intermediary rather than directly with a recruiting agency, and the worker said he did not receive receipts for all of the money he paid.
“At first they said it would take two or three months, but six or seven months passed. Whenever I asked for an update, the intermediary gave a different answer but never gave me a clear one. I had already done the medical and submitted my passport. Eventually they told me the Malaysian market had closed and there was nothing more they could do.”
By then, however, the full amount had already been paid, leaving him and his family with the financial burden.
“I thought I would go to Malaysia, earn money, and repay the loan. But I could not go. I got some of the money back, but they still have not returned the rest. Whenever I call, they just say, ‘Give us some more time.’ I do not know how long I am supposed to keep waiting. I am still here, but I am still paying off the debt I took to go abroad.”
The consequences also reached the rest of the household. His mother, who also spoke to Global Voices by phone and asked to remain anonymous, said, “My husband died a long time ago. We only had a small piece of land, so I sold it. I also borrowed money with interest and somehow managed the rest for my son. I thought that if he could go abroad and earn well, we would repay everything. But he could not go. Now we still have to keep paying the interest, whether we have enough for food or not.”
A wider pattern of recruitment debt
The family’s experience sits within a broader pattern of high recruitment costs and debt among Bangladeshis seeking work in Malaysia. Research by Verité, an independent nonprofit organization advancing fair labor worldwide, on the Bangladesh–Malaysia migration corridor found that workers paid an average of about USD 5,000 (approximately BDT 614,400) in recruitment-related costs, often financing the journey through multiple loans. Among the workers surveyed, 73 percent spent at least half of their monthly salary on recruitment debt, while 43 percent reported wage deception.
The role of intermediaries has also been identified as a major driver of those costs. An International Organization for Migration (IOM) study on recruitment practices in Bangladesh found that aspiring migrants often rely on sub-agents and informal intermediaries because they have little direct contact with recruiting agencies or do not fully understand the formal process. The study identified reducing the unauthorised involvement of such intermediaries as a key step towards lowering migration costs.
A separate IOM study on migrant debt found that limited information about official migration channels can push prospective workers towards intermediaries who charge high fees. It also identified limited access to formal finance and legal remedies as factors that can deepen migrant indebtedness.
What remains unclear in the new recruitment cycle
As Bangladesh and Malaysia move towards restarting recruitment, key details of the process remain unsettled. By September 30, 2026, the Bangladesh High Commission in Kuala Lumpur had begun attesting job-demand letters, but the government had yet to announce the final recruitment cost, departure timeline, or full procedure. Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said an official announcement would be made soon.
The structure of the new arrangement has also drawn criticism from within the recruitment industry. Some Bangladesh Association of International Recruiting Agencies (BAIRA) members argued that the 312 associate agencies should have direct access to Malaysia’s Foreign Workers Centralised Management System rather than relying on the 25 principal agencies to process workers. Other recruiters rejected concerns about renewed syndication, saying associate agencies could still obtain job demand and recruit workers.
In November 2025, UN human rights experts expressed renewed concern over the continued exploitation, deception and deepening debt bondage of Bangladeshi migrant workers in Malaysia. They called on both governments to investigate reported abuses, provide effective remedies including restitution and debt relief, strengthen oversight of recruitment practices and cooperate to dismantle exploitative recruitment networks.
The recruitment corridor has also faced repeated suspensions amid recurring allegations of syndication, excessive recruitment costs and worker exploitation. Malaysia suspended recruitment of Bangladeshi workers in 2018 following controversy surrounding the limited-agency system, and again in June 2024 amid concerns over excessive migration costs and workers arriving without jobs. The repeated disruptions have renewed concerns over whether restricted recruitment arrangements can ensure transparency and protect workers from exploitation.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian government has warned agencies not to collect money or passports before formal instructions are issued. Migration researcher Shariful Hasan also told The Daily Star that any reopening should clearly establish who controls recruitment, how much workers are required to pay and who is accountable when problems arise.
Bangladesh and Malaysia have made several government-level agreements over the years, but problems such as syndication, excessive recruitment costs and human rights abuses remain unresolved. Remittances are a major source of support for Bangladesh’s economy, yet migrant workers continue to bear significant human and financial costs. This highlights the need for urgent reforms by both governments that are transparent and centred on the rights and protection of workers.
Written by Maksuda Akter

items.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Internet Disruption: Wi-Fi Returns Monday After Emergency Rule Outage, Users Say
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Internet connectivity in parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) was disrupted after the president imposed emergency rule in the province on Sunday, according to the global monitor NetBlocks. Users say Wi-Fi started working again on Monday morning.
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa internet disruption began as the federal government suspended the provincial administration led by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI). Users report that both mobile data and Wi-Fi stopped working.
What NetBlocks reported
In a post on X late Sunday, NetBlocks said its network data showed a “major disruption to Internet connectivity in parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.” It linked the outage to President Asif Ali Zardari’s imposition of emergency rule and to protests demanding the release of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan.
Reports from users in the province say mobile SIM data stopped working and Wi-Fi went down as well. Wi-Fi began working again on Monday morning.
items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Internet connectivity in parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) was disrupted after the president imposed emergency rule in the province on Sunday, according to the global monitor NetBlocks. Users say Wi-Fi started working again on Monday morning.
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa internet disruption began as the federal government suspended the provincial administration led by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI). Users report that both mobile data and Wi-Fi stopped working.
What NetBlocks reported
In a post on X late Sunday, NetBlocks said its network data showed a “major disruption to Internet connectivity in parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.” It linked the outage to President Asif Ali Zardari’s imposition of emergency rule and to protests demanding the release of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan.
Reports from users in the province say mobile SIM data stopped working and Wi-Fi went down as well. Wi-Fi began working again on Monday morning.
The political backdrop
The president declared a state of emergency and suspended the KP government led by PTI. The federal government said that administration had failed to tackle militancy in the province, which borders Afghanistan.
Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said Governor Faisal Karim Kundi would take charge in KP. Hours later, the interior ministry authorized the deployment of army troops and assets to assist the civilian administration, according to a directive.
The move came about a week after PTI supporters gathered in the province intending to march on Islamabad. The march began Sunday from Lakki Marwat, led by Sohail Afridi, who had been in charge of the province and is a close aide of Khan. PTI members claim his arrest after the imposition of emergency in the province.
PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari called the emergency “more of a coup disguised as emergency,” saying it risks further instability and aims to stop the march. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government tried to avoid an emergency and had told PTI it had “no issue” with a march to the capital. His stated concern was terrorism.
A pattern with precedents
Connectivity restrictions around political events are not new in Pakistan. In May 2023, the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) confirmed it had suspended mobile broadband nationwide on the interior ministry’s instructions after Khan’s arrest. In November 2024, the federal government had decided to partially suspend internet and mobile services in Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab ahead of a PTI protest.
Some KP residents were already living with weak connectivity. In June, residents of Lower South Waziristan said mobile internet had been fully suspended in several areas for about two months, and they appealed to the PTA to restore it.
Why it matters
An outage that takes down both mobile and fixed-line access leaves people with no fallback. Students, delivery riders, small online sellers, and offices rely on one or the other, and often both.
It also affects verification. When connectivity drops during a political standoff, claims move faster than confirmation. Users cannot check what is happening around them, and outsiders cannot check what users report.
Wi-Fi returning on Monday morning suggests the disruption was not permanent, but it does not explain it. The questions left are whether mobile data has come back, whether it spread beyond “parts” of KP, and whether the PTA or the interior ministry will say what happened. Until they do, the verified facts are NetBlocks’ reading of the network data and users’ accounts.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Many people switch on a VPN before they open an AI chatbot and assume the job is done, but that assumption is only partly right.
A VPN, or virtual private network, builds an encrypted tunnel between your device and a server run by the VPN company. It changes the address websites see and shields your traffic from your internet provider. It does nothing about the more sensitive part of an AI chat: what you actually type.
VPN privacy with AI chatbots comes down to which party you are hiding from.
What a VPN does hide
Without a VPN, the AI company can see where you are connecting from. OpenAI’s privacy policy covers IP address, device information including unique identifiers, cookie data, and location, along with email address and payment details. Anthropic’s policy covers location, connection details, and device usage patterns, especially on its mobile app.
A VPN masks your real IP address from the platform. It also stops your internet provider from seeing that you are using an AI service. That is a real gain, though only a small part of the privacy picture.
Where the tunnel ends
The central point is about decryption. A chatbot cannot process a message it cannot read, so your prompt is decrypted when it arrives. The VPN’s protection ends at that moment.
From then on, the text is governed by the company’s policies, not by your VPN. That includes the prompts themselves, any files or images you upload, your account details, your conversation history, and your payment information.
Hidden by a VPN
Not hidden by a VPN
Your real IP address and approximate location
Yes
Visits to AI services as seen by your internet provider
Yes
Text of your prompts
Yes
Uploaded files and images
Yes
Account details and chat history
Yes
Payment information
Yes
The settings that matter more
Most consumer chatbots keep conversations on file and may use them to train future models. Controlling that falls to you, not your VPN.
On ChatGPT, the feature points to Settings, then Data Controls, where you can switch off the option to improve the model for everyone. Even then, chats may still be stored for safety and legal reasons.
On Claude, Anthropic asks every consumer user to decide whether chats can be used for training. According to the feature, the toggle is on by default. If it stays on, data can be kept for up to five years. If you decline, the period is 30 days. You can change this in account preferences or use Incognito mode to keep a conversation out of your saved history. The feature adds that paid business tiers come with stricter privacy agreements by default.
The gap between five years and 30 days is the number most users never see. It also shows why a VPN, which does nothing about retention, is the wrong tool for that problem.
Who you are really hiding from
Ask what a VPN protects you from, and the list is short: your internet provider, anyone watching the network, and the platform’s view of your location. The AI company is none of those. It is the party you are talking to, and it has to read your message to answer it.
That changes the question. Privacy with a chatbot is less about how your message travels and more about whether you trust the company that receives it and what it is allowed to keep. Switch off training, use temporary or incognito chats, and keep sensitive material out of the prompt. None of these involves a VPN, and all of them are free.
There is also a fairness problem. Retention and training defaults are set by the company, and the burden of changing them lands on the user. Because the burden of changing them lands on the user, the default is what applies to anyone who never opens the settings page.
A VPN is still a sensible tool for the job it was built for. Just don’t count it as protection for your conversations. For those, the safest prompt is one that never contained the secret.
