Says viral video is an old 2022 interview taken out of context
The media office of former Minister of Power, Chief Adebayo Adelabu, has dismissed a viral report claiming that he called on Nigerians to reject the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the allegation as false and misleading.
In a statement issued in October 2026, Adelabu’s media office said the video circulating on social media was an excerpt from an interview he granted in 2022, when he was the governorship candidate of the Accord Party in Oyo State.
It said Adelabu did not call on Nigerians to reject the APC, urging the public to disregard what it described as a deliberate attempt to misrepresent his position and create friction between him, President Bola Tinubu and the party’s leadership.
According to the statement, Adelabu had consistently maintained his loyalty to the APC and the President despite controversies surrounding the party’s governorship nomination process in Oyo State.
The former minister, who served under the APC-led Federal Government, reportedly left public office to pursue his governorship ambition in the state.
The statement alleged that the APC nomination process was marred by controversies, including the alleged imposition of a preferred aspirant and the failure to transparently release the primary election results.
It said Adelabu had nevertheless maintained that he had no intention of leaving the party and that his political ambition was not a do-or-die affair.
“His position has been consistent: loyalty does not preclude the demand for fairness, transparency and adherence to democratic principles,” the statement said.
It argued that Adelabu’s criticism of the party’s internal electoral process should not be interpreted as a call for Nigerians to reject the APC.
The media office explained that the 2022 interview reflected Adelabu’s view that political parties had disappointed Nigerians and that voters should focus on the credibility and character of individual candidates.
It added that the comments were made in the context of the political environment at the time and did not amount to opposition to the APC or Tinubu’s presidential ambition.
The statement also described Adelabu’s relationship with Tinubu as longstanding, saying it was based on mutual respect and trust.
It challenged those circulating the video to publish the full, unedited interview rather than selectively extracting portions of it.
The media office further claimed that Adelabu had not granted any media interview since the conclusion of the controversial APC governorship nomination process in Oyo State in which he made the alleged statement.
It urged APC members, the media and the public to verify information before sharing it, warning against the spread of unsubstantiated claims.
“Chief Adelabu remains committed to the APC, loyal to Mr President and supportive of the party’s broader political objectives,” the statement said.
The media office advised the public to rely on authentic statements from Adelabu or his authorised representatives.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
MrBeast has emerged as the world’s highest-paid content creator, earning an estimated $300 million as social media influencers expand their businesses into entertainment, technology, consumer products and streaming.
According to Forbes’ 2026 Top Creators ranking, the 50 creators featured on the list collectively generated $1.02 billion, representing a 20 per cent increase from $853 million recorded in the previous year’s ranking.
The publication, edited by Steven Bertoni, with reporting by Zoya Hasan and Alexandra York, alongside Sofia Chierchio and Martina Di Licosa, highlighted how digital creators are transforming their online popularity into lucrative business empires.
From YouTube personalities and TikTok stars to podcasters and entrepreneurs, the creators are increasingly competing with traditional entertainment companies through original productions, brand partnerships, merchandise and investments.
Forbes noted that creators are also making significant inroads into Hollywood and streaming. Examples include films developed from online content that have generated hundreds of millions of dollars at the box office, as well as digital personalities securing deals with major streaming platforms.
Here are the 10 highest-paid creators featured in the Forbes 2026 ranking, based on their reported earnings.
1. MrBeast — $300 million
Total followers: 873 million | Average engagement: 3.00%
Jimmy Donaldson, popularly known as MrBeast, tops the ranking with estimated earnings of $300 million.
He built his popularity through elaborate YouTube challenges, stunts and competitions before expanding into a business empire spanning entertainment, food, merchandise and technology.
His company, Beast Industries, oversees ventures including Feastables, Lunchly, analytics platform Viewstats, and toy and clothing licensing.
According to Forbes, his YouTube channels have more than 640 million subscribers and attract over five billion views annually.
MrBeast has also expanded into streaming with Beast Games on Amazon Prime Video, with its third season already in production at the time of the report.
In February 2026, Beast Industries acquired Step, a financial app designed to teach teenagers about investing and money management. Forbes also reported that the company had attracted venture investment at a valuation of $5 billion.
2. Dhar Mann — $65 million
Total followers: 171 million | Average engagement: 0.09%
Dhar Mann ranks second with estimated earnings of $65 million, driven by scripted videos that focus on life lessons, relationships and personal transformation.
His production team of approximately 200 people creates digital shows that, according to Forbes, generate nearly 300 million views in a typical week.
Mann’s content reaches audiences in 13 languages, helping him build a global following across social media platforms.
He has also expanded beyond short-form digital entertainment. His partnership with the NFL saw him serve as the league’s “Chief Kindness Officer” for Super Bowl LX, while a deal with Fox Entertainment will see him produce 40 vertical dramas over 18 months.
His business model demonstrates how creators can build production companies capable of supplying content to traditional broadcasters and emerging digital platforms.
3. Steven Bartlett — $52 million
Total followers: 38.7 million | Average engagement: 0.22%
British entrepreneur and podcast host Steven Bartlett ranks third, with estimated earnings of $52 million.
Bartlett is best known for The Diary of a CEO, an interview podcast that grew from a project he started at his kitchen table into a major media brand.
According to Forbes, his holding company, Steven.com, is valued at $425 million and has interests spanning media, publishing, live events and investments.
His commercial partnerships include Spotify, LinkedIn and Adobe. He has also invested in technology companies Replit and Lovable.
Bartlett continues to expand his television profile through Dragons’ Den, the investment programme in which entrepreneurs pitch business ideas to potential investors.
His success illustrates how podcasting can develop into a wider business involving advertising, investments and entertainment.
4. Markiplier — $38 million
Total followers: 76.8 million | Average engagement: 0.21%
Mark Edward Fischbach, known professionally as Markiplier, occupies fourth place with estimated earnings of $38 million.
Initially known for gaming videos and online entertainment, Markiplier has moved into filmmaking, demonstrating how established creators can use their digital audiences to support projects outside social media.
His self-funded and self-produced feature film, Iron Lung, screened in approximately 3,000 theatres across North America and generated $50 million at the box office, according to Forbes.
The creator also negotiated a 50-50 revenue split with theatres, an arrangement that gave him a direct stake in the film’s theatrical performance.
Beyond filmmaking, Markiplier continues to host the podcasts Distractible and Go! My Favorite Sports Team.
5. Rhett & Link — $37 million
Total followers: 45.6 million | Average engagement: 0.12%
Comedy duo Rhett McLaughlin and Link Neal rank fifth, with combined estimated earnings of $37 million.
The childhood friends are best known for Good Mythical Morning, their long-running YouTube talk show featuring food challenges, product reviews, trivia and discussions about popular culture.
Forbes reports that the programme produces approximately 240 episodes annually and attracts nearly 20 million viewers.
The duo also operates the Mythical Kitchen channel, which features the Last Meal series hosted by Josh Scherer. Guests have included Tom Hanks, Gordon Ramsay and Ed Sheeran.
Their expansion into Tubi and publishing, including their fourth food book, Spaghetti Head & Chicken Fingers, further demonstrates their ability to turn a digital entertainment brand into multiple revenue streams.
6. Charli D’Amelio — $18 million
Total followers: 209.8 million | Average engagement: 11.59%
TikTok star Charli D’Amelio ranks sixth with estimated earnings of $18 million.
She rose to global prominence through dance videos on TikTok and has since expanded her career into theatre, fashion and other forms of entertainment.
Following her Broadway run in & Juliet, D’Amelio returned to posting dance content and YouTube vlogs while maintaining major fashion partnerships.
She serves as a Prada ambassador and has appeared in campaigns for Kate Spade.
Her position on the list highlights the commercial value of a highly engaged social media audience, particularly for creators whose influence translates into brand partnerships and opportunities beyond digital platforms.
7. Druski — $20 million
Total followers: 38.5 million | Average engagement: 13.77%
Comedian and internet personality Druski, whose real name is Drew Desbordes, ranks seventh with estimated earnings of $20 million.
He gained recognition through comedy sketches shared on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram before expanding into mainstream advertising and television.
His commercial appearances include campaigns for T-Mobile and Dunkin’, while his collaborations have brought him alongside entertainment figures such as Kevin Hart, Timothée Chalamet, Jeff Bridges and Zoe Saldaña.
Forbes also highlighted his role as host of the BET Awards in June.
Druski’s career illustrates how internet comedy can serve as a launchpad for opportunities in advertising, live entertainment and mainstream media.
8. IShowSpeed — $30 million
Total followers: 184 million | Average engagement: 0.39%
Popular streamer IShowSpeed ranks eighth with estimated earnings of $30 million.
The creator, whose real name is Darren Watkins Jr., initially gained attention through gaming videos featuring titles such as NBA 2K and Fortnite.
His popularity grew significantly after clips of his energetic reactions and gaming outbursts went viral on TikTok.
He later diversified into football-related content, collaborating with global stars including Cristiano Ronaldo, before expanding into travel livestreams and videos.
His projects include Speed Does America and Speed Does Africa. His commercial partnerships include Dick’s Sporting Goods, Beats by Dre and Doritos.
Forbes also highlighted his World Cup 2026 Tour with FIFA as part of his expansion into football-related entertainment and global travel content.
9. Mark Rober — $30 million
Total followers: 90.7 million | Average engagement: 0.23%
Former NASA engineer and science communicator Mark Rober ranks ninth, with estimated earnings of $30 million.
Rober is known for highly produced YouTube videos that explain scientific concepts through experiments, engineering projects and elaborate stunts.
His content includes projects designed to teach physics through roller coasters, explore scientific approaches to escaping Alcatraz and demonstrate robotics in collaboration with football superstar Cristiano Ronaldo.
According to Forbes, his team of approximately 100 people produces episodes that can cost seven figures to make.
Rober also operates CrunchLabs, a business that sells science and engineering kits through a subscription model.
His work combines education and entertainment while attracting commercial partnerships with companies including Rivian, Google and Disney.
10. Codie Sanchez — $31 million
Total followers: 10 million | Average engagement: 0.37%
Entrepreneur and former journalist Codie Sanchez rounds out the top 10, with estimated earnings of $31 million.
Sanchez creates content focused on entrepreneurship, business ownership and investment opportunities, particularly in businesses that are often overlooked by technology-focused investors.
Her educational videos discuss ventures such as laundromats, vending machines and landscaping businesses, encouraging audiences to consider established industries that can generate recurring revenue.
She shares business advice across YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, with Forbes reporting that her content reaches more than seven million followers across these platforms.
Rather than focusing on get-rich-quick promises, Sanchez advocates acquiring and operating businesses as a route to building wealth.
Her position on the list highlights how financial education and practical business advice can become profitable creator-led enterprises.
Source: Forbes’ 2026 Top Creators ranking. Earnings and audience figures are Forbes-reported estimates and may reflect different measurement periods.
Vanguard News

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
Gov. Alex Otti of Abia has urged voters to resist financial and material inducements from politicians, warning that such offers could undermine the state’s future in the 2027 general elections.
Otti gave the warning on Sunday at the 2nd Session of the 7th  Synod of the Anglican Communion, Diocese of Aba Ngwa North, held at All Saints Anglican Cathedral, Abayi-Umuocham, Aba.
The governor, represented by his Chief of Staff, Dr Caleb Ajagba, charged citizens to prioritise long-term development over immediate material benefits offered by politicians.
He alleged that politicians responsible for the state’s challenges over 24 years were returning to seek voters’ support.
Otti warned against allowing such politicians to derail the progress his administration was pursuing.
“The people that created a problem that God now had to answer your prayer by sending someone after His own heart, are all over again.
“But the Bible says surely they shall proceed no further. Please, let us be careful.When God opens a door, may we not close it.
“Don’t use the ₦5,000, the ₦10,000, the wrapper or the rice they will give you and close the destiny of Abians for the next four years, because even prayer and fasting will not open it.
“May we not lose what God has given to us on the platter,” he said.
The governor also urged Christians to remain vigilant, warning that some politicians who previously neglected the Church were seeking its attention.
“Like we have been told the season is here again and politicians are everywhere and as the Bible says we are not ignorant of the devices of the enemy.
“These are devices, because many of them who have not been coming to church have started coming to church.
“Many of them who have not been accepting or taking your calls have suddenly started calling you. If you call them and you miss their call, they call you back. Those are devices,” he said.
Otti said the first three years of his administration had focused largely on laying a foundation for development, adding that the next four years, beginning in 2027, would prioritise consolidation.
“Those who build houses will understand that foundation-laying is the most crucial, and the foundation has been laid after 24 years of ruins.
“What will now be happening is consolidation and beauty will emerge.
“This present house (Abia State) you are seeing today, in the next four years, you will know that God has really come to tabernacle in the midst of man.
“Today Abia State has become a point of reference,” he said.
On the church’s development projects, Otti assured the congregation of his administration’s support towards their completion.
He, however, reiterated that public funds should be deployed to develop the state rather than finance religious projects.
The governor commended the guest speaker for delivering what he described as an appropriate and unadulterated message, urging Christians to verify information and examine issues critically before reaching conclusions.
He said the synod’s theme, “Don’t Just Absorb It; Think It Through,” drawn from Acts Chapter 17 verse 11 to 12, was relevant as the country approached another political season.
“As Christians, we have the capacity to change the negative narrative of this nation; especially our state,” he said.
Earlier, the Bishop of Aba Ngwa North Diocese, Anglican Communion,  Dr Nathan Kanu, said the theme challenged Christians to move beyond hearing messages to examining issues prayerfully and responding wisely.
Kanu commended Otti for identifying with the church and supporting its activities, presented gifts to the governor’s representative and prayed for God’s blessings on his administration.
In his sermon, the Guest Speaker and Bishop of Ohaji/Egbema Diocese, Rt. Rev. Chidi Oparajiaku, urged Christians to think critically before taking action.
Speaking on: “The Bereans Wisdom,” with his text from Acts chapter  17 verse 12 and 15, Oparajiaku said the synod’s theme was timely and encouraged believers to examine messages rather than accept or reject them without reflection.
“The theme of the synod is very important and apt in this our time, it didn’t say throw it away, it says think through it,” he said.
Oparajiaku regretted that Christians, who were expected to demonstrate sound judgement, sometimes fell victim to deception.
“When members of the church know the Bible they would not be deceived.
“This is because the church refused to behave like the Bereans. The Bereans Christian never took everything for granted they always thought through whatever they heard,” he said.
The Bishop thanked God for giving Abia the opportunity to be governed by Otti, whom he credited with changing the state’s narrative.
The synod attracted dignitaries, including the Labour Party’s National Vice-Chairman, South-East, Hon. Ishmael Onuoha; state chairman, Sir Peter Azubuike; and Osisioma Local Government Area Mayor, Hon. Chidi Agu.
Others were the Special Assistant to the Governor on Special Duties, Dr George Chiedozie; Special Adviser to the Governor on Labour Matters, Godson Anucha; and Aba industrialist, Mr Bob Udeagha.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress ((NDC), Peter Obi, has criticised the 30-day petrol discount announced by the President Bola Tinubu-led federal government, describing the initiative as a reactive policy that fails to address the economic hardship facing Nigerians.
Obi, in a post on X, said the temporary discount was an attempt to substitute “political optics for sound policy”, arguing that the government had failed to properly assess the effects of its economic reforms.
He said he delayed commenting on the announcement to allow time to assess its outcomes before concluding that the policy reflected what he described as a confused approach to governance.
Obi recalled that Tinubu removed the petrol subsidy on May 29, 2023, without adequate consultation or assessment of its potential impact on the economy and the livelihoods of ordinary Nigerians.
He also faulted the subsequent floating of the naira and tax reforms, saying the policies were poorly sequenced and implemented.
According to him, the combined effects of the policies included rising inflation, higher prices of goods and services, increasing poverty, unemployment and insecurity, as well as widening inequality and the migration of young Nigerians.
“Collectively, these policies stoked inflation in all sectors, pushing in most cases unbearable price hikes across board which placed severe shocks and other adverse consequences on Nigerians,” Obi said.
The former Anambra State governor accused the federal government of failing to conduct and publish detailed regulatory impact assessments of its policies.
He argued that such assessments would enable the government to consult stakeholders and citizens and develop more inclusive and sustainable economic strategies.
Obi also questioned the potential impact of the petrol discount, which he described as less than five per cent of fuel costs.
“What really does the President Bola Tinubu-led government want to achieve with a one-month discount of less than 5% on fuel cost. Will it reduce poverty, unemployment, insecurity, and inequality? Will it increase productivity and exports?” he asked.
He further questioned whether the initiative was intended to test public reaction to a possible restoration of subsidy or was politically motivated ahead of the 2027 elections.
Obi concluded his criticism by saying the government had raised too many questions about the policy without providing answers.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, a day after an attack claimed by the Yemeni group killed at least a dozen people and forced authorities to suspend operations there.
Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh has long militarily supported the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
The Iran-backed group on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the last 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting the kingdom’s transit hubs, calling them “a theatre of operations for our forces”.
Hours later, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group reported that a projectile struck King Khalid International Airport, sparking a fire. Air defences also intercepted a missile nearby, it added.
AFP journalists and locals reported hearing the sound of multiple blasts in the Saudi capital on Sunday.
“The birds went into a frenzy after the sound. The whole house shook,” said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the north of the city.
The civil aviation authority said the attack caused an unspecified number of injuries, and that a damage assessment was under way.
It later reported another attack on Dammam airport in the east — which the Houthis also said they had targeted — a day after the Saudi coalition reported a projectile landing nearby.
– ‘Full-fledged war crime’ –
The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on the Riyadh airport — where three people were also killed on Thursday — as well as on Saudi oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
Although Saudi Arabia has poured billions into its military, Houthi attacks continue to slip through.
“Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves,” said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University.
The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday’s attack a “full-fledged war crime” and vowed to “respond decisively”.
Houthi media reported two Saudi strikes in Yemen’s Houthi-controlled Sanaa governorate on Sunday.
Saturday’s attack drew condemnation from the United Nations and leaders around the world, including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose country does not have diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia, also denounced the “horrific terrorist attack”.
Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed, the civil aviation authority said, with 309 people wounded.
The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also said one of its citizens died on Sunday after being wounded the day before.
– Operations suspended –
Authorities suspended operations at the airport into Sunday, a senior aviation source said, with air traffic monitor Flightradar24 saying the closure was extended until 2100 GMT.
A second aviation source confirmed the halt in operations “until further notice”, adding radar and communications equipment was damaged and runways needed to be assessed.
Witnesses to Saturday’s strike described chaos in the aftermath.
“People who were in Terminal 3 started running towards us,” a 32-year-old Riyadh resident told AFP.
“Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood.”
The attack prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors, a medical source said.
The US, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh airport, while Australia urged its citizens on Sunday to stay indoors altogether and “shelter in place”.
– Fighting in Yemen –
Saturday’s airport strike, on the eve of Saudi Arabia’s high-profile convention and entertainment season, was the deadliest attack in the kingdom since a 2015 suicide bombing.
With the summer heat subsiding, October also usually marks the beginning of the high travel season for Umrah pilgrims, with millions of Muslims from across the world flocking to Mecca.
Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.
Ottawa University’s Juneau said the Houthis now “want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them”.
On the ground in Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing in their counter-offensive against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a key shipping route, military sources said Saturday.
The Houthis claimed to have repelled them.
Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
By Adeola Badru
Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has admitted that the political alliance he entered into with President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2023 general election failed to deliver the national unity, fairness and competent government he expected, declaring that he regrets supporting the President.
Makinde said his decision to back Tinubu, then the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), was driven by the belief that the incoming administration would bring together capable Nigerians from different parts of the country to address the nation’s challenges, rather than govern along narrow political or regional lines.
The governor made the disclosure during a live radio interview in Ibadan on Sunday, while revisiting the circumstances that led him and other aggrieved Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governors to support Tinubu instead of their party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in the 2023 election.
Explaining the motivation behind the alliance, Makinde said he had expected the President to prioritise the national interest, notwithstanding their different political affiliations and his lack of previous direct dealings with Tinubu.
“I supported the current president, even though in another party at that time, because I thought, even though I never dealt directly with him, I thought we would do what is right for the country,” he said.
Makinde said the expectation was that the administration would pursue national cohesion, fairness and equal opportunities, particularly after eight years of President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration, which he argued made the demand for a southern presidency a question of equity.
He said his position was not merely about securing political advantage for himself or his allies but about ensuring that the country’s leadership reflected fairness and inclusion.
“I supported fairness, justice and equity. I supported a united Nigeria, a Nigeria that gives opportunity to every part of this country,” the governor said.
According to Makinde, the disagreements that culminated in the alliance with Tinubu arose from the PDP’s handling of its presidential candidacy and the party’s leadership structure ahead of the 2023 election.
He said he and other aggrieved governors believed that the emergence of Atiku, a northerner, as the PDP’s presidential candidate, while Iyorchia Ayu, also from the North-Central, remained the party’s national chairman, did not adequately address their concerns about fairness and regional balance.
“So, in 2023, we felt that after eight years of President Buhari who hailed from the north, the presidency should come to the south,” he said.
Makinde disclosed that he initially supported the presidential ambition of the then Rivers State Governor, Nyesom Wike, within the PDP, but the party eventually settled for Atiku, deepening the disagreement between the party’s leadership and the group of governors who had demanded a different political arrangement.
He said the group sought to resolve the dispute by persuading the PDP leadership to replace Ayu with Taofeek Arapaja, who was then the party’s Deputy National Chairman (South), as part of efforts to address the question of regional balance.
Recounting a meeting with Atiku in London, Makinde said the request was straightforward: to allow the party to change its national chairman before proceeding with the election.
“We met with him in London. The only thing I said to him in London was, allow us to go and remove Iyorchia Ayu and then make Taofeek Arapaja the acting chairman because he was the Deputy National Chairman (South) at that time,” he said.
However, the disagreement remained unresolved, prompting the aggrieved governors to explore other political options ahead of the presidential election.
Makinde said he eventually agreed to support Tinubu after an intermediary linked the group to the then APC presidential candidate, despite having no prior direct political dealings with him.
“Because I had never had any political dealings with him (Tinubu) up until that point, someone else did the linking. I said, okay, fine. If this is what we will do, we will support you,” he said.
The governor maintained that the understanding was based on expectations that a Tinubu-led administration would transcend party divisions and assemble a team capable of addressing Nigeria’s economic and governance challenges.
He said he repeatedly made the expectations clear during the election campaign, stressing that the country needed a government built around competence and national unity.
“But even as a candidate, I must have mentioned it three or four times that our expectation would be a government of national unity; a government of national competence where you could start the process of resetting this country,” Makinde said.
However, assessing the administration against those expectations, the governor expressed dissatisfaction with what he described as a failure to establish the kind of inclusive and competence-driven government he had anticipated.
“But is it what we are seeing right now? Is it a government of national competence? Is it a government of national unity? The answer is no,” he said.
Makinde also recounted an episode involving a proposed ministerial appointment, saying Tinubu had asked him to recommend a candidate for a ministerial position.
According to the governor, he submitted the name of an Oyo indigene whom he considered suitable for the position of Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, but the nominee was not appointed to the portfolio.
Instead, Adebayo Adelabu, another Oyo-born politician, was appointed Minister of Power.
Makinde said the episode contributed to his concerns about the political understanding between him and the President, although he maintained that his principal concern remained the quality and inclusiveness of governance at the national level.
He further disclosed that Tinubu had indicated an interest in having him help organise the APC in Oyo State, an offer he rejected on the grounds that he remained a member of the PDP.
Quoting his response to the President, Makinde said: “No, sir, I can never help you organise APC in Oyo State because I am of the PDP.”
The governor’s latest remarks come against the backdrop of his subsequent decision to pursue his own presidential ambition, marking a significant shift from the alliance that helped shape the 2023 presidential contest.
In May 2026, Makinde formally declared his presidential ambition under an alliance between the PDP and the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), presenting the arrangement as part of a broader effort to establish an alternative political platform.
He has also argued that Nigeria requires a viable opposition to prevent the country from drifting towards a one-party state, maintaining that political differences should not eliminate democratic competition.
Reiterating why he had supported Tinubu in 2023, Makinde said he had believed the President would bring together capable people from across the country to help address the nation’s problems and initiate a process of national renewal.
“Reset the country, like I said, bring people from all over that can help the country. But unfortunately, that is not what we’re seeing. So I regret that action. Yes, I do,” he said.
The governor also defended his decision to publicly acknowledge his regret, saying responsible leadership required the willingness to admit mistakes and apologise when necessary.
He said no individual possessed complete knowledge of future events and that political decisions could sometimes produce outcomes different from those anticipated.
“I’m also not afraid to apologise to people when I wrong them, because it’s only God that is all-knowing, that knows the end from the beginning,” Makinde said.
The post 2023 Tinubu alliance failed to deliver national unity, competent govt – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Khalid Mehmood
items.content:
The federal government took control of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P) affairs on Sunday after imposing an emergency and governor's rule in the province, deploying the army to assist the civil administration, forming an 11-member advisory council and establishing a special administrative structure for 12 districts.
Meanwhile, roadblocks sealed key areas of Peshawar, public transport was suspended, educational institutions were ordered closed and matriculation examinations postponed, while police arrested dozens of PTI workers in Swabi amid unconfirmed claims that former chief minister Sohail Afridi and provincial party president Junaid Akbar had also been detained.
President Asif Ali Zardari imposed the emergency under Article 232 of the Constitution, citing escalating terrorist attacks, threats to citizens' lives and property, and attacks on government installations, infrastructure and law-enforcement personnel.
The proclamation said the provincial government had failed to take adequate measures against terrorism and referred to the governor's report highlighting a breakdown in the constitutional system.
Issued under Articles 232(1) and 234(1), the proclamation declared that the provincial government could not function in accordance with the Constitution under the prevailing circumstances. It empowered the federal government to direct the governor to assume some or all provincial government functions, while the powers of the provincial assembly would be exercised by Parliament or under its authority.
The chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general ceased to hold office with immediate effect. The federal government subsequently authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets under Article 245 to protect citizens, property and government installations for the duration of the emergency proclamation.
Under the deployment order, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi will determine the number of troops and resources required. The federal government also constituted an 11-member advisory council to assist the governor in administering the province.
Its members are Tariq Mahmood Pasha, Dr Amir Abdullah, Lieutenant General (retd) Nigar Johar, Samar Bilour, Dr Sarfaraz Ali, Aamir Javed, Dr M Irshad, Kifayatullah, Tayyab Qureshi, Usman Saifullah Khan and Asif Rafiq. Sanaullah Advocate was appointed the provincial advocate general.
The council held its first meeting at the Governor House under Governor Kundi's chairmanship. Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed briefed members on the law and order situation, while the governor acknowledged the challenges facing the administration and called for responsible and timely decisions.
Kundi said corruption would not be tolerated and stressed that the administration would focus on restoring peace, security, stability and development. He said strengthening the police and Counter-Terrorism Department would be a priority, alongside dismantling the wider support systems sustaining terrorism, including facilitation, financing, recruitment, extremist networks, illegal weapons, drugs and unlawful movement.
The governor also called for effective implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) and other counterterrorism measures. He said the province had paid a heavy price for terrorism, with police personnel, soldiers, Levies personnel, government employees, religious scholars, teachers, traders and ordinary citizens among those killed.
Later, a special security meeting chaired by Kundi reviewed terrorist threats and the overall security situation. The chief secretary, police chief, members of the advisory council, officials dealing with tribal and home affairs, senior police and CTD officers, and intelligence representatives attended. Participants were briefed that conditions across the province remained peaceful and normal following the emergency's imposition.
The meeting pledged to strengthen law enforcement agencies and improve their operational capacity, while the governor said he and his council would remain available to support the police and security forces.
In another administrative move, the federal government ordered the immediate establishment of an Area Development Secretariat (ADS) to oversee law and order, public safety, governance and development in 12 designated districts: Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan Upper and South Waziristan.
The ADS will operate under an Area Representative and Development Council headed by the additional chief secretary, who will also serve as administrator for the designated districts. The administrator will exercise powers over administration, security, law enforcement and development, issue directions to civil administration, police and military officials, supervise departments and order the allocation or transfer of funds.
Provincial officers and personnel in the designated districts will fall under the secretariat's administrative and operational control. The new arrangement is intended to coordinate federal departments, the armed forces and provincial institutions in implementing measures concerning security, economic stability, relief and the provision of basic services.
The federal government also appointed Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan as K-P chief secretary with immediate effect. The grade-22 Pakistan Administrative Service officer, who belongs to Mardan, previously served as secretary of the Power Division. The services of grade-20 officer Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada were also placed at the disposal of the provincial government.
Security restrictions meanwhile brought much of Peshawar's Cantonment and adjoining areas to a standstill. Containers blocked major roads leading to the Provincial Assembly, Governor House, Khyber Road and other government installations, while markets in Saddar and surrounding commercial areas remained closed or partially open. TransPeshawar suspended Bus Rapid Transit services, and authorities reported the closure of educational institutions in Peshawar district on Monday.
All educational boards across K-P also postponed matriculation examinations scheduled for October 12 until further notice. The examinations had initially been scheduled to begin on October 7 before being deferred to October 12 amid the PTI's long march.
Police began detaining PTI workers in Swabi after the emergency was imposed, with police sources putting the number arrested at 59. PTI claimed that Afridi and Junaid Akbar had also been arrested, but the administration had not confirmed their detention.
The emergency followed an increasingly strained relationship between the federal government and the PTI-led provincial administration, particularly over counterterrorism policy and engagement with the Afghan Taliban. The two sides' differences had contributed to the breakdown of talks on October 3, while PTI maintained that it had been excluded from security decisions affecting the province.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The federal cabinet on Sunday recommended that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif advise the president to invoke Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution to impose an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), citing the deteriorating security situation and the provincial government's detachment from the fight against terrorism.
The cabinet meeting, chaired by the prime minister, reviewed the worsening law and order situation and rising terrorist violence in the province. Members were given a comprehensive briefing on the security crisis before recommending the invocation of the constitutional provisions.
Addressing the meeting, Shehbaz criticised the K-P government for failing to tackle rising terrorism, saying the federal government would no longer remain a silent spectator. He expressed particular concern over the situation in Tank and Dera Ismail Khan, where residents have borne the brunt of terrorist attacks, and condemned the provincial leadership's silence and lack of empathy towards victims.
The prime minister said that, despite two days of negotiations between federal coalition leaders from the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and a Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) delegation, K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had rejected the final consensus draft at the eleventh hour.
"Despite reaching a finalised draft agreement, the K-P chief minister backed out at the eleventh hour," he said, alleging that the move reflected a lack of willingness to pursue peace. He added that calls to cancel upcoming protest marches had been met with defiance.
Shehbaz further accused the provincial leadership of undermining efforts to secure political agreement, while praising coalition leaders Rana Sanaullah, Mohsin Naqvi, Amir Muqam, Syed Naveed Qamar and Sherry Rehman, as well as mediator Maulana Fazlur Rehman, for participating in the two-day negotiations.
Criticising the provincial leadership over its "sinister role" and attempts to "invade Islamabad to reenact past foul play", Shehbaz said: "We will not remain silent in the face of such a situation. The law will take its course; we will not allow such acts."
He accused the provincial leadership of prioritising political obstruction over the safety of its citizens and urged cabinet members to take firm decisions to address the escalating security crisis. "They ruled for 13 years and are now pushing Pakistan to destruction," he said.
The prime minister recalled that all four provinces had voluntarily agreed under the 2010 National Finance Commission (NFC) Award to allocate an additional 1% share of financial resources to K-P. He said the allocation had amounted to roughly Rs800 billion over the years and was intended to strengthen the province's police force against terrorism.
Shehbaz said the funds were meant to bolster Counter-Terrorism Departments (CTDs), fortify police stations, improve intelligence capabilities, recruit personnel and procure modern weapons but neither the police nor the CTD had been meaningfully strengthened, while terrorism continued unchecked.
He criticised the provincial leadership for failing to condemn terrorist attacks or express sympathy for families whose children had been orphaned by violence. "Instead of standing up against terrorists, they are not only silent, but the situation is getting worse every day," he said, adding that the provincial government's alleged detachment from the counter-terrorism campaign amounted to aiding the menace.
Accusing the provincial leadership of plotting to march on Islamabad, the prime minister warned against a repeat of past disorder, disruption and economic damage. He said Pakistan's hard-won macroeconomic stability, reflected in State Bank reserves, controlled inflation and targeted fuel subsidies benefiting more than 50 million citizens, would not be sacrificed to political enmity.
 
Gulf mediation
The prime minister also highlighted Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to ease tensions in the Gulf and secure ceasefires, saying Islamabad was working closely with Saudi Arabia and Qatar while engaging with Iran.
He acknowledged the roles of Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in these efforts. Shehbaz condemned regional escalations and threats to key waterways, including the Bab-al-Mandab Strait, as well as drone attacks targeting holy sites.
 
President promulgates
Later, the advice to promulgate emergency in K-P was sent to the president, which was approved by Zardari, according to the President Secretariat Media Wing. "The President approved and signed the summary upon the Prime Minister's advice under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan," it said.
(WITH INPUTS FROM APP)

items.content:

Air France is now enforcing an Israeli order that keeps pilots and cabin crew with certain nationalities — including from Muslim-majority countries such as Pakistan — off flights to Israel, according to a Middle East Eye report on a Mediapart investigation.
The restrictions cover 31 nationalities. Those listed include Algerian, Tunisian, Iranian, and Pakistani. French citizens who also hold one of those nationalities are affected as well.
The directive targets nationality rather than religion. In practice, it excludes Muslim pilots and cabin crew from those countries from operating into Israel.
Air France Warns Staff Over Second Nationality
Air France told affected employees they can no longer operate flights to Israel under Israeli instructions. The airline also warned staff to declare a second nationality. Failure to do so could bring disciplinary sanctions, Mediapart reported.
Enforcement could expose Air France to a legal challenge in France. The airline has not publicly commented on Mediapart’s findings. Middle East Eye said it contacted Air France and had received no reply by publication.
Israeli Order Covers Countries Without Diplomatic Ties
Israeli broadcaster N12 reported that Israel’s Ministry of Transport issued the directive on 1 October. Airlines must ensure that pilots and flight attendants entering Israeli airspace do not hold the nationality — or dual nationality — of a country without diplomatic relations with Israel.
Channel 13 reported that at least one unnamed Israeli airline is running background checks on about 2,500 pilots and cabin crew.
Ban Follows Alleged Flydubai Hijack Attempt
The order comes after an alleged attempt by an Omani flydubai co-pilot to seize control of a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight on 30 September and crash it into a terminal at Ben Gurion Airport. The co-pilot told UAE investigators he acted alone. Those accounts have not been independently verified.
The suspect previously worked for Oman Air and Royal Air Maroc. He joined flydubai in January 2026. ProPakistani earlier covered related reporting on the FlyDubai pilot case and the Omani co-pilot incident.

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
Air France is enforcing an Israeli Transport Ministry order that bars pilots and cabin crew who hold the nationality — or dual nationality — of countries without diplomatic relations with Israel from flights to Israel and from entering Israeli airspace, according to a Mediapart investigation reported by Middle East Eye.
The restrictions cover 31 nationalities. The list includes Algerian, Tunisian, Iranian, and Pakistani citizens. French dual nationals who also hold one of the listed nationalities are affected as well.
What The Israeli Order Requires
Israeli broadcaster N12 reported that Israel’s Ministry of Transport issued the directive on 1 October 2026. It requires airlines to ensure that pilots and flight attendants entering Israeli airspace do not hold the nationality or dual nationality of a country without formal diplomatic relations with Israel.
Mediapart obtained an internal Air France note that relayed the Israeli instructions to pilots and cabin crew. Staff were told they could no longer operate flights to Israel under those rules. The airline also warned employees to declare a second nationality. Failure to comply may lead to disciplinary sanctions, according to the investigation.
Why Pakistani Crew Are Affected
Pakistan is among the 31 countries named in coverage of the ban. Reporting based on Mediapart’s documents and other regional outlets lists Pakistan alongside Afghanistan, Algeria, Bangladesh, Iran, Oman, Tunisia, and others that do not maintain formal diplomatic ties with Israel.
Countries that have normalized relations with Israel, such as Morocco and the United Arab Emirates, are not covered by the same nationality filter, according to French-language coverage of the note.
Related: FlyDubai Pilot Wanted to Do 9/11 Style Attack in Israel.
Link To The Alleged Flydubai Incident
The order followed an alleged attempt by an Omani flydubai co-pilot to seize control of a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight on 30 September 2026 and crash it into a terminal at Ben Gurion Airport. The co-pilot told UAE investigators that he had acted alone. Neither the Israeli nor the UAE account has undergone independent verification.
ProPakistani earlier covered the alleged incident: Omani Co-Pilot Stabs Indian Pilot to Crash FlyDubai Flight Full of Israeli Citizens.
Israeli Airlines Also Checking Crew
Israeli Channel 13 reported that at least one unnamed Israeli airline was conducting background checks on about 2,500 pilots and cabin crew working in the country’s aviation sector.
Air France Response And Legal Questions
Middle East Eye said Air France did not reply to its request for comment by publication. French coverage, including reporting cited by The Times of Israel, said Air France told Le Monde and AFP that it must comply with admission rules set by destination countries for passengers and staff.
Mediapart and other outlets noted that enforcing nationality-based restrictions could expose the airline to legal challenges under French labour and anti-discrimination law. Some French politicians publicly criticised the move after the internal note became public.
Air France has not issued a detailed public statement addressing Mediapart’s findings beyond noting that it must follow destination-country admission rules.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Erling Haaland said Manchester City’s 3-0 win at 10-man Liverpool showed they will “stick together” after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.
Haaland put City ahead at Anfield on Sunday before Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki netted to silence Anfield after Liverpool fans barraged them with taunts about the guilty verdict.
Enzo Maresca’s side showed no signs of being fazed by the abuse in their first match since the club discovered an independent commission had found them guilty of breaking over 100 financial regulations.
City, who are appealing against the decision, could face a massive points deduction that would likely lead to relegation or even be stripped of their titles.
But for now Norway striker Haaland insisted their defiant performance at old rivals Liverpool proved they are still committed to the City cause.
“Every single person that is part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time,” he said.
“It was hard, but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone. It’s always tough to come here.
“Important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That’s the only thing we can do.”
City were helped by Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch’s red card for two bookings just prior to Haaland’s opener.
They ran riot after that to move three points clear at the top of the Premier League.
Whether they are able to maintain a title challenge with a potential punishment looming remains to be seen.
Haaland said City’s players can only concentrate on their performances while the club’s Abu Dhabi-based owners deal with the legal ramifications of the verdict.
“You want to win games, it’s as simple as that. Perform well, play good football and win games. This was a mental battle,” he said.
“Proud that we managed to stick together, we are mentally strong. Plenty of games coming up so time to recover and go again.”
City midfielder Elliot Anderson delivered a composed display in his first taste of the rivalry with Liverpool after his close-season move from Nottingham Forest.
The England international echoed Haaland’s assessment of his side’s spirit, saying: “Togetherness, fight, a tough place to come and we stuck together and fought for each other. We’ve showed courage.
“The atmosphere was more than normal, arriving into Anfield and the first 10 minutes of the game.
“We did well to quieten the crowd. Struggled first half but second we were better and then the goals came.”

items.title: Zelensky says Russia hit power plant ‘after’ Trump’s energy ceasefire announcement
items.summary:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday that Russia had attacked an energy plant after US President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between the two countries.
“The Russians struck a power plant in Kyiv with a ‘shahed’ drone,” Zelensky said in a social media post, adding that strikes on other energy facilities followed in the Kharkiv region.
“And all of this happened AFTER the President of the United States made his statement about an energy ceasefire,” he added.
Earlier Sunday, US President Donald Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt strikes on each other’s energy infrastructure.
Zelensky was quick to say this was news to him and there has so far been no response from Moscow.
Vanguard News

By Udeme Akpan & Obas Esiedesa, Abuja
Days after the Federal Government announced measures to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices on consumers, petroleum marketers have increased petrol pump prices by up to N29 per litre in Abuja.
Checks across the nation’s capital on Sunday showed that AA Rano and AYM Shafa increased their pump prices to N1,409 per litre from N1,380 per litre last week.
Similarly, an NNPC Retail outlet in Azhata, Jikwoyi District, increased its pump price to N1,405 per litre from N1,380, while MRS, a partner retail outlet of Dangote Refinery, raised its price to N1,405 per litre from N1,370.
The increases came despite the Federal Government’s petrol discount initiative, under which the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) extended its N66-per-litre discount until October 31, 2026.
The discount, introduced on October 1 to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary, reduced NNPC Retail’s N1,405 pump price to N1,339 per litre for customers who pay digitally through its mobile application.
The Federal Government said the initiative was being funded through NNPC Retail’s decision to forgo its profit margin rather than through public funds, stressing that it did not amount to a return to petrol subsidy.
In Lagos, some stations in Ikorodu and other locations sold petrol at N1,360 per litre, while outlets in Coker, Orile and Second Rainbow retailed the product at N1,350 per litre.
However, some independent oil marketers sold petrol at between N1,360 and N1,400 per litre, depending on location.
The latest increases reflect continuing pressure on domestic petrol prices following the rise in global crude oil prices amid the Middle East conflict.
In a statement, NNPC Limited said its discount was intended to provide relief to consumers during the period of elevated global market uncertainty.
It stated: “We recognise that higher petrol prices affect everyday life, from the cost of commuting to the expenses of running a business. We understand the strain on families and livelihoods, and this discount is intended to provide direct relief to customers during this difficult period.
“Following the statement by the Honourable Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, on 8 October 2026, NNPC Limited reiterates its commitment to working with the government and stakeholders to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices on households, businesses and the wider economy.
“Before the announcement, NNPC Limited had introduced a sales discount on 1 October 2026 to commemorate Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary. This will now continue until 31 October 2026 across NNPC Retail stations nationwide. This discount is a customer relief initiative and does not represent the reintroduction of petroleum subsidy.
“This initiative supports the government’s responsible and proactive approach to providing practical relief to Nigerians during a period of heightened global market uncertainty. The initiative applies to NNPC Retail outlets and does not establish a uniform national pump price or alter the market-based pricing framework applicable to petroleum products.
“NNPC Limited remains committed to reliable product supply and collaboration with the government and stakeholders to help ease the burden on Nigerians. We therefore urge the public to disregard any interpretation of this discount as a subsidy restoration.”
It added: “We appreciate Nigerians’ continued patronage and support, and remain committed to clear communication about our products, prices and customer initiatives.”

By Luminous Jannamike
ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has accused the Kano State Police Command of suppressing dissent after operatives allegedly disrupted a ‘Tinubu Must Go’ rally and arrested the owner of the venue where it was held.
The council said the incident at The Avenue Event Center, Kano, exposed the tension between the government’s democratic claims and citizens’ right to protest, warning that police action could neither silence public frustration nor erase anger over hunger, insecurity and the rising cost of living.
In a statement on Sunday by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the council said the rally, led by Barrister Abba Hikima and organised by concerned youths, was disrupted when police operatives barricaded the venue and allegedly intimidated participants.
“This is not democracy. This is tyranny. For how long will the APC continue to use the police to suppress dissenting voices?” Ologbondiyan queried.
The ADC-PCC expressed particular outrage over the reported arrest of the event centre owner for allegedly allowing the gathering, questioning why a business owner should face arrest for providing a venue for a peaceful assembly.
“The message from Kano is loud and clear: Nigerians are tired, hungry and angry. You can stop a rally and arrest a venue owner, but you cannot arrest hunger in the land. You cannot barricade the anger and frustration of over 200 million people,” Ologbondiyan said.
The council accused the APC-led government of misdirecting its priorities, arguing that the effort deployed to stop the rally should instead be channelled into tackling insecurity, banditry and the cost-of-living crisis.
“If the APC government had deployed the same energy it used to stop a peaceful rally at The Avenue Event Center to tackle insecurity, banditry and the excruciating cost of living, Nigeria would be a safer and more prosperous nation,” he added.
The ADC-PCC commended Hikima and the participating youths for standing their ground despite the reported police intimidation. It also urged the Inspector-General of Police and the Kano State Police Command to ensure the immediate and unconditional release of the venue owner, if still in custody, and refrain from actions that could turn the police into an instrument of political oppression.
The council further called on civil society organisations, human rights groups and the international community to monitor what it described as an erosion of democratic freedoms.
“The right to protest is not a privilege granted by the police or the APC; it is a right guaranteed by the Constitution. No amount of intimidation will stop Nigerians from demanding change,” the statement said.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…Denies government involvement in NDC airport, secretariat incidents
Says Mbah’s performance more than enough to win free, fair election
The Enugu State Government said it has uncovered alleged plans by some opposition elements to import armed thugs and bandits into the state to create panic and a false sense of insecurity ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Prof. Chidiebere Onyia, made these known on Sunday while addressing a press conference at the Government House, Enugu, on the incidents involving the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport and the party’s state secretariat in Enugu on Saturday.
Onyia denied any involvement of the government or the Governor’s Chief Security Officer, Ifeanyi Osondu, in both incidents, describing the airport confrontation as a matter between the NDC and federal authorities, while noting that the shooting incident at the party’s secretariat was under police investigation.
According to the SSG, the government’s preliminary findings indicated that the airport incident followed the NDC’s attempt to hold what it described as a “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” at the facility without securing the necessary approval from the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN).
He said the party had published notices inviting its members and supporters to the event, including on the Facebook page of its governorship candidate in the state.
Onyia explained that the police had advised the party to obtain FAAN’s approval before security personnel could be deployed to the airport for the event.
“Further findings, however, revealed that the NDC did not secure the approval of FAAN to host a grand statewide rally at its facility. Security agencies, therefore, advised the organisers of the rally to rethink it,” he said.
The SSG alleged that the party proceeded to mobilise its members to the airport and attempted to gain entry into the facility, resulting in a confrontation with airport authorities.
He said security agencies intervened to disperse the “riotous” party members and restore order around the airport, which he described as a strategic national asset.
Onyia added that the state government’s account was consistent with the statement issued by the Enugu State Police Command on Sunday.
NDC Secretariat Shooting
On the shooting incident at the NDC state secretariat in the GRA area of Enugu, the SSG said security reports had established that a violent clash occurred at the party’s office and that the police were investigating the matter.
The SSG disputed reports alleging fatalities, stating that the government’s findings indicated that no death had occurred in the incident.
He disclosed that a 43-year-old man, identified as Ifeanyi Nworie, sustained a gunshot wound and was taken to the Enugu State University Teaching Hospital, Park Lane, where he was stabilised before being transferred to the National Orthopaedic Hospital, Enugu, for further examination.
“We can, therefore, authoritatively report that there were no deaths as falsely claimed by some reports and NDC leaders,” he said.
Onyia also faulted allegations that the Governor’s Chief Security Officer was present at the party secretariat and supervised the shooting, maintaining that the official was with Governor Peter Mbah at the Teachers Grassroots Movement mega rally at Okpara Square, Enugu, at the time of the incident.
The SSG further criticised the reported holding of a minute’s silence for an individual he said was still alive, describing it as an attempt to mislead the public for political advantage.
Reaffirming the state government’s position, Onyia said Governor Mbah had sworn to protect the lives and property of all residents, irrespective of their religious beliefs or political affiliations, and condemned.
He said the administration’s ambition to grow Enugu into a $30 billion economy and make it a preferred destination for investment, business, tourism and living depended significantly on sustained peace and security.
According to him, this informed the government’s substantial investments in security infrastructure and operations over the past three years.
“Consequently, the Enugu State Government strongly condemns in its entirety any form of violence, including politically induced violence in the state. We welcome healthy debate and freedom of association and peaceful assembly,” he said.
He, however, urged political parties and their candidates to exercise restraint and embrace issue-based campaigns ahead of the 2027 elections.
The SSG said democratic rights should be exercised responsibly, arguing that political parties ought to serve as models of decorum and integrity.
He questioned the decision to announce a statewide campaign flag-off at the airport and without the approval of the relevant authorities.
“Without holding brief for FAAN, is it not sheer rascality to attempt to hold a “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” of the NDC at the airport as publicised by the party and its gubernatorial candidate, especially without the approval by the appropriate authorities?
“Is it not equally gross mischief and a sign of political desperation to hold a minute silence for a living person, just to mislead the public for political traction?” he queried.
Onyia accused opposition elements in the state of attempting to create the impression that Enugu was unsafe and that the government was intolerant of opposing political parties.
He alleged that some opposition groups had been attributing internal disagreements and violent clashes to the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state.
As an example, he cited the September 12, 2026 incident at Obuofia in Nkanu West Local Government Area, claiming that investigations had identified the alleged perpetrators, who were being prosecuted by the police.
The SSG described the opposition as factionalised and alleged that some of its members were seeking to draw the state government into controversies for political relevance.
Onyia also reiterated the government’s allegation that some opposition elements were plotting to bring armed thugs and bandits into Enugu to create panic and undermine public confidence in the state’s security ahead of the 2027 general elections.
“We, however, make bold to say that the peace and security we have achieved in Enugu State in the last three years, and at huge material costs and sacrifices by our security agents, are non-negotiable and irreversible,” he said.
The SSG said the Mbah administration remained committed to protecting citizens’ democratic rights, including the freedom to campaign for and vote for candidates of their choice in the forthcoming elections.
He described the right of residents to elect their leaders through free, fair and credible polls as fundamental to the state’s democratic development.
Onyia added that the government was confident of securing a second term for Mbah based on what it described as the governor’s performance and delivery on campaign promises.
“Indeed, these inalienable rights of Ndi Enugu to elect their leaders in free, fair and credible polls are our surest hope for re-election come 2027,” he said.
He added that the administration had no reason to resort to desperate measures, maintaining that its record in office would be the basis for seeking a renewed mandate from the electorate.

Amnesty International Nigeria has condemned the alleged blocking of a “Tinubu-Must-Go” event in Kano State, accusing the police of violating the rights to freedom of association and peaceful assembly.
The human rights organisation disclosed this in a post on its X platform on Sunday, saying heavily armed police officers blocked both ends of the road leading to the venue of the event.

“The Nigeria Police must desist from such reckless violation of human rights. It is perfectly within the rights of supporters of all candidates and all political parties to carry out peaceful political activities,” the organisation said.
It maintained that the police had a responsibility to facilitate peaceful political gatherings, regardless of the political party or candidate being supported or opposed.
“The duty of the police is to facilitate peaceful conduct of such political gatherings — no matter the political party or candidate being supported or opposed,” Amnesty said.
The organisation stressed that freedom of association and peaceful assembly was not exclusive to any political party or its supporters.
It further described the Kano incident as part of what it called a troubling pattern of police repression targeting opposition members in different parts of the country.
According to Amnesty, repeated attacks and intimidation against opposition supporters could undermine their ability to associate freely and organise peaceful public gatherings.
The organisation did not provide further details about the event or the police operation in its post.

items.content:
— Says politicians who ruined state over 24 years are back
By Steve Oko
UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has warned voters against trading the state’s future for paltry financial inducements ahead of the 2027 general elections, cautioning that accepting as little as ₦5,000, ₦10,000, rice or wrappers from politicians could mortgage the state’s destiny for another four years.
Otti, who spoke on Sunday through his Chief of Staff, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, at the Second Session of the Seventh Synod of the Anglican Communion, Aba Ngwa North Diocese, alleged that politicians responsible for Abia’s 24 years of underdevelopment were returning to seek the people’s support.
He urged voters to scrutinise the records and intentions of politicians rather than allow temporary material benefits to influence their choices at the polls.
The synod, held at All Saints Anglican Cathedral, Abayi, Umuocham, Aba, had the theme, “Don’t Just Absorb It; Think It Through,” drawn from Acts 17:11-12.
Warning that the consequences of selling votes could outlast the immediate benefits, Otti said, “Don’t use the ₦5,000, the ₦10,000, the wrapper or the rice they will give you and close the destiny of Abians for the next four years. Even prayer and fasting will not open it.”
He added, “May we not lose what God has given to us on a platter of gold.”
The governor also cautioned Christians against being swayed by politicians who, according to him, had suddenly become attentive to the church and its members as the election season approached.
“Many of them who have not been coming to church have started coming to church. Many of them who have not been accepting or taking your calls have suddenly started calling you. If you call them and you miss their call, they call you back. Those are devices,” he said.
Otti urged the electorate to examine such political overtures critically and make informed decisions about the state’s future.
‘Next four years for consolidation’
The governor said his administration had spent its first three years laying the foundation for Abia’s development, expressing confidence that the next four years, beginning in 2027, would focus on consolidating the gains recorded so far.
“Those who build houses will understand that foundation-laying is the most crucial, and the foundation has been laid after 24 years of ruins,” he said.
According to him, the next phase would bring consolidation and further development, adding that Abia had become a point of reference.
On the church’s development projects, Otti assured the congregation of his administration’s support while reiterating that public funds must be deployed for the overall development of the state rather than individual religious projects.
He also urged Christians to verify information and think critically before reaching conclusions, saying the church had an important role to play in changing the country’s negative narratives.
“Christians, we have the capacity to change the negative narrative of this nation, and especially our state,” he said.
Church leaders preach political discernment
Earlier, the Bishop of Aba Ngwa North Diocese, Rt. Rev. Dr Nathan Kanu, said the synod’s theme challenged Christians to move beyond merely hearing messages to examining issues prayerfully and responding wisely.
Kanu commended Otti for identifying with the church and supporting its activities. He also presented gifts to the governor’s representative and prayed for God’s blessings upon the governor and his administration.
In his sermon, the guest speaker and Bishop of Ohaji/Egbema Diocese, Rt. Rev. Chidi Oparajiaku, urged Christians to examine what they hear before taking action.
Speaking on “The Bereans’ Wisdom,” with texts from Acts 17:12-15, Oparajiaku said the synod’s theme was particularly relevant in the present circumstances.
“It didn’t say throw it away; it says think through it,” he said, regretting that some Christians had become vulnerable to deception because they failed to examine issues in the light of biblical teachings.
“When members of the church know the Bible, they would not be deceived,” he added.
The cleric also thanked God for giving Abia Governor Otti, whom he credited with changing the state’s narrative.

By Luminous Jannamike
ABUJA – Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disclose who is printing sensitive materials for the 2027 elections, warning that opaque contracts and key departmental redeployments could undermine confidence in the polls.
His central concern is that Nigerians could head into a decisive election without knowing who is producing their ballots, how the contracts were awarded or what safeguards exist against political interference.
In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, for the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku demanded explanations for reported changes in INEC’s Electoral Operations Department and allegations that a substantial share of sensitive election materials had been allocated to private contractors.
Reports indicate that Director Isa Magaji Gum was moved from Electoral Operations to the Voter Registry Department, while Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi was appointed to head Electoral Operations. Dr Lawrence Bayode was also identified as head of Information and Communication Technology.
“These departments are at the heart of election administration. INEC must explain these decisions, publish the criteria applied and show that every appointment and redeployment followed due process, was based on merit and was free from political interference.”
Atiku also demanded that INEC confirm or deny whether Hitech, or any company associated with it, had secured a contract to print sensitive election materials.
He alleged that more than half of the materials, including presidential ballot assets, might have been allocated to an undisclosed company believed to be based in France. He further questioned reports that the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Plc was printing materials for only 15 to 17 states, leaving private firms to handle the remainder.
“Nigerians should not have to depend on unnamed sources to discover who is producing their ballots,” he said, demanding the disclosure of contractors, allocations, procurement methods and security arrangements.
Atiku argued that any contract awarded to Hitech or an associated company would raise questions about INEC’s neutrality, citing publicly reported business ties between the Chagoury family, which owns Hitech, and the Tinubu family.
The former vice-president also pointed to controversy surrounding Hitech contracts under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, including the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway project.
“If neither Hitech nor a company associated with it has been selected, INEC must say so clearly and put the matter beyond doubt,” he said.
He urged the Central Bank of Nigeria to disclose its banknote-printing allocations and explain the roles of domestic and foreign contractors, while calling on INEC to maximise domestic security-printing capacity and ensure every ballot and result sheet is protected by a transparent chain of custody.
Atiku warned that Nigerians battered by economic hardship would resist any attempt to subvert their votes, insisting that the 2027 election must not become an instrument for prolonging the Tinubu administration’s hold on power.
“Let there be no mistake: Nigerians will not accept a stolen election. Any attempt to rig the 2027 polls will be met with determined resistance through the ballot, lawful civic action, and every other democratic channel available to the people.”
He said the ADC would monitor INEC’s preparations and alert domestic and international observers to any lack of transparency, insisting that the commission must prove its impartiality through verifiable disclosures.
