items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
A well-known Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6 leaker has threatened to release a full playable version of the highly anticipated game, claiming that players could experience the entire story mode from beginning to end. However, the authenticity of the claim remains uncertain.
The leaker, known online as “cybeleek,” made the announcement on a website. According to the post, the alleged build includes the complete story mode and allows players to finish the game and reach the end credits.
GTA 6 Leaker Threatens to Release Full Playable Version of the Game
The threat has attracted attention because GTA 6 remains one of the most anticipated video games, with Rockstar Games keeping most details about its story and gameplay under wraps.
GTA 6 Leaker Sets a $30 Million Condition
According to the leaker’s website, the alleged playable build will become available if a cryptocurrency linked to the leaker reaches a market capitalization of $30 million.
The post also demands that Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, apologize for not releasing a physical version of GTA 6 and make the game available in physical format. However, the leaker has not provided a deadline for these demands.
It remains unclear whether the leaker actually possesses a complete playable build or is using the claim to attract attention to the cryptocurrency project.
Previous GTA 6 Gameplay Leaks Raise Questions
The latest threat follows several earlier leaks attributed to cybeleek. The leaker has reportedly shared more than an hour of GTA 6 footage online, including a video containing around 25 minutes of gameplay.
Some of the leaked footage also appears to contain modified character models and scenes. These details have raised questions about the source and condition of the material.
Many online observers believe the footage may come from an older development build rather than the latest version of the game. If that is the case, the alleged playable version might not represent the final product planned for release.
The possibility of a complete game leak remains unverified. The leaker has not provided enough publicly confirmed evidence to establish that the build exists in the claimed form.
Players should also avoid visiting suspicious websites claiming to host leaked game files, as such pages may contain malware or attempt to steal personal information.
See Also: Delayed Again? GTA 6 Online Could Take Years to Arrive After the Game’s Launch
GTA 6 Release Date Remains November 19, 2026
Rockstar Games currently plans to release Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19, 2026. The game is scheduled to arrive on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
With the release date approaching, any genuine leak of the full game could have significant consequences for Rockstar Games and its publisher, Take-Two Interactive. However, there is currently no confirmed evidence that the alleged build will be released.
For now, the threat should be treated with caution. Until the leaker provides verifiable proof, it remains uncertain whether the claim represents a genuine leak or simply another attempt to gain attention before the game’s launch.

The Budhi Gandaki is ​a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing.
"We have asked ​villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe," ​said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district's most senior bureaucrat.
Read More: Resilience in the age of climate breakdown
The flood swept away about a ‌dozen ⁠houses and two suspension bridges and damaged a hydroelectric project camp, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.
The flooded river carrying muddy sludge was rising and had washed away a highway bridge ​connecting Gorkha with the ​neighbouring Dhading district, ⁠said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the Authority.
National disaster authorities alerted people living along the river in the Gorkha, ​Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi districts about ​the flood.
"Please ⁠help ensure that people in at-risk areas are moved to safe locations in time and assist search and rescue operations as needed," the National Disaster Risk Reduction ⁠and ​Management Authority said in a social media post.
Officials ​said army and police rescue personnel had reached the area and were also monitoring the situation ​from a helicopter.

This is also the heaviest win from Pakistan against Sri Lanka.
Sri Lanka were never in the run as they kept losing wickets at regular interval.
After Salman Mirza removed in-form Lahiru Udara (5) early, it was Imran Randhawa who put great pressure by picking up the wickets of Sineth Jayawardena (22), Kusal Mendis (9) and Sahan Arachchige (0) in quick succession to break the back of the visitors.
Saim Aub then had Dasun Shanaka (9) before Shadab got rid of Kamindu Mendis (23) to leave Sri Lanka gasping at 74-6.
Chamindu Wickramasinghe resisted with 24-ball 29 before falling to Salman Mirza.
Maheesh Theekshana remained top-scorer with 32 not out which featured four fours.
Imran was ably backed by his new ball partner Salman Mirza with 2-28.
Earlier Maaz Sadqat and skipper Sahibzada Farhan did a glorious job to enable Pakistan post a big total on a batting track.
Maaz and Farhan shared 88 runs off 48 balls for the second wicket stand to take the hosts to a decent total in the end.
Farhan was dropped on 12 when he skied one early in the innings. However, he capitalised on the opportunity and went on to hit his second successive fifty of the series. He brought in his fifty off 31 balls and hammered five sixes and four fours in his commanding 44-ball 73.
Earlier, he, along with Fakhar Zaman provided a rapid start to the hosts, sharing 55 off 35 balls for the opening stand.
Fakhar fell for 17-ball 22 with four fours to off-spinner Maheesh Theekshana.
Maaz, who brought in his second successive fifty off 30 balls, then went after the ball and played some superb strokes.
He also hit Theekshana for three glorious sixes in one over which yielded 22 runs.
He along with Hasan Nawaz scored a rapid 72 runs for the third wicket partnership to take Pakistan to a huge total.
Maaz hammered seven sixes and six fours in his gallant 51-ball 96.
He lost his wicket off the final ball of the innings when he went for a big hit in a bid to complete his century but was held in the deep.
Hasan Nawaz remained not out on nine-ball 19 with one six and one four.
Pakistan scored 46 in the power-play, were 90-1 in ten overs, reached 145-2 in 15 and made 70 runs in the final five overs.
Theekshana remained the most expensive bowler as he finished with 1-55 in his quota of four overs.
Eshan Malinga (1-41) and Dasun Shanaka (1-30) were the other successful bowlers.
Earlier, Sri Lanka won the toss and elected to bowl first. Pakistan made one change, bringing in Salman Mirza in place of Razaullah who had made his T20I debut in the previous game at the same venue.
Sri Lanka made two changes.
The third and final game is scheduled for Tuesday at the same venue.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Dalal Street emerged as a founder’s paradise in 2025, with 18 Indian startups listing on the bourses and collectively mopping up a record ₹41,248 Cr from the public markets.
The surge was driven by a combination of macroeconomic tailwinds and regulatory support. While robust GDP growth projections helped revive investor appetite, SEBI’s reforms played a key role. Measures such as simplified DRHP filings reduced red tape, while more flexible ESOP rules allowed founders to retain meaningful ownership.
Retail investors also fuelled the frenzy as demat accounts crossed the 20 Cr mark. The OFS component dominated public issues last year, providing liquidity to the early backers of the new-age tech companies. Post-listing performance also followed the usual curve, with investors rewarding companies that prioritised profits, sustainable growth and governance over hype.
“⁠Besides the readiness that startups showed in their unit economics, there is also an increase in the founders committing to their businesses for next couple of decades and grow their businesses by adding adjacent profit pools – something that the public markets reward handsomely,” said Ashish Kumar, cofounder and general partner at Fundamentum Partnership.
Building on the momentum, fifteen new-age tech companies have already made their D-Street debut so far this year. Of these, ESDS Software Solution, Klassroom, RentoMojo, SEDEMAC, Kissht, LEAP India and Shiprocket made a bumper debut on the bourses.
Nevertheless, the IPO pipeline remains strong. Twenty six startups have already filed their DRHPs with SEBI, while over 25 are in various stages of finalising their IPO plans. Unicorns like OYO, Razorpay and Zetwerk alone could raise over ₹34,000 Cr in 2026, making it one of the biggest years for startup IPOs.
However, recalibration is likely to define 2026 as investors are expected to prioritise strong fundamentals, profitability and low cash burn when backing new-age tech companies.
“IPO-bound startups in 2026 will be increasingly defined by their ability to demonstrate predictable cash flows, sustainable unit economics, and operational discipline rather than headline growth alone. Public market investors will place greater emphasis on governance, capital efficiency and long-term value creation, favouring companies that balance scale with financial prudence,” Orios Venture Partners’ managing partner Rehan Yar Khan told Inc42.
There are other challenges as well. Average retail subscription levels are moderating, while foreign institutional investors (FIIs) are pulling back in droves, reflecting caution amid geopolitical tensions and muted secondary market performance. The ongoing conflict in West Asia has further complicated the situation.
Yet, the overall outlook remains bullish for new-age tech IPOs. Maturing business models, deeper domestic capital pools and an evolving regulatory framework favouring transparency position India as a leading startup IPO hub.
