items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
For years, Swiggy and Zomato have ruled the Indian foodtech sector with an iron fist, building vast restaurant networks and loyal customer bases that have made it difficult for new players to compete. But the duopoly is now facing fresh competition from three directions: Rapido’s Ownly, food delivery startup Swish’s new marketplace, Swish Go, and ecommerce giant Flipkart.
Ownly is already handling around 50,000 orders a day in Bengaluru and entered Hyderabad just two weeks ago. Swish, which started with quick food delivery, is expanding into restaurant aggregation with its new marketplace, Swish Go. Ecommerce giant Flipkart, too, is testing its food delivery service, Eat In, in Bengaluru.
All three are entering a market where consumers are already comfortable ordering food online. At the same time, restaurants are looking for alternatives to the high commissions charged by Swiggy and Zomato. But onboarding restaurants is only half the battle. What the emerging players need is to convince customers to order from their platforms regularly.
Hence, it is only natural for us to ask if these new players can challenge the dominance Swiggy and Zomato have built over the years and what gives the duopoly enough steam to keep the burgeoning rivals at bay.
Restaurants Are Hungry For An Alternative
Restaurant owners have long complained about the commissions and other charges they pay to Swiggy and Zomato. While online orders have become a major source of sales, delivery platforms can eat into margins, especially as restaurants become more dependent on them.
In July, National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI) president and Wow! Momo cofounder Sagar Daryani told Inc42 that food delivery had grown from 10% of a restaurant’s business before Covid-19 to around 50% for some restaurants.
This is where the new entrants see an opportunity. Rapido’s Ownly is trying to capitalise on the discontent by offering zero commission to restaurant partners. It has also integrated Ownly into the Rapido app, giving it access to an existing base of mobility users. The company can also draw on its delivery network for food orders, potentially reducing the cost of building a separate operation from scratch.
Ownly is already processing over 50,000 orders a day in Bengaluru. After entering Hyderabad last month, it has onboarded 10,000 restaurants in the city, with plans to expand that network to 30,000. The expansion gives Ownly a route to compete beyond Bengaluru.
Swish Go is taking a different approach. According to people familiar with the platform, its commission rates vary by order value, with one rate for orders below ₹100 and another for orders above that amount. Restaurant partners find this arrangement favourable, Inc42 has learnt. However, these attractive terms may not last forever.
An observer in the restaurant business believes Ownly could introduce commissions as it grows, with Swish Go potentially following the same path. The current offers are a way to attract restaurants that are unhappy with Swiggy and Zomato.
However, the person also questioned whether Swish ever intended to focus only on 10-minute food delivery. Established players such as Swiggy, Zepto and Rebel Foods have faced challenges with the format, making it difficult to sustain at scale.
Swish Go’s pricing also puts it in competition with Swiggy’s Toing. By waiving packaging and platform fees, Swish Go appears to be betting on a lower-cost ordering experience to attract customers.
The Real Battle Is Over The Users
Getting restaurants to join a new platform is one challenge, and convincing them to order from it regularly is another. Food delivery is already an established market, and new players must now give customers a reason to try their platforms and keep coming back.
An analyst cautioned that making money from these new services could prove difficult because their business models have not been tested at scale. This is pushing platforms towards restaurant aggregation, which allows them to offer a wider choice of food without running every kitchen themselves.
Swiggy and Zomato have also experimented with new food delivery formats, but those bets have not lasted. Swiggy shut down Snacc, its standalone app for 10-15 minute food delivery, in February 2026. Eternal, Zomato’s parent company, discontinued Zomato Quick, its 15-minute delivery service, and Zomato Everyday, which offered home-style meals, in May 2025. Earlier this year, Rebel Foods also shut down Quickies.
These show that even established platforms with large customer bases have struggled to make certain food delivery formats, primarily quick food delivery, work at scale. A new proposition may attract customers, but sustaining the business without compromising service or profitability will be crucial.
Meanwhile, a sectoral expert said that Swiggy and Zomato’s biggest moat is their large user base. But that advantage does not make their position immune to defeat.
Rapido already has a consumer base and delivery fleet it can draw on, while Swish is adding restaurants on top of its existing cloud kitchens and a loyal user base. Flipkart is also preparing to enter food delivery. With a user base of 500 Mn and the financial backing to fund expansion, Flipkart could also take a share of Swiggy and Zomato’s food delivery market. The company is likely to roll out the service before the end of 2026.
The likes of Swish and Flipkart are making moves at a time when Swiggy and Zomato remain much larger businesses. Eternal reported adjusted food delivery revenue of ₹3,537 Cr in Q1 FY27, up 33% year-on-year (YoY) from ₹2,657 Cr in Q1 FY26. This was up from around ₹3,135 Cr in Q4 FY26. Swiggy’s food delivery revenue reached ₹2,208 Cr in Q1 FY27, growing 23% from ₹1,799 Cr a year earlier and ₹2,075 Cr in the previous quarter.
Their restaurant networks are equally extensive. Zomato averaged around 3.28 lakh monthly active restaurant partners in Q1 FY27, while Swiggy reported over 2.7 lakh restaurant partners across more than 720 cities.
These numbers show the scale of the duopoly that Ownly and Swish Go must compete against. Beyond attracting restaurants with better commercial terms, the new entrants will need to build a large, active customer base and generate enough repeat orders to sustain their businesses.
They do not need to match Swiggy and Zomato across India immediately, but they must prove they can grow in select markets without relying indefinitely on low commissions and other attractive offers.
Quick Commerce: The Duopoly’s Strongest Moat
According to Anshika Jain, principal analyst at Counterpoint Research, Swiggy and Zomato’s biggest advantages are their established customer habits, wide restaurant selection and delivery networks built over years.
Ownly’s expansion into Bengaluru and Hyderabad, along with Swish Go’s Bengaluru pilot, puts these advantages to the test in local markets. Since customers and restaurants can use multiple platforms, the incumbents will need to keep their prices competitive and service reliable. Restaurants will also expect a steady flow of orders as new players offer better commercial terms.
However, Jain sees a higher entry barrier in quick commerce, which requires local inventory, supplier relationships, replenishment systems and substantial capital. These investments become defensible only when individual locations attract repeat demand and generate profits.
Quick commerce may therefore offer Swiggy and Zomato a stronger defence than food delivery alone.
For Swiggy and Zomato, food delivery remains an important source of business as they continue to invest in quick commerce. In due time, both businesses will turn self-sustaining at which point the new rivals may not have room to maneuver.
Their scale means there is a lot more that rivals have to do to compete in terms of bringing in users, but it does not prevent these new platforms from targeting restaurants with different commercial terms and undercut the two largest players.
For Flipkart, Rapido Ownly and Swish Go, the real test, for now, is whether early traction can turn into repeat orders. Only then can they loosen the duopoly’s hold.

items.content:
•He took death to the swamp so we 
  could live — Igbokoda residents 
•Black box, voice recorder, victims missing 
  seven days after tragedy
By Dayo Johnson, Akure
It was drizzling in Igbokoda on Monday morning, October 5, 2026.
 It was the kind of quiet rain that makes fishermen stay indoors and mothers keep their children close.Then the sky screamed.
Residents did not first see the aircraft, with tail number NGR 931, carrying 32 people, comprising 25 passengers and seven crew members, on a routine flight from Benin to Lagos. They heard it. A tortured, rattling roar, like metal begging for mercy.
“It sounded like the engine was coughing blood,” one fisherman told me at the edge of the swamp. “We looked up and saw it wobbling. It was coming down on our heads.”
Where to die
Residents said the aircraft was already in trouble long before it crashed. They were unanimous in their belief that, had the pilot not struggled to control it, Igbokoda could have been counting hundreds of dead.
“Honestly, the pilot should be commended,” said Jomiloju, a resident. “Many lives would have been lost. It would have been a national tragedy if he had allowed the aircraft to go down in the middle of the community. He struggled with it and brought it down inside a deep swamp, 200 metres away from the town.”
Another resident corroborated the account, saying: “If the captain had attempted to bring it down inside the town, it would have caused a bigger disaster. He eventually went into the river and crashed over there.”
In Igbokoda, the pilot is no longer just a casualty. He is regarded as a hero.
“He is a big hero because he averted a tragedy,” another resident said. “The aircraft was heading towards the community, but he manoeuvred it into the swamp. He should be celebrated in death for saving us from catastrophe. Although we are not happy, 32 persons died. They are family members who paid the ultimate price.”
Engine 
The residents’ account was echoed by Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa when he visited the crash site. According to the governor, eyewitnesses told him that the aircraft came down with a loud sound suggesting engine failure and appeared to be heading towards the town.
“But the pilot managed to manoeuvre the aircraft away from the community before it landed about 200 metres away and went straight into the swamp,” Aiyedatiwa said. “Only the pilot, if he had survived, could have explained what happened in those final moments.”
What followed was a scene the governor described as “a very gory sight”.
When he arrived at the swamp, body parts, military jackets, clothes and fragments of the aircraft were floating on water blackened by aviation fuel. The main fuselage was nowhere to be found.
“The aircraft has sunk deep. The nature and depth of the swamp could have caused it to become deeply submerged in the mud,” he said.
To reach the wreckage, the state deployed two amphibious excavators, known as swamp buggies, machines designed to float and dig at the same time. Despite the deployment, the main wreckage had yet to be recovered seven days after the crash.
Fragments
Divers from the Navy and local communities had been searching the swamp, bringing out only fragments of the aircraft.
“I saw the divers struggling to locate the main fuselage,” said the Commissioner for Environment, Dr Tob Loko. “One of them said he was able to spot it, but the small boats were insufficient to pull it out. That is why we had to deploy heavier equipment.”
The Commissioner for Works, Ayorinde Olawoye, expressed optimism that progress would soon be made.
“You can see the swamp buggy is set to float on water and go to where it happened. Within five hours, reasonable progress will be made,” he said.
However, the Commissioner for Health, Dr Banji Ajaka, painted a grimmer picture.
“It is not something a vehicle or speedboat can just go to. It has gone down with weight and force,” he said.
At the site, the Ondo State Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, who accessed the scene in a canoe, said there were no survivors.
“From what we have seen, there are no survivors. What we see is just body parts and clothes littered everywhere, floating in the water,” he said. “It is a very difficult terrain, the creeks, mangroves. Accessing the site was not easy.”
Journalists were initially denied access to the site. A television crew was reportedly arrested by Navy personnel for entering without clearance but was later released.
Voices 
For residents, the horror remained fresh.
“I was just trying to have my bath when I heard a loud noise. It was very frightening,” Jomiloju recounted. “We rushed towards the direction the sound came from. We had to sail to the location in canoes. All we saw was wreckage. The larger part of the plane was deep inside the swamp.”
Another resident, Lucky, added: “We have tried our best to rescue them, but the aircraft was deeply buried inside the swamp. Even the women and men took their canoes.”
Where is the black box?
Seven days after the crash, critical answers remained trapped in the swamp with the wreckage.
The Nigerian Air Force confirmed that the flight data recorder, commonly referred to as the black box, and the cockpit voice recorder had yet to be recovered.
“We hope to be able to find critical components of the aircraft that will speak to the investigators because the aircraft wreckage actually speaks to the investigators,”
Air Vice Marshal Ebimobo Ebiowe, NAF Superintendent of Standards and Evaluation, said at the site.
Investigation
The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, who visited Igbokoda and inspected the site, ordered a high-level investigation involving military and civilian aviation safety experts, the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau and retired senior officers.
“I have flown on this aeroplane. My family has flown on this aeroplane. I know each of the crew personally. They are highly trained, professional and intelligent officers. The best we can do is to honour the sacrifice they have made,” Aneke said, appealing to Nigerians to avoid speculation.
Governor Aiyedatiwa described the incident as a national tragedy, commiserating with President Bola Tinubu, the Nigerian Air Force and the families of the personnel who died while in active service.
Scan sonar
As of Saturday, the Navy had deployed side-scan sonar equipment to map the swamp and locate the submerged fuselage. Aviation fuel was also reported to be leaking into the water, raising concerns about pollution.
In Igbokoda, two tragedies are being mourned: the 32 lives lost in the swamp and the potentially greater tragedy that residents believe was averted by a pilot who, in his final moments, steered the aircraft away from the town.
Whenever it drizzles on a Monday morning, they will remember the day the sky screamed and a man, in their eyes, chose where to die.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Xiaomi 18 Pro Max mulai menunjukkan tanda-tanda kehadirannya di pasar internasional. Smartphone flagship tersebut terdeteksi dalam basis data Geekbench AI dengan nomor model 2611FPNFAG. Kemunculan ini mengindikasikan bahwa Xiaomi tengah menguji perangkat versi globalnya, meskipun jadwal peluncuran resminya belum diumumkan.
Sebelumnya, Xiaomi telah mengonfirmasi bahwa Xiaomi 18 Pro dan Xiaomi 18 Pro Max akan dipasarkan secara global, berbeda dari generasi sebelumnya. Jika rumor pembatalan Xiaomi 18 Ultra benar, model Pro Max berpotensi menjadi salah satu perangkat flagship tertinggi Xiaomi untuk memasuki 2027.
Global Xiaomi 18 Pro Max (2611FPNFAG) spotted on Geekbench AI
– Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
– 12GB RAM
– Android 17#Xiaomi #xiaomi18proMax pic.twitter.com/MsQfYrJDMU— Anvin (@ZionsAnvin) October 9, 2026
Dalam pengujian Geekbench AI, perangkat tersebut menggunakan chipset Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 yang juga dipakai versi China. Prototipe yang diuji dipadukan dengan RAM 12GB. Namun, hasil pengujian ini belum mengungkap seluruh konfigurasi perangkat yang akan tersedia ketika dipasarkan secara internasional.
Baca Juga: HyperOS 4 Dikabarkan Perkuat Integrasi dengan iPhone, Mac, dan iPad
Snapdragon Terbaru dan Konfigurasi Global
Di China, Xiaomi 18 Pro Max juga tersedia dengan RAM 16GB. Belum diketahui apakah varian tersebut akan hadir di pasar global atau Xiaomi hanya menawarkan konfigurasi RAM 12GB. Pilihan penyimpanan untuk versi China mencakup kapasitas 256GB, 512GB, dan 1TB, tetapi konfigurasi globalnya masih belum dikonfirmasi.
Perbedaan lain yang patut diperhatikan adalah kapasitas baterai. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max versi China membawa baterai 8.500 mAh, sedangkan Xiaomi 18 Pro menggunakan baterai 7.000 mAh. Kapasitas untuk model global, terutama varian yang dipasarkan di Eropa, masih menjadi tanda tanya. Belum ada kepastian apakah Xiaomi akan mempertahankan kapasitas yang sama atau menyesuaikannya untuk pasar tertentu.
Layar Ganda dan Kamera 200MP
Sebagai gambaran, Xiaomi 18 Pro Max versi China memiliki layar utama LTPO AMOLED 6,9 inci dengan resolusi 1208 x 2624 piksel, refresh rate 120Hz, dan kecerahan puncak 4.000 nit. Di bagian belakang, terdapat layar tambahan LTPO AMOLED 2,9 inci dengan refresh rate 120Hz dan tingkat kecerahan puncak yang sama.
Sektor kamera mengandalkan sensor utama 200MP dengan OIS, kamera periskop telefoto 200MP dengan OIS dan zoom optik 3,2x, serta kamera ultrawide 50MP. Kamera depannya memiliki resolusi 50MP. Versi globalnya diperkirakan menjalankan Android 17 dengan HyperOS 4, tetapi spesifikasi akhir, harga, dan tanggal peluncurannya masih menunggu konfirmasi Xiaomi.
Artikel berjudul Xiaomi 18 Pro Max Versi Global Muncul di Geekbench AI, Bawa RAM 12GB yang ditulis oleh Christopher Louis pertama kali tampil di Gizmologi.id

items.title: This ancient Indian kitchen leaf can replace aluminium foil
items.summary: Banana leaves are celebrated across various cultures for their role in food wrapping and presentation, offering an array of benefits. They're a sustainable choice, being both biodegradable and compostable, a marked improvement from plastic options. It's worth noting that banana leaves may not hold up for extended preservation or intense heat cooking. With proper preparation, including washing and softening, they greatly enhance their food packaging potential.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
A 45-year-old man shot and killed seven relatives and a family friend at a home in Pennsylvania before apparently taking his own life, authorities said Saturday.
The victims in the city of Erie included two young children and a woman who was eight months pregnant.
Police responded Friday evening to reports of shots fired and discovered two women dead in the street, Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah told reporters.
Video evidence showed the pair arriving at the residence appearing distressed, then attempting to contact neighbors and enter the house, Lorah said.
The gunman exited the house, shot them, and returned inside, he said.
The man barricaded himself inside the home as police surrounded the building and ordered him to exit. He was later found inside with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, Lorah said.
The shooter and seven of his victims were related, Lorah said. The eighth victim was a family friend.
Dead inside the home were a five-year-old boy and a one-year-old girl. The others were men and women ranging in age from 19 to 51. One of the women was eight months pregnant.
Local news outlet Erie News Now said responding officers were being offered counseling over the horrifying incident.
“Many people across our community are hurting today: the neighbors who witnessed what happened, the families and friends of those who were killed, the officers and first responders who answered these calls, and others struggling to make sense of something so terrible,” Erie Mayor Daria Devlin told reporters Saturday.
“We cannot undo what happened last night, and we cannot take away the grief that these families are carrying, but we can make sure that they don’t have to carry it alone,” she said.
Mass shootings occur frequently in the United States, where guns vastly outnumber people and efforts to increase firearm restrictions face steep political and legal hurdles.
AFP

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
At least nine persons have reportedly been killed in fresh attacks by suspected armed herdsmen on Tse-Nyaku, Tse-Biliji and adjoining communities in Mbatian Council Ward of Ngenev, Ukum Local Government Area of Benue State.
Several others were reportedly injured, while an unspecified number of residents were said to be missing following the attacks, which began at about 11pm on Friday.
A local source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the assailants invaded the communities in large numbers, shooting sporadically and forcing residents to flee their homes.
According to the source, nine bodies had so far been recovered from the affected communities.
“The attackers came in large numbers and started shooting in the communities. Luckily, many people managed to escape, except for the nine who have been confirmed dead for now because their corpses have been recovered.
“However, it is very likely that the number could increase because many people have not been seen, and no one knows whether they were killed or escaped to other communities.
“Our people discovered that one of armed herdsmen is in possession of the phones of one of the victims and he has been using it to make and receive calls.
“The attacked communities have also already been deserted. It is a very sad day for our people. The Sankera axis of Benue has become a shadow of itself due to the level of insecurity,” he said.
Reacting to the incident, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate for Ukum I (Ngenev) State Constituency in the Benue State House of Assembly, Livinus Tyodoo, described the invasion as “one attack too many.”
In a statement he personally signed, Tyodoo said he received disturbing reports of the deadly attacks on the communities on Friday night and in the early hours of Saturday.
He said the attacks, allegedly carried out by suspected herdsmen militia, had reportedly claimed more than nine lives, adding that several bodies had been recovered while other residents remained missing and some survivors sustained varying degrees of injuries.
“This is one attack too many. I unequivocally condemn the senseless killing, displacement and continued persecution of innocent citizens in their ancestral homes.
“The people of Ukum I (Ngenev) deserve to live in peace, cultivate their farmlands and pursue their legitimate means of livelihood without the constant fear of violence.
“Human civilisation has evolved beyond the Hobbesian state of nature, where life was characterised by insecurity and the constant fear of violent death. In the 21st century, the sanctity of human life must remain paramount, and no community should be abandoned to the mercy of armed assailants,” he said.
Tyodoo stressed that the incident should not be politicised, urging the authorities to take urgent and decisive action to prevent further bloodshed.
“This is not the time for politics or the exchange of blame. It is a time for urgent, coordinated and decisive action,” he said.
He called on the Benue State Government, Ukum Local Government Council and relevant security agencies to strengthen security operations in the affected communities and other vulnerable areas of the local government.
According to him, beyond issuing statements and ordering investigations, the government must ensure effective intelligence gathering, proactive security deployments, the arrest and prosecution of those responsible, and concrete measures to prevent further attacks.
“Our people must be able to return to their ancestral homes, reclaim their farmlands and carry on with their daily activities without fear. The protection of lives and property is a fundamental responsibility of government, and the people of Ukum deserve nothing less,” he added.
The PDP candidate also expressed condolences to the families of those reportedly killed, while praying for the safe return of missing persons and the speedy recovery of the injured.
“I pray for the peaceful repose of the souls of the departed, comfort for the bereaved families, the safe return of anyone still missing, and a speedy recovery for those who sustained injuries.
“May God comfort our grieving communities, protect our people and restore lasting peace to Ngenev, Ukum and Benue State at large. The time for urgent action is now. Our people deserve security, justice and lasting peace,” he said.
When contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, said he was yet to receive a report on the incident.
The post Benue: Suspected herdsmen kill nine in fresh Ukum attacks appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
The Ogun State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has called on its members and supporters to remain calm following the omission of its governorship candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, from a list published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), expressing confidence that the issue would be resolved ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
The opposition party alleged that the development was the result of pressure from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), which it accused of being apprehensive about the PDP’s chances in the forthcoming election.
The party, however, maintained that Adebutu remained a bona fide member of the PDP, insisting that he had fulfilled the party’s membership registration requirements within the stipulated period.
In a statement issued by its Publicity Secretary, Arc. Kayode Adebayo, the PDP said, participated in the party’s digital membership registration exercise, during which his membership card was printed and verified before being submitted to INEC within the prescribed timeframe.
“We state emphatically that our candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has never left the Peoples Democratic Party at any time. He duly registered as a member of the party within the designated period of the digital registration exercise, and his membership card was printed, verified and submitted to INEC at the stipulated time,” the statement said.
The party attributed the omission to what it described as political interference, alleging that the APC was seeking to undermine its chances ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
“The omission of our candidate’s name from INEC’s list is a consequence of the undue pressure allegedly mounted on the commission by the ruling party out of fear of losing the election to our party,” Adebayo stated.
The PDP, however, expressed optimism that Adebutu’s name would be included in the relevant list of candidates, reaffirming its commitment to participating in the 2027 governorship election.
It urged the people of Ogun State not to be distracted by the development, calling on its members and supporters to remain focused on their political objectives and continue mobilising for the forthcoming election.
“While we urge the good people of Ogun State not to be perturbed or distracted from our collective resolve to vote out the APC, we remain resolute, unfazed and unwaveringly confident that our candidate is marching towards a decisive victory in the 2027 governorship election,” the statement added.
The opposition party further maintained that the development would not diminish what it described as the determination of the people of Ogun State to demand better governance and positive change.
“No amount of desperate manipulation, political witch-hunts or calculated distractions can alter the mandate of the people of Ogun State, who are overwhelmingly eager for true leadership and positive change,” the PDP said.
Reiterating its appeal for calm, the party urged its members, supporters and other stakeholders to remain steadfast and undeterred as it intensifies its political activities ahead of the election.
“Once again, we call on all our teeming supporters, party faithful and the general public to remain steadfast, vigilant and unintimidated as the unstoppable movement to rescue Ogun State and bring relief to our people continues to gain momentum,” the statement said.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Yan Diomande earned Real Madrid a tight 1-0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday to keep them six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, even though winger Vinicius Junior was sent off for hair-pulling.
Brazil international Vinicius, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and then he was dismissed after a VAR review showed he pulled the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba.
Jose Mourinho’s Madrid battled through the final stages with 10 men but held on to win and go provisionally third.
Champions Barca lead La Liga after a 3-0 win over Getafe, while Atletico Madrid are five points behind in second after they edged Alaves 2-1.
Striker Kylian Mbappe was fit to start the match for Madrid at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium after suffering a knee problem playing for France during the international break.
There were a smattering of whistles for the superstar forward, with some fans believing he has been unprofessional in recent weeks, but also applause from other supporters.
Mbappe, a candidate for the Ballon d’Or trophy later this month, was Madrid’s most threatening player in the first half, although he had little competition.
Mourinho started with out-of-form winger Vinicius on the bench, following his trips to Australia and India with Brazil during the international break.
Madrid improved defensively, giving Villarreal few chances of note, but struggled to build much in attack themselves in a drab opening half.
Mbappe struck the post from Alvaro Carreras’s lay-off as Madrid pushed Villarreal back early on.
Villarreal soon gained a foothold and restricted Madrid’s opportunities, until Mbappe forced a good save from Peter Gulacsi.
There was some more mild whistling for Madrid’s display from their fans at half-time, but soon they were able to celebrate summer arrival Diomande’s first goal for the club.
The Ivorian winger, Madrid’s record 140-million-euro ($157 million) signing, produced a sharp low finish into the far corner after good work from Federico Valverde to play him in.
Vinicius thought he had doubled Madrid’s lead after Jude Bellingham charged in down the left and cut the ball back for him.
However the winger’s joy turned to anger after referee Isidro Diaz de Mera was called to watch Vinicius’s hair pull on Saliba in the build-up by VAR and sent off the Brazilian, voiding his goal.
Madrid’s Belgian goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who had made a couple of smart saves earlier in the half, produced an acrobatic stop to thwart Carlos Romero.
Mbappe was denied again by Hungarian goalkeeper Gulasci as the forward left the Bernabeu frustrated in his hunt for goals, although his team were able to clinch three important points to stay on Barca’s trail.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Nollywood actress Regina Daniels has disclosed that she has endured months of severe pain and difficulty walking, revealing that her condition has left her dependent on a wheelchair.
The actress shared the update in a video posted on her Instagram page on Saturday to celebrate her 25th birthday, using the opportunity to explain her absence from social media.
Daniels, a mother of two, said what initially appeared to be a minor health problem gradually worsened, leaving her unable to move freely and sometimes preventing her from walking.
“I know many of you may be surprised seeing me in a wheelchair. Well, welcome to another chapter of my life. Let me walk you through what my life has been since many of you have asked questions about my absence,” she said.
Recounting how her condition deteriorated, Daniels said she began experiencing more serious symptoms after hosting a children’s day carnival.
“For several months now, I have lost my freedom to move around as I please. It started as something minor, very minor, but eventually led to this.
“But things took a major turn after the last public gathering I hosted, my children’s day carnival. One test after another, I jokingly started calling myself a lab rat. The pain became excruciating. Sometimes I can walk, and sometimes I can’t move. I cried,” she added.
The actress expressed gratitude for the progress she said she had made in her recovery, noting that recent developments had encouraged her to speak publicly about her health.
“Well, me sitting here today, in front of this camera, sharing this with y’all, it’s because there’s been some really significant developments in my recovery. And I say, thank you, Lord,” she said.
Daniels also described the emotional difficulties associated with her condition, particularly having to rely on others for assistance with routine activities.
Despite the challenges, she said her faith in God had helped her through the experience and expressed hope for healing and peace.
The actress further disclosed that she had moved closer to her loved ones, especially her children, whom she described as being particularly dear to her.
She said she initially rented the property she moved into but later developed an interest in owning it.
Daniels married businessman and politician Ned Nwoko in 2019, and the couple have two children. Their relationship has since been marked by a public and contentious separation.

Tinubu said this on Saturday in Lafia at the North-Central Mega Rally organised by the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima.
The First Lady urged party members to take the campaign to communities across the region and mobilise voters for the party’s candidates.
She highlighted some achievements of the Tinubu administration across various sectors, saying continuity was necessary to sustain the gains.
“President Tinubu is a man who believes in the unity, security and prosperity of our nation.
“The Independence Day message of Mr President was titled ‘From Reforms to Prosperity’.
“Therefore, Mr President is saying that they are going to reform the sector, but now is the time for prosperity, and we can see our economy is stabilising.
“Foreign exchange is going down, and investors are coming back to Nigeria, our farmers too. You can see all our governors here; they are doing infrastructural development like no other time before.
“I have been in the Senate for 12 years. This is the best time I will see the government fixing roads and building a lot of infrastructure,” she said.
Tinubu also cited the administration’s food support programme, saying it was designed to provide nutritious food for children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.
“As you see now, we have just finished the food bank programme, where we are helping every child and mothers who are pregnant and also breastfeeding.
“This is to ensure that they can have more nutritious food, and also the children that are malnourished can get treatment and also get food to grow healthy,” she said.
She added that students were also benefiting from the administration’s education funding initiatives.
The First Lady urged party members to communicate the administration’s policies and programmes to Nigerians in their respective states.

She said the party’s campaign would focus on its programmes and policies without resorting to hate speech or actions capable of undermining national unity.
“Therefore, vote for continuity, vote for capacity, vote for prosperity, and vote for the re-election of Mr President and all the candidates of APC from top to bottom,” she said.

items.content:
A United States federal court has sentenced a Nigerian national, Edikan Adiakpan, to 30 months’ imprisonment for his involvement in a business email fraud scheme targeting American companies.
The U.S. Department of Justice disclosed this in a statement issued by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Texas.
The department said Adiakpan, 35, a Houston resident, pleaded guilty on May 12 to illegally transmitting proceeds from an email fraud scheme.
U.S. District Judge Andrew Hanen sentenced him to 30 months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release.
According to the department, Adiakpan operates a company known as Akama Lifestyle, which he advertised as a luxury car service.
However, prosecutors said he used the company between 2020 and 2022 to transfer money received from fraudsters in exchange for a percentage of the proceeds.
The funds originated from a business email compromise scheme that targeted more than 10 victims.
The department explained that the fraudsters sent emails impersonating legitimate suppliers and creditors to deceive businesses into transferring payments to fraudulent bank accounts.
One victim, a small utility trailer company in Mississippi, lost substantial funds after receiving fraudulent payment instructions.
According to prosecutors, the company transferred $927,080 to the fraudsters, believing it was paying a legitimate supplier.
The fraudsters subsequently transferred portions of the proceeds to Adiakpan.
The department said Adiakpan deposited and redeemed several cashier’s cheques payable to himself and his luxury car company.
It said the transactions involved $359,000 belonging to the Mississippi company.
A victim impact statement describing the financial consequences of the fraud was presented during Adiakpan’s sentencing hearing.
The department disclosed that Adiakpan had temporary legal status in the United States when he was arrested.
It also identified another Nigerian, Ayobami Omoniyi, 27, as having participated in the scheme, and was subsequently sentenced on March 24 to 32 months in federal prison for his role.
The investigation was conducted by the FBI’s Houston Field Office and Bryan Resident Agency, alongside the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation Division, while Assistant U.S. Attorney Belinda Beek prosecuted the case. (NAN)

Mr Rotimi Amaechi, vice presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s handling of fuel subsidy removal, citing its impact on Nigerians.
Amaechi, a former Minister of Transportation and Rivers governor, spoke on Saturday at a town hall meeting in Calabar.
He said the government should have consulted economists, political scientists and other stakeholders before implementing the policy.
The former minister argued that adequate measures should have been introduced to cushion the effects of subsidy removal on Nigerians.
According to him, courage in policymaking must be balanced with careful planning and consideration of the consequences for citizens.
Amaechi illustrated his argument with an analogy involving a moving train, warning that bold decisions could carry risks without proper preparation.
He said the administration’s approach raised questions about whether sufficient attention had been paid to the welfare of Nigerians.
The ADC chieftain also suggested that political considerations might have influenced the policy, linking the administration’s approach to the outcome of the 2023 presidential election.
He noted that subsidy removal had significantly increased transportation costs and other essential expenses across the country.
Amaechi questioned the government’s response to the rising cost of living, stressing the need for measures to ease economic pressure on households.
He also expressed readiness to debate members of the administration’s economic team on the policy and possible solutions to its consequences.
The former minister said the opposition would challenge the ruling party through democratic and constitutional processes ahead of the next election.
“The opposition intends to pursue the electoral process without resorting to post-election litigation, and we are confident in our approach,” he said. (NAN)

Chinda, 60, is running with Jack Major Miakiapuye as his deputy. His qualifications are listed as a First School Leaving Certificate and a law degree.
Pidomson, 56, is paired with Okumgba David Amapakaye, while Ejekwu, 60, will run with Ehuwa Pirinye Kabaka. The commission lists both men as holders of doctorate degrees.
Lulu-Briggs, 62, has Nwielaghi Barieenee Michael as his running mate. He is listed with a law degree.

The remaining candidates are Boms Chima Ernest of the Labour Party (LP), Opusunju Silva of the NDP, Pepple Wari Dienye of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), Minaibim Harry of the National Rescue Movement (NRM) and Kieghe Nature Dumale of the People’s Redemption Party (PRP).
West Ivy, 47, is the only woman on the list of governorship candidates. Six of the 17 deputy governorship candidates are women.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Dominic Solanke rescued a 1-1 draw for 10-man Tottenham to ramp up the pressure on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick on Saturday.
Solanke’s stoppage time header edged Spurs off the foot of the Premier League table after it seemed like they would pay a heavy price for not taking their chances in a dominant display at Old Trafford.
Bryan Mbeumo put United in front against the run of play 17 minutes from time before Rodrigo Bentancur was shown a straight red card.
But not for the first time this season, Carrick’s men failed to make a man advantage count.
Manchester City won 1-0 at Old Trafford last month despite playing for more than an hour with 10 men.
Solanke stooped to head in Sandro Tonali’s cross to leave United with just six points from their opening six league games.
Not since 1986/87 have United taken fewer points from their opening six league games.
“To not take all the points, everything looks and feels different,” said Carrick.
“We’re making it a little bit more difficult for ourselves. We can defend the whole phase a lot better as a team and be a lot more stubborn and ruthless to see the game out.”
Tottenham had three weeks to fester on dropping to the bottom of the table during the international break after a disastrous start to their £300 million ($397 million) rebuild in the transfer window.
Roberto De Zerbi’s men took until the closing stages of their fifth league game to even score a goal and a much improved performance was undone by a familiar lack of cutting edge up front.
“For the first time in this season we showed we are a team,” said De Zerbi. “We played for the team-mates, we played together. We believed until the end of the game.”
Before kick-off, the United supporters took aim at local rivals City, who have been found guilty on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.
But the home fans soon had their own troubles to concentrate on as Spurs penned United inside their own half.
Solanke should have opened the scoring when he fired too close to Senne Lammens before Mohammed Kudus blasted wide at the end of a flowing Tottenham move.
Chances continued to come and go for the visitors after the break, much to the frustration of a visibly animated De Zerbi.
Solanke spooned over and Destiny Udogie curled wide before the game appeared to run away from Spurs.
Carrick helped turn the tide with a triple substitution on the hour mark.
Carlos Baleba added more dynamism to United’s midfield on his first appearance since a £70 million move from Brighton, while the introduction of Joshua Zirkzee allowed Matheus Cunha to drop into a deeper role.
United had barely threatened Antonin Kinsky’s goal until Mbeumo was afforded too much room to spin onto Cunha’s pass and fire into the far corner.
To compound Tottenham’s woes, Bentancur was then shown a straight red card for a headbutt on Luke Shaw after an angry confrontation between the pair.
But United again failed make their man advantage count.
Solanke finally ended Tottenham’s wait since May for an away goal when he outmuscled Lisandro Martinez to glance in Tonali’s cross.
The point edges Spurs up to 18th with only goals scored keeping them inside the relegation zone.
United are just three points better off in 12th.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Michael Carrick said Manchester United need to become more “streetwise” and “stubborn” after they blew a late lead against 10-man Tottenham to draw 1-1 at Old Trafford on Saturday.
United have taken just six points from their opening six Premier League games, their lowest haul at this stage of a league campaign for 30 years.
Carrick’s men were booed off at half-time and at the end of the match after a Tottenham side that began the day bottom of the table dominated for large spells.
“I’m not happy with the amount of points that we’ve had so far, for sure. There’s no hiding from that,” said Carrick.
“I think it could have been different but for a couple of little things here and there, but the reality is the reality, we’ve got to accept it. We need to put things in a positive direction quite quickly.
“We’re more than capable of doing that. We’ve just got to be a little bit more streetwise in moments, a little bit more stubborn and a little bit more stronger and see out certain things.”
United also let the lead slip twice when they drew 2-2 away to Everton and were dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton last month despite taking an early 2-0 advantage.
It appeared that Tottenham would live to regret not taking a series of chances when Bryan Mbeumo put United in front 17 minutes from time.
Rodrigo Bentancur was then shown a straight red card for a headbutt on Luke Shaw.
But not for the first time in the past two seasons, United failed to make a man advantage count as Dominic Solanke headed in an equaliser in stoppage time.
Both Everton last season and City last month won at Old Trafford despite playing for over an hour reduced to 10 men.
“It’s different type of goals but it’s definitely something that, whether 10 men or not 10 men, if we’re leading the game, we’ve got to see games out,” added Carrick.
“Whether that’s taking a ball, controlling the game a little bit more, looking after the ball better in their half and around their box and pinning them in a little bit.”
Spurs remain without a league win this season, but Roberto De Zerbi was heartened by the response of his side.
“In that moment with 10 players maybe we played with more courage, we played with more energy and we changed again the game,” said the Italian.
“For a long time Tottenham played without this blood, this character and I want, now I am the coach, I want to see this character every game.”
Solanke was handed the captain’s armband by De Zerbi in a surprise move and repaid the faith shown by his coach with a first away league goal since April 2025.
“I wanted to put him as captain to show my confidence and the confidence of the team, because all other players were happy when I said Dominic Solanke was captain,” added De Zerbi.
“He is a great player and I wanted to show what is my confidence and what is the importance I give him in this team.”

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi
The Intelligence Response Team (IRT) of the Nigeria Police Force has foiled an alleged plot to kidnap a prophetess and assistant Pastor in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, and arrested four suspects with a locally fabricated firearm and a vehicle allegedly acquired for the operation.
Parading the suspects as part of recent operations targeting kidnapping, armed robbery and other violent crimes in the nation’s Federal Capital Territory, Commander of IRT, DCP Adamu Muazu noted that the alleged plot was particularly disturbing because some of the suspects were members of the same church with the intended victim, identified as Prophetess Elizabeth.
Muazu said the Prophetess Elizabeth had reportedly given testimony in church about her personal achievements and business success, after which some members of the congregation allegedly began planning her abduction.
He disclosed that one of the suspects, David Obaje, was said to have worked as Elizabeth’s driver for about three months and had been a member of the church for approximately four years, giving him knowledge of her movements and routines.
DCP Muazu added that another suspect, David Dennis, reportedly belonged to the church for about six years and worked as a bodyguard to the senior pastor.
The Commander said Police investigators alleged that the suspects used a WhatsApp group to coordinate the planned kidnapping and had also arranged for another person to be brought from Kogi State to participate in the operation.
He added that the suspects planned to attack Elizabeth after an evening church service on October 1 by using a vehicle to block or deliberately hit her car, creating the appearance of a road accident and forcing her to stop.
“She would then allegedly be overpowered and taken to a predetermined location where she was expected to be held”.
The IRT boss further explained that the investigation led to the recovery of the vehicle allegedly acquired for the operation, as well as a firearm reportedly procured for the planned abduction.
Revealing that the suspects claimed the weapon was purchased from a vigilante group for N120,000, the IRT Commander described the recovered weapon as a locally fabricated AK-47.
He said Investigators also recovered a security uniform allegedly obtained as part of preparations for the operation.
The Commander, however, disclosed that the planned abduction was disrupted after the IRT received intelligence about the alleged conspiracy and arrested the suspects before the operation could be carried out.
DCP Muazu warned members of the public against disclosing sensitive personal information, particularly details about their finances, businesses, properties, movements and personal achievements in public gatherings.
He urged churches to strengthen security around their premises, especially during evening services, through adequate lighting, controlled access and proper monitoring of people and vehicles.
DCP Muazu assured Nigerians that the IRT would continue to deploy intelligence-led operations to disrupt criminal networks and prevent planned attacks.

items.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi
The Nigerian Army and the Sokoto State Police Command have debunked a viral social media post claiming that more than 100 civilians, 10 soldiers and a Mobile Police officer were killed in an alleged attack on a community in Sokoto State.
The claim, published by a Facebook page (Hausaland Magazine) on October 5, 2026, alleged that armed men attacked a community identified as “Garin Gobir Gindin,” killing more than 100 civilians and security personnel, while kidnapping several others.
The post, which described the alleged incident as a “genocide” and a “war on Hausa,” attributed the attack to “Fulani terrorists” and claimed that the death toll was rising.
The viral post included an image showing several motionless individuals, some dressed in military-style clothing and others in civilian attire.
It also attracted comments from social media users who appeared to accept and amplify the allegations, with some making inflammatory statements targeting ethnic groups.
However, security authorities have denied that any such attack occurred in the state as there was no record of a community known as “Garin Gobir Gindin.”
Investigation identified a date discrepancy in the post while the publication claimed the attack occurred on Tuesday, October 5, 2026, that date fell on a Monday.
Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 8 Division, Nigerian Army, Lieutenant Colonel Olaniyi Osoba, dismissed the allegation, saying, “There was no such attack involving the reported mass casualties in the state.
The Public Relations Officer of the Sokoto State Police Command, Deputy Superintendent of Police Ahmed Rufa’i, debunked the claim, saying, “This incident did not occur within Sokoto.”
Verified security reports across the North-West also found no mass-casualty incident matching the description circulated by Hausaland Magazine.
Investigations, however, identified a separate attack on Sunday, October 4, 2026, in Ungushi village, Kebbe Local Government Area of Sokoto State, where bandits reportedly killed two people and injured another. The incident was confirmed by the Sokoto State Police Command

items.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi
ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has dropped the name of former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State.
Pantami, who appeared on the provisional list published on August 29, is conspicuously missing from the final list published in Saturday night.
He emerged as the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate after dumping the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19.
Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, one of the aspirants who sought the PDP ticket, challenged Pantami’s victory in court.
A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again.
His biggest obstacle, however, was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time.
A total of 16 candidates were cleared to contest the February 6, 2027 governorship election in the state.
They include Bala Bello Tinka of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Jamilu Isyaku Gwamna of the APC and Babayo Ardo Kumo of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).
Others are Zubairu Mu’azu Halilu of the Labour Party, Lamela L. Silas of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Ibrahim Jalo Abubakar of the People’s Redemption Party (PRP) and Adamu Mohammed Ma’aji of the Social Democratic Party (SDP).
Uncertainty had trailed Pantami’s participation in the election. Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had hinted on Trust TV’s Daily Politics that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027.

items.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has omitted the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, and his running mate from its final list of candidates for the February 6, 2027, governorship election.
The commission, in the list released on Saturday evening, published the names of 13 governorship candidates representing 13 political parties in Ogun State.
However, neither Adebutu nor his deputy appeared on the list.
The reason for the omission was not immediately clear as of the time of filing this report.
The final list indicated that the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Lawal Jimi Adebisi, and his running mate, Olutayo Florence Funlola Folake, were included pursuant to a court order.
The candidates listed for the Ogun governorship election are Okewole Shuaib Olaniyi of the Accord Party; Awofala Awolola Awoniyi of the Action Alliance (AA); Lawal Jimi Adebisi of the ADC; Anifowose John Kayode of the Action Democratic Party (ADP); and Adeola Solomon Olamilekan of the All Progressives Congress (APC).
Others are Babajide Rotimi Mathew of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM); Layi Labode Halima of the Action Peoples Party (APP); Adenuga Adekunle Dreher of the Boot Party (BP); Dasaolu Oluwaseyi Olamilekan of the National Democratic Party (NDP); and Akinbola Hammed Rotham of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP).
The remaining candidates are Fayoyin Olujobi Ezekiel of the National Rescue Movement (NRM); Ola Willams Adeyinka of the Social Democratic Party (SDP); and Johnson Cyrus Oluwaseun of the Young Progressives Party (YPP).
The omission comes as political parties prepare for the February 6, 2027, governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections.
Under Section 32(1) of the Electoral Act 2026, INEC is required to publish the names and addresses of nominated candidates at least 60 days before an election.
Section 32(2) also outlines a procedure for a registered political party to notify the commission if the name of its nominated candidate is missing from the published list.
The provision requires such notification to be made in writing, signed by the party’s national chairman and national secretary, and accompanied by an affidavit within 14 days of the publication.
The statutory procedure provides a formal avenue for a political party to draw the commission’s attention to the omission of its candidate and seek appropriate action in accordance with the law.
INEC Chairman Professor Joash Amupitan had earlier disclosed that 21 of Nigeria’s 22 registered political parties nominated a total of 936 governorship and deputy governorship candidates across the 28 states scheduled to hold governorship elections in 2027.
The parties also nominated 9,692 candidates for the State Houses of Assembly elections.
Ogun State is among the states scheduled to elect a new governor on February 6, 2027, alongside elections into the state legislature.
Adebutu’s exclusion from the final list leaves questions over the PDP’s participation in the Ogun governorship race, although the Electoral Act provides a procedure through which the party may formally raise the issue with INEC.

items.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has reiterated his commitment to prioritise local government autonomy, grassroots development and strategic investment in border communities if elected in the 2027 governorship election.
Adebutu made the pledge during a PDP campaign rally in Remo, Ogun State, where he outlined key elements of his ‘Itura De’ agenda, which he said was designed to return power to the people and strengthen development at the grassroots.
The PDP candidate said local governments should be empowered to address the specific needs of their communities and determine development priorities without undue interference.
According to him, functional local government autonomy would enable grassroots administrations to respond more effectively to the concerns of residents and deliver projects that directly improve their living conditions.
He said: “Local governments must be empowered to address the needs of their people and determine the development priorities of their communities. Governance should be felt at the grassroots, where its impact matters most to ordinary citizens.”
Adebutu also highlighted the importance of developing border communities, arguing that targeted investments in infrastructure and economic activities could unlock their potential and strengthen their contribution to Ogun State’s economy.
He noted that Ogun’s proximity to Lagos presented significant opportunities for economic integration, trade and investment, adding that the state could benefit from stronger economic connections with its neighbouring commercial hub.
According to him, improved infrastructure and deliberate economic planning would help border communities attract investment, create employment opportunities and contribute more meaningfully to the state’s overall development.
Also speaking at the rally, the PDP’s Ogun East senatorial candidate, Alhaji Abdul-Hameed Femi Omotayo, called for visible and measurable development across the senatorial district.
Referring to his visit to Sagamu two days earlier, Omotayo said his observations during the visit had raised concerns about the town’s development trajectory.
He criticised what he described as inadequate progress, using a metaphor to contrast urban development with the condition he said he encountered in the town.
“The current administration has turned town to bush instead of turning bush to town,” he said.
Omotayo’s remark underscored his concerns about the pace of development in Sagamu and the need for projects that residents can see and feel in their daily lives.
He maintained that Ogun East needed tangible results in infrastructure, employment generation and the creation of opportunities for residents, particularly young people.
The senatorial candidate also stressed the importance of addressing challenges affecting economic activities across communities in the district.
Poor road infrastructure, limited employment opportunities and inadequate access to economic opportunities remain important issues in discussions about community development. Deteriorating roads can increase transportation costs and impede the movement of goods, while a shortage of jobs can restrict the options available to young people.

items.author: Hasnaat Malik
items.content:
The jurisdictional dispute between the country's two apex courts remains unresolved as the Supreme Court appears to be cautious in fixing a hearing in the matter in which it raised legal questions over the Federal Constitutional Court's (FCC) order seeking records of cases involving PTI founder Imran Khan and directing that they be fixed for hearing before it.
The delay has left questions surrounding the FCC's jurisdiction and the implementation of the SC's order for Imran Khan's transfer to Shifa International Hospital unresolved.
The FCC raised questions on September 14 over the SC's August 18 order directing the transfer for medical treatment. However, the matter is yet to be fixed for hearing before the FCC. Meanwhile, the SC has also not fixed the matter for hearing despite its September 16 judicial order.
A three-member bench led by Justice Shahid Waheed adjourned the hearing for three weeks on September 16 at the request of Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan.
There is little chance that the matter will be listed for hearing next week, as the head of the bench, Justice Shahid Waheed, will be sitting at the SC's Lahore Registry to hear cases.
It is also learnt that, despite the judicial order, the SC office has yet to send the records of Imran Khan's cases to the FCC for hearing.
A senior law officer believes that although the SC's order remains in force, if it takes up the case again, the FCC will be compelled to stay the SC's August 18 order regarding Imran Khan's transfer to Shifa International Hospital.
He said the SC had no option but to follow the FCC's order, which was binding on it under Article 189 of the Constitution.
Legal experts believe that if the SC ultimately sends the case to the FCC, it would effectively establish the subordinate status of the SC.
"Will the SC judges accept their demotion or resign?" a senior lawyer questioned.
'Belated obituary of SC'
Barrister Tariq Mahmood Khokhar said the FCC order was "a belated obituary of the Supreme Court of Pakistan". He said the SC's decline had been a "predicted and predictable outcome" of the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments.
"The Constitution was amended, not for constitutional reasons but for state reasons," Khokhar said.
The jurisdictional dispute between the two apex courts has also left uncertainty over Imran Khan's health unresolved, as neither the FCC nor the SC is taking up the matter.
A senior government official told The Express Tribune that, in view of the latest report, Imran Khan was completely physically fit. He said the report would be submitted to the appropriate court before the case was fixed for hearing.
On August 18, the SC ordered the government to shift Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital for medical treatment. However, the order was not fully implemented.
Following this, petitioner Uzma Khan filed a contempt petition against Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and others over the non-implementation of the August 18 order. The same contempt matter was also fixed for hearing before the bench.
In its order, the court noted that it had been brought to its notice that certain cases arising from a judgment of the Islamabad High Court, delivered in a petition under Article 199 of the Constitution, had reached the FCC. The relief sought in those cases was substantially similar to that granted by the SC through its August 18 order.
The court noted that, before proceeding to adjudicate upon those matters, the FCC appeared to have considered it appropriate to examine the proceedings pending before the SC and had accordingly called for their records.
Referring to paragraph 6 of the FCC order, the bench questioned how the constitutional court could order the 'fixation' of cases whose records it was summoning from the SC.
However, the bench acknowledged that the FCC could summon records of cases under Article 175 E (5) of the Constitution.
At one point, Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan said Article 175 E(5) of the Constitution did not specifically mention that the FCC could summon records of cases from the SC, unlike Article 189, which states that the FCC's orders are binding on all courts, including the SC.
Justice Shahid Waheed remarked that the bench could not disregard the FCC's order. However, he also questioned whether the FCC's order was binding on the SC.
The presiding judge said that the enforcement of fundamental rights was involved in every matter.
He noted that, under the Constitution, appeals against orders of the FCC were heard by the SC, whose decisions were final. He asked whether the SC's order in a Sharia matter would be binding on the FCC.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed lower during the outgoing week, with the benchmark KSE-100 index shedding 1,066 points, or 0.6%, to settle at 167,089 on Friday, as persistent geopolitical tensions offset optimism over Pakistan's staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for disbursement of $1.2 billion in loan tranches.
On a day-on-day basis, Monday saw a negative start due to regional and domestic political conditions. The KSE-100 dived 2,288 points (-1.36%) to close at 165,867 by breaching the 166k level, a key support. Nevertheless, the market staged a strong comeback on Tuesday, with the index gaining 2,593 points (+1.56%) to 168,460, reclaiming the 168k level.
PSX witnessed consolidation on Wednesday, rising just 120 points (+0.07%) to close at 168,580. On Thursday, the IMF's successful review met geopolitical headwinds. The KSE-100 declined 1,139 points (-0.68%) to 167,442. On Friday, the index traded in both directions amid cautious investor sentiment, driven by geopolitical uncertainty and squaring of positions ahead of the weekend. The index lost 353 points (-0.21%) and settled at 167,089.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL) noted that the KSE-100 declined marginally by 0.6% week-on-week (WoW) to 167,089, shedding 1,066 points, as positive sentiment from the IMF staff-level agreement was partly offset by persistent geopolitical uncertainties. Pakistan and the IMF reached a staff-level agreement on the fourth Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and third Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) reviews, paving the way for $1 billion and $210 million in loan disbursements, respectively, subject to the executive board approval, which would bring total disbursements under both programmes to $5.7 billion.
AHL mentioned that the central government debt decreased by 0.5% month-on-month (MoM) to Rs82.95 trillion (+7.1% year-on-year – YoY) as of Aug'26 compared with Rs77.46 trillion in Aug'25. The government raised Rs381 billion in the recent Pakistan Investment Bond (PIB) auction against the target of Rs350 billion, with Rs208.4 billion allocated to three-year bonds. Yields increased by 26-41 basis points across three, five and 10-year tenors, declined 19 basis points for two-year bonds, while bids for 15-year papers were rejected.
Total cement dispatches rose 6% YoY to 4.62 million tons in Sept'26, driven by a 7% increase in domestic sales, while exports remained flat. 1QFY27 dispatches grew 4% YoY to 13.14 million tons, supported by an 8% growth in local sales despite an 11% dip in exports.
SECMC, a public-private partnership between the government of Sindh and Engro along with its affiliates, was expanding its Thar Block-II coalmine to supply additional coal to Lucky Electric Power Company Ltd (LEPCL). The expansion was expected to enable LEPCL to fully transition to local Thar coal, improving utilisation and regulated returns while reducing reliance on imported coal, which would support foreign exchange savings and strengthen energy security.
Meanwhile, Sazgar Engineering's four-wheeler sales remained flat YoY at 2,474 units in Aug-Sept'26, bringing 1QFY27 sales down 12% to 3,137 units, primarily due to a weak July. Three-wheeler sales rose 32% YoY to 5,173 units during Aug-Sept'26, driving 1QFY27 three-wheeler sales growth of 45% and overall sales growth of 22% to 10,872 units.
Oil production declined 6.4% WoW to 63.7k barrels per day due to lower flows from northern fields, while gas production fell 1.4% WoW to 2,999 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) amid reduced output from Mari, Sui and Sharf, AHL added in its report.
Wadee Zaman of JS Global noted that the KSE-100 index declined 0.6% WoW to close at 167,089, amid persistent US-Iran tensions and escalating clashes between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi forces, prompting the Makkah Defence Alliance to agree on a rapid force deployment. Brent crude remained above $100/barrel, while domestic fuel prices saw mixed adjustments, with motor spirit rising by Rs6.20/litre to Rs398.96/litre and high-speed diesel falling by Rs3.92/litre to Rs395.72/litre.
On the domestic front, Zaman said, Pakistan reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF to unlock $1.2 billion under the fifth tranche of the EFF and third tranche of the RSF. The Fund urged the government to phase out fuel subsidies, broaden the tax base and ensure timely energy tariff adjustments, cautioning that risks remained elevated amid geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices and trade disruptions.
In other developments, the government debt declined 0.5% MoM to Rs82.95 trillion in Aug'26, although it went up 7.1% YoY. Meanwhile, the SOE debt surged to Rs10.1 trillion by the end of Dec'25, according to the finance ministry. In the latest PIB auction, the government raised Rs352 billion, with yields rising 26-41 basis points across different tenors. Meanwhile, the SBP reserves remained stable at $21.5 billion, Zaman added.

items.content:
India on Saturday unveiled fresh measures to shore up the rupee, redirecting oil companies' dollar purchases away from the spot market and tightening hedging rules as the currency hovers near record lows.
The steps by the Reserve Bank of India come as persistent pressure on the rupee, fuelled by surging oil prices and global bond yields, has driven the currency down more than 7% this year. The central bank will open a special window to meet the daily dollar requirements of three state-run oil marketing companies, easing pressure on the spot market.
Under such an arrangement, used during periods of currency stress, the RBI provides oil companies dollars directly from its foreign exchange reserves. Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum will be allowed to access the facility from Monday, the RBI said.
"Addressing oil companies' dollar requirements removes one of the largest sources of demand from the FX market, which should help reduce volatility but it will show up in a depletion of reserves," said Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist at ANZ Bank in Mumbai.
After the steps were announced, the rupee strengthened by about 0.6% against the dollar in the non-deliverable forward market, albeit in thin trading. Elevated demand for protection against further rupee losses has weighed on the currency in recent months, with importers' appetite for dollars far exceeding exporter supply.
The central bank has responded by tightening rules on speculative corporate activity and raising the cost of protection against further rupee weakness. The RBI is "trying to moderate potentially destabilising derivative demand, improve the integrity of underlying exposure verification and discourage circumvention through multiple transactions or repeated rebooking," a person familiar with the central bank's thinking said, commenting on condition of anonymity.
The central bank has mandated that forex dealers maintain a 20% "foreign exchange risk reserve" on derivative contracts used to buy foreign currency against the rupee, for the purposes of hedging current account transactions. The requirement applies to transactions with a notional value exceeding $2 million. The reserve requirement will lift the cost of buying protection against further rupee weakness, helping to discourage excessive hedging, two bankers said. Chinese authorities have previously used similar tools to discourage one-way bets against the yuan.
India's central bank has also slashed the limits on the size of derivative transactions users can undertake without proof of underlying exposure to $5 million from $100 million. The lower cap applies across all derivative products, including exchange-traded futures.

items.author: Web
items.content:
At first glance, Ulanqab in north China's Inner Mongolia and Bahawalpur in southern Pakistan may appear worlds apart. Yet the two regions share a striking landscape of dry weather, vast open spaces and sandy terrain. Their development stories, however, are taking increasingly different directions: while Bahawalpur is exploring new opportunities in technology, higher education and innovation, Ulanqab has leveraged its geographic, climatic and energy advantages to become a growing hub for computing power and artificial intelligence.
A visit to Ulanqab's computing facilities shows how a region traditionally associated with energy and natural resources is becoming part of China's rapidly expanding digital infrastructure. The city has been integrated into China's national "East Data, West Computing" strategy, which channels computing resources towards western regions where land, energy and climatic conditions can support large-scale data centres.
For Pakistan, the transformation raises an important question: could regions with similar dryland environments develop new economic opportunities by connecting energy, education, technology and digital infrastructure?
According to Zhang Xiaoliang, who is associated with the Economic Bureau of Chahar High-tech Zone, Ulanqab possesses several advantages that make it suitable for data-centre development.
"Inner Mongolia has its own power grid," Zhang explained, noting that electricity availability and comparatively favourable power costs are important advantages for data centres, which require stable and large-scale energy supplies. He also highlighted Ulanqab's proximity to Beijing, its relatively cool climate and geological conditions as factors supporting the development of computing infrastructure.
The city's strategy is increasingly linking computing power with green energy. Centrin Data's Ulanqab computing-power cluster, located in the Chahar High-tech Development Zone, is part of the Inner Mongolia national computing hub. The company has planned several large data centres and is developing a source-grid-load-storage project combining wind, solar and energy storage.
The wider Inner Mongolia model is also increasingly associated with green computing. More than 85% of electricity used by regional data centres reportedly comes from clean energy, demonstrating how renewable power can be integrated with energy-intensive AI infrastructure.
But the lesson for Pakistan may not be about building identical data centres. Professor Dr Muhammad Kamran, Vice Chancellor of The Islamia University of Bahawalpur (IUB), argues that the more important question is whether computing infrastructure can be connected with universities, research, industry, energy and human capital. "Computing capacity has to be tied to reliable energy, research institutions, universities, industry and people who actually know how to use it," Kamran said.
For Bahawalpur, this perspective is particularly relevant. IUB is expanding its focus on emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and quantum computing. The university has introduced AI-related learning across disciplines and established an Artificial Intelligence Research and Advancement Lab. It has also launched an advanced Quantum Computing programme in 2026.
Kamran said the value of cooperation with China should extend beyond equipment or individual projects. International partnerships, in his view, can provide technology, expertise and exposure, but Pakistani universities ultimately need to develop their own research capacity, skilled graduates and stronger links with industry.
He stated that the comparison between Ulanqab and Bahawalpur does not mean Pakistan can simply reproduce Inner Mongolia's development model. The two regions have different energy systems, industrial structures and economic conditions. Instead, Ulanqab offers a case study on how natural advantages can be connected with infrastructure and economic demand. For Bahawalpur, the opportunity could therefore lie in connecting its universities, young population, research institutions and emerging technology capabilities with broader national and international digital networks.
