items.author: Baba Martins
items.content:
Former Vice President and Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of copying his production subsidy model.
Reacting to the 30-day fuel discount announced by the Federal Government, on Thursday, Atiku accused Tinubu of wrongly copying his production subsidy model.
The Presidential candidate made the declaration at the inauguration of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, on Friday.
“You copied my production subsidy proposal, stripped away the part that makes it work, and handed Nigerians a 30-day discount,” Atiku alleged.
The ADC Presidential candidate recalled that in his last press conference, he agreed to share his economic relief plan with Tinubu, but said instead of accepting that offer in the national interest, he gave citizens just 30-day discount.
Atiku however said, “I am glad you have finally acknowledged the failure of your approach,” adding that he offered a plan because Nigerians’ welfare matters more to him.
While describing President Tinubu’s petrol discount policy as deception, he added that for three and a half years, the government had driven up the cost of living.
“Now you offer a ₦50 petrol discount for 30 days and expect applause for returning a fraction of what Nigerians have lost?
“How can you make daily life unbearable for years and expect one month of token relief to wipe the record clean?” Atiku said.
Atiku also called for reforms in the electoral system, including the right of parties and observers to verify election results, and to broadcast state and national collation centers live.
“We also demand independent audits of election technology before and after elections, an independent commission to investigate and prosecute electoral offenses, electoral institutions whose transparent processes command public confidence, and severe penalties for vote suppression, result tampering and fraud.
“These are not threats to democracy; they are safeguards for the people’s mandate,” he said.
In his speech, Chairman of the ADC Campaign Council Kashim Ibrahim-Imam, called on Nigerians to collect their Permanent Voter’s Card (PVC) to vote out the All Progressives Congress (APC) government in 2027.
“Collect your voter’s card. Go out early. Stay until the result is counted and posted. Guard your vote with your eyes, not with your fists, because a peaceful people in their millions cannot be rigged out of their own country,” Imam said.
In his speech, Senator David Mark, the National Chairman of the ADC, charged members of the campaign council to leave no stone unturned.
“Leave no legitimate question unanswered. And leave no Nigerian behind. Go to every state, every local government, every ward and every community. Engage our traditional rulers, religious leaders, women, youths, workers, farmers, professionals, traders, artisans, students and persons living with disabilities. Listen to all Nigerians. Do not take any community for granted. Earn the confidence of the people.”
He said the campaign must be about the issues that matter to Nigerians such as, “High cost of living, poverty, the economy, security, jobs, food, education, healthcare, infrastructure, inflation, good governance, the rule of law and the future of our young people.
“Nigerians already know their problems. We do not need to lecture them about their sufferings.”

items.content: Wall Street ended higher on Friday as investors shifted their focus to next week, with third-quarter earnings season set to start and inflation data expected, which could shed light on the Federal Reserve's next policy decision, Reuters reported.The S&P 500 gained 46.35 points, or 0.60%, to end at 7,811.71 points, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 172.83 points, or 0.64%, to 27,365.00. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 429.90 points, or 0.84%, to 51,661.54.The three major indexes pared earlier gains after crude oil reversed its decline and Treasury yields resumed their climb.“It’s the kind of back-and-forth market we’ve been in where we have the reversal of sentiment around Iran,” Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird in Louisville, Kentucky told Reuters. “With conflicting headlines coming out of the White House and parties in the Middle East, there’s just no edge there.”“That’s why it’s a fairly tepid rally,” Mayfield added.Oil prices initially fell after President Donald Trump said the United States would not attack Iran before the midterm elections. He also described talks between Washington and Tehran aimed at ending the conflict as “productive.”Long-term Treasury yields edged higher, although the benchmark 10-year yield remained below the 24-year high reached on Wednesday.Banks prepare to report earningsThe third-quarter earnings season begins in earnest next week, with major US banks including Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Morgan Stanley scheduled to report results.Analysts expect aggregate S&P 500 earnings to rise 30.6% year over year in the July-September quarter, according to LSEG data. Energy and technology are projected to lead growth, with profits forecast to jump 123% and 66.5%, respectively.US consumer sentiment weakened this month, according to the University of Michigan. Near-term expectations fell to a record low, highlighting growing concerns among consumers, whose spending drives about 70% of the US economy.AI-linked momentum stocks broadly gained as the US bull market, driven largely by enthusiasm around artificial intelligence, approached its fourth anniversary.“Chips have been this year’s story,” said Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs in Dallas. “(It’s) a multidecade technological change and just at the beginning of whatever’s happening, not at the end.”SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide portfolio of low-band spectrum, mounting a direct challenge to established US wireless companies. T-Mobile US, AT&T and Verizon ended sharply lower.Humana jumped after US government data showed that 95% of the health insurer’s members were enrolled in Medicare Advantage plans rated four stars or higher for 2027.Apple declined after a media report said the company had asked some suppliers to reduce production of components for its newly launched iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Rising memory-chip costs and price increases were reportedly weighing on consumer demand.Delta Air Lines also fell after cutting its annual profit forecast.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.author: EngageMedia
items.content:
The provision could give the U.S. the power to exclude Chinese ICT suppliers in signatory countries
Originally published on Global Voices
Image remix on Canva by Ihsan Kamil/EngageMedia. Used with permission.
This article, written by Prapasiri “Nan” Suttisome, was first published by EngageMedia, a non-profit media, technology, and culture organization, and an edited version is republished here as part of a content-sharing agreement. It is also part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” You can support this coverage by donating here.
Around the world, one in every three people has no reliable access to the internet. Unequal access to the internet creates digital divides that can limit civic participation, undermine access to education and healthcare, and deepen inequality. It can also reduce innovation, industrial growth, and economic output. Reducing digital divides is recognized as essential for progress on the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals, as reaffirmed by the more recent Global Digital Compact, 2024.
However, this goal could be threatened by the controversial reciprocal trade agreements (ARTs) signed by the U.S. since February 2025. To date, the U.S. has signed ARTs with 10 countries — Malaysia, Cambodia, El Salvador, Argentina, Ecuador, Guatemala, Bangladesh, Taiwan, Jordan, and Indonesia — with framework deals in place with several others.
Hidden in most of these deals is a provision that requires these countries to refrain from using information and communication technology (ICT) suppliers that may “compromise the security, safeguards, and intellectual property of ICT infrastructure, including 5G, 6G, communication satellites, and undersea cables.” The ARTs with El Salvador, Guatemala, Indonesia, and Malaysia further require them to consult with the U.S. on which suppliers meet these standards.
The purpose of this provision is, simply put, to give the U.S. the ability to exclude Chinese ICT suppliers such as Huawei and ZTE from these countries, should it so choose. This could also benefit U.S. suppliers such as CISCO and Hewlett Packard, amongst others.
This provision therefore gives the U.S. a great deal of power, which, if misused, could significantly limit network rollout and development in the signatory countries, adversely affecting digital connectivity, increasing digital divides, and reducing economic growth.
This is significant, as most of the countries that have signed up to ARTs are low-income nations with significant digital divides. For example, internet penetration in Bangladesh, El Salvador, Indonesia, Guatemala, and Cambodia is 53.4 percent, 66.5 percent, 72.8 percent, 60.2 percent, and 68.5 percent, respectively. This has major implications for the connectivity of essential public infrastructure, especially in rural communities. For instance, over 100,000 schools lack internet connectivity in Indonesia, while approximately 12 percent of schools lack access to the internet in Guatemala. Cambodia fares worse, with only about 22 percent of schools having functional computers, let alone internet access.
A primary reason for the persistence of digital divides is the absence of necessary ICT infrastructure. The International Telecommunication Union has estimated a USD 1.6 trillion investment gap in ICT infrastructure by 2030.
In many parts of the developing world, China has filled the ICT infrastructure investment gap, including through soft loans provided through the Digital Silk Road (DSR), part of the Belt and Road Initiative. These loans are often provided at below-market rates and tied to the use of Chinese ICT suppliers. The scale of funding provided under the DSR is huge. For example, Chinese ICT infrastructure financing across Africa as far back as 2017 dwarfed the combined funds from African governments, multilateral agencies, and G7 nations.
Developing countries are caught between a rock and a hard place as it’s increasingly clear that foreign financial aid and investment —whether from China or the West — rarely comes without strings attached.
The fact that China is able and willing to subsidize network development on a global scale can be a draw for developing countries faced with significant budgetary pressures. However, excessive reliance on imported equipment comes with costs. For instance, a reliance on imports can create technological dependencies that could chill domestic technological sector growth by locking in foreign vendors. Many have also highlighted the possibility of foreign state surveillance or the possibility of “kill switches” being built into network equipment, giving rise to human rights, economic, and security-related concerns. Equally, development aid or loans can be leveraged in support of foreign geopolitical goals.
That said, it appears that U.S. and EU competitors may not have the capacity to service the burgeoning need for ICT equipment across the developing world. This is for many reasons ranging from Chinese control over the supply chains for critical elements required in the production of ICT equipment, the large subsidies, cheap labor, and access to manufacturing processes enjoyed by Chinese companies, as well as control over a significant number of essential patents in 5G and related technologies.
In fact, the U.S. has attempted to exclude Chinese ICT suppliers from its own telecom and communication networks for many years, but with limited success. Reports indicate that from 2019 through 2024, only 12 percent of Chinese equipment in the U.S. was actually replaced. It appears that Chinese ICT suppliers are deeply entrenched in U.S. communications systems, making the cost of replacement prohibitively high.
Despite being unable to replace Chinese equipment in its own networks, the U.S. government has pushed several of its allies, notably in the EU, to restrict market access for Chinese ICT companies. However, these countries have faced similar problems to the U.S. The European Commission, for instance, has pointed to how Chinese equipment can be up to 60 to 70 percent cheaper than equipment manufactured by Western counterparts, apparently due to large subsidies provided by the Chinese government. Replacing Chinese equipment is therefore difficult in practice, with some estimates suggesting a total cross-sectoral replacement cost of Chinese ICT equipment in the EU to be in the region of USD 430 billion.
This is why the provisions in the ARTs that could restrict the use of ICT equipment manufactured by Chinese companies are problematic. Even if Western companies want to fill the gap left by the exclusion of Chinese companies, they may not be able to do so quickly, at a reasonable cost, and at scale — particularly if China cuts them off from accessing crucial inputs and technologies.
All of this means that rollout of new-age ICT networks — 5G, 6G, and beyond — could be dramatically slowed in countries that have signed ARTs with the U.S. In fact, countries that have already contracted with Chinese manufacturers to build out their ICT infrastructure may well be placed in a predicament if they are forced to choose between an incumbent (Chinese) provider and an uncertain (Western) provider.
What is the alternative?
For low- and middle-income countries, trade agreements must promote a competitive global ICT hardware market, where they have a choice of global suppliers. This is particularly important given that low-income nations are unlikely to wean themselves off foreign technological imports any time soon. That said, they must be able to adopt policy measures that would enable them to develop their domestic industries, including by taking measures to enable fledgling industries to get off the ground. Key aspects of this may lie in ensuring technology transfers to enable domestic capacity building, promoting the use of innovative decentralized ICT networks that could utilize more domestic hardware, and also by enhancing global development financing.
Allowing any foreign country the power to decide which ICT equipment a country can purchase may prove a short-sighted move which, in addition to eroding sovereignty, could affect the country’s quality of life, economic growth, and competitiveness. It should be left to each country to decide what ICT equipment best suits its security, budgetary, technical needs, and other requirements. Such a model would eliminate constraints on domestic policy space and support progress towards globally accepted public interest goals.
Download the report “Trump’s ‘Agreements on Reciprocal Trade’ (ARTs) Threaten Equitable Access to the Internet in Developing Countries” from here for more details.
Written by EngageMedia

In many ways, it feels like coming back home,” wrote Singla in a LinkedIn post.
It is pertinent to note that Singla formerly previously served as head of engineering at fintech unicorn BharatPe. OTPless cofounders Bhavik Koladiya, Satyam Nathani and Tanmay Sagar were founding members at BharatPe. Singla stepped down from his role at the fintech unicorn in 2023.
He subsequently cofounded GenWise, a lifestyle app for senior citizens, along with fellow BharatPe alumni Nehul Malhotra and Rajat Jain. The startup went on to raise a $3.5 Mn seed round led by Z47, but eventually shut shop in December 2025.
After GenWise’s shutdown, Singla worked at Singapore-based wealthtech platform Syfe as an engineering leader for around a year before joining OTPless now.
Singla’s appointment as CTO comes in the middle of a major top-level reshuffle at OTPless. Just last month, cofounder Koladiya stepped down as OTPless’ CEO with Nathani taking up the mantle. At the same time, Sagar was named the company’s COO. Last week, Manas Poddar was also elevated to the post of chief business officer (CBO).
Founded in 2021, OTPless helps consumer internet enterprises offer authentication services through its SDKs and APIs. Its offerings include silent network authentication, WhatsApp authentication, device intelligence, and passkeys.
The Bengaluru-based startup’s offerings are aimed at reducing dependence on OTPs, PINs, and passwords while enabling enterprises to identify users, prevent fraud, and improve conversion during sign-ups and transactions.
The startup claims to have authenticated more than 30 Cr mobile users so far and serves enterprises such as Meesho, Navi, PhysicsWallah, ShareChat, Shiprocket and Zepto. It also claims to be clocking ₹36 Cr in annualised revenue and has been profitable for the past two quarters.
On the funding front, OTPless has raised over $6 Mn to date from the likes of Venture Highway, White Venture, FJ Labs, SIDBI, Piper Serica, among others.
At the heart of all this is the Indian identity and access management market, which is projected to become a $1.7 Bn opportunity by 2030.

items.content:
Elon Musk has ‘begged’ Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani to allow Starlink to launch in India’s internet market.
In a post on X on Friday, he called Ambani the ‘real boss of India’ and apologized sarcastically for failing to realize it.
“Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India,” Musk wrote.
He then asked Ambani to consider allowing Starlink to compete, despite what Musk described as his preference for maintaining a monopoly.
“Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” he said.
Musk argued that satellite internet could help people in areas without reliable internet access, giving children better educational opportunities and allowing small businesses to sell their products to international customers.
“Also, Starlink has proven to be essential for saving lives during natural disasters throughout the world, when all other communications systems have failed, so you would also be helping save men, women and children throughout India,” he added.
This follows Musk’s earlier criticism of regulatory hurdles delaying Starlink’s commercial launch in India. He previously questioned whether Ambani was the real power behind the company’s prolonged wait for approval.
Ambani’s Reliance Industries owns Jio, one of India’s largest telecom operators and a major player in the country’s internet market.
The Indian government has rejected Musk’s allegations that powerful business interests are blocking Starlink to protect existing operators.
Can you guess another country struggling to launch Starlink despite regulatory approvals? Comments.

Macquarie University in Australia has opened applications for its Road to Research Scholarship 2027, offering eligible Master of Research students tuition support and an AUD 40,900 living stipend.
The scholarship is available to applicants who can begin the Master of Research (MRes) in Session 1, 2027 and remain in Sydney during their candidature.
Applications will close on October 31, 2026, at 11:00 PM AEDT. Macquarie University expects to announce scholarship outcomes in early December 2026.

Scholarship Covers Tuition and Living Expenses
Successful candidates will receive a tuition fee offset for up to one year. Macquarie University will also provide an AUD 40,900 living allowance for one year, based on the 2027 scholarship rate.
Recipients may qualify for additional financial support in certain circumstances. Macquarie allows eligible students to receive supplementary minor awards and approved income from part-time work.
Students may also receive stipend top-up funding worth up to 100% of the main stipend, subject to scholarship conditions.
Separate funding may support research costs such as fieldwork, equipment, and other approved expenses that the main scholarship does not cover.
Who Can Apply for the Scholarship
Applicants must be onshore in Australia when they submit their application and must intend to live in Sydney throughout their research candidature.
Candidates need to start the Master of Research full-time in January 2027. They must also meet Macquarie University’s academic and English-language requirements for admission to the MRes.
This onshore condition is particularly important for international applicants. Pakistani and other overseas students can apply only if they are already in Australia and meet the applicable visa and admission requirements.
Research Areas Available at Macquarie University
The Master of Research covers a broad range of academic areas. Students can pursue research in fields such as arts and social sciences, business, criminology, education, engineering, health, information technology, language and linguistics, law, media, medicine, and psychological science.
Current Macquarie postgraduate coursework students who expect to complete their degree in Session 2, 2026 are also encouraged to apply if they meet the scholarship conditions.
How Macquarie University Will Select Candidates
Macquarie University will award the scholarship through a competitive ranking process. For eligible applicants, the university generally uses the Weighted Average Mark (WAM) to determine academic ranking.
Candidates who completed their qualification before 2020 or earned their degree from another university may instead be ranked using their Grade Point Average (GPA).
Macquarie will assess overseas qualifications using Australian Government guidelines to determine how they compare with qualifications under the Australian Qualifications Framework.
Supervisor Approval Is Important
Applicants need confirmation of supervision from an eligible Macquarie University researcher. This requirement is compulsory for candidates applying through the Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences.
For applicants in other faculties, securing supervision is strongly encouraged and may support the research application process.

Documents Required
Applicants should prepare their academic and supporting documents before starting the application.
Required materials include academic transcripts, degree documents, an essay or supporting statement, and two recommendation letters.
International candidates should also make sure their visa and residency information is accurate and current.
How to Apply
Eligible applicants must submit their application online for the Session 1, 2027 Master of Research intake.
Candidates should complete the required admission and scholarship information, provide supporting documents, and confirm supervision where required. Applications must be submitted by October 31, 2026, at 11:00 PM AEDT.

items.summary:
The University of Southampton has opened applications for a PhD research project that will use artificial intelligence and deep learning to predict nanoscale defects in semiconductor chip manufacturing.
The project, Deep Learning Modelling of Nano Defects in Chip Fabrication, combines semiconductor fabrication, experimental characterisation, machine learning and high-performance computing.
Applications will remain open until June 1, 2027.
According to the University of Southampton, the project provides funding for eligible students. UK and EU students can receive tuition fee coverage and a tax-free living stipend.
International candidates, including students from Pakistan, can also apply, although full international tuition support may depend on additional faculty funding.

items.content:
The University of Southampton has opened applications for a PhD research project that will use artificial intelligence and deep learning to predict nanoscale defects in semiconductor chip manufacturing.
The project, Deep Learning Modelling of Nano Defects in Chip Fabrication, combines semiconductor fabrication, experimental characterisation, machine learning and high-performance computing.
Applications will remain open until June 1, 2027.
According to the University of Southampton, the project provides funding for eligible students. UK and EU students can receive tuition fee coverage and a tax-free living stipend.
International candidates, including students from Pakistan, can also apply, although full international tuition support may depend on additional faculty funding.
University of Southampton PhD Scholarship Details

AI to Predict Defects Before Chip Manufacturing Fails
Modern processors, graphics chips and memory devices require thousands of tightly controlled manufacturing steps.
Small defects at the nanoscale can reduce chip quality, affect manufacturing yield and increase production costs.
Southampton researchers want to use deep learning to identify patterns that can predict these defects before they cause problems during fabrication.
The research aims to develop models that could help manufacturers improve production yield, shorten development cycles, and make semiconductor manufacturing more efficient.
PhD Combines AI With Hands-On Nanofabrication
This is not a purely software-based artificial intelligence project. The successful researcher will first manufacture nanoscale structures using techniques such as electron-beam lithography, plasma etching, and material deposition.
Microscopic and spectroscopic techniques will then be used to collect detailed information about the fabricated structures.
The researcher will apply AI and machine-learning algorithms to this experimental data to identify patterns linked to manufacturing defects.
Later stages will test these models in realistic fabrication scenarios to determine whether they can predict defects and help improve manufacturing processes.
Academic Requirements
Applicants need at least a UK 2:1 honours degree or an equivalent international qualification.
Relevant academic backgrounds include:
Electronic engineering
Physics
Materials science
Computer science
Closely related disciplines
Funding Rules for Pakistani Students
Pakistani students can apply as international candidates. However, applicants should carefully check the funding conditions.
Southampton states that UK and EU students receive tuition fee coverage together with a tax-free living stipend.
International students may need additional faculty funding to cover the difference between domestic and international tuition fees.
Pakistani applicants should therefore confirm the complete funding package before accepting an offer.
Documents Required for Application
Applicants should prepare their academic and supporting documents before starting the application. Southampton lists documents including a CV, research proposal, two academic references, degree certificates and academic transcripts.
Candidates may also need to provide proof of English-language proficiency depending on their academic background.
How to Apply
Applicants must submit their application through the University of Southampton’s postgraduate research admissions system.
Candidates should select the research route within the Faculty of Engineering and Physical Sciences and apply for the relevant PhD in Electronic and Electrical Engineering.
Applicants should also identify the project and supervisor when completing the application.
The deadline to apply for the Deep Learning Modelling of Nano Defects in Chip Fabrication PhD is June 1, 2027.

items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
Pakistani engineering graduates can apply for a fully-funded PhD at the University of Southampton in the UK, focusing on computational fluid dynamics, aeroacoustics, and aircraft engine noise.
Research under the High-fidelity CFD for Fan/OGVs Broadband Noise Modelling project will examine how turbulent airflow from an aircraft engine fan generates broadband noise when it interacts with outlet guide vanes.
Rolls-Royce and the EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Sustainable Sound Futures jointly fund the project. International students are eligible, and applications will close on September 1, 2027.

Why Aircraft Engine Noise Is the Main Research Focus
Modern Ultra High Bypass Ratio (UHBR) aero engines use larger and slower-moving fans as manufacturers work to improve aircraft efficiency and reduce noise.
However, these engine designs create new challenges for broadband noise prediction. Turbulent airflow left behind by the rotating fan interacts with stationary outlet guide vanes. This interaction produces broadband noise across a wide range of frequencies.
Current engineering models often simplify the behaviour of this fan wake turbulence. Such assumptions may not fully represent the complex airflow found in realistic aero engines.
Researchers at Southampton aim to identify which turbulence characteristics have the greatest effect on noise generation and improve the accuracy of future prediction models.
High-Fidelity CFD Using LES and DES
Advanced computational fluid dynamics will form a major part of the PhD. The researcher will use scale-resolving CFD techniques, including Large Eddy Simulation (LES) and Detached Eddy Simulation (DES), to model representative fan and outlet guide vane stages.
Analysis will cover turbulence intensity, integral length scales, velocity spectra, spatial coherence, and variations across the fan span.
Simulation results will also be compared with available experimental measurements to assess how accurately the CFD models reproduce real airflow.
Improving Broadband Aero Engine Noise Models
Acoustic analysis will examine how turbulent fan wakes create unsteady forces on outlet guide vanes and how these forces generate noise.
Researchers will investigate broadband noise across different frequencies and duct modes. Results from the simulations will help determine which turbulence statistics matter most for accurate noise prediction.
Those findings will then support improvements to semi-analytical engineering models, which can offer faster predictions than running full high-fidelity CFD simulations every time.
Researchers will compare the improved models with existing methods and experimental data.

What the Funding Covers
Southampton lists the PhD as fully funded for eligible international and UK students. Funding covers tuition fees and provides the successful candidate with a tax-free living stipend. A specific annual stipend amount is not stated in the project information.
Alongside financial support, the researcher will gain access to specialist facilities and research expertise within Southampton’s Institute of Sound and Vibration Research.
Documents Required for Application
Applicants should prepare their academic and supporting documents before starting the application.
Required materials include a CV, two academic references, academic transcripts, degree certificates, and proof of English-language proficiency where applicable.
Candidates should also clearly identify the relevant research project and supervisor in their application.
How to Apply
Applicants must submit a postgraduate research application to the University of Southampton for the 2027/28 academic year.
Candidates should select the research route under the Faculty of Engineering and Physical Sciences and identify the relevant engineering PhD and supervisor.
All required academic and supporting documents should be uploaded before final submission.
Applications for the fully funded CFD and aero engine noise PhD will close on September 1, 2027.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has announced a Tamgha for IT Minister Shaza Fatima on March 23 for her role in implementing the government’s petrol subsidy scheme, while hosting an afternoon tea for ministers and officials involved in the initiative.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, Shehbaz described the scheme as a risky undertaking that faced numerous challenges but said joint efforts by the federal and provincial governments had helped it reach more than 10 million registered citizens.
The scheme provides a monthly subsidy of Rs. 2,000 to eligible owners of motorcycles, Qingqi motorcycles, rickshaws, and vehicles with engines of up to 800cc. The government has allocated Rs. 75 billion for the initiative, which the prime minister said would continue.
Shehbaz praised the federal and provincial authorities for implementing the scheme through a digital process. He also thanked the Petroleum Division, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), State Bank of Pakistan, National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA), Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), and telecom operators for their contributions.
More than 10.85 million citizens had registered under the scheme, while vouchers had been issued to nearly 10.20 million people. A total of 27 million tokens had been issued, and subsidized petrol had been purchased using 19.4 million tokens.
Around 9.28 million citizens had used the facility for a second time. Shehbaz also claimed that nearly 96 percent of motorcycle riders had benefited from the scheme.
The prime minister compared the results with an earlier initiative launched in February, when 1.3 million tokens were issued at its peak. He credited cooperation between the federation and the provinces for the expanded reach of the current program.
Besides announcing the Tamgha for Shaza Fatima, Shehbaz said officials from other departments would receive shields in recognition of their work.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, and Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani were among those acknowledged for their roles in the scheme.
The prime minister also thanked provincial chief ministers and their teams for providing administrative and financial support.

These posts are in BS-14 and will be filled on a two-year contract, which may be extended. Successful candidates can be posted anywhere in Punjab. Applications will remain open until October 26, 2026.

Eligibility Criteria
Applicants can qualify through one of two routes. A candidate with a second-division graduation degree from an HEC-recognized university can apply if they also have basic computer knowledge.
PPSC will also consider graduates with five years of experience in the Intelligence Wing of a law-enforcement agency.
Only practical experience gained after completing the required qualification will count.
Age Limit
Male applicants can apply between the ages of 21 and 35 years. PPSC allows a five-year general relaxation, taking the maximum age to 40 years.
Female candidates also have a basic age limit of 21 to 35 years, with eight years of relaxation. Their maximum age therefore reaches 43 years.
For transgender candidates, PPSC will determine age and gender according to the details recorded on their CNIC.
Written Test Syllabus
PPSC will conduct a 100-mark MCQ-based test for the Intelligence Officer posts. Candidates will get 90 minutes to complete the paper.
Around 80% of the test will cover general ability subjects, including General Knowledge, Pakistan Studies, Current Affairs, Geography, Basic Mathematics, English, Urdu, Everyday Science, and Islamic Studies.
Non-Muslim candidates will receive general knowledge questions instead of Islamic Studies. The remaining 20% will cover Basic Computer Studies.
How to Apply for Punjab Police Jobs
Candidates must submit their applications online through the Punjab Public Service Commission.
Before applying, they should check their qualifications, age, domicile, and experience against the requirements listed in Advertisement No. 11/2026.
PPSC accepts the application fee through approved payment methods, including ATMs, mobile banking, internet banking, 1Link member bank branches, JazzCash, Easypaisa, UPaisa, and supported microfinance banks.

items.title: 50,000 Wheat Farmers Get Financial Support Under Benazir Kissan Card
items.summary:
The Balochistan government has provided direct financial support to 50,000 wheat farmers under the newly launched Benazir Kissan Card program.
According to an announcement from the Directorate General of Public Relations (DGPR), Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti has launched the initiative to provide direct subsidies to farmers across the province.
Under the program, 50,000 wheat growers have received financial assistance for wheat threshing.
The government said the support is being provided directly to eligible farmers through the Benazir Kissan Card program.
Officials presented the initiative as part of the provincial government’s efforts to support farmers and strengthen agricultural activity in Balochistan.
The announcement does not specify the amount of financial assistance provided to each farmer or give further details about the eligibility and application process.

items.title: Punjab Announces Major Incentives for Kissan Card Holders
items.summary:
The Punjab Agriculture Department has announced new incentives for Kissan Card holders who clear their outstanding amount within the given deadline.
According to the department’s announcement, farmers who have used funds through the Kissan Card will receive a bill payment message on October 15, 2026.
Kissan Card holders have been asked to deposit their outstanding amount by October 26, 2026.
Farmers must make the payment within the deadline. The department will make the amount available again within 48 hours.
The department has also announced prizes worth crores of rupees for eligible Kissan Card holders. The prizes mentioned in the notice include tractors, motorcycles and mobile phones.
Farmers can pay their Kissan Card bills through any Bank of Punjab branch, an ATM, or through Raast ID.
The Punjab Agriculture Department has advised farmers to complete the payment process within the announced deadline.

items.author: Ado Abubakar Musa, Jos
items.content:
Gunmen have reportedly killed a police officer on his way to duty post along the Kwi-Beco road, a community between Riyom and Barikn Ladi local government areas of Plateau State.
The incident, according to sources, occurred at about 7pm on Thursday.
The development came amid heightened tensions in Mangu, Bokkos and Barikin Ladi LGAs where government recently imposed curfew to douse tensions.
Our correspondent reports that the affected security operative was reportedly riding on a motorcycle to his duty post in the Chit area of Heipang District, when he was attacked and killed.
Benue govt shuts schools forcing parents to buy textbooks
ABU increases fees
Sources said the assailants also made away with the motorcycle after the attack.
The spokesman of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association (BYM), Rwang Tengwong, confirmed the incident and described it as disturbing.
Tengwong lamented that the killing of a security operative raised serious concerns about the safety of civilians in the affected communities.
He said the group was particularly troubled that security personnel deployed to protect residents were themselves vulnerable to attacks.
The BYM spokesman condemned the killing and called for urgent measures to address the security challenges confronting communities in the area.
The spokesperson of the state police command, DSP Alabo Alfred, did not respond to inquiry from our correspondent as of press time.
Daily Trust reports that despite the recent imposition of curfew, attacks and killings have continued in the state.

items.title: Remittances cool to $3.6b in Sept
items.summary:
Workers' remittances stood at $3.59 billion in September, down 1.9% from $3.66 billion in August but up 12.7% from $3.18 billion a year earlier, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) data showed. However, the pace cooled compared to August 2026.
Inflows in July-September reached $10.88 billion, 14% higher than $9.54 billion in the same quarter of FY26. The quarter was running ahead of last year's record pace.
July, August and September all cleared $3.5 billion, at $3.63 billion, $3.66 billion and $3.59 billion, respectively. The monthly average was $3,625 million, above the FY26 full-year average of $3,465 million.

Workers' remittances stood at $3.59 billion in September, down 1.9% from $3.66 billion in August but up 12.7% from $3.18 billion a year earlier, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) data showed. However, the pace cooled compared to August 2026.
Inflows in July-September reached $10.88 billion, 14% higher than $9.54 billion in the same quarter of FY26. The quarter was running ahead of last year's record pace.
July, August and September all cleared $3.5 billion, at $3.63 billion, $3.66 billion and $3.59 billion, respectively. The monthly average was $3,625 million, above the FY26 full-year average of $3,465 million.
The July-September quarter points to inflows of about $43.5 billion in financial year 2026-27, against $41.6 billion in FY26 and an SBP projection of around $44 billion. "We expect remittances for FY27 to clock in at $44.7 billion," Topline Securities predicted.
In September, the year-on-year growth slowed to 12.7% from 16.5% in August and 12.9% in July. May's $4.25 billion remained the monthly high. Remittances of $3.5 billion a month are now ordinary, not a peak.
Gulf leads the month
Saudi Arabia was the only large corridor to rise from August, sending $899.1 million, up 2.9% month on month and 19.7% from $751 million a year earlier. It remained the largest source.
Inflows from other GCC countries rose 4.7% to $342.1 million. Oman, Qatar and Kuwait all increased. The UAE was almost flat at $748.5 million, down 0.2% from August and up 10.5% year-on-year.
The month's softness sat in Europe, not the Gulf. Remittances from the UK fell 8.6% to $515.1 million. EU countries fell 9.7% to $447.7 million, led by Italy ($152.9 million to $133.5 million) and Greece ($56.8 million to $48.6 million).
Saudi Arabia and the UAE together accounted for 46% of September remittances. With other GCC countries, the Gulf stood at 55%. Inside the UAE, the quarter splits. Inflows from Dubai rose 30.1% to $1.83 billion in the quarter, Abu Dhabi fell 34.5% to $331 million – even it rose in September, from $91.1 million to $104.5 million. Dubai's remittances eased from $634.6 million to $617.5 million in September.
West is where the growth is
Over the quarter, remittances from the UK rose 19.4% to $1.63 billion, the fastest among the large corridors. Inflows from the US rose 15.5% to $931 million, after a decline in the previous year's comparison. September inflows from the US were $305.9 million, down 0.9% from August and up 13.7% year-on-year.
Australia rose 9.5% in the quarter and Canada 11.7%. The EU was slower, up 9.8% to $1.41 billion. France was the weak spot, down 4.5%. Smaller corridors grew faster: Ireland 24.4%, Japan 42.6%, and South Korea 21.9%.
The UK, EU, US, Canada and Australia accounted for about 40% of September remittances. Experts say the policy question is skilled migration and student-to-worker routes, not only Gulf labour exports.
At a $3.6 billion monthly pace, remittances still do the heavy lifting on the current account. The SBP has already credited sustained inflows for the reserves rebuild and a narrower external gap.
Furthermore, the Pakistani rupee extended its marginal gains against the US dollar in the inter-bank market on Friday, closing at 277.00 after appreciating by Rs0.01. In the previous session on Thursday, the local currency had settled at 277.01 against the greenback.
In international markets, the euro was on course for its fifth consecutive weekly decline on Friday, although selling pressure showed signs of easing. France's stabilising debt market and falling US Treasury yields helped temper the dollar's rally.
Meanwhile, gold prices in Pakistan rose, tracking gains in the international market, with the price of one tola increasing by Rs5,900 to settle at Rs440,936. Globally, gold rose for a second straight session on Friday to a one-week high, as bargain buying emerged after bullion touched a two-month low earlier this week, while traders assessed the likelihood of further US Federal Reserve rate hikes.
According to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the 10-gram gold climbed by Rs5,058 to Rs378,031. On Thursday, gold had gained Rs600 per tola to reach Rs435,036.
In the international market, spot gold rose 1.4% to $4,190.49 by 1544 GMT, heading for a weekly gain of about 1.2%. The metal fell to a two-month low on Wednesday as a stronger dollar and rising US Treasury yields weighed on the non-yielding metal, as per Reuters. US gold futures for December delivery also added 1.4%, trading at $4,215.60 per ounce.
Bullion gained due to "bargain hunting at the lows, as a floor has been building in the $4,000 region," said Rhona O'Connell, Head of Market Analysis at Stone X. "It is arguable that a further Fed hike is already priced in but so is the expectation for continued official sector net purchases. Without any Black Swan event, I find it hard to see gold breaking convincingly higher."
The US 10-year Treasury yields were off over two-decade highs hit on Wednesday. Meanwhile, silver prices in the domestic market rose by Rs144 to Rs6,512 per tola.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
A member of the National Tariff Policy Board has opposed a decision to impose up to 31% additional duty on some imports, which the government has decided to slap despite its new pro-trade liberalisation National Tariff Policy discouraging import substitution.
It is a wrong decision to impose additional customs duty on the import of tyres of vehicles and some parts of motorcycles, said Dr Rubina Athar, a member of the Tariff Policy Board, who was part of the National Tariff Policy formulation and one of the strongest proponents of trade liberalisation.
She was responding to a question during a panel discussion on Pakistan's tariff reforms, arranged by the United Kingdom-funded Revenue Mobilisation, Investment and Trade (REMIT) Initiative.
"Every tariff-related proposal should come to the National Tariff Policy Board before going to the cabinet, and as a member of the board I can say this matter has not come to the policy board for a decision before it was sent to the ECC," said Athar.
The finance ministry said on Thursday that the ECC approved the imposition of 11% additional customs duty on import of tyres to protect the local industry. It slapped 11% additional customs duty on the import of parts of motorcycles and 31% if the manufacturers import these parts instead of locally producing them.
The 31% duty is imposed on motorcycle components including licence plate, bracket, side reflector, right and left-side plate, front decorative connection part, foot plate, wheel assembly, windshield, seat, toolbox, centre covers and plates & parts.
But imports of these parts from China will still be taxed at zero duty under the Free Trade Agreement. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government had approved the National Tariff Policy with an aim to fully liberalise the economy by demolishing trade barriers. It is the first such decision where the government has added more bricks to the wall instead of tearing them down.
The Federal Board of Revenue had moved the summary for the approval of the ECC. When inquired about the motive, beneficiaries of the additional customs duty and the rationale to breach the tariff policy, it did not give a reply.
"It is the Ministry of Industries' proposal developed by the Engineering Development Board," said the FBR spokesman. In its response, the Ministry of Commerce said that the ECC considered the amendment in SRO 693(1)/2006, which pertains to the imposition of additional customs duty on parts being locally manufactured if imported by OEMs in kit form. The commerce ministry said that the list of items to be included in the SRO is to be reviewed bi-annually by the Ministry of Industries & Production.
The "auto sector SROs do not operate under the National Tariff Policy as was held by the Tariff Policy Board in its meeting held on 6th June, 2026, whereby it was decided that the SRO 693 does not fall within the purview of TPB being part of another policy", according to the commerce ministry. The mechanism available under the Auto Policy 2021-26 still exists in the shape of SROs, including SRO 693(1)/2006, and MOC, in principle, supported the amendment, it added.
However, the auto policy lapsed in June this year and there is no new approved auto policy. But the commerce ministry said that these SROs were still in the field. The ministry said that Service Long March locally manufactures these tyres.
The national tariff policy is aimed at opening the economy by ending the import substitution policy, said Rubina Athar. She said that the import substitution policies had made industries inefficient and the consumers did not benefit from it.
Dr Vaqar Ahmed, a senior economist, said that favouritism in the application of tariff policy would kill its purpose, but the auto sector has been explicitly excluded from the purview.
Zafar Mehmood, Chief Executive Officer of Nimir Chemicals, said that lowering the customs duties would not bring efficiency and reduce cost for the consumers, as other duties and taxes were causing more problems. He said that the National Tariff Policy has compromised the cascading principle of protection, which would severely impact many industries.
Member Customs FBR Shakil Shah agreed that import taxes, particularly advance income tax, were creating serious problems for the industries. The FBR withholds advance income tax at the import stage irrespective of whether the industry would make any profit or not, which is unnecessarily blocking the money of industries, said Shah.
"If the earned profits are less than the withheld advance income tax, the importer will never get refunds, and we need to eliminate these withholding taxes at the import stage," said Shah.
Zain ul Abideen, CEO Rubatech, said that the national tariff policy combined with the new energy vehicle policy was a death sentence to the auto industry. Zain said that preferential treatment being given to the NEVs would eliminate internal combustion engine cars.
But Rubina Athar argued that some shock had to be given to the industries to wake them up from inertia. Wajid Bukhari, Secretary General Pakistan Association of Large Steel Producers, said that the tariff policy did not impact the steel industry so far due to reduction in the interest rates and energy cost.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan has called for wider access to export credit insurance and financing to help Pakistani exporters enter new markets, manage payment risks and expand their business, with particular attention to small enterprises and first-time exporters.
The minister was speaking during a meeting with Exim Bank CEO Shahbaz H Syed. Khan emphasised that export support should reach emerging businesses and smaller producers seeking to enter international markets. He noted that access to capital, practical guidance and appropriate risk protection could help these enterprises become established exporters.
The minister proposed closer coordination between Exim Bank and Pakistan's trade and investment officers abroad to identify opportunities, facilitate business contacts and support exporters in destination markets. He also encouraged the bank to explore cooperation with international export credit agencies and financial institutions to broaden financing opportunities.
Speaking at the meeting, Shahbaz H Syed explained that Exim Bank's export credit insurance was protecting exporters from specified commercial and political risks associated with overseas transactions. These included buyer default and events that prevented payments or the transfer of funds from destination markets.
The CEO said coverage could extend up to 90% of the insured risk, subject to applicable terms and assessment, with exporters retaining a share of the exposure. He explained that the assessment focused on the overseas buyer's creditworthiness and the destination market's risk profile, allowing new exporters to seek coverage as well.
Syed highlighted the role of commercial banks as potential partners and distribution channels for export credit insurance. He explained that insured export receivables could support access to financing, subject to banks' requirements and the applicable regulatory framework.
Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul, who was present in the meeting, underscored the importance of connecting insurance protection with practical financing arrangements. The discussion considered how cooperation among Exim Bank, commercial banks and other financial institutions could help exporters use insured transactions to obtain working capital and pursue business growth.
The meeting also examined the financing needs of small enterprises, including businesses supplying larger exporters, and the importance of longer-term investment in production capacity alongside short-term working capital support.
Jam Kamal Khan encouraged Exim Bank to participate more actively in trade exhibitions, including FoodAg, where Pakistani exporters and international buyers could receive guidance on insurance and financing options.

items.content:
Federal Minister for Finance Muhammad Aurangzeb met a Dutch business delegation, led by the Founders Carbon Network (FCN) and accompanied by the Netherlands Ambassador Robert-Jan Siegert.
The minister emphasised the importance of strengthening business-to-business linkages, fostering mutual understanding and deepening bilateral economic cooperation. He noted that sustained engagement between the business communities of Pakistan and the Netherlands would help identify commercially viable investment opportunities, develop partnerships and build investor confidence.
Aurangzeb highlighted Pakistan's improving macroeconomic outlook and stressed the need for translating the gains of stabilisation into productive investment, capital formation, export expansion and private-sector-led growth. He emphasised that the next phase of Pakistan's economic development must be increasingly export-oriented, productivity-driven and employment-generating, supported by structural reforms and greater mobilisation of private capital.
Outlining the government's economic priorities, the finance minister underscored the need to consolidate macroeconomic stability and strengthen fiscal and external resilience; transition towards sustainable, inclusive and responsible growth; maintain momentum on implementation-focused structural reforms; shift from aid dependence towards trade and investment; broaden access to finance for SMEs, agriculture, housing and underserved communities; and position Pakistan to benefit from the "New Economy" through digitalisation and emerging technologies.
Referring to the strengthening external position, the minister noted that foreign exchange reserves had reached a historic high of $21.4 billion, providing over three months of import cover. He emphasised that sustaining these gains and building resilience against external shocks remained essential to reinforcing investor confidence and creating a durable foundation for economic growth.
Aurangzeb identified rapid population growth and climate change as two existential challenges facing Pakistan, underscoring their implications for economic sustainability, human development and long-term resilience. He called for addressing these challenges through sustained policy attention and coordinated reforms.
Highlighting opportunities for closer Pakistan-Netherlands economic cooperation, the minister pointed to the potential for Dutch expertise, technology and investment to complement Pakistan's development priorities across key sectors. He identified public-private partnerships as an important avenue for mobilising private capital, leveraging specialised expertise and translating investment interest into commercially viable projects.
Adviser to the prime minister on privatisation, who was present in the meeting, reaffirmed the government's commitment to expanding private-sector participation through privatisation and public-private partnerships. He noted that these initiatives were aimed at improving efficiency, attracting investment and creating greater opportunities for private enterprises across commercial activities.
Members of the Dutch delegation shared their perspectives on Pakistan's business environment and prospects for expanded bilateral cooperation. The discussions highlighted opportunities to strengthen B2B engagement, identify areas of mutual interest and develop commercially viable partnerships between Pakistani and Dutch enterprises.

items.content:
The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (Aptma), in collaboration with the Chainstore Association of Pakistan (CAP), hosted its first-ever Manufacturing Retail Working Session, bringing together leading Pakistani retail brands and textile manufacturers to strengthen domestic sourcing, develop internationally competitive products and create a pathway for Pakistani brands to expand into global markets.
The initiative forms part of a broader vision to increase Pakistan's textile exports by $3 billion within the next 12 months and $10 billion over the next few years, through greater value addition, stronger industrial collaboration and international expansion of Pakistani brands.
Speaking at the event, Aptma Chairman Asad Shafi highlighted Pakistan's unique retail landscape, where homegrown brands dominated the organised fashion retail sector, demonstrating the strength of local entrepreneurship, design capabilities and consumer understanding.
"Pakistan has already developed some exceptionally strong local brands that compete on quality, design and retail experience. The next step is to take these brands global. We should not limit our ambition to manufacturing products for international brands when we have the capability to develop, manufacture, establish brand and sell our own products to consumers around the world," said Shafi.
He noted that Pakistan had made considerable progress in value-added textile exports, with more than 80% of textile exports comprising value-added consumer products, including apparel and home textiles. "However, the country must now focus on capturing a greater share of the value generated beyond manufacturing."

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on Friday, damaging homes, cutting power, halting flights and sending residents into the streets, while triggering more than a dozen aftershocks.
The US Geological Survey said the earthquake struck at a depth of 12.6 km (7.8 miles) and that some casualties were possible.
Television images showed elderly residents in tears in the streets as a series of weaker aftershocks rattled the country.
"We're scared. It's just the two of us old folks here. The house has cracked, and we're afraid it could fall on us," said Ricardo Brown, 74, in Herrera province in southern Panama, where he noted the quake damaged several homes in his area of Las Minas.
A car damaged by falling debris after an earthquake struck near the southern coast of Panama, in Panama City, Panama, October 9, 2026. Photo: Reuters
The Panama Canal, about 126 miles (203 km) from the epicenter, was operating normally.
About 90 vessels, including bulk carriers, tankers and container ships, were waiting at both ends of the key waterway to transit or dock at berths serving storage terminals and trans-shipment services, according to monitoring data from LSEG's Workspace.
Major earthquakes are rare in Panama.
USGS estimated economic losses could amount to 1% to 10% of Panama's gross domestic product.
Power was down across six provinces, according to electricity provider Naturgy. The Tocumen International airport, a major regional hub, suspended flights.
Prolonged vibrations
Nestor Luque, director of Panama's geosciences institute, said the quake was triggered by the Azuero Sona Fault System that has long contained a build-up of pressure.
"It's a system of active faults that occasionally, due to the accumulation of stress, release this amount of energy," he said. "The seismic signals have traveled throughout the national territory, and that is why it could be felt everywhere."
🇵🇦 Footage of the Centenario Bridge in Panama after a 7.7 earthquake, with traffic still moving across it.
And it was a powerful one. The quake struck roughly 200 km from Panama City, but the shaking was still felt in the capital.
Despite that, the Panama Canal and this major… https://t.co/GT3jjSMDRm
— Mario Nawfal (@MarioNawfal) October 9, 2026
In Panama City, Luke said he counted 40 seconds of vibrations, though other areas may have felt even longer tremors.
Sabina Rios, who was on the sixth floor of an old US military-era building in Panama City, said the shaking was unusually strong and prolonged.
"The quake felt strong and lasted a long time, the longest I've felt in years," Rios said.
Traffic snarled across Panama City as many offices released employees early, unsure of conditions or potential structural damage to buildings, and the Metro halted service.
Students in uniform poured onto the streets of downtown Panama as schools were let out early across the city. Classes were suspended nationwide.
Damage to buildings
The quake's epicenter was close to the rural community of La Pitaloza in a sparsely populated area of Herrera, near the Pacific coastline. Shaking was also felt as far as San Jose, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica, according to a Reuters witness.
In Penonome, a city about halfway between the epicenter and Panama City, social media videos verified by Reuters showed a damaged church and nearby collapsed buildings.
primeras imagenes de los daños del terremoto de panama #earthquake #Terremoto #panama #sismo #temblor pic.twitter.com/zpymnIyo9j
— Tendencia en X HOY (@TendenciaenXHoy) October 9, 2026
Omar Smith, who heads Panama's civil protection agency, told news outlet Telemetro Reporta that impacts had also been reported in Chitre, the capital of Herrera, and along the coast in Los Santos province.
A tsunami threat triggered by the earthquake off Panama has passed, and no further tsunami danger remains, the US Tsunami Warning System said.
People gather in an open area after an earthquake struck near the southern coast of Panama, in Panama City, Panama, October 9, 2026. Photo: Reuters
Panama was due to hold a national evacuation drill on Monday next week to test the country's emergency response capabilities in the event of an earthquake.
Venezuela and Colombia have also suffered major earthquakes in recent months, causing thousands of deaths in total.

items.author: Naeem Asghar
items.content:
A young student who dreamed of studying at a US university was found hanging from a tree near a road in Islamabad on Friday, after her family allegedly lost around Rs7 million to a consultant who promised to secure her admission and scholarship, her relatives alleged.
The student had completed her bachelor’s degree from the International Islamic University Islamabad, earning a gold medal, and hoped to continue her studies abroad.
Her family said they sold a plot of land and jewellery to finance the dream, only to discover that the admission letter, scholarship letter and other documents provided by the consultant were all fake.
Read: Medical student dies in suspected suicide
According to an Islamabad police spokesperson, Sharif Ullah, the student’s body was found hanging from a tree near a road in the jurisdiction of the Ramna police station on Friday.
Police said the incident appeared to be a suicide at first, but the actual cause would be established after a post-mortem examination and further investigation.
Her body was shifted to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), where the post-mortem examination was under way.
Speaking to Express News outside the hospital’s mortuary, the student’s maternal uncle, Rana Amjad, said she was an exceptionally capable student who had completed her BS degree with a gold medal and wanted to pursue further education.
He said her father had been supplying milk on a motorcycle in Islamabad for the past 30 years and lived with his family in a rented flat in the capital.
According to Amjad, her niece met a man while visiting a place for an interview. The man claimed he could secure her admission to a university in the United States. After discussing the offer with her father, the family decided to pursue the opportunity despite opposition from her brothers.
Her father sold a plot in a private housing society and paid Rs2.1 million to the consultant, Amjad said.
Also Read: Domestic reasons suspected in Lahore university student’s suicide attempt: police
The consultant later demanded more money, saying it needed to be deposited in the student’s bank account to generate a bank statement required for the application, he added.
Amjad said his brother-in-law (the victim's father) then handed over his wife’s jewellery to the consultant. Instead of depositing the jewellery’s value into the student’s account, the man allegedly deposited it into his own account and gave her a fake bank receipt.
Amjad, a lawyer by profession, said the family approached him only after handing over the money and jewellery, when the consultant’s repeated delays in arranging his niece’s travel to the United States raised their suspicions.
He said he examined the documents provided by the consultant, including an admission letter purportedly issued by Harvard University, a scholarship letter and other university-related papers. He then had them checked through relatives living in the United States.
“We found out that all the documents were fake,” he said.
Amjad said he told his niece that the family had been defrauded, prompting her to break down in tears.
Read More: Student critically injured in fall at Lahore university
“She told me not to tell her father because he would not be able to bear it,” he said, adding that she remained deeply distressed over what had happened.
The student’s younger brother said she had wanted to continue her education, but the alleged fraud had shattered the family’s hopes.
The police said the circumstances surrounding her death would become clearer after the post-mortem examination and investigation.

US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel to American and global markets following talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump said on his Truth Social platform that he had concluded a "highly successful discussion" with Putin, resulting in an agreement to increase Russian diesel supplies.
"I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter," Trump said.
He added that another 3m tonnes would be delivered "within a short period", depending on the condition of Russian diesel refineries.
"Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be coming down, in record numbers, and fast!” Trump said.
The president described lower fuel prices as a priority, particularly for American farmers, ranchers and truckers.
Read More: Oil falls as Trump comments on Iran talks ease supply concerns
Trump also cited what he described as US "total control" of the Strait of Hormuz and reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.
US Treasury authorises Russian diesel supplies
Shortly after Trump's announcement, the US Treasury Department said on X that its Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) was "immediately issuing a temporary general licence to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market".
Today, at President Trump’s direction, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is immediately issuing a temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market.
— Treasury Department (@USTreasury) October 9, 2026
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to respond with missile and drone attacks across the region and effectively close the Strait of Hormuz.
The conflict has continued for more than seven months, driving up global energy prices as commercial oil traffic through the strategic waterway has effectively halted.
The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June following mediation efforts by Pakistan and Qatar to halt hostilities and pave the way for negotiations.
Implementation of the agreement has since stalled amid disagreements, including over security and navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
After improving its bottom line performance in the fiscal year FY25, D2C fashion brand Bewakoof reversed the trend and slipped deeper into the red in the fiscal year ended March 2026.
The company’s net loss increased 19.4% to ₹87.4 Cr in FY26 from ₹73.2 Cr in FY25. The brand had managed to improve its bottom line by 29% YoY in the previous fiscal.
The loss expanded despite an improvement in its top line performance in the fiscal. The brand’s operating revenue for the fiscal grew by 40.6% to ₹243.1 Cr from ₹173 Cr. It also earned ₹5 Cr in other income during the year under review, pushing total income to ₹248.2 Cr.
Profitability improved marginally on an EBITDA basis as its EBITDA loss narrowed by 7.2% to ₹54.8 Cr, compared to ₹59 Cr in the previous year.
Founded in 2012 by Prabhkiran Singh, Bewakoof is a D2C fashion and lifestyle brand that sells clothing, accessories, notebooks, and backpacks targeted at millennials and Gen Z consumers. It competes with the likes of MyDesignation, Snitch, and The Souled Store.
In late 2022, Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail (ABFRL), through its roll-up subsidiary TMRW, bought a majority stake in the startup for ₹200 Cr. The acquisition was completed in February 2023.
Notably, Bewakoof’s founder Singh had announced earlier this year that he planned to step down at the end of March to focus on personal goals. The brand is yet to clarify its new leadership structure.
Where Did Bewakoof Spend?
Bewakoof’s total expenses stood at ₹335.6 Cr in FY26, a 35.4% YoY jump. Let’s examine its top expenses. It incurred no tax expenses during the year.
Cost Of Materials Consumed: The startup’s raw material costs increased 29.6% to ₹70.6 Cr compared to ₹54.5 Cr in the year-ago period.
Purchases Of Stock-In-Trade: Expenses under this line item jumped 67.4% to ₹63.6 Cr in FY26 from ₹38 Cr in FY25.
Employee Benefit Expense: Bewakoof’s spending on personnel related expenses grew 10.6% YoY to ₹28.4 Cr from ₹25.6 Cr previously.
Depreciation, Depletion And Amortisation Expense: Depreciation costs more than doubled to ₹16.6 Cr in FY26 from ₹6.1 Cr in FY25
Other Expenses: Spending under this line item, which includes marketing, promotional and office expenses, increased 20.9% YoY to ₹146.6 Cr.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Amnesty International said on Friday that the Punjab Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill, 2026, raised "serious" concerns about the "right to a fair trial", further noting that the amendment allowed for "secret trials" that could result in grave human rights violations.
On August 31, the Punjab Assembly passed the Punjab Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amid protests and a walkout by opposition lawmakers.
In a public statement, Amnesty International noted that the amendment was a "glaring attack on the right to fair trial in Pakistan".
Pakistan: The Anti-Terrorism (Punjab Amendment) Act, 2026, raises serious concerns about the right to a fair trial.
In a new public statement, Amnesty International examines the amendment against Pakistan’s obligations under international human rights law and highlights how…
— Amnesty International South Asia, Regional Office (@amnestysasia) October 9, 2026
The statement added that the amendment created a mechanism for trials shrouded in "complete secrecy", exceeding permissible exceptions to the "right to a fair trial", which includes a public trial, under international human rights law, further adding that it deepened concerns regarding "past misuse" of anti-terrorism laws that had resulted in grave human rights violations.
Read: LHC seeks arguments on anti-terror bill's legality
The statement also noted that the process and criteria for designating a trial as a “special security case” were highly vague and lacked transparency.
"The text of section 21AAA(5)(b) suggests that the designated authority has full discretion to decide whether a case or a class of cases require extraordinary protection measures and that the chief justice is bound by this decision. Neither the amendment nor the original act offers a definition of what constitutes extraordinary protection," it added.
Amnesty further stated that the amendment allowed a level of secrecy with enormous potential for miscarriage of justice.
"The amendment is applicable to Punjab province, which is Pakistan’s most populous province consisting of 127,333,305 people (50.9% of the total population)37, and if this act is allowed to be implemented it could lead to a knock-on effect in other provinces who could pass similar legislation."
Background of law
The amendment inserted a new Section 21AAA into the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, creating a “special security case” mechanism for cases in which participants are considered to require extraordinary protection.
Read More: Punjab Assembly passes controversial anti-terror law
A designated authority — an officer of at least BS-20 whose identity would itself remain confidential — can declare a case or a class of cases a special security case. At the authority’s request, the LHC chief justice can assign the case to an Anti-Terrorism Court judge.
The amendment also said that the identities of judges, public prosecutors, defence counsel, police officers, witnesses and other persons involved in such proceedings “shall not be disclosed”.
Judicial orders will use official titles instead of judges’ names, and witnesses would be identified by codes issued by the designated authority.
The proceedings could be held at secure premises or conducted through video links, including from prisons. The amendment also allows the government to adopt other security measures it considers appropriate.
