items.content: Asian stocks dropped, tracking declines on Wall Street, as speculation about OpenAI’s revenue revived concerns over the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence spending boom. Oil edged lower.The MSCI Asia Pacific equities index edged 0.1% lower early Friday. Japan’s Nikkei fell over 1%, with Softbank Group Corp. declining more than 5%. The regional moves came after the Nasdaq 100 Index sank 1.4%, its worst day in seven weeks, while a US gauge of chipmakers slumped 3.4%. The S&P 500 Index dropped 0.5%. Markets are closed in South Korea and Taiwan. Read more: US stocks: S&P 500, Nasdaq end lower as crude prices jump, chip stocks weighThe declines in the US followed a Financial Times report that OpenAI’s annualized revenue was $20 billion below previously signaled levels. The ChatGPT maker is on track for roughly $50 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Also, Firmus Grid Ltd., an Australian data center company backed by Nvidia Corp., is set to postpone its initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.Elsewhere, American crude declined to around $91 a barrel after President Donald Trump said the US would not attack Iran ahead of November’s midterm elections. Global benchmark Brent fell 0.5% to around $103.80 a barrel. Treasuries held their gains from the US session, while a Bloomberg gauge of the dollar traded steady.“For now, the focus remains on whether the selling in AI and semiconductors develops into a broader risk reduction, or whether investors use the pullback to rebuild exposure ahead of earnings,” wrote Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone.The OpenAI revenue questions added to concerns over AI spending as elevated borrowing costs make the vast sums flowing into data centers and computing infrastructure harder to justify. Investors are increasingly looking for evidence that revenue can keep pace with the investment required to develop and run AI models.While OpenAI’s roughly $50 billion revenue is an uptick from the prior year, it’s still less than recently reported estimates.OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI firms have often touted their annualized revenue — a projection of annual sales based on a shorter period — as a key growth metric. However, not all companies measure it the same way. Anthropic’s annualized revenue hit $65 billion by the end of July, Bloomberg News previously reported. In stocks, the weakness remained concentrated in technology rather than spreading across the broader market. More than two-thirds of S&P 500 members advanced, while small-cap shares were little changed as investors rotated toward defensive sectors.Meanwhile, Treasuries advanced on Thursday after solid demand at a 30-year debt auction pulled long-dated yields back from more than two-decade highs. The rally extended after Trump said he would hold off on attacking Iran again until after the US midterm elections on Nov. 3.The gains provided some respite from a months-long selloff in longer-term debt, fueled by concerns that the Iran war will keep energy prices and inflation elevated, alongside mounting worries over government finances.The outlook for rates remained under pressure, however, as Federal Reserve officials signaled more tightening ahead. Governor Christopher Waller said further increases will probably be needed to bring inflation under control, while St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said rates should rise over the next six to nine months without endorsing a move this month.“To bring inflation back to target in a timely manner, more monetary policy firming will be required,” Musalem said Thursday at a Bloomberg event in New York.

items.content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja
ABUJA — The Federal Government has activated more than 1,400 primary healthcare centres, PHCs, across the country to provide primary eye care services as part of efforts to expand access to quality eye care and reduce avoidable blindness.
The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at an event to commemorate the 2026 World Sight Day.
The event, themed, “The Value of Vision: Investing in People, Productivity and Nigeria’s Future,” highlighted the need for sustained investment in eye health and stronger integration of eye care into the primary healthcare system.
Represented by the Director of E-Health Division, Mrs Doris Afam-Aneke, Salako said the integration of eye care into the primary healthcare system was central to the government’s strategy of making eye health services accessible, affordable and sustainable, particularly for Nigerians in underserved communities.
He said the government had also trained more than 3,000 healthcare workers across 16 states, equipping them with skills to provide essential eye care services at the community level.
According to him, the trained workers were helping to improve early detection of eye conditions, raise community awareness and facilitate prompt referral of patients requiring specialised treatment.
Salako said, “A major pillar of our eye health strategy has been the integration and expansion of primary eye care services across the country.
“The evidence is clear. Sustainable progress in eye health can only be achieved when services are available at the point closest to the people. This is why government has prioritised the strengthening of primary healthcare systems as the foundation for delivering essential eye care interventions.”
He added that the integration of primary eye care into the PHC system had expanded the capacity of frontline health facilities to prevent, detect and manage common eye conditions, while ensuring timely referral of patients requiring specialised care.
Salako also disclosed that more than 1.5 million pairs of prescription spectacles had been distributed to Nigerians across 16 states through the Effective Spectacle Coverage Initiative, known as Jigi-Bola 2.0.
He said preparations were at an advanced stage to extend the initiative to 10 additional states, adding that the expansion would further improve access to affordable vision correction for Nigerians with uncorrected refractive errors.
The minister further disclosed that more than 1.5 million school-age children had been screened for visual problems through the school eye health programme, with those requiring treatment linked to appropriate care.
He said four additional vision centres were being established in Enugu, Edo, Sokoto and Nasarawa states to strengthen secondary eye care services, improve referral pathways and expand access to specialised treatment.
Salako reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to eliminating avoidable blindness, announcing plans to conduct 25,000 free cataract surgeries across the country by the end of 2027.
He said improved vision would enhance learning, productivity and the quality of life of Nigerians.
The minister also said Nigeria would co-host the first Global Summit on Eye Health scheduled for November 2 in Antigua and Barbuda, describing it as an opportunity for the country to contribute to global efforts to integrate eye health into universal health coverage.
He said the National Eye Care Commitment was anchored on integrating primary eye care into PHCs, expanding the provision of ready-made spectacles through Jigi-Bola 2.0, improving effective cataract surgical coverage, strengthening the eye health workforce and removing barriers to eye care.
Over 80% of visual impairment avoidable
The National Coordinator, National Eye, Ear and Sensory Functions Health Programme, Dr Oteri Okolo Eme, said more than 80 per cent of visual impairment in Nigeria was avoidable, making the integration of primary eye care into the primary healthcare system a strategic priority.
Eme said the government had established a network of national master trainers across the six geopolitical zones and trained about 4,000 primary healthcare workers, while more than 2,200 others had received specific training in primary eye care.
She added that state-level trainers and facilitators had also been trained to support the expansion of primary eye care services.
The coordinator said the government was developing protocols for newborn eye screening to facilitate early detection and treatment of conditions that could lead to visual impairment.
“We are protecting our children and future generations. We are in the process of developing protocols for newborn screening because we believe that if we detect causes of visual impairment early, we will be able to address them and ensure better outcomes,” she said.
“We are also tackling national priority eye conditions by developing standardised guidelines.
“Nigeria will co-host the upcoming first-ever Global Summit on Eye Health in Antigua and Barbuda on November 2. This provides an opportunity to examine the current state of eye health and make the case for accelerated action.”
Eme called on governments, development partners, the private sector, health workers, teachers, the media and Nigerians to support efforts to improve eye health.
She urged governments to provide dedicated budgetary allocations for eye health and encouraged Nigerians to undergo regular eye examinations and take steps to protect their sight.
Also speaking, the Executive Secretary of the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities, Chief Ayuba Gufwan, said investment in eye health was an investment in people.
He added that supporting persons with visual impairment and ensuring accessible eye care services could significantly enhance participation in education, employment and community life.
The Chief Medical Director, National Eye Centre, Kaduna, Dr Amina Hassan Wali, called for stronger partnerships, greater public awareness, early presentation for eye problems, regular eye examinations and sustained investment in eye health.
“Let us work together to ensure that no one is left behind and that everyone can enjoy the gift of sight. Let us all love our eyes and make eye health a priority,” she said.
The high point of the event was the unveiling of the National Eye Health Commitments in alignment with the upcoming Global Summit on Eye Health.
The post World Sight Day: FG activates 1,400 PHCs for eye care appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
Pensioners in Ogun State have appealed to Governor Dapo Abiodun to release outstanding gratuities owed retirees from January 2021 to June 2025 and approve consequential pension increases for long-serving retirees.
The Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP), Ogun State Council, Comrade Waheed Oloyede, made the appeal at the 2026 Pensioners’ Day celebration held in Abeokuta, the state capital.
Oloyede, while commending the Abiodun administration for what he described as its unprecedented compassion towards pensioners, urged the governor to take further steps to address the financial challenges confronting retirees in the state.
He said pensioners appreciated the achievements of the administration but appealed for additional interventions to give hope to members still awaiting their retirement benefits.
He said, “As Oliver Twist, we want to ask for more. We humbly request that you benevolently approve that the remaining gratuity from January 2021 to June 2025 be released to would-be beneficiaries, to give our long-expectant members a ray of hope.”
The NUP chairman also called for the implementation of consequential adjustments in pensions arising from the 2019 Federal Government circular and subsequent increases in the national minimum wage.
According to him, many retirees who left service 10, 25 and even 30 years ago still receive as little as N30,000 monthly pension despite the sharp rise in the cost of living.
Oloyede said the situation had made life increasingly difficult for elderly citizens, particularly as the prices of drugs, food and other essential commodities continued to rise.
“The cost of drugs, food and other necessities has skyrocketed beyond the reach of the ordinary citizen, resulting in serious health challenges and, eventually, untimely deaths,” he said.
He urged the state government to approve the pension adjustments, saying the move would provide relief to retirees, promote parity and improve the welfare of senior citizens in the state.
Oloyede added that implementing the adjustment would also leave a lasting legacy for the governor, saying it would “imprint the governor’s name in gold in the history of the state.”
Pensioners commend Abiodun
The pensioners’ leader, however, commended Abiodun for what he described as significant improvements in the welfare of retirees, particularly the prompt and regular payment of monthly pensions.
According to him, unlike in many states where pensioners still face delays, Ogun retirees now receive their monthly pensions as and when due.
“You have restored our dignity and given us peace of mind. You have wiped away tears from the faces of our aged members,” Oloyede said.
He also commended the administration for clearing the backlog of gratuities owed by previous administrations up to December 2020 for state retirees and December 2021 for local government retirees, describing the payments as running into multiple billions of naira.
“For many years, many of our members died without receiving their gratuity. Your administration has changed that ugly narrative,” he added.
Oloyede further appreciated the state government for introducing a free health insurance scheme for state and local government pensioners.
He, however, raised concerns over complaints about the implementation of the scheme at some health facilities, urging the agency supervising the programme to investigate the complaints and address identified challenges.
NLC seeks resolution of grievances
In his goodwill message, the Ogun State Chairman of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Comrade Hameed Ademola-Benco, commended the governor for his interventions in the welfare of pensioners.
He urged the state government to consider all outstanding grievances raised by retirees, stressing that pensioners should not be made to struggle before accessing benefits due to them.
“We appreciate the governor for all he has done. We appeal to him to kindly look into every grievance that has been tabled because retirees should not have to struggle for their benefits,” Ademola-Benco said.
Abiodun responds
Responding, Governor Abiodun, who was represented by the Head of Service, Mr Olaranwaju Saka, said the demands made by the pensioners were legitimate.
He assured the retirees that the administration was already looking into their requests and would continue to honour its obligations to pensioners.
According to him, the government would deploy available resources towards addressing outstanding retirement benefits and ensuring the welfare of retirees.
The post Ogun pensioners demand gratuities, pension increases appeared first on Vanguard News.

…..As Vanguard summit holds today
By Sola Ogundipe
Nigeria’s response to the mental health challenges facing its young people comes under fresh scrutiny today as policymakers, psychiatrists, health professionals, security and correctional authorities, regulators, media and other stakeholders converge in Lagos for the 4th Vanguard Mental Health Summit holding at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos.
The summit, organised by Vanguard Media Limited, comes against growing concerns over depression, suicide, substance abuse, anxiety, trauma, social isolation and the mounting psychological pressures confronting young Nigerians online and offline.
With the theme, “Advancing Youth Mental Health in Nigeria through Access, Action and Advocacy,” and sub-theme, “Mental Health in a Digital Age: Navigating Social Media, Technology and Wellbeing,” the gathering is expected to move the conversation beyond awareness and confront the more difficult issues of access to care, early intervention, treatment, rehabilitation and accountability.
At the centre of the discussion is the question of what happens when a young Nigerian needs mental healthcare but cannot find, afford or access it. Beyond the expert presentations, the summit is expected to confront the gap between Nigeria’s mental health policies and the experience of young people who actually need care.
Chief Host of the summit is Lagos State Commissioner for Health, Prof. Akin Abayomi, while the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, and Chairman of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (rtd.) are Special G inuests of Honour.
The forum will be chaired by Corps Marshal Shehu Mohammed of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC). The Director-General of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, and the Controller of Corrections, Lagos State Command, Nigerian Correctional Service, Mr Daramola George are special guests.
Other stakeholders that will feature are President of the Association of Psychiatrists of Nigeria, Dr. Veronica Oluyemisi Nyamali; Professor Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, Professor of Psychiatry and Psychopharmacology at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria; Prof. Mashudat Bello-Mojeed, Professor of Psychiatry and Public Health, as well as senior officials of the Lagos State Ministry of Health, mental health practitioners, academics, development partners, civil society organisations, youth representatives and educators.
Nyamali will deliver the keynote address, while Sheikh will speak on “Mental Health as Our Social Capital.” The President of the Nigerian Medical Association will speak on “Making Youth Mental Health Everyone’s Business: From Policy to Practice,” bringing the perspective of the nation’s umbrella body for medical practitioners to discussions on how mental health policies can translate into practical support and services for young Nigerians.
A major panel session, “Who Takes Responsibility for Young People’s Mental Health?”, will examine the roles of government, families, schools, healthcare providers, communities, civil society and technology platforms in preventing young people from reaching crisis points.
The summit will also examine substance abuse and its intersection with the justice system and other attendant effects. Technology’s growing role in mental healthcare will also come under scrutiny, including the use of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in treating common mental health conditions among young people who do not respond adequately to conventional treatment.
As the stakeholders gather, health commentators note that the question is no longer whether Nigeria has a youth mental health problem, rather, the question is whether its institutions are ready to take responsibility for tackling it. Their participation underscores how deeply mental health now cuts across substance abuse, public safety, the justice system, correctional services and drug regulation.
The post Mental health: Nigeria’s action gap comes under scrutiny appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Ugochukwu Alaribe
UMUAHIA — The Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) has warned newly inducted medical doctors against professional misconduct in the discharge of their duties.
The Registrar of the council, Prof. Fatima Kyari, gave the warning in Aba while inducting 16 medical doctors who graduated from Rhema University.
Kyari, who was represented by Tijani Ali Mandaka, said medicine was one of the most regulated professions and that practitioners were subject to oversight by the council, the public and relevant government agencies.
She said allegations of professional misconduct against doctors were subject to investigation in accordance with the council’s procedures.
“Medicine and Surgery is one of the most regulated professions. The profession is under close watch by council and the public in the area of education, registration and practice. So, any allegation of misconduct against a doctor will be thoroughly investigated,” she said.
Kyari explained that the council had two disciplinary organs — the Medical and Dental Practitioners Investigation Panel and the Medical and Dental Practitioners Disciplinary Tribunal.
She said the Investigation Panel was responsible for preliminary investigations into allegations of professional misconduct, while cases established against practitioners could be referred to the Disciplinary Tribunal for further action in accordance with the law.
She added that sanctions available under the council’s disciplinary process could include admonition, suspension and removal from the council’s register, depending on the circumstances of each case and the applicable regulations.
The registrar urged the newly inducted doctors to take their housemanship programmes seriously as part of the requirements for registration and certification by the council.
She also advised them to uphold professional standards throughout their careers.
Describing the induction as a historic milestone, the Vice-Chancellor of Rhema University, Prof. Ogbonnaya Onwudike, reminded the new doctors that their medical degrees represented a responsibility to serve humanity.
Onwudike urged them to maintain good character, which he described as an important professional asset.
“As you take the physician’s oath, remember that a medical degree is not merely a certificate; it is a call to serve humanity. You are called to a life of great responsibility as human beings will trust their lives to your knowledge, judgment and compassion,” he said.
The Vice-Chancellor commended the MDCN for its role in maintaining standards in medical education and expressed appreciation for its support during the training and induction process.
He said the university remained committed to providing medical education in line with applicable national and international standards.
The Provost of the university’s College of Medicine, Prof. Maduka James Awa, urged the new doctors to be worthy ambassadors of the institution and apply their knowledge responsibly in their professional careers.
He also commended the Chancellor and Founder of the university, Bro Emma Okorie, for his vision for the institution.
Okorie, in his remarks, said the 16 newly inducted doctors had undergone the required training and urged them to contribute positively to the medical profession.
The event featured the presentation of awards to outstanding graduates, including the best graduating student, Dr Ugwokaegbe Anointing.

items.content:
By Adeola Badru
IBADAN — The Senator Sharafadeen Alli Campaign Organisation (SSACO) has alleged attacks on All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates, supporters and political activities in Ibadan, Oyo State.
The organisation alleged that Alhaja Tawakalitu Alli, wife of the APC governorship candidate, Sharafadeen Alli, was attacked during a medical outreach she organised at Ibikunle House, Ayeye, Ibadan.
It also alleged that the campaign teams of the APC candidate for Oyo South Senatorial District, Aderemi Oseni, and the party’s candidate for Ibadan North-West/Ibadan South-West Federal Constituency, Folake Olunloyo-Oshinowo, were attacked during separate campaign events at Agbaje Market, Orita-Merin, and Idi-Arere, Ibadan.
In a statement issued by its Director of Media and Publicity, Bisi Oladele, SSACO described the alleged incidents as attempts to disrupt political activities ahead of the 2027 elections.
The organisation called on Governor Seyi Makinde and the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) governorship candidate, Bimbo Adekanmbi, to ensure that political actors are allowed to campaign freely.
“The SSACO is at the least miffed by the unwarranted and barbaric attacks by Allied People’s Movement (APM) hoodlums on Alhaja Tawakalitu Alli during a medical outreach she organised at Ibikunle House, Ayeye, Ibadan, on Wednesday,” the statement said.
It further alleged that Oseni and Olunloyo-Oshinowo were attacked during separate campaign events in the city.
SSACO said the alleged incidents would not force the APC to suspend its campaign activities, stressing that its candidates and supporters were entitled to associate, assemble and campaign within the law.
“The SSACO calls on Governor Seyi Makinde and the party’s governorship candidate, Hon. Bimbo Adekanmbi, to rein in on their supporters,” it said.
The organisation also called on security agencies to investigate the alleged attacks, identify those responsible and prosecute them where appropriate.
“The SSACO calls on security agencies to fish out these perpetrators of violence and bring them to book in order to serve justice to the victims and also serve as a deterrence to violence in our dear state,” it said.
SSACO further urged the state government to protect residents irrespective of their political affiliations, saying the alleged attacks posed a threat to peaceful political participation.
“As the chief security officer of the state, Governor Makinde carries the responsibility to protect all residents irrespective of their political leanings,” the organisation said.
The campaign organisation alleged that the incidents were connected to tensions ahead of the 2027 elections, but provided no independent evidence in the statement to substantiate its allegation that the governor or Adekanmbi sponsored the attacks.
It also urged political parties to focus on issue-based campaigns and policy proposals rather than violence.
“The good people of Oyo State deserve issue-based campaigns, not violence. We advise Governor Makinde, Adekanmbi and other political parties to focus on presenting their programmes and policies to the electorate,” SSACO said.
The organisation maintained that the alleged attacks would not deter APC candidates from campaigning across the state.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Henry Ojelu
The Lagos State AIDS Control Agency, LSACA, has urged employers and workers in the food sector to end stigma and discrimination against people living with HIV, stressing that the virus cannot be transmitted through the preparation, handling or serving of food.
The agency made the call at a sensitisation meeting for food handlers and representatives of food-sector associations on HIV-related workplace practices and applicable legal provisions, held Thursday at the STO Resource Centre Hall, CBD, Ikeja.
The meeting was aimed at dispelling misconceptions about HIV transmission and promoting safe, inclusive and non-discriminatory practices in the food sector.
Speaking at the event, the Chief Executive Officer of LSACA, Dr. Folakemi Animashaun, represented by the Director, Projects, Mr. Michael Essien, said there was no scientific basis for excluding people living with HIV from food-related employment.
Animashaun said HIV was not transmitted through handling, preparing or serving food, sharing utensils or through ordinary workplace and social contact.
According to her, “a person’s HIV status does not make them a food-safety risk,” urging food-sector stakeholders to base workplace decisions on scientific evidence rather than fear and misinformation.
She cautioned against using legitimate food-safety and medical fitness requirements as a basis for discriminatory HIV screening or exclusion from employment.
The LSACA boss also stressed the need to protect the confidentiality of workers’ HIV-related information, saying such information must be handled with appropriate consent, respect and dignity.
She noted that stigma and discrimination could discourage people from testing, accessing treatment and using health services for fear of losing their jobs or having their status disclosed without consent.
Animashaun urged food establishments and associations to review their workplace policies to ensure compliance with the principles of confidentiality, informed consent and non-discrimination.
Also speaking, the facilitator, Mr. Tiamiyu Hussein of the Lagos State Safety Commission, stressed the importance of maintaining safe and healthy workplaces without discriminating against workers.
Hussein explained the distinction between legitimate medical fitness assessments for food handlers and HIV screening, urging employers to ensure that occupational health and safety procedures were appropriately implemented.
He further encouraged employers and workers to protect the confidentiality of health information and ensure that no person was subjected to unfair treatment on account of HIV status.
The sensitisation also covered HIV transmission, prevention and treatment, with participants reminded that there is no risk of acquiring HIV from food prepared, handled or served by a person living with the virus.
Participants were encouraged to challenge misconceptions, promote fair employment practices and support appropriate referral and grievance mechanisms across the food sector.

items.content:
To review pensions of former governors
By Henry Obetta
THE Lagos State Governorship Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Funso Doherty, has unveiled a 34-point manifesto he said would take the state to the next level, if elected. He also unveiled Mrs. Tolani Animashaun as his running mate in the February 6, 2027 governorship poll.
Presenting his manifesto titled: Ònà Tuntun (New Road), yesterday, in Lagos, Doherty said the manifesto contained 34 specific commitments across health, education, housing, transport, environment, jobs and small business and honest governance.
Specifically, Doherty, among others, promised to deliver in four years 150,000 homes, provide free healthcare for pregnant women and children under-16, free education through secondary school and technical colleges. He also promised to provide free textbooks, and nutritious meals for students in public schools.
He added: “Then for those children who are in public schools, Lagos State Public Schools, who need to be transported to their school, public transport for children in school uniforms going to their school will be provided.
“The whole objective is that there should be no child in Lagos State that will not benefit from a quality education because his or her parents cannot afford it or because of the circumstances of his or her birth. Because if we don’t, it is our future that we are mortgaging.”
On transportation, Doherty pledged to modernise the state’s transport system, particularly the Red and Blue Line rail networks, by improving connectivity between them. He also promised to establish decentralised road maintenance frameworks across the local governments to ensure more efficient and timely maintenance of roads.
The NDC governorship candidate pledged to run a transparent administration, promising to lead by example and ensure strict enforcement of the Code of Conduct for Public Officers.
He pledged to review all major public-private partnerships, PPPs in Lagos, saying the review would determine whether corrective actions were necessary. He also promised to review public servants’ salaries and allowances to ensure public officers receive reasonable remuneration, arguing that poor pay could undermine efficiency and integrity in the civil service.
The candidate also promised to subject the benefits and packages of former governors to an independent review and make the outcome public.
He further pledged to enforce compliance with government rules and prosecute criminal activity regardless of the position of those involved. “And this applies from the top all the way to the bottom,” he said, adding that his administration would regularly publish its progress and openly acknowledge areas where it fell short.
Doherty also criticised the current Lagos state government, arguing that it had failed to adequately meet the needs of residents despite the state’s substantial financial resources. He said the government should translate its revenue into improved public services and a better quality of life for Lagosians
In her remarks, the NDC deputy governorship candidate, Mrs Tolani Animashaun, pledged to work with Doherty, to build a Lagos where the government prioritises the needs of residents.
Citing her experience in education, finance and community mobilisation, she said the ticket would promote better opportunities for young people, improve education and ensure accountability in the management of public funds.
“Government that works for the people. That is what this team believes in and that is why I am here,” she said, urging residents to support the campaign and “lend us your hand” to achieve our vision for the state.

Rotimi Amaechi, vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has described President Bola Tinubu’s decision to remove the petrol subsidy as “reckless,” declaring that only a madman would vote for the president in the 2027 general election.
Amaechi made the remarks on Thursday at the ADC town hall meeting in Edo State, where he urged Nigerians to reject Tinubu, accusing his administration’s economic policies of worsening hardship across the country.
“I read on social media that it is in 2027 that we will know how many madmen we have in Nigeria. It is only a madman that can vote for Tinubu,” he said.
“If you are not mad, then Tinubu should not win here.”
The former Minister of Transportation also accused supporters of the president of being motivated by self-interest.
Amaechi faulted the removal of the petrol subsidy, rejecting Tinubu’s description of the policy as an act of courage.
He argued that the president’s decision to proceed with the policy despite having been advised against it amounted to recklessness.
“There is a difference between courage and recklessness. Tinubu wasn’t courageous; he was reckless,” Amaechi said.
The ADC chieftain lamented the rising cost of living, saying many Nigerians could no longer afford basic necessities.
“People are not able to feed. Things are difficult,” he said, attributing the hardship faced by households to the administration’s economic policies.
Amaechi also criticised Nigeria’s energy sector, arguing that the country had failed to harness its abundant natural resources to drive industrial production and economic growth.
He noted that Nigeria had substantial crude oil and natural gas reserves, particularly in the South-South region, but had failed to translate its resource wealth into sustainable prosperity for its citizens.
The former minister called for policies that would stimulate domestic production rather than increase the financial burden on consumers and businesses.
He said Atiku Abubakar, the ADC presidential candidate, would introduce production subsidies to strengthen local industries, boost domestic production and ease economic pressure on Nigerians if elected president in 2027.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
President Donald Trump on Thursday ruled out attacking Iran before the US midterm elections on November 3, saying Washington was holding “productive discussions” with Tehran.
Trump’s post on his Truth Social platform followed a surge in oil prices on Thursday driven by media reports suggesting potential new US strikes prior to those elections.
“I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect…we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections,” he wrote.
“We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran,” he added, without providing additional details.
The Atlantic magazine reported on Wednesday that the White House had asked the Pentagon to develop options to strike Iranian targets that could be used before the midterms. The New York Times published a similar report on Thursday, saying the plans were being developed despite Trump’s “ambivalence”.
The rise in crude oil prices has also been fueled by persistent tensions in the Strait of Hormuz — a strategic chokepoint for the global oil trade — as well as hostilities between Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia.
In a recent sign of those tensions, an oil tanker sailing off the north coast of Qatar reported being struck “by multiple projectiles,” causing an unspecified number of casualties, the UKMTO maritime agency said Wednesday.
Polls suggest that US voters are strongly dissatisfied over rising fuel prices, linked to the conflict launched by the United States and Israel against Iran in February.
The US leader has repeatedly insisted in recent weeks that the United States has effectively won the Iran war, despite ongoing unrest and a recent security threat that forced the withdrawal of American bombers from a base in England.
But Trump’s claims that prices will fall as soon as the Iran war is over have so far fallen on deaf ears with voters.
The midterm elections will shape the final two years of Trump’s presidential term as his Republican Party risks losing its current grip on Congress.
Although Trump is not on the ballot, he is heavily involved in the campaign, holding numerous rallies in an attempt to limit the damage or even turn the political tide.
Trump has warned he faces a possible third impeachment if Democrats retake the House of Representatives, and the White House is preparing for a slew of investigations into corruption and abuse of power.
The US president also on Thursday sought to calm a furor over his comments at a rally earlier this week that Iran could “take out” the cities of Los Angeles and San Diego.
Trump, 80, blamed the “fake and artificial news” for misinterpreting the remarks, which Democrats pounced on.
“In actuality, what I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a small price to pay for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon and, if you want to see a big price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles?” Trump said on Truth Social.

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri
Former Governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai, has failed to persuade the Federal High Court in Abuja to stop the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and other anti-graft agencies in the country from freezing his bank accounts.
In a ruling by Justice Joyce Abdulmalik, the court dismissed a suit filed by the former governor, who has been in detention, seeking an order restraining federal government agencies from moving against his assets.
The court held that the suit not only lacked merit but was speculative, as no reasonable cause of action was disclosed against the agencies the applicant listed as defendants.
Therefore, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF) were struck out from the case.
In the suit he filed on February 24, El-Rufai prayed the court for an interim injunction directing the respondents to maintain the status quo ante regarding his assets.
According to him, the order was necessary to prevent him from being placed in a state of helplessness. He insisted that the severance pay he received upon completing his tenure as governor of Kaduna State between 2015 and 2023 could not reasonably be suspected to be proceeds of any unlawful activity.
He urged the court to declare that properties purchased from his severance pay were lawfully acquired.
The banks the applicant prayed the court to protect from the respondents included Zenith Bank Plc, Naira Account Number: 1007158671; Zenith Bank Plc, Domiciliary Account Number: 507 1511327; Guaranty Trust Bank (GTB) Plc, Account Number: 0023824978; Access Bank, Dollar Account Number: 1396386493; and Access Bank, Naira Account Number: 1396382103.
El-Rufai also sought a declaration that any attempt by the respondents to apply for, obtain or execute any interim or final forfeiture or freezing order, without first establishing a reasonable suspicion supported by credible evidence as required by relevant law, would amount to a breach of his rights.
He relied on Section 17(1) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Related Offences Act, 2006, and the Supreme Court decision in Melrose General Services Ltd v. EFCC (2024) SC/1519/2019, to pray the court to declare that, as a citizen of Nigeria, he is entitled to the presumption of innocence and the protection of his fundamental rights.
He argued that any action by the respondents seeking to circumvent his constitutionally guaranteed rights through ex parte applications that conceal material facts would amount to a breach of Section 36(5) of the Constitution and a violation of the principles of fair hearing.
The post El-Rufai fails to get order stopping ICPC, EFCC from freezing accounts appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Six-time French champions Bordeaux, who were sanctioned in the summer for financial irregularities, will play the current season in the sixth tier of French football, the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league confirmed on Thursday.
Bordeaux were sanctioned for failing to provide the roughly 10 million euros ($11.6 million) needed for the 2025-2026 financial year as well as 2026-2027 and meet debt payments.
Once one of France’s leading football clubs and the team where the country’s new head coach Zinedine Zidane made his name, Bordeaux was sold last month for a symbolic one euro to US-based investment group Park Bench who agreed to take on the remaining debt.
Two days after appearing before the oversight commission of the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league, which approved their recovery budget and issued “a positive opinion on their possible participation in Regional 1,” the club was unanimously approved to play in the top tier.
“Rebuilding can now begin,” said Dominique Delport, the new president chosen by Park Bench, speaking to AFP.
The new owners are due in commercial court on October 20 to ratify the new continuation plan, which now runs over 12 years, with the debt halved from 26 to 13 million euros.
The team is largely amateur although they are permitted five players on professional contracts, one of which will go to former Ligue 1 striker Baptiste Guillaume.
The club has produced many big names of French football including academy products Bixente Lizarazu and Christophe Dugarry who both played alongside Zidane in the 1998 World Cup-winning team.
A decade earlier Alain Giresse and Jean Tigana were part of a celebrated France midfield that won the European championships in 1984.
However, they were relegated to Ligue 2 in 2022 and then placed in judicial restructuring in 2024, which caused them to relinquish their professional status and their highly-rated academy.
AFP

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has denied allegations of partisanship over the 22nd All Nigeria Editors Conference (ANEC) in Enugu and urged Nation Newspaper to apologise over its editorial on the conference.
The Guild was reacting to an editorial published by the newspaper on October 8, 2026, titled “Journalists Failed Journalism,” which questioned the NGE’s conduct over the participation of Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Prof. Pat Utomi, a chieftain of the party, at the conference.
In a statement signed by the NGE President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh, the Guild said the editorial made serious allegations against its leadership, including the suggestion that the NGE acted in a partisan manner by allowing Obi and Utomi to address editors at the conference.
The Guild said the conclusion was not supported by the facts, stressing that ANEC 2026 was a professional gathering of editors and other stakeholders devoted to interrogating critical issues concerning democracy, elections, the media, artificial intelligence, disinformation and the future of Nigeria.
According to the NGE, the conference programme specifically provided for an “Executive Session” on the second day, designed to feature governors, political party chairmen, heads of government agencies and parastatals and other stakeholders.
It said the purpose of the session was to provide a platform for engagement between the media and key actors in Nigeria’s political and public space.
The Guild said it officially invited political parties, including the All Progressives Congress (APC), African Democratic Congress (ADC) and NDC, to participate in the relevant engagement.
It listed the APC chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yelwatda; ADC chairman, Senator David Mark; and NDC chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, among those invited.
The NGE said the invitations were followed by reminders, adding that Anaba personally spoke with Yelwatda and ADC Vice-Presidential candidate, Chibuike Amaechi, in connection with participation at the conference.
It added that Ukeh personally followed up with Paul Ibe, media aide to the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to encourage the participation of the party and its leaders.
“These are verifiable facts. They fundamentally undermine the central premise of The Nation’s editorial,” the Guild said.
The NGE questioned whether the absence of some invited political figures should have prevented a candidate who was available and willing to attend from participating.
“If the Guild duly invited the political parties, sent reminders and personally followed up with their leaders and representatives, and some of those invited chose not to attend, should it prevent a candidate who was available and willing to attend from participating?” it asked.
The Guild acknowledged the right of Nation Newspaper and other media organisations to scrutinise its activities and express editorial opinions about the conduct of the conference.
It said such scrutiny was an important part of the accountability expected of professional institutions, including the media.
However, the NGE said the editorial ignored the broader range of political and governmental voices that featured at the conference.
The Guild noted that Tunde Rahman, media adviser to President Bola Tinubu, spoke on the administration, while the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, was represented at the conference by the Managing Director of the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN).
It also pointed out that Vice President Kashim Shettima addressed editors virtually from the United States.
“These engagements demonstrate the very opposite of the partisan picture painted by the editorial,” the Guild said.
The NGE also rejected the description of Obi’s appearance as an “ambush”, arguing that he attended a professional conference at which hundreds of editors and stakeholders were present.
“There is a fundamental distinction between providing a platform for engagement and supporting a political position,” it said.
The Guild described as “particularly unfortunate” the newspaper’s reference to its conduct as an “impunity of silence.”
It argued that the conference was a public professional gathering attended by hundreds of editors, journalists and stakeholders.
The NGE said the fact that Nation Newspaper or another newspaper chose not to report an occurrence did not make it secret or establish professional misconduct.
The Guild reaffirmed its commitment to providing platforms for robust and independent engagement with political actors, public officials, civil society organisations, electoral institutions and other stakeholders, without fear or favour.
“That is not partisanship. That is journalism,” the Guild said.
The NGE called on Nation Newspaper’s Editorial Board to acknowledge what it described as omissions in its editorial, correct the “misleading impressions” and offer an apology to the Guild and its leadership.
The post Enugu Conference: NGE denies partisanship, urges Nation Newspaper to apologise appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Mumini AbdulKareem, Ilorin
items.content:
Nigerians have questioned President Bola Tinubu’s motives following the Federal Government’s announcement of a 30-day petrol discount at Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) filling stations.
Some described the move as an attempt to win public support ahead of the 2027 general election.
The reactions followed Thursday’s announcement by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, that the government would offer discounted petrol for an initial 30 days, prioritising public transport operators.
The measure comes more than three years after Tinubu announced the removal of petrol subsidy.
It has triggered fresh questions about why the government is introducing temporary relief now, following prolonged complaints over rising fuel prices, transportation costs and the cost of living.
Some Nigerians who reacted to the announcement on social media questioned whether the intervention was designed primarily to ease economic hardship or improve the electoral prospects of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).
Political commentator, Ugo Egbujo, said that the latest move was part of an attempt by the president to improve his chances in the 2027 election.
“Tinubu will do anything to win this election. He can temporarily return fuel subsidies and unfriend Chagoury and seize Wike’s Rolls-Royce. After winning, he will return his old habits,” Egbujo wrote.
Other Nigerians also questioned the timing and duration of the intervention.
Haroun El-Yahya Hassan asked why the government had waited so long before introducing the measure.
“Where were they 40 months ago? He must go forever, God’s willing,” he wrote.
Similarly, Almajir Abdullahi invoked a Hausa expression to suggest that the intervention had come too late.
“In Hausa we say, ‘Masa ta bayan biki,’ which literally means, no benefit to make a guest’s food after the ceremony,” he said.
The comments reflects a broader concern among critics that the administration, having defended the removal of petrol subsidy as a necessary economic reform, was now introducing a temporary concession as the next general election approaches.
Under the new arrangement, Oyedele said the government would offer a discount on petrol sold at NNPCL stations for 30 days, with priority given to public transport operators.
“We are offering a discount on petrol dispensed by NNPC Limited for the next 30 days in the first instance, with priority for public transporters nationwide. So, it’s not a subsidy; the government is just saying we sell to you at cost,” he said.
The minister also disclosed that the government was negotiating a ceiling of N1,350 per litre on petrol’s ex-gantry or landing cost, subject to monthly reviews, to moderate the impact of fluctuations in global crude oil prices and exchange rates on pump prices.
However, the announcement has not convinced some Nigerians that the intervention will provide lasting relief.
Abdulrahman Abba Saleh said he preferred a government that demonstrated commitment to a permanent solution rather than a temporary intervention.
“We prefer the person who has demonstrated readiness for a permanent solution (subsidy reversal) than one-month solution,” he wrote.
Ovie Ezimeruwe also questioned the sustainability of the arrangement.
He asked: “What will they do for that one month? Why can’t they do it after then? After one month, what next?”
For his part, Isiya Al’majir Keta questioned the change in the government’s position on fuel prices.
According to him, “They said petrol can never reduce the price, what has changed the story?”
Daily Trust reports that the latest development comes against the backdrop of Tinubu’s May 29, 2023, inauguration, when he declared that “fuel subsidy is gone”.
The decision led to sharp increases in petrol prices and transportation fares.
The administration has consistently defended the policy as necessary to reduce the financial burden of subsidising petrol and redirect public resources towards development.
However, the immediate consequences have remained a major source of public dissatisfaction, with higher transport and production costs feeding into the prices of food and other essential goods.
The fresh intervention has reopened the debate over whether the government is responding to the economic realities confronting Nigerians or seeking to address mounting public discontent ahead of the 2027 polls.
Usman Auwal Hassan suggested that the announcement would not have been made without the approaching election.
“If not because of the election, they shouldn’t say that,” he wrote.
Michael Otues argued that even a substantial reduction in petrol prices would not necessarily change his political preference.
“If you guys like, make the price of fuel N100, it is not going to change our mind to vote for APC. Nigerians are wise now,” he said.
Abdullazeez Abdullahi also called for the government to focus on winning public acceptance rather than resorting to electoral manipulation.
“All options considered… No way to rigging; let’s do what is acceptable by the masses. It’s too late,” he wrote.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Adeola Badru
The abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members travelling to their orientation camps has triggered fresh calls for the Federal Government to overhaul the transportation and security arrangements for young graduates deployed across the country for national service.
The call came as the 20 prospective corps members, who were abducted in Imo State, returned safely to Ibadan on Thursday after seven days in captivity and were taken to the Department of State Services (DSS) headquarters in the Aleshinloye area of the city for debriefing.
The mother of one of the rescued corps members, Faith Felicia Abiala, said the incident had exposed the dangers faced by young graduates travelling long distances by road to fulfil their national service obligations.
Abiala, who described her daughter’s safe return as a moment of overwhelming relief, urged the government to provide stronger security arrangements for corps members travelling to their states of deployment or consider transporting them by air.
“My advice to the government is that when Corps members are posted to their service states, they should ensure proper security arrangements, or allow them to travel by air to avoid these kinds of dangerous road journeys,” she said.
The mother recalled the emotional trauma that followed the abduction of her daughter, saying she was so devastated when she received the news that she could not eat.
“I cannot recount all the tears and sorrow, but I give thanks to God that I am seeing her alive today. On the day she was taken, I was so devastated I couldn’t even eat, but today my heart is filled with joy,” Abiala said.
She also commended the DSS and the security teams from Oyo and Imo states for their efforts in securing the victims’ return.
“I thank God, and I thank the DSS officials—they really tried! The team from Oyo State and the team from Imo State, they really tried and stood by us until our children came out safe and sound,” she said.
Another relative of one of the victims, Alhaja Alimot Akande described their release as a major relief after days of uncertainty.
“It is good news! Good news! Good news!” she said.
She said the confirmation of the victims’ release finally enabled their families to sleep peacefully after days of anguish.
“Ah! Immediately I heard they were released yesterday, I slept soundly!” Akande said.
The abductors had reportedly demanded N50 million for each of the 20 victims, amounting to N1 billion, before the demand was allegedly reduced to N5 million per victim, bringing the total to N100 million.
The parents had earlier visited the private residence of the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, in Ibadan, seeking his intervention in securing the release of their children.
The Oyo State Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Abimbola, and the Aseyin of Iseyinland, Oba Sefiu Adeyeri, were also involved in efforts to secure the victims’ release.
The Olubadan subsequently announced the freedom of the prospective corps members after receiving confirmation from Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma.
“The kidnapped graduates have been released. The Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma, confirmed this in a telephone conversation at about 5.00pm,” Ladoja stated in a statement issued by his media aide, Adeola Oloko.
The 20 victims were among 30 prospective corps members travelling in two buses from Oyo State towards orientation camps in Abia State when gunmen attacked them along the Owerri-Onitsha Road in Umunoha, Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State.
Ten of the prospective corps members escaped into the bush during the attack and subsequently made their way to safety, while the remaining 20 were abducted.
The victims spent seven days in captivity before regaining their freedom and being brought back to Ibadan, where they were received at the DSS facility.
The incident had generated widespread anxiety among their parents and relatives, with the families seeking intervention from government officials, security agencies and traditional rulers.
The post NYSC abduction: Mother demands airlift, security escorts for corps members nationwide appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has expressed deep sorrow over the passing of Professor Idowu Akanbi Sobowale, an eminent Mass Communications scholar and former Commissioner for Education in Lagos State, who died at 85.
President Tinubu described the death of the renowned academic and journalist as a great loss to Nigeria, particularly the academic community, the media profession, and generations of students whose lives and careers he shaped through his scholarship and mentorship.
The President also condoled with the Association of Communication Scholars and Professionals of Nigeria on the passing of its Board of Trustees Chairman.
He acknowledged Professor Sobowale’s immense contributions to mass communication education and his enduring impact on journalism and media studies in Nigeria.
“Professor Sobowale was committed to intellectual excellence, professional ethics, and the training of young Nigerians. His life’s work helped strengthen the foundations of media education and professional journalism in the country.
“As a journalism educator, he emphasised empirical evidence over opinion. It was therefore no surprise that he led the first nationwide opinion poll to predict the outcome of the 1979 elections.
“He served my administration in Lagos State as special adviser and later education commissioner, performing creditably well in both roles.
“I commiserate with the family, colleagues, former students, and the entire academic and media communities.
“I urge them to find comfort in his remarkable legacy of service, scholarship and mentorship.
“May his soul rest in perfect peace,” Tinubu remarked.
The post Tinubu mourns communications scholar Idowu Sobowale appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
With an eye on entering the homegrown electric two-wheeler (E2W) market, Vietnamese EV maker VinFast has signed letters of intent (LoIs) with more than 50 dealers across India.
The EV maker said that the agreements will pave the way for establishing 50+ electric motorcycle showrooms across 34 cities in 15 states and union territories (UTs). These showrooms will be set up across Delhi NCR, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, among others.
In a statement, the EV giant said that the agreements will expand its distribution network and strengthen its position in the Indian E2W market. The LoIs were signed at VinFast’s manufacturing facility in Vietnam’s Hai Phong.
Citing its rationale for signing the agreements, VinFast said that the aforementioned cities have large two-wheeler markets, which offers a significant headroom for electrification. The company said that it plans to leverage these dealer locations to bring electric mobility solutions “closer to local consumers”.
As part of its local push, the company also plans to build charging infrastructure and strengthen after-sales services in the new cities.
“Partnering with more than 50 dealer partners across 15 states and territories and 34 cities marks the beginning of our journey to bring VinFast e-motorcycles across India. Alongside, we are also building charging infrastructure and strengthening after-sales services to ensure that customers across these locations receive the support they need throughout their ownership journey,” said Anurag Saxena, the India CEO of VinFast’s escooter division.
With this, VinFast is entering the burgeoning Indian E2W space, which is being driven by government incentives, new launches by domestic manufacturers, rising fuel prices, EV mandates, a growing charging infrastructure and rapid adoption by gig platforms.
The E2W segment is currently dominated by legacy players such as TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp. But the space has also spawned the rise of listed homegrown new-age mobility players such as Ather and Ola Electric.
However, unlike incumbents that focus on escooters, VinFast claims to be eyeing the Indian electric motorcycle market. Even here, the company will lock horns with homegrown players such as Oben Electric, MATTER and Ultraviolette.
This comes nearly a year after VinFast first said that it would enter the Indian E2W market in 2026. At the time, the company had said that it would invest $2 Bn in India to scale its annual production capacity from 50,000 units to 1.5 Lakh.
However, much has happened since then. Earlier this year, reports surfaced that the company was halting the production of select cars in India to reassess costs. Last month, it was also reported that the Vietnamese EV maker was in initial discussions with local suppliers to develop two new models for the Indian market.
That said, EVs continue to increase their share of India’s two-wheeler market. E2W registrations surged 12.2% month-on-month (MoM) to 2.07 Lakh units in September from 1.84 Lakh units in August.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
The Benue State Education Quality Assurance and Examinations Board, BEQAEB, has sealed Orenda and Opal Schools in Makurdi over alleged victimisation of learners and violation of the state government’s policy on textbook reuse and purchase.
The Executive Secretary of BEQAEB, Dr. Terna Francis, who led officials of the Board’s Directorate of Enforcement and Compliance to the schools, said the action followed several complaints by parents alleging that their children were being victimised for failing to purchase exercise and test books directly from the schools.
A court order authorising the sealing of the schools was served on the proprietor before officials of the Board locked the premises.
Francis said the enforcement action became necessary after repeated attempts by the Board to engage the schools and resolve the complaints failed.
According to him, “We went out with the enforcement team of the Benue State Education Quality Assurance and Examinations Board to seal Orenda and Opal schools here in Makurdi. This closure is as a result of the many complaints we received from parents regarding the victimisation of their learners in these schools.”
He said, “The schools have insisted that learners and their parents must buy exercise books and test books from their school, otherwise they will not be attended to, even after paying school fees. It is quite unfortunate because the Benue State Government, through the Ministry of Education and Knowledge Management, as well as the Benue State Education Quality Assurance and Examinations Board, have continually reminded school owners, proprietors and administrators that there is a textbook reuse policy in Benue State.”
Francis explained that the Board initially contacted the proprietor by telephone and directed her to stop the alleged practice, but the complaints persisted. “We approached this particular school, first through a phone conversation, and we spoke with the proprietor and asked her to desist from that victimisation. They went on and continued in the same manner,” he said.
He added that the Board subsequently wrote officially to the school and invited the proprietor, school management and PTA chairman for a meeting aimed at resolving the matter. “They came without the proprietor, and we asked why the proprietor did not attend our meeting. We rescheduled and asked the school administrator and the principal to pick a convenient date, which they did. On that day, they failed to come, and there was no reason given,” he said.
According to the Executive Secretary, complaints from parents subsequently indicated that the alleged victimisation had extended beyond the purchase of books. “We continued to hear from the parents of these learners that the victimisation done to the learners went to the extent that when they submit their homework, the teachers were directed not to mark, and they were not being marked,” he alleged.
He further said, “Their books were not allowed into the classroom, even after paying school fees. And so, the children started feeling withdrawn and demoralised, and of course, this is against the child protection laws of Benue State and the Federation.”
Francis stressed that the state’s textbook policy was designed to give parents flexibility and prevent them from being subjected to unnecessary financial pressure. He said, “If a particular school has textbooks for sale, it should not be made mandatory for parents to buy from the school. Parents are allowed the freedom to bring the textbooks of their older children and transmit them to the younger ones for use.”
He added that schools were also required to give parents the freedom to source prescribed textbooks elsewhere. “If the list of textbooks is available in a school, parents should be given a copy, and they should decide whether to buy it outside of the school in bookstores or to pick from the school. It is a matter of option and not a matter of necessity that parents must buy books from the school,” he stated.
Francis said the Board, in conjunction with the office of the Attorney-General of the State, approached a court of competent jurisdiction after the alleged violations persisted. “The continual victimisation of these parents and the children led us to approach the Court of Competent Jurisdiction, where, together with the Attorney-General of the State, we instituted and presented the facts before the court on this matter, and the court graciously granted us an order to seal the schools,” he said.
Asked how long the schools would remain sealed, the BEQAEB boss said, “The school will remain sealed indefinitely until we come to terms with the owner of the school and the administrators, and they are ready and willing, and until they demonstrate clearly before us through the conditions that we are going to put before them, and we are convinced that they are willing to operate the schools in a responsible manner, with respect for every learner and the parents that have enrolled their children in those schools,” he said.
On compliance by other private schools in the state, Francis said the Board had not received similar petitions against other schools but warned proprietors and administrators against violating government policies. “Our learners are in school at the moment. We have staff of the Board that are out on monitoring exercise, and they are interacting with parents.”
He urged parents facing similar challenges in other schools to report such cases to the Board with supporting evidence. “We call on parents who have such challenges in other schools to launch their complaints. They should bring before us petitions with evidence of victimisation, and we’ll take it from there,” Francis said.
The Executive Secretary described the action against Orenda and Opal Schools as “a deterrent to other proprietors, and we want to warn that if there is a breach in any school at all by any administrator or proprietor, we are going to clamp down on the school aggressively,” he warned.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
The Presidency on Thursday explained that the measure taken by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) to forgo its petrol retail profit margin and sell to Nigerians at cost to cushion the impact of global crude oil price shocks and volatility on vulnerable households has the approval of President Bola Tinubu.
The Presidency, however, explained that the measure should not be interpreted to mean that the government is out to reverse a necessary reform designed to set the country on the path towards sustained prosperity.
It stated that it is to ensure its gains reach more Nigerians, faster and in more tangible ways.
A statement by the Special Adviser to President Tinubu on Information and Strategy, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, noted that the subsidy removal came at a price.
“To be clear, none of these measures restores a blanket subsidy. Doing so would create longer-term harm for a short-term cure. Each measure is designed to reach the people who need help, without putting the wider economy at risk.”
According to the statement, the Presidency acknowledged the challenges the people face over the high cost of fuel.
“Removing the fuel subsidy came at a price. But the alternative has been tried. Nigeria has already lived through that cycle: scarcity, smuggling, a collapsing currency and a fiscal crisis. We cannot afford to live through it again, least of all in response to a temporary disruption, and at the very moment the results of reform are gathering pace.”
“Government is not out to reverse a necessary reform designed to set our country on the path towards sustained prosperity. It is to ensure its gains reach more Nigerians, faster and in more tangible ways. That is our work, and we are committed to doing it.
“The Federal Government is also working on a comprehensive package of fiscal measures to bring inflation down to single digits sustainably in the near term.”
It stressed that the NNPC’s decision to forgo its petrol retail profit margin and sell to Nigerians at cost was aimed to cushion the impact of global crude oil price shocks and volatility on vulnerable households.
“NNPC Retail, which already sells petrol at the lowest price in the market, will offer this new deal within the next 30 days. This means if NNPC’s landing cost is N1300, it will sell fuel to Nigerians, especially commercial vehicles, at the same price,” it stated.
It further stated that the company’s discount gesture, backed by President Tinubu, was among the raft of measures the Finance Minister and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, had earlier announced.
Oyedele had said he hoped other marketers would take a cue from the NNPC, as the sharp rise in crude and petrol prices is not expected to last long.
The presidency said that Oyedele was emphatic that NNPC agreeing to sell at a discount must not be misinterpreted as the restoration of petrol subsidy, which ended on May 29, 2023.
“In addition, Oyedele announced forward sales of crude to domestic refineries. As production rises and previously committed crude is freed up, this is expected to shield pump prices from global market volatility.
“Oyedele also said the Federal Government is negotiating a ceiling of N1,350 a litre on the ex-gantry or landing cost of petrol, to keep pump prices stable. Where costs rise above the ceiling, refiners and importers will carry the shortfall and recover it later, when crude prices or the exchange rate allow, without breaching the ceiling.
“This is neither a subsidy nor a price control: it is designed to smooth prices over time rather than suppressing them. The reasoning is simple. 1,400 naira a litre today and 1,400 tomorrow is better than 1,500 today and 1,300 tomorrow, because volatility itself adds to uncertainty and cost.
“And when fares rise sharply, they rarely fall as fast. The ceiling will be reviewed monthly, reset as costs require, and the figures published for transparency,” the presidency quoted Oyedele as having said.
Continuing, it said, “Oyedele also said that, under the 2025 tax reform laws, the Federal government, in collaboration with the states and security agencies, is reining in the collection of road taxes and levies that inflate fares and logistics costs.
“The Federal government is also increasing funding for cash transfers to the most vulnerable households and subsidised credit for small businesses and consumers.”
Other measures announced, it said, included a faster CNG rollout.
“The federal government is scaling up CNG deployment with the states. The government expects transporters to pass the savings on to passengers in lower fares. CNG is 60-70 per cent cheaper than petrol,” it said.
On excess profit tax, the statement said: “This will be considered for operators who take undue advantage of consumers, anywhere along the energy value chain.
“The government said it will use proceeds from taxes on price gouging exclusively to cushion the impact of fuel prices through transport support or vouchers for urban minimum-wage earners, who are most vulnerable. The Federal Government will also work with the National Assembly to consider enhanced tax relief for low-income earners under the 2027 Finance Bill.
Less red tape
“The Federal Government is cutting regulatory costs that feed into the cost of doing business and, indirectly, into higher prices of goods and services.
National Strategic Fuel Reserve
“To protect households and businesses from future energy shocks, the Federal Government is investing in a National Strategic Fuel Reserve. The government will release refined products into the market under clear, published rules whenever a global disruption or hoarding threatens supply and price stability.
“This is not a subsidy, and it does not fix prices; rather, it secures supply and reduces price volatility. It will prevent artificial scarcity, deter market manipulation, and anchor long-term energy security, so a deregulated market delivers stable growth rather than sudden price shocks.
Better traffic and logistics management
“Traffic management agencies will improve traffic flow, especially in major urban centres, to reduce fuel consumption. Also, NIPOST’s newly launched address codes will help make logistics more efficient and cheaper.”
The post NNPC discount measure for petrol pump price has Tinubu’s backing – Presidency appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief
The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation, NDIC, has paid N1.48 billion to 10,312 insured depositors of 47 recently closed microfinance banks, MFBs, as part of efforts to strengthen confidence in the banking system.
Managing Director of the Corporation, Mr. Thompson Sunday, disclosed this in Abuja on Thursday while speaking at the NDIC’s 2026 Customer Service Week celebration, with the theme, “Go the Extra Mile.”
Sunday said the payments, which were made as of July 31, 2026, covered depositors of recently closed microfinance banks, including Abia SME Microfinance Bank, Frontline Microfinance Bank and Goldman Microfinance Bank.
He said the Corporation leveraged the Bank Verification Number, BVN, system to identify depositors and obtain alternative bank accounts, a development that simplified and accelerated the payment of claims.
The NDIC boss charged the Corporation’s staff to go beyond routine responsibilities in delivering professional and efficient services to depositors and other stakeholders.
He said: “Let us remember that service excellence is not a one-week activity. Customer Service Week may provide the occasion for us to celebrate and reflect, but the commitment to excellent service must continue in our daily work, in every Department, Zone, Unit and Office, at every level, and in every interaction.
“This year’s theme, ‘The Extra Mile’, adequately captures the spirit of excellence and commitment that we seek to demonstrate in all we do. It reminds us that excellent service is not simply about meeting expectations; it is about going beyond what is required to create a positive experience and meaningful value for those we serve.”
According to him, the NDIC’s responsibility goes beyond the payment of insured deposits, stressing that the Corporation remains a critical component of Nigeria’s financial safety net through deposit insurance, banking supervision in collaboration with the Central Bank of Nigeria, failure resolution and orderly liquidation of failed banks.
He said the stability and dependability of the financial system were essential to the wider economy, as individuals and businesses depended on financial institutions to safeguard funds, facilitate transactions, provide access to credit and create confidence for investment and growth.
Sunday, however, noted that the discharge of the Corporation’s mandate was not only about policies, processes and procedures, but also about how depositors and other stakeholders were treated.
“Fulfilling this responsibility is not only about the policies we develop, the processes we establish or the mandates we discharge. It is also about how we serve the people and institutions we interact with daily,” he said.
“It is about the experience we create in every encounter and our willingness to do a little more to ensure that our stakeholders receive the quality of service they deserve.”
He explained that going the extra mile did not necessarily mean doing something extraordinary, but could be demonstrated through everyday actions such as responding promptly to complaints, resolving issues professionally, showing empathy and collaborating across departments to ensure that assignments were completed properly and on time.
The NDIC managing director said the Corporation had itself gone the extra mile through its NDIC ASCENDS restructuring programme**, which he said was designed to strengthen its structures, improve processes, enhance collaboration and leverage technology and data to make the Corporation more efficient and responsive in delivering its mandates.
He added that the NDIC had also recently completed a comprehensive review of its Strategic Plan, resulting in a refreshed mission, strategic themes, objectives and initiatives, as well as a new set of core values captured in the acronym EPIIC — Excellence, Professionalism, Integrity, Innovation and Collaboration.
According to him, the initiatives were designed to continually improve the Corporation’s capacity to serve depositors and other stakeholders.
Sunday stressed that customer service was not the responsibility of a particular department or group of employees, insisting that every staff member was a service provider.
“Whether we interact directly with depositors, stakeholders and the public, or provide support to colleagues within the Corporation who do so, our actions contribute to the experience people have with the Corporation,” he said.
He commended NDIC staff for their dedication and commitment, saying their professionalism and continuous pursuit of improvement remained critical to the success of the Corporation.
The NDIC boss urged employees to use the Customer Service Week to renew their commitment to professionalism, responsiveness, empathy, integrity, accountability and excellence.
He said the celebration should also provide an opportunity for staff to learn, share experiences, explore innovative approaches and challenge themselves to raise the standard of service across the Corporation.
Sunday assured that the NDIC would continue to place depositors at the centre of its operations, noting that confidence in the financial system remained fundamental to economic stability and growth.
The post NDIC pays N1.48bn to 10,312 depositors of 47 closed MFBs appeared first on Vanguard News.
