items.content: The Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on Wednesday raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, its first rate hike in nearly four years, as rising oil prices amid US-Iran tensions and a weak monsoon threaten to push inflation higher.The six-member rate panel voted unanimously in favour of the rate hike. The committee changed its policy stance to calibrated tightening from neutral, signaling further rate hikes may be on the table.The repo rate was last raised in February 2023, when it was increased by 25 basis points to 6.50%.ALSO READ | Why RBI MPC lifted repo rates for the first time in nearly four years in October policy Of the 21 economists and bank executives polled by ET, 20 had expected the RBI to raise rates.The move marks the first rate hike under Governor Sanjay Malhotra, who took office in December 2024 and oversaw a series of rate cuts last year. It also puts the RBI in line with several Asian peers like Bank of Japan and Bank of Korea that have started tightening policy in response to renewed inflation pressures.The MPC “observed, in light of the available data, that it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year,” Malhotra said in a televised statement from the RBI headquarters in Mumbai. Against that backdrop, he added that “recalibrating the policy rate” had become “an imperative.”The RBI’s revised stance “underscored that given the current conditions, rate cuts are off the table in the near term, and policy action can only be a hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions,” Malhotra added.ALSO READ | RBI raises FY27 GDP forecast to 7.1% from 6.7%Since the RBI’s last policy meeting in August, oil prices have surged above $100 a barrel, the rupee has weakened and inflation has accelerated.With inflation nearing 5% in the last three month and expected to move closer to the upper end of the RBI’s 2%-6% tolerance band in the December quarter, economists expect the central bank to continue tightening.On the macroeconomic front, the central bank upgraded India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2026-27 to 7.1% from 6.7%. In addition to this, it revised its FY27 inflation target upward to 5.2% from 5.0%.Consequently, the standing deposit facility (SDF) rate stands adjusted at 5.25% and the marginal standing facility (MSF) rate and the Bank Rate at 5.75%.ALSO READ | RBI MPC Meeting at a Glance: Your one step guide for all decisionsThe RBI's hike acknowledges that cyclical inflation risks are no longer benign, said Radhika Rao, senior economist, DBS Bank, adding that a change in stance also underscored the RBI MPC's "hawkish intent.""Against a backdrop of elevated oil prices, tighter global conditions, and risks to food inflation from unfavourable weather, policymakers have chosen to reinforce inflation credibility before risks become entrenched."ALSO READ | Central bank raises inflation forecast to 5.2% for FY27The benchmark 10-year bond yield rose as much as seven basis points to 7.27% after the decision. The rupee was largely steady at 96.40 to a dollar.Crude back above $100 a barrelEscalating conflict in the Middle East has pushed crude prices above $100 a barrel, threatening to raise costs across an economy that imports most of its energy. A weak monsoon, meanwhile, could add to pressure on food prices.Brent crossed $101 today. It ended September at around $103, well above the RBI’s FY27 forecast of $85 a barrel. Goldman Sachs has also outlined a scenario in which oil prices could rise to as much as $120 a barrel if attacks on vessels in the Middle East intensify. If exports return to normal, the bank expects oil prices to move back towards $80 a barrel.The combination of higher crude prices and supply disruptions has added to inflation concerns globally. Domestically, economists see inflation potentially rising above the RBI’s 6% tolerance limit in the third quarter.The narrowing interest-rate differential between India and the US is another factor that weighed on the RBI’s decision.A narrower gap can make US assets relatively more attractive to investors and add pressure on the rupee.Foreign investors have pulled a record amount from Indian equities this year, amid elevated US yields, high oil prices and a weaker rupee. The NSE Nifty 50 has declined for eight consecutive weeks—its longest losing streak in 25 years.Too much cashThe RBI is also dealing with a large pool of excess liquidity that has pushed overnight borrowing costs below the policy rate, making financial conditions easier than intended.Much of the surplus came from the RBI’s June push to attract foreign-currency deposits to support the rupee. The move brought in about $133 billion, far above initial expectations of $50 billion-85 billion. While the inflows strengthened India’s external buffers, they also injected a large amount of liquidity into the banking system at a time when inflationary pressures were building.The central bank has already drained more than ₹1 lakh crore ($10.4 billion) through bond sales and other measures, as per Bloomberg.Traders will now look for signals on how aggressively the RBI plans to absorb the remaining surplus alongside further rate hikes.

items.author: Bambang Dwi Atmoko
items.content:
Jakarta Running Festival 2026 tinggal menghitung hari. Menjelang ajang lari yang akan digelar pada 22-25 Oktober 2026 tersebut, para peserta kini memasuki fase persiapan akhir yang sering dianggap sebagai periode paling krusial sebelum race day.
Pada fase ini, pelari umumnya tidak lagi berfokus menambah jarak tempuh atau mengejar pace yang lebih cepat. Sebaliknya, perhatian utama justru beralih pada bagaimana menjaga kondisi tubuh tetap prima, mengelola pemulihan, sekaligus memastikan performa berada di level terbaik saat hari perlombaan tiba.
Baca juga: Samsung Resmi Luncurkan Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, Kini Lebih Tipis tapi Lebih Tangguh
Melihat kebutuhan tersebut, Samsung menyoroti pentingnya pendekatan latihan berbasis data melalui ekosistem Galaxy yang terdiri dari Galaxy Watch Ultra2, Galaxy Watch9, dan Galaxy Z8 Series. Integrasi antardevais ini dirancang untuk membantu pelari memantau kondisi tubuh, mengevaluasi progres latihan, hingga membuat keputusan latihan yang lebih presisi menjelang Jakarta Running Festival 2026.
Menurut Tipe Sultan, MX Product Marketing Manager Samsung Electronics Indonesia, banyak pelari masih beranggapan bahwa peningkatan performa hanya bisa dicapai dengan menambah intensitas latihan. Padahal, memahami respons tubuh terhadap setiap sesi latihan memiliki peran yang sama pentingnya.
“Di fase krusial menjelang Jakarta Running Festival, meningkatkan jarak lari tanpa memperhitungkan beban kardio dan pemulihan justru meningkatkan risiko cedera. Pelari membutuhkan data presisi mengenai respons tubuh terhadap setiap sesi latihan,” ujar Tipe Sultan.
Fitur Unggulan Galaxy Watch Terbaru: Cardio Load Hingga Running Coach
Salah satu fitur yang diunggulkan Samsung adalah Daily Cardio Load, yang tersedia melalui Galaxy Watch Ultra2 dan Galaxy Watch9. Fitur ini dirancang untuk memberikan gambaran mengenai beban kerja sistem kardiovaskular berdasarkan histori aktivitas dan data detak jantung pengguna.
Dengan informasi tersebut, pelari dapat menentukan apakah tubuh masih siap menjalani sesi latihan intensif atau justru membutuhkan recovery. Pendekatan ini dinilai penting untuk mengurangi risiko overtraining yang sering terjadi menjelang kompetisi.
Selain itu, smartwatch Samsung juga dapat memantau sejumlah indikator kesehatan seperti Sleep Score, Vitals, dan Energy Score. Data tersebut kemudian menjadi referensi tambahan untuk memahami tingkat kesiapan tubuh setiap harinya.
Tak hanya memantau kondisi tubuh, Samsung juga menyediakan fitur Running Coach yang mampu menyusun program latihan sesuai target pengguna, mulai dari 5K, 10K, half marathon hingga marathon.
Sementara itu, fitur Fitness Index memungkinkan pelari melihat perkembangan kebugaran dari waktu ke waktu melalui metrik seperti VO2 Max dan kapasitas kardio. Data tersebut bisa dimanfaatkan untuk menyesuaikan program latihan maupun strategi tapering menjelang Jakarta Running Festival 2026.
Tren penggunaan data kesehatan semacam ini memang semakin populer di kalangan pelari. Kehadiran smartwatch tidak lagi sekadar berfungsi sebagai pencatat jarak atau pace, tetapi juga menjadi alat bantu pengambilan keputusan saat berlatih.
Peran Smartphone dalam Persiapan Jakarta Running Festival 2026
Samsung juga mengintegrasikan pengalaman tersebut dengan lini smartphone foldable terbarunya. Pada Galaxy Z Fold8, pengguna dapat memanfaatkan fitur Multi Window untuk membuka grafik Samsung Health berdampingan dengan catatan latihan atau training log.
Sementara Galaxy Z Flip8 diposisikan sebagai perangkat yang lebih praktis untuk dokumentasi aktivitas olahraga. Smartphone ini didukung fitur FlexCam dan Photo Assist yang memudahkan pengguna mengabadikan aktivitas latihan maupun momen bersama komunitas lari.
Melalui kombinasi wearable dan smartphone foldable, Samsung ingin menghadirkan pengalaman yang lebih menyeluruh bagi peserta Jakarta Running Festival 2026, mulai dari tahap persiapan, evaluasi latihan, hingga momen setelah melewati garis finis.
Bagi Gizmofriends yang sedang mempersiapkan diri menghadapi Jakarta Running Festival 2026, pemanfaatan data kebugaran bisa menjadi salah satu cara untuk berlatih lebih cerdas. Sebab menjelang lomba, yang terpenting bukan lagi berlari lebih banyak, melainkan memastikan tubuh benar-benar siap ketika race day tiba.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Bengaluru-based quantum compute startup Quanfluence has raised $10 Mn (around ₹92 Cr) in a funding round led by Chiratae Ventures, with participation Rainmatter by Zerodha and existing backer Pi Ventures.
Quanfluence plans to deploy the fresh capital to further develop its full-stack photonic quantum computing system, bringing together indigenously designed photonic chips, control electronics and software into a single architecture.
The startup is targeting early processors by 2027, followed by larger and scalable quantum machines by 2029.
Founded in 2021 by Sujoy Chakravarty, Ravi Mehta, Biman Chattopadhyay, Aditi Vaidya, Anil Prabhaka, and Sandeep Goyal, Quanfluence is building a universal photonic quantum computer and has deployed a quantum-inspired optical Ising machine.
The IIT-Madras incubated startup’s core technology includes an optical Ising machine that uses light waves as computational units. The system can process hundreds of interconnected variables simultaneously, making it 100X faster than traditional optimisation methods.
Chakravarty told Inc42 that Quanfluence has already commercialised its optical Ising machine, selling the physical systems to customers as well as offering remote access to the machines on a usage-based model.
The startup has sold around three machines and currently runs paid pilots with 10-15 corporations.
The approach could help Quanfluence generate commercial traction while it works on the significantly harder problem of building a scalable universal quantum computer. The startup’s immediate challenge, however, is less about proving the underlying concept and more about integrating its components, scaling manufacturing and navigating long chip-production and hardware-delivery cycles.
With a current team size of 25 employees, it is expecting to scale their workforce to 40-member team over the next year.
Previously, Quanfluence raised $2 Mn (around ₹16.7 Cr) in a seed funding round in December 2024, to scale up its near-term products and accelerate development of its quantum computer.
Since then, the startup has designed and fabricated multiple photonic integrated circuits (PICs) and electronic integrated circuits (EICs). It has also developed low-loss chip-to-fibre coupling designs and demonstrated the generation of quantum light states.
The funding comes as investors increasingly look at exploring deeptech bets that are moving towards commercial and industrial applications.
Quantum computing is still largely at the experimental stage, with the industry yet to achieve the scale required for widespread commercial workloads. Quanfluence is taking a photonics-led approach to this challenge, betting that its architecture can eventually scale from a prototype to systems with millions of qubits.
The development also comes as India’s National Quantum Mission is creating closer links between startups, researchers and government-backed quantum hubs.
Quantum cybersecurity startup QNu Labs recently raised ₹200 Cr (around $21 Mn) in its Series A1 funding round co-led by the state-backed National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest, in September.

items.content:
Data on sectoral deployment of credit by non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) for the month of August 2026, collected from major NBFCs and housing finance companies (HFCs), are set out in the Statement1.
On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, NBFCs’ credit registered a growth of 15.8 per cent in August 2026 as compared to 10.0 per cent a year ago.
Highlights of the sectoral deployment of credit by NBFCs for the month ended August 31, 2026, are given below:
Credit to agriculture and allied activities recorded a robust growth of 17.4 per cent (y-o-y) in August 2026 as against 5.1 per cent a year ago.
Credit to industry grew marginally to 8.4 per cent (y-o-y) in August 2026 as compared with 8.3 per cent in August 2025. Within industry, credit growth in ‘infrastructure’ remained steady.
Credit growth in services sector moderated to 16.2 per cent (y-o-y) in August 2026 from 24.0 per cent a year ago. While credit to ‘commercial real estate’ marked buoyant expansion, credit growth in ‘trade’ and ‘transport operators’ segments witnessed deceleration.
Retail loans growth accelerated to 22.0 per cent (y-o-y) in August 2026 compared to 13.6 per cent a year ago. Within retail loans, ‘housing loans’ and ‘loans against gold jewellery’ segments witnessed accelerated credit growth, while ‘vehicle loans’ maintained its robust growth with marginal uptick.
Ajit Prasad          
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)    
Press Release: 2026-2027/1261
1 Provisional data as reported on the last day of the month. Sectoral credit data of NBFCs are based on sample of (i) NBFCs in Upper and Middle Layers, and (ii) HFCs, accounting for about 87 per cent of total credit with respect to data published in ‘Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2024-25’ (RTP 2024-25, outstanding as on September 2025).

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
OpenAI Agents Hit Wikimedia
OpenAI is under fresh scrutiny over its “rogue” agents. Wikimedia Foundation claims that the AI juggernaut’s agentic system made unauthorised edits on its platforms, crashed its query services and generated millions of automated requests. So, why is the episode raising alarm bells?
Rogue AI Vs Wikipedia: The non-profit said that it found unauthorised edits as well as potentially malicious changes to a citation tool’s configuration. OpenAI agents also tried exploiting its Etherpad tool to access other websites and generated millions of API and WDQS queries. This possibly contributed to the Wikipedia outage in May.
The foundation found no evidence of data compromise but warned that such scale imposes significant costs on public internet infrastructure.
OpenAI’s Safety Gap: The AI giant said that it was reviewing Wikimedia’s findings but offered no acknowledgment or responsibility. This fits into a broader pattern. OpenAI has faced repeated criticism in the past few months after its agents bypassed safety controls and accessed Australia’s Medicare system and Hugging Face infrastructure. As such, these incidents have revealed gaps in real-time monitoring and transparency at OpenAI.
The Hidden Vectors: The latest episode comes as AI is accelerating cyber threats, enabling rapid exploitation and hyper-personalised attacks. Deepfakes can bypass KYC, while attack timelines have shrunk from weeks to hours. Meanwhile, automated agents continuously scan and exploit vulnerabilities in real time, outpacing human response teams.
The New Security Playbook: Experts warn that traditional safeguards built around isolated testing are inadequate for agentic AI. Defenders are shifting from periodic audits to continuous threat exposure management, least-privilege access and resilience-first design. As agents grow more autonomous, here is how the latest Wikimedia row has raised concerns over OpenAI’s safeguards…
From The Editor’s Desk
Fuzzy Dynamics Eyes $12 Mn
Currently in stealth mode, the frontier AI startup is in advanced talks to raise about ₹115 Cr in its maiden funding round. Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst are exploring co-leading the round, which could peg the startup at a $50 Mn valuation.
Founded in 2025, FYDY claims to be developing “cognitive machines” that learn from experience. Its long-term goal is to build safe artificial superintelligence capable of acting autonomously in the real world. Its AI research studio is currently in private beta.
The funding talks come amid growing VC interest in AI startups that cater to research and enterprise applications. As per Inc42 data, AI startups raised $438 Mn across 35 deals in Q3 2026, up 265% YoY, making AI the most funded sector.
AITMC Files UDRHP
The drone tech startup has filed its updated DRHP with SEBI for an IPO, which will consist entirely of a fresh issue of up to 3.5 Cr shares. This comes nearly ten months after it received SEBI’s nod to go ahead with its listing.
Founded in 2016, AITMC Ventures manufactures drones and offers courses for drone pilots and technicians. It claims to have so far trained 1 Lakh candidates and sold 190 drones. The startup reported a profit of ₹13.4 Cr in FY26 against a top line of ₹106.8 Cr.
Separately, Swara Baby Products, a contract manufacturer of hygiene products and a subsidiary of FirstCry’s parent Brainbees Solutions, has received approval from the SEBI to float its proposed ₹1,000 Cr IPO.
Tracking FY26 Founder Salaries
Sixteen founders across 10 startups earned a combined ₹43.4 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26, up 8.2% from ₹40.2 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. Of these, 12 founders saw an increase in fixed pay, three saw reductions, and one reported unchanged remuneration.
Lenskart cofounder Peyush Bansal drew the highest fixed remuneration in FY26 at ₹5.7 Cr. Meesho cofounders Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Kumar followed with ₹4.8 Cr each, while Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma received ₹4 Cr, unchanged from FY25.
However, fixed pay tells only part of the story. Peyush Bansal received ₹12 Cr in bonuses and performance incentives. Meanwhile, Swiggy’s Sriharsha Majety reported an ESOP gain of ₹549.3 Cr, while Kapil Bharati of Delhivery recorded ₹6.9 Cr in ESOP gains.
StockGro To Raise ₹110 Cr
The IPO-bound investment tech startup is raising $10.4 Mn in its ongoing Series B round led by existing backer BITKRAFT Ventures. The startup’s board has approved issuing 14,004 Series B CCPS to investors at ₹78,668 apiece.
While BITKRAFT is infusing ₹60.1 Cr, Aditum Venture Capital Fund is pumping in ₹23.1 Cr. Rest of the amount will be contributed by India SME Growth Fund, Systematix Fincorp and other angel investors.
This comes weeks after StockGro’s parent AssetGro Fintech Ltd filed its DRHP with SEBI via the confidential route. The startup is looking to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr via the IPO, which is likely to include a fresh issue of ₹800 Cr and an OFS component.
Govt’s ₹10,000 Cr SME Fund
The Union Cabinet has cleared a proposal for setting up a ₹10,000 Cr SME Growth Fund to unlock growth credit for small and medium enterprises. The fund will back SMEs across manufacturing, services, technology and innovation-driven sectors.
Under the framework, the government will commit ₹10,000 Cr to alternative investment funds (AIFs), which will subsequently invest in high-potential SMEs. This will help businesses expand operations, adopt new technologies and enter international markets.
As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, the MSME sector accounts for nearly 31.1% of India’s GDP. With over 7.47 Cr enterprises employing over 32.82 Cr persons, the sector is the second-largest employer in the country after agriculture.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Procurio Make Manufacturing In India Less Chaotic?
In India, finding suppliers for manufacturing is the easy part. But ensuring they meet quality standards, fulfil deadlines and manage export paperwork is much harder. Procurio is addressing this execution gap with its one-stop-shop sourcing platform for businesses.
Beyond Discovery: Founded in 2025, Procurio helps global companies source and manufacture engineering parts in India. Unlike a supplier directory, it takes responsibility for qualification, pricing, production, inspection, documentation and delivery. The startup claims to work with 400+ local suppliers across aerospace, defence and energy.
A Single-Window Platform: The startup’s workflow begins with understanding a buyer’s requirements. Procurio then assesses feasibility, shortlists suppliers, negotiates quotes and oversees production. It also conducts quality inspections, manages export documentation and coordinates shipping.
Growing Global Traction: Procurio serves 12 clients across the US, Canada, the UK and Europe. The startup, which supports both standard components and custom-built parts, earns money from commission on each order, depending on the project complexity. It competes against the likes of deep-pocketed giants such as Zetwerk and Karkhana.
With the homegrown contract manufacturing market projected to cross $49.4 Bn by FY30, can Procurio connect global manufacturers with India’s supplier ecosystem?

items.title: Kingston Pertahankan Posisi Pemasok Modul DRAM Terbesar Dunia
items.summary:
Kingston Technology kembali mempertahankan posisi sebagai pemasok modul DRAM pihak ketiga terbesar di dunia berdasarkan peringkat pendapatan terbaru dari TrendForce. Perusahaan tersebut diperkirakan menguasai 62% pangsa pasar pada 2025, atau hampir dua pertiga dari total pasar modul DRAM pihak ketiga secara global.
Menurut laporan TrendForce, pasar modul DRAM global mencatat pendapatan sekitar US$21,2 miliar pada 2025, naik 59% secara tahunan. Pertumbuhan tersebut jauh lebih tinggi dibandingkan kenaikan 7% pada 2024. Kenaikan pendapatan terutama didorong oleh meningkatnya harga DRAM serta volume pengiriman yang lebih tinggi pada paruh kedua 2025.
Di sisi Kingston, pendapatan perusahaan dari bisnis modul DRAM disebut tumbuh 48% YoY sepanjang 2025. Kondisi pasar tersebut turut memperkuat posisi Kingston, sementara lima pemasok modul DRAM terbesar secara keseluruhan menyumbang sekitar 77% pendapatan pasar. Angka ini menunjukkan bahwa pasar modul DRAM masih memiliki konsentrasi yang cukup

Di sisi Kingston, pendapatan perusahaan dari bisnis modul DRAM disebut tumbuh 48% YoY sepanjang 2025. Baca Juga: Biwin Black Opal DW100 DDR5-6000 CL28 Hadir dengan Profil AMD EXPO ULL
Permintaan Server dan AI Dorong Pasar DRAM
Perubahan pola permintaan menjadi salah satu faktor penting dalam perkembangan pasar DRAM sepanjang 2025. Pada awal tahun, produsen modul meningkatkan persediaan DDR4 karena adanya kekhawatiran terhadap tarif dan rencana pemasok DRAM menghentikan produk DDR4. Memasuki akhir tahun, permintaan dari penyedia layanan cloud meningkat seiring berkembangnya beban kerja agentic AI.
Peningkatan kebutuhan DRAM untuk server kemudian berdampak pada ketersediaan memori untuk PC dan perangkat konsumen. Kondisi tersebut ikut mendorong kenaikan harga DRAM sekaligus memperkuat pendapatan pasar modul. TrendForce juga mencatat adanya pergeseran fokus produsen menuju segmen server dan enterprise, bersamaan dengan percepatan transisi dari DDR4 ke DDR5.
Kingston Perluas Fokus ke Segmen B2B
Kingston menyebut kemampuan pengadaan dan pengelolaan persediaan menjadi salah satu faktor yang membantu perusahaan menghadapi perubahan kondisi pasar sepanjang 2025. Ketika harga DRAM meningkat pada paruh kedua tahun tersebut, perusahaan mengatakan dapat merespons permintaan dari kanal distribusi sekaligus mempertahankan ketersediaan produk.
Selain distribusi konsumen, Kingston juga melihat pertumbuhan pada bisnis B2B yang mencakup pelanggan enterprise, pusat data, dan industri. Portofolionya mencakup modul DDR4 hingga DDR5 untuk berbagai kebutuhan, mulai dari PC dan gaming hingga server, infrastruktur AI, sistem embedded, pengawasan, dan otomatisasi.
Meski demikian, dominasi pangsa pasar tersebut juga berlangsung di tengah kondisi DRAM yang sangat dipengaruhi oleh harga dan perubahan alokasi produksi. Dengan meningkatnya kebutuhan memori untuk server dan AI, persaingan mendapatkan pasokan DRAM berpotensi terus memengaruhi harga serta ketersediaan produk untuk segmen konsumen. Kingston sendiri menilai kemampuan menjaga kontinuitas pasokan akan menjadi bagian penting dari strategi bisnisnya ke depan.

items.summary: Rising oil prices, now exceeding 1%, raise alarms over potential storm disruptions affecting U.S. oil production and refineries. With Brent crude passing $101 per barrel and WTI crude hitting $90.38, concerns are amplified by supply issues from Saudi Arabia and mixed signals on U.S. inventories. Coupled with ongoing tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, analysts predict sustained high prices unless significant diplomatic progress is made.

By Steve Oko
UMUAHIA — A 19-year-old motorcycle accident victim has survived emergency brain surgery at the Abia State Specialist Hospital and Diagnostic Centre, Umuahia, after doctors evacuated more than 100 millilitres of blood clot compressing his brainstem.
The victim was reportedly brought to the hospital on Sunday, October 4, in a deep coma with a Glasgow Coma Scale, GCS, score of six out of 15, which later deteriorated to five.
The four-hour operation was performed after investigations revealed massive bleeding inside the victim’s skull.
Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this on Tuesday while briefing journalists at Government House, Umuahia, on the outcome of the State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Alex Otti.
Giving details, the Commissioner for Health, Prof. Enoch Uche, a neurosurgeon, said the bleeding was compressing the patient’s brainstem, making immediate surgery necessary.
He said transferring the patient to another facility could have proved fatal, given the severity of his condition.
“Because we now have facilities to undertake brain surgery, and then we have brain surgeons in the state employed by His Excellency, that surgery was done,” Uche said.
He disclosed that more than 100ml of blood clot was evacuated from the patient’s brain, adding that the young man had subsequently started moving his limbs while recovering in the Intensive Care Unit.
Speaking with Vanguard, the Chief Medical Director of the hospital, Dr Chimezie Okwuonu, described the procedure as the facility’s first brain surgery.
He said the successful operation demonstrated the growing capacity of the hospital to manage complex medical conditions locally.
Okwuonu said the surgery was performed by a multidisciplinary team led by Uche, the hospital’s neurosurgeon, Dr Kalu and other specialists.
He disclosed that the hospital, which had only one specialist consultant when the current management assumed duty, now has 28 consultants.
According to him, the expansion was part of efforts to strengthen specialist manpower and improve healthcare infrastructure in the state.
Okwuonu said the hospital would build on the development by expanding its capacity for brain and spine surgeries and providing specialised neurological care within Abia.
He added that the development would complement the state’s efforts to reduce medical tourism, citing the commencement of kidney transplant services as another area in which the state was building local capacity.
Other health interventions
Meanwhile, Kanu disclosed that the state had paid N502.1 million as counterpart funding under the Basic Healthcare Provision Fund, a requirement for accessing Federal Government intervention for vulnerable residents.
He also said specialised trauma equipment for orthopaedic, brain and spine surgeries was being attracted to the state through collaboration with a Swedish organisation.
Kanu said health interventions had commenced in flood-affected communities to prevent disease outbreaks.
He added that no cases of Lassa fever, Ebola, diphtheria or COVID-19 had been recorded during the period under review.
Also, the Administrator of the Abia State Eye Health Management Bureau, Dr Betty Emeka-Obasi, said the state had commenced activities to mark the 2026 World Sight Day.
She said free eye screening for commercial drivers was among the programmes being implemented under the campaign, themed “Safe Eyes, Safe Roads and Safe Lives.”
According to her, the campaign would run until October 15, with the bureau collaborating with the Ministry of Transport, the Federal Road Safety Corps and transport unions.
Emeka-Obasi also disclosed plans to establish a vision corridor at the Nnenna Otti Bus Terminal, where commercial drivers would be able to conveniently assess their eyesight.
She said the initiative was aimed at reducing road risks associated with poor vision among drivers.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Chioma Gabriel
There are lives that can be measured by what a man accumulated, and there are lives that must be measured by what he was prepared to lose for an idea.
Chief Ralph Obioha belonged to the second category.
For a man who built businesses, entered politics, sat in the House of Representatives, helped organise one of Nigeria’s most consequential pro-democracy struggles and spent years in exile, his life was a remarkable intersection of enterprise, public service, political conviction and sacrifice.
Obioha died on October 3, 2026, at the age of 80. His family, announcing his death on October 6, described him as a beloved husband, father, grandfather, brother and friend, as well as a patriot, elder statesman, political leader and businessman committed to Nigeria’s progress.
But beyond the formal descriptions lies a more compelling story: that of a man who moved from the world of business into politics and, eventually, into the dangerous theatre of the struggle against military dictatorship.
Born into enterprise
Ralph Obioha was born into the influential Obioha family of Arondizuogu in present-day Imo State.
His father, Chief Louis Nwakire Obioha, was a prominent businessman and industrialist whose entrepreneurial activities became part of the economic history of the area. He established NIPROC, a large-scale palm-kernel processing enterprise at Arondizuogu.
It was a background in which enterprise was not merely about personal wealth. Business was also a vehicle for employment, community development, and social influence.
Ralph inherited that entrepreneurial instinct.
Before he became known nationally as a politician and NADECO leader, he had already established himself as a businessman with interests across several sectors. At one point, his business empire included First African Trust Bank, Safari Brewery, Castle Cement’s cement-bagging operation in Port Harcourt and a vegetable-oil company.
The scale of those enterprises offers an important window into the man he was before politics consumed much of his life.
In a 2018 interview, Obioha said his businesses had employed about 2,700 Nigerians and 17 expatriates. He would later lose virtually all of them as a consequence of his involvement in the struggle for democracy. That loss became one of the defining chapters of his life.
Politics and the Second Republic
Obioha’s political journey began long before he became associated with NADECO.
He served as a member of the House of Representatives during Nigeria’s Second Republic. A profile of his political career also records that he chaired the House Committee on Finance during that period.
But the political turbulence that repeatedly interrupted Nigeria’s democratic journey would eventually pull him into a far more dangerous form of politics.
The annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election transformed the country’s political landscape.
For Obioha, it was not simply another disagreement between politicians. He regarded the annulment of what he believed was Moshood Abiola’s electoral mandate as an assault on democracy itself. That conviction would change his life.
The June 12 struggle
Obioha became one of the prominent figures associated with the National Democratic Coalition, NADECO, the movement that emerged as a major force against military rule and demanded the restoration of the June 12 mandate.
When General Sani Abacha’s regime intensified its crackdown on pro-democracy activists, Obioha went into exile.
He became a leading figure in NADECO’s activities in Canada and the United States, campaigning internationally against military rule and for the restoration of Abiola’s mandate.
It was a decision that came at an extraordinary personal cost.
The businessman who had built companies and employed thousands of Nigerians was suddenly separated from his businesses, his country and, for a period, his normal family life.
In his own recollection, he had expected the exile to last months. Instead, it lasted years. He eventually returned to Nigeria in 1998.
Looking back years later, he was remarkably unapologetic.
He lost the bank.
He lost the brewery.
He lost the cement operation.
He lost the vegetable-oil company.
But he insisted he did not regret the struggle.
“I will never regret being part of the struggle,” he said in an interview, describing the experience as a wider sphere of experience for him.
That perhaps captures the paradox of Ralph Obioha’s life: a man who lost much materially while believing that he had gained something larger in the service of his country.
The price of exile
The story of Nigeria’s pro-democracy struggle is often told through its most famous names — Abiola, Kudirat Abiola, Alfred Rewane, Wole Soyinka, Gani Fawehinmi and others.
But there were men and women whose contributions were made away from the cameras.
Obioha became one of those voices abroad.
From Canada and the United States, he helped keep international attention on Nigeria’s political crisis. His argument was simple: the military could suppress activists at home, but it could not easily silence those speaking to the international community.
He later recalled that the struggle was motivated by both patriotism and what he described as the denial of a mandate freely given by Nigerians.
For him, democracy was not an abstract word.
It was a principle worth paying for.
The politician after exile
When Nigeria returned to democratic rule in 1999, Obioha did not disappear from public life.
He remained politically engaged and became national chairman of the Justice Party. The party later fielded Rev. Chris Okotie as its presidential candidate in the 2003 election.
He also became involved in affairs concerning Ohanaeze Ndigbo and served as chairman of its caretaker committee at one stage, although his involvement in the organisation was accompanied by disputes over its leadership and representation.
His politics was often outspoken.
He spoke about power, corruption, insecurity, tribalism, the condition of the South-East and the wider question of Nigerian nationhood.
But beneath many of his interventions was one recurring belief: Nigeria’s problems could not be solved by merely replacing one ethnic group with another at the top.
He repeatedly argued for competence, institutional development and leadership capable of producing results.
A voice on Nigeria’s contradictions
Obioha’s later years were characterised by an unusual combination of nostalgia and criticism.
He remembered a Nigeria that, in his view, possessed enormous economic promise, yet he was deeply frustrated by the country’s failure to convert its human and natural resources into prosperity.
In his 2018 conversation with Vanguard, he identified electricity, employment, education, healthcare and functioning institutions among the issues holding Nigeria back.
He was particularly concerned about tribalism.
His argument was that Nigeria should search for its best people irrespective of whether they were Igbo, Yoruba, Hausa, Ijaw, Efik, Kanuri or from any other ethnic group.
It was a striking position from a man who was himself an important voice in Igbo affairs.
His nationalism did not require him to abandon his identity.
Instead, he appeared to believe that ethnic identity and Nigerian citizenship could coexist without one destroying the other.
The elder statesman
Even in old age, Obioha remained politically engaged.
In January 2026, shortly before his death, he spoke forcefully against the description of the January 1966 coup as an “Igbo coup”.
Having lived through the era, he argued that the coup should not be collectively attributed to the Igbo people. He acknowledged the prominent participation of Igbo officers but rejected the idea that the Igbo as a people had organised or authorised the coup.
It was characteristic of the older Obioha: still argumentative, still willing to enter difficult national conversations and still convinced that historical narratives mattered.
His voice remained recognisable — measured, sometimes blunt, but deeply concerned about Nigeria’s direction.
Recognition that came late
In 2026, President Bola Tinubu included Obioha among Nigerians selected for national honours for their roles in the June 12 struggle.
But Obioha declined the honour, according to reports, citing concerns including insecurity and the continued detention of Nnamdi Kanu.
There was something symbolic about that decision.
The man who had spent decades demanding justice for a political mandate had reached the twilight of his life still insisting that the country had unfinished business.
What remains
Ralph Obioha’s life cannot be reduced to NADECO.
Nor can it be reduced to his businesses, his parliamentary career, his political disagreements or his role in Igbo affairs.
His story is ultimately about the choices a man makes when personal comfort collides with public conviction.
He had something to lose, and he lost it.
He had businesses to protect, and they collapsed.
He had a country to return to, but exile became his temporary home.
He had opportunities to remain silent — yet he chose to speak.
And when the struggle ended, and democracy eventually returned, he did not pretend that Nigeria had suddenly become the country the pro-democracy activists had imagined.
He continued to question it.
He continued to criticise it.
He continued to believe in its potential.
That may be the most enduring thread in the life of Ralph Obioha.
He was a businessman who entered politics, a politician who became a dissident, a dissident who became an elder statesman, and an elder statesman who never quite stopped being an activist.
His life traversed some of Nigeria’s most turbulent decades.
And in the final reckoning, his greatest possession may not have been the businesses he built or the political offices he occupied.
It may have been the conviction that Nigeria was worth fighting for — even when the fight demanded that he give up almost everything he had.
Ralph Obioha died at 80. But the questions he spent a lifetime asking about democracy, justice, leadership and the Nigerian project remain very much alive.

Untuk performa, Moto G67 mengandalkan chipset MediaTek Dimensity 6300, RAM 4GB yang dapat diperluas secara virtual melalui RAM Boost hingga 12GB, serta penyimpanan internal 128 GB.
Ponsel ini langsung menjalankan Android 16, dan dibekali baterai 5.200 mAh dengan TurboPower 30W. 
“Untuk kebutuhan fotografi, perangkat ini mengusung kamera utama 50 MP dengan sensor Sony LYTIA 600 berteknologi Quad Pixel dan moto ai, dipadukan dengan kamera ultrawide 8 MP serta kamera depan 32 MP,” kata Zulfahmi
Spesifikasi Moto G77 Power
Moto G77 Power. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson)
“Kalau di Moto G77 Power, salah satu perbedaannya adalah kami menggunakan sensor Sony LT600 pada kamera utama. Ada juga kamera ultrawide 8MP, sensor cahaya untuk membantu fokus, serta kamera depan 32MP.”
Perusahaan juga meningkatkan kapasitas baterai di Moto G77 Power menjadi 7.000 mAh, dan sudah mendukung pengisian daya 32W dan reverse charging. “Dari sisi performa, kami menggunakan MediaTek Dimensity 6400 dan RAM 4GB yang bisa diperluas melalui RAM Boost hingga 12GB,” papar Zulfahmi.

“Di Moto G77 Power, Dolby Atmos tetap tersedia, begitu juga jack audio 3,5 mm. Pengguna juga mendapatkan slot microSD hingga 1TB dan built-in FM radio,” ucapnya.
Dengan tiga model tersebut, Motorola kini memiliki pilihan Moto G yang mencakup kebutuhan berbeda di pasar Indonesia. Moto G37 menargetkan konsumen yang mengincar 5G dengan harga lebih rendah, Moto G67 menawarkan layar AMOLED dan kamera lebih lengkap, sementara Moto G77 Power menempatkan baterai 7.000 mAh sebagai daya tarik utama.

vivo V80 Bawa Kamera ZEISS dan Telefoto 3x
Kamera utama vivo V80 menggunakan sensor Sony LYT 700V 50MP dengan dukungan optical image stabilization (OIS) dan autofocus. Kamera ini mampu merekam video hingga resolusi 4K, termasuk opsi 4K 60fps dan mode cinematic. Di bagian belakang, kamera tersebut ditemani kamera ultrawide 8MP.
Menariknya, vivo turut menyematkan kamera telefoto Sony IMX882 50MP yang juga memiliki OIS dan mendukung optical zoom 3x. Sementara itu, kamera depan menggunakan sensor 50MP wide dengan autofocus. Kombinasi ini membuat V80 tidak hanya mengandalkan kamera utama untuk kebutuhan fotografi jarak jauh.
Baterai 7.200 mAh dengan Pengisian 90W
Salah satu spesifikasi yang cukup menonjol adalah baterai berkapasitas 7.200 mAh. vivo memasangkan baterai tersebut dengan dukungan pengisian cepat 90W. Kapasitas ini berpotensi memberikan daya tahan lebih panjang, meski penggunaan aktual tetap akan bergantung pada pola penggunaan dan kondisi perangkat.
Untuk fitur lainnya, vivo V80 memiliki pemindai sidik jari di dalam layar, sertifikasi IP69, Wi-Fi dual-band, Bluetooth 5.4, GPS, NFC, dan dukungan eSIM. Bodinya menggunakan frame aluminium dan bagian belakang berbahan kaca, dengan ketebalan 7,79 mm serta bobot 210 gram.
Di India, vivo V80 tersedia dalam pilihan warna Horizon Blue, Stellar Black, dan Sunrise Anthem. Harga mulai INR 62.999 atau sekitar Rp11,70 juta untuk varian 8GB/128GB. Varian 8GB/256GB dibanderol INR 69.999 atau sekitar Rp13,00 juta, sedangkan varian 8GB/512GB mencapai INR 79.999 atau sekitar Rp14,86 juta. Konversi menggunakan kurs sekitar Rp185,79 per INR pada 7 Oktober 2026.

items.content: Mumbai: Aggregate revenue and net profit of the Nifty 50 companies are expected to grow in double digits year-on-year for the September quarter led by select companies from the automobiles, banking and finance, metals and oil and gas sectors. Revenue and net profit are likely to grow by 19.9% and 22.3% respectively according to the ETIG estimates. Their performance will also benefit from the lower base of 9% and 8.4% growth in revenue and profit in the year-ago quarter."The broader earnings outlook remains healthy, supported by improving domestic demand, strong credit growth, government spending and a recovery in private capex," said Feroze Azeez, Joint CEO, Anand Rathi Wealth.134753222Gautam Duggad, MD and Head of Sales, Institutional Equities, Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) expects Nifty earnings to grow by 27% and that of the companies covered by the broking firm to increase by 22%."Excluding oil marketing companies, aggregate earnings for the MOFSL Universe are expected to grow 24% year-on-year during the quarter," Duggad said.Read more: How a 9-year-old Warren Buffett learnt a lesson on compounding by rolling snowballs on the lawn of his Nebraska homeThe operating margin at the aggregate level is likely to contract by a tad 20 basis points to 21.9% from the year ago amid input cost inflation. Azzez expects margins to remain mixed as benefits of lower commodity costs are normalising while wage inflation and higher crude prices are creating some pressure on margins. "For capital goods, infrastructure and manufacturing, margins likely to remain stable to improving, supported by healthy order books, capacity utilisation and operating leverage," he mentioned, adding that for banking and finance companies, earnings growth would be driven more by strong loan growth than by expansion in margins.Read more: Why junk bonds deliver equity-like returns but with far inferior volatility, explains Saurabh MukherjeaDespite near-term challenges in the form of volatile energy prices, geopolitical and tariff risks, and weakening rupee against major currnecies, analysts are optimistic about medium-to-long term growth trajectory. Duggad believes that the risk-reward for Indian equities over a medium and long term has meaningfully improved given healthy earnings growth, resilient macroeconomic environment and cooling valuations. "With earnings growth increasingly concentrated in select themes, we expect market performance to remain firmly bottom-up, favouring growth-oriented businesses that are successfully scaling up and strengthening their competitive positioning," Duggad said. He expects 15-16% earnings growth over FY26-28 for the companies under his coverage.Azeez of Anand Rathi remains constructive for FY27 driven by strong healthy domestic demand and credit growth, government and private capital expenditure, and improving corporate earnings. "For FY27, Nifty 50 earnings per share (EPS) is expected to rise to ₹1,240 from ₹1,088 with 14% earnings growth," he said.Sector viewAutomobilesDemand across automobile segments remained resilient with sales volume growing in double digits year-on-year in the September quarter, barring lower tractor volume amid irregular monsoon. While revenue of majority of the auto makers is expected to rise in double digits, profits and profitability may remain muted due to higher input costs.BankingNet interest income is expected to grow in low double digits year-on-year while non-interest income may decline amid lower treasury income due to firm bond yields. Net interest margin may show weakness depending upon the extent of FCNR deposits raised by banks. The asset quality is likely to stay stable.Capital GoodsFresh orders from segments including power generation, transmission and distribution, data centres, and infrastructure kept the order book ringing during the quarter. While domestic execution gained pace amid scattered monsoon trend, geopolitical disturbance in the West Asian region may result in slower order ramp up. Higher raw material costs will weigh on profitability though the impact may soften due to pass-though of higher costs in some projects.CementCement demand is expected to grow in higher single digit in the September quarter, helped by sustained construction activities in an otherwise seasonally weak quarter due to monsoon. Demand was steady in the North, Western and Central regions. Cement prices showed a gradual recovery, largely to offset higher input costs. However, profitability is likely to remain under pressure.FMCGBarring ITC, fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies are likely to report double digit revenue growth amid stable sales volume, higher product prices and low base in the year ago quarter. ITC is expected to show weaker sales volume, which is expected to result in lower revenue and profit for the quarter.Information TechnologyClients continued to observe caution while ramping up large, discretionary assignments. This is expected to keep top line growth muted for most top tier IT companies. The sequential revenue growth for the top tier companies is expected to remain under 2-3% for the quarte keeping currency rates constant. Operating margins may show a slight uptick in the absence of major wage increases for most of the top companies. Over 8.7% depreciation in the average rupee rate against the dollar during the quarter will support the rupee-denominated performanceMetalsElevated prices of aluminium, copper, and zinc are expected to help non-ferrous companies to post strong performance in the September quarter. Ferrous companies, too, are expected to benefit from firm domestic demand from the infrastructure segment.PharmaceuticalsCompanies with domestic focus are expected to show continued traction in the September quarter while US focused pharma companies such as Dr Reddy's Labs and Cipla are likely to report weakness with a double-digit drop in revenue. A weaker rupee is expected to soften the blow in reported profits.

By Olasunkanmi Akoni
Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, has pledged continued government support for the creative industry through skills development, expanded training opportunities and provision of infrastructure to drive the sector’s growth.
Hamzat spoke on Tuesday at the official commissioning and grand opening of Euphoria360 Hub, established by actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo, in Oregun, Lagos.
He said the state was committed to developing a sustainable pipeline of skilled creative professionals capable of competing and earning in the global market.
According to him, Lagos has no shortage of creative talent but needs the right structures and opportunities to harness its potential.
“The state is already investing in creative infrastructure, which includes the development of theatres in Ikorodu, Badagry, among other divisions.
“Besides, the government is exploring further opportunities to expand training in areas such as filmmaking, acting, photography and other creative disciplines, as well as training up to one million Lagosians across various fields,” he said.
The deputy governor said the government’s focus should go beyond training young people to creating a sustainable pipeline of globally competitive talent and linking skills development directly to employment opportunities.
He said the objective was to create an enabling environment where creative professionals could showcase Nigerian culture to the world while earning commensurate economic value from their work.
Citing the growing global influence of Nigerian films and storytelling, Hamzat said the country’s productions had become an important means of projecting Nigeria’s identity and culture across Africa and beyond.
“I want to challenge you, our elders and stakeholders in the creative industry, to identify the major barriers limiting growth and work with the government to develop practical solutions, particularly in areas such as intellectual property, contracts and skills development,” he said.
Hamzat congratulated Adebayo, the Chief Executive Officer of Euphoria360, on the establishment of the mega audio-visual project, describing it as an important contribution to the growth of Lagos’ creative ecosystem.
Also speaking, Special Adviser to the President on Media and Public Communication, Mr Sunday Dare, described Nigeria’s entertainment industry as a powerful force that had significantly enhanced the country’s visibility and global influence.
Dare said government needed to support and strengthen the creative sector, noting that the industry had significant economic potential and could create jobs for a large number of young people.
Earlier, Adebayo said the vision behind Euphoria360 Hub was to establish a one-stop facility where producers, filmmakers, creators, film enthusiasts and event planners could access quality facilities and professional services needed to bring their projects to life.
He said the hub was designed to bring everything required to produce and deliver world-class projects under one roof, adding that it would become a landmark destination for creativity, collaboration and excellence in the entertainment industry.
Adebayo said the facility brought together key players across the entertainment value chain while providing access to modern facilities and professional services needed to develop and deliver world-class productions.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
ABUJA —The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) has issued a public warning over the spread of fraudulent employment advertisements and forged appointment letters being used by scammers to deceive job seekers.
The warning was contained in a public notice issued by the Fund and circulated to regional and branch managers via a memorandum dated October 5, 2026, signed by Samaila Abdu, Esq., Executive Director, Administration.
According to the notice, the NSITF said it is not currently recruiting for any position and described employment advertisements circulating on social media, particularly Facebook, as fake
The Fund stated that the fraudulent advertisements reflect a growing trend of individuals and groups falsely claiming to represent the NSITF in recruitment exercises.
NSITF urged members of the public to disregard such advertisements and avoid making payments to anyone over purported employment opportunities.
The Fund emphasised that it neither charges fees for employment nor conducts recruitment through unofficial social media platforms or channels.
It added that any genuine employment opportunities would be announced through its official channels.
“Stay alert, stay safe,” the Fund urged, advising members of the public who encounter suspicious recruitment advertisements or requests to avoid responding and report them to the appropriate NSITF authorities.
As part of measures to protect the public and safeguard the integrity of its recruitment process, NSITF management has directed all Regional and Branch Managers to prominently display the public notice at strategic locations within their offices.
The directive covers reception areas, main entrances and exits, notice boards, SERVICOM desks and other conspicuous locations accessible to staff and members of the public.
The Fund said the notice should be displayed immediately and kept visible to ensure that members of the public are adequately informed and protected from fraudulent recruitment activities.
NSITF urged Nigerians, particularly job seekers, to exercise caution and verify every recruitment claim through the Fund’s official communication channels before taking any action.
The development comes amid growing concerns over fraudulent online recruitment schemes targeting unemployed Nigerians with promises of government jobs in exchange for money or personal information.
NSITF’s latest warning underscores the need for job seekers to remain vigilant, as legitimate public-sector recruitment does not require applicants to pay individuals or unofficial agents for employment.

MacBook dan Mac Studio dengan Chip Baru
Salah satu produk yang disebut akan hadir pada peluncuran kedua adalah lini MacBook Ultra. Mereka juga dikabarkan sedang mempersiapkan MacBook Pro 14 inci dan iMac yang ditenagai chip M6. Laporan tersebut muncul di tengah kabar bahwa Apple akan memperkenalkan MacBook dengan layar sentuh dalam waktu dekat.
Selain itu, Apple disebut sedang menyiapkan varian Mac Studio yang menggunakan chip M5 Ultra. Salah satu konfigurasi yang dikabarkan bahkan dapat membawa kapasitas RAM hingga 512GB, meskipun detail lengkap mengenai perangkat dan konfigurasi tersebut belum dikonfirmasi secara resmi.
Jika benar diluncurkan dalam waktu dekat, rangkaian perangkat tersebut menunjukkan bahwa Apple berpotensi memperbarui lini Mac secara cukup agresif pada akhir tahun. Namun, belum diketahui apakah seluruh produk yang dirumorkan akan diperkenalkan dalam acara yang sama atau justru dibagi ke beberapa pengumuman.
iPad mini OLED Juga Berpotensi Hadir
Selain perangkat Mac, Apple juga disebut dapat memperkenalkan iPad mini generasi baru. Tablet berukuran ringkas tersebut dikabarkan akan menggunakan layar OLED dan chipset A20 Pro, yang berarti peningkatan cukup besar dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya jika informasi tersebut benar.
Meski demikian, status iPad mini tersebut masih berada dalam ranah rumor. Begitu pula dengan MacBook Ultra, MacBook Pro M6, iMac M6, dan Mac Studio M5 Ultra. Apple belum memberikan konfirmasi mengenai jadwal peluncuran maupun spesifikasi produk-produk tersebut.
Dengan adanya dua laporan mengenai agenda peluncuran pada Oktober, perhatian kini tertuju pada apakah Apple benar-benar akan menggelar dua pengumuman terpisah. Jika terwujud, perusahaan kemungkinan akan memiliki dua momentum produk dalam satu bulan, dengan HomePad sebagai perangkat smart home dan jajaran Mac serta iPad sebagai fokus peluncuran berikutnya.

items.author: Idowu Isamotu
items.content:
A cross-section of Nigerians have lauded troops over their recent exploits where they neutralized a senior leader of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP).
This is just as Taraba State governor, Agbu Kefas, hailed President Bola Tinubu and the military high command being led by General Olufemi Oluyede, for establishing 10 Division of the Nigerian Army in the state.
It was learnt that the terrorists’ leader, identified as Abdussamad Ohida, was killed in a forest around Owo, Ondo State during a covert operation conducted by the troops in conjunction with other security forces on their hideouts.
Ohida, popularly known as Anwar, who was killed alongside many members of the terrorist organisation by the security forces, was said to be strategizing on how to attack some parts of the Southern region of the country soon.
The killed commander, was said to have masterminded several attacks in different parts of the country including attack on Kuje Correctional Centre, Abuja on July 11, 2022 before he met his waterloo.
Checks by Daily Trust showed that the eliminated ISWAP leader previously served as deputy to ISWAP Central Nigeria leader Abu Ikrimah, also known as Abu Uwais before he (Ikrimah) was arrested in 2023.
Sources revealed that following Ikrimah’s arrest, Ohida assumed leadership of ISWAP activities across parts of North central and Southern parts of the country.
The killed ISWAP leader was said to have played a key role in the planning, coordination and execution of terrorist operations in the North Central and Southern part of the country.
According to security sources, Ohida planned and executed the 31st December 2025 invasion of Ipele Divisional Police Station, Owo, Ondo State.
During the attack, the terrorists carted away AK-47 rifles before bringing down the station with an explosive.
 
Nigerians laud military’s efforts
Reacting to the terrorist commander’s killing, a farmer, Aliyu Garba, said Nigerians should thank God for clearing the terrorists’ commanders one after the other.
He said, “The killing of terrorist commanders by the troops deserve commendation. If the military can sustain the tempo, we will win this ‘war’.
“It is time Nigerians support the military because they are doing wonderfully well. It is a tedious job they are doing. May God continue to be with them”.
Also speaking on the terrorist killing, a retired police officer explained that Ohida’s plan was to attack civilians during the festive period and ultimately disrupt the 2027 general elections.
“Ohida’s elimination, which came a few months after the killing of ISIS leader Abu Bilal al-Munik, is a very big blow to ISWAP’s efforts to expand its operational presence in Nigeria, and underscores the growing efficiency of our security services,” he said.
On her part, Hajiya Salamatu Abdullahi, called on women to always pray for members of the armed forces to succeed in the ongoing fight against terrorism.
She said she was always happy anytime she hears that the terrorist commander is eliminated, saying Nigeria will be great again if their logistics network is disrupted.
 
Katsina traditional rulers praise military for foiling fresh abduction
In a related development, traditional rulers in Katsina State have commended the military and other agencies for foiling another mass abduction attempt in Bakori Local Government Area of the state.
The traditional rulers praised the troops for their timely response and intelligence-led operation that led to the rescue of 18 captives, including women and children, before suspected armed bandits could carry out the attack.
The incident occurred in Unguwan Hudu village, Kakumi Ward, after security operatives reportedly received intelligence on the movement of the suspected attackers and moved to block their route.
The commendation came less than two weeks after security forces reportedly foiled another mass abduction attempt in Gidan Iyado, also in Kakumi Ward, where the Katsina State Government said 18 bandits were killed during a joint operation involving the military, DSS and Community Watch Corps.
One of the district heads in Bakori said the continued collaboration among security agencies, traditional institutions and local communities had helped prevent attacks on farming settlements in the area.
“We thank the Almighty Allah for the continued collaboration among the security agencies, traditional institutions and local communities.
“This has helped to stop criminal elements from attacking farming communities in our domain,” he said.
Another traditional ruler said the suspected attackers, allegedly led by a bandit identified as Rabiu, were forced to flee after security operatives intercepted their route.
He said the fleeing suspects abandoned 18 captives, comprising 14 females and four males, including children and toddlers.
The traditional ruler also disclosed that blood traces found along the escape route suggested that some of the fleeing bandits may have sustained gunshot injuries, although this could not be independently confirmed.
He added that one of the rescued victims, 14-year-old Zainab Ashiru, sustained a gunshot wound and was receiving treatment at General Hospital, Bakori.
The traditional rulers said the latest success demonstrated the importance of timely intelligence and strong cooperation between formal security agencies and community-based security groups.
The traditional rulers expressed optimism that sustained collaboration would further strengthen efforts to protect farming communities and disrupt criminal networks operating across Katsina State.
 
Troops repel terrorists’ attack along Kwanar Isa-Shinkafi Road
Meanwhile, troops of the Nigerian Army have repelled terrorist activity along the Kwanar Isa–Shinkafi road in Isa Local Government Area of Sokoto State
The incident occurred at about 10:35 a.m. on September 29, when troops of 26 Battalion, Forward Operating Base Isa, responded to reports of terrorist activity along the major route.
The troops engaged the terrorists, forcing them to withdraw from the area.
Following the encounter, the soldiers sustained patrols and dominated the area to prevent the terrorists from regrouping and posing further threats to motorists and communities along the axis.
Security operations remain ongoing as the troops continue efforts to deny criminal elements freedom of movement and strengthen security across the area.
 
Stay fit, CDS tells military personnel
In the same vein, the CDS General Oluyede urged personnel of the Armed Forces of Nigeria to maintain high standards of physical, mental and emotional fitness to effectively meet the demands of military service.
General Oluyede gave the charge at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Chief of Defence Staff Independence Day Military Badminton Championship, organised to commemorate Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary.
He was represented by the Chief of Defence Administration, Rear Admiral GJ Kachim.
The CDS said fit and resilient personnel remain essential to effective service delivery, particularly amid evolving security challenges confronting the nation.
He stressed that operational effectiveness depends not only on professional competence, but also on the physical and mental preparedness of personnel to respond to demanding operational environments.
He noted that sports play an important role in developing resilience, discipline, concentration, perseverance and teamwork, while also strengthening camaraderie among personnel of the various Services.
According to him, participation in sporting activities helps personnel develop endurance, mental alertness and team spirit required to perform effectively under pressure.
General Oluyede added that the championship provided an avenue for military athletes to compete in a healthy and disciplined environment, build stronger inter-Service relationships and promote sports as a means of enhancing operational readiness, personal wellbeing and professional development.
The championship featured players from the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy and Nigerian Air Force, providing a platform for healthy competition, talent development and greater interaction among personnel.

items.content:
The Zamfara chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on Governor Dauda Lawal to account for the N20 billion projects executed in each of the Local Government Areas of the state.
This is contained in a statement issued in Gusau by the State ADC Chairman, Kabiru Garba.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that Gov. Lawal recently said his administration had executed over N20 billion worth of projects in each of the 14 Local Government Areas of the state.
“The Zamfara chapter of the ADC is demanding that the State Government provide a comprehensive and verifiable account of capital projects executed across the 14 Local Government Areas of the state since the commencement of the present administration.
“As citizens of Zamfara and stakeholders in the political development of our dear state, we believe that government must be accountable to the people. Public resources belong to the people, and citizens have the right to know how such resources are being utilised and what tangible benefits they are receiving from government expenditure.
“The ADC carefully listened to the governor’s recent statement regarding the administration’s investment of more than N20 billion in capital projects in each Local Government Area,” Garba said.
According to him, if the figure is accurate, it represents a very significant public investment and deserves to be properly documented and explained to the people of Zamfara.
“Therefore, on behalf of the ADC Zamfara chapter, I respectfully challenge the government to provide the people with a clear breakdown of these investments,” he urged.
Reacting to the development, the Director-General, Media and Communications to the Zamfara Government, Malam Nuhu Anka, said the governor’s statement was clear and well understood.
Anka said the governor’s claim of spending N20 billion in each of the 14 LGAs was accurate considering the ongoing infrastructural projects, including road networks, education and healthcare across the local government areas.
“When you look at government spending on the security sector on a daily basis, on agriculture and empowerment projects in each of the 14 LGAs, you will understand the statement made by Gov. Dauda Lawal in this matter.”
The director-general described the ADC’s demand for an explanation as politically motivated.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
A 50-year-old murder suspect, Bethlehem Nwanlia, reportedly slumped and died shortly after proceedings began at the Bayelsa State High Court in Yenagoa on Tuesday.
Nwanlia was standing trial alongside two other defendants over alleged conspiracy, kidnapping and multiple murder when the incident occurred at Court 11.
He reportedly collapsed in the court’s holding area shortly after Justice Amadise Michael Ekadi adjourned judgment in the case to October 27, 2026.
According to people who witnessed the incident, Nwanlia suddenly clutched his chest before collapsing.
Officers of the Nigerian Correctional Service, police personnel and lawyers reportedly attempted to revive him, but their efforts were unsuccessful.
A medical personnel was subsequently called to examine him, after which his body was taken to a hospital for further confirmation.
The Bayelsa State Judiciary’s Public Relations Officer, Mr Enoch Okunobo, confirmed the incident to newsmen on Tuesday evening.
He said the deceased’s body had been deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) mortuary.
“Somebody collapsed and died today. He was a murder suspect, who had been coming to court. His corpse has been deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC),” Okunobo said.
Nwanlia and the two other defendants were facing allegations linked to the 2022 killing of three people in Kalaba community, Yenagoa Local Government Area of the state.
The allegations against the defendants had not been finally determined by the court before Nwanlia’s death.
Reports also indicated that the deceased had experienced health complications while in custody.
However, authorities had yet to establish the cause of his death as of the time of filing the report.
The incident reportedly caused confusion among court officials, lawyers, security personnel and others present at the court premises.
When contacted, the Bayelsa State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Musa Mohammed, said he was not aware of the incident.
Mohammed, however, promised to make inquiries and revert, but had yet to do so as of the time of filing the report.

items.author: Hamisu Kabir Matazu
items.content:
The political landscape of Borno State has been thrown into turmoil following the decision of the factional state leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) headed by Dr. Muhammad Khala to declare Hon. Muhammad Attom Magira as the party’s gubernatorial candidate for the 2027 general elections.
The development comes on the heels of a legal victory at the Court of Appeal.
In the judgment for case No: CA/ABJ/CV/608/2026—delivered by Justice Okon Efreti Abang—the appellate court ruled in favor of the appellant, setting aside the actions of the Senator David Mark-led national faction regarding the status of state executives.
The legal battle stems from a prior dispute where the tenure of the old state chairmen and executives was allegedly terminated prematurely.
Aggrieved leaders challenged the decision at the Federal High Court in Abuja, which ruled in their favor.
The David Mark-led faction appealed the verdict, but the Court of Appeal reaffirmed the lower court’s position and slammed a N10 million fine against the appellants.
Riding on the back of this judgment, Dr. Khala’s faction has thrown its weight behind Magira.
According to Magira’s legal team, he purchased his nomination and expression of interest forms and participated in primaries backed by the Dr. Khala-led state structure, emerging as the legitimate candidate based on the appellate court’s interpretation.
However, the faction loyal to Senator David Mark has vehemently rejected Magira’s candidacy.
Speaking to journalists, the acting chairman of the ADC in Borno State, Hon. Bukar Kolo, dismissed Magira’s emergence as “laughable, null, and void.”
Kolo argued that the Court of Appeal judgment did not automatically translate to candidate selection, noting that the matter is already before the Supreme Court.
According to Kolo, the legitimate primaries that produced Hon. Babagana Buhari as the gubernatorial candidate were duly conducted by the national leadership under Senator Mark in compliance with the Electoral Act.
He emphasized that state executives lack the constitutional power to conduct primaries, a mandate strictly reserved for national leadership in conjunction with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).
“I wonder how Muhammad Attom Magira, who participated in the last primaries and came third, would be declared a candidate after the fact,” Kolo stated, challenging Magira and his legal team to produce court or INEC documentation recognizing him as the candidate.
Countering Kolo’s claims, Attom Magira expressed profound satisfaction with the appellate court’s decision and thanked Dr. Khala’s faction for re-endorsing him.
Speaking in Maiduguri on Tuesday, Magira challenged Kolo to provide evidence of his legitimacy as the acting state chairman. Expressing his readiness to lead the party into the 2027 polls, Magira urged the people of Borno State to rally behind his mandate to usher in positive change.
The acclaimed candidate rolled out an ambitious manifesto, promising to prioritize security, healthcare, education, agriculture, poverty alleviation, job creation, women and youth empowerment, and infrastructure across the 27 local government areas of the state.
“If given the mandate, I will operate an open-door policy, introduce tax waivers for Keke Napep riders, and implement a minimum wage of N100,000 for civil servants across the state,” Magira pledged.
As the legal battles march toward the Supreme Court, the battle for the soul of the Borno ADC and the 2027 gubernatorial ticket promises to remain a fiercely contested political soap opera.

MPs voted to replace Agila Saleh with Al-Salhin Abdelnabi al-Obeidi, the parliament’s spokesman announced on X.
Libya has been beset by violence and instability since the overthrow of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.
It remains divided between the UN-recognised government in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah, and a rival administration in the east backed by military commander Haftar.
Haftar’s camp relies in particular on the parliament, which sits in the eastern city of Benghazi under their control.
Saleh, 82, has long been considered a staunch ally of the Haftar clan, but he appeared to be weakened as Haftar’s sons, in particular Saddam Haftar, consolidated their positions.
Emadeddin Badi, an analyst at the London-based Chatham House, said: “Agila Saleh appears to be the latest casualty of Saddam Haftar’s drive to centralize decision-making in eastern Libya and bulldoze his way into a political role.”
His removal comes as a US initiative aimed at reviving the political process and unifying Libya’s institutions is under discussion.

By Luminous Jannamike
ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has questioned the implementation of defence budgets for the maintenance of Nigerian Air Force aircraft following Monday’s crash of an ATR-42 aircraft at Igbokoda, Ondo State.
The opposition party said the tragedy should not only prompt investigations into the immediate cause of the crash but also renewed scrutiny of how much money meant to keep military aircraft operational is actually released and spent.
In a statement released in Abuja on Tuesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the crash as tragic and unfortunate and expressed condolences to the families of the victims.
The party said official figures showed that as of December 2025, only N4.5 billion, representing about 13.98 per cent of the N34.71 billion budgeted for the maintenance of Nigerian Air Force aircraft, had been released.
By contrast, it said N20.74 billion was allocated for the maintenance of the Presidential Air Fleet, with N20.27 billion, representing 97.76 per cent, released within the same period.
“Put simply, while the fleet that serves a handful of people in power got almost every kobo it asked for, the fleet that serves and protects 200 million Nigerians was left with crumbs,” the ADC said.
The party stressed that it did not want to prejudice the ongoing investigation into the crash but said the incident provided another opportunity to examine the funding and maintenance of military equipment.
“While we do not intend to prejudice ongoing investigations into the cause of this tragic crash, we believe that this sad moment also provides an opportunity to raise, yet again, questions about the non-implementation of the defence budget and the perennial neglect of military equipment,” it said.
The ADC said the safety of military personnel should receive the same level of attention as the safety of political leaders.
“The safety of the President matters. But what also matters is the safety of the pilots and airmen who put their lives on the line in defence of the country. Patriotism does not replace spare parts, and condolence messages do not take the place of accountability,” the party maintained.
The party therefore called for the crash investigation to go beyond determining the immediate cause of the accident to examining the maintenance of defence equipment, particularly the Nigerian Air Force fleet.
It also demanded an audit of maintenance expenditure and budgetary releases to determine whether funds appropriated for the upkeep of military aircraft were released and properly utilised.
