items.content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has announced a massive drop in the country’s dependence on crude revenues, signaling what government said was a decisive shift toward a diversified economy.
He noted that his administration has built a diversified, high-growth economy unlocking the potential of agriculture, manufacturing, and the digital and creative industries to shift the landscape away from single-sector dependence.
Speaking on Tuesday in Abuja during the fifth anniversary of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), the President who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, explained that through the joint effort of security agencies, operators, host communities, and the Commission, oil production is “now steadier and stronger”.
As a result, he declared that investors who once abandoned Nigeria in search of better deals were now returning, a development he said has ranked the country first among Africa’s leading destinations for upstream investment for two years running.
Announcing a drop in oil revenue dependence, President Tinubu said, “These gains matter well beyond the oil and gas industry. Under the Renewed Hope Agenda, we are building a diversified economy in which agriculture, manufacturing, the digital and creative industries all play their part.
“We have already reduced our dependence on oil revenue, and we intend to go further. But a diversified economy still needs energy, foreign exchange and investment, and that is where this sector serves the nation. Our gas can power homes and factories. Petroleum earnings support a stable naira and help fund the Federation.”
He stated that a well-run upstream industry is capable of creating jobs for Nigerian engineers, fabricators, and service companies, as his administration plans to use petroleum resources to build the wider economy, rather than depend on them.
The Nigerian leader promised to “pursue an energy transition that is just and suited to Nigeria’s needs,” declaring that this is the decade of Gas.
The President also vowed that his administration will not rest on its oars until Nigeria becomes the destination of choice for hydrocarbon investment, maintaining that in the next phase, the government will insist on compliance and accountability.
“Operators who enjoy incentives must deliver on their commitments to work programmes, local content, the environment and host communities, and the Commission must also account publicly for its own performance. We will uphold the rule of law and the sanctity of contracts, so that disputes are fewer and, where they arise, are resolved quickly and fairly,” he stated.
On his part, Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Oil, Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, said NUPRC has recorded significant achievements in the last five years, attributing the progress to the leadership and reform agenda of the Tinubu administration.
According to him, Nigeria, with crude oil production of about 1.7 million barrels per day and over 37 billion barrels of oil reserves, still requires increased investment, additional licensing rounds, and intensified exploration to unlock the full potential of the nation’s petroleum resources.
The Minister urged the Commission to build on its successes by adopting decisive regulatory measures and eliminating bureaucratic bottlenecks that might discourage investment.
Also speaking, the Chairman of the NUPRC Governing Board, Senator Magnus Abe, said the creation of the Commission under the PIA was evidence that Nigeria was making progress in reforming the oil and gas sector.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed his continued availability for Portugal after explaining his decision to leave the national team camp and accusing head coach Jorge Jesus of breaking an agreement over his playing time.
The 41-year-old Al Nassr forward had raised questions about his international future following his departure from the squad, but said he remained committed to representing Portugal.
“If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team,” Ronaldo said in a statement shared with Reuters.
Ronaldo also apologised to his teammates and the Portuguese public for leaving the camp, adding that he would accept any disciplinary action imposed by the Portuguese Football Federation.
The forward left the squad after remaining an unused substitute during Portugal’s 2-1 away victory over Norway in the Nations League on September 27.
According to Ronaldo, he and Jesus had previously agreed that he would miss the Norway and Denmark matches as part of a plan to manage his fitness.
However, Ronaldo said the coach changed the arrangement on the day of the Norway match and told him he would play for 30 minutes.
“Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from halftime onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn’t called on,” he said.
“The manager had broken his word to me.”
Ronaldo said it was the second time he believed Jesus had failed to honour an understanding between them and that the coach’s public comments did not correspond with their private discussion.
“It was the second time he had broken his word to me. I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises,” he said.
Jesus, however, denied after Portugal’s victory over Norway that he had reached such an agreement with Ronaldo, while leaving the door open for the veteran forward to return to the national team.
Ronaldo also rejected suggestions that he had interfered with tactical or technical decisions during his international career.
“Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of career,” he said.
“I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.”
Addressing speculation about a possible farewell to international football, Ronaldo said he expected to have one or more farewell matches in the future but remained focused on competing for Portugal.
“I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that. But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competing,” he said.
Ronaldo, Portugal’s record goalscorer and most-capped player, has scored 146 goals in 234 international appearances.
He also recalled remaining with the Portugal squad following the death of his father during an international camp, saying his commitment to the national team had remained strong throughout his career.
The dispute between Ronaldo and Jesus has cast uncertainty over the forward’s immediate international involvement, but his latest statement makes clear that he intends to remain available for Portugal, subject to his fitness and any disciplinary sanction.

Kenya as future hosts of the World Athletics Championship must strive for  zero tolerance for drugs in sport, the World Anti Doping Agency (WADA) boss said on Tuesday.
Despite a long-running doping crisis, Kenya were last month awarded the 2029 World Athletics Championships, the first time the event will be held in Africa.
“Kenya proudly calls itself the Home of Champions. But for that home to remain respected and credible, it must also be clean,” WADA chief Witold Banka said at the end of a three-day visit to the east African country.
“That is why Kenya needs a strong culture of clean sport, zero tolerance for doping, and a more determined approach to preventing and fighting doping.
“Kenya is a great sporting nation full of great athletes and you become, the more important area of sport when it comes to organising major sporting events.
“It’s a big honour for you but it’s a bigger responsibility as well and brings pressure and big requirements from our side as well”, Banka added.
Banka said that joint cooperation with Kenyan authorities would help lay the foundations for a cleaner sport.
“WADA or ADAK (Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya) alone cannot achieve its vision if we do not cooperate with those who have the power to go against those who are producing, smuggling and trafficking dangerous steroids to your athletes,” he said.
“We’ve found a common understanding and we are on the same track and there’s a clear goal within Kenya for zero tolerance for doping policy and it has to be established immediately with joint actions and a more aggressive approach to those who are destroying the image of the country and the reputation of the athletes.”
More than 140 Kenyan athletes, mainly long-distance runners, have been suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) since 2017.

items.content:
As drums pounded and chants rang out, 16-year-old Yanis, flanked by a knot of friends, rattled off why he had joined tens of thousands surging through the streets of Paris on Tuesday to demand better learning conditions.
“There are no toilets, no toilet paper, everything is broken,” he said, his schoolmates nodding and chiming in.
“We go to class from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm with a one-hour break.”
“There are 36 of us in class. We can’t study,” the teenager from the northern Paris suburb of Sarcelles told AFP, calling conditions at his high school “unacceptable”.
He was among some 56,000 people who poured onto the streets of Paris on Tuesday as part of a protest movement that began in late September.
Across France, students and teachers have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds, protesting against teacher shortages, overloaded timetables, ill-equipped classrooms and buildings not designed to cope with rising temperatures.
On Tuesday, protesters flooded into the Place de la Republique in central Paris, hoisting signs.
“2026 is the new 1789,” declared one, a nod to the French Revolution.
Another placard took the form of an oversized middle finger.
The scent of merguez sausages — a fixture of French demonstrations — drifted through the square.
Demonstrators danced and clapped to pounding drums, breaking into chants calling for President Emmanuel Macron to resign and denouncing the far right ahead of presidential elections next year.
– ‘I don’t have a future’ –
But beneath the festive atmosphere, some of the young protesters struck a bleaker note.
Fidele, 15, who had come with Yanis, dreamt of becoming a lawyer but said conditions at his school had left him pessimistic about whether he could get there.
“When I see the system, I tell myself that I don’t have a future” in this country, he said.
Nearby, 16-year-old Noham had his sights set on becoming a computer engineer, but worried that overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages were putting that ambition out of reach.
“Without access to an education, I can’t have the job I dream of,” he said. “It’s an enormous amount of stress.”
Nadine Zilliacus, an educator for 20 years, said she had seen the same disillusionment take hold among even younger pupils, who increasingly expressed a “really dark” view of what lies ahead.
“We tell them you have to prepare for the future with a job you like,” she said.
“Even in middle school they tell us: ‘There’s no point, anyway we won’t have jobs’.”
– ‘We’re neglected’ –
Further along the route, the crowd pressed towards the march’s endpoint, clapping and chanting before voices swelled into a rendition of the Marseillaise, France’s national anthem.
From a balcony overhead, a silver-haired woman leaned out to encourage the protesters below.
Spotting her, the crowd turned their faces upwards and broke into chants of “Mamie! Mamie!” — an affectionate French term for grandmother.
Among those making their way through the crowd was Ami, 17, who had travelled into Paris with a group of friends to protest against conditions at her high school in the city’s suburbs.
“Compared with schools in central Paris, we’re neglected,” she said.
As the march reached the Nation roundabout, the festive mood began to shift, with police carrying riot shields barring the route and some protesters throwing stones at the officers.
As Ami and her friends drew closer, the boom of tear gas canisters fired by police cut through the singing.
The girls screamed and stopped in their tracks, unsure whether to keep moving forward.
Nearby, a middle-aged woman had mascara streaking down her face after being caught in the tear gas, while a young man comforted her.
Ami said she did not understand the police response.
“We’re just protesting, we’re singing, and that’s all,” she said, adding that she was scared.
After a day of drums, chants and dancing through the capital, she was ready to leave.
“We just want to go home,” she said.
ekf/ah/gv

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
The Benue State Government and the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) have sharply disagreed over the planned removal of unauthorised billboards across the state, with the PDP alleging the exercise was politically motivated and targeted opposition campaign materials ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
The state government, through the Benue State Signage and Advertisement Agency, Benue State Internal Revenue Service, BIRS, and the Urban Development Board, had on Tuesday issued a two-week ultimatum to owners and operators of unauthorised billboards to regularise them or face removal.
The directive, contained in a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said enforcement would commence on October 20, 2026, with the removal of every billboard that had not been regularised.
But the PDP, through its State Publicity Secretary, Bright Antyo, described the directive as “a desperate, anti-democratic and politically motivated attempt to cripple opposition campaigns ahead of the 2027 governorship election.”
The party urged the state government to abandon what it described as an attempt to intimidate political opponents and monopolise public spaces.
Explaining the government’s position, Iorpev said the relevant agencies had “observed with concern the arbitrary erection of billboards across the State by individuals, groups and political parties.”
According to him, “These structures have been put up without a permit from the Signage and Advertisement Agency, without clearance from the Urban Development Board, and without payment of the prescribed fees.”
“This practice breaches the law. It deprives the State of legitimate revenue, endangers public safety, and undermines the orderly development of our towns and cities,” he added.
The government, however, said it was giving billboard owners the opportunity to comply rather than immediately commence enforcement.
Iorpev explained that the authorities were “prepared to assume that many of those responsible acted out of ignorance of the law and not out of deliberate defiance. For this reason, the Agencies are giving everyone who has erected a billboard a grace period of two weeks, beginning today, Tuesday, 6th October 2026,” he said.
The commissioner urged owners and operators of unauthorised billboards to use the period to “retrace their steps and do the right thing” by approaching the Benue State Signage and Advertisement Agency to begin the permit process, obtain clearance from the Urban Development Board, and pay all required fees.
He warned that the deadline would not be extended saying “Let it be clear that there will not be another notice before enforcement which will commence on Tuesday, 20th October 2026. The enforcement teams are expected to begin removing every billboard that has not been regularised from the set date.
Billboards taken down will be at the owners’ cost, and no further notice will be given.
“Anyone who ignores this window should expect no sympathy and no exception, regardless of status, affiliation or political party. We are a law-abiding people, and we believe every Benue citizen wants to do the right thing. This grace period is a sign of the Government’s goodwill and of its preference for compliance over confrontation. We urge all concerned to make use of it,” the commissioner stated.
However, the PDP rejected the government’s explanation, arguing that the timing of the directive suggested a political motive.
In its reaction signed by Antyo, the opposition party said it had “noted with alarm the directive issued by the Benue State Government threatening to commence the removal of billboards and posters across the state from October 20, 2026.”
The PDP said it “condemns this action in the strongest possible terms” and described it as “a desperate, anti-democratic and politically motivated attempt to cripple opposition campaigns ahead of the 2027 governorship election.”
According to the party, opposition billboards carrying “messages of hope, security, economic revival and political change” had recently appeared in major towns and communities across the state.
It alleged that rather than address issues raised by residents, Governor Hyacinth Alia’s administration was attempting to intimidate political opponents.
“The sudden two-week ultimatum issued by the government is not a coincidence. It bears all the markings of a calculated operation aimed at clearing public spaces of opposition campaign materials and restricting the visibility of alternative political voices as the 2027 election approaches,” the PDP alleged.
The party questioned the timing and manner of the government’s proposed enforcement saying, “If the Alia administration was genuinely interested in enforcing signage laws, why did it wait until now?
“Why were these regulations not vigorously enforced before opposition campaigns began gaining traction? Why has the government suddenly become eager to dismantle structures carrying messages that challenge its record?” the PDP asked.
The PDP claimed the directive targeted political opponents, alleging that the administration was unsettled by what it described as growing dissatisfaction with the government and increasing acceptance of alternative political options ahead of the 2027 election.
The party further alleged that government institutions could be deployed against political opponents, describing the directive as “draconian, vindictive and dangerous for democracy.”
It said: “It creates the impression that government agencies are being mobilised, not for public service, but as instruments of political warfare against perceived opponents.”
The opposition party also warned the governor against what it described as an attempt to restrict political competition.
“Benue State is not a monarchy, and Governor Alia is not the only candidate who will participate in the 2027 election.
The people have a constitutional right to hear different voices, evaluate competing visions and make informed choices at the ballot box.”
The PDP argued that political contests should be determined by public confidence and performance, not by the visibility or removal of campaign materials.
“We remind the Governor that democracy is not sustained by pulling down opponents’ billboards and posters. Democracy is sustained by winning the trust of the people through good governance, accountability, transparency and tangible results.”
The party also used the controversy to raise several issues it said were confronting the state, including insecurity, the condition of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), abandoned projects, debt, infrastructure and the economic situation.
“Today, Benue people are asking hard questions about insecurity, the plight of IDPs abandoned projects, mounting debt, neglect of 22 local governments, deteriorating rural infrastructure and the worsening economic situation. Destroying opposition campaign materials will not make these questions disappear,” the PDP said.
The party therefore warned that “any selective removal of opposition campaign materials under the guise of enforcement will be interpreted as a direct attack on democratic freedoms and a dangerous abuse of state institutions for partisan purposes.”
It called on civil society organisations, election observers, the media, security agencies and other stakeholders to monitor the implementation of the directive.
“We call on civil society organisations, election observers, the media, security agencies and all defenders of democracy to closely monitor the excesses of Governor Alia and his administration and ensure that no government agency is used as a tool for political persecution,” the party said.
The PDP urged the state government to reverse course, saying, “The Governor must abandon this path of political intolerance. Any attempt to intimidate opponents, monopolise public space and create the illusion of an unchallenged political landscape will fail because democracy belongs to the people, not to those temporarily entrusted with power.
“Benue belongs to all the people. The democratic space belongs to everyone. No government has the right to reserve it for itself,” it stated.

items.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye
Rival Premier League clubs are calling for Manchester City to face a range of punishments, including title stripping and transfer bans, if the club’s appeal against its financial breaches verdict fails, according to the BBC.
An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.
City have appealed against the verdict.
However, sources told BBC Sport that a number of Premier League clubs want any eventual sanctions to cover both the period in which the breaches occurred and City’s future participation in the competition.
There is also a feeling in at least four Premier League boardrooms that a single points deduction resulting in relegation to the Championship would not be sufficient punishment given the scale of the findings.
One senior club source said City should be stripped of the titles they won during the period covered by the verdict.
The source added that there was “no great rush” among clubs to redistribute the trophies, but rather to take the honours away and leave them vacant.
The source warned that the credibility of the Premier League would be undermined if City were allowed to retain the eight major trophies they won during the period in which they were found guilty of the breaches.
However, BBC Sport said it had previously been told there was little appetite among some other clubs for City to be stripped of their titles, highlighting the differing views across the league.
On future sanctions, some Premier League figures believe a points deduction imposed in only one season would amount to a “bump in the road” for City, given the likelihood of the club returning to the top flight at the first opportunity.
As a result, some clubs believe any points deduction should be spread over multiple seasons.
There is also support in some quarters for transfer bans covering several windows, which could make it harder for City to rebuild and return to the Premier League quickly if they are relegated.
One club source described it as “bizarre, almost obtuse” if City were allowed to operate in the January transfer window while the process remained ongoing and sanctions had yet to be imposed.
Another proposal being discussed is a “tariff-based system”, under which City’s past league finishing positions could be adjusted through a points deduction.
Rival clubs could then receive compensation from City based on where they would have finished compared with their actual positions.
City have consistently maintained their innocence and are challenging the independent commission’s findings through an appeal.
Meanwhile, BBC Sport understands City manager Enzo Maresca will address his players collectively after they return from international duty on Thursday, ahead of Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Liverpool at Anfield.
The match will be City’s first since the verdict became public.
Merseyside Police said it had received queries about the fixture and confirmed it would have “an appropriate policing operation in place on the day”.
Liverpool sources told BBC Sport the club was treating the fixture as “business as usual”, with no additional measures planned.
One source said supporters had “the right to express their feelings” but hoped they would not overstep the mark.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja
The House of Representatives Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has issued a seven-day final summons to officials of the six Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Councils over outstanding audit queries involving about N100 billion.
The committee’s action followed the failure of the six Area Council chairmen to honour its invitation to appear and respond to financial queries contained in the Auditor-General’s reports.
The affected councils are Abaji, Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC), Bwari, Gwagwalada, Kuje and Kwali.
The chairmen had requested September 22, 2026, as the date for their appearance, but failed to attend the sitting or send representatives.
Consequently, the committee summoned the Directors of Personnel Management and Finance, as well as Heads of Audit of the six councils, to appear before it on October 14, 2026, or face sanctions in line with relevant service rules.
Chairman of the PAC, Rep. Bamidele Salam, disclosed this while speaking with journalists in Abuja on Tuesday.
Salam said the committee had repeatedly invited the councils to provide explanations and supporting documents needed to resolve the audit queries.
“The last date of appearance of the Abuja Area Councils was September 22, 2026, which was a date they requested for and which was graciously granted by the committee. Yet, they failed to appear or send in any representation.
“The committee has therefore decided to issue summons to the Directors of Personnel Management and Finance of these local governments, including their Heads of Audit, to appear without fail on Wednesday, October 14, failure of which they will be made to bear consequences according to service rules,” he said.
The queries are contained in the Annual Audit Report of the Auditor-General for the Six FCT Area Councils for the year ended December 31, 2021.
According to the report, the councils had outstanding liabilities of about N7.65 billion arising from unremitted pension deductions, Pay As You Earn (PAYE), Value Added Tax (VAT), withholding tax and unpaid obligations to contractors.
AMAC accounted for the highest liability at N2.19 billion, followed by Bwari with N1.49 billion and Kwali with N1.46 billion.
Gwagwalada had N1.01 billion in outstanding liabilities, while Kuje and Abaji had N892.2 million and N593.8 million respectively.
The Auditor-General said the liabilities were due for remittance to the Nigeria Revenue Service, FCT Inland Revenue Service, Pension Fund Administrators and contractors.
The report also raised concerns over the councils’ management of fixed assets, particularly the failure to properly maintain and update asset registers.
Gwagwalada was specifically queried over non-current assets valued at N336 million, whose ledger records, according to the report, were not properly maintained and updated.
The Auditor-General warned that the poor record-keeping could create room for assets to be lost without being traced, adding that the lapse was common among the FCT Area Councils.
The PAC is also demanding explanations and supporting documents on N24.87 billion spent by the six councils on personnel, overheads and capital expenditure in 2021.
AMAC accounted for N5.03 billion, Gwagwalada N4.66 billion, Kuje N3.85 billion, Kwali N3.84 billion, Bwari N3.74 billion and Abaji N3.71 billion.
Salam disclosed that the committee had uncovered additional concerns in the audit reports for 2022 and part of 2023, including alleged understatement of Internally Generated Revenue, unauthorised disposal of assets, non-disclosure of statutory revenue and failure to remit withholding tax.
He also said the councils had failed to audit and submit their financial accounts for 2023, 2024 and 2025, contrary to statutory requirements.
The lawmaker said the committee would insist on transparency and accountability in the management of public resources, stressing that officials found culpable would be held responsible in accordance with the law.
The post N100bn Audit Query: Reps give FCT area councils seven-day final ultimatum appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye
UEFA is monitoring Manchester City’s financial-rule case and will wait until the end of the Premier League’s disciplinary process before considering any potential action against Manchester City, Sky Sports reports.
Manchester City were found guilty by an independent commission of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules between 2009 and 2018, including five charges relating to breaches of UEFA’s Financial Fair Play rules.
City have appealed the verdict and continue to deny any wrongdoing, insisting that they have a “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence” to support their position.
According to Sky Sports chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol, UEFA is monitoring developments and will wait until the Premier League disciplinary process is completed before deciding whether to take any potential action against City.
The independent commission found that City’s owners had put £830 million into the club, which was disguised as sponsorship income over nine seasons.
The commission also found City significantly breached both Premier League and UEFA spending limits and broke “well over 100” Premier League regulations.
UEFA previously took action against City over Financial Fair Play breaches.
In 2014, the club agreed a settlement with UEFA which included a £49 million fine, of which £32 million was suspended.
In 2020, UEFA found City guilty of breaching its Financial Fair Play rules, imposing a €30 million fine and a two-year ban from European competitions.
City appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which overturned the European competition ban, ruling that UEFA had not established that the club’s owners had disguised equity funding as sponsorship contributions. Other alleged breaches were found to be time-barred.
CAS subsequently reduced the fine to €10 million for City’s failure to cooperate with UEFA’s investigation.
UEFA’s statute of limitations for financial-rule breaches is five years, while the Premier League has no such limitation, according to Sky Sports.
The Premier League’s independent commission, which had access to evidence unavailable to UEFA during its investigation, found City guilty of serious financial breaches spanning nine seasons.
City lodged its appeal on October 1 and maintains that the commission’s decision contains “clear material errors, of law, principle and fact” and is “unsafe.”
Under the Premier League’s new appeal rules, the process is expected to be concluded within 12 weeks, although City could argue that the new rules should not apply because the case began before they were introduced.
Sky Sports reports that such an argument could potentially push the appeal process into 2027.

items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
A commercial driver, Igba Agenewe, has been killed by suspected armed men while three soldiers travelling in his vehicle were reportedly abducted along the Anyiin-Ayilamo road in Logo Local Government Area (LGA), of Benue State.
Agenewe, a member of the National Union of Road Transport Workers, NURTW, Wurukum branch, Anyiin section, was reportedly returning to Makurdi from Anyiin when the gunmen emerged from the bush and opened fire on his vehicle.
The incident, which occurred on Monday, has thrown members of the union and the deceased’s colleagues into mourning.
Agenewe, who operated from the Wurukum Park in Makurdi, had earlier driven his Sharon bus to Anyiin town with passengers.
According to a member of the union, Iorember Tser, the deceased was warned against returning to Makurdi through Ayilamo because of the worsening security situation on the route.
Tser said, “When he got to Anyiin, he wanted to return to Makurdi. Some drivers told him that the road was not safe because of the prolonged suspected herders-farmers crisis in Ayilamo, which is a 10-minute drive from Anyiin. He however, insisted on returning to Makurdi, saying, ‘I just passed through the road.’
It was gathered that Agenewe subsequently picked up three passengers said to be military personnel and headed towards Makurdi.
However, “when he passed a town called Akwana heading towards Ayilamo, unknown gunmen emerged from the bush and shot him. He died on the spot.
The three soldiers were abducted but later regained freedom and returned to Anyiin.”
He said the incident has heightened concerns about the safety of motorists and commuters using the Abinsi-Tyulen-Anyiin-Wukari road, particularly the Ayilamo axis, which has seen security challenges linked to the prolonged conflict in the area.
The owner of the Sharon bus, Mr Aondona Tyulen, described the killing of his driver as unfortunate and appealed to security agencies to apprehend the perpetrators.
Tyulen called on the authorities to intensify security operations in the area and ensure that those responsible for the killing were brought to justice.
The remains of Agenewe had, as of the time of filing this report, been deposited at the Ayilamo mortuary.
Efforts to obtain a reaction from the Benue State Police Command were unsuccessful, as the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, had not responded to enquiries on the incident as of press time.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
The convener of The Alternative movement, Segun Sowunmi, has said Peter Obi cannot successfully contest the 2027 presidential election alone, arguing that the contest requires a strong political structure.
Sowunmi stated this during an interview on News Central on Tuesday while responding to a question on whether he considered Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, a threat ahead of the 2027 election.
He said political actors must recognise the importance of alliances and political structures when preparing for a presidential contest.
“As for Peter, there are seasons and there are times you have to know you are not going to singularly run into an election that requires structure, and you are not going to pretend that you’re not smelling the coffee,” Sowunmi said.
He argued that Obi should also consider the political position of governors in the South-East and the benefits their states were receiving from the Federal Government.
“If you have five governors in your zone, which is the South-East zone, and all of them are saying, from what we can see, from the resources we’re getting, from the construction that is going on, from the integration, let’s keep it there. Maybe you are good to think it that way,” he said.
Sowunmi also cited the Federal Government’s infrastructure projects in the South-East, particularly the work of the Minister of Works, as a factor that could influence political calculations in the region.
“If you see your Minister of Works doing exceedingly more than anybody since the Civil War to return infrastructure to the South-East, you may say, ‘Okay, why not?” he said.
The former PDP chieftain, however, said nobody should be prevented from contesting an election, even where such a candidate may not have sufficient political structure to win.
“But nobody has the right to force anybody not to go into the field to lose an election,” he said.
Sowunmi also advocated political cooperation among regions, saying the South should collaborate while the incumbent completes his term, after which political power could rotate.
“Now that it’s in the South, let the South collaborate together, and let the man that is on the seat finish his term, and let it swing to the North then it will swing back, and there will be opportunities for this negotiation and recalibration,” he said.
He added that democracy required contestants, winners and losers, urging candidates who lose elections to accept the outcomes.
“Democracy needs somebody to lose. That’s why you need people to also contest elections. So the winner will win, and the losers will lose,” Sowunmi said.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
ABUJA – The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) has issued a public warning over the spread of fraudulent employment advertisements and forged appointment letters being used by scammers to deceive job seekers.
The warning was contained in a public notice issued by the Fund and circulated to regional and branch managers via a memorandum dated October 5, 2026, signed by Samaila Abdu, Esq., Executive Director, Administration.
According to the notice, the NSITF said it is not currently recruiting for any position and described employment advertisements circulating on social media, particularly Facebook, as fake
The Fund stated that the fraudulent advertisements reflect a growing trend of individuals and groups falsely claiming to represent the NSITF in recruitment exercises.
NSITF urged members of the public to disregard such advertisements and avoid making payments to anyone over purported employment opportunities.
The Fund emphasised that it neither charges fees for employment nor conducts recruitment through unofficial social media platforms or channels.
It added that any genuine employment opportunities would be announced through its official channels.
“Stay alert, stay safe,” the Fund urged, advising members of the public who encounter suspicious recruitment advertisements or requests to avoid responding and report them to the appropriate NSITF authorities.
As part of measures to protect the public and safeguard the integrity of its recruitment process, NSITF management has directed all Regional and Branch Managers to prominently display the public notice at strategic locations within their offices.
The directive covers reception areas, main entrances and exits, notice boards, SERVICOM desks and other conspicuous locations accessible to staff and members of the public.
The Fund said the notice should be displayed immediately and kept visible to ensure that members of the public are adequately informed and protected from fraudulent recruitment activities.
NSITF urged Nigerians, particularly job seekers, to exercise caution and verify every recruitment claim through the Fund’s official communication channels before taking any action.
The development comes amid growing concerns over fraudulent online recruitment schemes targeting unemployed Nigerians with promises of government jobs in exchange for money or personal information.
NSITF’s latest warning underscores the need for job seekers to remain vigilant, as legitimate public-sector recruitment does not require applicants to pay individuals or unofficial agents for employment.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
The Insurance Brokers Association of India (IBAI) has said that the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India’s (IRDAI) recently proposed norms could trigger a 60-70% revenue collapse across the insurance broking sector.
Addressing a press briefing, the industry body representatives also said that the insurance distribution sector, which employs over 83 Lakh people, could see the loss of up to 10 Lakh jobs lost as a result of the economic impact of the proposed policies.
This comes days after IRDAI proposed reintroducing product-wise commission caps for insurance distributors. The regulator also proposed tighter limits on insurers’ overall expenses over concerns related to disproportionate increases in commissions paid to distributors.
The industry body has also sought an extension of the deadline to submit feedback on the proposed norms to December-end from October 25 currently.
While noting that the association supports the regulator’s goal of making insurance more affordable and accessible, the IBAI representatives noted that the proposed sweeping changes threaten small businesses and MSMEs.
The resulting job losses could impact insurance awareness, policy renewals, assistance to policyholders, and penetration of insurance among underserved communities, the representatives added.
The brokers also countered IRDAI’s data that showed that general insurance premiums sourced through brokers had risen 37% whereas commission payouts zoomed 173% between FY23 and FY27. The industry body argued that the rise in commissions since FY23 largely reflected the reclassification of off-book marketing expenses following regularisation, and did not reflect inflationary pressures on insurance consumers.
The IBAI also claimed that the entire general insurance industry’s operating expenses averaged around 26.5% of gross premiums as against the mandated limit of 30%. Making its point, the representatives also claimed that policyholders received back ₹84.4 in non-life insurance claim payouts for every ₹100 of premium paid over a five-year period.
This is more than the global average of 72-75%, demonstrating the efficiency of the market in delivering value, the body’s representatives claimed.
The industry body said it was ready to work with IRDAI to address specific market anomalies, such as misselling or disproportionate remuneration. It has also submitted formal letters to the Prime Minister’s Office and the Finance Ministry on the matter.
Notably, the pushback comes as insurtech platforms continue to be up in arms against the proposed norms. Last week, Sanjib Jha, founder of insurtech startup Coverfox, said that the proposal could impact the viability of distributing insurance to rural and low-income borrowers.
Pune-based insurance broker Quickinsure has also trimmed more than 100 jobs in response to the proposal as its founder Anand Shrikhande projected that the industry would see more than 1 Lakh jobs affected due to the changing economics.
The news has also triggered a major sell-off in listed insurtech majors PB Fintech, which operates Policybazaar, and Turtlemint over fears that the IRDAI’s new policies would dent their core businesses.

items.author: Gargi Sarkar
items.content:
Enterprise software major ServiceNow is betting that its next leg of growth in India will come not just from digitisation of IT functions, but from enterprises putting AI to work across business processes, even as the rush to adopt the technology creates a parallel challenge around governance, security and identity.
At its World Forum in India on Tuesday, October 6, ServiceNow announced AI Workflow Factory and Autonomous Engineer, two products aimed at helping enterprises identify where AI can improve work and then build, run and extend AI-powered workflows across the organisation.
The launches come at a time when Indian enterprises are moving beyond AI experimentation, with CIOs increasingly looking at how to deploy the technology across customer experience, employee operations, software development and business processes.
For ServiceNow, that creates an opportunity to move beyond its traditional identity as an IT service management company and position itself as the layer through which enterprises orchestrate AI across their existing technology stack.
But the company is also betting that as AI becomes more deeply embedded into enterprises, security and governance will become inseparable from the adoption story.
ServiceNow’s India AI Push Moves Beyond Pilots
ServiceNow’s India strategy rests on three interconnected opportunities: domestic enterprises, global capability centres (GCCs) and its large technology partner ecosystem, ServiceNow India tech and business centre head Sumeet Mathur said in an interview with Inc42.
The company has been expanding beyond its traditional strength in IT service management, with ambitions to become an “enterprise operating system” spanning IT, HR, customer service, finance, supply chain, legal and workplace operations.
AI is now becoming the connective tissue across these functions. The company is seeing a growing willingness among Indian CIOs and CISOs to explore disruptive AI use cases rather than simply run small pilots.
“The willingness is very high, and once you start to open your mind that I want to use this piece of technology in 10 different ways, then of course the problems are very visible,” Mathur said.
That appetite, however, is running ahead of the governance structures needed to deploy AI safely. A ServiceNow AI maturity assessment cited by the company found that only 22% of Indian enterprises have AI testing, auditing and risk-assessment processes in place.
Amit Zavery, president, COO and chief product officer at ServiceNow, said on the sidelines of the event that governance cannot become an excuse for delaying AI adoption but needs to be built into the process early.
“It just slows you down enough to run faster later. If you’re going to run faster without any kind of brakes around it, it will crash,” Zavery said.
The distinction is becoming increasingly important as enterprises move from individual AI experiments to multiple deployments across an organisation. The question is no longer simply whether an AI application works, but whether it can be governed, monitored and scaled without creating new operational or security risks.
From IT Workflows To An Enterprise Operating System
ServiceNow’s pitch is that enterprises do not need another standalone AI application. They need a layer that can connect AI models, existing applications, data and workflows.
AI Workflow Factory is designed to help enterprises identify opportunities where AI can improve workflows and then build and operate those workflows. Autonomous Engineer, meanwhile, brings more autonomous capabilities into software development, including planning, building and testing.
The proposition addresses one of the biggest problems emerging as companies scale AI: fragmentation. Enterprises building AI applications often have to stitch together different models, data sources, applications and workflows. They also have to manage changes when models are updated or prompts and underlying systems change.
AI Workflow Factory brings more of that lifecycle onto a common platform, including building, deployment, governance and ongoing management.
The broader ambition is to make ServiceNow the operating layer through which enterprises can introduce AI into existing business processes without having to rip out their existing technology infrastructure. This is also where ServiceNow believes it can differentiate itself from hyperscalers and model providers.
Microsoft, Google and AWS can provide infrastructure and AI models, while companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic provide frontier models. ServiceNow, however, wants to sit one layer above these technologies, connecting them to the enterprise systems where work actually happens.
AI Agents Create A New Identity Problem
That strategy becomes more complicated as enterprises move from generative AI assistants to autonomous AI agents. Today, many enterprise agents still operate on behalf of a human. But as agents begin interacting directly with email, CRM systems, databases and other enterprise applications, the identity and access problem becomes significantly more complex.
An AI agent could initiate another agent, access sensitive data and execute an action without a human manually intervening at every step.
“The hardest problem I believe for agentic AI to become a reality is identity,” said Tarun Thakur, cofounder and CEO of identity security startup Veza, which ServiceNow acquired earlier this year. Veza was founded around the problem of understanding not just who an employee is, but what that identity can actually access across an enterprise’s applications and systems.
Its Access Graph maps identities, permissions and relationships across enterprise systems, giving security teams visibility into effective permissions rather than simply relying on roles and groups.
ServiceNow historically had extensive visibility into enterprise assets through its configuration management database (CMDB), but lacked the same depth of access context. The Veza acquisition brings those two pieces closer together — what an enterprise has and who or what can access it.
That becomes particularly important as the definition of an “identity” changes. “Agent identity is ephemeral — it comes and goes,” Thakur said, pointing to a future where enterprises could have large numbers of temporary machine identities being created and removed as AI agents perform specific tasks.
ServiceNow has also integrated Veza into its broader security portfolio, while using its AI Control Tower to help enterprises discover and manage AI agents across their technology environment.
The company believes AI security could eventually become a significant new cybersecurity category as enterprises move towards more autonomous systems.
The India AI Opportunity
The AI opportunity also gives ServiceNow a broader opening in India than its traditional IT-service customer base. India is home to more than 2,100 GCCs employing around 2.35 Mn people, according to Mathur. These centres are increasingly responsible for technology, product development, cybersecurity and global technology decisions for their parent companies.
For ServiceNow, that means the India opportunity can extend beyond selling to Indian businesses. GCCs can also influence technology decisions made for global organisations.
The company’s partner ecosystem further strengthens that position. Mathur said around 30,000 engineers are working on ServiceNow in India across major system integrators including Accenture, Deloitte, KPMG and EY.
BFSI remains among the company’s strongest verticals in India, while healthcare and life sciences, consumer and retail and the public sector are also important markets. Interestingly, in July, ServiceNow’s venture arm invested $40 Mn in Delhi NCR-headquartered BUSINESSNEXT, which sells software to banks, insurers and other financial institutions.
Betting On The Orchestration Layer
The larger strategic question is whether ServiceNow can establish itself as the control and orchestration layer as enterprises adopt AI from multiple vendors. The company is not trying to own the underlying AI models. Instead, it is building an open platform that can work with different frontier, open-weight and domain-specific models.
Zavery said customers ultimately care about the outcome rather than which model powers a particular task. ServiceNow therefore tests different models and can route workloads depending on the task, performance and economics.
That model-agnostic approach could become increasingly important as enterprises seek to avoid being locked into a single AI provider. ServiceNow is also competing in a market where Microsoft, Google, AWS and Salesforce increasingly position themselves as orchestration or control layers for enterprise AI.
According to Mathur, ServiceNow’s advantage comes from its existing position across enterprise workflows. “ServiceNow was always a platform company,” he said, arguing that its role is to coordinate different systems and business processes rather than own every underlying technology.
That positioning is increasingly extending into cybersecurity as well. ServiceNow’s security business was already generating more than $1 Bn in annual contract value globally before its recent acquisitions, according to Mathur, and the company is now seeking to build a much larger cybersecurity franchise around identity, vulnerabilities, incident response, OT/IoT and AI security.
The Veza acquisition therefore fits into the same broader thesis: as more AI agents enter the enterprise, ServiceNow wants visibility into not just the applications and workflows they interact with, but the identities and permissions behind them.
For Indian enterprises, the next phase of AI adoption could therefore shift the question from what AI can do to what AI can do inside their organisation, especially at scale. That is the gap ServiceNow is betting its India strategy can fill.

items.title: FBR Suggests New Way for Late Filers to Join ATL Without Fine, But With a Condition
items.summary:
With just a week left before the final deadline, the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has proposed a new way for individual taxpayers who file their income tax returns late to join the Active Taxpayers’ List (ATL) without paying the Rs. 25,000 surcharge.
Sources told ProPakistani that late filers seeking this facility would have to undertake that they will not purchase or acquire any property, or obtain ownership or beneficial interest in any property, for six months after submitting the undertaking. FBR has given stakeholders seven days to submit objections or suggestions before the proposed amendment moves toward finalization.
FBR issued the draft amendment to the Income Tax Rules, 2002, on October 6, 2026. The proposal would amend Rule 81B by adding new sub-rules (2B), (2C), and (2D).
If approved, an individual taxpayer who files the latest tax year’s income tax return after the due date or extended deadline could submit an undertaking through Form ATL-U in IRIS under Section 182A(3).
items.author: Jehangir Nasir
items.content:
With just a week left before the final deadline, the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has proposed a new way for individual taxpayers who file their income tax returns late to join the Active Taxpayers’ List (ATL) without paying the Rs. 25,000 surcharge.
Sources told ProPakistani that late filers seeking this facility would have to undertake that they will not purchase or acquire any property, or obtain ownership or beneficial interest in any property, for six months after submitting the undertaking. FBR has given stakeholders seven days to submit objections or suggestions before the proposed amendment moves toward finalization.
FBR issued the draft amendment to the Income Tax Rules, 2002, on October 6, 2026. The proposal would amend Rule 81B by adding new sub-rules (2B), (2C), and (2D).
If approved, an individual taxpayer who files the latest tax year’s income tax return after the due date or extended deadline could submit an undertaking through Form ATL-U in IRIS under Section 182A(3).
After submitting the undertaking, the taxpayer could be included in the ATL without paying the ATL surcharge. The six-month restriction would start from the date of the electronic acknowledgement generated after the successful submission of Form ATL-U through IRIS.
During this period, the taxpayer would not be allowed to purchase or acquire any property or obtain ownership or beneficial interest in any property.
FBR would be able to verify using information obtained from relevant authorities, agencies, registries, financial institutions, or other available sources.
If FBR finds that the taxpayer acquired property during the six-month period, the taxpayer would first be given an opportunity to explain the matter.
If the violation is established, the benefit of joining the ATL without paying the surcharge would be withdrawn from the date of the violation. The taxpayer’s ATL status would then be determined under Rule 81B(2A).
The draft also proposes adding Part XV to the First Schedule to introduce Form ATL-U.
The form would require details including the taxpayer’s name, CNIC or NTN, tax year, return filing date, IRIS acknowledgement or reference number, and the date of the undertaking.
The proposed amendment is not yet final. FBR has invited objections and suggestions within seven days of the issuance of the draft.
If approved, the proposal would give late filers a new route to enter the ATL without paying Rs. 25,000, but with a small restriction.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday directed the authorities concerned to take all necessary measures to ensure the uninterrupted import of gas in view of the prevailing regional situation, while ordering a comprehensive strategy and proactive steps for winter gas load management.
Chairing a high-level meeting on winter gas load management, the premier noted that a robust public awareness campaign should be launched to support the implementation of the gas load management strategy.
During the briefing, the participants of the meeting were informed that domestic consumers would remain the top priority for local gas supply, while RLNG will be prioritized for power generation and industrial sectors.
To reduce pressure on domestic gas reserves, a public awareness campaign will be initiated to promote alternative energy sources at the household level. Furthermore, measures are underway to ensure uninterrupted supply from natural gas reserves located in the northern areas of the country.
The meeting was also told that a proposal was under consideration to introduce bank financing for electricity-operated appliances used for water and space heating.
NHA
Separately, the prime minister directed that all ongoing projects of the NHA be subjected to a third-party audit and asked for a strategy to build national highways, motorways and expressways under the public-private partnership (PPP) mode.
He issued the directives while chairing a review meeting on NHA affairs at the Prime Minister House. The meeting reviewed the progress of ongoing development work on national highways, motorways and expressways, a Prime Minister's Office news release said.
Addressing the participants, the prime minister said improved transport connectivity was indispensable for the development and prosperity of any country.
He said the government was working on a priority basis to connect remote areas with the rest of the country so that people there could have the best travel facilities and more opportunities for business and employment could be created.
The meeting was briefed on ongoing and proposed NHA projects. It was informed that the NHA's revenue had increased from Rs 109 billion to Rs 130 billion in the last fiscal year and was expected to reach Rs 160 billion during the current financial year.
ILO facilitation
The prime minister said Pakistan valued its promising partnership with the ILO in creating opportunities for productive employment for the country's youth and skilled labour.
He expressed these views during a meeting with ILO Director General, Gilbert F Houngbo, who called on him along with his delegation at the Prime Minister's Office, a news release said.
The prime minister welcomed the ILO Director General and appreciated the robust cooperation between Pakistan and the organization. He underlined the need for greater ILO facilitation in the international certification and professional training of Pakistan's skilled labour, in line with the standards of the international labour market.

items.author: Yasir Ali
items.content:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Tuesday said the PTI had originally planned to take the long march towards Peshawar. However, he announced a change in the route, saying the march would first head towards Khyber and then proceed to Peshawar.
"We are playing a Test match; there are still many overs and players left. The change in route is part of the PTI's strategy," the CM said while addressing participants of the protest at University Chowk in Kohat on the third day of the march before departing for the next destination.
He also referred to the earlier change in the march's date from September 27 to October 4, saying the authorities had reacted strongly to the postponement and were now concerned about the duration of the protest.
Afridi said the march would eventually move towards Islamabad when the PTI decided to do so, declaring: "When we say we are going to Islamabad, no one will be able to stop us."
Afridi vowed to continue the PTI long march, saying all constitutional and legal avenues had been exhausted and the party was now compelled to take to the streets to seek justice for Imran Khan. He said the era of what he called "fake, imposed and mandate-stealing rulers" was nearing its end.
Thanking the people of Kohat for their enthusiasm and patriotism, he said PTI workers would not be intimidated by anyone. "My young people, your chief minister is not afraid of anyone, and the youth of my Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa are also not afraid of anyone," he said.
Afridi said the objective was to bring Imran Khan out of prison and make him prime minister again, claiming that the country would witness development and prosperity under his leadership.
He said Pakistan had enjoyed peace between 2018 and 2022, when, according to him, Imran Khan had not compromised the country's interests.
The chief minister said the seven-point demands of the long march had already been made public on social media and challenged anyone to identify even one demand that was unconstitutional or illegal.
Afridi said demands for Imran Khan's medical treatment, a meeting with him and his release in accordance with law were not unconstitutional. He questioned why courts were not hearing Imran's cases, claiming that if the cases were heard, the PTI founder would be released within an hour.
The chief minister alleged that Imran Khan was being kept in prison because he had refused to submit to powerful figures in Pakistan and abroad. He also alleged that restrictions had been placed on the former prime minister's name and image in the national media because of his popularity.
Afridi further expressed concern over reports about Imran Khan's health and alleged that his health was being "played with". He warned that the jail administration, prime minister and other relevant officials would be responsible if any harm came to the PTI founder.
He said courts, assemblies and state institutions operated with taxpayers' money and argued that people therefore had the right to demand justice. "If the courts do not provide justice, the people will seek justice on the streets," he said.
Afridi maintained that the PTI had exhausted available democratic, constitutional and legal channels before resorting to street protest.
He said since becoming chief minister, he had repeatedly approached the authorities and requested a meeting with Imran Khan. According to Afridi, he had also contacted the prime minister over the matter but was told that the request would be considered, after which no meeting was arranged.
He said the K-P Assembly subsequently passed a resolution seeking his meeting with Imran Khan, while he had also approached the chief justice of Pakistan without receiving a response.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has condemned the arrest of Qasim Khan, an extended family member of party founder Imran Khan, who was taken into custody while on his way to Adiala Jail, alleging that he had no involvement in political activity.
PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said Qasim had reached the jail on Tuesday to meet family members on the scheduled day for relatives to meet the incarcerated former prime minister.
Akram said Qasim was neither a political office-bearer nor involved in political activities, questioning the legal basis for his detention.
"Qasim Khan is not part of any political activity. He is an ordinary citizen and a member of Imran Khan's family," Akram said, according to a statement issued by the party.
Qasim has in recent months become a visible figure around Imran Khan's family, particularly as the former prime minister's incarceration has increasingly involved his relatives, lawyers and party representatives.
He was initially seen accompanying and assisting Imran Khan and was later seen alongside the former premier's sisters as they campaigned for his release and sought to ensure that he received appropriate medical treatment following reports about his deteriorating health in jail.
Qasim also became involved in coordinating the family's affairs, including communication and arrangements involving Imran Khan's family, the media, lawyers and, at times, the party. He was seen helping coordinate meetings and other matters concerning the former premier and his family.
His visibility increased as Imran Khan's wife, Bushra Bibi, and his sisters faced arrests and restrictions while seeking access to him.
Akram described Qasim's detention as another instance of what he termed the targeting of Imran Khan's family.
He questioned why the Punjab government would be concerned about a person who, according to him, had never held political office, engaged in political activity or issued political statements.

Secretary SIFC held a meeting with representatives of the Hunza Chamber of Commerce & Industry, local hotel, traders and food associations to discuss issues faced by the local business community.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The salaried class has paid Rs144 billion in income tax in this fiscal year, which is Rs90 billion more than the taxes paid by retail and realty sectors, highlighting a widening disparity under the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme that has endorsed a 50% cut for real estate and a fixed tax scheme for retailers.
Official record of the past two fiscal years and provisional figures of the first quarter (July-September) of the current fiscal year suggested that at the completion of two years of the IMF programme, the tax contribution of the salaried class had multiplied.
But the influential trading and real estate sectors remained largely outside of the net, with the IMF either endorsing tax concessions for them or keeping its eyes closed. The IMF executive board had approved the three-year $7 billion loan package in September 2024 and the Fund's staff has completed its ongoing visit to Pakistan for the fourth review of the programme.
According to the FBR's provisional tax collection data, income tax collection from the real estate sector dived 38% to a mere Rs35.2 billion in the first three months of the current fiscal year. It was Rs22 billion less than the comparative period of the last fiscal year after the government cut income tax for the realty sector by 50%, which the IMF also endorsed.
In fiscal year 2024, the realty sector had paid Rs200 billion in income tax, which hardly increased to Rs236 billion in the last fiscal year, but it has now been halved. In the budget, the government reduced the advance tax on sale and purchase of immovable property by 50%. On the sale of property, three slabs have been merged, and a single rate of 2.75% has been introduced against 5.5%.
On the purchase of property, the tax rate has been reduced from 2.5% to 1.25%. Because of this steep reduction, the advance income tax collection on the sale of property decreased from Rs39.5 billion to Rs23 billion in three months, a reduction of Rs16.5 billion, or 42%.
Likewise, on the purchase of properties, the income tax collection dipped from Rs17.7 billion to Rs12.2 billion, a reduction of Rs5.5 billion, or 31%, according to these statistics.
Official data showed that withholding taxes paid by wholesalers and retailers almost remained stagnant during the first three months of the current fiscal year. The combined withholding taxes paid by wholesalers and retailers amounted to Rs18.4 billion during the first three months. These were Rs244 million, or 1.3%, more than the last fiscal year.
Wholesalers paid Rs6.2 billion in three months, down by Rs701 million, or 10%. Instead of using the data of wholesalers to go after the retailers, the Federal Board of Revenue introduced a fixed tax scheme that has miserably failed. The traders, after making promises to become tax return filers, stayed outside of the net amid a lack of political will to go after them.
Retailers paid Rs11.3 billion in income tax, higher by Rs945 million, or 8.3%, than the comparative period of the last fiscal year. The combined taxes paid by retailers and the real estate sector amounted to a mere Rs54 billion. It was Rs90 billion less than the taxes paid by the salaried class.
According to tax officials, the income tax collection from the salaried class amounted to Rs144 billion during the July-September period of the current fiscal year. It was higher by Rs13.4 billion, or 10.2%, compared to the same period of last year.
In the budget, the government claimed that it had given a Rs52 billion relief to the salaried class by up to 3% reduction in the tax rate and abolishing the 9% surcharge calculated on the basis of the highest tax rate of 35%. It also increased the applicability limit of the maximum tax rate of 35% from Rs4.1 million to Rs7 million annually.
The massive reduction in collection from real estate has widened the gap between income tax payments made by the salaried class and the real estate sector. Before the start of the IMF programme, the annual contribution of the salaried class was Rs391 billion, which within two fiscal years of the IMF programme increased to Rs629 billion as of June 2026.
The salaried class, like other middle- and lower-middle-income groups, is also adversely impacted by the government's decision to fully recover international oil prices, charge a petroleum levy of Rs80 per litre and climate support levy of Rs5 per litre. The daily price fluctuation is also causing a hike in fruit and vegetable prices.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had promised to substantially reduce the tax burden of the salaried class once the tax base was broadened. However, instead of increasing tax collection from the highly undertaxed sectors, his government has further slashed their burden.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has released its Annual Report on Payment Systems, highlighting that fiscal year 2025-26 witnessed a strong momentum in the ongoing transformation of the payment landscape, with consumers, businesses, and financial institutions increasingly embracing mobile apps, internet banking, e-money wallets, QR-based payments, and other digital channels. This growth has been supported by various policy measures, improved digital infrastructure, and industry-led initiatives.
Retail payments through formal banking channels during FY26 registered a significant growth, reaching 14.3 billion transactions valued at Rs673 trillion, representing a year-on-year growth of 58% in volume and 10% in value. Digital channels continued to gain traction as consumers increasingly adopted mobile banking apps, internet banking, and e-money wallets for everyday payments.
Out of the 14.3 billion transactions conducted through formal banking channels, 13.2 billion transactions were conducted through digital channels, representing a year-on-year growth of 65%. Furthermore, digital channels accounted for 92% of total retail payment transactions, up from 88% in FY25. Mobile phone-based solutions led digital transactions with over 11.1 billion transactions, registering a 79% growth, while internet banking portals processed 0.3 billion transactions, up 15% from the previous fiscal year.
The expansion of digital acceptance infrastructure at merchants/retailers' outlets further supported this growth. The POS network expanded to 337,791 terminals across 295,367 merchant locations, supporting nearly 1.5 million daily card payments compared to 1 million in the previous fiscal year.
E-commerce payments also continued to gain traction, with account-based online payments accounting for 96% of total e-commerce transactions conducted through banking channels. Branchless banking mobile app users increased to 99.1 million, while banks' mobile app users reached 30.4 million, highlighting the continued shift of everyday banking activities towards smartphone-based platforms.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The government has allowed Mari Energies to carry out airborne field detection survey operations in different areas in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), including Waziristan, and Balochistan.
Mari Energies has also been allowed temporary import of aircraft to conduct surveys of different sites in the two provinces.
Sources said that Mari had been granted a conditional NOC for carrying out an airborne Strike Field Detection (SFD) survey operation in the following areas, which included (Wali) West, Waziristan and Karak Block in K-P, Block-28, Hanna, Hanna South, Ziarat and Ziarat North Blocks in Balochistan.
However, different conditions and security points have been attached to this approval. The firm shall ensure that the survey remains limited to the areas mutually agreed. The firm shall arrange transportation, lodging and make other administrative arrangements for the duration of the survey and shall not ask for any charges in this regard.
The company must provide at least two weeks' notice regarding the arrival of the aircraft and the survey team. No photo and survey equipment will be loaded on the aircraft, other than those sensors/equipment required for survey and communication.
Mari will provide an undertaking that no survey data will be transmitted out of the country without clearance from the Strategic Plans Division (SPD). In addition, each survey sortie will be cleared by the SPD team, after having assessed the survey data acquired during the previous sortie.
The firm will permit pre-inspection of the aircraft by a team of SPD and two officers of SPD will be on board during each survey sortie for monitoring and coordination. Schedule of each survey sortie is to be communicated at least 48 hours in advance to the SPD team for clearance.
In case of presence of strategic minerals, SPD shall have priority rights and the firm shall provide space and passage to SPD in case SPD plans to carry out any activity in that area. Foreign experts, if any, may only be allowed to visit after necessary security clearance.
Use/carrying of maps, survey equipment, GPS and technical gadgetry on the project site other than the required equipment is prohibited.
Routing/safe transit of each mission (from take-off till landing) shall be devised in consultation with the Directorate of Air Traffic Services. Survey team should not be allowed to visit/photograph any key point of vital defence installation.
Foreigners will not be allowed to visit any other area without proper security cover. Local authorities will ensure personal security of the foreigners. Adequate arrangement will be made for the security of guests by the host district to avoid any untoward incident.
Mari has been advised to fulfil all the conditions/requirements in true letter and spirit and to furnish a certificate for the observance of all the mentioned conditions.

items.content:
Pakistan is set to complete 16 major road and highway projects including GT Roads, National Highways and Motorways, with the projects now in their final stages and expected to be ready for inauguration soon.
The development was shared during a meeting on National Highway Authority (NHA) projects chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif at the Prime Minister House in Islamabad today.
The projects include upgrades, new roads, interchanges and additional carriageways across different parts of the country.
Major projects nearing completion include the upgrade of GT Road from Tee Chowk Islamabad to Banth, remodelling of the Islamabad Chungi No. 26 Interchange, and the extension of Margalla Avenue from GT Road to Motorway M-1.
The list also includes the upgrade of the Pindi Bhattian-Faisalabad section of M-4, Quetta Western Bypass, Pindi Gheb-Jand Road and Bhong Interchange on the Multan-Sukkur Motorway M-5.
Other projects include the Nokandi-Mashkhel Road, conversion of Old Bannu Road into a dual carriageway, and upgrades of several sections of Indus Highway N-55.
These include the Sehwan-San section, Ratodero-Shikarpur section and an additional carriageway on the Pataro-Sindh section.
The meeting was also informed that NHA revenue increased from Rs. 109 billion to Rs. 130 billion during the last fiscal year. Revenue is expected to reach Rs. 160 billion during the current fiscal year.
Several major projects are being funded through NHA’s own revenue, including the Sialkot-Kharian Motorway M-12, Kharian-Rawalpindi Motorway M-13, Peshawar Northern Bypass, reconstruction of the Jaglot-Skardu Road, M-4 upgrade and Multan-Lodhran N-5 upgrade.
Prime Minister Shehbaz directed that all ongoing NHA projects undergo third-party audits. He also called for a strategy to develop national highways, motorways and expressways through public-private partnerships.
The meeting was further informed that several projects will soon be launched, including the Kharian-Rawalpindi Motorway M-13, Sukkur-Hyderabad Motorway M-6 and rehabilitation and reconstruction projects on different sections of GT Road and N-5.
The government is also considering the Guru Nanak Expressway to connect Kartarpur with Nankana Sahib. Another proposed project is the Mansehra-Chilas Expressway through Naran, which could reduce the distance between the two cities by 146 kilometers.
Prime Minister Shehbaz said better transport links are essential for economic development and directed the government to prioritize connecting remote areas with the rest of the country to improve travel facilities and create more business and employment opportunities.

items.title: Govt Launches Winter Gas Management Plan
items.summary:
Pakistan is preparing a comprehensive plan to manage gas supplies during the upcoming winter as the government moves to take early measures to address seasonal demand.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday directed the authorities to finalize a comprehensive gas load management plan and take necessary steps in advance.
A meeting chaired by the prime minister reviewed preparations for managing gas supplies during the winter season.
Officials briefed the meeting on measures being taken ahead of the expected increase in demand. The government will launch a public awareness campaign to encourage households to use alternative energy sources instead of locally produced gas.
The government is also taking steps to ensure uninterrupted transmission of gas from reserves located in the northern areas of the country.
A proposal to provide bank financing for electric appliances used for water and space heating is also under consideration.
