items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Pakistan can produce world-class textiles, surgical instruments, sports goods and even FIFA World Cup footballs, but foreign brands often take the credit and much of the value, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said on Tuesday.
Speaking at a national branding conference in Islamabad, Iqbal called for a major shift in how Pakistan sells itself to the world, saying the country needs to build internationally recognized Pakistani brands instead of remaining a manufacturer for foreign companies.
He pointed to Pakistan’s export performance as a major concern. While Pakistan’s exports have remained around $40 billion since 1990, Vietnam’s exports have grown to roughly $475 billion, he said.
The minister argued that Pakistan needs to move away from low-value commodity exports and focus on differentiated products that carry a strong Pakistani identity in international markets.
The government is now looking at seven areas to build that identity.
Under its “Nation Brand Lens,” Pakistan’s branding strategy will focus on Culture, Exports, Governance, Diplomacy and Defence, Entertainment, Tourism and Sports.
The idea is to bring these areas together under one broader national brand instead of promoting Pakistan’s products, culture and tourism separately.
The National Center for Brand Development (NCBD), established under the Ministry of Planning, will lead the effort. It will work with local industries to help them move from domestic markets toward direct exports and develop a stronger “Made in Pakistan” identity.
The minister said Pakistan already has the ability to produce products that compete internationally. The challenge, he said, is making sure the Pakistani name travels with those products.
The government also wants the initiative to improve Pakistan’s global image, increase demand for local products and help businesses develop internationally recognized brands.
The roundtable in Islamabad brought together experts and stakeholders to discuss Pakistan’s proposed Country Brand Framework, global slogan, brand measurement and policies for improving the country’s international image.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Huawei and Qualcomm have signed a broad multi-year patent cross-licensing agreement covering technologies including 5G, computing, artificial intelligence, and networking.
The agreement marks the first licensing deal between the two companies that also includes 5G, among other technologies.
Qualcomm Will Buy Huawei US Patents
As part of the agreement, Qualcomm will acquire several US patents from Huawei covering developments in computing, AI, networking, and other technologies.
The transaction still requires regulatory approval. Huawei has remained subject to US trade restrictions since 2019, meaning the deal will also require scrutiny from US authorities.
Huawei Patent Deals Could Exceed $6.9 Billion
Huawei and Qualcomm did not disclose the financial terms of the agreement in their joint announcement.
However, Reuters reported that once the deal closes, the total value of Huawei’s patent licensing agreements will exceed $6.9 billion.
Huawei has increased its research and development spending in recent years as it has worked to develop chips and other technologies that it previously sourced from companies such as Qualcomm.
Both Companies Highlight Their Technology Contributions
Huawei Chief Intellectual Property Officer Alan Fan said the company’s long-term investment in research had contributed to advances in mobile communications and other technology areas.
He highlighted Huawei’s work on 4G and 5G standards, including polar-code-based signal transmission technology, and said the agreement recognizes the value of innovation from both companies.
Qualcomm Technology Licensing Executive Vice President and General Manager John Han said Qualcomm’s investments in foundational wireless technologies have supported several generations of mobile communications.
He said the agreement reflects recognition of Qualcomm’s 5G technology and licensing program while also recognizing Huawei’s intellectual property and continued innovation in 5G and other areas.

items.author: Muhammad Bilal
items.content:
All Pakistan Anjuman-e-Tajiran President Ajmal Baloch has criticized the government’s policies and warned that traders could shut down Islamabad and march toward the Prime Minister’s House if their demands are not addressed.
Baloch said there was no proper planning in the country and that the government was relying on force to deal with problems.
He claimed that traders and the public had faced severe difficulties over the past four years and alleged that 120 million people had fallen below the poverty line during this period.
“I have never seen traders treated this way in my 28 years of experience,” Baloch said, adding that the difficulties faced during the coronavirus pandemic were not as severe as those being experienced now.
He also criticized the enforcement of restrictions on shopping bags, claiming that more than 100 cases were being registered against traders in a single day over the issue.
Baloch said that if shopping bags were to be banned, factories producing them should also be shut down and an alternative provided to traders.
Trader leaders announced that they would begin protests if their demands were not accepted. They warned that Islamabad could be completely shut down and that traders could march toward the Prime Minister’s House.
The traders said their final course of action, including a possible shutdown, would be announced after a protest at Aabpara Chowk on Thursday.

The phone focuses on basic hardware, a high-refresh-rate display, and a large battery.

The Realme P4s Lite features a 6.75-inch LCD with HD+ resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate.
It is available in Moonlight Silver and Nebula Black.
The phone also carries an IP64 rating for protection against dust and water splashes.
Internals and Software
The P4s Lite is powered by the Unisoc T7250 chipset.
It comes with LPDDR4X RAM and UFS 2.2 storage.
Connectivity options include 4G, Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.2, and GPS.
The phone also includes a side-mounted fingerprint sensor and a 3.5mm headphone jack.
Cameras
The Realme P4s Lite has a 13MP rear camera with autofocus.
On the front, it gets a 5MP camera for selfies and video calls.
Battery and Pricing
The phone packs a 7,000mAh battery.
Realme says the battery can maintain optimal health for up to six years.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
Frontier AI research startup FYDY (Fuzzy Dynamics), which is operating in stealth mode, is in advanced talks to raise $12 Mn (about ₹115 Cr) in its maiden funding round, sources told Inc42.
Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst are co-leading the round, the sources said.
While questions sent to FYDY didn’t elicit any response, Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst did not respond.
As per FYDY’s LinkedIn page, the startup was incorporated in 2025. It has five cofounders – Alapan Chaudhuri, Shivansh Subramanian, Anvay Karmore, Tanishq Chaudhary, and Zeeshan Ahmed.
FYDY says its founding team includes ICPC World Finalists and Physics & Astronomy Olympiad alumni.
The San Francisco-headquartered startup’s employees are spread across India and the US. It is currently hiring researchers and engineers, among other roles.
FYDY describes itself as a frontier AI research business operating in stealth. It is developing “cognitive machines” that learn continuously from experience, with the long-term goal of building safe artificial superintelligence capable of understanding and acting autonomously in the real world.
FYDY has also launched OpenScientist, an AI research studio currently in private beta. According to its website, the startup initially built the platform for its own research and is rolling it out to a small group of labs and researchers.
The platform is designed to help users search research papers and databases, explore mathematical problems, run experiments, and analyse data.
“We are working with leading researchers across reinforcement learning, world models, robotics and neuroscience. These are the fields we believe converge into machine cognition,” it says on its website.
The funding talks come as Lightspeed and General Catalyst continue to back AI startups across scientific research and enterprise applications.
In August, AI-powered materials discovery startup Discovered Materials announced a $9 Mn seed round led by Lightspeed India Partners. The startup is developing AI agents to automate semiconductor materials research, including simulation, synthesis, and experimental validation.
Meanwhile, Sol Foundry emerged from stealth last month with $4 Mn from General Catalyst, Nexus Venture Partners, DeVC, Peercheque, and Kunal Shah. The startup is building an AI assistant that acts on commitments made over email, preparing research, documents, and other tasks for users to approve.
According to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026, AI startups raised $438 Mn across 35 deals during the quarter, making AI the most funded sector. Funding rose 265% YoY, although capital remained largely concentrated in startups building AI applications.

items.author: Yasir Ali
items.content:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Tuesday announced a change in the route of the PTI's long march, saying it would first head towards Khyber and then proceed to Peshawar.
“We are playing a Test match; there are still many overs and players left. The change in route is part of the PTI’s strategy,” he said while addressing participants of the protest at University Chowk in Kohat on the third day of the march before departing for the next destination.
CM Afridi also referred to the earlier change in the march’s date from September 27 to October 4, saying the authorities had reacted strongly to the postponement and were now concerned about the duration of the protest.
Read: CM Afridi urges PTI workers to join long march as convoy enters Kohat
He said the march would eventually move towards Islamabad when the PTI decided to do so, declaring: “When we say we are going to Islamabad, no one will be able to stop us.”
"یہ لوگ انتشار پھیلانے کی کوشش کریں گے، آپ کو اشتعال دلائیں گے آپ لوگوں نے پرامن رہنا ہے میں نے ان کی دُم پر پاؤں رکھا ہوا ہے۔ خواجہ آصف جو ایک بزرگ عورت سے سیٹ ہار چکا ہے اگر یہ غیرت مند باپ کا بیٹا ہوتا تو ایک عورت کی سیٹ پر نہ بیٹھا ہوتا مجھے تمہاری غیرت کا بھی پتہ ہے اور… pic.twitter.com/2PsiJ2LSa4
— PTI (@PTIofficial) October 6, 2026
Afridi vowed to continue the PTI long march, saying all constitutional and legal avenues had been exhausted and the party was now compelled to take to the streets to seek justice for founder Imran Khan. He said the era of what he called “fake, imposed and mandate-stealing rulers” was nearing its end.
Thanking the people of Kohat for their enthusiasm and patriotism, he said PTI workers would not be intimidated by anyone. “My young people, your chief minister is not afraid of anyone, and the youth of my Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa are also not afraid of anyone,” he said.
Afridi said the objective was to bring Imran out of prison and make him prime minister again, claiming that the country would witness development and prosperity under his leadership.
He said Pakistan had enjoyed peace between 2018 and 2022, when, according to him, Imran had not compromised the country’s interests.
The chief minister said the seven-point demands of the long march had already been made public on social media and challenged anyone to identify even one demand that was unconstitutional or illegal.
Afridi said demands for Imran’s medical treatment, a meeting with him and his release were in accordance with law and were not unconstitutional. He questioned why courts were not hearing Imran’s cases, claiming that if the cases were heard, the PTI founder would be released within an hour.
یہ عمران خان کی صحت سے کھیل رہے ہیں۔ ہمارا مطالبہ ہے کہ انہیں شفا انٹرنیشنل ہسپتال منتقل کیا جائے اور ذاتی ڈاکٹر و ہمشیرہ کی نگرانی میں علاج ہو۔ سپریم کورٹ نے آرڈرز جاری کیے، مگر پاکستان پر قابض لوگ اور ان کے لائے جعلی حکمران خود کو آئین و قانون سے بالاتر سمجھ کر انہیں نہیں… pic.twitter.com/TqnyDU0ksX
— PTI (@PTIofficial) October 6, 2026
The chief minister alleged that Imran was being kept in prison because he had refused to submit to powerful figures in Pakistan and abroad. He also alleged that restrictions had been placed on the former prime minister’s name and image in the national media because of his popularity.
Read More: ‘Absolutely not’: CM Afridi rejects ‘closed-room’ decisions on military operations in K-P
Afridi further expressed concern over reports about Imran’s health and alleged that his health was being “played with”. He warned that the jail administration, prime minister and other relevant officials would be responsible if any harm came to Imran.
He said courts, assemblies and state institutions operated with taxpayers’ money and argued that people therefore had the right to demand justice. “If the courts do not provide justice, the people will seek justice on the streets,” he said.
"ہم نہتے پرامن لانگ مارچ کررہے ہیں، ہم نے اپنی ڈیمانڈز سوشل میڈیا پر شیئر کی ہیں میں پورے پاکستان کو چیلنج کرتا ہوں اگر سات نکات میں سے ایک بھی ڈیمانڈ غیرآئینی غیرقانونی ثابت کردیں میں اپنا لانگ مارچ آج ہی کینسل کردوں گا ۔ عمران خان کا علاج غیر آئینی نہیں ہے، عمران خان سے… pic.twitter.com/WkOr1sptoJ
— PTI (@PTIofficial) October 6, 2026
He said that since becoming the chief minister, he had repeatedly approached the authorities and requested a meeting with Imran. According to Afridi, he had also contacted the prime minister over the matter but was told that the request would be considered, after which no meeting was arranged.
Afridi stated that the K-P Assembly subsequently passed a resolution seeking his meeting with Imran, while he had also approached the chief justice of Pakistan without receiving a response.
He further alleged that even orders of high courts and the Supreme Court concerning access to Imran and his medical treatment had not been implemented.
Afridi also criticised the handling of negotiations, saying PTI had always maintained that political problems should be resolved through dialogue. He alleged that attempts were being made to “trade the blood of Pashtuns” to protect political positions.
On the security situation in K-P, he underlined that successive military operations and drone strikes over the past 22 years had failed to eliminate terrorism, further claiming his government had a policy that could restore peace in the province within 100 days.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
,JazzCash has reportedly closed more than 100 aggregator accounts following directives from the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), according to sources familiar with the matter. The move comes as Pakistani authorities increase scrutiny of digital payment channels linked to suspected illegal financial activities.
The accounts were reportedly shut down directly in response to FIA notices. Other accounts were flagged and suspended by JazzCash during an internal review of its aggregator network.
Sources said the affected accounts were generating significant revenue for the company. Their closure could therefore affect JazzCash’s earnings in the coming year, particularly because transactions connected to aggregators made up a notable share of the platform’s overall transaction activity.
JazzCash Shuts Down 100+ Aggregator Accounts Following FIA Directives
The development follows a similar disruption involving Easypaisa. Earlier this month, transactions processed through Easypaisa’s merchant and payment intermediary channels faced delays at several payment firms. Companies including Simpaisa, ajarPay, RapidPay, Zero Technologies and Finza Tech, along with international payment processor dLocal, reported settlement-related issues.
Despite those problems, Easypaisa’s regular wallet services and person-to-person transfers continued to operate.
FIA Investigation Into Illegal Financial Networks
The recent actions are linked to a wider investigation by law enforcement agencies into the alleged use of mobile wallets, bank accounts and cryptocurrency channels for illegal online gambling and digital hawala activities.
In September 2026, the FIA investigated eight suspects allegedly connected with six gambling platforms. During the investigation, authorities traced transactions worth around Rs119.93 billion, equivalent to approximately $433.5 million.
Investigators also found that about Rs8.586 billion had moved through nearly 10.5 million transactions involving just five branchless banking collection accounts.
These findings have increased pressure on financial technology companies and payment service providers to strengthen monitoring of transactions passing through their platforms.
SBP Tightens Rules for Payment Intermediaries
The crackdown also comes after the State Bank of Pakistan introduced a stricter regulatory framework for payment intermediaries and aggregators in May 2026.
The framework includes stronger requirements for documentation, foreign exchange compliance and monitoring of financial flows. These measures aim to improve transparency and help prevent payment systems from being misused for illegal activities.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority has also taken action against illegal digital platforms. The regulator recently blocked 46 illegal gambling and unregulated trading applications in Pakistan. Authorities have also arrested several individuals accused of promoting illegal gambling activities.
Wider Impact on the Fintech Sector
The latest developments indicate that regulators are paying closer attention to aggregator accounts and other intermediaries within Pakistan’s digital payments ecosystem.
For JazzCash, closing the accounts could result in lower transaction volumes and reduced revenue from aggregator-related business. However, the measures also reflect growing efforts by authorities to prevent mobile wallets and payment networks from being used to move illicit funds.
The recent Easypaisa payment delays and JazzCash account closures could also lead to increased scrutiny of other mobile wallet providers. Fintech companies may face greater pressure to strengthen customer verification, transaction monitoring, and compliance systems as investigations continue.

Read: Govt increases petrol by 88 paisas, cuts diesel by Rs1.88 for Oct 6
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices were steady on Tuesday after recovering earlier losses, as the market weighed increases in Middle Eastern crude exports and a planned ‌Group of Seven release of emergency diesel and crude stockpiles against supply concerns related to attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.
Brent futures were down 29 cents, or 0.3%, at $100.03 a barrel at 12:33 pm EDT (1633 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 16 cents, or 0.2%, to $89.59.
"The price of the global crude benchmark, Brent, is once ​again toiling around $100/barrel, as its reasons for trading much beyond the psychological 3-digit mark are being eroded ... for now the assumption of more crude getting through has ​dampened price fervour," said John Evans, an analyst at oil broker PVM.

items.author: Staff
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s retail payment transactions surged 58 percent to 14.3 billion in fiscal year 2025-26, with digital channels accounting for 92 percent of the total volume, as mobile-based payments emerged as the main driver of the country’s accelerating shift away from cash.
According to the State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) Annual Payment Systems Review FY2025-26, retail payments reached 14.3 billion transactions worth Rs672.7 trillion during the year, compared with 9.1 billion transactions valued at Rs611.6 trillion in FY25.
While transaction volume jumped 58 percent, the value of retail payments increased by only 10 percent, highlighting the rapid expansion of high-frequency, relatively low-value digital transactions.
The share of digital payments in total retail transactions increased to more than 92 percent in FY26 from 88 percent in FY25 and 85 percent in FY24. In value terms, however, digital payments accounted for only 38 percent of retail payment value, although this was up from 29 percent a year earlier.
The SBP said 13.2 billion retail transactions worth Rs257.1 trillion were processed through digital channels during FY26, compared with 8 billion transactions worth Rs178.6 trillion in FY25.
Mobile phone-based solutions remained the biggest contributor to the digital payments boom, processing 11.1 billion transactions during the year—79 percent higher than the previous year.
These channels, including bank and branchless banking mobile apps, e-money wallets, USSD, SMS banking and call centre/IVR services, accounted for 78 percent of all retail transactions and 84 percent of digital transactions.
However, the value of mobile-based transactions remained comparatively low at Rs155 trillion, or 23 percent of total retail payment value, reflecting their predominantly low-value and high-frequency nature.
Internet banking also maintained strong growth, with transactions increasing 15 percent to more than 341 million, while their value jumped 55 percent to over Rs60.9 trillion.
The digital payments infrastructure expanded sharply during the year. The number of QR-enabled merchants more than tripled from 1.09 million in June 2025 to 3.84 million by June 2026, while POS devices increased 49 percent to 337,791.
POS-enabled merchants also rose from 190,823 to 295,367, while daily card payments at POS outlets reached nearly 1.5 million compared with around one million a year earlier.
The number of e-commerce merchants registered with banks increased from 9,584 to 23,356. Account/wallet-based payments accounted for almost 96 percent of e-commerce transactions processed through banks.
The expansion was also reflected in digital banking users. Branchless banking mobile app users rose from 79.2 million to 99.1 million, while mobile banking users increased from 24.1 million to 30.4 million. Internet banking users climbed from 14.9 million to 17.5 million, whereas e-money wallet users increased 37 percent to 7.9 million.
Despite the rapid digitalisation of payment volumes, over-the-counter (OTC) channels continued to dominate in terms of value. OTC transactions through bank branches and branchless banking agents amounted to Rs415.7 trillion in FY26, accounting for about 62 percent of total retail payment value.
The SBP report said OTC fund transfers alone represented 46 percent of retail payment value, compared with 28 percent for digital fund transfers, indicating that higher-value transactions have yet to fully migrate to digital channels.
Merchant payments through accounts also gained significant traction, increasing 141 percent during FY26, while card-based merchant payments grew 47 percent. Account-based merchant payments accounted for 13 percent of total retail payment transactions, compared with 4.4 percent for card-based merchant payments.
The report also highlighted a continued migration of bill payments to digital channels. Digital bill payments and mobile top-ups accounted for 89 percent of such transactions, up from 87 percent in FY25 and 85 percent in FY24.
Meanwhile, Pakistan’s large-value payment infrastructure also recorded strong growth. PRISM+, the upgraded real-time gross settlement system launched in August 2025, processed 6.3 million transactions worth Rs1,565.8 trillion during FY26, up 5 percent in volume and 24 percent in value.
The value settled through PRISM+ was equivalent to 12.3 times Pakistan’s nominal GDP of Rs126.9 trillion, compared with 11.1 times in FY25.
The SBP said PRISM+ marked Pakistan’s transition to the ISO 20022 global messaging standard across both retail and large-value payment systems, aimed at improving efficiency, transparency and security.
The central bank noted that despite substantial progress in digital payment adoption, significant scope remained to digitise higher-value transactions involving businesses, government entities and financial institutions.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Cellular consumers continue to face hefty charges for mobile data and hybrid services, with monthly packages costing as much as Rs2,800 and some high-volume bundles requiring users to spend over Rs1,000 even for 15 days, according to the latest Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) tariff data.
The PTA’s cellular hybrid bundles tariff, updated as of September 30, 2026, shows that despite operators offering large headline data volumes, consumers seeking substantial data, voice minutes, and SMS services have to pay hundreds or even thousands of rupees for relatively short validity periods.
The tariff data reveals a sharp increase in prices as consumers move from basic to high-volume packages, putting comprehensive mobile connectivity beyond the reach of many low-income and price-sensitive users.
PTA Tariff Data Reveals Rising Cost of Mobile Data Packages in Pakistan
In the 15 Day category, Telenor’s 15 Day Extreme package carries 130 GB of data but costs Rs1,043, while Jazz’s 15 Day AIO package provides 10 GB for Rs869. Telenor’s 15 Day Max offers 30 GB for Rs869, whereas its 15 Day Plus package provides only 2 GB for Rs391.
The weekly packages also reflect a wide variation in price and data allocation. Jazz’s Super Woman Bundle costs Rs234 for 12 GB for seven days, while its Weekly Super Plus and New Weekly Super packages cost Rs521 for 10 GB and 15 GB, respectively.
Jazz’s Weekly Super Max package costs Rs608 for 30 GB, indicating that consumers requiring larger data allowances have to pay substantially more even for a single week of connectivity.
The monthly segment is even more expensive for users requiring sizeable data volumes. Jazz’s Monthly Bachat Offer costs Rs478 for 6 GB of selected social and messaging data, while its 10 GB YouTube and social package costs Rs608.
Its 20 GB YouTube and Social Plus package costs Rs1,043, while the Monthly Video and Social Max package costs Rs1,304 for 30 GB.
The tariff structure means that consumers requiring uninterrupted access to mobile internet, voice calls and SMS can face a monthly bill running into thousands of rupees, particularly when smaller bundles expire and have to be renewed.
The PTA data also shows that the apparent affordability of some packages is linked to restrictions on the type of data offered. Several cheaper bundles provide data only for specific applications such as WhatsApp, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok or other social platforms rather than unrestricted internet access.
This limits the practical value of low-priced packages for consumers who need mobile connectivity for broader activities, including education, work, online services and business.
See Also: Jazz Emerges as Pakistan’s Most Expensive Operator for Standard Mobile Data at Rs 5/MB
Although operators have introduced increasingly large data allowances, the tariff structure suggests that higher-volume packages remain relatively expensive, while cheaper options often come with limited data, shorter validity or application-specific restrictions.
The situation is particularly significant as Pakistan continues to push digitalisation and greater reliance on mobile internet for economic and public services.
The PTA has advised consumers to check operators’ websites, mobile applications and call centres for updated package details, particularly in the case of regional and location-based offers.
The regulator has also clarified that applicable taxes are included in the listed tariffs, while withholding tax and sales tax are imposed on mobile recharges and usage.
The latest tariff data therefore presents a mixed picture of Pakistan’s cellular market. While operators are advertising increasingly large data bundles, affordable, unrestricted, and longer-validity connectivity remains costly for ordinary consumers.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
On September 30, Inc42 hosted the inaugural edition of the CTO Summit 2026 at JW Marriott, Bengaluru, bringing together 200+ senior technology leaders as delegates and speakers to discuss how India’s technology ecosystem is building and scaling in the AI era.
The summit brought together CTOs, engineering, product, data, and AI leaders from India’s leading tech startups like Meesho, Swiggy, Flipkart, and Rapido for conversations around AI adoption, engineering productivity, infrastructure, architecture, and the systems needed to build at India’s scale.
Across 10+ sessions, the discussions went beyond AI experimentation to examine what happens when the technology moves into production, from the economics of running AI workloads and the quality of data powering applications to verification, resilience, and the changing role of engineering teams.
Speakers explored how AI is reshaping products and the way users interact with them. Swiggy’s CTO Madhusudhan Rao joined the summit to share his views on how the listed food delivery platform is using AI agents to take commerce beyond its app, while Flipkart CPTO Balaji Thiagarajan discussed the shift from keyword-led product discovery towards systems that can understand consumer intent.
The conversations also moved into the engineering organisation itself. As AI-assisted coding increases the amount of software teams can generate, technology leaders discussed how design, review, testing, and verification are becoming increasingly important, while exploring how AI could make systems thinking more important as routine coding becomes increasingly automated.
Building for India’s scale emerged as another key theme. Leaders discussed the challenges of building AI products for users across budget smartphones, multiple languages and patchy connectivity, while keeping infrastructure and inference costs under control.
The conversation highlighted the need for technology teams to account for these constraints when designing AI systems for a market as diverse as India.
The summit also featured three technical demos that offered a closer look at AI being applied in real-world systems. Dushyant Garg, lead, strategy & enterprise growth at Nugget (by Zomato), showcased how Zomato’s experience operating AI at India scale is being translated into enterprise systems through specialised agents, real-time intelligence and governance layers.
Srivatsa Katta, CTO at Rapido, walked through how the company has adapted its engineering organisation and infrastructure for the AI era, including its use of coding agents, an LLM Gateway and AI Catalyst.
Prabu Ram, SVP, Engineering at Razorpay, showcased Slash, the company’s autonomous engineering agent built to combine company context, connected tools and workflow triggers to execute engineering tasks.
The summit also examined the infrastructure and data foundations behind these systems. Discussions around architecture focused on capacity planning, resilience and preparing for failures beyond a company’s own technology stack, while leaders from PhonePe Payment Gateway, OceanBase and Fibe discussed data quality, access controls and the need for reliable data foundations for AI applications.
PhonePe Payment Gateway’s CTO Srijon Biswas shared how fintech is using AI across internal workflows, with more than 200 AI agents being used by around 1,600 employees daily. He discussed examples of AI-driven efficiency gains, including around 22 person-days saved per app release and audit processes that were reduced from four days to three minutes.
As AI takes on more routine engineering work, Biswas said, “You need more people who can make stronger decisions and get them correct more often.”
Oracle’s Palanivel Saravanan also underlined how companies are bringing AI models closer to their data. “Everybody is looking at how they can get the models much closer to their data, so that the model can learn better and respond to the user better,” said Saravanan.
From AI agents and product discovery to engineering productivity, infrastructure resilience and data governance, the conversations reflected a technology ecosystem moving from asking whether AI should be adopted to figuring out how it can work reliably and economically at scale.
But none of these conversations would have been possible without the support of our sponsors and partners, who helped bring the inaugural Inc42 CTO Summit to life. Thank you for powering these conversations.
Presenting Partner
PhonePe Payment Gateway
PhonePe Payment Gateway is a digital payments and financial services platform offering services across payments, financial products and commerce.
At the Inc42 CTO Summit 2026, PhonePe CTO Srijon Biswas joined Inc42 CEO and cofounder Vaibhav Vardhan for ‘How PhonePe Is Combining DPI And AI For 720 Mn+ Users’, where they discussed how the company is using AI to improve efficiency and build more personalised financial experiences at scale.
Biswas also discussed how India’s digital public infrastructure could provide the foundation for more personalised AI-led financial experiences, while navigating consent, privacy and data governance.
PhonePe also featured in ‘Building The Data Foundation For AI At Scale’, where Kisalay Ranjan, head of engineering, merchant payments, PhonePe, shared perspectives on data quality, access controls and the need for reliable data foundations for AI applications.
Co-presenting Partner
Oracle
Oracle is an enterprise technology company offering cloud infrastructure, databases, applications and other technology solutions for businesses.
At the CTO Summit, Oracle was part of the conversation around the architecture and infrastructure decisions required as Indian technology companies scale.
Palanivel Saravanan, head of infrastructure cloud engineering at Oracle, participated in the session ‘The Architecture Of 10X: Engineering For India’s Next Scale Curve’, alongside Vikas Goyal, cofounder & CTO, Kuku; Noel Curtis, CTO, BookMyShow; and Prabu Ram, SVP, engineering, Razorpay.

items.content:
Invest tech startup StockGro, which pre-filed its IPO papers last week, raises ₹110 Cr (around $10.4 Mn) as a part of its ongoing Series B round.
As per MCA documents accessed by Inc42, existing investor BITKRAFT Ventures is set to lead the fresh round of funding. Aditum Venture Capital Fund, India SME Growth Fund, and actor Suniel Shetty are among the other investors participating in the round.
As per the filing, StockGro’s board approved issuing 14,004 Series B CCPS at a price of ₹78,668 per share, aggregating to ₹110.16 Cr. Out of this total amount, BITKRAFT is infusing ₹60.1 Cr, followed by Aditum Venture Capital Fund with ₹23.1 Cr.
Rest of the amount will be contributed by India SME Growth Fund, Systematix Fincorp, and angel investors like Vanaja Sundar Iyer, Jignesh Vijay Shah, Suniel Shetty, among others.
The fresh capital will be used to fuel growth and expansion of the startup’s operations, meeting working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes.
It is pertinent to note that the startup has raised capital across multiple tranches under its Series B funding round. In December last year, StockGro raised ₹150 Cr from Param Capital founder Mukul Agarwal. Days after, it announced a fundraise of $13 Mn in a Series B1 funding round from existing investor BITKRAFT Ventures.
The fresh tranche seems to be an extension of the Series B round. StockGro declined to comment on Inc42’s queries on the fresh funding round.
The investment comes in the run up to the startup’s public market debut. StockGro’s parent AssetGro Fintech Ltd pre-filed its draft IPO papers with SEBI via the confidential route on September 26.
The startup is planning to raise up to ₹2,000 Cr-₹2,500 Cr via the IPO, which is likely to include a fresh issue of around ₹800 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders. The final issue size and structure could change during the IPO process.
StockGro is focused on stock-market research, investing and trading. The app combines market research with a social layer, allowing users to track stocks, study portfolios, follow other investors and interact with market experts.
It also offers users research and trade ideas from SEBI-registered analysts, along with tools for deeper analysis. Its AI-powered research assistant Stoxo helps users analyse stocks, markets, mutual funds and other investment themes.
The startup has raised about $110 Mn to date and claims to have served over 4.5 Cr users. It counts the likes of Roots Ventures, General Catalyst, and Nazara cofounder Nitish Mittersain, among its backers.

items.title: Trump blames France unrest on 'mass migration', Islam
items.summary:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday blamed mass student protests in France on "mass migration" and Islam, pushing his global right-wing narrative ahead of tough midterm elections at home.
French students have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools across the country since late September to demand better conditions, in protests that have descended into sporadic clashes with security forces. A quarter of a million demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday.
"What's happening in France is nothing less than out-of-control mass migration. This isn't about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great country!" Trump said in a post on Truth Social.
Trump:

Trump and his admi
items.author: AFP / Reuters
items.content:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday blamed mass student protests in France on "mass migration" and Islam, pushing his global right-wing narrative ahead of tough midterm elections at home.
French students have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools across the country since late September to demand better conditions, in protests that have descended into sporadic clashes with security forces. A quarter of a million demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday.
"What's happening in France is nothing less than out-of-control mass migration. This isn't about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great country!" Trump said in a post on Truth Social.
Trump:
What’s happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration. This isn’t about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great Country! pic.twitter.com/SzfOqAjiDv
— Clash Report (@clashreport) October 6, 2026
Trump and his administration have long blamed European social issues on migration, calling on Europe to shut its borders and echoing far-right parties by warning of what they call civilizational decline. Leading voices in Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement have been using the French protests to ram home points about immigration ahead of the US midterm elections next month.
MAGA commentators have repeatedly posted videos of the French unrest, with Trump ally Glenn Beck saying on Monday that the “riots in France are a clear warning to the rest of the West”. Republicans are doubling down on migration and anti-transgender rhetoric amid fears that Trump’s unpopularity and his Iran war risk losing them control of Congress.
Police fired tear gas at protesters today outside French high schools as students, teachers and parents took to the streets on the biggest day of what Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu described as the ​most violent school protests in decades.
The protests, in which a teenager lost a hand on Monday, were the latest manifestation of public anger in a country where the far right ‌and far left are surging ahead of a presidential election in the spring.
The government is under pressure to tame public debt amid weak growth, and has struggled with basic tasks such as passing a budget since President Emmanuel Macron's allies lost their majority in a 2024 parliamentary vote.
Lecornu told lawmakers at least 215 teenagers and 85 school staff had so far been injured in clashes, "the heaviest toll in decades paid by the school system". His office said more than 700 police officers were also hurt.
Read: Teenager's hand blown off as French school protests enter third week
Macron has convened Lecornu and other senior ministers ​at an emergency meeting on Tuesday, broadcaster BFM reported.
In Marseille and Nantes, protesters held up signs reading "The state has killed national education". In Toulouse, parents linked arms at the front of a march through ​the city.
In Strasbourg, Lyon, Rennes and Paris, the demonstrations at times turned violent, with police firing tear gas and protesters lighting fires in the streets and hurling projectiles.
The ⁠Paris police said the clashes there had come about when some 300 people attempted to face off against security forces, adding that the protest was generally unfolding well elsewhere.
Nearly 2,000 high schools across France are closed as student protests over deteriorating school conditions enter their third week. The protests began in lower-income suburbs around Paris before spreading nationwide, with students joining in solidarity. Some parents and teachers… pic.twitter.com/Sc2g9aYfVi
— CBS News (@CBSNews) October 6, 2026
By late afternoon, they said they were still ​clashing with a small contingent of people. Three storefronts had been damaged.
The protests began in September in the deprived suburbs of Paris, before spreading nationwide.
"There is such a gap between the elites and us," said Hugo Vetzel, a ​recent high-school graduate in Strasbourg.
The High School Students Union said more than half of France's high schools were blockaded or would close for the day. Some local education authorities have tried to move classes online.
Students complain about schools facing basic maintenance problems, from water leaks to rat infestations.
🇫🇷 🪧 #France braced on Tuesday for a day of nationwide high-school ​blockades and trade union-led street #protests in support of #students demanding that President Emmanuel #Macron's cash-strapped government tackle the issue of understaffed and dilapidated schools. pic.twitter.com/974rzEqfem
— FRANCE 24 English (@France24_en) October 6, 2026
Thousands of arrests
Rights groups, students and parent groups have accused authorities of using disproportionate force against minors. The government says the protest movement has been hijacked by outsiders and in some places deteriorated into urban violence.
France's interior ministry said ​6,100 people have been arrested since the protests began, the overwhelming majority of them minors. More than 1,800 people are being prosecuted for unspecified crimes, including 1,483 minors, the justice ministry said.
A teenager's hand was blown off ​as high-school protesters clashed with riot police in northern France on Monday. The regional newspaper La Voix du Nord said the 15-year-old lost his hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police grenade intended to be non-lethal.
"They want to ‌divide the young ⁠people into good and bad protesters," said Omar Slaouti, a high-school teacher in Argenteuil, a northwestern suburb of Paris. "If there were no trash cans on fire, the government would not have stepped back and become aware of the issues at stake."
Six months before an election to replace Macron, his government and far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally party have accused hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) lawmakers and mayors of stoking the unrest. LFI denies the accusation.
"All the young people are in the streets. Everywhere there aren't police, everything is going smoothly," said Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's presidential candidate.
🇫🇷 🪧 💥 'Gen Z has risen up': Tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday, as unions and teachers joined high school students who for days have been demanding better learning conditions in protests punctuated by violent confrontations ➡️… pic.twitter.com/p4Gcpqdqw4
— AFP News Agency (@AFP) October 6, 2026
Prime minister promises a response
Lecornu has ordered his ministers to tackle the students' leading demands. Those include ensuring absent teachers are ​replaced, reviewing the length of the 8 am to ​6 pm school day and the need for longer ⁠lunch breaks.
The government will also look at repairs needed to ageing school buildings, said Lecornu, who demanded ministers send in their first proposals by the end of October.
Parent Emilie Lhomme said at a protest outside the Helene Boucher school in Paris that the government's words were not enough: "That's all fine and dandy, but that's not what's ​going to change the daily lives of our children," she said.
Finding spare cash to implement educational reforms will be difficult.
The government is under pressure to try ​to narrow a ballooning budget ⁠deficit as investor concerns about France's growing debt, weak growth and reluctance to rein in spending push the cost of borrowing higher. The yield on France's 10-year bonds briefly hit a 24-year high of over 5% last week.
The surge in French borrowing costs has started to spill into the broader euro area, with the sliding euro currency the latest alarm bell for policymakers. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said on Tuesday there was no need for the European Central Bank to step in.
Le ⁠Pen, the far-right ​euro-sceptic populist leading the presidential race ahead of next spring's election, set out plans to slash public spending if elected, seeking to establish ​her fiscal credibility as the bond market crisis deepens.
French spending on education has lagged inflation, and the country's students are trailing their OECD peers in overall performance, data from the PISA 2025 assessment shows.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Paramount Skydance on Tuesday completed its blockbuster $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, creating a Hollywood heavyweight called ‌Skydance and handing CEO David Ellison control of one of the world's largest entertainment companies.
The deal brings together the studios behind "Mission: Impossible", "Harry Potter" and DC Studios alongside major television and streaming networks such as CBS, CNN, Paramount+ and HBO Max — forming an expansive entertainment company spanning film, TV and news.
Shares of the combined company ​moved to the New York Stock Exchange from Nasdaq on Tuesday to trade under the ticker "SKYD".
Settlements with a coalition of US ​states and a Hollywood writers union removed the main legal barriers to the merger, one of the largest ⁠in media history. It comes as Hollywood faces declining cable-TV subscriptions, high cost of competing for streaming audiences and persistent pressure from unions ​over jobs and creative workers' rights.
Ellison said last week the Skydance name was chosen to retain the individual identities of Paramount and Warner Bros studios, ​rather than combining them under a new brand.
Read More: Paramount clears final hurdle for Warner takeover
Analysts, however, said the name reinforces the extent of Ellison's control, highlighting how some of Hollywood's most iconic brands now answer to him and how he has a platform to impose his strategy and culture.
In just 16 years, Skydance has gone from an independent studio to the ​centre of one of Hollywood's biggest power plays. Founded in 2010 by the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, it built its reputation ​as a financial backer and producer of Paramount's blockbuster "Top Gun: Maverick".
After merging with Paramount last year, Skydance set its sights on Warner Bros, entering a heated bidding ‌contest with ⁠Netflix while drawing interest from other potential suitors, including Comcast.
Warner Bros shareholders received an additional $41.9 million in "ticking fee", based on the number of days between September-end and the deal-closing, according to a regulatory filing.
Broader Hollywood bet
Ellison named Mattel's former CEO Ynon Kreiz as Skydance co-CEO to run day-to-day operations and lead the integration, while Ellison oversees creative direction and overall strategy.
The duo faces the task of combining two large companies while delivering $6 ​billion in planned cost savings, a ​big part of which Paramount ⁠said would come from "non-labour sources" — by combining streaming technologies and cloud providers of the two companies. However, the scale of the cuts is expected to affect jobs across Hollywood.
Skydance plans to combine its streaming services, ​including HBO Max and Paramount+, into a single service and has pledged to release at least 30 films ​each in the first ⁠two years after closing, rising to 32 a year for the following three.
The combined company is also expected to carry about $80 billion in debt, putting pressure on Ellison to grow streaming, preserve cash flow from cable networks and improve theatrical film performance.
Analysts at MoffettNathanson forecast EBITDA of $16 billion for 2028, ⁠rising to $19 ​billion in 2030. The brokerage also predicted about $67 billion in revenue in 2028 for ​the company, growing to roughly $70 billion in 2030.
CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss will continue in their respective leadership roles.
Ellison's annual base salary will be $5 million, ​with a target annual bonus of $5 million, according to the filing.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the government’s ₹10,000 Cr SME Growth Fund (SGF) to offer growth credit capital to small and medium enterprises.
Announced in Budget 2026-27, the fund will invest in high-potential SMEs across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains. A majority of the allocation of the fund will go towards manufacturing-focused enterprises.
The initiative aims to widen access to equity and liquidity for MSMEs and help promising Indian businesses scale into globally competitive companies.
The SGF is meant to fill the gap in growth capital for SMEs, as most existing funds focus on early-stage and micro enterprises. Under the framework, the government will commit ₹10,000 Cr to alternative investment funds (AIFs), that will subsequently invest in high-potential SMEs.
This will help businesses expand operations, increase manufacturing capacity, adopt new technologies, enter international markets and integrate into global supply chains.
Centre’s MSME Funding Push
The SGF is part of the government’s wider push to support the MSME sector via credit, digitalisation, ease of doing business, public procurement and other initiatives.
The fund will also support SMEs in industrial clusters across Tier II and Tier III cities, with the aim of strengthening local supply chains and creating jobs.
As part of the ‘Creating Champion MSMEs’ strategy announced in Budget 2026-27, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman had also proposed an additional ₹2,000 Cr for ‘Self-Reliant India Fund’ to support micro enterprises and provide them with access to risk capital.
The Budget also proposed several measures to improve cash flow for MSMEs through the Trade Receivables e-Discounting System (TReDS). This includes making TReDS the settlement platform for purchases from MSMEs by central public sector enterprises (CPSEs).
The government also proposed a credit guarantee mechanism through CGTMSE for invoice discounting on TReDS, linking the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) with TReDS and allowing TReDS receivables to be used as asset-backed securities.
As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, India’s MSME sector accounts for approximately 35.4% of manufacturing, around 48.58% of exports, and 31.1% of India’s GDP.
With over 7.47 Cr enterprises employing over 32.82 Cr persons, the sector holds its position as the second-largest employer after agriculture.
“With India’s manufacturing sector positioned for greater global integration, MSME sector’s role is critical in enabling effective supply-chain participation, fostering local value addition, and supporting inclusive regional growth,” the Survey said.

Swara Baby Products, a contract manufacturer of disposable hygiene products and a subsidiary of omnichannel kidswear brand FirstCry’s parent Brainbees Solutions, has received approval from SEBI for its proposed ₹1,000 Cr IPO.
Swara Baby Products filed its DRHP in July this year. According to SEBI’s latest processing status update, the regulator issued the final observation today.
The IPO will comprise a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹500 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of shares aggregating up to ₹500 Cr.
Brainbees Solutions, which owns a 76.6% stake in Swara Baby Products, will sell shares worth up to ₹300 Cr through the OFS. Another promoter selling shareholder, Anadya Bon Merchari LLP, will offload shares worth up to ₹200 Cr. The company may also consider a pre-IPO placement of up to ₹100 Cr.
Swara Baby Products plans to use the net proceeds from the fresh issue primarily to expand its manufacturing capacity and pare debt.
Around ₹198.2 Cr will be used to set up a new manufacturing facility in Madhya Pradesh, while ₹100 Cr will go towards repayment or prepayment of certain borrowings. Another ₹27.5 Cr will be invested in subsidiaries Solis Hygiene, Swara Hygiene and K.A. Enterprises Hygiene Pvt Ltd (KAEHPL) for debt repayment.
The company also plans to pursue inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions, alongside general corporate purposes.
Inside Swara Baby Products’ Business
Founded in 2018 by Alok Birla, Rahul Bubna and Ritum Jain, Swara Baby Products manufactures disposable hygiene products across the baby care, adult incontinence, and feminine hygiene categories.
Its portfolio includes baby pant-style and tape-style diapers, adult diapers, sanitary napkins and panty liners. The company primarily operates as a contract manufacturer for corporate customers, while also selling its own brands, including Cuddles in baby diapers and Shield in adult diapers.
Swara Baby Products counts Brainbees Solutions, Piramal Pharma, and Himalaya Wellness among its customers. It acquired feminine hygiene manufacturer KAEHPL in December 2025.
According to the DRHP, Swara Baby Products was India’s largest hygiene contract manufacturer by value in FY25 across baby diapers, adult diapers and sanitary napkins.
It held a 37% market share by value in India’s baby diaper contract manufacturing segment in FY25 and grew 21.9% YoY in FY26. In adult diapers, it held an estimated 36% market share by value in FY25, with the business growing 24.9% YoY in FY26.
The company currently operates four manufacturing facilities spread across 24 acres in Pithampur and Indore in Madhya Pradesh.
On the financial front, it reported a net profit of ₹95.6 Cr in FY26, up 18.5% from ₹80.7 Cr in FY25. Operating revenue grew 23.4% to ₹1,163 Cr from ₹943 Cr in FY25.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Jazz has emerged as Pakistan’s most expensive mobile operator for standard pay-as-you-go internet usage, charging Rs 5 per MB across several prepaid packages, according to the latest tariff data published by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA).
The PTA figures, updated on September 30, 2026, show that Jazz charges Rs 5 per MB under its listed Budget, Champion, Easy, One, and Lite packages, putting it above the standard mobile data rates offered by the country’s other major cellular operators.
At this rate, a prepaid Jazz user consuming just 100 MB of mobile data without an active bundle could spend Rs 500 before applicable taxes. One gigabyte of usage would theoretically cost more than Rs 5,000, highlighting the steep difference between standard tariffs and discounted bundle rates.
Jazz’s standard voice charges are also among the highest in the market. Most listed packages carry a rate of around Rs 3.50 per minute, while the Lite package reaches Rs 3.60 per minute. A Rs 0.15 call set-up fee also applies, while domestic SMS charges reach Rs 2.50 on several packages.
By comparison, Telenor and Zong charge Rs 4 plus tax per MB for standard mobile internet, while Ufone’s listed rate stands at Rs 2.75 plus tax per MB, making Jazz the costliest among the four major operators for standard data usage.
Telenor’s standard voice rates range from approximately Rs 2.92 to Rs 2.93 per minute plus tax, while Zong charges between Rs 2.68 and Rs 2.97 per minute plus tax depending on the package. Ufone charges Rs 3.50 per minute for standard voice calls.
The figures underline how quickly prepaid balances can be depleted when consumers use mobile services outside bundled packages. The impact can be particularly significant for low-income or occasional users who may not maintain weekly or monthly bundles.
Taxes further reduce the value available to consumers. According to PTA tariff information, a 15% withholding tax is deducted on mobile recharges, while a 19.5% sales tax applies to usage in applicable provinces and the federal territory.
As a result, the amount paid by a subscriber during a recharge is already reduced before the remaining balance is used for calls, messages, or mobile internet.
The tariff structure also creates a substantial gap between bundled and standard mobile services. Operators generally offer significantly lower effective data and voice rates through packages, but once a bundle expires or its allowance is exhausted, subscribers may automatically fall back on much higher standard tariffs.
For Jazz customers, that fallback can be particularly costly because of the Rs 5 per MB standard data rate.
The issue raises broader affordability concerns at a time when mobile internet has become essential for digital banking, education, employment, e-commerce, communication, and access to government services.
PTA advises consumers to verify current tariffs through operators’ official websites, mobile applications, and customer support channels, as promotional and regional offers may differ.

Telenor:
Telenor has the widest tariff range among the four operators, with monthly line rents starting at Rs600 for Freedom 500 and climbing to Rs4,741 for SMART 3000. Its packages offer varying combinations of data and voice allowances, with the higher-end packages carrying a substantially higher monthly cost.
Jazz:
Jazz’s postpaid line rents range from Rs1,600 for its Value package to Rs3,500 for Red Z/Postpaid Elite. Data allowances rise from 15 GB to 200 GB across the listed packages, while voice allowances also increase substantially at the higher end. Consumers therefore have to pay more than twice the entry-level rent to access the operator’s premium offering.
Zong:
Zong’s postpaid packages range from Rs800 for Bronze to Rs4,000 for Titanium. Data allowances range from 10 GB to 400 GB, while the higher-priced packages offer up to 5,000 on-net minutes and 5,000 SMS. The Rs4,000 Titanium package represents a five-fold increase over the entry-level Bronze tariff.
Ufone:
Ufone’s Prime postpaid range starts at Rs1,000 and rises to Rs2,400. Its data allowances range from 20 GB to 200 GB, with Prime Mega offering 200 GB data, 10,000 on-net minutes and 2,000 off-net minutes.
The comparison makes the pricing gap particularly evident: Telenor’s top-end monthly rent of Rs4,741 is nearly eight times its Rs600 entry-level package, while Zong’s Rs4,000 premium package is five times its Rs800 entry-level tariff. Jazz’s top package is more than twice its entry-level plan, while Ufone’s premium package costs 2.4 times its entry-level offering.
The disparity extends beyond monthly line rents. Standard usage charges also vary between operators. Jazz charges Rs2 per minute for on-net calls, compared with Rs1.25 per minute for Zong, while Telenor charges Rs1.40 per minute for on-net calls and Ufone Rs1.90.
For consumers, this means that the advertised monthly line rent does not necessarily represent the final cost of maintaining cellular connectivity, particularly for users who exhaust bundled data, minutes or SMS and subsequently rely on standard usage rates.
The PTA data further shows that monthly line rents include government taxes, while a 15 percent withholding tax is applicable on every recharge and 19.5 percent sales tax is charged on usage, adding to the overall cost of mobile communications.
The regulator has advised consumers to check operators’ websites, applications or call centres for the latest tariff details, as packages and promotional offers may change.
With mobile connectivity increasingly essential for banking, digital payments, education, employment and business, the wide variation in postpaid tariffs and the cost of premium packages underline the financial burden faced by consumers requiring larger data and voice allowances.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp has started blocking some users from logging into their accounts if their phones are running outdated operating systems. The new restriction affects selected users on both Android and iOS devices.
Affected users see a message asking them to update their phone’s operating system before they can access WhatsApp again. The restriction is applied through a server-side update, so it doesn’t depend on the WhatsApp version installed on the device.
WhatsApp has not yet confirmed exactly which Android or iOS versions are affected by the new login block.
WhatsApp Blocks Logins on Some Devices Running Outdated Operating Systems
According to information reported by WABetaInfo, affected users see a new screen directing them to their device settings. They are asked to install the latest operating system update available for their phone.
The prompt also provides instructions for users who are unsure which operating system version their device is currently running. After installing the required update, users can return to WhatsApp and log into their accounts.
There is currently no option to skip or bypass the requirement. Users who do not install the update remain unable to access their WhatsApp accounts.
Why WhatsApp Is Introducing the Restriction
Keeping a phone’s operating system updated is important for security. Older software can contain vulnerabilities that attackers may exploit to install malicious software or gain access to information stored on a device.
WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption to protect messages while they are being sent. However, the security of the device itself remains important. If a phone is compromised, attackers may potentially access information before it is protected by encryption or after it reaches the device.
The latest login restriction appears to be part of WhatsApp’s broader efforts to improve security and reduce risks linked to outdated or compromised devices.
WhatsApp Also Targets Unofficial Clients
WhatsApp has been taking additional steps to protect users from security threats. In Android beta version 2.26.35.1, the company reportedly began testing a warning for users who have unofficial WhatsApp Web clients connected to their accounts.
The move followed a case in Italy in which around 200 users were reportedly notified after their devices were compromised through a fake version of WhatsApp.
The company is also working on features designed to identify suspicious messages and warn users about potential scams. Another feature under development is restricted chats, which can keep selected conversations limited to a user’s primary device.
For now, users who receive the new operating system update prompt should follow the instructions and install the latest available software before trying to log into WhatsApp again.

items.content:
Google has contracted for 3,590 megawatts of power from Constellation Energy in the US' largest power grid, with new nuclear energy accounting for about ​a quarter of that supply, the companies said on Tuesday.
The deal will enable ‌more than $4.3 billion of new investment by Constellation and involves adding capacity at several of the power company's nuclear reactors in the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions, the companies said.
Major tech companies are racing to ​secure massive amounts of electricity supplies to power data centers across the US by ​striking unprecedented deals with the country's power companies.
Over the last two years, ⁠Constellation unveiled an agreement to restart its Three Mile Island reactor in Pennsylvania to ​serve Microsoft data centers, while Google contracted to restart NextEra Energy's nuclear power plant in Iowa.
In ​the latest arrangement, Google entered into a 20-year power purchase agreement for 890 megawatts of electricity from multiple Constellation-owned nuclear power plants, which would be upgraded to produce more electricity from existing reactors.
Read More: Instagram turns 16 with 3 billion users under shadow of data privacy, mental health concerns
Electricity from the ​first of the upgraded plants is expected to be delivered in 2028, the companies ​said.
Google also entered into a long-term supply agreement for an additional 2,700 megawatts of power from Constellation in ‌PJM. ⁠That power is not tied to a specific generation source and serves as long-term revenue certainty for Constellation's operating plants, Google said.
Maryland-based Constellation is the largest US nuclear power plant operator and owns a major fleet of natural-gas-fired power plants.
"We’re committed to meeting our growth responsibly ​by actively investing in ​clean, reliable power ⁠that brings new capacity to our nation's grids," said Amanda Peterson Corio, Google's global head of energy and power, in a statement.
The 11 ​nuclear units expected to be upgraded as part of the arrangement ​with Google ⁠are in Illinois, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey, within the footprint of the largest US electric grid - PJM Interconnection.
PJM management has proposed requiring data center customers connected to the 13-state grid to either ⁠bring ​their own power or face being shut off from ​grid power remotely in times of peak demand.
The deal between Google and Constellation is in response to PJM's "bring your ​own power" proposal, the companies said.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The federal government has accelerated work on its proposed “One Patient, One ID” initiative, which aims to create a unified medical record for every citizen and make patient histories accessible across hospitals and healthcare institutions.
A review meeting on the project was jointly chaired by Federal Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal and Minister for IT and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja, where officials assessed progress and agreed on a joint roadmap to accelerate implementation in line with the prime minister’s directions.
Under the proposed system, a citizen’s Computerized National Identity Card (CNIC) number would serve as the unique medical record number, allowing a patient’s medical history to remain linked to a single identity rather than being scattered across different hospitals and institutions.
Officials said the system would make it easier for doctors to access a patient’s previous medical history when they are transferred from one hospital to another, potentially improving continuity of care and reducing duplication in treatment and testing.
Shaza Fatima Khawaja said the initiative represents a closer integration of technology and healthcare, with digital medical records expected to make treatment systems more transparent, efficient, and modern.
The meeting also emphasized the need to finalize clear Terms of Reference (TORs) and practical implementation measures to ensure the project does not face further delays or unnecessary duplication.
Health Minister Mustafa Kamal stressed that the initiative should move beyond prolonged discussions and be converted into a documented, actionable framework. He said issues that have remained under discussion for the past 14 to 15 months should now be formally recorded and addressed through specific responsibilities and timelines.
The government has also decided to conduct a third-party review and audit of the project. According to Kamal, the review will provide an independent assessment of progress, identify weaknesses, and recommend corrective measures needed before wider implementation.
Officials agreed that possible shortcomings and corresponding remedies should be incorporated into the project’s TORs, while all relevant institutions should be assigned clearly defined responsibilities.
The meeting also agreed to activate an IT wing within the Ministry of Health to support the operation, understanding and management of the system once it becomes functional.
Kamal said Pakistan currently lacks a universal medical record database and that the proposed system is intended to address this gap by placing a patient’s full health history under a single digital identity.
Once implemented, the Universal Medical Record system is expected to allow authorized healthcare providers to access a patient’s medical history across participating institutions, helping doctors make more informed decisions when patients move between hospitals.
The government said all relevant departments have agreed to work through a common mechanism to bring the project to completion and move it into practical implementation as quickly as possible.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
In ancient mythology, the phoenix was a miraculous bird with a cyclical pattern of life and death, perishing in flames only to rise again from the ashes. Astronomers have now found a world that rightly can be called a phoenix planet.
Researchers said this exoplanet, as planets beyond our solar system are called, appears to have been born from material expelled into space during the death throes of a star a bit bigger than the sun, and now orbits the highly compact stellar remnant that was left behind, called a white dwarf.
It is classified as a second-generation planet, meaning it did not form from the swirling disk of material surrounding a newborn star, as Earth and other first-generation planets did, but rather from the leftovers of a doomed star.
"This is the first example of a planet forming around a white dwarf," said Jamie Williams, a doctoral student in astrophysics at the University of Warwick in England and lead author of the study published this week in the journal Nature Astronomy.
The white dwarf is located about 250 light-years from Earth, near the constellation Cetus. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, 5.9 trillion miles (9.5 trillion km).
The planet is a gas giant perhaps slightly more massive than Jupiter, our solar system's largest planet. It orbits the white dwarf every 4.4 days at only 4% the distance between Earth and the sun.
It is so close that the blazingly hot white dwarf's extreme ultraviolet radiation is causing the planet's outer atmosphere to evaporate, with a portion then falling into the white dwarf.
The planet's chemical pattern points to its second-generation origin. It is rich in niobium, copper and zinc, the type of elements that certain dying stars cast off when they expand in their death throes, indicating the planet formed from a disk of this expelled material that surrounded the stellar corpse.
"In myths, a phoenix is born again from its own ashes. In the case of this planet, it is born again from the ashes of its dying host star, and therefore the planetary system is reborn. A second-generation planet is defined as one born after its host star dies - in this case after it has become a white dwarf," Williams said.
Read More: Chinese rocket firm, disease research lab to test space pharmaceutical payloads
The researchers used data from the orbiting Hubble, TESS and FUSE telescopes, and hope to use the James Webb Space Telescope to confirm their conclusions.
A small number of potential second-generation planets previously have been identified orbiting pulsars, a rare type of neutron star, another type of stellar remnant.
"White dwarfs are much more common than pulsars, and over 95% of stars in the Milky Way will evolve to become a white dwarf. Therefore, there would be many more second-generation planets around white dwarfs than around pulsars," Williams said.
While the newly discovered planet would be inhospitable for life, another second-generation planet potentially could be habitable.
"If a gas giant formed around a white dwarf, then a rocky planet could form, too. White dwarfs cool predictably over time and as they get cooler, their cooling slows. So if a second-generation rocky planet formed close enough to the white dwarf then it could remain in the habitable zone for billions of years," Williams said.
A red dwarf and a brown dwarf
A second study published in the same journal describes another exotic celestial phenomenon roughly 300 to 500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Taurus.
Researchers used the Zwicky Transient Facility at Palomar Observatory in California to discover a red dwarf star about 8% of the mass of the sun in a tight orbit with a brown dwarf, an object too small to be a star and too big to be a planet.
The brown dwarf is about 30 times the mass of Jupiter and a third of the mass of the star.
These two companions orbit each other every 87 minutes at slightly more than half the distance between Earth and the moon, and the star's gravitational pull appears to be siphoning material from the brown dwarf.
The researchers detected a hot spot on the star's surface where this material appears to be landing.
"This is the first observed example of this phenomenon," said Aaron Householder, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology graduate student in astrophysics and lead author of the study.
"The two objects are so close together that the entire orbit would fit inside the sun," Householder said.
