Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Physioplus’ AI Stack Track India’s Recovery Journey?
Physiotherapy often breaks down between appointments. While patients struggle to follow exercises, therapists lack real-time visibility into progress. To solve this, Physioplus is building a digital layer that keeps assessment and recovery tracking connected beyond the clinic.
A Digital Coach: Founded in 2022, Physioplus’ AI-powered platform helps patients discover physiotherapists, book consultations, request home visits and receive support for chronic pain and post-surgery rehabilitation. The platform is designed to make access more convenient while helping clinicians understand a patient’s history before treatment begins.
The Rehabilitation Stack: For practitioners, Physioplus combines digital practice management, patient records, clinical assessments, documentation and tech-enabled monitoring. Its monitoring layer also supports home-based rehabilitation by capturing exercise adherence, pain changes and functional progress over time.
Growing Steadily: Physioplus claims to have so far onboarded over 1,000 patients. It is now focusing on scaling product development, expanding its physiotherapist network and fueling growth across India. With the homegrown digital health and rehabilitation market projected to become a $14.8 Bn opportunity by 2033, can Physioplus make physiotherapy more measurable and consistent beyond the clinic?

items.content:
From: Promise Adagba (Akure), Baba Martins, Idowu Isamotu (Abuja) & Abdullateef Aliyu (Lagos)
 
Residents of Igbokoda in Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State have recounted moments when a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft crashed into a swampy area near the coastal community on Monday.
Some of the witnesses, who spoke to Daily Trust, said they heard a loud explosion from the direction of the waterways as people thronged the area in panic.
They described seeing bodies, pieces of the aircraft and personal belongings scattered across the waterlogged crash site.
The aircraft, later confirmed by the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) as an ATR-42 with tail number NGR 931, was carrying 32 people — 25 passengers and seven crew members — on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos on Monday when it crashed into the swamp opposite the Naval Base in Igbokoda.
A community leader, Hosea Maha, said the explosion was the first indication that something had gone wrong.
“We were fishing on the other side of the river when we heard a big explosion inside the water. We mobilised ourselves to the area around 10 a.m. We later discovered that an incident must have happened,” he said.
Maha said the difficult terrain prevented residents from getting close to the wreckage.
“We couldn’t enter where the aircraft was because it was a deep swamp area that our boat could not even reach, but we saw body parts scattered all over the waterside. We immediately reported the situation to naval officers,” he said.
Oluboyo Olusola, one of the residents who got close to the crash area, said he saw aircraft parts, clothes and remains around the site.
“After the incident, I was here personally. I saw many things. I saw parts of the aircraft, I saw parts of bodies that were scattered and clothes. Other bodies are inside the water,” he told Daily Trust.
According to Olusola, some of the clothing found at the scene appeared to belong to women and children.
“We also saw children’s clothes and female clothing,” he said.
For Abayomi Festus, reaching the crash site was difficult because of its location inside the creek.
“We heard a very loud sound in the area where the incident occurred, but we could not get there because the place is a swampy area inside the creek; we were just looking at it from afar,” he added.
He said security personnel later moved into the area as residents waited anxiously for news from the crash site.
Debris from the crash
“The police and the military people later came around there for rescue, but the occupants of the aircraft might have died there,” he said.
Another witness, Akinte Oluwatere, said the aircraft had already gone deep into the swamp, making it impossible for residents to rescue anyone.
“There was nothing we could do to rescue anybody because the plane had already entered the swamp,” he said.
He added that naval personnel arrived shortly afterwards and joined the effort to access the crash location.
“It was around 10 a.m. It took naval officers like 30 minutes to arrive. They entered that place with us, but when we got there, there was nothing we could do to rescue them,” he said.
Ayedugbe Abel said the heavy rainfall at the time further complicated efforts to locate the exact crash site.
“This morning, it was raining here around 10:30. We just heard a sudden cry of a jet. We did not know exactly whether it was a plane, jet or helicopter. We knew that something dropped there,” he said.
According to him, residents immediately mobilised to search for the aircraft and its occupants.
“Our people here tried a lot. Even women and men took canoes to cross to that place to rescue them,” he said.
Abel said the community’s efforts were constrained by the difficult terrain.
“We tried our best, but unfortunately we could not locate the exact place. Police have come, naval personnel and government agents have come. Some people even swam to the place,” he said.
Chief Press Secretary to the Chairman of Ilaje Local Government Area, Taiwo Sadare, who joined officials moving towards the crash scene, said the local government, naval personnel and the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) were involved in the response.
“The chairman of the local government, naval personnel and NEMA personnel were moving to the scene where it happened. I was in the entourage. A helicopter was deployed from Abuja to monitor the situation and locate the place,” he said.
Sadare said preliminary information from the scene suggested that bad weather may have affected the aircraft.
“When I got to the scene, I made findings there. They said it was poor weather conditions that affected the pilot. He was trying to manoeuvre, but the poor weather conditions affected him. The aircraft caught fire before it eventually crashed into a swampy area very close to the water, behind the Naval Base,” he said.
However, the cause of the crash had yet to be officially established as of the time of filing the report.
For the traditional ruler of Igbokoda, Oba Afolabi Odidiomo, the location of the crash prevented what could have been an even greater tragedy.
The monarch said he initially feared that the aircraft might have been a passenger plane and could have crashed into the densely populated part of the community.
“I was praying and hoping it was not a plane because the number of casualties would be high. Our first gratitude is to Almighty God that it did not crash inside the town,” he told Daily Trust.
According to him, the aircraft came down across a river in a bushy and waterlogged area.
“It fell across the river into the bush. The area is currently waterlogged because of the rains,” he said.
The monarch added that there were no reports of survivors at the time he spoke.
“So far, there have not been any survivors,” he said.
In a statement issued by his Chief Press Secretary, Ebenezer Adeniyan, the Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, also expressed sadness over the incident and extended condolences to the Nigerian Air Force and the families of those on board.
 
NAF, Keyamo speak on crash
The Nigerian Air Force, while confirming that one of its aircraft crashed, said it had activated search-and-rescue operations.
Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, also confirmed the crash, saying air traffic controllers lost contact with the aircraft at about 9:13 a.m.
Ehimen Ejodame, an Air Commodore, noted that the Force was committed to ensuring the success of the ongoing search and rescue efforts.
The senior military officer said in a statement issued after the incident that further details would be provided to the public as the rescue operations progress.
He said, “The Nigerian Air Force has activated an immediate Search and Rescue operation following an ATR-42 aircraft accident in the Igbokoda area of Ondo State on 5 October 2026.
“The aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred. Search and Rescue operations, in coordination with relevant authorities and emergency response agencies, are currently ongoing.
“The NAF is committed to ensuring the success of the ongoing Search and Rescue efforts. Further details will be communicated in due course.”
Keyamo, in a statement, said the aircraft, with registration number NGR 931, disappeared while en route from Benin to Lagos at about 9:13 a.m.
He said air traffic controllers alerted authorities after attempts to establish radio contact with the aircraft failed.
According to the minister, subsequent information confirmed that the military aircraft had crashed close to the Naval Base in Igbokoda, with the wreckage already located.
He said search and rescue operations were ongoing.
“Preliminary information suggests that there were 25 passengers and seven crew members on board,” Keyamo said.
The minister clarified that the control and regulation of military aircraft are outside the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).
He, however, said he had spoken with the Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and pledged the ministry’s “total cooperation and assistance” in the ongoing search and rescue operation.
“Further information on this unfortunate incident will be made available subsequently,” he added.
Residents watch as search for missing persons continues
 
Timeline of plane crashes
Daily Trust reports that with the latest incident, about 20 military plane crashes have been recorded since 2015.
On August 29, 2015, the Dornier 228, NAF030, crashed into Ribadu Cantonment (Old NDA) in Kaduna State on Saturday, killing all seven passengers. On October 10, 2015, one person was killed when an F-7NI fighter jet crashed during training in Kaduna. AgustaWestland 101 helicopter handed to the Nigerian Air Force by the Presidency suffered a “mishap” while taxing on a tarmac in Makurdi, Benue State, on November 15, 2016.
On July 6, 2017, an Agusta 109 light utility helicopter ditched after a technical fault in Borno State. No deaths were recorded. Months later, on September 28, 2018, two F-7NI fighter jets collided during Independence Day rehearsal in Abuja, killing one person. On January 2 2019, five persons – Flight Lieutenant Perowei Jacob, Flight Lieutenant Kaltho Paul Kilyof, Sergeant Auwal Ibrahim, Lance Corporal Adamu Nura and Meshack Ishmael were killed when a Mi-35M attack helicopter crashed during a combat support operation in Damasak, Borno,
On June 12, 2019, a NAF helicopter crash-landed in Katsina while returning from an anti-banditry combat mission in the Northwest Theatre under Operation HADARAN DAJI. No lives were lost in the incident. Two months later, on August 17, 2019, an RV-6A Air Beetle trainer aircraft crashed in Kaduna, killing one person. The following month, on November 14, 2019, a NAF training helicopter crashed in Enugu, but nobody died.
On February 21, 2021, a Beechcraft King Air 350i crashed after engine failure in Abuja, killing seven persons. The following month, on March 31, Alpha Jet lost radar contact during a combat operation in Borno. Two crew members died in the crash. Less than two months later, on May 21, 2021, Beechcraft King Air 350 with registration number NAF 203 crashed near Kaduna Airport, killing 11 persons, including the Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Ibrahim Attahiru.
On July 18, 2021, an Alpha Jet was shot down during a counter-insurgency operation in Zamfara. However, the pilot ejected and survived. Nine months later, on April 19, 2022, a Super Mushshak trainer aircraft crashed in Kaduna, killing two crew members: Flt. Abubakar Muhammed Alkali and Flt. Elijah Haruna Karatu. On July 14, 2023 FT-7NI trainer aircraft crashed during training in Makurdi, Benue. Two pilots successfully ejected.
On August 14, 2023, an MI-171E helicopter crashed during a casualty evacuation mission in Niger State. Eleven persons, including two pilots and two crew members, were killed. On December 1, 2023, an MI-35P attack helicopter crashed shortly after takeoff in Port Harcourt, but all five crew survived.
Three months later, on March 7, 2024, a NAF Super Mushshak trainer crashed in Zaria, Kaduna State. No deaths were recorded during the incident, as the pilots survived the crash.
No fewer than 8 people were killed on October 24, 2024 Sikorsky S76C+ helicopter, with registration number 5N-BQG, crashed into the Atlantic Ocean near Bonny Finima, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.
The aircraft, operated by Eastwind Aviation, was en route from Port Harcourt Military Base to NUIMANTAN oil rig when it crashed.
An investigation conducted by the NSIB after the incident revealed that the helicopter was not fitted with a Flight Data Recorder (FDR) in accordance with the Nigeria Civil Aviation Regulations 2023, and the radio altimeter was faulty.
On December 6, 2025, a NAF Alpha Jet was in an in-flight emergency during a post-inspection test flight, near Karabonde, Borgu LGA, close to NAF Base Kainji. Two pilots were injured and subsequently ejected for treatment.
In the same month, a Hawker 800XP private jet, operated by Flybird Aircraft Management, had a nose gear collapse during landing in Lagos. All eight occupants escaped unharmed.
 
Tinubu orders probe of crash
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has expressed sadness over the latest crash in Ondo State and directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash.
This was disclosed by Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy in a statement on Monday.
Onanuga said the president extended his deepest condolences to the family of the 25 passengers and seven crew members involved, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and all officers, airmen and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force.
The president also declared a three-day national mourning for those who died in the crash and directed that flags should be flown at half-mast throughout the country as a mark of respect to the officers.
He said the Air Force would release the officers’ names after contacting their families.
The statement read in part, “The president explained that he had been briefed about what happened. This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation. Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten.
“The Chief of Air Staff has briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences. I commend the Nigerian Air Force for activating an immediate Search and Rescue operation following the accident.
“I pray for the repose of the souls of the gallant officers and for Almighty God to grant their families and the Nigerian Air Force the fortitude to bear the unfortunate loss.”
President Tinubu also assured the Nigerian Air Force of the continued support of his administration as “they continue their vital role in securing our nation.”
“I also commend the swift response of first responders and the Ondo State Government at the crash site,” he added.
 
NSIB offers assistance
The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) has offered to provide technical support to the Air Force through its investigators and Flight Safety Laboratory for the recovery, readout and analysis of flight recorder data if formally requested.
In a statement signed by its Director General and Chief Executive Officer, Captain Alex Badeh Jr., the Bureau expressed condolences to the Nigerian Air Force and the families and colleagues of those on board.
The NSIB said search and rescue operations had been activated and were ongoing in coordination with relevant authorities and emergency response agencies.
It also commended the first responders and search and rescue teams working at the crash site.
However, the Bureau clarified that investigative responsibility rests with the Nigerian Air Force because the accident involved a military aircraft.
“The Bureau will provide assistance upon a formal request from the Air Force,” the NSIB said.
The NSIB’s offer of technical assistance means that, although the military retains responsibility for investigating the accident, the civilian aviation safety agency could provide specialist expertise, particularly in the recovery and analysis of flight recorder data.
The statement said, “The NSIB stands ready to assist the Nigerian Air Force, at its request, with whatever technical support may be required. That support can include the deployment of investigators and the use of the Bureau’s Flight Safety Laboratory for the recovery, readout and analysis of flight recorder data.
“As this occurrence involves a military aircraft, investigative responsibility rests with the Nigerian Air Force. The Bureau will provide assistance upon a formal request from the Air Force. The NSIB commends the swift activation of Search and Rescue and the efforts of first responders at Igbokoda.
“The public is urged to rely exclusively on official updates from the Nigerian Air Force on the rescue operation and on any investigation. Further comment from the Bureau will be issued only as appropriate, and in consultation with the Nigerian Air Force.”

items.author: Hamisu Kabir Matazu
items.content:
Twin sisters died forty eight hours apart in Yobe State, Daily Trust gathered. The deceased sisters—Dr. Hadiyah Usman and Dr. Aidah Usman (PharmD), who were 28-years-old, were children of Dr. Hadiza Usman and Dr. Usman Abdullahi.
The mother of the deceased, Professor Hadiza Abdullahi Usman, is the Medical Director of the Federal Medical Centre, Nguru, Yobe State, while their father, Professor Usman Abdullahi, is a senior consultant.
According to family sources, one of them, Hadiyah, fell ill due to a sickle cell crisis which she has battled for years, and was admitted to FMC Nguru. She later succumbed to the crisis and passed away on Friday. Funeral prayers were held on the same say at the emir’s palace in Nguru.
Our correspondent gathered that within the same period, her twin sister, Aidah, had a crisis and was receiving treatment at the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital.
One of the family members, who spoke to our correspondent, said it was not unusual as it was a long-standing pattern where the twins took ill simultaneously even when apart at different locations.
“In fact the family was used to it. Anytime one of the twins took ill, the parents knew that the other will fall ill as well,” he said.
He said after Aidah recovered and was discharged from the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital, she travelled to Nguru, to join her grieving parents and mourn her sister’s death.
“On arrival, Aidah insisted that she would visit her sister’s grave to pay her respects. Her mother, a medical doctor, was not comfortable with it, but had to give in when she saw that the girl was determined to go to the site”, he said.
Also speaking to our correspondent, was an uncle to the twins, Ibrahim Hasbunallah, who served as their guardian in Maiduguri.
The twin sisters
He said he was fortunate to hold the twins on the day they were born as they were handed to him by their parents shortly after their birth.
“They were handed over to me at birth, and I used the same hands to put them in their graves—one on Friday and the other one on Sunday,” he recounted.
He said the sisters, both born with sickle cell anemia, shared a bond that defied ordinary sibling relationships.
According to him, they kept strictly to themselves, having no friends.
“They were always indoors; they read together, ate together, played together and slept together. That was their routine,” he said.
He said, despite their health condition, the sisters excelled academically, gaining admission to study Medicine and Pharmacy at the University of Maiduguri.
It was gathered that after graduation, they worked at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) Nguru.
“Sadly, both sisters fell ill simultaneously, one receiving treatment at the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital (UMTH) and the other at FMC Nguru, while their mother was away in Saudi Arabia,” he said.
Hasbunallah said the eldest twin passed away before the mother could return, while the surviving twin died shortly after their mother returned.
“When the younger twin came in from Maiduguri, she refused to sleep throughout the night, insisting that she wanted to visit her sister’s grave,” he said.
Accompanied by her mother, husband, younger sister (now the family’s sole surviving child), and Hasbunallah, she visited the graveside.
After we prayed, she refused to leave. Right from home, she told me that she must follow her sister. She said her sister cannot die and leave her. ‘What am I going to do here?’ she said,” Hasbunallah recalled.
“She later appeared weak and started shaking, so her husband and younger sister rushed to support her, but she fainted before they could steady her. She was rushed to the hospital at around 3:30 p.m, where she passed away in the Intensive Care Unit. She died shortly after the Asr prayer around 4:10 p.m”, the uncle narrated.
When Daily Trust reached out to their father, he only managed to confirm the incident as he could barely speak.
Speaking in a calm tone, he asked for understanding and time, saying he would speak to our correspondent at a later date.
In an appreciation message issued after the burial, the mother, Professor Hadiza Usman, thanked relatives, friends, colleagues, professional associations, religious leaders, traditional rulers, government officials, staff of FMC Nguru and other well-wishers who have stood by the family.
“I am deeply touched by the overwhelming show of love, solidarity, prayers and support we have received”, she said.

items.title: Why kids keep touching your face while talking, per psychology
items.summary: Children frequently display physical affection towards their parents, such as gently touching their faces while talking. This interaction not only nurtures a sense of closeness but also helps them assess their parents' engagement. Studies indicate that such affectionate gestures are crucial for emotional growth throughout childhood. Parents must recognize the importance of these moments while also upholding appropriate boundaries to enhance emotional safety and deepen the parent-child relationship.

items.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said the number of registered voters in Nigeria has risen to more than 103 million ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this on Monday 5 October, in Abuja at a strategic workshop with media executives organised by the Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) in collaboration with the commission.
The workshop was themed, “Strengthening Democracy Through Partnership Among Editors, Civil Society and Electoral Institutions.”
Amupitan said the three-phase Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise attracted 10,772,421 new registrants, comprising 2,611,266 in the first phase, 4,121,835 in the second and 3,867,997 in the third phase.
He, however, said the figures remained subject to final verification following the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) exercise.
“Following the conclusion of our three-phase Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise, which captured over 10.6 million new applicants, our Voter Register Department has completed the final Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) cleanup. Nigeria’s National Register of Voters is now over 103 million,” he said.
The INEC chairman said the commission had completed eight of the 14 major statutory activities contained in its timetable for the 2027 elections, describing the preparations as having entered the “amber zone” as the election countdown intensifies.
He said the preliminary display of the voters’ register for claims and objections would take place from October 9 to 15, 2026.
Amupitan also announced that nationwide collection of Permanent Voters’ Cards (PVCs) would commence on Friday, October 9, with newly produced cards to be distributed to Local Government Area collection centres.
He said the commission had introduced printable PVC technology to reduce the waiting period for voters to obtain their cards.
According to him, the technology would also help eligible voters who lose their cards or have them stolen to avoid being disenfranchised.
The commission, Amupitan said, had acquired 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines as part of efforts to strengthen its technological infrastructure ahead of the elections.
He said INEC deliberately chose to improve existing electoral technologies rather than introduce untested systems shortly before the 2027 elections.
According to him, the upgraded BVAS, enhanced electronic result management system and other technologies were being deployed to ensure that every valid vote counted and was seen to count.
He said the commission had also introduced an enhanced eEC8A form designed to digitise and cryptographically authenticate polling-unit results before their upload to the INEC Result Viewing (IReV) portal.
Amupitan added that INEC was deploying artificial intelligence-driven systems to detect anomalies in database traffic and strengthen cybersecurity around the electoral process.
On vote-buying and illegal campaign financing, the INEC chairman said the commission was working with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) to monitor campaign spending.
He said a joint financial monitoring mechanism would track suspicious and illegal campaign expenditure, while surveillance around polling units would also be strengthened and warned politicians and their agents that violations of the Electoral Act would attract arrest and prosecution.
The INEC chairman also expressed concern over the spread of false information on social media, describing malicious disinformation as “citizenship terrorism through social media.”
He urged editors and journalists to verify information before publication, warning that false reports could suppress voter turnout, create panic and ultimately undermine credible elections.
Amupitan recalled instances where old photographs, manipulated images and fabricated reports had been presented as current election-related events.
He said INEC was particularly concerned about deepfakes, manipulated audio-visual materials, coordinated fake news and premature declaration of unofficial results.
The chairman said INEC was also strengthening logistics and field operations, adding that readiness audits had been completed in the South-West and North-West geopolitical zones.
He added that all electoral officers and temporary staff would be required to take an oath of neutrality under Section 26 of the Electoral Act 2026.
Earlier, President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors, Eze Anaba, called for a credible and transparent electoral process that would ensure voters, rather than the courts, determine the outcome of elections.
Anaba said elections were not merely about casting ballots but about building citizens’ confidence that their votes would count and that institutions responsible for conducting elections would act fairly and professionally.

items.content:
Gombe State approaches the 2027 general election amid competing ambitions, shifting loyalties and a complicated struggle for succession. Beneath the three-party contest lies a deeper calculation: who controls the structures of mobilisation, and which combination of interests can produce a winning coalition across the state’s diverse constituencies? The roles of the key actors suggest the election will test the durability of godfatherism, the limits of party authority and the capacity of established actors to turn personal influence into electoral support.
The most consequential development is Pantami’s victory in the PDP’s fresh governorship primary on Tuesday, September 29. Having initially emerged through a disputed process subsequently nullified by the Federal High Court, Pantami returned to the contest and defeated Khamisu Mailantarki and Usman Aliyu Garry, polling 2,054 votes against 389 and 112, respectively. The rerun followed a September 24 judgment ordering a fresh primary after irregularities in the earlier process.
His national profile as a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Islamic scholar and public intellectual, provides considerable visibility, but visibility and electoral strength are different resources. His immediate challenge is to convert primary support into a broader coalition, beginning with the relationships exposed by the legal dispute between him, Mailantarki and Garry that led to the litigation. Whether the PDP reconciles these interests will determine whether his victory becomes a foundation for party unity or another episode in its internal disagreements.
Meanwhile, the APC enters with Jamilu Isiyaku Gwamna, whose emergence followed Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s consultations with party stakeholders. Gwamna represents an attempt to sustain the outgoing governor’s political legacy. However, Gwamna must mobilise support independently while maintaining the relationships that made his emergence possible.
In Gombe Central, Goje’s exclusion from the APC senatorial ticket has exposed tensions within the party. After four consecutive terms representing the zone, the former governor lost the ticket to retired Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohammed Ahmed Deba. This dispute reflects competing interests, including the argument for rotation between Akko and Yamaltu/Deba.
Goje’s public declaration has sharpened the disagreement. While reaffirming his APC membership, he reportedly urged supporters not to vote for candidates he associated with the denial of his ticket, including the party’s candidates for Gombe Central, Akko and Yamaltu/Deba federal constituencies. He described his treatment as a betrayal and called those responsible “mugaye” (wicked).
Goje is not necessarily abandoning the APC; he is challenging the assumption that his supporters must automatically accept every candidate the party produces. The people Goje called “mugaye” may include Governor Inuwa Yahaya and Usman Bello Kumo (World), the APC candidate for Akko Federal Constituency and a figure associated with Goje’s political network. Their disagreement illustrates the changing nature of political mentorship, described as godfatherism but really about the redistribution of authority between established figures and emerging politicians.
The consequences may extend beyond the senatorial contest: if Goje’s supporters withhold support from APC candidates, the party could face difficulties where his networks remain influential. Yet that influence cannot be assumed; it depends on whether personal loyalty translates into actual voting behaviour.
In Gombe North, the anticipated confrontation between Dankwambo and Inuwa adds another dimension. Their rivalry dates to the 2015 governorship election; now their ambitions converge on the senatorial seat—Inuwa on the APC ticket, Dankwambo seeking re-election under the PDP. Inuwa, ending his second term, seeks to maintain his political presence through the Senate; Dankwambo must defend his seat against a challenger with access to the governing party’s structure.
The ADC’s governorship candidate, Alhaji Bala Bello Tinka, offers a third-party option that could attract dissatisfied members and voters seeking an alternative to the two dominant parties, especially the APC. Though his influence depends on building a credible structure beyond his immediate supporters Alhaji Saidu Alkali, who contested against Gwamna before withdrawing, reaffirmed his party loyalty, but the distinction between formal membership and active campaign commitment will matter considerably. Whether his supporters align with Gwamna or explore alternative arrangements could influence the APC’s position in the zone.
Gombe South, a zone comprising Balanga, Billiri, Kaltungo and Shongom, may emerge as an important balancing ground. Its significance lies not simply in the votes it contributes but in the relationships required for a statewide coalition. The APC has Jerry Damara as its senatorial candidate and the PDP Anthony Siyako Yaro; how the three campaigns approach geographical representation, local alliances and development expectations will matter greatly. The choice of running mates will attract attention, as the zone’s distinct political interests and development concerns require more than symbolic representation.
No single district can determine the governorship election; the outcome will depend on how support is distributed statewide and how well candidates consolidate their constituencies. Gombe South could nevertheless prove decisive if the contest is close.
These developments also unfold within a competitive communication environment. As we see on social media, disagreements over tickets become narratives of betrayal, court judgments become stories of legitimacy, and defections are read as courage or opportunism. Political influence is exercised not only through party structures but through shaping how voters understand political developments. The real test will be whether these narratives translate into credible responses to the challenges confronting the people of Gombe.
The significance of the election campaign lies in the changing relationship between political influence and political authority. Goje’s experience demonstrates how a long-standing political structure can encounter resistance from within its own party. The Dankwambo-Inuwa contest illustrates how political rivalry can survive changes in office. Pantami’s emergence shows how a political setback, including judicial intervention, can create another opportunity for consolidation. Gombe South, meanwhile, reminds both parties that statewide electoral success requires a coalition extending beyond their immediate stronghold.
Dr Danladi ia Editor-at-Large, Media Trust

items.title: 5 Game Indie Asia Tenggara di App Store Soroti Satwa Langka, Ada Badak Jawa
items.summary:
Biasanya isu konservasi swasta selalu dihadirkan lewat film dokumenter atau kampanye lingkungan. Namun kali ini, sejumlah developer game indie di Asia Tenggara memilih pendekatan berbeda ke dalam game buatan mereka yang rilis di Apple App Store.
Bertepatan dengan Hari Hewan Sedunia pada 4 Oktober, para developer ini memasukkan satwa terancam punah ke dalam dunia permainan mereka. Dengan gameplay, karakter pendamping, hingga misi khusus, pengembang mencoba mengenalkan satwa asli kawasan Asia Tenggara kepada pemain global.
Menariknya, beberapa spesies yang diangkat dan tampil di dalam game yang tampil di App Store tersebut berasal dari Indonesia, termasuk badak Jawa yang kini masuk kategori satwa paling terancam di dunia.
Daftar Game Indie Asia Tenggara di App Store Pilihan Apple
Nah, berikut ini adalah 5 game indie Asia Tenggara yang menghadirkan satwa langka pilihan Apple untuk bisa langsung di download dari App Store.
Submarine Quest: Misi Menyelamatkan Dugong Thailand
Submarine Quest
items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Biasanya isu konservasi swasta selalu dihadirkan lewat film dokumenter atau kampanye lingkungan. Namun kali ini, sejumlah developer game indie di Asia Tenggara memilih pendekatan berbeda ke dalam game buatan mereka yang rilis di Apple App Store.
Bertepatan dengan Hari Hewan Sedunia pada 4 Oktober, para developer ini memasukkan satwa terancam punah ke dalam dunia permainan mereka. Dengan gameplay, karakter pendamping, hingga misi khusus, pengembang mencoba mengenalkan satwa asli kawasan Asia Tenggara kepada pemain global.
Menariknya, beberapa spesies yang diangkat dan tampil di dalam game yang tampil di App Store tersebut berasal dari Indonesia, termasuk badak Jawa yang kini masuk kategori satwa paling terancam di dunia.
Daftar Game Indie Asia Tenggara di App Store Pilihan Apple
Nah, berikut ini adalah 5 game indie Asia Tenggara yang menghadirkan satwa langka pilihan Apple untuk bisa langsung di download dari App Store.
Submarine Quest: Misi Menyelamatkan Dugong Thailand
Submarine Quest: Misi Menyelamatkan Dugong Thailand. (Doc: Apple)
Dikembangkan oleh studio asal Thailand, Submarine Quest mengajak pemain menjelajahi bawah laut menggunakan kapal selam sambil menyelesaikan teka-teki dan mengelola sumber daya.
Dalam konten bertema konservasi, pemain ditugaskan membantu penyelamatan dugong, mamalia laut yang populasinya terus menurun di perairan Thailand dan beberapa wilayah Asia Tenggara.
Book dan Toon dari Khaolam Interactive mengatakan, dugong dipilih karena statusnya yang semakin mengkhawatirkan di alam liar.
“Dugong benar-benar terancam punah di perairan Asia Tenggara. Kami ingin meningkatkan kesadaran tentang satwa ini lewat gameplay yang terasa alami, sehingga pemain bisa memahami kondisi dugong hanya dengan bermain,” ujar mereka dalam keterangan resminya, Selasa (6/10/2026).
Menurut tim pengembang game Submarine Quest, pendekatan tersebut membuat pesan konservasi tidak terasa menggurui. Pemain juga dapat memperoleh hadiah kosmetik bertema dugong selama bermain.
2. That’s My Balloon: Saat Badak Jawa Tidak Boleh Disentuh
That’s My Balloon
Game arcade buatan Singapura yang tampil di App Store ini memiliki konsep sederhana: pemain harus memecahkan balon yang muncul di layar secepat mungkin. Namun, ada aturan berbeda ketika balon bergambar satwa langka muncul.
Alih-alih dihancurkan, pemain justru harus membiarkannya terbang sebagai simbol perlindungan terhadap spesies yang terancam punah. Salah satu satwa ditampilkan adalah badak jawa, spesies endemik Indonesia yang kini hanya bertahan di habitat terbatas di Ujung Kulon.
Baca Juga: Foto Rosé BLACKPINK Pegang iPhone 18 Pro Disebut Editan, Apple Ikut Buka Suara
Pengembang Vikas Pawar mengatakan ide tersebut muncul dari keinginan membalik aturan utama permainan. 
“Ketika balon bergambar satwa langka muncul, pemain justru harus membiarkannya pergi. Saya merasa itu cara yang menyenangkan dan alami untuk menyampaikan pesan konservasi tanpa mengubah kesederhanaan gameplay,” kata Pawar.
Ia berharap pemain setidaknya dapat mengenal satu fakta baru tentang satwa liar Asia Tenggara setelah memainkan game tersebut.
3. BagMaster Isekai Hadirkan Saola, “Unicorn Asia”
BagMaster Isekai
Saola sering dijuluki sebagai “unicorn Asia” karena sangat langka dan jarang terlihat di habitat aslinya di Vietnam dan Laos. Satwa tersebut menjadi inspirasi utama dalam BagMaster Isekai, game roguelike RPG asal Vietnam di App Store.
Pemain dapat membawa saola sebagai pendamping dengan kemampuan khusus selama petualangan berlangsung. Binh Diep, salah satu pengembang game tersebut, mengatakan saola dipilih karena menjadi salah satu satwa paling ikonik sekaligus paling langka di Vietnam.
“Saola memiliki penampilan yang sangat khas dan dikenal sebagai ‘unicorn Asia’. Kami selalu mencari cara untuk memperkenalkan unsur Vietnam kepada pemain di seluruh dunia, dan saola adalah salah satu simbol yang tepat,” ujar Diep.
Ia menambahkan desain saola yang terlihat kuat sekaligus menggemaskan membuat satwa tersebut cocok diterjemahkan menjadi karakter pendamping dalam game.
4. My Little Village Ajak Pemain Merawat Bangau Sarus
Berbeda dari game aksi lainnya, My Little Village menawarkan pengalaman simulasi desa yang santai.
Game buatan pengembang asal Vietnam ini menghadirkan bangau sarus sebagai bagian dari ekosistem desa yang dibangun pemain. Semakin baik lingkungan dan lahan pertanian dikelola, semakin banyak bangau yang kembali ke habitat tersebut.
Thong Nguyen dari COROCHTI mengatakan kehadiran bangau sarus sengaja dirancang sebagai indikator kesehatan lingkungan dalam permainan.
“Kami ingin tindakan pemain benar-benar membawa perubahan bagi desa. Ketika lingkungan menjadi lebih sehat, bangau akan perlahan kembali ke sawah dan muncul lebih sering,” kata Nguyen.
Menurut dia, melihat satwa liar kembali ke habitatnya seiring desa menjadi lebih hijau merupakan salah satu pencapaian paling bermakna dalam permainan tersebut.
5. Climb Knight Perkenalkan Tarsius Filipina
Tarsius merupakan primata kecil yang dikenal memiliki mata besar dan kemampuan melompat hingga beberapa meter dari satu cabang ke cabang lain. Satwa tersebut menjadi fokus dalam Climb Knight, game platformer bergaya 1-bit asal Filipina.
Melalui cerita bertajuk Tarsier Tales, pemain diajak mengenal kehidupan tarsius sekaligus ancaman yang dihadapi, termasuk hilangnya habitat akibat deforestasi dan perdagangan satwa ilegal. Pengembang Darius Immanuel Guerrero mengaku terinspirasi dari buku cerita yang ia baca saat kecil.
“Tarsier Tales memberi kami kesempatan membuat petualangan kecil yang memperkenalkan salah satu satwa paling menarik di Asia Tenggara kepada pemain,” ujarnya.
Guerrero berharap kisah tersebut dapat memicu rasa ingin tahu pemain terhadap tarsius dan hutan tempat satwa itu hidup. “Jika ada orang yang menjadi penasaran lalu ingin mempelajari tarsius lebih jauh, saya merasa karakter ksatria kami sudah menjalankan tugasnya,” kata Guerrero.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Smart kitchen brand Beyond Appliances has raised ₹110 Cr ($10.4 Mn) in a Series B funding round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital and a host of other undisclosed investors.
The Bengaluru-based startup plans to use the fresh capital to set up a new manufacturing plant. The plans also feature the startup’s plans to expand into new product segments. Founder Eshwar K Vikas shared with Inc42 that Beyond Appliances will be coming out with its ovens within the next 9-12 months.
On the manufacturing front, Vikas said that the startup is eyeing setting up a new manufacturing facility in South or West India. Beyond Appliances currently operates two facilities in Delhi NCR and Bengaluru and manufactures about 90% of its products in-house.
Founded in August 2024 by Vikas and Rakesh Patil, Beyond Appliances is building connected kitchen appliances like smart chimneys and smart hobs. Its flagship product is an Android-powered chimney equipped with a display that functions as a domestic kitchen management system.
The chimney allows users to access OTT and music applications, set cooking reminders and manage grocery lists through integrations with Zepto and Blinkit. It also features Chef Verse, an app offering curated recipes from chefs, alongside 3D suction technology.
The startup also recently introduced the Cube Chimney, which is designed for compact kitchens and rental homes.
It takes an omnichannel approach to its sales, with 60% of its products being sold online and the remainder offline. The startup claims retail presence across 20 select stores in Bengaluru. Its customer base of around 1,200 users spans Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune and Delhi NCR.
“We are currently scaling our offline presence very fast. We have about 300-400 touchpoints for customers across GT (general trade) and AT (alternate trade), and exclusive outlets as well,” Vikas added.
The brand is further looking to get to at least 1,500-2,000 touchpoints for the customer as it has signed up with some large format retails. On the exclusive outlet front, the startup operates 3 stores till date with a pipeline of 15-20 stores.
On the financial front, Vikas told Inc42 that Beyond Appliances recorded a net revenue of ₹40 Cr in FY26 but refrained from disclosing the bottom line performance.
The latest round comes a year after Beyond Appliances raised $4 Mn in its Series A funding round which was also led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital.
Beyond Appliances’ fundraise comes as more Indian startups expand in the home appliance market which comes at the behest of consumers spending more on interiors and devices to complement them.
For instance, consumer tech startups like Karban, Fanzart, Magnific, XSCACE, NUOS, Noctics Labs and Glazonoid are building products ranging from designer fans and integrated air purifiers to in-wall speakers, smart switches and home automation systems.
These startups are combining aesthetics with functionality, rather than relying on design alone to justify premium pricing. Karban, for instance, combines air purification, circulation and lighting in ceiling-mounted products, while NUOS integrates automation into premium switch panels.
The category is also creating a new distribution channel through architects and interior designers, who can specify products before construction or renovation begins. Around 40% of NUOS’ home automation sales and 20% of Karban’s sales come through these channels.
As the segment is getting more consumer interest, investors are also bullish to cash on this wave.
For instance, Nester raised ₹19 Cr in a pre-Series A round in February 2026. The startup is targeting the broader home appliance market with products including steam air fryer ovens, toasters and juicers.
Similarly, cooling solutions startup Optimist is building air conditioners designed for Indian conditions. The startup was reported to be in talks to raise about $10 Mn.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The United States on Monday warned foreign financial institutions that if they conducted any business with Iran or its banking sector they could be sanctioned by Washington.
“Foreign financial institutions continuing to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions could be targeted at any time without advance notification and should take immediate action to terminate such activity and relationships,” the US Treasury said in an “alert” statement.
The United States launched its war against Iran in late February, killing the country’s leadership and demanding it cease any nuclear-related activities.
The war has plunged the Middle East into violence, with Tehran’s retaliatory action targeting Washington’s Gulf allies and sending global energy and fertilizer prices skyrocketing after it virtually shut a key trading route.
Since late August, Washington has stepped up its campaign to economically isolate Tehran, warning its allies that they would be hit by secondary sanctions if they continued to conduct transactions with the country’s government.
The US Treasury has also announced a slew of new sanctions as part of that push, targeting Iran’s financial, cryptocurrency, rail, automotive and manufacturing sectors.
It has also taken action against two banks — one in the United Arab Emirates and another in Turkey — over their alleged aid to the authorities in Tehran.
In Monday’s statement, the Treasury said Iran’s government operated so-called “shadow banking” channels to circumvent US sanctions, and that foreign financial institutions should aim to identify and avoid any such activities.
AFP

items.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi
Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa Rtd, has expressed deep sorrow over the tragic crash of NAF ATR 42 aircraft and the loss of officers and airmen who were involved in a routine flight mission to Lagos, describing them as personnel who exemplified the highest standards of loyalty and commitment to the defence of the country.
In a statement he personally signed, Gen Musa offered condolences to President Bola Tinubu, the leadership of the Armed Forces, and most especially, the immediate families, loved ones, and colleagues of our fallen heroes.
He said, “It is with a profound sense of grief and heavy heart that I, on behalf of the Ministry of Defence and the entire Armed Forces of Nigeria, express deep sorrow over the tragic crash of our military aircraft with tail number NAF 931 involving dedicated personnel of the Armed Forces.
“This painful incident claimed the lives of brave officers and airmen who were engaged in routine flight mission while serving our nation with courage, unyielding devotion, and selfless patriotism.
“The loss of these valiant patriots is an irreparable blow not only to the military high command and their comrades-in-arms, but to the entire Federal Republic of Nigeria.
“These fine officers and men exemplify the highest standards of military professionalism, loyalty, and commitment to the defence of our Fatherland.
“On behalf of the Ministry of Defence, I extend our heartfelt condolences to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the leadership of the Armed Forces, and most especially, the immediate families, loved ones, and colleagues of our fallen heroes.
“We share in your immense grief and stand shoulder-to-shoulder with you during this tragic hour.
“Our hearts also go out to the families of the civilians on board the ill-fated aircraft, we share your grief.
“A comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding this unfortunate crash has been ordered to ascertain the cause and ensure all necessary operational safety protocols are reinforced across our military aviation units.
“We pray that the Almighty God grants the souls of the departed eternal repose, and give their families, the military community, and all Nigerians the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss.”

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Michael Olise came off the bench to inspire France to a 4-1 win over Belgium in the UEFA Nations League on Monday, handing Zinedine Zidane his first home victory since taking charge.
Use up and down arrow keys to resize the meta box pane.
Dodi Lukebakio put Belgium on course for their first competitive win over Les Bleus in 45 years when he fired the visitors in front in the first half at the Stade de France.
But France turned the match on its head in a blistering finish, scoring four times in the final 13 minutes to preserve Zidane’s unbeaten start and move closer to the quarter-finals.
Desire Doue hauled France level in the 77th minute with a low drive from the edge of the area before Olise teed up Rayan Cherki to fire them ahead four minutes later.
Olise then put the result beyond doubt with a third goal before adding another in stoppage time to cap a stunning French comeback.
France, who also beat Belgium 1-0 in Brussels last week thanks to a late Olise goal, moved three points clear of Italy at the top of Group A1, with Belgium another point back. Italy beat Turkey 3-1 in Bologna to condemn their opponents to a fourth straight loss.
Former World Cup and Ballon d’Or winner Zidane heavily rotated his team for the last match of this two-week long international window, with only Dembele keeping his place among the 10 changes.
Manchester United defender Leny Yoro and Toulouse goalkeeper Guillaume Restes made their France debuts, with Ousmane Dembele again captaining the side in the absence of the injured Kylian Mbappe.
Belgium were without the suspended duo of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans but caught France cold when Romeo Lavia’s superb ball split open the home defence, allowing Lukebakio to race clear and tuck away a clinical finish.
Maarten Vandevoordt, making his debut in goal for Belgium, kept out efforts from Esteban Lepaul and Cherki as France pressed for an equaliser, but the dam eventually burst.
Doue gathered the ball and shot on the turn, beyond the reach of Vandevoordt, to haul France level. Cherki then turned home a cutback from Olise to give the hosts the lead as the Bayern Munich winger stole the show late on.
Olise scrambled in a third in the 88th minute and rolled in a fourth after skilful work from Doue to complete a remarkable turnaround.
AFP

items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
President Bola Tinubu on Monday evening arrived in Abuja after spending a few days in Lagos following his return to Nigeria from a working vacation in Europe.
The President’s aircraft touched down at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, at about 7:45 p.m.
He was received on arrival by the National Security Adviser, NSA, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu; Director of Protocol at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Ibrahim Sule Dan Agundi, and some senior security officials.
Tinubu’s return to Abuja brings to an end his stay in Lagos, where he had carried out a series of official and political engagements following his return from Europe.
Recall that President Tinubu had returned to Lagos on Tuesday last week from working vacation in Europe, during which he stayed in London and Paris and held meetings with political and business interests.
Speaking briefly with journalists shortly after his arrival in Lagos, Tinubu dismissed concerns over his health and declared himself fit and ready to resume full duties.
“Ready to kick, ready to work. There’s nothing wrong. Rumour will always be emanating from politics, but the facts remain I’m here: healthy, sound and ready to go”, the President had said.
Asked about his vacation, Tinubu simply replied “I enjoyed myself”.
Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, who was among senior officials who received him in Lagos, had expressed optimism that the President would return to work with renewed energy after his time away.
While in Lagos, Tinubu participated in activities marking Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary, including the national premiere of MKO, a documentary on the life and democratic struggle of the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola.
The President, accompanied by First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu, attended the October 1 screening at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts in Lagos.
The documentary chronicled Abiola’s political journey, the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election and the pro-democracy struggle that followed.
Tinubu also received senior government officials and political leaders during his stay in Lagos, including Vice President Kashim Shettima, who visited him at his residence on Saturday.
After the meeting, Shettima said he had remained in regular contact with the President throughout his stay abroad and described Tinubu as fully engaged with developments in the country.
The Vice President also defended the administration’s economic reforms, saying difficult decisions taken since 2023 were necessary to stabilise the economy and lay the foundation for recovery.
It is expected that Tinubu’s return to Abuja will kick-start his re-election campaigns in different parts of the country.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Cynthia Alo
Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa has said no survivor has been recovered from Monday’s military aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of the state, with only wreckage of wings, identity cards and uniforms seen.
Aiyedatiwa said rescue teams are yet to access the main body of the aircraft because it went deep into the swamp.
The governor disclosed this on Monday night during an interview on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme.
He said the aircraft, with 32 persons on board, 25 passengers and seven crew members, was a surveillance aircraft on its way from Benin to Lagos, which lost radio signal at about 9:15 a.m.
He said information got to him at about 10:30 a.m. from the chairman of Ilaje Local Government that residents heard a sound like an air tremor before the aircraft dived into a swamp directly facing the Naval Forward Operating Base in Igbokoda.
“They saw the wreckage from the wings, some ID cards and uniforms indicating it was a military aircraft. The main body went deep into the swamp area. They haven’t been able to search the aircraft itself yet,” he said.
He said naval personnel, local emergency officials, Amotekun and residents moved into the creek with boats immediately the crash occurred, but no living soul was found.
He said the site has been cordoned off, while hospitals in Igbokoda and Okitipupa have been placed on standby with ambulances recently procured for the 18 local governments.
The governor said the Nigerian Air Force and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau are investigating and will need to recover the black box to determine the exact cause.
Speaking on the recent elimination of Abdussamad Ohida, a top ISWAP coordinator in Ondo forest, Aiyedatiwa said the clearance operation took place about five days ago after months of top secret surveillance.
He said it was a joint operation involving the DSS, Nigerian Army, British intelligence officers and Amotekun, with no casualties recorded on the side of security forces.
The governor explained that the coordinator took over after his former superior, a Central Nigeria ISWAP leader, was arrested by the DSS in 2023, adding that intelligence was generated from that arrest and from tracking of another leader earlier eliminated by DSS.
He revealed that the criminals carry sophisticated weapons beyond AK-47, including GPMG, and had retaliated when security first launched attack.
“When we launched the first attack, they retaliated. So we had to move back, heavily arm, do serious intelligence and mapping before we re-launched,” he said.
Aiyedatiwa said the role of the UK was provision of intelligence and precision targeting equipment that Amotekun does not have, while Amotekun provided knowledge of terrain because many of its operatives are recruited local hunters.
He said Ondo’s vast forests sharing boundaries with Kogi, Edo, Ekiti and Oyo have become a corridor for criminals fleeing military operations in Kogi and Kwara axis.
According to him, what started as farmer-herder clashes years ago has graduated to terrorism, linking the group to the 2025 December 31 attack on Ipele police station and the 2022 Owo massacre.
On whether the group plans to disrupt 2027 elections, he said their agenda in totality is to kill, destroy and disrupt in any form.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By James Ogunnaike
No fewer than nine persons lost their lives in a fatal road traffic crash along the JBD/ORE route in Ijebu-Ode, Ogun State on Monday.
According to the statement signed by Afolabi Odunsi, Chief Route Commander and Sector Public Education Officer, FRSC Ogun State Sector Command, the crash occurred at about 4:55 p.m. at the Bethel area within the Ijebu-Ode Unit Command.
According to the FRSC, the crash involved a white Toyota Hiace commercial bus, with registration number 14B-299DT, belonging to Delta Line, and a white Sino Truck commercial vehicle, with registration number AAB162XD, belonging to Bill Gas Solution Ltd.
The nine occupants of the two vehicles were all killed in the crash.
The FRSC said the incident occurred while it was raining and the road pavement was wet.
“Preliminary investigation identified speed violation (SPV) as the probable cause of the crash,” the statement said.
The road safety agency said its rescue team arrived at the scene within two minutes of receiving the report, at about 4:58 p.m.
It added that the bodies of the victims were evacuated and deposited at the General Hospital morgue, Ijebu-Ode, while the vehicles were towed to the Ilese Police Station by the Ilese Police Motor Traffic Division.
The Sector Commander, FRSC Ogun State Command, Corps Commander Oludare Ogunjobi, urged motorists, particularly commercial vehicle operators, to exercise maximum caution while driving in the rain.
Ogunjobi advised motorists to obey speed limits, maintain safe following distances and avoid driving behaviours capable of endangering lives.
He warned that speeding on wet roads was particularly dangerous because reduced tyre grip and visibility could make it difficult for motorists to control their vehicles or stop safely.
The FRSC expressed condolences to the families of the victims and urged all road users to make safety their priority at all times.

He also directed that flags should be flown at half-mast throughout the country as a mark of respect to the officers.
President Tinubu had earlier expressed profound sadness over the crash of the Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 jet.
The accident occurred near a naval base in the Igbokoda area of Ondo State.
A statement by the presidential spokesman, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, said the aircraft, carrying 25 passengers and seven crew members, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed.
“This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation. Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten,”
President Tinubu declared in a condolence message to the Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and all officers, airmen, and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force.
“The Chief of Air Staff has briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences.
“I commend the Nigerian Air Force for activating an immediate search and rescue operation following the accident,” he said.
The Air Force will release the officers’ names after contacting their families.

items.title: Israel Has Been Working on Plague Vaccine Since 2025
items.summary:
Researchers in Israel are developing an experimental mRNA vaccine against pneumonic plague, as concerns about potential outbreaks continue to draw attention to the disease.
The vaccine is being developed by researchers from Tel Aviv University and the Israel Institute for Biological Research, led by Prof. Dan Peer.
Researchers have so far tested the experimental vaccine in mice. The vaccine uses mRNA technology to target pneumonic plague, a severe form of plague caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis.
The project remains at the experimental stage, and the vaccine has not yet been approved for use in humans.
Reports have described Israel as the only country currently developing an mRNA vaccine specifically against pneumonic plague. However, there is no firm confirmation that no other research teams worldwide are working on similar vaccines.
For now, the Israeli project remains an early-stage attempt to determine whether mRNA technology can protect against pneumonic plague.

items.content:
By Gabriel Ewepu
The Federal Government, on Monday, disclosed that early procurement under the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative has generated ₦61.58 billion in savings as Nigeria targets the delivery of 1.1 million metric tonnes of fertiliser in 2026 amid renewed efforts to boost food production and strengthen the country’s agrifood system.
The disclosure was made by the Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, at the Annual Community of Practice (CoP) Meeting on the implementation of the Comprehensive Africa Agriculture Development Programme (CAADP) Kampala Declaration, held yesterday in Maiduguri, Borno State.
Kyari also said the government targets the delivery of 1.1 million metric tonnes of fertiliser in 2026 amid renewed efforts to boost food production and strengthen the country’s agrifood system.
Kyari said the Federal Government, state governments, non-state actors and development partners were working together to translate the Kampala Declaration into concrete action capable of improving food security, strengthening rural economies and building resilience across Nigeria’s agricultural sector.
He said the collaboration had become more urgent as Nigeria begins implementation of the CAADP Kampala Declaration and its Strategy and Action Plan for 2026–2035, which adopts a broader agrifood systems approach covering sustainable production, investment and finance, food and nutrition security, trade, inclusion, resilience and governance.
According to the minister, the Federal Government’s efforts were already yielding results, with reductions of up to 50 per cent in the prices of some essential food commodities, alongside expanded input delivery, rural infrastructure investments and support for smallholder farmers.
“The task now is to sustain these gains and deepen their impact,” Kyari said.
He stressed that closer alignment between the Federal Government, states and development partners was critical to achieving sustainable food security.
“Alignment between the Federal and State Governments and partners is indispensable to sustainable food security and resilient livelihoods.
“That alignment must translate into compatible policies, reliable data, complementary investments and clarity of responsibility for delivery. We need one coherent agrifood system in which national direction and State-level execution reinforce one another,” he said.
The minister said Nigeria’s newly validated 10-Year National Agrifood System Strategy and Action Plan would serve as the vehicle for domesticating the Kampala commitments and harmonising implementation across the country.
He explained that the strategy integrates CAADP Biennial Review indicators into Nigeria’s planning, budgeting and reporting systems, while efforts were underway to align national and state budgets, reduce duplication and channel investments towards agreed priorities.
Kyari also announced that the government was pushing ahead with a new mechanisation drive following the unveiling of the National Agricultural Mechanization Policy and National Agricultural Mechanization Investment Strategy in August.
He said the framework would move the country away from fragmented equipment interventions towards a sustainable mechanisation ecosystem, including plans for a mega tractor assembly plant capable of producing between 2,000 and 4,000 tractors annually.
“We are also expanding all-season production through irrigation, improving access to quality seed, supporting our National Agricultural Research Institutes and strengthening the translation of research into practical solutions for farmers,” the minister said.
He added that the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones were designed to link production areas more effectively with processing facilities and markets, stressing that such investments must be integrated with rural infrastructure, extension services, agricultural finance, nutrition and sustainable management of land and water resources.
On the broader agricultural strategy, Kyari said Nigeria could not afford a one-size-fits-all approach, given the country’s diverse agricultural potentials.
He said the National Agricultural Technology and Innovation Policy recognises the distinct production potentials and natural-resource endowments of Nigeria’s five major agricultural zones.
“Our task is to build on those comparative advantages with adaptable technologies, infrastructure and market linkages, rather than expect every State to produce everything,” he said.
The minister also called for greater participation of women and young people across agricultural value chains, as well as stronger conditions for private investment and development finance.
He challenged state governments to ensure that their agricultural action plans were aligned with the Kampala commitments and national priorities, particularly in rural infrastructure, extension, credit, quality inputs, labour-saving technologies, post-harvest loss reduction and climate-resilient agriculture.
The Governor of Borno State, Prof. Babagana Zulum, represented by his Deputy, Hon. Usman Kadafur, described the meeting as more than a gathering of policymakers, development experts, researchers, farmers and private-sector actors.
He said the Community of Practice should serve as a platform for translating shared experience into practical solutions for Nigeria’s agricultural sector.
“A Community of Practice should not simply be a gathering where ideas are presented and applauded. It should be a platform where experience becomes knowledge, knowledge becomes action, and action produces measurable improvement in the lives of our people”, Zulum said.
Also speaking, the Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy in Nigeria, Dr Karin Jansen, said Germany welcomed Nigeria’s leadership in implementing the CAADP Kampala Agenda and remained committed to supporting the country in moving from commitments to coordinated action.
Jansen said transforming Nigeria’s agrifood system required stronger cooperation between the Federal Government and states, alongside active participation by non-state actors.
She identified the Community of Practice as a critical mechanism for linking national priorities with implementation at the state level, while providing room for knowledge exchange, learning and joint problem-solving.
She said Germany, through the Sustainable Agricultural Systems and Policies (AgSys) project, funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), was supporting Nigerian partners to strengthen agricultural policy processes, scale successful approaches and deepen civil society participation.
In his closing remarks, the Minister of State for Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Aliyu Sabi Abdullahi, said Nigeria’s path to food security depended on states identifying and exploiting their respective comparative advantages.
He warned against the siloed approach of the past, arguing that agricultural development must reflect the specific strengths and potentials of each state.
Abdullahi also stressed the need for greater coordination among government ministries and agencies, particularly those responsible for agriculture, health, environment and rural development.
“The challenges facing our agrifood systems are multidimensional. They require the kind of integrated, multi-sectoral approach that we have championed here.
“The synergy between the Ministries of Agriculture, Health, Environment and Rural Development is not merely a bureaucratic ideal; it is a practical necessity”, he said.
He noted that the relationship between food production, nutrition, environmental sustainability and rural development remained central to Nigeria’s economic prosperity.
The Maiduguri meeting was attended by Commissioners of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries, Health, Environment, Commerce and Rural Development, as well as researchers, farmers, private-sector operators, development partners and other stakeholders in the agricultural sector.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The Federal High Court sitting in Abuja has affirmed Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim as the presidential candidate of the Accord Party for the 2027 presidential election.
The court’s declaration, on Monday, brings a major legal dispute over the party’s presidential ticket to a decisive conclusion.
Justice Mohammed Umar, in his judgment, dismissed the preliminary objections filed against Hashim’s suit and rejected the purported letter relied upon to communicate the cancellation of the party’s presidential primary to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).
The court also ordered the Accord Party to upload Hashim’s name to INEC as its presidential candidate, effectively recognising his emergence from the party’s presidential primary held on May 30, 2026.
Hashim had approached the court seeking recognition as the duly nominated presidential candidate of Accord Party, where he maintained that he was the sole aspirant and winner of the May 30, 2026 primary.
His case was argued by Henry Akunebu, SAN, who urged the court to compel the party to recognise Hashim and forward his name to INEC.
Akunebu had challenged the validity and evidential value of documents relied upon to dispute Hashim’s emergence, particularly a purported letter notifying INEC of the cancellation of the presidential primary.
He argued that the alleged cancellation letter lacked the party’s official stamp and imprimatur and questioned the circumstances surrounding its receipt by INEC.
Accord’s position was represented by T.W. Olusesi, who maintained that the presidential primary had been cancelled and that no valid primary produced Hashim as the party’s candidate.
Counsel for INEC, D.J. Gusen, similarly argued that the commission did not monitor the purported primary because it had received notification that the exercise had been cancelled.
Justice Umar, however, dismissed the preliminary objections and rejected the purported cancellation letter, paving the way for the court to recognise the outcome of the May 30 primary.
The judgment follows months of legal contest over the Accord Party presidential ticket and the party’s failure to submit Hashim’s name to INEC despite his claim that he had emerged as the winner of the primary.
Hashim had argued that the party’s refusal to upload his name violated the Constitution, Electoral Act 2026 and relevant INEC regulations and guidelines governing the nomination of political party candidates.
In his originating summons, he asked the court to determine whether Accord Party could validly refuse to upload his name to INEC’s nomination portal after the conduct of a primary in which he emerged as the winner.
He had also sought, in the alternative, an order directing the party to conduct a fresh presidential primary in which he would be allowed to participate.
Hashim maintained throughout the proceedings that he was a registered and financially compliant member of Accord Party, had paid the prescribed ₦50 million presidential nomination fee and contributed ₦7 million towards the party’s electronic membership registration programme.
He also maintained that INEC officials monitored the May 30 primary at which he emerged as the sole aspirant.
In his reaction to the ruling, Hashim dedicated the victory to God and called for reconciliation among stakeholders and party members.
“I give God the Glory for this victory, I dedicate the victory also to all stakeholders and our dear party members and my hardworking legal team. We are grateful to the Judiciary that has done justice on this matter.
“We won’t leave anybody behind…We should all come together and work for the party’s victory in the January 16, 2027 presidential election and all other elections. The march to a New Nigeria has started,” said Hashim.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
In a major development that may have far-reaching implications for the region, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Monday activated the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments under the Makkah Alliance for Defence, a collective security arrangement signed in the holy city of Makkah on August 7.
According to a joint-statement issued on Monday night, the activation entails immediate deployment of "the agreed military forces and capabilities to the Kingdom in response to security threats".
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defense Committee of the alliance, held in Riyadh to discuss the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia is currently engaged in an active conflict with Houthis of Yemen who have been targeting the various strategic and economic assets in the Kingdom.
Without naming anyone, the emergency meeting condemned in the strongest terms the attempted targeting of Makkah and Madinah, as well as continuing attacks targeting cities and civilian and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia.
The three countries reaffirmed their unequivocal rejection of any attack or threat against the Kingdom's security and territorial integrity.
Pakistan and Turkiye also commended the vigilance and readiness of the Saudi Armed Forces and praised their professionalism and competence in countering threats and attacks against the Kingdom and safeguarding its security and territorial integrity.
The committee reviewed the outcomes of political and military consultations held ahead of the emergency meeting and approved the recommendations submitted to it.
It reaffirmed that the Makkah Alliance for Defense represented a firm commitment to collective defence and a unified position in confronting threats.
Under the decision, the three countries will immediately move towards practical implementation of their collective defence commitments and take necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities, ensuring their rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia.
The deployment will be carried out in accordance with approved arrangements and the national legislation of the three participating countries, the joint statement said.
These measures aim to enhance military readiness and integration and strengthen the collective capacity of the three countries to confront and counter threats.
The parties affirmed that the security of each member state is an integral part of the collective security of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
The countries also decided to appoint Pakistan's Lt Gen (retd) Nauman Mahmood as the alliance's first secretary-general for a three-year term. The parties welcomed the appointment and expressed confidence that Lt Gen Nauman would contribute to advancing the alliance and achieving its objectives.
They said translating the Makkah Agreement into practical measures demonstrated the credibility of their commitment to collective defence, strengthened deterrence effectiveness, and reaffirmed their unity and determination to defend their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
The decisions were taken in accordance with the provisions of the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defense.
The emergency meeting occurred amid heightened security concerns in Saudi Arabia, with the three countries reiterating their commitment to collective action in protecting the Kingdom and responding to threats against its territory and vital facilities.
The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, formally the Makkah Alliance for Defence, is a defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye signed into force on August 7, 2026.
It builds upon the earlier Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed between Pakistan and KSA on September 17, 2025. The pact's ratification was officially announced amidst the US-Israel-Iran war.
The Makkah Alliance for Defence enshrines a collective security arrangement modelled on Article 5 of NATO, with its official announcement stating that "any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all".
