items.author: Kamran Yousaf
items.content:
Simmering tensions between Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban regime overshadowed a regional conference on Afghanistan in Moscow on Monday, with the two sides trading sharp accusations over terrorism and cross-border attacks and failing to agree on a joint statement.
The breakdown marked a significant setback for the Moscow Format, a Russia-led regional mechanism established in 2017 to build consensus on Afghanistan. It was the first time since the inaugural meeting that participants failed to issue a joint statement.
The eighth meeting brought together senior representatives from Russia, Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Iran, India and Central Asian states to discuss Afghanistan's political, security and economic situation, including counterterrorism and regional connectivity. Belarus and Egypt attended as guests.
But the worsening confrontation between Islamabad and Kabul quickly became the dominant issue.
Pakistan was represented by Special Representative for Afghanistan Ambassador Mohammad Sadiq, while the Taliban delegation was led by Acting Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi.
Addressing the meeting, Sadiq delivered a blunt assessment of the security situation, putting terrorism at the centre of Pakistan's concerns.
"Terrorism remains at the core of Afghanistan's problems, with roots in the nexus between the Taliban Regime and terrorist groups," Sadiq said, according to the transcript of his statement.
He specifically referred to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan and other terrorist organisations operating from Afghan territory. "Over the last three years alone, more than 4,700 innocent Pakistanis have lost their lives to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan," Sadiq said.
He accused the Taliban regime of being complicit in the problem and defended Pakistan's military operations inside Afghanistan as acts of self-defence.
"The Taliban regime is complicit in this," Sadiq said, describing Pakistan's counterstrikes as "precise, intelligence-based and defensive in nature."
The Pakistani position effectively challenged the narrative Kabul has been presenting to regional countries that the recent escalation is primarily the result of Pakistani action against Afghanistan.
Muttaqi, in his address, took the opposite position, accusing Pakistan of relying on military pressure rather than diplomacy.
He said Kabul wanted its disputes with Islamabad resolved through dialogue and diplomacy and rejected what he described as a policy of accusations, propaganda and military action.
"Our fundamental position is that the existing problems between Afghanistan and Pakistan, whether security, political or economic, can be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy," Muttaqi said.
The Taliban foreign minister also maintained that Afghanistan had the right to defend itself against aggression and insisted that Kabul would formulate its domestic and foreign policies independently rather than under external pressure.
The sharply contrasting positions made agreement on language concerning terrorism virtually impossible.
Russia's special presidential envoy for Afghanistan, Zamir Kabulov, later confirmed that the dispute between the Pakistani and Afghan delegations prevented the participants from adopting the final document.
"When drafting the final joint statement, we encountered one problem - that problem was that our Afghan and Pakistani colleagues didn't see eye to eye. We regret this," Kabulov said.
He explained that the Afghan side objected to the draft because it referred to Afghanistan too frequently in the context of terrorism. Kabulov noted that similar wording had been used in the statement issued after last year's meeting.
Kabulov nevertheless said the failure to issue a statement would not spell the end of the Moscow Format, arguing that the platform could continue to function despite the disagreement.
The failure to forge a regional consensus was accompanied by unusually strong Russian support for the Taliban government. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, who opened the meeting, praised the Taliban's performance since its return to power in 2021 and described it as a "national government".
"The national government led by the Taliban movement came to power and it put under control the territory of the country, and we should recognize that it has been successfully ruling it," Lavrov said.
Lavrov also praised the Taliban for its efforts against Da'ish and other extremist groups and for combating drug trafficking.
He welcomed what he described as the Taliban government's achievements after the withdrawal of US and NATO forces, while reiterating Moscow's opposition to any return of Western military infrastructure to Afghanistan or neighbouring states.
"I'd like to highlight that we have zero tolerance to the deployment of NATO military infrastructure in the territory of Afghanistan and/or in neighboring countries under any pretext whatsoever," Lavrov said.
Russia has already gone further than other major powers in its engagement with Kabul. Moscow formally recognised the Taliban administration in 2025, making it the first country to do so.
The Russian position at the Moscow meeting therefore stood in marked contrast to Pakistan's emphasis on the Taliban's links with terrorist groups operating against Pakistan.
The meeting also highlighted a broader problem for the regional approach to Afghanistan: countries that once broadly agreed on the need for an inclusive, stable and secure Afghanistan are increasingly divided over how to deal with the Taliban regime and, more importantly, how to assess the security threat emanating from Afghan territory.
The collapse of the joint statement in Moscow has therefore exposed not merely a Pakistan-Afghanistan disagreement, but a widening gap among regional powers regarding Afghanistan's future and how to deal with the Taliban regime.

By Davies Iheamnachor
Governorship Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, has stated that his political movement is not threatened by the activities of the Rainbow Coalition led by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, in the state.
Lulu-Briggs noted that the result of the 2027 elections would not determine the coalition, rather people of the state, stating that the ‘rainbow ‘ has already lost its colour.
The governorship candidate spoke on Monday at the unveiling of his manifesto and campaign roadmap tagged, “Reset Rivers State”, at Buguma City in Asari-Toru Local Government Area of Rivers State.
While fielding questions on the growing strength of the Wike’ rainbow coalition, Lulu-Briggs stated that he is not bordered about the said platform, adding that the state was interested in people who would change the leadership narrative of the state.
Lulu-Briggs noted that the totality of the coalition is less than 7% of the population of the State, urging his followers to have confidence in their ability to achieve the utmost results.
He said: “I am not bothered about any form of coalition. I know that the rainbow has already lost its colour. Our people should have confidence in their ability to achieve the utmost.
“If you put their numbers together they are less than 7% of the population of the state. The coalition is something we can overcome.”
I’ll not take salaries, allowances as governor
Lulu-Briggs said if he is elected to be governor of the state that he would not take salaries, revealing that his monthly pay would be used to serve less privileged individuals in the state.
Lulu-Briggs promised to run an administration anchored on transparency, accountability and personal sacrifice, adding that he would emulate his presidential principal, Peter Obi, in making the sacrifice.
Lulu-Briggs promised people of the state that every naira entrusted to his administration would be accounted for.
He said: “When we have the opportunity to manage government resources, I can promise Rivers people that every penny will be accounted for.
“I’m sure I’m going to be like my principal, the Presidential Candidate, Peter Obi. I will not even be asking for any salary. Every month, any salary will go into assisting one widow or the other.”
He said his financial independence would enable him to serve without depending on government remuneration, adding that his businesses would continue to provide for him even after leaving office.
He said: “The way we have gone, there will be no need to even pension me because I’m sure that my businesses will still be running.”
The governorship candidate decried what he described as a frightening trust deficit between Rivers people and those governing them, assuring to deliberately rebuild the relationship if elected.
“People need to begin to have faith in their government again. The trust deficit between the ruled and the rulership is frightening.”
He stated that his administration would pursue a comprehensive “reset” of Rivers State, covering the economy, politics, governance and access to opportunities.
“Just give us your support, give us your prayers. Let’s navigate this mucky waters of Rivers politics and we reset Rivers State.
“We will not be defined by the things that God has blessed us with only, but by the innovative things that we are able to create,” he said.

Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, a staunch ally of President Donald Trump, will join Fox News to provide “commentary and analysis,” the conservative TV network announced Monday.
She will make her debut on November 1, according to a statement from Fox News Media’s Suzanne Scott touting Leavitt’s “a distinct understanding of today’s political landscape.”
Leavitt, who gave birth to her second child in the spring, stepped down in late August to focus on her family, while making clear that she intended to continue promoting the “MAGA” (Make America Great Again) brand of right-wing American politics.
“I look forward to bringing my unique perspective from my experience as White House Press Secretary, along with the same energy and candor that defined my tenure,” Leavitt said.
She was already a frequent guest on Fox News in her former role.
Trump has yet to appoint a new press secretary.
Since Leavitt’s departure, the White House has stopped holding regular press briefings.
Since leaving the White House, Leavitt has joined an election fundraising organization: MAGA Inc., a pro-Trump political group.
At 28, she was the youngest person ever appointed to the high-profile position of press secretary.
A native of New Hampshire in the northeastern United States, whose meteoric rise alongside Trump illustrated the spread of his ideas among Gen Z, she spearheaded an aggressive communications strategy targeting traditional media.
She also opened the White House to influencers and content creators aligned with the MAGA ideology.
Since her departure, Trump’s hostility toward the press has intensified further. He sought to bar CNN and MS NOW, as well as the news outlet Politico, from the White House.
A judge ordered the administration to reverse course.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Steve Oko
Abia State Governor Alex Otti has approved a N1 billion appreciation fund for teachers and ordered the immediate reinstatement of disengaged teachers who are below the statutory retirement age of 65 years.
The governor also directed the payment of outstanding salaries to teachers affected by verification issues, as well as the 4,075 newly recruited teachers who are yet to receive their wages.
Otti gave the directives Monday in Umuahia while addressing teachers at the 2026 World Teachers’ Day celebration, declaring that no teacher below 65 years should remain out of service on account of previous disengagement.
The governor said the N1 billion fund would be shared equally among teachers in the state, irrespective of when they joined the teaching service.
“I have instructed the Accountant-General of the State to share money equally to all of you.
“Whether you joined today or you joined 64 years ago, the total amount that I have — the amount for all of you — is one billion naira,” he said.
Otti also directed that all teachers whose salaries had been withheld because of verification challenges should be paid by the end of October.
He similarly ordered the payment of the 4,075 newly recruited teachers who have not received their salaries.
The Governor directed the Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education to immediately return to service all affected teachers below 65 years.
“I want to give instructions from here to the Honourable Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education that anybody who is less than 65, if they have been disengaged, you must return them back.
“You don’t require any further approval, I’ve given the approval from here — please bring all of them back, even if it is six months before retirement. Bring them back,” Otti ordered.
The governor said the decision was in line with his administration’s commitment to fairness and transparency, stressing that government must be consistent with its pronouncements.
On promotion arrears, Otti directed the Abia State Universal Basic Education Board, ASUBEB, to conclude the processing of teachers’ 2021 and 2022 promotions and harmonise the process with the State Head of Service for his approval.
He directed that the affected teachers be promoted before the end of October.
The governor also ordered the immediate payment of outstanding check-off dues, giving the Accountant-General seven days to clear the arrears.
Otti said several of the concerns raised by the Nigeria Union of Teachers had already been addressed, while others were receiving attention.
He said his administration’s investment in education was aimed at repositioning the sector as the foundation for the state’s development, stressing that the ongoing development of smart schools across the 17 local government areas was designed to prepare pupils for the future without undermining conventional education.
He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to free and compulsory education, while congratulating Abia pupils who excelled at the international schools debate championship in Qatar and those who topped the National Examinations Council, NECO, examinations.
Earlier, the Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Elder Goodluck Ubochi, said the theme of the 2026 World Teachers’ Day celebration, “Standing with Teachers: Protecting the Profession, Advancing Citizens, and Serving Our Teachers,” underscored the strategic role of teachers in nation-building.
Ubochi listed teacher recruitment, professional development, improved school infrastructure, modern learning environments and smart schools among the reforms being implemented by the administration.
The state Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Teachers, NUT, also acknowledged improvements in the sector, including increased budgetary allocation, mass recruitment, free and compulsory basic education and the extension of teachers’ retirement age from 60 to 65 years.
He, however, appealed for further improvement in teachers’ welfare and resolution of outstanding challenges.
The celebration featured a march-past by teachers from across the state.

Nwosu was the former ADC National Chairman who stepped down for the Mark leadership of the party. (NAN)

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has directed the Chairman of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) to produce in court the list of the personnel who were on duty on Jan. 19, 2022 at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu State.
Julius Mba, counsel to Abba Kyari and Insp. Simon Agirgba (1st and 3rd defendants), made this known on Monday before Justice Emeka Nwite while seeking an adjournment, following the absence of the defence witness in court.
Kyari, the former head of the defunct Police Intelligence Response Team (IRT), alongside four other suspended IRT officers, including the two now convicted drug traffickers, were initially being prosecuted by the NDLEA on an eight-count charge.
The agency accused Kyari and the officers of tampering with the cocaine the IRT officers recovered from the arrested drug traffickers at the airport.
The four officers are ACP Sunday J. Ubua; ASP Bawa James, Insp. Simon Agirgba and Insp. John Nuhu, named as 2nd to 5th defendants respectively.
Although the two convicted drug traffickers, Chibunna Umeibe and Emeka Ezenwanne, listed as 6th and 7th defendants, pleaded guilty to the counts, Kyari and his men pleaded not guilty to the counts against them.
When the case was called on Monday, NDLEA lawyer, Joseph Sunday, informed the court that the matter was scheduled for continuation of hearing.
He said the prosecution was ready to proceed, subject to the convenience of the court.
Responding, Mba said he confirmed that the case was slated for continuation of the evidence of the 2nd defence witness (DW-2), John Nwonke, who is a subpoenaed witness.
He, however, said unfortunately, there was a letter filed on behalf of the same witness, informing that he was illed.
He said the letter, dated Oct. 2, was addressed to the deputy chief registrar of the court and that the lead defence counsel, Onyechi Ikpeazu, SAN, was also copied.
The lawyer told the court Nwonke was illed at the moment and they were only praying that he gets well to continue and conclude his evidence.
“On that note, we may not be able to put in a witness today because this is a criminal trial and a very serious one at that matter,” he said.
Mba stated further that they had the instruction of Ikpeazu, who was representing Kyari and Agirgba, but unavoidably absent, to equally file a “subpoena duces tecum” to be served on the NDLEA boss.
He said the subpoena duces tecum was filed on Sept. 30 and graciously signed by Justice Nwite on Oct. 2.
“But we only received this, this morning my lord,” he said.
According to him, the subpoena duces tecum is requiring the NDLEA, through the DG, to produce before this court for inspection and use of this honourable court, the certified true copy of all the list of personnel of the agency who were on duty on 19th day of January, 2022, at Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu State for proper consideration and for the defence of 1st and 4th defendants sir.
A subpoena duces tecum is a legal court order that commands a person or business to bring specific physical or digital evidence to a legal proceeding.
Responding, the NDLEA lawyer said he was just seeing Nwonke’s letter.
“We have been here since morning and there is no courtesy at all to show us the letter and tell us the position of the witness.
“In any case, we will be opposing the application for adjournment,” Sunday said.
The lawyer argued that the his objection was predicated on the fact that the application was in bad taste which was calculated to subvert the administration of criminal practice.
He said contrary to Mba’s submission, on the last adjourned date, a lawyer (A.A. Akas) who appeared for Kyari notified the court that the DW-2 (Nwonke) was on official duty outside the country.
Sunday recalled that the court, before the adjournment, ordered that Nwonke should “be present in court today so that the case could proceed with the warning that any unseriousness will warrant the foreclosure of the defence.”
According to him, interestingly today, Akas Esq. is not present in court and the counsel in court has totally circumvented the specific orders of my lord.
Sunday alleged that Mba came up with a letter from a purportedly sick witness.
But Mba disagreed with Sunday’s use of words.
“My Lord, I cannot stand here and be insulted by my learner brother.
“This is not my letter; a letter is not coming from me, and for my learner brother to say I circumvented the order of courr, I take exception to this sir,” Mba said.
After the judge’s intervention, Sunday moved an oral application seeking an order foreclosing the evidence of the DW-2.
The NDLEA argued that the letter did not disclose the withess’ nature of sickness and the hospital he was receiving treatment.
Besides, he said “the DW-2 has turned himself into a medical doctor and taking the position of God to determine that the sickness will be for exactly two weeks.”
Sunday submitted that this was not a letter the can could consider.
“I don’t think we can base any adjournment on this matter,” he argued.
Resoonding to the issue of subpoena, the NDLEA lawyer said none of the prosecution team had been served with the letter.
“We don’t conduct trial by ambush. We are not aware of any subpoena my lord,” he said.
The lawyer, who urged the Court to order the defence to proceed on their next witness, prayed the court to foreclose Nwonke’s evidence “and treat him as having given a testimony that was not subjected to cross-examination.”
But Mba disagreed with Sunday’s argument.
He stated that his application was predicated upon fair, just and full determination of their defence on the merit and in the interest of justice, equity and fairness.
“It is not a matter of sentiment my lord,” he said.
He clarified that the information available to Akas, as at the last adjourned date, was that the witness was on official assignment.
“That has not changed,” he said, adding that upon his arrival, he wrote to court that he was indisposed.
He also restated that though they had applied for the subpoena lettter some day’s ago, he only received it on Monday after it was signed by the judge on Oct. 2.
Delivering the ruling, Justice Nwite held that Nwonke (DW-2)’s letter was not convincing enough for the court to grant the request for an adjournment.
The judge, however, held that in the interest of justice, the case would be adjourned until Oct. 7 for the continuation of the witness’ testimony and cross-examination.
“Failure of the witness to appear on the said date means that his testimony will be foreclosed,” he ruled.
The judge also ordered lawyers to the 1st to 5th defendants to submit to the court the names of the witnesses they intend to call before the next adjourned date. (NAN)
The post Alleged drug deal: Court invites NDLEA chairman in Abba Kyari’s trial appeared first on Vanguard News.

The IPO has further strengthened our net worth and enhanced our capacity to fund future growth, giving us greater balance sheet flexibility as we scale,” said RentoMojo cofounder, MD and CEO Geetansh Bamania.
In an investor presentation alongside the financial disclosures, the recently-listed startup noted that its EBITDA improved 17.5% YoY to ₹40.9 Cr in Q1 FY27, while EBITDA margin contracted to 32.2% from 41% in Q1 FY26.
The EBITDA took a hit as the company booked ₹11.4 Cr in costs related to “exceptional items”, which pertained to the fire at the company’s sub-leased warehouse in Noida in June this year.
“… The fire has resulted in significant damage to the said warehouse and the items of property, plant and equipment stored therein. The management has ascertained the total financial impact of ₹11.37 Cr attributable to derecognition of net carrying value of the property, plant and equipment, cost of consumable, other assets and other financial assets related to the warehouse / items of property, plant and equipment stored therein…,” the financials read.
RentoMojo also claims to have filed an insurance claim for the loss of property and equipment, adding that the first information report (FIR) and insurance surveyor report is still pending. The company has also received a legal notice from the sub-leasor, but believes that RentoMojo has “assessed as no liability arising from contractual obligations in terms of the sub- lease agreement”.
Founded in 2014 by Bamania and Ajay Nain, RentoMojo operates a subscription-based platform for renting furniture, appliances and home essentials. Backed by Accel, Chiratae Ventures and Bain Capital, the startup has raised over $45 Mn in funding to date.
On the operational front, RentoMojo claims to have operated 23 warehouses and 89 offline stores across India at the end of June 2026. It had a portfolio of 9.2 Lakh live products across furniture and appliances in Q1 FY27, up 41% YoY, and catered to 2.8 Lakh active users, up 36.3% YoY.
The company clocked an average revenue per product of ₹1,662.6 in the quarter under review, up 6.8% YoY and QoQ. Meanwhile, occupancy rate improved to 86.8% in Q1 FY27 as against 84.8% in the year ago quarter.
The financials come weeks after RentoMojo made a strong stock market debut. The stock listed at ₹482.45 on the NSE, a premium of 19.42% over its issue price of ₹404. On the BSE, RentoMojo opened at ₹480, up 18.81% from the issue price.
The startup’s public issue had comprised a fresh issue worth ₹150 Cr and an OFS of up to 2.74 Cr shares worth ₹1,105.6 Cr.
Separately, the company’s board also appointed company secretary Deepika Bhandiwad as the compliance officer to comply with SEBI norms.
The board also gave its nod to appoint Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP as the statutory auditors of the company for a term of five consecutive years. This proposal is, however, subject to shareholder nod.
“Our ambition is to build Rentomojo into a scaled, technology-led platform for flexible living, while remaining disciplined on profitability and capital efficiency. The IPO is an important milestone in that journey, but it is only the beginning,” added Bamania.
Shares of RentoMojo closed Monday’s trading session 2.83% lower at ₹510.8 on the BSE.

items.title: 10 oldest universities in Africa
items.summary:
By Mmesoma Goodness
African universities have a long and rich history of scholarship, with some of the continent’s most important centres of learning dating back more than 1,000 years.
Some of these institutions began as mosques, madrasas and centres of Islamic scholarship before evolving into institutions recognised as universities in the modern era. Others began as colleges or higher-education institutions during the 19th century and later acquired full university status.
Because of these differences, the ranking below is based broadly on the earliest documented origins of the institution or educational tradition that developed into the present-day institution, rather than strictly on the date when each institution acquired modern university status.
Here are 10 of Africa’s oldest universities and higher-learning institutions.

items.content:
By Mmesoma Goodness
African universities have a long and rich history of scholarship, with some of the continent’s most important centres of learning dating back more than 1,000 years.
Some of these institutions began as mosques, madrasas and centres of Islamic scholarship before evolving into institutions recognised as universities in the modern era. Others began as colleges or higher-education institutions during the 19th century and later acquired full university status.
Because of these differences, the ranking below is based broadly on the earliest documented origins of the institution or educational tradition that developed into the present-day institution, rather than strictly on the date when each institution acquired modern university status.
Here are 10 of Africa’s oldest universities and higher-learning institutions.
1. Ez-Zitouna University — Tunisia
Educational origins: 737 AD
Ez-Zitouna University in Tunis traces its educational history to the Great Mosque of Ez-Zitouna, where Islamic sciences were being taught from around 737 AD, according to the university’s official history. The mosque itself dates to an earlier period, with the university describing it as having been founded in 734 AD.
Over the centuries, Ez-Zitouna became an important centre of Islamic scholarship, teaching subjects including Islamic jurisprudence, Quranic studies and Arabic.
The institution’s modern university structure is much more recent, but its long educational tradition is why Ez-Zitouna is frequently included among Africa’s oldest centres of higher learning.
2. University of Al-Qarawiyyin — Morocco
Founded: 859 AD
The University of Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez is traditionally dated to 859 AD, when Fatima al-Fihri established the institution that developed around the Al-Qarawiyyin mosque.
It became an important centre of Islamic and Arabic scholarship and attracted scholars and students from across the Muslim world.
Al-Qarawiyyin is widely recognised as one of the world’s oldest continuously operating institutions of higher learning. However, as with several institutions on this list, its early form was different from the modern university system that developed centuries later.
3. Al-Azhar University — Egypt
Origins: 970–972 AD
Al-Azhar University in Cairo traces its origins to the Al-Azhar Mosque, whose construction began after the Fatimid conquest of Egypt. The first Friday prayer at the mosque was held in 972 AD.
Al-Azhar subsequently developed into a major centre of Islamic scholarship, particularly in theology, Islamic law and Arabic studies.
Although its modern university structure developed much later, Al-Azhar’s more than 1,000-year history as a centre of learning makes it one of Africa’s most historically significant educational institutions.
4. Sankore and the Historic Centres of Learning in Timbuktu — Mali
Major period of scholarship: 14th–16th centuries
Timbuktu should not be listed as a “University of Timbuktu founded in 982 AD.” There is no reliable historical basis for that specific founding date.
Instead, Timbuktu is better described as a historic centre of higher learning, particularly through institutions associated with the Sankore, Djingareyber and Sidi Yahia mosques.
UNESCO describes Timbuktu as an intellectual and spiritual capital of Africa during its 15th and 16th-century golden age, with the University of Sankore and other madrasas playing a major role in Islamic scholarship.
Sankore became particularly renowned for scholarship in areas including Islamic law, literature, mathematics, astronomy and other fields of knowledge. Historical accounts associate Timbuktu with a large network of scholars, students and manuscript collections.
The city therefore deserves a place in a list of Africa’s oldest centres of higher learning, but not with the incorrect 982 AD founding date.
5. Fourah Bay College — Sierra Leone
Founded: 1827
Fourah Bay College in Freetown was founded on 18 February 1827 by the Church Missionary Society.
The University of Sierra Leone describes it as the first Western-style university institution established in sub-Saharan Africa.
The college was originally established to train teachers and missionaries. In 1876, it became a degree-granting institution through its affiliation with Durham University in England.
In 1967, Fourah Bay College became a constituent college of the University of Sierra Leone.
Its nearly two-century history makes it one of the most important landmarks in the development of Western-style higher education in Africa.
6. University of Cape Town — South Africa
Origins: 1829
The University of Cape Town (UCT) traces its origins to 1829, when the South African College was established in Cape Town.
The college initially combined secondary and tertiary education. It expanded considerably during the late 19th and early 20th centuries and eventually developed into a fully fledged university.
UCT was formally established as a university in 1918.
The institution is now one of Africa’s leading research universities and remains South Africa’s oldest university.
Thus, while 1829 is used to describe UCT’s historical origins, the university in its formal modern form dates from 1918.
7. University of Liberia — Liberia
Origins: 1862
The University of Liberia was established in 1862 as Liberia College.
According to the university’s official history, Liberia College opened its doors to students in February 1863, with seven students in its first group. It became a full university in 1951.
The institution was established during the early years of the Liberian republic to provide higher education and help develop the country’s professional and intellectual class.
Today, the University of Liberia is a public university with campuses and programmes covering a range of academic disciplines.
8. Stellenbosch University — South Africa
Origins: 1866
Stellenbosch University’s educational roots can be traced to the Stellenbosch Gymnasium, established in 1866.
The institution subsequently evolved through several stages, becoming a college and later Victoria College before achieving full university status.
Stellenbosch University was officially established as a university on 2 April 1918, alongside the University of Cape Town and the University of South Africa.
The university therefore has a distinction between its 1866 educational origins and its 1918 formal university status.
It has since grown into one of South Africa’s major research universities, with strengths across science, engineering, agriculture, medicine, the humanities and social sciences.
9. University of South Africa — South Africa
Origins: 1873
The University of South Africa (Unisa) traces its history to the University of the Cape of Good Hope, established in 1873 by an act of the Cape Colony’s Parliament.
The institution was modelled on the University of London and initially served largely as an examining and academic standards body for affiliated colleges. It was renamed the University of South Africa in 1916.
Unisa later developed into a major distance-learning institution. Its transition to distance education became particularly significant in the 20th century, and it is now one of the world’s largest open-distance learning universities.
Therefore, 1873 represents the origin of the institution’s predecessor rather than the establishment of Unisa under its present name.
10. Cairo University — Egypt
Founded: 1908
Cairo University traces its origins to the Egyptian University, which was inaugurated on 21 December 1908 as a private university.
The institution was later incorporated into the state university system. In 1925, the government established a state university under the name Egyptian University, incorporating the earlier institution and several higher schools.
The university was subsequently known as Fuad I University before becoming Cairo University.
It has played a major role in Egyptian education, research and intellectual life and remains one of the country’s leading universities.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has given the Federal Government a 14-day ultimatum to pay outstanding salary arrears.
SSANU National President, Mr Mohammed Ibrahim, announced the ultimatum in a communique issued on Monday in Abuja, after the union’s 56th National Executive Council (NEC) meeting.
Ibrahim said that the meeting, held at the University of Uyo, Akwa Ibom, from Sept. 30 to Oct. 1, deliberated on workers’ welfare, university funding and implementation of the 2026 FGN/SSANU Agreement.
He said failure to meet the demand within the stipulated period would compel the union to embark on an indefinite strike without further notice.
He said the NEC demanded immediate payment of all outstanding arrears arising from implementation of the 2026 FGN/SSANU CONTTA salary structure, effective from Jan. 1, 2026.
“NEC categorically demanded the immediate release and payment of all outstanding arrears arising from the implementation of the 2026 FGN/SSANU CONTTA salary structure, calculated from the effective date of Jan. 1, 2026,” he said.
Ibrahim said some universities had implemented the salary structure largely through internally sourced funds, without direct financial backing from the Federal Government.
He urged Vice-Chancellors and Governing Councils of universities that were yet to implement the agreement to emulate institutions that had taken proactive steps toward compliance.
The SSANU president also demanded immediate payment of two months’ salaries withheld during the 2022 industrial action, alongside one-year arrears from the 25 per cent and 35 per cent salary increases.
Ibrahim described the outstanding payments as “legitimate entitlements” owed to affected workers, saying, “continued delay had worsened the financial hardship confronting members”.
He expressed concern over uneven implementation of the agreement in state-owned universities and called on state governments to provide the necessary funding for full compliance.
On university funding, Ibrahim called for increased investment in electricity, laboratories, workshops, libraries, ICT facilities, security systems and infrastructure maintenance, while rejecting virtual accreditation as a substitute for physical verification.
He also rejected any arrangement to concede, privatise or transfer management of King’s College, Lagos, or other public educational institutions to private bodies, urging government to preserve public ownership and accessibility.
Ibrahim further expressed concern over insecurity, rising living costs and food insecurity.
He called for stronger protection of farming communities and educational institutions, including policies to protect workers’ incomes. (NAN)

items.author: M Yasir
items.content:
Karachi mobile dealers have handed over 3,386 stolen, snatched, and missing mobile phones worth more than Rs. 285 million to the Citizen-Police Liaison Committee (CPLC) over the past 10 years, according to exclusive details shared with ProPakistani.
The phones were identified when customers brought them to mobile dealers for resale and were checked against CPLC records.
According to the Karachi Electronic Dealers Association (KEDA), dealers also recently handed over 231 stolen, snatched, and missing phones worth around Rs. 5 million to the CPLC. The phones are expected to be returned to their rightful owners who had registered complaints.
Under an arrangement between KEDA, CPLC, and local police, dealers check new and used smartphones against CPLC records before reselling them. Phones reported stolen, snatched, or missing are handed over to the authorities.
KEDA President Rizwan Irfan told ProPakistani that dealers have been following standard operating procedures to prevent stolen and snatched phones from entering the resale market.
He said dealers inform sellers when a phone is flagged in CPLC records. In several cases, however, suspected criminals tried to sell large quantities of suspicious phones despite being warned.
Dealers and the association have so far detained around 20 such suspects and handed them over to the police.
Irfan said the used mobile phone market remains important for both traders and consumers, offering better margins for dealers and relatively cheaper phones for buyers.
He added that a significant number of stolen and snatched phones are still traded through informal markets and smuggled across the borders with Afghanistan and Iran.
The government had considered banning the resale of used mobile phones in 2016, but traders later developed a verification mechanism with authorities to keep the market operational while preventing stolen phones from being resold.

items.author: Fiaz Mahmood
items.content:
The absence of an investigation officer (IO) during hearing of the bail petitions of rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha irked an anti-terrorism court (ATC) judge who summoned a DSP and threatened to send him to jail, in case he failed to satisfy the court.
ATC Judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain on Monday took up the couple post-arrest bail petitions in a case that includes terrorism charges and violation of Section 144,
When the judge asked the court staff about the investigating officer, he was informed that the investigator had not shown up. Expressing displeasure, the judge directed the staff to summon the DSP. "Verbal statements will not be accepted," he remarked as the court took a short recess.
When DSP Legal Naeem Yousaf appeared before the court, the judge expressed severe displeasure over the investigating officer's absence and asked where the case record was.
When the DSP began speaking in English, the judge told him to speak in Urdu. The DSP said that, according to his information, the investigating officer was out of the city along with the record.
The judge expressed further anger.
"You should be ashamed," the judge remarked, warning that he could have the DSP stand facing the wall in the courtroom and send him and the SP to jail in uniform for six months if he failed to produce evidence of the investigator's absence from the city.
The judge also directed the security officials to ensure the DSP did not leave the court premises without permission. The DSP sought some time to provide the relevant information. He subsequently produced a WhatsApp printout, claiming that the investigating officer was in Gilgit-Baltistan.
The judge refused to accept the WhatsApp copy and threw it back toward the DSP, directing him to produce the original document before the court.
He again ordered that handcuffs be brought into the courtroom and directed the security in-charge to remain there, saying that if he ordered the DSP's arrest, the DSP should not be allowed to leave. He also instructed the gate security not to let the police officer leave the premises.
Addressing Advocate Riasat Ali Azad, the judge said the judiciary should have a "judicial force" capable of ensuring immediate implementation of court orders. "The same system of 1898 and 1860 is still operating," the judge remarked.
Later, the DSP submitted a report to the court, stating that the investigating officer was indeed in Gilgit-Baltistan and that his phone was switched off. He said it could take 10 to 15 days to establish contact with the officer.
The judge said he would issue a detailed order regarding the absence of the investigating officer.
The lawyers requested that the matter be adjourned until Tuesday (today) but the judge adjourned the hearing until October 13, stating that he would pass an order concerning the investigating officer.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) said on Monday it was ready to hold local government (LG) elections in Punjab
However, the electoral watcheog said legal and administrative complications were continuing to hold up polls in Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Quetta and the cantonment boards.
The assessment was made at a special meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja to take stock of preparations for LG elections across the provinces, the federal capital and the cantonments.
The commission reviewed the province-wise progress of the exercise.
According to an ECP statement, preparations in Punjab had reached the stage where the commission was ready to proceed with the elections and had already sent a draft election schedule to the provincial government.
The commission has also sought lists of district returning officers, returning officers and assistant returning officers to facilitate their appointments, and asked the Punjab government to respond to the proposed schedule at the earliest.
In Sindh, the ECP said preparations had also begun for holding local body elections on time, with instructions issued to its relevant office to take all necessary steps.
In Islamabad, delimitation has been completed, but the Islamabad Capital Territory Amendment Ordinance 2026 has lapsed, the meeting was informed.
The ECP said a National Assembly Standing Committee had already approved legislation in line with the ordinance. It therefore decided to approach the federal government for the "immediate completion of legislation".
However, in the event that the legislation was not completed, the commission said it would proceed with the elections under the existing Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act 2015.
The ECP was also told that delimitation in all cantonments had been completed and that it was ready to conduct local body polls there.
However, the amended Cantonments Act requires the federal government to make a formal request to the ECP for holding the elections under Section 19-D.
"Despite reminders and a letter from the chief election commissioner to the prime minister, no request had been received," the statement said.
"The ECP decided to write a final letter to the Ministry of Defence, failing which it would take an appropriate decision regarding holding of elections".
In Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, the ECP recalled that delimitation had been completed in 23 districts and was in progress in seven others when the provincial government amended Section 6 of the K-P Local Government Act 2013.
The amendment increased the population threshold for village and neighbourhood councils from 5,000-15,000 to 30,000-40,000.
In Balochistan, the ECP noted that the term of the local government institutions would expire on Feb 8, 2027. However, it said LG elections in Quetta could not be held despite orders of the Federal Constitutional Court.
The commission said it had completed delimitation on May 21, 2026, in compliance with the court's order, but the provincial government subsequently bifurcated Quetta into two districts without providing details of the new boundaries and other required data.

items.title: WhatsApp Starts Testing Restricted Chat
items.summary:
WhatsApp has started rolling out its new Restricted Chat feature to some users in its Android and iOS beta programs.
The feature was first spotted in development last month as an upgrade to Advanced Chat Privacy.
According to WABetaInfo, Restricted Chat is available to some users running WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.36.4 and WhatsApp beta for iOS version 26.39.10.20.
What Restricted Chat Does
Restricted Chat is optional and is not enabled for conversations by default.
Users have to turn it on manually from the chat info screen.
Once enabled, WhatsApp displays a message inside the conversation and applies four restrictions to the chat.
Users in a Restricted Chat cannot:
Automatically save media to their devices
Export the chat
Use Meta AI features inside the conversation
Access the chat through linked devices
WhatsApp says blocking linked-device access can help prevent people from using unofficial clients or AI agents to access the conversation.
End-to-End Encryption Still App
items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
WhatsApp has started rolling out its new Restricted Chat feature to some users in its Android and iOS beta programs.
The feature was first spotted in development last month as an upgrade to Advanced Chat Privacy.
According to WABetaInfo, Restricted Chat is available to some users running WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.36.4 and WhatsApp beta for iOS version 26.39.10.20.
What Restricted Chat Does
Restricted Chat is optional and is not enabled for conversations by default.
Users have to turn it on manually from the chat info screen.
Once enabled, WhatsApp displays a message inside the conversation and applies four restrictions to the chat.
Users in a Restricted Chat cannot:
Automatically save media to their devices
Export the chat
Use Meta AI features inside the conversation
Access the chat through linked devices
WhatsApp says blocking linked-device access can help prevent people from using unofficial clients or AI agents to access the conversation.
End-to-End Encryption Still Applies
WhatsApp says messages and calls remain protected by end-to-end encryption whether Restricted Chat is enabled or not.
The new feature adds extra controls on top of that encryption by limiting how content can be accessed or moved outside the conversation.
Public Rollout Still Unknown
WhatsApp has not announced when Restricted Chat will become available to all users.
For now, the feature is limited to some users enrolled in WhatsApp’s beta program.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The debt level of state-owned companies jumped to a record Rs10.1 trillion by the end of December 2025, higher by 242% than the central bank statistics, which raises questions about governance reforms.
The finance ministry disclosed that the per-working-day loss of SOEs increased to Rs2.8 billion (Rs730 billion annually) and the per-day financial support swelled to Rs6.6 billion (Rs1.7 trillion per year). At the given per-day losses and fiscal support, the cumulative annual impact comes to Rs2.5 trillion, which is Rs1.5 trillion more than this fiscal year's federal development budget.
These figures were disclosed by the Ministry of Finance on Monday in an excellent analytical report on SOE monitoring for July-December 2025, which stated "financial engineering and debt re-profiling measures alone remain insufficient" to address the circular debt problem in the power sector. The findings negate the claims made by the federal government, the IMF and the World Bank about improvements in the SOE affairs, particularly the reduction in the circular debt stock and flow.
According to the Central Monitoring Unit (CMU) of the finance ministry, the total debt of SOEs jumped to Rs10.1 trillion as of end-December, an increase of Rs1.3 trillion, or 14.3%, over the same period of the preceding year. The total debt the CMU reported was Rs7.1 trillion, or 242%, higher than the total public debt and liabilities of SOEs reported by the State Bank of Pakistan. The SBP bulletin put the debt and liabilities of SOEs at Rs2.95 trillion till December last year.
The broader SOE balance sheet remains highly leveraged, with debt exposure exceeding Rs10 trillion, including Rs2.6 trillion in foreign currency-denominated liabilities, said the CMU. The publication of the report was delayed for a while and it came just two days before the end of IMF talks.
The CMU said the Rs2.6 trillion foreign liabilities of SOEs were "exposing the sovereign to elevated exchange rate pass-through risk, refinancing pressure, imported inflation sensitivity and external account volatility". The report showed the government gave Rs2.1 trillion in cash development loans to SOEs as of December last year, higher by Rs416 billion, or 25%, in a year. Likewise, there was a 40% hike in foreign loans, which jumped to Rs2.6 trillion.
The report stated that banks also gave Rs3.1 trillion in loans to SOEs and the cost of unfunded pension liabilities was Rs2 trillion, up 11%. "The aggregate loss profile of loss-making SOEs is estimated at Rs2.8 billion on a per-working-day basis, while fiscal support through subsidies, grants, loans and equity injections reached nearly Rs6.6 billion per day, equivalent to 11% of total federal budgetary receipts."
Concurrently, the CMU stated that Pakistan's combined circular debt escalated to Rs3.3 trillion and despite restructuring initiatives and the partial warehousing of liabilities through Central Power Purchasing Agency-linked financing arrangements, serviced via the Debt Servicing Surcharge (DSS), the stock still increased within the six-month period.
"This deterioration demonstrates that financial engineering and debt re-profiling measures alone remain insufficient in the absence of deep-rooted operational reforms across generation, transmission, distribution, tariff rationalisation, governance enforcement, theft control and recovery mechanisms," said the finance ministry.
The report stated that additional fiscal fragilities arise from sovereign guarantees exceeding Rs2.1 trillion and unfunded pension liabilities approaching Rs1.9 trillion, both of which represent latent contingent obligations capable of crystallising into direct federal liabilities under stressed macroeconomic conditions.
The CMU said the anticipated IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss (ECL) provisioning requirements within the oil & gas sector could trigger incremental provisioning shocks approaching Rs500 billion, materially impairing profitability, retained earnings, dividend flows to the government and overall market capitalisation within one of the few currently profitable segments of the portfolio.
The report commented on performance of the power sector that was on the decline. Losses relating to DISCOs were primarily attributable to technical losses exceeding Nepra benchmarks, persistent under-recoveries and continuing circular debt accumulation arising from operational inefficiencies.
The circular-debt flow attributable to DISCO inefficiencies amounted to Rs112 billion, while under-recoveries contributed an additional Rs31 billion during the six-month period. Notably, despite broader restructuring initiatives, the underlying circular debt flow continued to rise to Rs374 billion on a gross basis over the first half of 2026 fiscal year as per Power Division's numbers.
The CMU said that overall the loss profile of the SOE sector continued to remain concentrated in structurally weak infrastructure and energy entities, particularly within the power distribution segment, where inefficiencies, technical losses and tariff distortions continued to transmit significant fiscal pressure onto the sovereign balance sheet.
The most pronounced increase was recorded in equity injections during the first half of last fiscal year, which surged by 190% to Rs225 billion. These injections were primarily one-off in nature and directed largely towards clearing power-sector circular debt obligations through payments to Independent Power Producers (IPPs). However, despite these interventions, the circular debt stock continued to accumulate, increasing by Rs143 billion during the six-month period, it added.
To improve fiscal transparency and mitigate the accumulation of unaccounted-for subsidy payables, the implementation of structured Public Service Obligation (PSO) frameworks supported by accurate and verifiable costing methodologies is recommended across applicable SOEs, according to CMU.
It said that Pakistan's SOE portfolio represented a material and increasingly systemic macro-fiscal vulnerability, characterised by excessive dependence on a narrow subset of profitable entities within the oil and financial sectors, while a substantial portion of the broader portfolio remained structurally loss-making and fiscally dependent.
Profitability within the oil sector itself remains materially exposed to international commodity price volatility and limited portfolio-level hedging mechanisms, thereby increasing earnings sensitivity and dividend instability during adverse pricing cycles. Accordingly, the portfolio exhibits elevated concentration risk, whereby a limited group of profitable SOEs effectively subsidises broader systemic inefficiencies across the federal SOE landscape.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) is seeking a review of the incremental consumption package introduced for industrial and agricultural consumers following an increase in the cost of electricity.
The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) conducted a public hearing on Monday to review the consumption package. A tariff of Rs22.98 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) had been fixed under the package for industrial and agricultural consumers. The incentive scheme covers industrial and private agricultural electricity consumers across jurisdictions of ex-Wapda power distribution companies and K-Electric. It applies to both Time-of-Use (ToU) and Non-Time-of-Use (N-ToU) consumers as well as covers peak and off-peak incremental electricity consumption.
The Power Division submitted a review motion during the public hearing. According to the presentation, Nepra had approved the package on December 9, 2025. The decision was formally notified on December 10, 2025 to remain in effect for three years. The division argued that there was a significant pressure on the scheme's tariff of Rs22.98/kWh as average marginal costs exceeded the announced rate over several months. The weighted average marginal cost reached Rs27.58/kWh from December through May. The loss-adjusted marginal cost produced an even higher weighted average of Rs31.83/kWh, according to the Power Division.
The division contended that the average marginal cost hit Rs36.71/kWh during April and remained at Rs33.98/kWh during May. The loss-adjusted cost rose to Rs42.37/kWh in April and Rs39.22/kWh in May.
Until such approval of the power-sector regulator, the difference is being borne by other consumers across the board that creates a central issue for the ongoing semi-annual review.
The package also contains a separate safeguard linked to consumption growth. A review is triggered when combined industrial and agricultural consumption exceeds 25% above the baseline. January recorded a monthly growth of 25.13%, while February registered a rise of 26.20%. April recorded the highest monthly growth of 34.81%. Other months remained below the 25% threshold.
The semi-annual review creates another basis for considering a tariff adjustment. Any decision taken requires reviews to maintain cost-revenue alignment. The Power Division said it also allowed marginal tariffs to be adjusted, when necessary. "The scheme must terminate if upward adjustments become necessary during two consecutive reviews." The division was required to submit such data after stakeholder consultations. The expected timeline was the first week of June 2026. Instead, raw data was provided to Nepra on July 29, 2026.
After Nepra requested a proposal following consultations, the division responded on September 9 and asked the regulator to kick off proceedings, according to the presentation. The six-month weighted average marginal rate stood around Rs32/kWh and four months had already passed under the second review period. It raised the question about whether the package should be suspended amid continued higher marginal prices. Average tariff comparisons also show different effective break-even prices. For B1 peak consumers, the effective break-even price was Rs31.15/kWh, for B2 Time-of-Use consumers, the break-even price was Rs29.05/kWh and for B3, B4 and B5 categories, the rates were Rs30.03, Rs29.62 and Rs32.91 per kWh, respectively.
The immediate issue is whether the tariff of Rs22.98/kWh reflects current marginal costs. The presentation indicates that actual costs have remained materially higher. Nepra's hearing will determine whether the rate should go up or suspension should follow. Its outcome will shape the future of the incremental consumption package.
Intervener Rehan Javed called for revising the rate according to the actual marginal cost, effective from June 2026. He also asked for refunding the marginal price charged to non-beneficiary consumers from June 2026. He pleaded to recover it from the beneficiaries at the revised rate and any residue from the government as sponsor of the package.
Amir Sheikh, another intervener, said the package was increasing the cross-subsidy cost for domestic/commercial users, adding that a majority of industries had to cross-subsidise a few large consumers.
"Gas levy has led to captive-grid conversion, so the package is not required," he said, arguing that resorting to load-shedding and allowing a reduced cost package to industrial and agricultural consumers were self-contradictory. "The only fair and sound decision is to suspend the package," he said.

items.title: Thar coalmine begins third expansion

items.content:
The third-phase expansion of the Thar Block-II coalmine has commenced in Sindh's Tharparkar district, further increasing the mine's annual production capacity from 7.6 million tonnes to 11.2 million tonnes and the use of indigenous resources for affordable power generation.
Sindh Engro Coal Mining Company (SECMC) began commercial operations in Thar Block-II in 2019 with an annual mining capacity of 3.8 million tons per annum. The second phase, completed in 2022, increased capacity to 7.6 million tons. With the third phase, the annual production will rise by another 3.6 million tonnes, the third expansion in seven years.
SECMC contributes 14% electricity to the national grid. The additional coal will be supplied to Lucky Electric Power Company Limited (LEPCL), which operates a 660-megawatt power plant. With its inclusion, SECMC will supply coal to power plants with a combined generation capacity of 1,980 MW, including 660MW Engro Powergen Thar Limited (EPTL), 330MW Thar Energy Limited (TEL) and 330MW ThalNova Power Thar Limited (TNPL).
After the expansion, the levelised coal tariff is projected to decline from $36.72 to $32.01 per tonne, resulting in an estimated annual reduction of around Rs15 billion in generation costs and saving an estimated $220 million in fuel imports. The expanded power generation will provide reliable electricity to around 4.5 million households.
Speaking at a ceremony to mark the occasion, SECMC Chief Executive Officer Amir Iqbal said, "Thar's story is a journey from the impossible to excellence, achieved through vision, collaboration and resilience." He said Thar is contributing not only to Pakistan's energy security but also to the country's economic growth.
PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said the scale of development witnessed in Thar was unmatched elsewhere in Pakistan, highlighting the transformation in the region's health and education systems. He felicitated SECMC on its achievement, with the Thar mine now ranked among the top 4% of mines globally.

items.content:
The Privatisation Commission (PC) board on Monday considered and approved key measures to advance the ongoing privatisation transactions across the power, aviation and financial sectors.
The board met under the chairmanship of Muhammad Ali, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Privatisation and Chairman of the Privatisation Commission, said a press release. As a major agenda item, the board approved the prequalification of nine interested parties (IPs) for the privatisation of Gujranwala Electric Power Company (Gepco). The board was informed that 11 Expressions of Interest (EOIs) had been received for Gepco for the acquisition of 51% to 100% shareholding, together with management control. Following evaluation of the submissions against the approved prequalification criteria, the financial adviser recommended nine interested parties for prequalification and progression to the next stage of the transaction.
The prequalified parties included Aktor Elektrik Enerji Yatirimlari San Ve Tic AS, Genvera Enerji AS, Cengiz Enerji Sanayii Ve Ticaret AS, Engro Energy Limited, Sapphire Fibres, Hub Power Holdings consortium, Shirazi Investments Ltd consortium, Artistic Milliners Ltd consortium and AKD Securities' consortium.
The prequalified parties include three Turkish energy companies, alongside leading Pakistani business groups and investment consortia, reflecting continued domestic and international investor interest in Pakistan's electricity distribution sector. Of the remaining parties, K-Electric formally withdrew its Expression of Interest through a written intimation to the Privatisation Commission, while Al Sharif Contracting & Commercial Development Co was unable to provide the documents required under the Request for Statement of Qualification (RSoQ).
The nine prequalified parties will now proceed to the next stage of the transaction in accordance with the approved process, including access to the Virtual Data Room for detailed buy-side due diligence.
In the aviation sector, the board considered the reconstitution of the negotiating committee for the outsourcing/concession of the Allama Iqbal International Airport, Lahore; Jinnah International Airport, Karachi; and Islamabad International Airport, as part of the commission's ongoing efforts to advance the airport outsourcing programme through a structured transaction process.
The board also reviewed progress on key financial-sector transactions and advised transaction advisers to fast-track the privatisation processes for House Building Finance Company Limited (HBFCL) and Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited (ZTBL), with a view to ensuring timely progress on both transactions.
The board reaffirmed its commitment to advancing the government's privatisation programme through transparent, competitive and professionally managed transactions, with a focus on attracting credible domestic and international investment, improving efficiency and service delivery, and maximising value for the government and people of Pakistan.

Pakistan has significant potential to expand inclusive insurance coverage, which can strengthen social protection and support progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), said Michael J McCord, Managing Director of MicroInsurance Centre at Milliman.
He made these remarks while speaking at a session of the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) Talk Series on "Inclusive Insurance: Global Insights."
In his lecture, McCord highlighted the potential to expand insurance protection for underserved households, farmers, workers and small businesses in Pakistan. He stressed that insurance could help protect livelihoods, strengthen financial resilience and provide a wider social safety net.
McCord said insurance products must deliver meaningful value to consumers and emphasised that products should be easy to understand, affordable and responsive to customers' actual needs.
He urged insurers to build public trust through timely and reliable claims' payments, noting that customers' experience while filing a claim would shape perception about the industry's reputation. He also highlighted the importance of digital technology and alternative distribution channels in reducing costs and extending coverage.
Earlier welcoming the session participants, Commissioner Insurance Imtiaz Haider said microinsurance could help low-income families, farmers and small businesses recover from illness, accidents or natural disasters without depletion of their savings or selling productive assets. He reaffirmed the SECP's commitment to an inclusive and trusted insurance sector, stressing that affordable risk protection was essential for wider financial inclusion.

Can Premium Hongqi Cars Find Buyers in Pakistan?
Hongqi’s expected arrival would add another premium brand to Pakistan’s automotive market.
However, the bigger question will be whether there is enough demand for such vehicles in the country.
Luxury cars already represent a relatively small part of Pakistan’s overall vehicle market, and Hongqi would have to compete for buyers looking at established premium brands.
Dewan Motors has not yet revealed which Hongqi models it plans to introduce, their prices, or the exact launch date.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Marico has acquired an additional 24.09% stake in plant-based nutrition and personal care brand Plix for ₹1,012.03 Cr in an all-cash deal, taking its total holding in the startup to 84.09%.
The latest transaction is part of an agreement to acquire a total 38.18% stake from Plix’s founders and certain other shareholders.
Marico plans to acquire 14.09% stake in July 2027. The consideration for this tranche will include a base amount of up to ₹592 Cr, along with additional payments linked to milestones.
Marico said the investment in Plix parent Satiya Nutraceuticals and its wholly owned subsidiary Juzio has helped broaden its addressable market across value-added foods and nutrition, while strengthening its presence in the growing personal care and wellness segments.
Founded in 2020 by Satiya and Zaveri, Plix Life is a Mumbai-based D2C startup that sells a wide range of plant-based nutrition products, such as workout supplements, ingestible sunscreens, hair growth serums and skincare products.
To note, Plix parent’s consolidated revenue nearly doubled to ₹864.31 Cr in FY26 from ₹432.84 Cr in FY25.
Marico acquired 37.75% stake in D2C nutrition brand Plix for ₹369.01 Cr in July 2023, and it further acquired 25.25% of the paid-up share capital by May 2025. Plix’s cap table featured names like Guild Capital and RPSG Ventures.
The deal is in line with Marico’s broader push into high-growth consumer categories as the company looks to build businesses beyond its established portfolio of food, personal care and consumer products.
Marico kicked off 2026 with an acquisition spree. Marico snapped up a 93.27% stake in gourmet popcorn brand 4700BC’s parent Zea Maize from PVR INOX for ₹226.8 Cr. In February, it picked up a 60% stake in Bengaluru-based plant-based protein startup Cosmix Wellness for ₹226 Cr. It also acquired a 75% stake in Vietnam-based Skinetiq Joint Stock Company for an estimated ₹262-350 Cr.
The rapid growth of Plix comes as large FMCG companies continue to expand into newer consumer categories, particularly health, nutrition, personal care and wellness.
For instance, FMCG major ITC completed the acquisition of 100% of Yoga Bar’s parent Sproutlife Foods, buying the remaining 52.5% stake for around ₹645 Cr, only a few weeks ago. Prior to that, FMCG major Emami acquired a 60% stake in IncNut Digital, the parent entity of D2C beauty and personal care brands Vedix and SkinKraft, for up to ₹321 Cr in an all-cash transaction, in May.
Hindustan Unilever Ltd (HUL) also acquired the remaining 49% stake in OZiva parent Zywie Ventures for ₹824 Cr, in February this year.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
India’s startup funding market remained selective in the third quarter of 2026, with investors backing fewer startups even as the overall capital deployed saw a modest uptick.
Indian startups raised $2.2 Bn in Q3 2026, up 5% from $2.1 Bn in the year-ago quarter, despite the number of funding deals falling 13% to 210. The pool of active investors also shrank 24% YoY to 511 from 676, pointing to a more concentrated funding environment.
The trend was particularly visible in the early-stage ecosystem, where investors became more discerning about the startups they backed. At the same time, venture debt continued to be the most prominent source of capital, with debt firms bagging the top most active investors spot this quarter as well.
Stride Ventures led the overall investor leaderboard with 38 deals, followed by Alteria Capital with 31. The duo have maintained this lead throughout 2026.
Among equity investors, 3one4 Capital topped the list with 19 investments, followed by Rainmatter with 16, IvyCap Ventures with 15 and Antler with 14.
With the funding market becoming more selective, these investors stood out for the breadth and consistency of their deployment during the quarter.
With that, here’s a look at the most active startup investors of Q3 2026.
Access Free Report
Stride Ventures
The venture debt firm continued to be the most active startup investor in Q3 2026, backing 38 startups during the quarter. Its notable investments included Branch, FreshToHome and GIVA, among others.
The firm has been expanding its global presence and currently manages seven debt funds across India, the GCC, the UK and Europe. It is also planning to deploy $1 Bn across global credit markets over the next few years.
The firm counts 16 unicorns among its 220+ portfolio companies, including Zetwerk, Udaan, Upstox, Ola Electric and Perfios.
Alteria Capital
The firm continued to be the second most active investor this quarter after closing 48 deals in the first half of the year. In the September quarter, Alteria closed 31 deals backing startups like Curefoods, Ultrahuman, Yubi, River Mobility and Miraggio, among others.
The Mumbai-headquartered firm is known for backing early to growth stage startups across sectors like foodtech, agritech, fintech, deeptech, EV and retail.
Alteria Capital manages four funds and has deployed more than $750 Mn to date. The firm has over $550 Mn in assets under management and has backed more than 15 unicorns, including Zepto, BharatPe, Mensa Brands and Spinny.
Google
Google emerged as the third most active investor in Q3 2026, backing 20 startups via its Google for Startups Accelerator: India 2026 programme.
Announced in July, the 2026 cohort comprises 20 AI-first startups selected from nearly 2,500 applications. The startups completed an in-person bootcamp at Google’s Bengaluru campus. As part of the programme, Google will work with the selected startups to refine their products, optimise their technology architecture and prepare them for scaled deployment.
Later in September, the company also selected four Indian startups — Terrastack, Varaha Climate, Farmers for Forests and Climitra Carbon — for its debut AI focused accelerator ‘Google DeepMind Accelerator: AI for the Planet (APAC)’. The accelerator aims to address urgent environmental challenges using AI.
3one4 Capital
Early-stage venture capital firm 3one4 Capital backed 19 startups during Q3 2026, including Elixir Foods, Smalle and Unbox Robotics.
The early-stage focused VC also completely exited EV startup Yulu via a secondary transaction as part of its $93 Mn Series C round which was led by GEF Capital Partners
Since inception, 3one4 Capital has invested in more than 110 startups including Licious, DarwinBox, Open, Kuku FM, Jupiter, BetterPlace and Tracxn.
As of now, the firm is gearing up to launch its fifth fund, with a target corpus of $225 Mn, 3one4 Capital IFSC – Fund V. The corpus will primarily target startups operating in sectors like AI and SaaS, enterprise and manufacturing automation, fintech, deeptech and consumer internet.
Access Free Report
Rainmatter
Zerodha’s startup investment arm Rainmatter closed 16 deals in Q3 2026. Its notable investments during the quarter included Arboreal, Econovus, Minimac, Quanfluence and SolarSquare.
Rainmatter operates as a “perennial” fund using Zerodha’s own capital, allowing it to take a long-term approach to its investments. While it initially focused on fintech, the firm has expanded into areas such as climate tech, D2C and healthtech.
The Zerodha-backed investor is increasingly betting on engineering-heavy businesses developing indigenous IP, components and systems upstream of manufacturing. Since its inception in 2016, Rainmatter has built a portfolio of around 160 investments and manages assets worth more than ₹1,500 Cr.
Its portfolio includes smallcase, Ultrahuman, The Whole Truth Foods, GalaxEye and Lissun, among others.
IvyCap Ventures
The VC firm backed 15 startups in Q3 2026, including BatX Energies, Blitz, BotSync, Celcius Logistics and SwitchOn.
The firm currently manages more than $650 Mn in assets and has a portfolio of over 65 startups.
The investment mix reflects the VC’s focus on tech-led businesses solving problems across India’s physical and consumer economy, rather than a concentration in a single sector. Its portfolio spans deeptech, enterprise technology, healthtech, consumertech, fintech and emerging areas such as EVs and agritech.
InnoVen Capital
The venture debt firm backed 14 startups in Q3 2026, including the likes of BharatPe, Enerzolve, Infinite Uptime, NuPlayAI and QPi, among others.
The firm typically backs startups that have already raised equity and are looking to extend their runway or support growth and has backed more than 200 startups. Meanwhile, its portfolio across Asia includes more than 420 companies.
Across markets, the firm has invested more than $1.9 Bn through over 770 debt transactions and counts more than 50 unicorns among its portfolio companies. Its India portfolio includes Swiggy, OYO, Myntra, boAt and Cars24.
Antler
Global early-stage venture capital firm Antler backed 14 startups in Q3 2026, including Green Aero, Mandrake, Navana, ProLearn and Rovia.
Founded in Singapore in 2017, Antler is now present across more than 25 cities and has made over 2,000 investments globally.
The firm launched its India operations in 2020, starting with a programme in Bengaluru. In 2023, Antler India closed commitments of ₹500 Cr for its maiden pre-seed fund and was targeting a final close of ₹600 Cr.
Antler India typically invests at the idea-to-pre-seed stage, with initial cheques ranging between $200K and $400K. It has backed more than 115 startups through its India fund, including Armory, HouseEazy, Dodo Payments, Inspecity and Green Aero Propulsion.
AJVC
Early-stage venture capital firm A Junior VC (AJVC) backed 13 startups in Q3 2026, including Alchemic, Bejan, Dialflo and MoroMaa.
Founded by Aviral Bhatnagar, AJVC initially launched with a ₹100 Cr fund. The firm later raised ₹165 Cr for its maiden fund against an initial target of ₹100 Cr.
The firm is looking to back 80-90 startups through the fund and plans to invest in another 60-70 ventures by early 2028. Typically, AJVC invests about ₹1.5 Cr per startup for a 9% stake.
Finvolve
Finvolve participated in 13 investment deals in Q3 2026, backing early-stage startups such as Evigway, Kepler Aerospace and Rezlytix.
Incorporated in 2022, the firm focuses on startups across sectors such as dronetech, spacetech, clean energy, mobility, circular economy and social impact, as well as businesses leveraging ONDC.
To date, Finvolve has made more than 40 investments across deeptech, spacetech, clean energy and fintech. Its portfolio includes Droom, Matter, IG Defence, Recur Club and Sunfox.

A 1-Trillion-Parameter Model
MiMo-V2.6-Pro uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 1 trillion total parameters and 42 billion active parameters during inference.
It supports a 1-million-token context window and up to 128,000 output tokens.
The model is released under the MIT license, allowing commercial use and modification.
Built for Agents and Long Tasks
Xiaomi positions MiMo 2.6 Pro for complex projects, long-running tasks, research, cybersecurity, and agentic workflows.
The model supports tool calling, web search, structured output, streaming, and context caching.
Xiaomi has also used large-scale reinforcement learning to improve software engineering performance. During recent training, MiMo 2.6 Pro reportedly improved from 58.4 to 72.6 on DeepSWE v1.1.
The training involved around 750,000 trajectories across MiMo 2.6 Flash and Pro, with Xiaomi saying the Pro model’s portion cost roughly $2.62 million.
