items.author: Muhammad Bilal
items.content:
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal has said teachers are the builders of a nation’s future and must prepare students not only with knowledge but also with character, discipline, critical thinking and confidence.
Speaking at a Teachers’ Day event in Narowal, Iqbal said every achievement in Pakistan had the contribution of a teacher behind it. He paid tribute to teachers across the country, particularly those educating and training students despite limited resources.
Iqbal said peace, education and development were closely connected, with peace giving children the opportunity to learn, education creating opportunities for young people and development providing families with hope for a better future.
He said schools, colleges and universities were the foundation of Pakistan’s future, but teachers were what made educational institutions truly great. He added that the education system must adapt to rapid changes brought by artificial intelligence, automation and climate change.
The minister urged teachers to develop students’ ability to ask questions, conduct research, assess evidence and solve problems. He called for classrooms where curiosity is encouraged, effort is valued and mistakes are treated as opportunities to learn.
Iqbal also said teachers must continue learning throughout their careers and remain familiar with new teaching methods, technology and discoveries. He stressed the need for responsible use of artificial intelligence, saying students should be taught to verify information, think critically and take responsibility for their decisions.
He said education should aim not only to produce skilled workers but also responsible citizens. Honesty, empathy, a sense of duty, respect for others and awareness of civic responsibilities should be an essential part of educating the next generation.
Iqbal urged teachers to give every child a fair opportunity to progress, particularly students facing poverty, family difficulties or a lack of confidence. He said a child’s current circumstances should not be treated as the limit of their potential.
He also stressed the importance of giving girls confidence to pursue their ambitions and ensuring children from low-income families understand that they have an equal right to opportunities.
The minister said education should be connected with practical life so students can observe problems around them, conduct research and develop solutions. He said the goals under the Uraan Pakistan initiative, including exports, technology, environmental protection, infrastructure and equitable development, could only be achieved by developing human capabilities.
Iqbal called for better teaching materials, facilities, practical training and professional support for teachers. He also said curricula, teacher training and examination systems must be aligned, warning that asking teachers to develop creativity while examinations reward memorization sends a contradictory message.
He said the real objective of education reforms should be to have an effective impact at the classroom and student level. Teachers, he added, should identify and encourage the potential of every student, as a few words of encouragement from a teacher can change a child’s life.
Iqbal said students might forget a particular lesson taught by a teacher, but they would remember a teacher who listened to them, treated them fairly and taught them to believe in themselves.
He said every classroom in Narowal should be a place where talent is discovered, character is strengthened and hope is renewed. He expressed hope that a generation trained by teachers would help build a Pakistan that is confident in its identity, capable in its work, compassionate toward its people and respected around the world.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Walmart-owned Flipkart picked up a minority stake in Delhi-based B2B travel tech startup TravClan to bolster its international travel offerings, expand holiday packages offered by subsidiaries Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel as well as enhancing on-ground support across.
The ecommerce giant also aims to leverage the partnership to expand its own curated international leisure offerings by tapping into TravClan’s technology and partner network.
On the other side of the table, the fresh capital infusion will support TravClan’s team expansion in business development, engineering, and destination operations, as well as allow for further investments in global supply, technology, and destination expansion.
“Travellers today are looking for more than a flight or hotel booking. They want a holiday that is curated around their interests and supported throughout the journey. TravClan’s supplier network and destination capabilities will help us build that experience across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel,” said Nishant Verman, Flipkart’s SVP, Corporate Development and Partnerships.
Founded by Arun Bagaria, Chirag Agrawal, and Ashish Thapliyal in 2018, TravClan assists travel agents to build and grow online businesses. It works with over 15,000 travel agents to customise and book real-time packages, hotels, and activities.
The startup’s cap table also includes angel investors like Cars24 cofounders Vikram Chopra and Mehul Agrawal and Trip.com’s Travis Katz, as well as institutional investors like Leo Capital.
Flipkart’s Diversification Push
For Flipkart, the travel tech investment adds on to its push to build out its other business verticals beyond its flagship ecommerce platform.
While the company has been eyeing new entries in the food delivery and the event ticketing industry, it has been aggressively doubling down on its quick commerce arm, Flipkart Minutes.
Ahead of its annual Big Billion Days, the ecommerce giant announced that it has expanded its dark store network to nearly 1,200 Flipkart Minutes microfulfillment centres across 150-plus cities. The company is now expected to add another 1,000 dark stores by mid-2027 or the Big Billion Days sale of 2027.
In recent years, it has also expanded its in-house Flipkart Travel beyond flight booking services into bus bookings and hotel bookings. Cleartrip, an online travel aggregator which Flipkart acquired in 2021, also later expanded into corporate travel.
Besides, Flipkart made some additional investments in AI startups last week. Its investment arm Flipkart Ventures backed Alive, an AI-powered platform for live consumer experiences, and Keploy, a native-AI software testing platform.
To date, Flipkart has made over 20 startup investments via Flipkart Ventures across AI, consumer internet, fintech, e-commerce adjacencies and logistics tech.
It claims to support portfolio ventures with strategic mentorship, operational expertise and access to its ecosystem in order to help them scale, besides the capital they get.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Monday increased the price of petrol by 88 paisas per litre, while decreasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.88 per litre for October 6.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs393.64 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs397.76 per litre for Tuesday.
The latest revision comes after the government increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.1 and 30 paisas per litre, respectively, from October 3 to October 5.
Read: Govt increases petrol by Rs2.1, diesel by 30 paisas till Oct 5
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices edged lower on Monday after crude exports from the ​Middle East increased and the Group of Seven nations pledged to boost supplies, though selling was limited by ‌ongoing disruption fears linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Brent crude futures were down $1.10, or 1.08%, at $101.15 a barrel by 11:59 am ET (1559 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 89 cents, or 0.98%, at $90.22.
"A truce in the Middle East remains elusive, and ‌renewed hostilities ⁠between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis will ensure that attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels will continue, keeping the geopolitical risk premium at an elevated level," said PVM Oil Associates analyst Tamas Varga.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
A teenager's hand was blown off as high-school protesters clashed with riot police in northern France on Monday, a ​local official said, on the eve of a national demonstration by the pupils' union against underfunding, overcrowding and dilapidation.
The regional newspaper La Voix du Nord said the 15-year-old ‌lost his hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police dispersal grenade that detonated in the town of Lens as the wave of school protests entered its third week.
François-Xavier Lauch, prefect of Pas-de-Calais, declined to comment on the exact circumstances, saying some 200 to 250 protesters had been hurling objects at police.
Six months before an election to replace President Emmanuel Macron, his government and the far-right National Rally, led by presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, ​have accused hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) lawmakers and mayors of stoking the protests. The LFI denies the accusation.
Speaking after meeting with students in the northern Paris suburbs, Education Minister Edouard Geffray ​said participation in the protests had been declining in recent days.
The government would launch a platform for students to express their dissatisfaction and kick off ⁠an action plan for particular schools, he said.
French police accused of excessive force against pupils
Rights groups accuse police of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including batons, tear gas and flash-ball guns.
Among several investigations into ​police methods, authorities are examining the case of a 16-year-old who suffered an eye injury after police fired rubber bullets into a crowd of protesters, according to his friends. The Interior Ministry did not ​immediately respond to a request for comment on the allegation of using excessive force.
The LFI, headed by presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, denies encouraging violence and accuses the government of politicising the issue and neglecting pupils' interests.
France's Justice Ministry said 5,060 people have been arrested since the protests began, with 87% of them minors. More than 1,800 people are being prosecuted, including 1,483 minors, the ministry said, without specifying the crimes. It said 790 cases had been dismissed.
The protests ​have put more pressure on a government trying to narrow a budget deficit as investor concerns about state finances grow, briefly pushing the yield on France's 10-year bonds to a 24-year high over 5% ​last week and raising the likely cost of future borrowing.
The protests began in September in Paris, focusing on poor suburbs, before spreading nationwide. The government says they have been hijacked and morphed into urban violence.
"Our priority is to restore ‌order," government ⁠spokesperson Maud Bregeon told CNews television.
Some 400 to 500 high schools were closed or partially closed ahead of Tuesday's nationwide protest.
Read More: Student protests spread across France, Belgium
wo dozen schools have been burned or ransacked, 78 teaching staff have been injured in the demonstrations and at least 190 students have been injured, Geffray said. He said the goal was for classes at affected schools to restart on Wednesday.
"We’re going to keep blocking until the government hears us," said Sami Karen, 18, who was demonstrating outside Charles de Foucauld high school in Paris. "As long as they don’t listen to us, we won’t stop this fight."
Students and police clash in Lille, Toulouse and Paris
On ​Monday, BFMTV showed images of police and students ​clashing in Lille in northern France, tear ⁠gas being used in Toulouse in the southwest, and a fire being lit as people tried to break into a school in central Paris.
Carole Zerbib, head of the vandalised Lycee Vauquelin in Paris, said it had been attacked by a "very determined" group wearing hoods and masks who had tried to break through ​the entrance door and then lit a fire, forcing the school to be evacuated and classes suspended.
"It was very violent and happened very quickly," ​she said, adding that ⁠she did not believe the attackers were from the school.
Since last Monday, 5,000 people, 85% of them teenagers, have been arrested and dozens injured. Teachers and members of the public have been attacked, while damage to property is estimated in the millions of euros.
Bregeon said the government would fast-track a bill on October 27 to make youngsters found to have damaged property, or their parents, financially liable.
Security officials fear that Tuesday's organised protests ⁠in central ​Paris in particular could bring further violence amid concerns that far-left and anarchist groups could try to take them over.
Sophie Binet, ​head of the CGT labour union, told TF1 television on Monday that her members would attend Tuesday's demonstrations to protect the students.
"We've been appalled by what we have seen over the past 10 days and by the unprecedented crackdown that the ​government has organised," she said.

items.title: ICC provides more details on arrest warrants for two Taliban leaders
items.summary:
The International Criminal Court provided more details on Monday on arrest warrants issued last year for two Taliban leaders, Haibatullah Akhundzada, the group's supreme spiritual leader, and Abdul Hakim Haqqani, who has been chief justice since 2021.
The ICC had already announced the existence of the warrants in July 2025, saying the men were accused of committing the crime against humanity of persecution on gender grounds against girls, women and other people who did not conform with the Taliban's policy on gender, gender identity or expression.

— Int'l Criminal Court (@IntlCrimCourt) October 5, 2026
The precise contents of the warrants had remained sealed. Now the court has given more information about the findings of the judges who issued the warrants.

items.content:
The International Criminal Court provided more details on Monday on arrest warrants issued last year for two Taliban leaders, Haibatullah Akhundzada, the group's supreme spiritual leader, and Abdul Hakim Haqqani, who has been chief justice since 2021.
The ICC had already announced the existence of the warrants in July 2025, saying the men were accused of committing the crime against humanity of persecution on gender grounds against girls, women and other people who did not conform with the Taliban's policy on gender, gender identity or expression.
#ICC Pre-Trial Chamber II unseals four warrants of arrest issued in the #Afghanistan situation against Mr Haibatullah Akhundzada, Mr Abdul Hakim Haqqani, Mr Habibullah Agha and Mr Neda Mohammad Nadim⤵️ https://t.co/LKmot06bf6
— Int'l Criminal Court (@IntlCrimCourt) October 5, 2026
The precise contents of the warrants had remained sealed. Now the court has given more information about the findings of the judges who issued the warrants.
They found the suspects "implemented a governmental policy that resulted in severe violations of fundamental rights and freedoms of the civilian population of Afghanistan, in connection with conducts of murder, imprisonment, torture, rape and enforced disappearance".
Also Read: Pakistan hits Afghan terror hideouts; 22 killed
While the Taliban have imposed strict rules and prohibitions on the entire Afghan population, they have specifically targeted women and girls by denying them the right to education, freedom of expression and freedom of movement, the judges found.
According to UN figures, half of Afghan women now leave their homes only once or twice a month as Taliban-imposed restrictions curtail their freedom of movement and participation in public life. Afghanistan remains the only country in the world to ban girls from secondary education and women from attending university, said UN Women, which promotes gender equality.
Afghanistan rejects ICC arrest warrants for Taliban ministers
The Taliban government on Monday condemned the International Criminal Court for issuing arrest warrants for two Afghan education ministers, adding it "does not recognise" the court and the ministers did nothing that merits punishment.
"We are bound by the rulings of Islamic Sharia and its courts, not by intelligence entities or so-called courts," Taliban government chief spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said in a statement. "Afghanistan calls on such entities not to make claims beyond their authority and jurisdiction."

The Apex PB400, PB400 Pro and PB445 each pack 20,000mAh batteries, while the PB332 MagnaCharge has a 10,000mAh battery. The flagship PB445 supports 45W two-way charging, while the PB332 MagnaCharge offers 15W magnetic wireless charging and a built-in stand. Prices for the new models range from Rs. 1,999 to Rs. 2,899 in India.

Original | October 5, 2026 10:00 IST
Snapdeal parent AceVector made a weak stock market debut, listing at ₹28.30 on the BSE, an 11.6% discount to its issue price of ₹32 per share.
On the NSE, the stock debuted at ₹28.32, an 11.5% discount to the IPO price.
At its BSE listing price, AceVector commanded a market capitalisation of ₹1,540.1 Cr (about $161 Mn), down from its IPO valuation of ₹1,741.4 Cr (about $181.7 Mn).
AceVector had set the IPO price band at ₹30-₹32 per share. The company’s ₹420 Cr IPO comprised a fresh issue of shares worth ₹287 Cr and an OFS of up to 4.16 Cr shares, worth ₹133 Cr at the issue price.
The IPO closed with an oversubscription of 4.93X. The issue received bids for 36.61 Cr shares against 7.42 Cr shares on offer.
The OFS delivered sharply different outcomes for selling shareholders. SoftBank’s Starfish I Pte Ltd received ₹88.3 Cr from the sale of 2.76 Cr shares, but recovered just 0.08X its acquisition cost on those shares. Individual investor Kenneth Stuart Glass, meanwhile, booked a 5.4X return multiple on his ₹4.2 Cr share sale.
Ahead of the IPO, AceVector raised ₹189 Cr from anchor investors. The only two mutual funds which participated were Helios Mutual Fund and Taurus Ethical Fund.
AceVector has earmarked ₹132 Cr from the fresh issue proceeds for Snapdeal’s marketing and business promotion, and ₹50 Cr for technology infrastructure. The remaining proceeds will fund acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2010 by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, the business began as Snapdeal and adopted the AceVector identity in 2022. Besides the marketplace, the group’s businesses include listed ecommerce SaaS company Unicommerce and consumer brands business Stellaro Brands.
Snapdeal now focuses on value ecommerce, with fashion contributing more than 60% of its business. Around 84% of its customers come from non-metro geographies. Ahead of the IPO, Bahl told Inc42 that the marketplace would prioritise volume growth, expansion within its existing categories, and better merchandising.
However, Snapdeal faces a wide gap in scale with rival Meesho, which clocked net merchandise value of ₹41,560 Cr in FY26, about 38 times Snapdeal’s ₹1,093.1 Cr.
On the financial front, AceVector’s restated net loss narrowed nearly 64% to ₹45.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹126.3 Cr in FY25. Operating revenue rose 29.2% to ₹510.3 Cr from ₹395 Cr.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
IPO-bound Razorpay announced today that it has deepened its partnership with AI major OpenAI to help Indian brands advertise on ChatGPT.
Under the partnership, the company’s growth marketing platform, Razorpay Engage, will enable brands to prepare product catalogues, launch and manage campaigns on ChatGPT Ads.
Brands onboarded by Razorpay include Tanishq, Fastrack, Traya, Tata Neu, Rivaah by Tanishq, Shaadi.com, Axis Max Life, Palmonas and Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies (NMIMS).
Razorpay Engage To Become ChatGPT Ads Layer
Razorpay Engage will provide the technology and operational infrastructure for businesses looking to get started with ChatGPT Ads.
Its offering will include assessing catalogue readiness, improving and structuring product feeds, creating and managing campaigns, and measuring and optimising campaign performance.
The platform will also use an AI agent built around ChatGPT Ads best practices to help create and manage campaigns across different contexts where consumers may encounter a brand’s products.
The agent will monitor campaign performance and make ongoing adjustments, while Razorpay’s team will provide human oversight where required.
“The way people discover products is changing. The next customer may not search for a product or scroll through an ad; they may simply ask an AI assistant for help deciding what to buy. For businesses, we believe that opens up an entirely new moment to be discovered,” Razorpay COO Rahul Kothari said.
The Broader Context Behind OpenAI-Razorpay Partnership
The partnership comes as consumer discovery of brands is shifting from traditional keyword-based searches on engines to conversational interactions with AI chatbots. An early trend of users describing what they are looking for to an AI bot, comparing options and refine their choices via subsequent conversations is emerging at the moment.
As this trend gains more footing, ChatGPT started rolling out ads on ChatGPT in India, with the initial rollout covering logged-in adults on the Free and Go plans at the end of August. Ad agencies WPP and Omnicom are OpenAI’s first agency partners in India.
For brands, this creates a new channel where products need to be structured and represented with sufficient information and context to surface across different consumer queries. Razorpay said managing this process manually at scale can be challenging.
The advertising push builds on Razorpay’s earlier efforts to turn ChatGPT into a commerce channel. The fintech company has been working with OpenAI and NPCI on infrastructure that allows merchants to create ChatGPT-native storefronts, sync product catalogues and eventually complete purchases within the chat interface. In August, Razorpay said it was working with around 50 brands and several ecommerce marketplaces on agentic-commerce pilots.
The company has also earlier said that its technology can reduce the time required for a Shopify merchant to set up a ChatGPT storefront from around eight to 10 weeks to roughly 30 minutes by automating catalogue syncing and the submission process.
The broader proposition is that merchants need more than visibility on AI platforms: they also need structured catalogues, storefronts and payment infrastructure that can work inside conversational interfaces. Razorpay has been building these layers as it seeks to establish itself as an infrastructure provider for AI-led commerce.
This also marks a continuation of Razorpay’s partnership with OpenAI and NPCI around agentic payments. The company has been experimenting with UPI Circle and UPI Reserve Pay to enable purchases within ChatGPT, while keeping payment credentials away from the AI model and requiring user consent for transactions.
Razorpay’s push comes as other payment companies, including Cashfree and Pine Labs, are also building infrastructure for agentic commerce, suggesting that payment providers see the AI interface as a potential new layer between consumers and merchants rather than simply another checkout channel.
The partnership also marks another step in Razorpay’s expansion beyond its core payments business.
Razorpay was founded in 2014 by IIT Roorkee alumni Shashank Kumar and Harshil Mathur and has expanded from payments into a broader suite of business and banking solutions.
Razorpay launched Engage in 2023 as a full-stack growth marketing platform, offering businesses customer acquisition, retention and engagement tools. The platform provides personalised incentives, gift cards and targeted rewards across an inventory of more than 5,000 options.
Its AI push, meanwhile, extends beyond commerce and advertising. In August, Razorpay launched Vulcan, a proprietary AI foundation model designed to improve payment success, fraud detection and transaction routing, underlining the company’s broader attempt to build AI into its payments infrastructure.
Razorpay has also been developing Agent Studio, its platform for deploying task-specific AI agents for businesses. Around 200 businesses were using the platform in beta as of August, with use cases including reconciliation, abandoned-cart recovery, subscription recovery and finance operations.
The company has previously described this as a broader “distribution layer” across different agentic touchpoints, including merchant websites, independent agent platforms and large language model platforms, rather than a bet solely on ChatGPT.
The startup, which has raised over $800 M from investors like Tiger Global, Y Combinator, Lightspeed, is gearing up for a public markets debut soon.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Monday accused the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) of pursuing negotiations with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), saying the party’s policy had contributed to the security crisis in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
In a detailed statement on X, Asif said the issue between the presidency and the K-P government was “not politics but terrorism”, while questioning the provincial government’s handling of police capacity, counterterrorism infrastructure and security funds.
He said the PTI had exercised political control or influence in K-P for around 13 years and criticised its leadership for advocating negotiations with the TTP.
“Imran Khan has always had a soft corner for TTP, and the party's thinking has been more aligned with the idea of negotiations with terrorists rather than the state's policy of eliminating terrorism,” Asif said.
He claimed that after becoming prime minister, Imran had said he knew how to end terrorism in K-P and called for talks with terrorists.
ریاست اور خیبر پختونخوا کا مسئلہ سیاست نہیں بلکہ دہشت گردی ہے۔ کچھ حقائق دیکھنا ضروری ہے
- صوبے کا گزشتہ دو سال کا ڈیٹا: تقریباً 6,200 دہشت گردی کے واقعات، 1,200 شہادتیں اور افغان شہریوں کی جانب سے 37 خودکش حملے کیے گئے۔ صرف رواں سال 14 خودکش حملے ہو چکے ہیں، جن میں اکثریت…
— Khawaja M. Asif (@KhawajaMAsif) October 5, 2026
Asif also criticised the role of former Inter-Services Intelligence chief General Faiz Hameed, alleging that he had been used to advance the talks agenda.
Hameed was sentenced to 14 years in prison by a military court in December 2025 on charges including violation of state secrets and interfering in politics.
The defence minister blamed the PTI founder for using the state apparatus to pursue talks with the TTP and its allies.
“The full price of this policy has been paid by K-P and Pakistan, yet even today, the same party is talking about negotiations and engagement with TTP and Tehreek-e-Taliban Afghanistan (TTA).”
He reiterated the military’s stated policy towards terrorism, saying, “Terrorists will be eliminated.”
Asif said the state’s current policy was to eliminate terrorists rather than negotiate with them. He also questioned PTI criticism of military operations, asking whether the army was not fighting terrorism and who else was doing so.
“You say this is a war for dollars. Tell us, how many billions of dollars has America provided to Pakistan in the past few years for the war against terrorism and security?” he asked.
The minister also referred to reported drone attacks in Kohat and Peshawar, as well as attacks by the TTA on security posts. He questioned why the military should not use drones for defence when militants were using them.
K-P security crisis
Asif said official K-P data showed that the province had witnessed around 6,200 terrorism incidents and 1,200 deaths over the past two years, including 37 suicide attacks allegedly carried out by Afghan nationals. “Just this year, 14 suicide attacks have already occurred, the majority by Afghan nationals,” he added.
He questioned the deployment and capacity of the provincial police, saying the K-P police force had around 125,000 personnel, of whom about 13,000 were deployed on VIP security duties. He said around 17,000 posts remained vacant despite the province’s frontline role in counterterrorism.
Asif also criticised the functioning of the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in the merged districts, claiming that it had only 17 bulletproof vehicles and around 3,300 personnel, most of whom were contract employees. “Only 25 are permanent, while the rest are contract employees,” the defence minister said.
He also questioned PTI leaders’ engagement with the security situation, asking whether they had personally visited military checkpoints, met families of soldiers martyred in the fight against terrorism, reviewed the functioning of courts and police stations in the merged districts or regularly attended apex committee meetings on security.
Also Read: Govt has kept 'all doors of dialogue open' with opposition: parliamentary secretary
He pointed to more than 3,000 pending prosecution cases in K-P and questioned why, despite the large number of cases, no terrorist had been executed or punished in the province.
According to Asif, the state’s policy in areas affected by militancy was based on a “Hold, Build and Transfer” model — first securing an area, then rebuilding infrastructure and institutions, and finally handing control to the civilian administration. He demanded that the PTI leadership explain its policy for ending terrorism.
Asif also alleged that the provincial police had sought Rs42 billion for the reconstruction and fortification of police checkpoints but had received only Rs1.2 billion, or 2.8%, from the K-P government. “Papers claim that Rs42 billion were spent, while in reality, this amount was embezzled,” he stated.
Federal funds
Addressing PTI claims that K-P had been denied adequate financial resources by the federal government, Asif said the province had received around Rs8.5 trillion in federal assistance between July 2010 and 2025. “There is no shortage of funds, but corruption and weak governance diminish their impact,” the minister said.
According to figures cited by Asif, the amount included Rs5.867 trillion transferred under the Seventh National Finance Commission (NFC) Award between 2010 and 2025.
Read More: K-P received Rs34.88tr in federal funds over past five years
He said Rs705 billion had been provided under the 1% share of the divisible pool allocated for the war against terrorism. For the merged districts, Rs704 billion had been disbursed since 2019, he added.
The figures also included around Rs482.78 billion in direct transfers, including royalties and gas development surcharge; Rs481.43 billion spent under the Benazir Income Support Programme in K-P between 2016 and 2025; and Rs117.166 billion in assistance for internally displaced persons.
He added that the province had received Rs46.44 billion under the latest NFC payment issued on December 17, 2025.

K-P government rejects criticism
Provincial Finance Adviser Muzammil Aslam on Monday rejected the impression that the K-P government was neglecting security or failing to allocate adequate resources to the police and other institutions, saying the province had been prioritising spending on law and order since February 2024.
“The current government of K-P has been allocating resources on a priority basis to police, law and order, judiciary, and temporarily displaced persons (TDPs) since February 2024,” he said in a post shared by the K-P government on X.
Aslam said K-P was fighting the war against terrorism alongside the federal government and armed forces, while bearing a “major burden of expenses” related to containing the threat.
He acknowledged that terrorism remained a major issue for the province but highlighted K-P’s performance on conventional crime, saying its police had a better record than Punjab in cases involving robbery, kidnapping, mobile phone theft and vehicle theft.

خیبرپختونخوا کی موجودہ حکومت فروری 2024 سے پولیس، لاء اینڈ آرڈر، عدلیہ اور ٹی ڈی پیز پر ترجیحی بنیادوں پر وسائل خرچ کر رہی ہے۔ مزمل اسلم
خیبرپختونخوا پولیس کا جرائم ریکارڈ (ڈکیتی، اغواکاری، موبائل و… pic.twitter.com/VbdVBgc4bc
— Government of KP (@GovernmentKP) October 5, 2026
Aslam said the province had been spending beyond its available resources on police infrastructure in the merged districts, arguing that K-P itself was bearing a substantial share of the financial burden of counterterrorism.
The finance adviser said the police budget had increased from Rs121 billion in 2024-25 to Rs173.8 billion in the 2026-27 budget, representing a 43.6% increase.
He said the allocation for purchasing weapons for the police had also risen from Rs3.3 billion to Rs14.5 billion. “The total police budget in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa is 191 billion rupees, the highest budget rate in all of Pakistan,” he added.
Aslam also compared K-P’s spending with that of other provinces, saying the provincial government was allocating substantial resources to the police.
He disputed claims that K-P was not spending sufficiently on the judiciary, saying the province had allocated Rs6 billion for judicial development, compared with Rs5.2 billion in Punjab, Rs2 billion in Sindh and Rs900 million in Balochistan.
He said K-P had been waiting for a “fair share for the merged districts” under the NFC for the past eight years and had been meeting the related expenditure from its own resources.
Aslam said financial assistance for temporarily displaced persons remained a major point of disagreement between the federal and provincial governments.
He claimed that the federal government had stopped making payments for internally displaced persons (IDPs) in 2022 and said the Centre owed K-P Rs54 billion in outstanding TDP payments.
He said the province had received no payment against the outstanding amount and was instead bearing the full cost from its own resources.
The finance adviser said the federal government’s financial obligations towards K-P should be taken into account when assessing the province’s spending on security and other sectors.
Earlier in the day, PTI-backed K-P Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati also responded to concerns raised by the federal government over the security situation in the province, saying the assembly had already initiated a parliamentary process to address the issue.
He said the legislature had convened a “peace jirga” last year, during which all political parties adopted a joint declaration to constitute a “Special Committee on Security”.
“The Committee has already received detailed briefings, in the presence of the parliamentary leaders of all political parties, from the Inspector General of Police, Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), Additional Chief Secretary Home, Home Department, Chief Secretary, and other relevant provincial institutions,” he said.
Swati said federal leaders had also been informed about the parliamentary process.
“Letters were sent to the Hon'ble Prime Minister of Pakistan, the Chairman of the Senate, the Speaker of the National Assembly and the Federal Minister for Interior, informing them that the Assembly was moving towards comprehensive parliamentary recommendations on the security situation,” he said.
He added that only one major stakeholder’s briefing remained — that of the Peshawar Corps Commander. The speaker said he had spoken to the military leader, who had assured him of his participation in a meeting of the special committee, which had yet to take place.
“I am therefore going to summon another meeting of the Special Committee,” he said, adding that he hoped to bring all relevant authorities and institutions to the same table to present their positions on the “critical” matter.
In view of the concerns being expressed by the Federal Government regarding the prevailing law and order situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, it is important to first look at the comprehensive parliamentary process that the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly has already initiated.

— Babar Saleem Swati (@BabarSaleemSwat) October 5, 2026
Swati said the meeting would discuss all facts that had been heard, observed and emerged during the committee’s proceedings.
He urged relevant institutions to present their “perspectives, facts and responsibilities” at the upcoming meeting, saying this was necessary for the committee to formulate its recommendations.
“These recommendations will then be presented before the Assembly and, after approval, forwarded to both the Provincial and Federal Governments so that responsibilities, policy direction and practical measures are clearly defined.”
The speaker said the people of K-P wanted peace and that all stakeholders needed to play their part in achieving a sustainable solution. He also avoided assigning blame for the deteriorating security situation.
“Our objective is not to assign blame. Our objective is to bring the facts to the table, clearly identify the responsibilities of the relevant institutions, and work collectively towards implementing the National Action Plan and finding a path to lasting peace,” Swati said.
He said maintaining peace was a collective responsibility and assured that the provincial assembly would continue to support efforts to restore peace.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s National Cyber Emergency Response Team has identified a series of suspicious phishing domains impersonating major government and public-sector institutions, raising fresh concerns over the theft of citizens’ personal and sensitive information.
According to the National CERT Threat Intelligence Centre, several suspicious domains linked to well-known national institutions were found active on October 4, including websites designed to resemble official login portals and public-service platforms.
The affected names reportedly include the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA), Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), Higher Education Commission (HEC), Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) and the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP).
Suspicious domains were also identified using the names of the Benazir Income Support Programme, Prime Minister’s Youth Programme, and Punjab Safe Cities, according to the threat intelligence findings.
One of the domains was reportedly designed to resemble a secure NADRA login page, a tactic commonly used in phishing campaigns to persuade users to enter personal information, passwords, identification details, or other sensitive data.
National CERT warned that the suspicious phishing domains remain active, increasing the risk that unsuspecting users could mistake them for genuine government websites.
Such impersonation campaigns typically rely on familiar institutional names and convincing login pages to gain users’ trust before attempting to collect credentials or other confidential information.
The cybersecurity authority said it is continuing to monitor phishing activity and threats involving the impersonation of national institutions.
Citizens and government organizations have been advised to exercise caution when opening links received through email, messaging platforms, or social media, particularly when the links direct users to login pages or request sensitive information.
Users should verify website addresses carefully before entering credentials and avoid interacting with suspicious or unfamiliar domains claiming to represent government agencies.
The latest findings underline the growing challenge posed by phishing campaigns that exploit the credibility of public institutions to target citizens and potentially compromise personal or organizational data.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
After three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza that has killed tens of thousands, Tel Aviv's relations with its traditional Asian allies have increasingly fractured, deepening its diplomatic isolation.
A recent illustration of that isolation came at the UN General Assembly late last month, where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cut a lonely figure as scores of delegates walked out of his speech.
The departing delegates included representatives from Asian nations such as Pakistan, Malaysia, Indonesia and Bangladesh.
Here is a look at how Asian countries have responded to Israel and the Gaza war.
East Asia
Israel has faced strong state-level criticism from its longtime East Asian allies, such as Japan and South Korea.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi opposed US sanctions against International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane, who sought an arrest warrant for Netanyahu over alleged war crimes in Gaza.
Takaichi reaffirmed Tokyo’s consistent support for the ICC during the UN General Assembly, pushing back against pressure from the US, and saying that the country takes the US sanctions against Akane “very seriously.”
Washington sanctioned Akane, the first Japanese national to head the ICC, in August, accusing the court of encroaching on state sovereignty.
Read More: Gaza residents face another winter amid shelter shortages, dwindling aid
With Seoul, tensions began in April after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung shared a video on social media alleging that Israeli soldiers abused a Palestinian child and then threw him off a rooftop.
Lee said it was necessary to determine the authenticity of the video and assess what actions were taken, stressing the seriousness of the allegations.
“Wartime homicide is no different from matters that we take issue with, such as the forced (enslavement of) comfort women, and the massacre of Jewish people,” he said.
The issue of “comfort women” refers to the sexual enslavement of thousands of women and girls, many of them Korean, by the Imperial Japanese Army during World War II.
Israel strongly criticised Lee for posting the video, calling it “unacceptable.”
Israel’s Foreign Ministry claimed that Lee relied on a “fake account” and had revived an incident from 2024 that had already been investigated.
The ministry accused Lee of trivializing the massacre of Jews on the eve of Holocaust Remembrance Day in Israel.
China, which has long supported a two-state solution, continued to reiterate its call.
President Xi Jinping said the two-state solution is the “right direction” for resolving the longstanding Palestine issue.
South and Southeast Asia
Sri Lanka, one of the first countries to recognise the State of Palestine, called at the UN General Assembly for the “early” recovery and reconstruction of Gaza, reiterating its support for Palestinians’ “inalienable” rights and a two-state solution.
“Recovery and reconstruction of Gaza must be an early priority,” Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said in his address.
He added that Colombo supports resolving the Palestine issue in line with the 1967 borders.
Pakistan, a member of the Gaza Peace Board, also reiterated its “unwavering” support for the Palestinian people and the establishment of an independent State of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
Addressing the UN General Assembly, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said that Palestine must also be granted full membership in the UN.
India, for its part, continued to pursue its strategy of maintaining diplomatic and strategic ties with Israel while continuing to express traditional support for a two-state solution and Palestinian statehood.
India under Prime Minister Narendra Modi has significantly deepened its strategic relationship with Israel, including through Modi’s February meeting with Netanyahu, when the two countries elevated their ties to a “Special Strategic Partnership.”
According to Jatin Desai, a Mumbai-based political analyst, India has historically stood with the Palestinian people. He said India’s position was clear even before the establishment of Israel.
Thailand, which has maintained long-standing ties with Israel, continues to cooperate closely with Israel, particularly in agriculture and education.
Every year, around 100,000 Israeli tourists travel to Thailand, and thousands of Thai workers, both skilled and unskilled, are employed in Israel. The country is also a popular destination for Thai students pursuing academic studies.
Bangkok established diplomatic relations with Israel in 1954, while it officially recognized Palestine in 2012.
Pacific nations
In January, US President Donald Trump, as chair of the Board of Peace for Gaza, invited Australia, Vietnam and Thailand to join the international body.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Canberra would consider the offer, though no decision had so far been taken.
“We’ve received correspondence from the president that arrived, I think, last night. That’s something we haven’t had time to consider. We’ll consider all of these approaches respectfully and through our proper processes,” Albanese said after receiving the invitation.
Thailand said it was reviewing the details of the offer.
Vietnam’s Communist Party General Secretary To Lam accepted Trump’s invitation to join the Gaza Peace Council and “affirmed Vietnam’s readiness to participate as a founding member state of the council.”
Read More: Over 800 Palestinian teachers killed by Israel since Gaza war: education ministry
New Zealand, which did not join neighboring Australia and other European nations to recognise the State of Palestine last year, said recognition of Palestinian statehood is “inevitable.”
In his final speech as foreign minister in the incumbent government earlier this month, Winston Peters said his decision in 2025 not to join most other UN member states in recognising Palestine was an example of truly independent foreign policy.
But he said that recognition was a question of when, not if.
The Pacific, a cluster of small island nations, has provided Israel with a bloc of supportive voices in international forums, even as global criticism intensifies and more countries move to recognise Palestine.
Fiji further strengthened ties with Israel in September 2025 by opening a new embassy in Jerusalem. Days earlier, it abstained in a UN vote on a two-state solution. Like many of its neighbors, Fiji does not recognise Palestine.
Papua New Guinea followed a similar path. In September 2023, it also opened an embassy in Jerusalem and has since repeatedly opposed calls for a ceasefire at the UN. The country continues to reject recognition of Palestinian statehood.
Nauru has long been a loyal supporter of Israel. It recognised Jerusalem as Israel’s capital in 2019 and, in September last year, voted against a resolution backing a two-state solution.
Palau and Micronesia have consistently voted in line with Israel at the UN.
Samoa signed a visa-waiver deal in 2019 but took a slightly different line in September last year, when it abstained in the two-state resolution. Still, like most of its neighbors, it has not recognised Palestine.
Other Pacific nations such as Vanuatu, the Marshall Islands, Kiribati, the Solomon Islands, Tuvalu and Tonga maintain diplomatic relations with Israel, regularly support it at UN forums and do not recognise Palestine.
Tonga and Israel signed a visa-waiver agreement in 2010, while Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands have consistently backed Israel in UN votes.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Transactions routed through Easypaisa and linked to several merchant and payment intermediary firms have reportedly faced delays and disruptions, raising concerns across Pakistan’s digital payments sector.
According to industry sources, the impact has been most visible in payments associated with SWICH, Simpaisa, ajarPay, RapidPay, Zero Technologies and Finza Tech, where some merchant transactions have experienced processing delays and settlement issues.
However, available information suggests that the situation does not amount to a nationwide Easypaisa outage. There are no indications that all wallet services, person-to-person transfers, or routine consumer transactions have been suspended across the country.
International payment processor dLocal has also flagged processing issues involving Easypaisa in Pakistan and said the matter is being investigated.
The disruption has emerged at a time when law enforcement agencies are increasing scrutiny of digital payment channels that may potentially be used for online gaming, gambling, suspicious financial activity, unauthorized fund transfers, and other illicit transactions.
Recent investigations by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) have examined cases involving the alleged use of bank accounts, mobile wallets, and cryptocurrency-related channels for illegal online gaming and gambling platforms. Investigators have also looked into the movement of funds through multiple accounts, possible transaction layering, digital hawala and hundi systems, and the use of crypto assets including USDT.
Separately, the State Bank of Pakistan introduced a new regulatory framework in May 2026 for payment intermediaries and aggregators involved in certain payment and remittance arrangements. The framework tightened requirements related to documentation, compliance with foreign exchange rules, settlement procedures, and monitoring of financial flows.
Industry sources say the immediate concern is the delay in settlement of legitimate merchant transactions, leaving some businesses and customers uncertain over when pending payments and affected funds will be cleared.
The development also highlights a broader challenge for Pakistan’s fast-growing fintech and digital commerce ecosystem: how regulators and enforcement agencies can strengthen oversight without disrupting legitimate business activity.
Easypaisa was approached multiple times for comment on the matter. A company representative said the organization did not wish to comment at this stage.

items.summary:

Monogatari Corp., operator of the Yakiniku King barbecue restaurant chain, said information belonging to more than 10 million customers was leaked after unauthorised access to its reservation and rewards app, according to Kyodo News.
The compromised information included customers’ names, email addresses, phone numbers and membership numbers.
The breach was detected Friday, the company said, adding that it had found no evidence so far that the leaked information had been misused.
Separately, Daiwa Securities Group said data belonging to around 110,000 customers of its brokerage unit may have been compromised following unauthorised access to a contractor-operated server, Kyodo reported.

Monogatari Corp., operator of the Yakiniku King barbecue restaurant chain, said information belonging to more than 10 million customers was leaked after unauthorised access to its reservation and rewards app, according to Kyodo News.
The compromised information included customers’ names, email addresses, phone numbers and membership numbers.
The breach was detected Friday, the company said, adding that it had found no evidence so far that the leaked information had been misused.
Separately, Daiwa Securities Group said data belonging to around 110,000 customers of its brokerage unit may have been compromised following unauthorised access to a contractor-operated server, Kyodo reported.
Read More: OpenAI safety employee quits, says ‘time for trial and error is over’
The intrusion occurred between Friday evening and Saturday morning on a server operated by Scala Communications Inc., which provides Daiwa Securities with an online customer inquiry management service.
Potentially exposed information includes names, email addresses and account numbers.
Including inquiries that contained no personal information, around 220,000 pieces of data may have been affected.
Daiwa said the compromised information could not be used to conduct transactions, including online trades.
The brokerage has also found no evidence so far that the potentially compromised information has been published or circulated online.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Japanese automaker Honda Motor said on Monday it ​has developed technology that ‌can wirelessly charge electric vehicles, including large trucks, while being driven, ​and plans to test the ​technology on a Japanese highway.
Honda ⁠plans to test the ​technology along with construction firm Taisei ​and road builder Taisei Rotec in the financial year beginning in April ​2027 or later, it ​said in a statement
The system, developed by ‌Honda's ⁠research arm with the two firms, aims to transfer electricity wirelessly from charging units embedded ​in ​roads to ⁠vehicles in motion, which could lead to fewer ​charging stops.
According to technology.com, the technology is being developed by Honda Research and Development and Taisei Rotec. The system is based on magnetic coupling technology designed to transmit power to moving EVs, mainly logistics trucks.
Honda may launch its first trials in late 2026, with public demonstrations planned for April 2027. The website said the system has three components: a DC power supply, a power transmitter embedded in the pavement, and a receiver under the vehicle.
A Honda engineer declined to comment on the cost compared with a conventional high-speed charging network, saying its economic viability would need to be assessed.

items.content:
Indonesia Comic Con 2026 tidak hanya menjadi ruang bagi budaya pop dan komunitas, tetapi juga dimanfaatkan UniPin untuk memperkenalkan karya studio game lokal kepada audiens yang lebih luas. Lewat UniPin Gaming Pavilion, pengunjung bisa mencoba langsung empat game buatan studio Indonesia sekaligus mengikuti berbagai aktivitas komunitas.
UniPin Gaming Pavilion hadir di Indonesia Comic Con (ICC) 2026 yang berlangsung pada 3–4 Oktober 2026 di JIEXPO Kemayoran, Jakarta. Pavilion tersebut digelar bersama RedBull, Rabit, HyperX, dan JBL Quantum, dengan dukungan Tokopedia serta H3RO by Tri.
Di ajang tersebut, UniPin tidak hanya menempatkan game lokal sebagai materi showcase. Empat game yang dibawa ke acara tersebut dapat dimainkan langsung oleh pengunjung, sehingga studio pengembang mendapatkan ruang untuk memperkenalkan karyanya sekaligus berinteraksi dengan calon pemain.
Empat Game Lokal di UniPin Gaming Pavilion
Empat gim yang tampil di UniPin Gaming Pavilion berasal dari empat studio berbeda, yakni Lentera Nusantara, Khuga Labs, Team Fossil, dan Yellow Hearts. Judul yang diperkenalkan masing-masing adalah 101 Forgotten dari Lentera Nusantara, Khuga Bash dari Khuga Labs, Asbak dari Team Fossil, dan Type Caster dari Yellow Hearts. Seluruh gim tersebut dapat dicoba langsung selama penyelenggaraan Indonesia Comic Con 2026.
Format seperti ini membuat kehadiran gim lokal di event tidak berhenti pada materi promosi. Pengunjung bisa langsung berinteraksi dengan game yang ditampilkan, sementara studio memperoleh kesempatan untuk memperkenalkan produknya kepada audiens yang memang datang ke event dengan ketertarikan terhadap gaming dan budaya pop.
UniPin mengaitkan kehadiran empat gim tersebut dengan kampanye “Bangga Main Lokal”, yang bertujuan mendorong masyarakat untuk mengenal, mencoba, dan mengapresiasi karya gim Indonesia.
Poeti Fatima, General Manager Business UniPin Global, mengatakan Indonesia memiliki talenta dan karya gim yang semakin beragam. Menurutnya, Indonesia Comic Con menjadi salah satu ruang bagi studio lokal untuk memperkenalkan karya sekaligus mendekatkannya kepada masyarakat. “Melalui Indonesia Comic Con 2026, UniPin ingin memberikan ruang bagi studio gim lokal untuk memperkenalkan karya mereka sekaligus mendekatkannya kepada masyarakat,” ujar Poeti Fatima.
Selain mencoba game lokal, pengunjung UniPin Gaming Pavilion juga dapat mengikuti Stamp Rally Card yang berisi sejumlah aktivitas interaktif. UniPin menyediakan berbagai hadiah dalam aktivitas tersebut, mulai dari kursi gaming dan Trading Card Game (TCG) hingga UniPin Credits yang dapat digunakan untuk membeli produk digital di platform UniPin.
Pendekatan ini membuat Pavilion berfungsi lebih sebagai area aktivitas gaming daripada sekadar tempat memajang produk. Pengunjung memiliki beberapa alasan untuk berinteraksi dengan area tersebut, baik melalui game showcase maupun aktivitas pendukung yang disiapkan UniPin.
Dukung Aktivitas Komunitas GameHers
Dukungan UniPin di Indonesia Comic Con 2026 tidak berhenti pada showcase gim. Perusahaan juga mendukung aktivitas komunitas melalui GameHers, yang menggelar talkshow bertajuk “Beyond the Screen: Gaming, Creativity & Finding Yourself”. Talkshow tersebut menjadi bagian dari rangkaian menuju acara puncak GameHers yang dijadwalkan berlangsung pada 5 Desember 2026.
Kehadiran GameHers menambah dimensi lain pada aktivitas UniPin di ICC 2026. Jika UniPin Gaming Pavilion berfokus pada game dan pengalaman bermain, dukungan terhadap GameHers memperluasnya ke ruang komunitas dan percakapan mengenai gaming, kreativitas, serta pengalaman personal di dalam ekosistem tersebut.
UniPin menyebut keterlibatan di Indonesia Comic Con 2026 sebagai bagian dari upayanya mendukung perkembangan ekosistem gim Indonesia melalui karya lokal, pengalaman interaktif, serta ruang bagi komunitas dan pelaku industri untuk terhubung dengan masyarakat.
Bagi empat studio yang ikut serta, nilai utama dari format ini bukan semata-mata keberadaan mereka di sebuah event besar, tetapi kesempatan untuk membawa game dari layar promosi ke tangan calon pemain. 101 Forgotten, Khuga Bash, Asbak, dan Type Caster menjadi contoh bagaimana karya lokal dapat diperkenalkan melalui pengalaman bermain langsung, bukan hanya melalui materi komunikasi.
UniPin sendiri menyatakan telah memiliki pengalaman lebih dari 14 tahun sebagai penyedia layanan hiburan digital, dengan 25,9 juta pengguna aktif di 33 negara. Layanannya mencakup UniPin Credits yang dapat digunakan untuk berbagai game dari penerbit berbeda.

Norway's government said on Monday it plans to propose a temporary ban on the use of ​AI glasses in selected places, saying it is concerned ‌people could be photographed, filmed or audio-recorded without their knowledge.
The proposal mirrors a broader global backlash against smart glasses equipped with cameras ​over privacy concerns
Ban could apply to places where the public ​regularly gather, such as parks, beaches, museums, shopping ⁠centres and public events, the government said in a ​statement
"I am worried that new, powerful technology is being introduced ​where people risk being photographed, filmed or audio-recorded without knowing it," Digitalisation and Public Governance Minister Torgeir Micaelsen said.
Read More: LISA teams up with Meta for exclusive smart glasses collection
It could also apply ​to schools, playgrounds and youth clubs and to privacy-sensitive ​places such as doctors' offices, swimming pools and gyms with changing rooms
The ‌government ⁠said it was not eyeing a total ban and that private use, and use where others are not at risk of being filmed without consent, would still be allowed
It ​said it ​would examine which ⁠technology the ban would cover, including whether it would apply to glasses with camera ​and audio recording, glasses with camera and ​AI functions ⁠or also other body-worn technology with camera, audio recording and/or AI
The minority government said it would present a bill to ⁠parliament ​as soon as possible, and would ​also set up an expert group to advise on permanent national regulation ​of body-worn technology.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Russian officials on Monday downplayed reports that a laboratory technician in Siberia had died of plague, insisting the situation was under control and that post-mortem tests had not found traces of the disease.
Reports on Friday that a 28-year-old woman named Darya Shipilova, who had been working for the anti-plague institute in Siberia’s Irkutsk region, had died of plague sparked alarm.
The news outlet People of Baikal, citing unnamed sources close to the regional security services, said she may have contracted pneumonic plague from a broken test tube.
Other media reported a possible link between her death and a lab accident at the facility.
But Irkutsk regional governor Igor Kobzev said Monday that a special expert commission inspection in the region had found that “the cause of death was pneumonia of undetermined etiology.”
He said on Telegram that Russia’s consumer and health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor had determined, following tests, that “no microorganisms linked to the young woman’s professional work were found in her biological samples.”
He added that there had been “no new cases of staff from the anti-plague institute seeking medical attention” since the woman’s death.
Kobzev said the sanitary-epidemiological situation in Irkutsk was “stable.”
“The situation remains under our control and that of the experts.”
Asked about the situation on Monday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters to “rely on Rospotrebnadzor’s official statements rather than ... rumors and speculations.”
Plague is a bacterial disease that can occur in several forms, including pneumonic plague, the most contagious type. Pneumonic plague can be fatal if not treated early, according to the World Health Organisation.
Woman dies of plague in Siberia, dozens under quarantine
Earlier, a laboratory worker at a plague research institute in ​Siberia has fallen ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of ‌people and the head of Russia's health watchdog to fly to the Irkutsk region.
The death has sparked public health fears on social media, but the authorities said on Monday the situation was under control.
Plague is endemic to Siberia, home to the first known prehistoric human outbreak, as the bacterium that causes it, Yersinia pestis, is present among small wild mammals in its vast wilderness and their fleas. It is rare for Russians ⁠to fall ill with plague, however, though cases in other parts of the world - notably Africa - occur ​every year.
Local media named the woman as Darya Shipilova, an employee at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of ​Siberia and the Far East.
BREAKING:
5 hospitals have been closed for quarantines in Siberia due to a possible plague outbreak.
The 28-year-old lab technician Darya Shipilova, died yesterday after breaking a test tube with live Yersinia pestis the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute on September 25th while… pic.twitter.com/N6tKLRyAJ5
— Visegrád 24 (@visegrad24) October 4, 2026
There were conflicting reports about how and where the laboratory worker, whose age was given as 28, had fallen ill. Still, the authorities said she had died of pneumonia of as-yet unestablished origin.

Authorities say no new cases ​reported, all contacts traced
Russia's health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, told state media the institute had not found evidence of ​any accidents involving the handling of pathogens after rumours spread on social media that the woman had dropped a test ‌tube containing ⁠live bacteria.
Nevertheless, Anna Popova, the head of Rospotrebnadzor, flew to Siberia for an emergency meeting over the weekend.
An unspecified number of people who had been in contact with the dead woman were quarantined, parts of the hospital in the town of Shelekhov where she died were cordoned off, and an aluminium plant told its ​workers to wear masks.
Read More: WHO asks Ukraine to destroy ‘high-threat pathogens’ to prevent disease spread
Authorities ​urged people to remain ⁠calm and said there was no evidence that the woman's death was linked to her work.
Igor Kobzev, the governor of the Irkutsk region, said in a statement ​that she had died of "pneumonia of unknown aetiology", adding: "Importantly, over the past few ​days, no new ⁠cases of staff from the Anti-Plague Institute seeking medical attention have been identified."

He said the situation was under control and that all known contacts of the dead woman had been identified, examined and placed under medical supervision.
Plague ⁠comes in ​three forms affecting different parts of the body. Pneumonic plague, ​an infection of the lungs, prompts the patient to cough out infectious airborne droplets.
If identified quickly, it can be treated with antibiotics. But ​if left untreated, it can be fatal in one to six days.

items.author: Michael Robuck
items.content:
Ghana awarded 5G spectrum licences to Telecel Group and MTN’s local unit, ending the exclusive wholesale-network model previously used for the country’s 5G rollout, Bloomberg reported.
The exclusivity previously belonged to Next-Gen Infrastructure Company (NGIC), a joint venture (JV) combining Reliance Industries’ Radisys unit, Tech Mahindra, Nokia, and the Ghanaian government, alongside local partners Telecel and AT Ghana.
The JV aimed to reproduce India’s low-cost mobile data model by allowing operators to share infrastructure, but rollout delays prevented it from meeting its targets. Ghana’s government cancelled NGIC’s concession years before its scheduled expiry in 2034 and moved to direct competitive bidding.
Under the new arrangement, Telecel and MTN will build out their own independent networks.
“We plan to launch the service in December this year on our own network,” Telecel CEO Moh Damush told Bloomberg.
Ghana had 49 operational 5G sites earlier this year, compared with a target of 1,200 by 2027. The new licensing model allows established operators to use their existing network footprints to expand coverage. A filing on the Accra bourse showed MTN secured two lots of 700MHz spectrum and three in the 3GHz band, with each 15-year licence priced at about $100 million.

Head of MODENA Subscription, Lusty Aprian Balenguru, mengatakan kebutuhan konsumen terhadap peralatan rumah tangga kini tidak hanya berkaitan dengan produk, tetapi juga kemudahan dalam penggunaan dan perawatan.
“Melalui MODENA Subscription, kami ingin lebih banyak konsumen mendapatkan akses terhadap mesin cuci berkualitas tanpa harus melakukan investasi besar di awal. Dan bukan hanya produknya, konsumen juga mendapatkan layanan service dan maintenance sehingga penggunaan mesin cuci menjadi lebih praktis,” ujar Lusty saat ditemui Gizmologi di Prive at Ambiante, Jakarta Selatan (4/10).
Mesin Cuci MODENA Bisa Berlangganan Mulai Rp270 Ribu
Kategori mesin cuci dalam MODENA Subscription mencakup dua model front load, yaitu Front Load Washer 10kg EcoMotion Inverter WF 1040 VODG dan Front Load Washer 8kg EcoMotion Inverter WF 0840 VGWH. Keduanya tersedia dengan biaya berlangganan mulai Rp270 ribu per bulan, dengan pilihan masa berlangganan selama 3 hingga 7 tahun.
Kedua model menggunakan motor EcoMotion Inverter yang menurut MODENA dirancang untuk membantu menghemat konsumsi listrik, menghasilkan suara lebih halus, serta mengurangi getaran saat mesin digunakan. Mesin cuci tersebut juga memiliki teknologi MSense dan AutoDose+. Sistem ini menyesuaikan penggunaan air dan deterjen sesuai kebutuhan pencucian untuk membantu mencegah penggunaan yang berlebihan.
Untuk pilihan program pencucian, kedua model memiliki 16 program, termasuk AllergyCare yang menggunakan air bersuhu hingga 85 derajat Celsius. Model WF 1040 VODG juga memiliki DryClean dengan Ozone untuk mode pencucian tanpa air.
Dengan skema tersebut, konsumen tidak perlu membayar harga pembelian mesin cuci secara penuh di awal. Sebagai gantinya, biaya penggunaan dibayarkan setiap bulan selama periode subscription yang dipilih.
Apa Bedanya MODENA Subscription dengan Sewa?
Head of MODENA Subscription, Lusty Aprian Balenguru
Perbedaan utama MODENA Subscription dengan skema sewa atau cicilan terletak pada layanan yang mengikuti produk. Dalam skema subscription MODENA, konsumen mendapatkan akses terhadap produk sekaligus layanan maintenance dan service selama masa berlangganan. Sementara itu, konsep sewa dan cicilan pada dasarnya berfokus pada akses atau pembayaran terhadap produk.
MODENA juga memasukkan maintenance sebagai bagian dari paket. Untuk mesin cuci, perawatan dilakukan secara berkala dan mencakup sejumlah bagian yang membutuhkan perhatian setelah digunakan dalam periode tertentu.
Layanan tersebut meliputi product inspection setiap enam bulan, pembersihan detergent drawer setiap enam bulan, pembersihan rubber seal setiap enam bulan, serta pembersihan internal dan eksternal setiap enam bulan. Ada pula filter cleaning setiap 12 bulan dan debris filter maintenance setiap 36 bulan. Jika terjadi kerusakan selama masa berlangganan, layanan service juga sudah termasuk dalam paket.
Menurut Lusty, aspek perawatan menjadi salah satu alasan MODENA mengembangkan model subscription. “Memilih produk elektronik rumah tangga berkualitas perlu diikuti dengan perawatan agar performanya tetap optimal. Namun, dalam praktiknya masih ada gap antara kebutuhan tersebut dengan kebiasaan konsumen dalam melakukan maintenance,” ujarnya.
Bukan Hanya Mesin Cuci, MODENA Subscription Mencakup Banyak Home Appliances
Masuknya mesin cuci membuat pilihan produk dalam MODENA Subscription semakin beragam. Layanan ini mencakup sejumlah kategori home appliances dengan biaya berlangganan mulai Rp175 ribu per bulan. Produk yang tersedia mencakup mesin cuci, AC, kompor, cooker hood, kulkas, water heater, dan water purifier.
Model tersebut membuat subscription dapat digunakan untuk kebutuhan rumah tangga yang berbeda. Konsumen yang baru menempati rumah, misalnya, dapat menggunakan skema berlangganan untuk memenuhi beberapa kebutuhan elektronik tanpa mengeluarkan seluruh biaya pembelian sekaligus.
Hal serupa berlaku bagi penghuni rumah sewaan yang membutuhkan perangkat selama periode tertentu. Pemilik bisnis yang membutuhkan beberapa peralatan elektronik juga dapat menggunakan biaya bulanan sebagai alternatif terhadap pembelian langsung.
Namun, pilihan subscription tetap memiliki konsekuensi yang perlu diperhatikan konsumen. Masa berlangganan mesin cuci yang ditawarkan MODENA berada pada rentang 3 hingga 7 tahun, sehingga konsumen perlu menyesuaikan periode tersebut dengan rencana penggunaan dan kebutuhan rumah tangga.
MODENA Subscription Menawarkan Model Penggunaan
Perluasan ke kategori mesin cuci menunjukkan bahwa konsep yang dibawa MODENA tidak berhenti pada pembelian perangkat dengan pembayaran berkala. Produk dan layanan perawatan ditempatkan dalam satu paket penggunaan. Dalam model ini, konsumen membayar biaya bulanan untuk mendapatkan akses terhadap perangkat, sementara maintenance dan service menjadi bagian dari layanan selama periode berlangganan.
Artinya, nilai subscription bagi konsumen bukan hanya terletak pada rendahnya biaya awal, tetapi juga pada kemudahan mengelola perawatan perangkat. Bagi pengguna yang tidak ingin mengurus maintenance secara terpisah, aspek ini dapat menjadi pertimbangan selain harga bulanan.
MODENA sebelumnya memperkenalkan layanan tersebut dengan nama Seamless Go Subscription Service. Kini layanan tersebut menggunakan nama MODENA Subscription agar lebih mudah dikenali sebagai layanan subscription untuk home appliances.
Untuk memperkenalkan konsep ini kepada konsumen, MODENA juga menjalankan Recharge Day, kegiatan komunitas yang digunakan untuk mengenalkan layanan berlangganan dan penggunaannya dalam kebutuhan sehari-hari.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
IPO-bound study abroad platform Leverage Edu is targeting ₹600 Cr in revenue in FY27, up over 60% from the ₹372 Cr it reported in FY26, sources told Inc42.
The startup’s management wants to reach this revenue milestone before taking it public. Alongside its listing preparations, Leverage Edu is exploring a ₹500 Cr pre-IPO funding round to bring a large private equity firm onto its cap table.
The startup has held talks with a couple of global PE firms and is expected to close the round soon, the sources said.
“Akshay has committed to the board that the company will file DRHP by the end of next year. He is currently out in the market to finalise investment bankers for the IPO,” one of the sources said, referring to founder and CEO Akshay Chaturvedi.
Leverage Edu did not respond to Inc42’s questions till the time of publication.
Preparing For A Public Listing
Inc42 earlier exclusively reported that the startup is planning a ₹2,000–3,000 Cr IPO, comprising a fresh issue of shares and an OFS. The split between the two components is yet to be decided.
The startup is targeting a valuation of over $900 Mn for the IPO. Pitch decks prepared by investment bankers and accessed by Inc42 position Leverage Edu alongside platform businesses such as Zomato, ixigo, and Shadowfax, with expectations of similar valuation multiples.
It turned EBITDA profitable in FY26, posting an EBITDA of ₹9.5 Cr, according to the sources.
Meanwhile, Leverage Edu has been expanding its international presence. In July, Inc42 reported that the startup entered South America through the acquisition of Brazil-based international education company Mundus Agency. Leverage Edu confirmed the acquisition but did not disclose the deal’s financial terms.
Founded in 2017 by Chaturvedi, Leverage Edu helps students apply to foreign universities. Besides its flagship app, it offers courses through the Leverage IELTS and Leverage TOEFL apps.
The startup’s services spanning fintech, accommodation, travel, and career support account for 25–33% of its total revenue. It also claimed to have added over 55,000 students in FY26, taking its total customer base to over 1.75 Lakh.
Leverage Edu has raised about $73 Mn in funding to date from investors including Blume Ventures, DSG Consumer Partners, and Kaizenvest.
