items.author: Dr Fahd Rehman
items.content:
Global value chains (GVCs) have been the carriers of international trade since the 1990s. These chains describe the international disintegration of production, where different stages of manufacturing, marketing and distributing a product materialise across multiple countries.
These chains are dominated by lead firms which are based in advanced countries while suppliers are dispersed across developing countries. In the jargon, the lead firms are located in the Global North and the suppliers are based in the Global South.
Most of the writings on GVCs pay attention to governance, where the lead firms control the suppliers located in developing countries and mainly discuss the prospects of upgrading for the suppliers. A few writings describe the process of value creation, where the lead firms call the shots and capture the value from the suppliers in the chain. Few studies discuss the process of financialisation of GVCs.
The financialisation of GVCs starts with the objectives followed by the lead firms. Since the lead firms are listed on stock exchanges, they have been increasing dividend payouts to shareholders since early 2000. They have also increased share buybacks by using surplus cash.
US-based lead firms are more financialised than those of Europe. The US tax structure incentivises firms to distribute cash to shareholders. On the other hand, the European firms distribute less cash to shareholders. Thus, the surplus cash is used by the lead firms to meet financial objectives.
Lead firms have also financialised their operations as they tighten their grip on the suppliers from developing countries. They have increased the number of payment days for the suppliers since 2000. In addition, they have reduced the number of collection days from their customers. This is how they have boosted their cash position. Hence, the lead firms strengthen their cash position at the cost of suppliers.
Lead firms have reduced their sourcing cost as the number of suppliers from developing countries sprang up since early 2000. In addition, these suppliers have to meet tight deadlines. In this way, the lead firms have increased their profit margins.
Macro environment also provides financial options to the lead firms. Policy rates have been low since early 2000 across the world. Lead firms, tempted by these low policy rates, raised cash through bond issuance. They did not raise capital from stock markets since bonds remained attractive for them. This shows that the lead firms preferred bonds to raise capital.
Lead firms have been following financial goals since early 2000. These firms have been involved in financial activities. They set short-term goals where downsizing is a norm. Downsizing immediately raises the profitability of firms. Such profits are then distributed to shareholders. This is known as downsize and distribute.
Before financial globalisation, the firms used to set long-term goals. They spent on research and development (R&D) to discover new processes, products and technologies. In addition, these firms trained workers who were required to steer R&D. Capital outlays were done to upgrade physical assets with a lasting value. These long-term goals used to kindle industrial capitalism.
In short, the financialisation of GVCs has brought a change in the strategic orientation of the lead firms. These firms extract value from their GVCs and distribute it among shareholders. Lead firms are in pursuit of short-term financial gains while long-term goals have been set aside. Last but not the least, the financialisaton of GVCs has created more challenges than opportunities for the suppliers of developing countries.
The writer is an independent economist and authored a book: Pakistan's Structural Economic Problems in the era of Financial Globalisation

items.content:
Pakistan, once again walking a high-stakes economic tightrope, staged a financial balancing act as record-breaking remittances reduced the surmounting debt pressures. As of August 2026, Pakistan had a current account deficit of $98 million, relatively low given the regional economic complexities due to oil price volatility and closure of the Strait of Hormuz. This was largely driven by an increase in remittances, which have been at record-breaking levels in recent months.
However, the trade balance remains strained as export growth fails to increase, showing its susceptibility to regional uncertainty. Debt obligations in FY26 were above $21.5 billion, with $10 billion expected to be rolled over. However, the positive news is the rising foreign exchange reserves as Pakistan has reported highest-ever levels at more than $21 billion after the receipt of Eurobond sale proceeds. This crucial cushion is providing shock absorbers at a time when uncertainty is growing globally.
This may be the right time to address long-term relevant issues regarding the balance of payments, especially as the IMF programme approaches its latter phases. True economic sovereignty will only be realised if Pakistan can structurally transform its economy into one that is productivity-driven, which generates much-needed export competitiveness and reduces its dependence on external financial support and funding from its ever-so benevolent diaspora.
Pakistan is at a crossroads with its new trade and industrial policies that propel the manufacturing sector but at the same time make its local producers globally competitive. Pakistan has one of the lowest levels of value addition in the manufacturing sector as percentage of GDP, gross fixed capital formation (an indicator of investment) as a percentage of GDP, exports and imports as a percentage of GDP in the Asian region.
The lack of capital accumulation, poor levels of industrialisation and an inward-looking industrial strategy have not only affected its ability to produce and export output effectively but has created an industrial sector that is unproductive and uncompetitive as regional competitors investing in their physical and human capital continue to propel industrial growth and diverge away in terms of economic activity and growth.
The recent draft of the Auto Policy 2026-2031 provides insights into the final document as the government has set export and localisation targets to increase domestic exportable production, while implementing the National Tariff Policy 2025-2030. A clearly laid path to tariff reforms will definitely help reduce uncertainty and allow businesses across the economy to implement long-term decisions. The less competitive businesses are likely to exit, leaving a larger playing field for the more competitive and efficient ones.
Furthermore, the new auto policy has provided significant incentives to the new electric vehicles, offering them tax incentives that would increase their penetration. This will help not only reduce the oil bill, but also lower the adverse environmental impact as Pakistan relies mostly on petrol and diesel consumption to power its transportation sector.
In order to better understand the potential of growth in the auto industry, two examples of developing countries that have undertaken a massive restructuring of their auto sectors and benefitted are Vietnam and Morocco. While Pakistan produces approximately 200,000 units, Morocco produced more than 500,000 units in 2025. While Morocco primarily manufactures and exports cars to the EU as more than 80% of its OEM production is exported, Vietnam has strong linkages in parts and accessories trade with the EU, US and Japan.
Both these countries take advantage of almost negligible tariff rates offered by their trading partners on their exports. It is also important to note that these countries have developed a vast network of deep trade agreements with their major trading partners that not only involves lower tariffs on both imports and exports but also ensures that the burdening costs associated with non-tariff measures (NTMs) are significantly reduced.
Unfortunately, Pakistan has not only failed to integrate itself with its major trading partners by creating a more extensive network of free trade agreements, especially within the Asian region, but has also made little progress to remove the costs associated with the non-tariff measures. The resistance to the National Tariff Policy 2025-2030 is a clear indication of the challenges in propelling productivity and trade growth.
Morocco did not try to reinvent the wheel by adopting an inward-looking strategy as it focused on attracting FDI, offering a predictable and low tariff regime as well as free zones to encourage investments. Vietnam ensured that its local producers meet the same requirements that are expected from foreign companies in terms of standards of production, while creating an effective ecosystem to support local production. However, Pakistani producers have focused on extracting benefits from a captive market without any desire to compete and innovate as they have been successful in locking out foreign competition.
The analysis of GVC-related data extracted from the UN ESCAP's Regional Integration and Value-Added Database paints a stark picture for the auto industry. Pakistan's gross exports, which crossed borders more than once, in the transportation equipment sector was about $100 million, of which 32.8% was foreign value added. Approximately $58 million of direct value-added exports were consumed in the export destination.
Vietnam reported a massive increase of GVC-related exports from about $3.6 billion in 2015 to $11.5 billion in 2024. A larger proportion of its exports are intermediate parts and accessories rather than final goods, which are assembled downstream in its trading partners. More than $4 billion worth of its exports in the auto sector incorporate foreign inputs. Vietnam's focus is mainly on the supply of parts and accessories, which is vastly different than other Southeast Asian countries, which focus on exports of final product. Their localisation rates remain low, with parts and accessories produced mainly for export. Unfortunately, ESCAP does not report data on Morocco.
Although some of the concerns of manufacturers, such as security-related issues, are valid and require a long-term geopolitical solution, many of the concerns regarding high costs of business must be tackled through business reforms and better industrial strategies. Policies must compel OEM to allow participation of their local vendors in regional and global value chains and contracts that limit export sales must be discouraged. This will require incubation of smaller-sized vendors with better financing, R&D facilities and easier access to quality certifications.
Pakistan must harmonise its global standards to ensure that its exporters are able to more easily access more competitive markets. The current SRO regime has done significant damage to industries across the economy and the plan to dismantle it must continue. In essence, the approach must be holistic with wide-ranging reforms that can structurally improve the industries and provide a platform to boost export sales.
THE WRITER IS AN ASSISTANT PROFESSOR OF ECONOMICS AND RESEARCH FELLOW AT CBER, IBA

items.content:
Syria strongly condemned on Sunday Israeli excavation work near a separation line with the occupied Syrian Golan Heights, calling it a “flagrant breach” of the 1974 disengagement agreement.
In a statement, the Foreign Ministry denounced work on the project known as “Sofa 53,” as Israeli forces resumed excavations west of al-Asha village in the countryside of the southern Quneitra province.
The ministry described the work as part of continuing Israeli violations in the buffer zone covered by the disengagement agreement.
“The continuation of the Israeli occupation’s aggressive approach, accompanied by attacks and incursions on the ground, poses a direct threat to regional security and stability and undermines international law,” the ministry warned.
It urged the international community to take deterrent measures to halt such practices and prevent their recurrence.
The ministry also reaffirmed Syria’s right to exercise full sovereignty over all its territory under international law and relevant UN resolutions, calling on the international community to fulfill its legal and moral responsibilities to protect state sovereignty and respect borders.
According to Syria’s Al-Ikhbariya television channel, the project involves excavation and construction of a military road along the separation line within the buffer zone.
Read More: Over 800 Palestinian teachers killed by Israel since Gaza war: education ministry
Israel began working on the project, also referred to as the “Great Storm” or “Sofa 53,” in mid-2022 near Hader in northern Quneitra, before extending it through Jabata al-Khashab, al-Hamidiyah, al-Qahtaniyah, Ruweihina, Bir Ajam and Bariqa.
Its route continues south through al-Asha toward the point where the Syrian, Jordanian and Israeli boundaries meet.
As part of the project, the Israeli army built a military road approximately 8 meters wide, flanked by earth berms reaching around 5 meters in height, according to the Syrian broadcaster.
It also established observation posts and military positions along the route adjacent to the ceasefire line in the occupied Golan Heights.
Syrian accounts indicate that Israeli forces have advanced between 300 and 1,000 meters beyond the ceasefire line, with military construction accelerating in late 2024, particularly after the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime.
Residents previously told Anadolu that the project’s expansion had rendered thousands of dunams of agricultural land in rural Quneitra unsuitable for farming and grazing, while disrupting water flows and altering the area’s natural landscape.
Since Assad’s fall on Dec. 8, 2024, Israel has expanded its military operations in Syria, moving troops into the Golan buffer zone and nearby positions.
Syria demands the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the areas they occupied and maintains its commitment to the 1974 disengagement agreement. Israel claims its movements are driven by security considerations.

items.title: ‘Every moment in Somali pirates’ captivity felt like years,’ says injured Pakistani sailor
items.summary:
After five and a half months in the hands of Somali pirates, the return home brought relief to the surviving crew of the Honour 25 — but could not erase memories of the night when they were forced onto the deck and caught in a deadly exchange of fire.
The Palau-flagged MT Honour 25, carrying 18,500 barrels of oil and a 17-member crew, including 10 Pakistanis, was seized on April 21, around 30 nautical miles off Puntland while sailing from Oman to Somalia. Puntland’s Maritime Police Force said it rescued the tanker in an operation off Dharin-baar, but the pirates opened fire on the hostages, killing five people, including three Pakistanis, and injuring four others.
For Pakistani sailor Ameen bin Shams, the horrific night remains etched in his memory: pirates herding the hostages onto the deck in freezing temperatures, Somali naval forces closing in and, eventually, bullets tearing through the vessel.

items.author: Abbas Naqvi
items.content:
After five and a half months in the hands of Somali pirates, the return home brought relief to the surviving crew of the Honour 25 — but could not erase memories of the night when they were forced onto the deck and caught in a deadly exchange of fire.
The Palau-flagged MT Honour 25, carrying 18,500 barrels of oil and a 17-member crew, including 10 Pakistanis, was seized on April 21, around 30 nautical miles off Puntland while sailing from Oman to Somalia. Puntland’s Maritime Police Force said it rescued the tanker in an operation off Dharin-baar, but the pirates opened fire on the hostages, killing five people, including three Pakistanis, and injuring four others.
For Pakistani sailor Ameen bin Shams, the horrific night remains etched in his memory: pirates herding the hostages onto the deck in freezing temperatures, Somali naval forces closing in and, eventually, bullets tearing through the vessel.
Read: Aircraft carrying four injured crew members, remains of three MT Honour 25 sailors lands in Karachi
“Every moment we spent in the captivity of Somali pirates felt like years. We lived in constant fear of death, never knowing when the pirates might kill us,” said the injured sailor.
Shams said the nightmare they had feared eventually unfolded when Somali security forces launched an operation against another vessel anchored some distance from the Honour 25 and managed to free it.
Following the development, the pirates aboard their vessel ordered the crew to start the ship’s engines and move forward. It was nighttime, and the Somali naval vessel was approximately 10 nautical miles away.
“That night was nothing short of a nightmare. The pirates gathered all of us on the ship’s deck in freezing temperatures. We remained there throughout the night without proper clothing or footwear,” Shams said.
At daybreak, the pirates allowed the crew to go below deck. However, just as they were preparing to rest, they were ordered back onto the deck. All crew members, except Imran and Hussain Yousuf, were tied to the deck railing.
Imran later informed the Ansar Burney Trust by phone that he and Hussain Yousuf were inside the ship’s main engine room, while the remaining crew members had been taken back to the deck by the pirates.
By then, the pursuing Somali naval vessel had closed the distance to just one nautical mile. Security personnel gave the pirates 30 minutes to surrender the vessel and release the hostages, but they refused to comply.
Also Read: Bodies of Pakistanis killed in Somalia being repatriated, arrive in Addis Ababa: PMO
According to Imran, gunfire suddenly erupted, with bullets penetrating the interior of the vessel. The intense exchange of fire continued for more than two hours.
There were 41 pirates aboard the Honour 25. After spending five and a half months in captivity, the crew members had come to know most of the pirates by name, while the pirates also knew their names.
Imran said a pirate identified as Arab panicked during the Somali forces’ operation and opened fire in the section of the vessel where the hostages had been tied up.
The security forces soon gained control of the ship. Five pirates were killed in the operation, while 13 others were injured and arrested.
All four injured Pakistani sailors who arrived in Karachi were shifted to Aga Khan Hospital, where they are currently receiving treatment.
Ameen’s wife, Ayesha, said her husband had sustained four bullet wounds and had been admitted to the hospital.
Meanwhile, Muzammil, son of deceased crew member Mahmood Ansari, told the media at the airport that the families had repeatedly appealed for the safe recovery of the hostages, but the government had failed to listen.
“What is the point of offering compensation now?” he questioned.
The bodies of all three deceased crew members have been handed over to their families, who are making arrangements for their funerals.
The oil tanker Honour 25, sailing under the Somali flag from Oman to Somalia, was hijacked by pirates on April 21. There were 17 crew members aboard, 10 of them Pakistani nationals. The families of the Pakistani hostages spent months seeking the safe release of their loved ones, staging peaceful protests and repeatedly approaching government authorities.
During their captivity, the pirates initially demanded a ransom of $3 million, which was later reduced to $1.9 million and subsequently to $1 million. All the Pakistani crew members who were killed or injured were from different areas of Karachi.
The pirates came under pressure during a rescue operation and, while retreating from the vessel, opened indiscriminate fire on the abducted crew before fleeing the ship. Five sailors were killed, including three Pakistanis — Second Officer Kashif Umar, Third Engineer Mahmood Ansari and Boiler Rafiullah. The other two deceased crew members were an Indian sailor, Tanveer, and the chief engineer from Myanmar.
Four sailors were injured — Usman, Yasir, Ameen and Vicky from Indonesia — while Hussain Yousuf, Imran Ali and Yaseen remained safe. The two surviving Pakistani crew members later contacted the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust in Karachi using the ship captain’s mobile phone and provided details of the incident.
Puntland police said the Honour 25 had 18,500 barrels of oil on board when it was hijacked. The police had been pursuing three hijacked vessels off the Somali coast and had also rescued another oil tanker, Sibu 1, on Friday. However, 28 of the 41 pirates arrested during that operation later escaped while being transferred to jail, with several Puntland security officials accusing local police of complicity.

items.author: ProPK Staff
items.content:
Images of the upcoming Toyota Corolla Altis facelift have surfaced in Pakistan, giving the clearest indication yet that Toyota is preparing to update its popular sedan lineup.
For several weeks, reports from Toyota dealerships had suggested that a Corolla facelift was on the way, along with the possibility of fresh bookings. The latest local sighting now strongly supports those reports.
What’s New in the Corolla Altis Facelift?
The most noticeable changes appear at the front.
Toyota has redesigned the headlights, introduced a slimmer upper grille, and revised the front bumper. Together, these changes give the Corolla a cleaner and more modern appearance.
Toyota has also updated the rear design. The facelift gets revised tail lamps and a refreshed bumper treatment.
The vehicle spotted in Pakistan also carries Altis and 1.8 X badging.
However, the overall body shape remains largely the same. This confirms that Toyota is updating the existing Pakistan-spec Corolla rather than introducing an entirely new generation.
Engine Options May Remain Unchanged
So far, there is no official confirmation of major mechanical changes.
The current Toyota Corolla in Pakistan uses naturally aspirated petrol engines that have been available for several years.
The existing 1.6-liter 1ZR-FE engine produces 120 hp and 154 Nm of torque. Meanwhile, higher variants use the 1.8-liter 2ZR-FE engine, which produces up to 138 hp and 173 Nm.
Since the spotted model appears to be a facelift rather than a new-generation Corolla, Toyota may continue with the same engine lineup.
However, Toyota has not yet confirmed the engines, transmissions, or final equipment levels for the updated model. Therefore, it is still too early to say whether the mechanical package will remain completely unchanged.
A more important question may be the feature list.
Newer sedans and crossovers now offer better safety equipment, more technology, and stronger value for money. Toyota could use the facelift to improve the Corolla’s equipment and make it more competitive.
Why the Corolla Facelift Matters in Pakistan
Pakistan remains one of the markets where Toyota continues to sell the 11th-generation Corolla platform, even though several international markets moved to newer generations years ago.
Despite its age, the Corolla remains one of Pakistan’s most established sedan nameplates.
Its popularity comes from strong resale value, a wide dealership network, easy parts availability, and familiarity among local buyers.
However, competition has increased significantly.
Customers now have access to more crossovers, hybrids, and feature-rich Chinese vehicles. As a result, Toyota can no longer depend on brand reputation alone.
That makes this facelift important for the Corolla.
Toyota needs to improve the sedan’s styling and technology while retaining the qualities that continue to attract Pakistani buyers.
Toyota Corolla Facelift Price and Launch Date
Toyota has not yet announced the official launch date, prices, or final variant lineup for the facelift.
For comparison, the outgoing Corolla lineup currently starts at around Rs. 6.12 million for the 1.6 MT.
At the other end of the range, the Corolla 1.8 Grande is priced at roughly Rs. 7.73 million.
However, final prices may change once Toyota formally introduces the facelift and announces any revisions.
For now, the latest images confirm one key development: the Toyota Corolla Altis facelift is already in Pakistan, and the earlier dealership reports were accurate.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Former federal minister Khawaja Saad Rafique has urged political parties to stop creating “yes men and mirasis” and give their members greater freedom to speak and disagree within their own parties.
Speaking recently, Rafique said political parties need to build stronger internal institutions instead of producing people who simply praise their leadership.
Rafique argued that political parties need to overcome the fear of speaking against their own leadership. He said people who have spent decades in a political party should be able to express their views and expect the leadership to listen.
He also criticized the culture of political accusations and personal attacks. He opined that ordinary people are more concerned about their daily problems, justice and economic hardships than politicians trading allegations against each other.
The former minister said political parties must bring greater democracy into their own structures and develop a culture of consultation.
He also called for an empowered local government system with constitutional protection and said provincial finance commissions should receive a status similar to the National Finance Commission.
Rafique further argued that simply creating smaller provinces would not solve Pakistan’s problems. He said the country needs to address the concentration of power and improve political institutions instead.
He warned that political parties could eventually lose their relevance if they fail to reform themselves.
Rafique also called for greater acceptance of electoral outcomes. He said political parties should widen their consultation process instead of allowing decision-making to become concentrated in the hands of a few individuals.
He criticized the existing electoral structure which hardly allows middle class candidates to enter parliament. He called for credible election institutions and an electoral process free from interference.
The former minister warned that political and institutional failures could eventually push younger generations to demand change in ways that may become difficult for political parties, governments and state institutions to manage.

items.title: Woman Caught Smuggling Rs. 1 Crore Foreign Currency
items.summary:
Customs officials at Karachi Airport have seized foreign currency worth more than Rs. 11.8 million from a woman passenger traveling to Dubai.
The passenger was traveling on a private airline flight to Dubai and allegedly provided incorrect information and a false declaration regarding the currency she was carrying.
A search of her luggage led to the recovery of multiple foreign currencies, including $33,600, €300, £2,570 and AED 19,815.
The total value of the recovered currency was assessed at approximately Rs. 11.8 million.
Customs officials seized the currency under the Customs Act, 1969, following the alleged incorrect declaration by the passenger.
An FIR has also been registered against the woman, while further legal proceedings are underway.

items.title: Wi-Fi 5 vs Wi-Fi 6: What Is the Difference?
items.summary: Wi-Fi Alliance launched the Wi-Fi 6 standard in September 2019. There are many key differences between Wi-Fi 5 and Wi-Fi 6. The Wi-Fi 5, or 802.11ac, standard was introduced in 2013 by the Wi-Fi Alliance. The technical standard is now 13 years old. However, various devices still ship with support for Wi-Fi 5. The Wi-Fi 6, 802.11ax, standard is relatively new. The Wi-Fi Alliance introduced Wi-Fi 6 in September 2019, making it only seven years old. Most flagship smartphones ship with support for Wi-Fi 6. However, Wi-Fi 7 is now the most advanced standard, which was introduced in 2024. Wi-Fi 6 is much better at handling high-bandwidth tasks, delivering a maximum theoretical speed of up to 9.6Gbps. However, real-world speeds could be lower depending on the devices. Yet, it is better for playing competitive games online, watching high-definition (HD) content, and downloading multiple large files simultaneously.

items.title: Over 800 Palestinian teachers killed by Israel since Gaza war: education ministry
items.summary:
Israel has killed more than 800 Palestinian teachers and injured over 3,300 others since the start of its war on the Gaza Strip in October 2023, the Palestinian Education Ministry said Sunday.
In a statement ahead of World Teachers’ Day, observed annually on October 5, the ministry said educators across the occupied Palestinian territories are fighting “a real battle for survival” to protect the right to education amid systematic targeting.
The education sector in Gaza and the West Bank has suffered “comprehensive genocide” since the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, the ministry said.
The ministry said more than 170 teachers remain detained “in harsh conditions.”
It said movement restrictions and harassment at hundreds of checkpoints have compounded educators’ daily suffering, particularly in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron, the village of al-Mughayyir in the central West Bank, the Jordan Valley and areas classified as Area C
items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
Israel has killed more than 800 Palestinian teachers and injured over 3,300 others since the start of its war on the Gaza Strip in October 2023, the Palestinian Education Ministry said Sunday.
In a statement ahead of World Teachers’ Day, observed annually on October 5, the ministry said educators across the occupied Palestinian territories are fighting “a real battle for survival” to protect the right to education amid systematic targeting.
The education sector in Gaza and the West Bank has suffered “comprehensive genocide” since the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, the ministry said.
The ministry said more than 170 teachers remain detained “in harsh conditions.”
It said movement restrictions and harassment at hundreds of checkpoints have compounded educators’ daily suffering, particularly in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron, the village of al-Mughayyir in the central West Bank, the Jordan Valley and areas classified as Area C.
Under the 1995 Oslo II agreement, intended as an interim arrangement, the West Bank was divided into Areas A, B and C.
Area A is under Palestinian civil and security control, while Area B is under Palestinian civil administration and Israeli security control. Area C, which accounts for about 60% of the West Bank, remains under full Israeli control.
The ministry said abuses against Palestinian teachers have been accompanied by severe financial hardship, undermining their material and psychological stability as Israel withholds Palestinian tax revenues.
Read More: Gaza health officials say Israeli strike kills 5
Known as clearance revenues, the funds are taxes collected by Israel on behalf of the Palestinian Authority on imported goods and transferred under the 1994 Paris Protocol.
Israel began deducting sums from these revenues in 2019 and subsequently halted transfers, worsening the Palestinian Authority’s financial crisis and its ability to pay public employees’ salaries in full.
Clearance revenues account for approximately 56% of total Palestinian public revenues, making their withholding a major obstacle to paying salaries, providing public services and meeting government obligations.
The ministry urged the international community, the UN, and education and human rights organizations to take urgent action to curb violations and provide international protection for students and education personnel.
It also called on unions worldwide to press for the release of detained teachers and withheld financial entitlements to ensure educators can live with dignity.

items.title: PTI says access to Imran Khan, K-P counterterrorism policy led to talks deadlock
items.summary:
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Sunday expressed regret over the failure of negotiations between its joint team with Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) and government representatives, urging the government to address the reasons for the deadlock and demonstrate its willingness to engage in meaningful dialogue.
In a statement on X, the party said the negotiations concluded without substantive progress despite “serious efforts” to address political stability, restoration of democracy, supremacy of the Constitution and law, access to PTI founder Imran Khan, his health and medical treatment, and the worsening security situation in K-P and other parts of the country.
PRESS RELEASE
PTI Responds to Inconclusive Negotiations and Federal Ministers’ Press Conference
Party Says Denial of Access to Chairman Imran Khan Remained Central Impediment; Calls for Consensus Based Counterterrorism Strategy and Immediate Attention to Khan’s Medical Care…
— PTI
items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Sunday expressed regret over the failure of negotiations between its joint team with Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ain Pakistan (TTAP) and government representatives, urging the government to address the reasons for the deadlock and demonstrate its willingness to engage in meaningful dialogue.
In a statement on X, the party said the negotiations concluded without substantive progress despite “serious efforts” to address political stability, restoration of democracy, supremacy of the Constitution and law, access to PTI founder Imran Khan, his health and medical treatment, and the worsening security situation in K-P and other parts of the country.
PRESS RELEASE
PTI Responds to Inconclusive Negotiations and Federal Ministers’ Press Conference
Party Says Denial of Access to Chairman Imran Khan Remained Central Impediment; Calls for Consensus Based Counterterrorism Strategy and Immediate Attention to Khan’s Medical Care…
— PTI (@PTIofficial) October 4, 2026
PTI said the principal point of deadlock was its demand for immediate access to Khan so that the party leadership could consult him on matters of national and political importance.
It said its negotiating team had conveyed that other demands could be set aside if the government agreed to this single request. However, according to the party, the government declined to make access to Khan part of the proposed agreement.
The party maintained that consultation with political leadership was an essential part of the democratic process, arguing that just as leaders of other political parties remained central to their parties’ policy and decision-making, PTI should also be able to consult its chairman on major political and national issues.
“Restricting such consultation, particularly during a critical period for the country, inevitably limits the scope for meaningful political engagement,” it said.
PTI further stated that the situation in K-P was another major issue discussed during the negotiations.
According to the party, the government side sought the provincial government’s unconditional support for counterterrorism measures and operations undertaken by the federation and relevant authorities, as well as support for emergency measures within 72 hours in the merged districts and adjoining areas.
PTI reiterated its “unequivocal condemnation” of terrorism and stressed that eliminating terrorism, protecting citizens and restoring lasting peace must remain a national priority.
The party paid tribute to officers and personnel of the armed forces, police, security forces and other law-enforcement agencies who had sacrificed their lives in the fight against terrorism, while expressing solidarity with civilians and families affected by terrorist violence.
It said the people of the province had paid an “extraordinary price” over the years through loss of life, destruction of property and businesses, prolonged insecurity and displacement. “Their concerns and experiences must therefore remain central to any future counterterrorism policy,” PTI said.
Also Read: Naqvi blames K-P CM for talks ‘collapse’, warns Afridi will ‘be responsible’ if anyone dies during march
The party maintained that terrorism could not be defeated through force alone or through unilateral measures that could expose civilians to further loss of life, property damage or displacement.
“Past experience must inform future policy,” it said, adding that any effective strategy must combine firm action against terrorism with protection of civilian populations and sensitivity to local realities.
PTI proposed that authorised representatives of the federal and K-P governments meet within 72 hours to develop a “clear, comprehensive and mutually agreed strategy” for peace and counterterrorism.
It further proposed consultations with political parties represented in the K-P Assembly, elected representatives, tribal elders and other relevant stakeholders so that any policy could enjoy public confidence and be implemented effectively.
The party also rejected attempts to characterise the position of Chief Minister Sohail Afridi as political obstinacy, arguing that had access to Khan been facilitated, the chief minister could have consulted the PTI chairman directly on security and counterterrorism policy, potentially helping bridge differences and create greater consensus.
PTI said effective cooperation among the federal government, provincial government and relevant authorities was indispensable for national security. Such cooperation, however, must respect constitutional requirements, the role of the elected provincial government and the legitimate concerns of the people directly affected, it added.
It further said the health and medical treatment of Khan was also raised as a matter of “fundamental importance”.
The negotiating team sought immediate access to him, his transfer to Shifa International Hospital and the constitution of an appropriate medical board with the participation of his personal physician to ensure proper examination, diagnosis and treatment, according to the statement.
Read More: Kundi, Naqvi slam K-P govt over counterterrorism role during talks
PTI said the government had agreed only to restore meetings between Khan and his family members and lawyers from Tuesday, but had not agreed to additional measures concerning his medical assessment and treatment.
The party welcomed the resumption of family and legal meetings but stressed that such access could not substitute for proper medical examination and necessary treatment. “Khan’s health must be addressed with seriousness, transparency and humanitarian consideration,” it said, adding that all medically necessary steps should be taken without delay.
Responding to the subsequent press conference by federal ministers, PTI said the government should refrain from placing responsibility for the inconclusive negotiations entirely on the opposition and instead address the substantive issues that prevented progress.
It called on the government to explain why immediate access to Khan was considered unacceptable, why the requested measures regarding his medical care were not accommodated, and why a broader consultative approach involving the provincial government, political representatives, tribal elders and other stakeholders was not accepted for developing a sustainable security strategy for K-P.
PTI reiterated that it remained prepared to engage in political dialogue, constitutional processes, meaningful consultation and national consensus to address Khan’s health and treatment, restoration of democracy, supremacy of the Constitution and law, political stability, terrorism and other challenges confronting the country.
The party stressed, however, that meaningful negotiations could not succeed through predetermined positions or demands for unconditional endorsement. “Serious dialogue requires flexibility, mutual confidence, consultation and a genuine willingness to translate discussions into practical progress,” it concluded.
Salman Akram Raja says talks broke down over K-P counterterrorism policy
PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja also said that the deadlock in negotiations with the federal government emerged over the issue of counterterrorism policy in K-P.
Speaking to a private news channel on Sunday, he stated that PTI’s negotiating team maintained that any future strategy against terrorism in K-P should not be determined solely by the federal government.
He said that if the federal government wanted administrative measures that could displace people from their homes, the provincial government could not be held responsible for the consequences if it had no meaningful role in policy formulation.
Raja added that as drafts were amended during talks with the government, PTI’s negotiating team realised that the government’s intentions on some issues were broader than initially understood.
He said the drafts were shared with CM Afridi and the PTI negotiating team because the provincial leadership, being directly responsible for running the province, could better assess the consequences of the proposed measures.
حکومت اور پی ٹی آئی/تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان مزاکرات کی ناکامی کی بنیادی وجہ حکومتی اصرار تھا کہ خیبر پختونخواہ حکومت وفاق اور اسکے اداروں کے ان تمام اقدام اور آپریشنز کی تائید کرے جو صوبے میں دہشت گردی کے حوالے سے کئے جائیں گے۔ ضم اضلاع اور ان سے متصل علاقوں میں 72 گھنٹوں میں…
— salman akram raja (@salmanAraja) October 4, 2026
Raja underlined that PTI therefore proposed that the federal and provincial governments jointly formulate a strategy, followed by consultations with all political parties, including Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz and Pakistan Peoples Party, as well as tribal elders and other relevant stakeholders.
Raja said the government rejected suggestions of a “roadmap” and a “joint strategy” and instead wanted emergency measures imposed in several districts within 72 hours.
Rejecting claims that the K-P government had already agreed to the proposals, he said there was no fundamental disagreement between Afridi and the PTI negotiating team.
He added that an English draft contained a provision for imposing an emergency within 72 hours, while the same provision had reportedly been removed from the Urdu version. He said that once the government’s intentions became clear, PTI agreed it could not accept the proposal.
Commenting on the Police Act 2026, Raja said the K-P government was willing to review the legislation, adding that the law could be examined within 72 hours alongside legislation in Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan to identify provisions that could be applied in the case of K-P.
He also stated that there was no disagreement over the National Action Plan, which was a “national, consensus-based document”, further noting that the dispute was over its implementation.
He further said that PTI could not support measures such as drone strikes and operations that displaced people from their homes, adding that the party had consistently opposed such actions in the past.
Raja said that if an emergency was imposed in certain districts and the federal government then decided what action to take without consulting the provincial government, there could be no jointly agreed strategy. “In that situation, anything can happen.”
Leaving all other issues and much noise aside, the primary reason for the failure of the talks around 3am this morning between the government team and the PTI-TTAP team was the following: the PTI-TTAP team stood firm on its principled position that anti-terorrism actions in KPK…
— salman akram raja (@salmanAraja) October 4, 2026
He further said PTI could neither endorse such a policy nor take responsibility for its consequences. PTI, he said, had proposed that the federal and provincial governments formulate a mutually agreed strategy within 72 hours and then implement it.
He rejected allegations that PTI and the K-P government’s position was aligned with the interests of militants, calling such claims “extremely unfortunate” and “completely wrong and contrary to facts”.
He added that PTI stood firmly against terrorism and supported “zero tolerance” for terrorist groups, adding that the party wanted to work with the federal government to eliminate terrorism.
On the security situation in K-P, Raja acknowledged that the government’s writ had weakened in some districts and that militant groups wielded significant influence.
However, he said the underlying causes needed to be understood rather than simply blaming the provincial government. PTI lawmakers and ministers, he added, were themselves among those being targeted by militants. “The realities on the ground in K-P cannot be understood while sitting afar in Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi,” he maintained.
Raja said a comprehensive strategy should also take into account ground realities, local communities and tribal traditions, while facilitating dialogue among tribes living on both sides of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
He maintained that a sustainable policy against terrorism in K-P required consultation between the federal and provincial governments, political parties and local stakeholders, rather than unilateral measures that could potentially fuel further displacement and instability. “Military operations alone cannot resolve the security crisis in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he stated.
Raja said PTI had proposed that the two sides “sit together for 72 hours, discuss the matter thoroughly and then move forward with an agreed policy”.
On negotiations concerning Imran Khan, he said the issue of access to Imran’s personal doctors had remained unresolved. “PTI’s position is that Imran should be transferred to a hospital with an international medical board and doctors personally trusted by his family be involved in his treatment”.
He added that the proposed arrangement for access to Imran included a meeting with his family and lawyers on Tuesday, while the question of meetings with other political figures remained unresolved.
Raja identified two issues as fundamental deal-breakers: the proposed counterterrorism policy in K-P and the treatment of Imran’s personal and legal matters.
Responding to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s claim that many of the political issues had been agreed upon, Raja said minor issues could not outweigh the unresolved major ones.
He underlined that the government was effectively asking PTI to abandon its position on counterterrorism and accept the policy the federal government had decided to implement.
Raja said PTI could not set aside what he described as the personal victimisation of Imran and accept the treatment he was receiving in prison. “These two issues were such that they overshadowed everything else,” he added.
He concluded that it was PTI’s responsibility to speak out and that the party would continue its political struggle regardless of the obstacles it faced.
Amir Muqam rejects PTI’s account of failed talks, says key issues had been agreed upon
Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, while presenting the government’s position on the talks, rejected Raja’s account of the breakdown in negotiations, saying the talks had been conducted in good faith and that most of the issues raised by PTI had been resolved.
Muqam said representatives from both sides held extensive discussions, including a session lasting around 12 hours, with the aim of preventing the dispute from escalating into a confrontation between the federal and K-P governments.
He stated that PTI’s concerns relating to Imran had been addressed, adding that an agreement had been reached that Imran would continue to meet his lawyers and family members in prison and that arrangements concerning his medical treatment would also be discussed.
Muqam said the wording of the draft agreement had been revised following discussions with PTI and that the issue concerning Imran’s meetings had effectively been settled.
He said the remaining disagreement concerned the issue of terrorism and the role of the K-P government in implementing the counterterrorism policy.
Muqam said the federal side had told PTI from the outset that the K-P government’s participation was necessary because the matter directly concerned the province. He added that PTI representatives had sought time to consult the provincial leadership in Peshawar and subsequently returned saying they had obtained full authority to negotiate on its behalf.
Also Read: Asif, Tarar fire fresh salvoes at PTI after talks deadlock
Rejecting the claim that the government had demanded an emergency in several districts within 72 hours, Muqam said the proposal was instead to use the 72 hours to formulate and sign an agreed course of action between the provincial government and the interior ministry.
He underscored that the 72-hour timeframe was intended for the two sides to sit together, settle the outstanding issues and determine how the counterterrorism strategy would be implemented.
He also rejected PTI’s claim that the federal government wanted to impose its policy unilaterally on K-P. He said the National Action Plan was a national policy and could not be treated as a policy applicable only to K-P.
Referring to a resolution passed by the K-P Assembly, Muqam said the resolution itself contained provisions concerning the use of police and the Counter Terrorism Department to combat terrorism and opposition to military operations.
He further questioned PTI’s position, arguing that the party could not simultaneously demand that the military be excluded from operations while also seeking greater authority and resources for the provincial government.
He also criticised what he described as changes made by the K-P government to its own counterterrorism policy and said powers had subsequently been withdrawn from relevant institutions. “This is a national issue,” he said, adding that the government could consider legitimate proposals but could not make every provincial demand part of the agreement at that stage.
On the question of whether it had been decided that an emergency would be imposed in K-P, Muqam indicated that the matter was still part of the ongoing discussions and did not confirm that a final decision to impose emergency measures had been taken.
Asad Qaiser says access to Imran at heart of talks deadlock
PTI leader Asad Qaiser also stated that the deadlock in negotiations with the government centred on the party’s demand for access to PTI founder Imran Khan.
“The root cause of the deadlock was that we were under the impression that first you would provide us access to Imran Khan,” he said, adding that PTI had withdrawn all its other demands and retained only the request for its political leadership to meet Imran.
In a post on X, Qaiser said the government had told PTI that Imran would not be part of the agreement and that his involvement was “not under consideration” at that stage. He stated that PTI should be able to consult Imran on major policy decisions, just as other political parties consult their leadership.
“If the PML-N consults Nawaz Sharif or Shehbaz Sharif on every matter, or the PPP consults Bilawal Bhutto and Asif Zardari, then our leader Imran Khan — who is the most popular leader and is in jail — shouldn’t we consult him on whatever policy is made?” Qaiser asked. “Shouldn’t we take his direction? So that’s our biggest issue,” he said.
ڈیڈلاک کی بنیادی وجہ یہ تھی کہ ہم یہ سمجھ رہے تھے کہ سب سے پہلے آپ ہمیں عمران خان تک ایکسیس دیں۔ اور ہم نے کہا کہ ہم تمام مطالبات واپس کرتے ہیں، ہمارا ایک ہی مطالبہ ہے کہ ہماری پولیٹیکل لیڈرشپ کو عمران خان تک رسائی دی جائے۔ تو انہوں نے کہا کہ ابھی تک وہ ایگریمنٹ میں شامل نہیں… pic.twitter.com/gbRfkCuXqA
— Asad Qaiser (@AsadQaiserPTI) October 4, 2026
Rejecting the suggestion that PTI was seeking to give the issue of terrorism a political dimension, Qaiser said the party had proposed a mechanism for greater coordination between the federal and provincial governments to address militancy.
He said PTI’s proposed text called for “effective, continuous and meaningful consultation” to eliminate terrorism in K-P, protect lives and property and establish lasting peace.
He further stated that the proposal envisaged regular reviews of existing policies and measures, with amendments where necessary, adding that it also called for authorised representatives of the federal and provincial governments to meet within 72 hours and jointly prepare a “clear, comprehensive, feasible and agreed-upon roadmap” for peace and security.
“All responsible leaders and stakeholders of political parties” would also be included in the process so that the resulting policy could secure wider public trust, Qaiser said.
Earlier on Sunday, the party launched the first phase of its long march from Lakki Marwat to Swabi amid a government-opposition deadlock and mounting political tensions, with no plan for a march towards Islamabad announced so far.
The long march, initially scheduled for September 27, was postponed to October 4, but the standoff between the federal and provincial governments remains unresolved.
On Saturday, talks between the government and opposition failed to break the deadlock over the PTI’s long march, with both sides maintaining their positions and pressing competing demands.
The talks, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, followed an initial round on Friday in which the two sides exchanged their positions but failed to reach an agreement.
The government wanted the PTI to take the initiative by cancelling the march, while the opposition wanted the government to first facilitate a meeting with its jailed founder, according to sources familiar with the talks.

items.title: WhatsApp Mulai Gulirkan Fitur Restricted Chat Untuk Pengguna Versi Beta, Apa Fungsinya?
items.summary:
Aplikasi berkirim pesan milik Meta, WhatsApp terus menggulirkan fitur-fitur baru demi memberikan penggunanya kemampuan untuk berkirim pesan lebih nyaman dan aman. Dan yang terbaru, WhatsApp sedang menguji coba fitur baru yang mereka sebut dengan “Restricted Chat”. Dan sesuai namanya, fitur ini memberikan lapisan keamanan ekstra dalam berkirim pesan, menambahkan sejumlah syarat khusus.
Sama seperti sebelum-sebelumnya, WhatsApp selalu menggulirkan fitur baru kepada para pengguna aplikasi versi Beta lebih dulu. Tujuannya? Selain untuk sempurnakan fitur sebelum akhirnya digulirkan ke semua pengguna, juga untuk memutuskan apakah fitur tersebut benar-benar bermanfaat—karena bisa saja tidak jadi digulirkan ke pengguna versi non-Beta.
Dan informasi terbaru terkait fitur WhatsApp Restricted Chat, diinformasikan oleh WABetaInfo. Sejatinya sejak bulan lalu, kehadiran fitur ini sudah diperkirakan. Dan akhirnya pengguna Android maupun iOS sudah bisa menikmati fitur ini lewat aplikasi WhatsApp Beta
items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
Aplikasi berkirim pesan milik Meta, WhatsApp terus menggulirkan fitur-fitur baru demi memberikan penggunanya kemampuan untuk berkirim pesan lebih nyaman dan aman. Dan yang terbaru, WhatsApp sedang menguji coba fitur baru yang mereka sebut dengan “Restricted Chat”. Dan sesuai namanya, fitur ini memberikan lapisan keamanan ekstra dalam berkirim pesan, menambahkan sejumlah syarat khusus.
Sama seperti sebelum-sebelumnya, WhatsApp selalu menggulirkan fitur baru kepada para pengguna aplikasi versi Beta lebih dulu. Tujuannya? Selain untuk sempurnakan fitur sebelum akhirnya digulirkan ke semua pengguna, juga untuk memutuskan apakah fitur tersebut benar-benar bermanfaat—karena bisa saja tidak jadi digulirkan ke pengguna versi non-Beta.
Dan informasi terbaru terkait fitur WhatsApp Restricted Chat, diinformasikan oleh WABetaInfo. Sejatinya sejak bulan lalu, kehadiran fitur ini sudah diperkirakan. Dan akhirnya pengguna Android maupun iOS sudah bisa menikmati fitur ini lewat aplikasi WhatsApp Beta terbaru. Lantas apa saja manfaat fitur Restricted Chat di dalam WhatsApp?
Baca juga: Cara Membuat Username WhatsApp, Alternatif Tanpa Perlu Berbagi Nomor ke Orang Lain
Fitur Restricted Chat Bakal Hadir Opsional
Menurut laporan WABetaInfo, fitur Restricted Chat sudah tersedia bagi mereka yang sudah mendapatkan pembaruan aplikasi WhatsApp Beta, lebih tepatnya versi 2.26.36.4 pada Android atau versi 26.39.10.20 pada perangkat iOS. Dan setelah ditelusuri lebih lanjut, ini merupakan fitur yang bersifat opsional.
Seperti fitur Advanced Chat Privacy, fitur Restricted Chat juga tersembunyi pada menu Settings akun personal yang sedang pengguna chat atau lakukan obrolan, yang kemudian bisa pengguna aktifkan secar manual. 
Saat diaktifkan, akan ada proteksi atau limitasi tambahan yang dijalankan. Apa saja? Mulai dari media yang tidak bisa tersimpan langsung ke penyimpanan atau galeri perangkat, tidak bisa ekspor pesan, tidak bisa mengakses fitur Meta AI secara langsung dari dalam ruang obrolan, hingga tidak bisa mengakses pesan tersebut lewat perangkat yang terdaftar pada Linked Devices.
Sehingga sama seperti ketika menerima notifikasi OTP, pesan yang dikirimkan lewat fitur Restricted Chat, hanya bisa diakses dari perangkat WhatsApp utama, tidak bisa dari perangkat sekunder yang sudah disambungkan. WhatsApp sebutkan bila alasannya agar tidak ada agen AI atau ekstensi lainnya yang bisa akses, alias untuk menutup celah.
Jadi Bagian dari Penambahan Fitur Secara Rutin
Hadir sebagai fitur opsional, WhatsApp tetap sebutkan bila meski aktif atau tidak, semua obrolan yang terjadi di dalam WhatsApp tetap terenkripsi sepenuhnya. Dan hingga saat ini, masih belum bisa dipastikan apakah fitur Restricted Chat bakal digulirkan dalam waktu dekat ke semua pengguna atau tidak.
Sebelumnya, juga sempat diinformasikan bila WhatsApp sedang menguji fitur scam alert, alias pendeteksi otomatis pesan penipuan yang masuk ke dalam platform. Menariknya, fitur ini disebut bisa dijalankan tanpa pihak WhatsApp perlu membaca isi chat.
Sementara dalam beberapa pekan terakhir, semua pengguna WhatsApp secara rutin mendapatkan kemampuan baru. Mulai dari melakukan panggilan video secara langsung dari WhatsApp Web, hingga opsi untuk membuat username sehingga tidak perlu membagikan nomor pribadi.

items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
Indian actor Janhvi Kapoor has condemned an AI-generated deepfake that manipulated footage from her Devara: Part 1 song Chuttamalle, calling the non-consensual use of her image a “deeply violating” act and warning that the issue reflects a broader reality faced by women.
The altered video, which circulated widely online, digitally manipulated footage featuring Kapoor from the 2024 film and presented her in a sexually explicit manner that was not part of the original production. The incident has triggered strong reactions across the Indian film industry, while renewing concerns about the misuse of artificial intelligence to target women.
Breaking her silence on the controversy on Instagram, Kapoor said the issue extends well beyond the particular video involving her. She argued that the misuse of technology reflects a broader problem surrounding the way women’s bodies, choices and boundaries are treated.
"The criminal misuse of technology to objectify women and circulating fictionalised content without consent is deeply violating, bordering on sexual assault. Almost every woman in my industry has faced some version of this. And women everywhere are increasingly being subjected to it," she wrote.
According to Kapoor, consent should not be viewed as complicated or open to interpretation. A woman’s decisions about her body, appearance and personal boundaries remain hers alone, regardless of what she wears or what choices she may have made previously.
She further argued that the growing threat posed by AI-generated abuse comes on top of the physical and social pressures women already face. In her view, technology has created another avenue through which women can be subjected to harassment and violations of their privacy.
"It is about the larger reality of being a woman. The gaze, the judgement, the constant negotiation for safety and the feelings that our boundaries somehow remain open to interpretation. That threat has now expanded into the digital sphere," she said.
Screengrab: janhvikapoor/Instagram
Kapoor also called for a wider change in social attitudes, saying responsibility should not rest solely on women or their families to protect themselves from harassment. Instead, she said society must challenge the attitudes that lead people to believe they are entitled to cross another person’s boundaries.
The actor thanked her Devara co-star Jr NTR for speaking out against the manipulated video. NTR had earlier condemned the clip and said he would pursue legal action against those responsible for creating and circulating it.
The controversy has once again highlighted the growing challenges posed by AI deepfakes, particularly when the technology is used to fabricate intimate or degrading material involving people without their knowledge or consent.
Kapoor ended by emphasising the importance of recognising women’s right to control their own images, bodies and boundaries.
"I hope everything unfolding around us right now forces those who participate in any form of harassment to introspect. Is it really too much for a woman to ask to simply be treated and seen as a human being? Her body, her image, her boundaries, her choice".
Her message ultimately centred on a basic principle: women should be treated as people with the right to control their own images, bodies and boundaries.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
The leader of Yemen's Saudi-backed government announced the beginning of a major military operation against the Iran-backed Houthis on Sunday, aimed at seizing the ‌territory under their control.
Regional and western officials had told Reuters earlier this week that Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies were planning to launch an assault on the Houthis, with the Saudis leading aerial combat and Yemeni forces fighting on the ground.
"Today, I announce the start of military operations to retake the remaining territory of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory," Yemeni ​President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address.
The Houthis, meanwhile, said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area ​of Saudi Arabia, claiming the attacks caused major fires, in response to what they said were 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes on ⁠Yemen in the past 12 hours.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.
'Opportunities for de-escalation exhausted'
Al-Alimi said the decision to launch the counteroffensive came after all opportunities for de-escalation had been ​exhausted, accusing the Houthis of responding to efforts to calm the conflict with further mobilisation and escalation.
"Our position today is to assume the national responsibility of confronting the Houthi militia, after ​all opportunities for de-escalation have been exhausted," he said.
Al-Alimi said he had ordered the armed forces, security forces and all military formations to begin carrying out their assigned tasks under approved plans.
Saudi Arabia entered neighbouring Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition in support of the internationally recognised government, which the Houthis had driven out of the capital Sanaa.
Al-Alimi thanked Saudi Arabia for its support, saying the ​kingdom had "stood alongside Yemen in the darkest circumstances," and called on Yemen's regional allies and international partners to support the country, its armed forces and state institutions.
The US is already ​providing intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen, while some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, six people with knowledge of the Saudi preparations told Reuters.
A truce agreed ‌between the ⁠warring parties in 2022 largely held until this year, when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure in a spillover from the Iran war.
Houthis' lightning offensive
The Houthis have so far maintained the initiative on the ground, weeks after seizing the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait in a lightning offensive down the coast that saw government forces collapse.
Bab el-Mandeb is the southern exit passage of the Red Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia that has assumed even more importance this year as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, ​which has been effectively closed by the ​Iran conflict.
Read More: Araghchi says Tehran serious about diplomatic path, rules out ‘military solution’ to end war
The Houthis already controlled the northwest ⁠of the country, where most of the population live.
In the last 48 hours, the Houthis have also made gains against government and local forces on strategic hilltops near Yemen's Taiz, military sources said, advancing on the last road between the city and Aden on the southern coast, ​where the Saudi-backed Yemeni government is based.
Houthi control over the Taiz-Aden road would lead to an effective siege of the city, Yemen's ​third-largest, inhabited by hundreds of ⁠thousands of civilians and where thousands of government forces are also stationed.
It would also consolidate control of that flat coastal Bab el-Mandeb area by seizing the rugged mountains overlooking them in the western Taiz countryside, according to Mohammed Al-Qadhi, a veteran Yemeni journalist from Taiz now working as a political analyst.
"This will help them protect their back in case of any operation against the coastline, and ⁠make recapturing ​those areas much more difficult," he said.
The city is important not just for its strategic location; Yemeni President Rashad ​al-Alimi is from the region, and a siege of Taiz would amplify an already-dire humanitarian situation in the country.
Three-in-four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry from the impact of the surge in fighting, which has displaced ​tens of thousands of people and disrupted supplies to millions, the World Food Programme said last week.

items.title: POCO C95 Pro Jadi Kembaran REDMI 17 dengan Satu Penyederhanaan Utama
items.summary:
Tak lama setelah Xiaomi meresmikan REDMI 17 setelah resmi di Indonesia beberapa pekan lalu, Xiaomi Global memutuskan untuk rilis saudara kembar dengan penamaan yang berbeda. Dinamakan POCO C95 Pro, smartphone terbaru POCO satu ini membawa tampilan yang cukup identik, begitu pula spesifikasinya. Meski ada satu fitur ekstra yang absen alias tidak ikut diturunkan dari REDMI.
Ya, ini merupakan situasi yang lumrah dilakukan oleh Xiaomi maupun POCO. Umumnya, opsi yang ditawarkan lewat merek POCO bisa ditawarkan dengan harga sedikit lebih terjangkau. Bagaimana bisa? Tidak lain dengan metode penjualan yang dibuat berbeda, di mana smartphone POCO umumnya hanya dijual secara eksklusif online, alias tidak tersedia secara luring.
Lain halnya dengan smartphone Xiaomi yang lebih mudah didapatkan secara langsung, terutama ketika kini toko resmi luring Xiaomi sudah semakin banyak tersedia di berbagai wilayah di Indonesia. Lantas apakah spesifikasi POCO C95 Pro benar-benar identik?

items.content:
Tak lama setelah Xiaomi meresmikan REDMI 17 setelah resmi di Indonesia beberapa pekan lalu, Xiaomi Global memutuskan untuk rilis saudara kembar dengan penamaan yang berbeda. Dinamakan POCO C95 Pro, smartphone terbaru POCO satu ini membawa tampilan yang cukup identik, begitu pula spesifikasinya. Ya, ini merupakan situasi yang lumrah dilakukan oleh Xiaomi maupun POCO. Umumnya, opsi yang ditawarkan lewat merek POCO bisa ditawarkan dengan harga sedikit lebih terjangkau. Bagaimana bisa? Tidak lain dengan metode penjualan yang dibuat berbeda, di mana smartphone POCO umumnya hanya dijual secara eksklusif online, alias tidak tersedia secara luring.
Lain halnya dengan smartphone Xiaomi yang lebih mudah didapatkan secara langsung, terutama ketika kini toko resmi luring Xiaomi sudah semakin banyak tersedia di berbagai wilayah di Indonesia. Lantas apakah spesifikasi POCO C95 Pro benar-benar identik?
Baca juga: Spesifikasi POCO F9 Pro, Flagship POCO Siap Rilis Resmi 5 Oktober
Spesifikasi POCO C95 Pro, Tak Dilengkapi Lampu RGB
Dari tampilan desain POCO C95 Pro, memang terlihat sangat mirip dengan REDMI 17 4G, mulai dari opsi warnanya hingga bentuk modul kamera belakangnya. Dimensinya pun sama persis, tergolong cukup bongsor mengingat ukuran layarnya tergolong sangat luas. Memiliki ketebalan hingga 8,8mm, dengan bobot sedikit melampaui 232 gram.
Bodi POCO C95 Pro juga membawa sertifikasi IP64, sehingga tahan dari debu dan cipratan air. Namun bila dilihat secara seksama pada bagian bodi belakang, terlihat sedikit perbedaan dibandingkan desain REDMI 17. Yakni ada pada modul kamera utamanya—sama-sama mengusung dua lingkaran hitam dengan lampu kilat.
Namun begitu, spesifikasi POCO C95 Pro tak dilengkapi dengan lampu RGB khusus—sebuah fitur yang diperkenalkan lewat REDMI 17 4G, tidak hanya untuk fitur personalisasi tambahan, namun juga fungsi pemberitahuan seperti notifikasi ketika smartphone diletakkan dengan layar menghadap ke bawah. Selain fitur satu ini, semua spesifikasi kedua smartphone terbilang identik.
Mulai dari layar 6,9 inci HD+ 120Hz, chipset Helio G91-Ultra 12nm dari MediaTek, hingga kapasitas baterai besar 7500 mAh. Sudah tersedia untuk pasar global, harga POCO C95 Pro dibanderol mulai USD169 (Rp3 jutaan) untuk varian memori 6+128GB. Dan bila nantinya tersedia resmi di Indonesia, besar kemungkinan bakal dijual sedikit lebih terjangkau dibandingkan harga REDMI 17 4G.
Tetap Andalkan Daya Tahan Baterai Andalan
Melihat halaman produk resminya, POCO C95 Pro membawa kapasitas baterai besar 7500 mAh yang diklaim bisa digunakan hingga dua hari penuh, atau memutar musik hingga 91 jam maupun memutar video hingga 28 jam nonstop. Proses pengisian dayanya pun bisa berjalan cepat lewat dukungan fast charging 45W, membutuhkan waktu kurang dari 100 menit untuk isi daya dari nol sampai penuh.
Pengguna juga bisa memanfaatkan baterai POCO C95 Pro sebagai powerbank, yang bisa alirkan daya hingga 22,5W. Layar POCO C95 Pro juga sudah terproteksi Gorilla Glass 7i, membawa sertifikasi TUV agar lebih nyaman dipandang mata, serta diperkuat setup speaker stereo dengan mode volume maksimal sampai 300%. Dan untuk setup kamera POCO C95 Pro sendiri, diperkuat sensor utama 50MP f/1.8, dan dipasangkan bersama sensor sekunder, serta 8MP f/2.1 di sisi depan.
POCO sematkan dukungan perekaman video dari kedua sisi kamera sekaligus alias dual video. Smartphone ini jalankan Android 16, dengan tampilan antarmuka HyperOS 3, dengan fitur-fitur ekstra di dalamnya termasuk Xiaomi HyperIsland untuk tampilan notifikasi lebih intuitif.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
In the northern Finnish town of Muhos, 36-year-old farmer Joni Pitkanen is preparing for life with a new neighbour -- just kilometers away, tech giant Google is planning to build new data centres.
The planned data centres are part of an announced 13-billion-euro ($15-billion) investment in Finland over the next two years -- the US tech giant's single biggest investment in Europe.
A few kilometers down the gravel road that passes by Pitkanen's farm, the forest has already been cut down on land acquired by Google, with excavators now clearing the ground and rumbling trucks shuttling back and forth to the construction area located next to major power lines.
"The project is so massive that it's basically hard to really grasp, even though we're right here on the sidelines," Pitkanen said, as a few cows dozed in a meadow in front of the barn.
Google's expansion plans include the Finnish municipalities of Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala as well as Hamina, where it already operates a data centre. 
The massive investment prompted US President Donald Trump to urge Google to rethink its plans in a message on his Truth Social network.
Pitkanen said he was so far "fairly positive" about the project, as it will bring "large-scale business activity" and "life" to the rural municipality with a population of only around 8,800 people.
"But of course we are concerned about... how we can prepare for the energy consumption," he added.
In his office in the small village centre, Muhos mayor Kimmo Hinno told AFP that Google's "massive investment" kept him busy these days as "no industry of this type" existed here at present.
"This will completely change the situation for the entire municipality and the Oulu region," he said, adding that he expected "thousands of workers" of different nationalities during the construction period -- who will need both housing and other services.
Read More: OpenAI safety employee quits, says ‘time for trial and error is over’
Outside a grocery store, 60-year-old nurse Aila Heilima said she hoped the investment would "motivate young people to stay" in Muhos for work, instead of moving to bigger towns in search of job opportunities.
But Google's plans have already sparked controversy.
The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) is currently investigating whether company Tuike Finland, which represents Google, had cleared more than 300 hectares of forest in Muhos without a mandatory environmental impact assessment.
"In our view, operations at this construction site should be suspended until it is clarified whether the project is in compliance with the law," Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the board of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, who filed the request with the agency, told AFP at the edge of the deforested area. 
"From the satellite images, we've seen that nature sites which should be preserved have also been logged," she added, explaining that the size of the clear-cut area was comparable to 420 football fields.
Google, meanwhile, told AFP in an email that "tree felling activities have been taking place in compliance with Forestry Act requirements" and they "were awaiting further guidance from LVV on this matter."
"We have conducted extensive nature surveys covering the entire area as part of the zoning and Environmental Impact Assessment processes, to ensure high-value nature zones within the sites have been protected during forestry works," said Sondre Ronander, communications manager for Google in Finland.
Finland has seen a spike in data centre investments, with its cool climate and relatively stable and cheap electricity that is mostly produced without fossil fuels thanks to nuclear plants as well as extensive wind and hydro power.
Prime Minister Petteri Orpo's right-wing government has prioritised attracting data centre investments to the Nordic country, which is grappling with record-high unemployment and sluggish economic growth.
But, as dozens of the energy guzzling centres are now under construction and many more planned by companies including Microsoft and TikTok, uncertainty around energy prices, grid capacity and environmental effects have sparked a public debate in Finland. 
A citizen's initiative demanding stricter regulation regarding data centre energy use and consequences for the environment gathered more than 50,000 signatures in just three days after it opened, meaning it will have to be reviewed.

items.title: A taste of home in orbit: How China keeps its astronauts well-fed
items.summary:
Although called Tiangong, or "Heavenly Palace," China's space station is becoming less distant and more like home, as astronauts bring the comforting tastes into orbit.
The Chinese space kitchen now serves nearly 200 food items. Alongside dumplings and mooncakes, home-style dishes such as Kung Pao chicken, mapo tofu and fried rice have made it onto the station's menu.
