items.content:
By Esther Onyegbula
The Federal Government has stepped up efforts to increase local production of essential medicines and position Nigeria as a major pharmaceutical manufacturing hub in Africa, with a target of producing 70 per cent of the country’s essential medicines domestically.
The government also disclosed plans to deepen incentives for local pharmaceutical manufacturers and strengthen regulatory systems to enable Nigerian drug manufacturers expand into West Africa and the wider African market.
The Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment, Senator John Owan Enoh, represented by the Director of Chemical and Non-Pharmaceutical Industry, Mr John Okpe Oluwa, disclosed this at the 8th Nigeria Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Expo, NPME 2026, held at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos.
Enoh said the Federal Government was committed to moving Nigeria from an import-dependent market towards greater self-sufficiency under the Renewed Hope Agenda.
According to him, increasing domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity would not only strengthen Nigeria’s medicine security but also provide the foundation for the country to become a major exporter of pharmaceutical products across Africa through the African Continental Free Trade Area, AfCFTA.
He said: “The government is targeting 70 per cent domestic production of essential medicines while developing a resilient ecosystem capable of meeting the country’s medical needs.”
To achieve the target, the minister listed proposed interventions, including expanded tax exemptions, tariff waivers on raw materials and machinery, incentives for backward integration in the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and excipients, as well as dedicated pharmaceutical intervention funds.
He added that the government was working with regulatory agencies, including the Standards Organisation of Nigeria and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, to ensure that locally manufactured pharmaceutical products meet international standards and become more competitive in export markets.
The move comes as pharmaceutical manufacturers seek policy consistency and stronger investment support to enable them expand production, reduce dependence on imported medicines and compete in the African market.
The Chairman of the Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Group of the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, PMGMAN, Oluwatosin Jolayemi, said the Nigerian pharmaceutical manufacturing sector was undergoing significant transformation, noting that the group now represents more than 200 local pharmaceutical manufacturing companies.
Jolayemi, however, said the gains recorded by the industry must be protected through policy consistency and a predictable investment environment.
He identified high energy and production costs, supply-chain challenges, port inefficiencies, limited access to long-term capital and market-access constraints as some of the challenges limiting the industry’s growth.
He therefore appealed to the Federal Government to extend the Presidential Executive Order supporting local pharmaceutical manufacturing, whose current policy window is expected to expire in March 2027, by another two years.
According to him, the extension would enable manufacturers deepen investments, expand production capacity and consolidate gains made in medicine security.
Jolayemi said Nigeria’s ambition to become a regional pharmaceutical manufacturing hub must be anchored on a competitive, scalable and resilient domestic manufacturing ecosystem.
He called for coordinated action among government, regulators, manufacturers, financiers and development partners to address structural barriers and move the industry beyond domestic production towards a globally competitive and regionally integrated manufacturing ecosystem.
Earlier, the Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to expanding domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing as a pathway to medicine security, healthcare resilience and economic development.
Salako stressed the need to strengthen capacity across the pharmaceutical value chain, covering research and development, innovation, sourcing of active pharmaceutical ingredients and excipients, formulation, manufacturing and quality assurance.
He also called for increased investment in sophisticated areas of pharmaceutical production, including biologics, vaccines and other critical health technologies.
The minister urged stronger regional cooperation to address regulatory barriers limiting access to African markets.
The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, disclosed that 37 local manufacturing facilities were undergoing retrofitting and construction upgrades to meet international standards.
Adeyeye said NAFDAC had made significant progress towards WHO global benchmarking and strengthened regulatory enforcement against non-compliant facilities.
She said reforms under the 5+5 policy had contributed to reducing drug importation and encouraging local manufacturers to improve their standards.
She stressed that Nigeria could not afford to reverse the gains recorded in local pharmaceutical manufacturing and urged the country to intensify efforts towards the production of vaccines and other critical health commodities.
Also speaking, the Director-General of the African Medicines Agency, Dr Delese Mimi Darko, called for stronger regulatory cooperation among African countries to accelerate access to quality-assured medicines and create a more integrated pharmaceutical market.
Darko said the African Medicines Agency was established to strengthen and coordinate national regulatory systems rather than replace them.
She said regulatory harmonisation would enable manufacturers to navigate African markets more efficiently.
Darko also stressed the need for African manufacturers to invest in research and development, technology transfer, skilled manpower, intellectual property and quality systems, arguing that localisation must go beyond simply producing medicines locally.
In his welcome address, the Chairman of NPME 2026, Pharm. Dr Patrick Ajah, said no nation could achieve sustainable greatness without manufacturing what its citizens consume, describing the pharmaceutical sector as fundamental to national development.
Ajah recalled that Nigeria’s drug consumption had historically been skewed towards imports, with about 70 per cent of medicines imported and 30 per cent produced locally.
He, however, said public-private collaboration over the past two years had begun to shift the balance.
He called on stakeholders to partner with PMGMAN to drive sustainable growth, stressing that the expo had created opportunities for businesses to expand across Nigeria, Africa and the global market.
The Lagos State Government, represented by the Special Adviser on Health, Dr Kemi Ogunyemi, pledged continued support for the pharmaceutical manufacturing sector, particularly in addressing energy costs, infrastructure, long-term financing, skilled manpower and regulatory predictability.
The expo attracted representatives of the European Union, UNICEF, European Investment Bank, Bank of Industry, IFC/World Bank, NAFDAC, Pharmacy Council of Nigeria, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, as well as other industry and academic institutions.
One of the highlights of the expo was the Founders and Industry Leaders Session, which brought together leading figures in Nigeria’s pharmaceutical manufacturing industry, including Dr Stella Okoli of Emzor Pharmaceuticals, Dr Fidelis Ayebae of Fidson Plc, Dr Olakunle Ekundayo of Drugfield Pharmaceuticals and Elder Varkey Verghese of Jawal International Limited.
The session provided emerging pharmaceutical entrepreneurs with insights into leadership, investment, innovation, succession, manufacturing and the challenges of building sustainable pharmaceutical businesses in Africa.
PMGMAN also unveiled its Industry Self-Regulation Quality Plus, ISRQ+, Project, which includes a five-year Medicine Security Industry Advocacy Strategy for 2027–2031, an ISRQ+ laboratory and a Data Repository and Learning Centre.
The group said the initiative was designed to strengthen industry intelligence, quality capacity, evidence-based advocacy and continuous learning, with its various components expected to be commissioned progressively within the next six to 10 months.
As the 2026 edition came to a close, PMGMAN said its focus would shift towards translating progress recorded in domestic manufacturing into a stronger, more integrated and competitive regional pharmaceutical ecosystem.
The closing remarks, delivered by Pharm. Frank Muonemeh, emphasised the need for stakeholders to remain committed to closing Nigeria’s medicine access gap and advancing greater medicine security across Africa.
PMGMAN also announced plans for the 9th Nigeria Pharma Manufacturers Expo in 2028, while preparations continue towards the commissioning of the ISRQ+ project.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Governor Dauda Lawal declared that his administration’s rescue mission is transforming Zamfara State across critical sectors.
On Thursday, the governor began a series of events and project commissioning to mark Zamfara State’s 30th Anniversary.
The 30th Anniversary and commissioning were attended by the Pioneer Military Administrator of Zamfara State, Col. Jibril Bala Yakubu (Rtd.), former governors Ahmed Sani Yarima and Mahmud Aliyu Shinkafi, and other dignitaries.
During his speech at the National Independence Day parade and Zamfara’s 30th Anniversary at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, Governor Lawal said Zamfara has moved from despair to an era of clear execution, transparency, and sustainable development.
He said, “Today, we join Nigerians in celebrating Independence Day and mark three decades since Zamfara State was created on October 1, 1996. Alhamdulillah for Allah’s grace, mercy, and protection that have guided us through trials and triumphs, uniting us in a shared destiny.
“As we watched our gallant security forces, paramilitary agencies, vibrant students and youth march in unity on this parade ground, we were reminded of the resilience that defines the Nigerian spirit and, most specifically, the strength of character of our people.
“We must reflect intentionally on the profound sacrifices of our founding fathers, who fought tirelessly to break the chains of colonial rule and give birth to a free, sovereign nation. We owe them an eternal debt of gratitude for protecting this country’s unity, peace, and territorial integrity.
“As we look forward to the next decade, we must understand that true independence demands collective responsibility. Government alone can’t do this. I call on traditional rulers, religious scholars, civil servants, traders, and our resilient youth to unite. We must set aside divisions—ethnic, political, sectarian—and protect the peace we fought for.”
On Friday, Governor Lawal commissioned phase III of the renovated and modernised J.B. Yakubu Secretariat in Gusau as part of his effort to rebuild government institutions and create a modern, efficient, technology-enabled, results-oriented Public Service for Zamfara State.
The J.B. Yakubu Secretariat houses critical Ministries, Departments, and Agencies whose responsibilities span virtually every aspect of governance and service delivery.
Governor Lawal said modernising the Secretariat will deepen coordination among MDAs, strengthen communication, promote institutional synergy, and support faster, more effective implementation of government decisions.
“Today’s occasion is significant as we welcome His Excellency, Col. Jibril Bala Yakubu (Rtd.), Zamfara’s pioneer Military Administrator, after whom this Secretariat is named. As Zamfara marks thirty years since its creation, it’s fitting that a leader from our foundation is here to witness this milestone.”
Earlier, the pioneer Military Administrator of Zamfara State, Col. Jibril Bala Yakubu (Rtd.), lauded Governor Lawal’s giant strides, particularly in infrastructure, education, and health.
On the same Friday, His Eminence, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, CFR, mni, commissioned the reconstructed and remodelled Jumu’at Mosque (Yardole) and its attached shopping complex.
The mosque, named after Malam Sambo Dan Ashafa, a renowned Islamic scholar and companion of the great (MUJADDADI) and leader of the 1st Sokoto Jihad, Sheikh Uthman Ibn Fodiyo, will also serve as an Islamic and research learning centre.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Governor Uba Sani has granted clemency to 27 inmates in correctional facilities across Kaduna state, to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence anniversary, in an effort to give deserving innates opportunity to rebuild their lives.
A statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Malam Ahmed Maiyaki on Friday, stated that the latest clemency brings the number of beneficiaries to more than 500, since the Governor assumed office.
The Commissioner added the intervention included the release of eligible inmates as well as the payment of fines and compensation of over N300 million for victims since 2023.
The statement quoted state Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Sir James Kanyip, as saying that the latest exercise is part of the Governor’s practice of extending mercy to deserving inmates on national occasions.
According to the Chief Law Officer of Kaduna State, previous exercises were carried out on New Year day, during Democracy Day and Independence Day celebrations.
He said the prerogative of mercy was exercised through established processes, taking into consideration accountability, rehabilitation and the responsibilities that come with freedom.
Kanyip said the beneficiaries were expected to return to society with a renewed sense of responsibility and appreciation of their obligations to others.
The statement said the payment of fines and compensation is also intended to give the clemency a restorative justice dimension by addressing barriers to the release of deserving inmates while recognising the interests of victims.
It said the interventions were based on the belief that public safety, human dignity, rehabilitation and the possibility of redemption should form part of the administration of justice.
The statement added that clemency goes beyond freeing inmates from custody, as it also provides an opportunity for beneficiaries to reconnect with their families and communities.
The statement further said the administration would continue to support rehabilitation, reconciliation and the reintegration of deserving inmates into society.
According to the statement, the government remains committed to a justice system that protects society, respects victims’ interests and gives deserving individuals an opportunity to become responsible and productive members of their communities.

items.title: One feared dead in Aguleri, Umuoba Anam clash
items.summary:
By Vincent Ujumadu
AWKA — One person was feared dead and several others injured following a fresh communal clash between Amaeze Aguleri and Umuoba Anam communities in Anambra East Local Government Area of Anambra State.
Several buildings, including a microfinance bank in Aguleri, were reportedly set ablaze during the violence.

By Vincent Ujumadu
AWKA — One person was feared dead and several others injured following a fresh communal clash between Amaeze Aguleri and Umuoba Anam communities in Anambra East Local Government Area of Anambra State.
Several buildings, including a microfinance bank in Aguleri, were reportedly set ablaze during the violence.
The latest incident is believed to be linked to a longstanding land dispute between the two communities, which dates back to 1999 and had previously attracted the intervention of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo.
Accounts surrounding the dispute indicate that Amaeze Aguleri had decades ago given a portion of its land to Umuoba Anam on trust. The ownership of the disputed area later became a source of disagreement between the communities.
The Anambra State Police Command confirmed the death of one person and said it had deployed personnel to the affected communities to restore peace and maintain law and order.
The Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Oji Ama, led the state Deputy Governor, Dr Onyekachukwu Ibezim, other government officials, security agencies and community stakeholders on an on-the-spot assessment of the affected areas.
The visit was aimed at assessing the security situation, safeguarding lives and property and preventing further escalation of the conflict.
The delegation assessed the extent of the reported destruction and the impact of the violence on residents and the affected communities.
The stakeholders also reviewed immediate measures to restore peace and strengthen security, while exploring longer-term steps to prevent a recurrence.
During the assessment, Oji Ama reiterated the commitment of the Police Command to protecting lives and property and ensuring that residents could carry out their legitimate activities without fear.
He urged residents of Aguleri and Umuoba Anam to remain calm and refrain from actions capable of escalating the situation.
The police commissioner also appealed to residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing credible and timely information that could assist ongoing investigations and peace-building efforts.
Speaking during the visit, Deputy Governor Ibezim urged traditional rulers, community leaders, youth organisations, town unions and other stakeholders to work with the government and security agencies towards finding a lasting solution to the dispute.
He said security was a shared responsibility requiring the cooperation and commitment of all stakeholders.
The Police Command assured residents of Aguleri and Umuoba Anam that security measures were being strengthened in the affected areas to prevent further breaches of peace.
It added that efforts were ongoing to address the underlying issues through dialogue and other lawful channels.

items.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu
AWKA — The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) secured 1,370 convictions from 1,889 cases filed in court during the first half of 2026, the commission’s Executive Chairman, Ola Olukoyede, has said.
Olukoyede disclosed this on Thursday while speaking at the commissioning of the EFCC Awka Zonal Directorate Complex, which will serve Anambra and Imo states.
He said the commission also recovered ₦1,233,612,040,411.11, $684,478,457.32, £373,905.78 and €9,343,803.66 during the period, in addition to recoveries in other currencies.
Giving a broader account of the commission’s activities, Olukoyede said that between October 2023 and July 2026, the EFCC received 49,673 petitions, investigated 39,615 cases, filed 14,476 cases in court and secured 10,872 convictions.
He said the figures represented a conviction-to-filing ratio of 75.1 per cent.
According to him, the commission had introduced reforms aimed at improving its operations, including changes to its processes and procedures, which he said had contributed to its performance across various law-enforcement indicators.
On the new Awka directorate, Olukoyede said its establishment was part of the EFCC’s expansion programme, supported by appropriations from the National Assembly and interventions by the Federal Government.
He said Anambra and Imo required effective institutional presence because of their economic activities, describing the states as centres of enterprise, commerce and industry.
Olukoyede said the EFCC’s mandate went beyond arrests and prosecution to include prevention and coordination in the fight against economic and financial crimes.
“The EFCC exists not merely to arrest and prosecute. Our official mission encompasses prevention, enforcement and coordination in the effort to eradicate economic and financial crimes,” he said.
He said preventing financial crimes before they occurred could help reduce the economic and social costs associated with fraud and diversion of public resources.
“If we can identify vulnerabilities before billions of naira are lost, prevent fraudulent transactions before citizens lose their savings, strengthen procurement systems before public resources are diverted and interrupt criminal financial flows before they mature, then we would have saved the nation enormous economic and social costs,” he said.
The EFCC chairman said the Awka directorate would place emphasis on corruption prevention and engagement with government institutions, businesses, financial institutions, professional bodies, schools, markets, civil society organisations, traditional institutions, religious bodies and communities.
He urged members of the public to provide credible information about suspected economic and financial crimes, while cautioning against using whistleblowing to settle personal scores.
“Whistleblowing must become an act of responsible citizenship,” Olukoyede said.
“However, whistleblowing must be responsible and based on fact. It must not become an instrument for settling scores.”
He called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, town unions, market associations, professional bodies, youth and women’s groups, civil society organisations and the media to support efforts to prevent corruption.
Olukoyede also urged the new directorate to build sustained relationships with state and local governments, tertiary institutions, the organised private sector and community structures in Anambra and Imo.
Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, said the commissioning reflected the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen the capacity of anti-corruption agencies.
The President said his administration had, since assuming office, worked to improve the institutional capacity of anti-corruption agencies to carry out their mandates.
He said the Awka directorate would strengthen the EFCC’s presence in Anambra and Imo, particularly in major commercial and industrial centres.
“From the industrial towns of Onitsha and Nnewi, to the oil and gas town of Egbema and the rapidly growing economic city of Owerri, Imo State, the presence of EFCC will improve the ease of doing business,” Tinubu said.
He said the government would continue to provide an enabling environment for anti-corruption agencies to carry out their responsibilities.
Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, assured the commission of the state government’s cooperation in carrying out its duties.
Soludo said reducing financial crimes was in the interest of the state and expressed satisfaction that Anambra would host the regional directorate.
“Some people might be asking why we’re so excited about having the zonal office in our state. The reason for our excitement is that it will enhance quicker investigation,” he said.
The governor, however, observed that the EFCC’s staffing capacity made it difficult for the commission to establish offices in every local government area.
“Ideally, EFCC should have offices in the 774 local government areas of the country, but with only about 6,000 staff, it is difficult to have offices in all LGAs,” he said.
Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma, commended the EFCC for bringing its services closer to residents of the two states.
Uzodinma also appealed to the commission to establish a dedicated state office in Imo to enhance its coverage and operations in the state.

items.content:
Demands review of long-distance NYSC postings
By Adeola Badru
IBADAN — The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Southwest Zone D, has raised concern over alleged ransom demands of up to ₦50 million for some prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members abducted while travelling from Ibadan to their orientation camps.
The association also called on the Federal Government to review compulsory long-distance postings and introduce safer deployment and transportation arrangements for prospective corps members.
The demand followed the attack on two buses conveying prospective corps members and other passengers along the Owerri-Onitsha Road near Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State.
The Imo State Police Command confirmed that the buses were travelling from Ibadan to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, and Bende, Abia State, when they were attacked by suspected armed men.
The police said 10 victims were rescued and both buses recovered, while the exact number of persons abducted was still being verified as security agencies continued search-and-rescue operations.
In a statement jointly signed on Friday by NANS Southwest Zone D Coordinator, Adeyemo Josiah; General Secretary, Ojetola Babatunde; and Public Relations Officer, Olugbemi Timothy, the association described the incident as a serious security concern requiring urgent government action.
NANS said information available to its leadership indicated that graduates from institutions in the South-West, including the Federal Polytechnic, Ede, and Osun State Polytechnic, Iree, were among those affected.
The association expressed concern that the victims were travelling to comply with the compulsory national service programme, arguing that the government should take greater responsibility for the safety of graduates required to travel long distances for the programme.
“A country cannot summon its youths and abandon their security,” the association said.
On the alleged ransom demands, NANS said it had received reports and seen fundraising appeals suggesting that as much as ₦50 million was being demanded for each victim.
It, however, urged security agencies and NYSC authorities to verify the reports and establish direct communication with the affected families before any conclusion was reached on the amounts allegedly being demanded.
“If confirmed, it would be completely unacceptable for families whose children were kidnapped while travelling for national service to be left to crowd-fund tens of millions of naira to secure their freedom,” the association said.
NANS also called for the immediate implementation of the risk-sensitive deployment framework approved by the Federal Executive Council in June 2026 as part of comprehensive reforms of the NYSC.
The reforms approved by the FEC include a technology-driven call-up process, risk-sensitive deployment to improve the safety of corps members, a redesigned six-week orientation programme, skills-based primary assignments and improved orientation camp standards.
The association argued that the latest incident underscored the need to move from policy approval to practical implementation of the safety measures.
It also called for a review of compulsory long-distance interstate deployment and proposed state-based or zonal service options, particularly where security conditions make interstate travel difficult.
“Until Nigeria’s security situation substantially improves, the Federal Government must seriously consider state-based and zonal service options, while making long-distance interstate deployment voluntary where circumstances justify it,” NANS said.
“National integration remains important, but patriotism should never require a graduate to gamble with his or her life.”
The students’ body further demanded organised and secured transportation arrangements for prospective corps members travelling to orientation camps.
It proposed the use of accredited transport operators, designated travel corridors, vehicle-tracking systems and closer coordination between NYSC and security agencies during mobilisation periods.
NANS also urged the authorities to review deployments to remote and high-risk communities and establish stronger emergency-response mechanisms for corps members serving across the country.
The association disclosed that its Southwest leadership was reviewing more than 500 complaints and reports from students and graduates concerning the NYSC process.
According to NANS, the complaints cover issues including delayed mobilisation, omissions from Senate and Academic Board lists, Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) and institutional-record challenges, accreditation issues, registration and call-up difficulties, relocation, transportation, accommodation and reports concerning conditions in some orientation camps.
It said the latest abduction had added an urgent security dimension to the administrative and welfare concerns surrounding the NYSC scheme.
NANS called on the Federal Government, the Federal Ministry of Youth Development, NYSC management and security agencies to intensify rescue efforts until all remaining abducted persons were safely recovered.
It also demanded verification of the reported ransom claims, direct official liaison with affected families and implementation of the approved risk-sensitive deployment framework.
Other demands included a review of compulsory interstate deployment, consideration of state-based and zonal service options where necessary, secured transportation for prospective corps members and attention to outstanding mobilisation and welfare complaints.
The association urged the Ministry of Youth Development, NYSC management and student representatives to convene an engagement on the security and welfare of prospective and serving corps members.
Appealing to President Bola Tinubu, NANS called for urgent intervention in the incident, saying the government should ensure the safe recovery of the victims and take steps to prevent similar incidents.
“When young Nigerians answering a compulsory Federal Government call are abducted on their way to orientation camp, while their families reportedly begin searching for enormous sums of money for their release, government cannot afford silence or delayed intervention,” it said.
The association said the incident had generated anxiety among students, graduates and affected families, urging the government to provide clear updates on rescue efforts.
NANS clarified, however, that while its Southwest leadership was responsible for raising concerns and escalating issues through the appropriate structures, any broader national decision or course of action remained the responsibility of the national leadership of the association.
Reiterating its call for a comprehensive review of the NYSC scheme, the association said the security, economic and technological circumstances facing Nigerian graduates had changed considerably since the programme was established in 1973.
“Nigeria in 2026 is not Nigeria in 1973 when NYSC was established. The country’s security realities, economy, technology and circumstances confronting graduates have changed, and NYSC must evolve accordingly,” it said.
“We will not accept kidnapping as an unavoidable price of national service. We will not accept preventable danger as patriotism, and we will not normalise administrative hardship simply because the scheme has existed for decades.”
The association expressed solidarity with the families of the affected prospective corps members and urged security agencies to sustain search-and-rescue operations until all victims were reunited with their families.
“National service must never become national endangerment,” NANS said.
The post Abducted Corps Members: NANS raises alarm over ₦50m ransom appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Adeola Badru
IBADAN — More than 250 members and chieftains of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party have defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The defectors were received by the Oyo State leadership of the APC, led by its chairman and former Deputy Governor, Moses Alake Adeyemo, during a reception held at Watershed, Old Ife Road, Ibadan, on Friday.
Addressing the new members, Adeyemo assured them of full integration into the party, saying they would not be discriminated against or denied equal participation in the affairs of the party.
He said the APC was gaining support in the state amid what he described as dissatisfaction with the administration of the state government, adding that the party was positioned to provide an alternative in the 2027 election.
According to him, “The people of Oyo State are tired of the maladministration of the APM, hence their desire for a change.”
“APC remains the only party that can produce the required change in 2027. You have made the right decision. I am assuring you that you will not regret your action.”
Also speaking, the APC governorship candidate, Sharafadeen Alli, outlined some of the policies he said his administration would pursue if elected governor in 2027.
Alli said his proposed administration would prioritise education and healthcare, as well as review the state’s security architecture to address kidnapping, banditry and other security challenges.
He said, “Our government will revamp the education, health and other sectors of the economy.
“We are going to rejig the security architecture to bring an end to the reported cases of kidnapping, banditry and other vices in the past seven and half years.
“There will also be a civil service reform with the training and retraining of workers.
“Also, our administration will revisit the issue of the Circular Road that has left thousands of people homeless.
“The local government autonomy will be the topmost priority of our administration.”
Alli also pledged to pursue civil service reforms through continuous training and retraining of workers and review issues surrounding the Circular Road project.
He identified local government autonomy as another priority of his proposed administration.
Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Hon. Olamiposi Ojo, popularly known as Bibire Forum, who led members from Accord, said their decision to join the APC was based on what he described as the party’s commitment to internal democracy.
Ojo also cited the leadership of President Bola Tinubu and what he described as the President’s impact on the country as factors behind their decision.
He said, “Our decision is based on the leadership quality of President Bola Tinubu and the way he has been able to transform the country.”
Similarly, Taoheed Ademola Lucky described the defection as a “homecoming” and expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects ahead of the 2027 elections.
He pledged that his supporters would mobilise and work for the success of the APC at both the state and federal levels in the forthcoming elections.

items.content:
By Femi Bolaji
JALINGO — The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University (TSU) chapter, has rejected the constitution of a fresh committee by the Taraba State Government to review staff remuneration and workforce in tertiary institutions.
The union described the move as unnecessary and capable of further delaying the implementation of an agreed salary structure for university workers.
ASUU-TSU Branch Chairperson, Comrade Garba Mbave Joshua, stated the union’s position on Friday, October 2, 2026, at a press conference held at the union’s secretariat in Jalingo.
Mbave said the government’s decision to constitute another committee was coming after several verification, consultation, financial computation and reporting processes had already been concluded by government and union representatives.
He said the union had been negotiating the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government of Nigeria/ASUU Agreement with the state government since February 2026.
According to him, TSU remained the only university in the 19 northern states yet to implement the agreed remuneration framework.
Mbave said a government-backed verification team had earlier visited tertiary institutions across the six North-East states and submitted its report on September 22.
He said the report established that neighbouring states had implemented the agreed salary table without variations.
Following the verification exercise, he said, a tripartite committee comprising relevant stakeholders was constituted to determine the financial implications and accumulated arrears.
The committee, according to him, submitted its final report to the Ministry of Tertiary Education on September 24.
Mbave said the government, during a meeting on September 24, appealed to the union to suspend the industrial action it had contemplated following the expiration of its ultimatum.
He said the appeal was reinforced by a formal request from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service for an additional two weeks to resolve the outstanding issues.
According to him, the union subsequently convened its members on September 29 and agreed to grant the government the additional time requested in the interest of industrial harmony.
“Notwithstanding the frustration and legitimate disappointment expressed by our members, Congress, acting in good faith and in the prevailing interest of industrial harmony, nevertheless acceded to the Government’s request and resolved to grant the Government the additional time sought,” he said.
Mbave said TSU was among the institutions that had obtained approval to embark on industrial action but remained the only one that did not do so because the union decided to honour the government’s appeal for more time.
He, however, said the constitution of another review committee had raised concerns among members because it followed processes that the union considered already concluded.
“The constitution of yet another review committee, following the conclusion of the verification, consultation, negotiation, financial computation and reporting processes, gives rise to a legitimate and serious concern that the process is being subjected to further avoidable and unjustifiable delay,” he said.
The union chairman said members viewed the latest development as potentially frustrating the implementation of the agreed remuneration framework.
He reiterated that, to the best of the union’s knowledge, TSU remained the only university within the 19 northern states yet to implement the remuneration framework arising from the 2025 Federal Government/ASUU Agreement.
ASUU-TSU therefore called on the state government to proceed with implementation of the agreed remuneration framework, settle accumulated arrears and give effect to the outcomes of the verification and tripartite processes already concluded.
The union also urged the government to honour the assurances and commitments it made when requesting additional time to resolve the matter.

items.content:
Opens anniversary with community-driven projects
By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha
ASABA — The Asagba of Asaba, His Royal Majesty, Prof. Epiphany Chigbogu Azinge, SAN, has said his two years on the throne have marked a shift from traditional rulership to a broader model of traditional governance focused on the welfare and development of the Asaba people.
Azinge spoke on Monday as activities marking his second coronation anniversary began in Asaba, Delta State, with the unveiling and commissioning of several community-driven projects, including a smart nursery and primary school donated to the Delta State Government.
Reflecting on his tenure, the monarch said he felt fulfilled by the support and participation of the Asaba community, stressing that leadership could not succeed without the active involvement of the people.
“Leadership without followership is as good as dead. I draw a lot of strength and inspiration from the teeming number of Asaba people who have graciously donated their time, talent and treasure to whatever we have been doing,” he said.
Azinge said his administration had deliberately expanded its focus beyond customs and traditions to address issues affecting the everyday lives of the people.
“Like I’ve told many who care to listen, I’ve long migrated from being a traditional ruler, and I’m now into traditional governance.
“Hence, I’m not only trying to think about the customs and traditions of our people; I’m also thinking about the welfare, healthcare, education, among so many other things, to make sure that my people are happy,” he said.
Community donates smart school
A major highlight of the anniversary was the commissioning and handover of the Smart Nursery and Primary School built by the Asaba community and donated to the Delta State Government.
Azinge described the project as a demonstration of community participation in education and a commitment to complementing government efforts.
He said the project was particularly significant because the community had not only built the school but decided to hand it over to the state government for use.
“I believe in the history of Delta State, and I dare say in the history of Nigeria, today is the first time that a community will come together, not just to build a smart school, but also to have it donated to the state government,” he said.
According to him, the project was initially funded through the community’s welfare fund before additional resources were mobilised to complete it.
He commended the project supervisor for helping to mobilise additional funds after the community had exhausted its initial resources.
Azinge also highlighted the facilities provided at the school, saying the community paid particular attention to the quality and suitability of the furniture.
He said some of the specially designed chairs and tables cost about N100,000 each, with more than 80 units expected to be available for the school.
However, while handing over the facility, the monarch appealed to the Delta State Government to provide an access road to the school.
“If Asaba can donate a school to you, please donate a road to us so that we can achieve this. Donate a road so that people can access this place easily and then be able to school here,” he said.
Delta lauds community partnership
Representing the state government, the Commissioner for Primary Education, Chief (Mrs) Rose Ezewu, commended the Asaba community for the initiative.
Ezewu described the project as an example of community participation and partnership in advancing education.
“This occasion is significant not merely because we are unveiling a new school facility, but because we are witnessing the power of community vision, responsible leadership and purposeful partnership in advancing the cause of education,” she said.
The commissioner said the government recognised that it could not meet every educational need alone and required collaboration with communities, traditional institutions, parents and other stakeholders.
She assured the Asagba and the people of Asaba that the facility would be integrated into the state’s basic education system and managed in line with the educational needs of the pupils.
More projects unveiled
Other projects unveiled during the anniversary activities included a community cemetery, the beautification of Ogbeke Square, upgrading of Kanebisi Roundabout, formerly known as Traffic Light Junction, facilitated by Providus Bank, and a 1,000-capacity event centre at the permanent Asaba Palace grounds.
Azinge said the projects formed part of a broader development vision for Asaba, adding that more projects were in the pipeline.
“This is just a tip of the iceberg. I know that going forward, like I’ve promised, we are going to return here, and it’s going to be a totally new, transformed Ogbe-Ogo with all that everybody can think about,” he said.
The monarch also announced plans to end burial activities within the community, saying a final proclamation would be made by December after further consultations with the Asaba-in-Council.
Azinge said the anniversary was ultimately an opportunity to celebrate the collective spirit and unity of the Asaba people.
“The support, the commonality of the things we do in Asaba is something that excites me, because once we voice it out, every other person supports, and that is not something that I want us to take for granted,” he said.

items.content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki
ABAKALIKI — Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, has said his administration is working with the management of the state university to resolve the dispute over the payment of pensions and gratuities owed some retired workers of the institution.
Nwifuru spoke while responding to an appeal by more than 200 retirees who sought his intervention over the non-payment of their retirement benefits.
The governor explained that the responsibility for employing workers of the university rested with the institution’s management, rather than directly with the state government, adding that the existing legal framework did not automatically make the state responsible for their retirement benefits.
According to him, the key issue was determining the appropriate authority responsible for the payment of the affected workers’ pensions and gratuities.
“The problem now is who actually is responsible for the payment of the pensions and gratuities of these people, since the government of Ebonyi is not the one employing them. They are not the ones hiring,” he said.
Nwifuru said the state could not automatically assume responsibility for workers it did not employ, stressing that employment and termination responsibilities were linked.
“The law is very clear. You cannot fire who you did not hire. That’s the problem that they are facing,” he said.
The governor, however, said his administration had reached an understanding with the university management to accommodate the affected retirees and explore ways of addressing their concerns.
“We have gotten to a point that we agreed with the management of the university. We agreed that what we should do is accommodate these people that are already crying,” he said.
Nwifuru further explained that universities operated under different financial and administrative structures, with responsibility for workers’ pensions depending on the status and management structure of the institution.
“If they are being run by government, it is the responsibility of government; their staff are staff of that state government. But if they are not being run by government, then you cannot say that the government should also pay,” he stated.
He said the university management was working with relevant authorities to resolve the matter and develop a workable arrangement for the affected retirees.
On infrastructure development, Nwifuru said work was progressing at the ICT University despite the state’s limited resources.
The governor said his administration had deliberately reduced spending on elaborate project commissioning ceremonies and publicity, arguing that scarce public resources could be redirected to infrastructure development.
“We are not spending much money in order to commission projects. We have small resources, so the money we would spend on television houses, media houses and social media for commissioning projects can be used to do one kilometre of road,” he said.
Nwifuru also disclosed that President Bola Tinubu would commission projects at the ICT University, including the Senate building, during his planned visit to Ebonyi State.
“We have Mr President. Anytime Mr President is coming here, he will commission that project,” he said, adding that another project would also be commissioned during the visit without disclosing details.

By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo
OSOGBO — Two suspected members of a cult group were reportedly killed during a suspected cult clash in Osogbo, Osun State capital, on Friday evening.
The incident occurred at a lounge around Owoeba, in the Owode-Ilesa Garage area of the city, causing panic among residents and forcing some business owners to shut their shops.
Sources said a rival group stormed the lounge where one Adebayo Taoreed, popularly known as Small Rugged, and other persons were relaxing and opened fire.
Taoreed was said to have been linked to the Eiye cult group, although the claim could not be independently verified.
Another person, identified only as OSHA, was also reportedly killed, while four others sustained gunshot injuries.
The shooting triggered panic along the Ilesa Garage-Ayepe axis as gunmen allegedly fired sporadically while fleeing the scene.
Some residents and traders reportedly ran for safety, while business owners hurriedly closed their shops to avoid being caught in the violence.
Confirming the incident, the Osun State Police Command spokesperson, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, said the command was aware of the shooting, which he described as a suspected cult clash.
Ojelabi said two persons were killed at the scene, identifying one of them as Small Rugged, while the identity of the second victim had yet to be established.
According to him, four other persons sustained gunshot injuries and were taken by the police to a nearby hospital for treatment.
“The command is aware of a shooting incident suspected to be cult clash around Owoeba area, Osogbo.
“Two persons died at the spot, one identified as Small Rugged, while the other’s name is yet unknown.
“Four other people sustained gunshot injuries and have been rushed by the police to a nearby hospital for treatment,” he said.
The police spokesperson added that the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, had directed tactical teams to apprehend those responsible for the shooting.
Meanwhile, claims linking Taoreed to alleged thuggery and political violence during the 2026 Osun State governorship electioneering could not be independently verified.
The police had not announced any arrest in connection with the incident as of the time of filing this report.

items.content: U.S. stocks finished higher on Friday after a weaker-than-expected jobs report reduced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its meeting later this month.The S&P 500 rose 0.76% to 7,724.38. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.19% to 27,191.33, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.51% to 51,186.71.Nonfarm payrolls rose by 29,000 last month, the Labor Department reported, well below economists’ forecast of 90,000. Employment figures for the previous two months were also revised sharply lower.Following the report, traders priced in a 22.7% chance of a rate increase of at least a quarter-point at the Fed’s late-October meeting, down from 24.4% on Thursday and 64.2% a week earlier, according to CME FedWatch.“Cautious optimism is kind of where people are,” said Robert Bernstone, head of trading at SummitTX Capital. The data eased near-term rate concerns, he said, though investors remain wary about the economy and inflation.Rate-sensitive shares advanced as investors reassessed the likelihood of another Fed increase. The S&P 500 real estate index rose about 1%, while the small-cap Russell 2000 also gained roughly 1%, its strongest daily performance in a month.Nvidia and Tesla were among the biggest contributors to the S&P 500’s advance. Tesla’s rise helped lift the consumer discretionary sector by about 1%, making it the best-performing of the 11 major S&P sectors.Recent economic data pointing to resilient activity and slower price increases, along with cautionary comments from two senior policymakers, had already led investors to scale back rate-hike bets this week.Despite Friday’s gains, the Dow and S&P 500 each recorded a fourth weekly decline in the past five weeks. The Nasdaq, however, ended higher for the week—its fifth weekly gain in six.Nike shares fell after the sportswear maker forecast a sharp annual revenue decline, citing weakness in China. The company also announced job cuts and plans to reorganize its global business divisions.Data-storage stocks also dropped. Western Digital and Seagate Technology were among the weakest performers in the S&P 500 technology index after Nikkei reported that Toshiba plans to double production capacity for hard drives used in AI data centers by fiscal 2027.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The 277th Corps Commanders' Conference forum underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any attempt to cause agitation or create a May 9-like situation, "on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination", the military's media wing said on Friday.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir presided over the 277th Corps Commanders' Conference at General Headquarters, Rawalpindi.
The forum reviewed the prevailing security environment and resolved to maintain a high state of readiness, ISPR said.
The statement further added that it affirmed Pakistan's right to self-defence and targeted action against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, stressing that "only the Taliban delusional leadership, facilitating terrorism on behalf of India, bears responsibility for its consequences".
"The forum appreciated sustained successful intelligence-based counter-terrorism operations by law enforcement agencies, however, emphasised complementing these kinetic efforts with non-kinetic measures, including people-centric governance at grassroot level, strategic engagement with public, dismantling of terror-crime nexus operating under patronage of vested interests and police capacity building, in line with the National Action Plan and Vision Azm-e-Istehkam," ISPR said.
The forum welcomed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, noting its contribution to longstanding strategic and collective defence ties, the statement added.
"It strongly resented Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, expressed solidarity with the Kingdom and affirmed Pakistan's commitment to the security and sanctity of the Haramain Sharifain," ISPR stated.
The forum also reiterated Pakistan's principled position on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK) and support for resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people, it added.
"The forum offered fateha for the Shuhada of the Armed Forces, Law Enforcement Agencies and civil society who laid down their lives for the motherland and paid rich tribute to their supreme sacrifices," ISPR said.
According to the statement, in his concluding remarks, CDF Munir commended the formations for their operational preparedness and professionalism. "He directed commanders to continue to strengthen intelligence-based operations and enhance combat capabilities through absorption of modern technology, training and multi-domain integration".
The field marshal expressed confidence that the Armed Forces, with unwavering support of the nation, remain fully prepared to safeguard Pakistan's sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security, the statement concluded.

items.author: Rameez Khan
items.content:
The country held its breath on Friday, as the government and the opposition were set to resume talks on Saturday (today) after failing to bridge major differences in a first round aimed at averting a planned Oct. 4 long march by the Pakistan Tehrik-e-Insaf (PTI).
The meeting, chaired by NA Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq in his chamber, included representatives of the government, Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and the opposition.
The negotiations come amid continued tensions following PTI's announcement of an Islamabad march. Although the protest was postponed from September 27 to October 4, the standoff between the federal and provincial governments remains unresolved.
According to the NA spokesperson, detailed discussions were held on the country's political situation, with the government, PPP and opposition apprising each other of their respective positions. Various matters were discussed in detail and with patience, the spokesperson said.
The second round of negotiations will be held at 2pm on Saturday in the speaker's chamber, the spokesperson added. The government and PPP stressed the need to resolve national issues with the opposition through negotiations.
According to the statement, the NA Speaker played a key role in facilitating negotiations between the government, PPP and the opposition.
Federal minister Amir Muqam, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political and Public Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry attended the meeting. Senator Sherry Rehman and NA members Naveed Qamar and Ijaz Hussain Jakhrani also participated.
Opposition leaders including PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Malik Amir Dogar and former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, as well as Salman Akram Raja, attended the meeting.
The delegations were welcomed by Speaker Sadiq upon their arrival. "I am only playing the role of a mediator," he said.
Sadiq said his office was "always open" to resolving issues through negotiations and that he had consistently invited the opposition to engage in dialogue. He maintained that negotiations were the only way to resolve differences and issues, adding that positions and offices were temporary.
"Parliament is the only forum where solutions to issues can be found," he said.
In an earlier post on X, the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan said the opposition side was being led by the leader of the opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas.
According to sources, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi opened the talks by raising concerns over the law-and-order situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, including the performance of the provincial government and Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.
Naqvi blamed the provincial government for the security situation and recent attacks by the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
Senate opposition leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas rejected the government's position, saying the opposition had come to discuss political issues, not terrorism, and that linking the two would not resolve the dispute.
Nasir Abbas also raised the arrests of lawmakers and restrictions on meetings with Pakistan Tehrik-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan. According to sources, he said the PTI leadership could not take major political decisions without consulting Khan.
He said a meeting between Mahmood Khan Achakzai and himself and Khan could help open a path toward resolving the political dispute. Pakistan Peoples Party leader Sherry Rehman asked whether such a meeting would guarantee a resolution.
Nasir Abbas said the opposition would take responsibility and that the situation would improve if a meeting with Khan took place.
The government team, meanwhile, made clear that it would not allow any advance on Islamabad. It said calls for a long march, threats or an attack on Adiala jail were unacceptable, adding that flexibility would be required from the opposition as well.
Tensions rose several times during the talks, according to sources. Rana Sanaullah and Nasir Abbas exchanged heated remarks over judicial matters.
Nasir Abbas voiced concerns over what he described as incomplete implementation of court orders and restrictions on meetings with Khan. Sanaullah responded that the courts were carrying out their functions and that court orders relating to any long march would be enforced.
National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq urged both sides to exercise restraint and seek a way forward through dialogue.
Speaking to the media after the meeting, PPP's Rehman said the party believed in resolving issues through negotiations.
She said that PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had stated the party's stance on the long march and that the PTI had to call it off "unconditionally".
"They will have to call it off rather than postponing or deferring," she said.
"Both parties have time; we will meet tomorrow. We will try to conclude this by tomorrow," she stated.
Talking about the opposition's reported demand of facilitating a meeting with incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, she said she could not answer the question. However, she said the opposition had asked for time and "we should respect it".
"A political and democratic attitude requires sitting at the negotiation table and resolving the issues through dialogue," she stated.
Meanwhile, the PTI rejected reports that negotiations between the government and the opposition in Islamabad were conditional on the party calling off its planned long march as sources familiar with the meeting said the two issues were discussed on parallel tracks.
The sources expressed frustration over "factually incorrect accounts of the talks", particularly the claim that the government had made cancellation of the protest a condition for continuing the dialogue.
They said the government had asked PTI to call off the protest and had repeated its publicly stated position during the meeting, but maintained that the demand was not presented as a precondition for negotiations.
According to the sources, PTI's position was that the dialogue should address the root causes that had led to the proposed protest. They said the party had conveyed its willingness to work with the government if there was seriousness about addressing those issues, but rejected the imposition of conditions before the dialogue could produce an understanding.
The sources said the government's stance on calling off the protest was already publicly known and had also been voiced during the meeting. However, they stressed that the dialogue and the long march were being pursued on parallel tracks rather than one being made conditional on the other.
They also said participants had agreed to exercise discretion over matters discussed during the Islamabad meeting and that the only position to be formally communicated to the media would be through a joint statement once it had been finalised.
The sources expressed particular frustration over "inaccurate accounts" subsequently given to the media, specifically disputing a version attributed to Pakistan Peoples Party leader Sherry Rehman regarding the status of the long march.
They said the account that PTI had agreed, or had been asked as a condition of dialogue, to call off the protest did not accurately reflect what was discussed during the meeting.
TTAP spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain said the alliance had lodged a protest over a breach of the understanding regarding discretion on the proceedings, specifically over remarks attributed to Sherry Rehman.
He also maintained that the dialogue had not been made conditional on calling off the march.
It was later revealed that Sherry had sought to clarify her position to TTAP leaders, saying she had only reiterated her party's position on the issue and had not made a specific demand during the meeting.
According to the sources, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi led much of the meeting, with his concerns focused primarily on security and administrative affairs in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Asked whether governor's rule was discussed, the sources said it was among the issues raised during the meeting, but maintained that Naqvi's broader focus was on the security situation and administration of the province.
The sources said the government's concerns were repeatedly framed around the failure of the provincial administration to ensure peace, security and tranquillity in K-P.
According to them, the same narrative that had been advanced publicly before the meeting was reflected in the government's position during the talks.
The PTI side, however, rejected that assessment and questioned the government's suggestion that the provincial authorities were protecting or harbouring non-state actors.
The sources said PTI responded to Naqvi by arguing that if a government could not even protect its own ministers in a province it governed, it could hardly be accused of protecting non-state actors.
They said the PTI side maintained that the approach being taken towards K-P was misplaced and did not adequately reflect the situation on the ground.
However, according to the sources, PTI made clear that negotiations could not proceed on the basis of conditions imposed before the dialogue itself had produced an understanding.
The sources also expressed surprise over the PPP's position during the meeting, saying the party appeared to have blindly supported the government's stance while disregarding long-held positions for power politics.
According to the sources, PTI also raised the issue of Imran Khan's sisters with PPP leader Sherry Rehman and asked her to take up his issue as well. The comment was met with silence.

items.author: Kamran Yousaf
items.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye have agreed to convene an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh next week as the alliance confronts escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and a growing diplomatic push to contain the crisis.
At a news conference, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday that the meeting would assess the "ground reality" and discuss the situation facing Saudi Arabia, particularly following attacks on civilian and economic infrastructure and the recent strike on a power facility in Madinah.
The development marks the latest step in the rapid institutionalisation of the three-way defence arrangement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye on August 7, under which an armed attack against one member is to be treated as an attack against all three.
The emergency SPDC meeting comes less than two weeks after the three foreign ministers met on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on September 24. Dar, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan discussed the implementation of the agreement and agreed to convene an urgent meeting of the three countries' military chiefs.
The military chiefs subsequently met in Riyadh on September 25, reviewing threats facing Saudi Arabia and discussing intelligence sharing, military coordination and greater integration of defence capabilities. They reaffirmed their commitment to collective defence and to translating the Makkah agreement into practical military cooperation.
The alliance's political and military response has gained urgency following a series of attacks attributed by Saudi Arabia to Yemen's Houthis, including an attack on a power distribution station in Madinah.
Pakistan on Friday strongly condemned the attack and reaffirmed its support for Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and the security of the Two Holy Mosques.
The Houthis have denied responsibility for the Madinah attack.
Dar also disclosed a new diplomatic dimension to the crisis, saying Iran was distancing itself from the Houthis and Iraqi armed groups.
According to Dar, he had discussed the issue with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who suggested that the groups should be engaged politically rather than targeted militarily.
Dar said Araghchi had conveyed that Iran wanted the matter resolved, while Pakistan had made clear that it was now part of a defence agreement and, "as Muslims", would honour its commitments.
The Iranian proposal, however, does not amount to a formal offer at this stage. Dar described it as an exchange of views between the two foreign ministers and said the question of whether political engagement could replace military action would be considered by the SPDC.
The issue is likely to add another layer to Pakistan's already delicate balancing act between its commitments to Saudi Arabia under the new defence pact and its longstanding policy of maintaining dialogue with neighbouring Iran.
Pakistan has repeatedly advocated diplomacy and de-escalation even as it has publicly condemned attacks on Saudi territory. Dar spoke with Araghchi on September 19, with the two ministers discussing regional developments, energy supplies and the safe passage of shipping.
The emergency meeting will also come as the alliance moves towards establishing a permanent institutional structure.
The first SPDC meeting was held in Istanbul on August 31, bringing together the foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs of the three countries. The meeting agreed to establish a permanent secretariat in Saudi Arabia, initially headed by a Pakistani secretary general for three years.
The agreement also envisages defence-industry cooperation, joint technology development and production.
Retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood was subsequently appointed as the first secretary general, with the secretariat to be established in Riyadh.
Dar told reporters that more than six countries had expressed interest in joining the Makkah agreement. However, he indicated that membership would not be considered until the alliance's secretariat and institutional mechanisms were fully operational.
He also stressed that the agreement was defensive in nature and contained no offensive objective, while allowing other countries to join. The document itself, he said, is open to other countries provided they agree to the principles laid down by its three founders.
He added that any decision on membership would be taken jointly by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, and Pakistan could not decide alone.
He said the prime minister also highlighted terrorism emanating from Afghanistan and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and credited Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of Defence Forces, for his role in the US-Iran mediation process.
Dar said the country had played a full role in strengthening multilateralism during the United Nations Security Council presidency as a resolution Pakistan moved on multilateralism and peaceful settlement of disputes last year, was adopted unanimously for the first time in 12 years, he said.
On the US-Iran talks, he said that Pakistan had brought the two sides to one table for the first time in 47 years, with six sessions over 21 hours. This led to a signing on June 18.
On the energy crisis stemming from Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb, he said the prime minister had flagged its impact on supply chains and prices, which had almost doubled in Pakistan. Despite financial constraints and the IMF programme, he said, the government approved a fuel relief scheme, now benefiting millions, for two-wheelers, three-wheelers and small four-wheelers of up to 800cc.
Answering a question about the Middle East, he said conflict was not a solution to anything. Even after the world wars, he noted, the warring countries had to sit down and build institutions.
Replying to a question, Dar said Pakistan's stance on Kashmir was "absolutely clear". The Kashmiri people, he said, must decide their future through a plebiscite under UN Security Council resolutions. India's actions of August 5, 2019, he added, must be reversed and no demographic change should be allowed in occupied Kashmir.
He said after the Pahalgam incident, Pakistan was blamed at once, and India then used the resulting sentiment to take its next steps.
This time, he said, the Foreign Office did not let India's narrative take hold internationally and that Pakistan had offered an independent, neutral investigation without delay. When India claimed strikes at 15 places and the downing of F-16s, Pakistan challenged the claims and asked India to say how many aircraft had fallen. India, he said, lost its own credibility.
On the Indus Waters Treaty, he said India's decision to hold it in abeyance was not accepted by Pakistan. The national security leadership and the civil-military leadership, he said, had resolved not to give up "even a drop" of Pakistan's water, which he described as a trust of 250 million people.
DPM Dar said he attended a meeting of the Arab-Islamic group of eight countries on Gaza, hosted by Egypt. He also attended the regional four-nation meeting of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Egypt, and a UN Security Council briefing on artificial intelligence. He attended OIC Contact Group meetings on Jammu and Kashmir and on Afghanistan, which he said Pakistan had pushed to be held regularly.

The three injured victims were rescued from the wrecked vehicle with the assistance of Good Samaritans and taken to Duck-Yard Hospital within the Military Zone for emergency medical treatment.

items.content: Federal Reserve officials have gone quite a long way to offer strong signals into possible direction of interest rates despite chairman Kevin Warsh's strong reluctance to give any guidance whatsoever, and that has helped traders reassess their positions on the rate decision, according to a Bloomberg report.Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams have in recent days suggested that policymakers believe the central bank has time to assess the economy before considering another increase.The remarks do not mean the Fed has ruled out further policy tightening, Bloomberg reported. Officials continue to warn that inflation remains too high, while consumer price data due on October 14 could play a major role in determining the next policy move.Ellen Meade, an economics professor at Duke University who advised Fed officials during a decades-long career at the Board of Governors, told Bloomberg the speeches by Jefferson and Williams did not necessarily amount to traditional forward guidance.“This is the Fed behaving like the Fed,” said Meade. “But I think there’s a difference between forward guidance that locks in a rate change and forward guidance that says we’re going to take our time making a decision and collect a lot of data. Subtle, but there’s a difference,” she said.William English, a professor at the Yale School of Management and a former Fed division director, said he did not believe the Jefferson and Williams speeches were coordinated, according to Bloomberg.“These were people who were giving speeches that they thought were the right speeches, giving their views about the economy and policy,” he said.Meanwhile, three regional Fed presidents appearing together at a conference in Asheville, North Carolina, declined to provide clues about their expectations for the central bank’s final two meetings of the year. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin, Boston Fed President Susan Collins and Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid instead pointed to upcoming economic data.“Let’s see how things develop,” Barkin said.Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee on Friday said there is room for both a rate hike and a rate cut on the table. He said the latest jobs data show the labor market is steady and that too-high inflation remains the Fed's bigger policy priority, but added that he would look at more evidence "that suggests we're headed back to 2% inflation".The Jefferson and Williams remarks were followed by comments from Michelle Bowman, a Fed governor and the central bank’s top banking regulator, who said there was little urgency to move rates again.Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, one of the Fed’s strongest advocates for rate hikes this year, said multiple additional increases would probably be needed to bring inflation fully back to the central bank’s 2% target. However, she also pointed to rising term premiums in bond markets, or the additional yield investors demand to hold longer-dated debt. Higher term premiums could also help slow the economy, she said.The comments triggered a sharp repricing of expectations for Fed interest rates over the remainder of the year.Eric Wallerstein, chief macro strategist for Clocktower Group and previously an adviser to former Fed Governor Stephen Miran, told Bloomberg the remarks from Jefferson and Williams represented clear attempts to correct market expectations.“Officials are doing what they’ve always done,” Wallerstein said. “Talking to the market when pricing reflects the ‘wrong’ reality.”Close observers of the Fed said the broader takeaway from the speeches was that traders had moved too far in betting on another hike following the Fed’s Sept. 16 increase, particularly as a sharp rise in bond yields pushed borrowing costs higher.Before Williams spoke on Tuesday, traders saw a 70% probability of a hike at the Oct. 27-28 meeting, based on federal funds futures pricing. By the time Jefferson finished his speech on Thursday, those odds had fallen to about 25%, with softer-than-expected inflation data also contributing to the shift.As president of the New York Fed, Williams has a permanent vote on monetary policy and, by tradition, serves as vice chair of the Federal Open Market Committee. Alongside the chair and vice chair, the New York Fed president has historically been viewed as part of the central bank’s leadership “troika” on monetary policy.Under some previous Fed chairs, investors interpreted comments from the vice chair or New York Fed president as signals of the broader views of the troika. There is no evidence, however, that Jefferson and Williams coordinated their speeches with each other or with Warsh, Bloomberg reported.Goldman Sachs economists said the combination of the Jefferson and Williams speeches reinforced their view that an October rate hike is unlikely, a conclusion echoed by other analysts.“We think the joint message from Jefferson and Williams is authoritative,” Krishna Guha, head of economics at Evercore ISI, and colleagues wrote in a note to clients Thursday after Jefferson made his remarks.Michael Feroli, chief US economist at JPMorgan Chase & Co., told Bloomberg the two speeches represented a clear effort to manage market expectations.“In both cases, it’s the message that you don’t have to keep piling hike on hike, meeting per meeting, and that you can kind of space things out a little bit here,” he said.Fed policymakers last month unanimously voted to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point, marking the first increase since 2023 as the broader economy accelerated and inflation remained stubbornly high. In projections released after the decision, officials indicated support for one additional rate hike this year.Warsh, however, has moved away from actively steering market expectations through forward guidance. He does not participate in the quarterly rate projections and has avoided signaling future policy moves in public remarks. Instead, he has encouraged investors to focus on incoming economic data.The shift has attracted support from some economists and market observers. Critics of forward guidance argue that it can be useful during a crisis but has less value when economic conditions are changing rapidly and policymakers have limited visibility into the outlook.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
