items.content:
Samsung baru saja meresmikan lini tablet flagship terbarunya, Galaxy Tab S12 Series yang tersedia dalam dua ukuran layar berbeda. Dan tidak membutuhkan waktu lama bagi Samsung Indonesia untuk meresmikannya di Indonesia, di mana harga Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Series dibanderol Rp20 jutaan baik untuk varian Tab S12+ hingga S12 Ultra.
Kehadiran Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Series tentu menjadi kompetitor terkuat tablet kelas flagship lainnya yang sudah tersedia di pasaran lebih dulu, baik dari Apple hingga HUAWEI. Samsung mencoba untuk menarik minat konsumen dengan paket bundling menarik, tidak hanya dengan aksesori pelengkap, namun juga software eksklusif termasuk Adobe Photoshop.
Widyantoko Utomo, MX Product Marketing Manager Samsung Electronics Indonesia mengatakan bila Galaxy Tab S12 Series hadir sebagai penawaran tablet terbaik dari Samsung saat ini, dan siap untuk mendukung berbagai aktivitas multitasking penggunanya. “Pengguna utamanya adalah kalangan profesional, kreatif, hingga longlife learner yang banyak melakukan multitasking dalam kesehariannya.”
Baca juga: Samsung Galaxy A08 Resmi di Indonesia, Bawa Baterai 6.000 mAh dan Dukungan Update 6 Tahun
Lewat Opsi Trade-In, Harga Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Series Terasa Lebih Murah
Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra
Sama seperti generasi sebelumnya, tablet teranyar Samsung kali ini tersedia dalam dua opsi berbeda, yakni Galaxy Tab S12+ dan Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra. Harga Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ dibanderol Rp21,999 juta dan Rp23,499 juta, masing-masing untuk varian Wi-Fi dan 5G. Sementara untuk harga Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra, dibanderol Rp25,499 juta dan Rp27,999 juta, juga tersedia dalam opsi Wi-Fi dan 5G.
Di Indonesia, Galaxy Tab S12 Series hanya tersedia dalam satu varian memori 12+256GB saja, alias tidak ada opsi RAM atau penyimpanan lebih lega. Meski memang, kabar baiknya masing-masing tablet dilengkapi dengan slot kartu microSD yang mendukung kapasitas sampai 2TB. Dan untuk membuat harga Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Series terasa lebih terjangkau, diberikan sejumlah benefit menarik senilai hingga lebih dari Rp6 juta.
Tidak seperti tablet rilisan Apple, paket penjualan Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Series di Indonesia sudah termasuk dengan stylus S Pen, serta Book Cover Keyboard Slim. Plus, gratis berlangganan Google AI Pro hingga 6 bulan yang sudah termasuk penyimpanan cloud 5TB, serta gratis berlangganan Adobe Photoshop hingga 4 bulan dengan akses penuh termasuk fitur-fitur AI di dalamnya.
Samsung juga memberikan opsi trade-in agar konsumen bisa mendapatkan harga Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Series lebih terjangkau. Sebuah simulasi resmi dari Samsung menunjukkan bila konsumen bisa melakukan trade-in dari Galaxy Tab S11 ke Galaxy Tab S12+, dengan membayar sekitar Rp11,4 jutaan, yang bisa diubah menjadi opsi cicilan senilai Rp954 ribuan per bulannya selama 12 bulan.
Andalkan Peningkatan Performa Untuk Produktivitas Maksimal
Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+
Dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya, peningkatan utama yang dibawa lewat kehadiran Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra, tidak lain chipset yang lebih kencang, di mana kini mengusung Dimensity 9500 octa-core 3nm. Cip tersebut memberikan peningkatan performa hingga 17% pada aspek CPU,19% pada GPU, dan hingga 61% pada NPU untuk pemrosesan AI. Dan karena sudah menjalankan One UI terbaru berbasis Android 17, sudah mendukung fitur QuickShare ke perangkat iOS.
Spesifikasi layarnya sendiri masih sama, berukuran 14,6 inci dengan panel AMOLED 120Hz, namun kini membawa teknologi Vision Booster yang disempurnakan demi kemudahan akses visual layar pada berbagai situasi pencahayaan berbeda. Dan pada sektor audio, juga membawa efek audio spasial 4-channel (vs 2-channel pada generasi sebelumnya).
Sementara untuk Galaxy Tab S12+, sesuai namanya, mengusung dimensi layar lebih luas dibandingkan Galaxy Tab S11 standar sebelumnya, kini mencapai 12,6 inci. Dengan begitu, kapasitas baterainya juga lebih besar, dan juga membawa sertifikasi IP68, baik pada perangkat tablet serta stylus S Pennya.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Huawei has launched the Mate 90 Pro Max in China, bringing several high-end features aimed at users who prioritize photography and display quality. The flagship comes with a 200MP RYYB periscope telephoto camera, a large 6.9-inch dual-layer OLED display, a 6,800mAh battery, and support for an optional modular camera system with a 1-inch sensor.
Huawei Mate 90 Pro Max launches with 12,000-nit display and 200MP periscope camera
The camera system is one of the biggest highlights of the Mate 90 Pro Max. The phone features a 50MP primary camera with a 1/1.28-inch sensor, RYYB technology, optical image stabilization (OIS), and a variable f/1.4-f/4.0 aperture.
Huawei has paired the main camera with a 40MP ultrawide sensor and a 200MP periscope telephoto camera. The telephoto camera also uses a 1/1.28-inch sensor, RYYB technology, and OIS.
The camera system supports up to 4x optical zoom, 8x optical-quality zoom and up to 100x digital zoom. Huawei has also added its third-generation Red Maple primary-color camera to improve color reproduction in photos.
The Collector’s Edition offers an even more advanced camera setup through Huawei’s optional Ruiying Z10 module. The accessory features a 1-inch RYYB sensor, a 10x continuous optical zoom and a 24-240mm focal range. It also has a variable f/2.0-f/4.5 aperture.
The phone can record videos in 4K resolution. For selfies and video calls, it has a 13MP autofocus ultrawide front camera along with a 3D depth-sensing camera.
12,000-nit OLED Display
The Mate 90 Pro Max features a 6.9-inch OLED display with a 2848 × 1320 resolution. The dual-layer panel supports an adaptive refresh rate from 1Hz to 120Hz, which can help balance smooth visuals and power consumption.
The display can reach a local peak brightness of up to 12,000 nits. It also supports the BT.2020 color gamut and uses 1440Hz high-frequency PWM dimming.
Huawei protects the standard model with Kunlun Glass, while the Collector’s Edition gets Basalt Kunlun Glass.
Large Battery and Flagship Hardware
The Mate 90 Pro Max packs a 6,800mAh battery and supports 100W wired charging and 50W wireless charging.
Huawei uses its Kirin 9050 Pro chipset in the 16GB variants. The phone runs HarmonyOS 7 and includes several modern connectivity features, including Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, NFC, eSIM support and StarLight E2.0.
The device also carries IP68 and IP69 ratings for protection against dust and water.
Huawei Mate 90 Pro Max price in China
The Huawei Mate 90 Pro Max starts at CNY 9,499 for the 12GB RAM and 512GB storage version, which is around $1,417 based on the stated conversion.
The 16GB+512GB model costs CNY 9,999, while the 16GB+512GB Collector’s Edition costs CNY 10,999. The top-end 16GB+1TB Collector’s Edition is priced at CNY 12,999.
The phone comes in Rose Gold, Jade Green, Crystal White, and Obsidian Black.
The optional Ruiying Z10 module camera costs CNY 5,999, while the complete Pro Max camera kit costs CNY 19,499. Huawei also offers a small rig teleconverter kit for CNY 1,799.
The Mate 90 Pro Max is currently launching in China, with Huawei positioning the device as a flagship that combines high-end hardware with an advanced modular camera system. The pricing and availability in Pakistan and other markets are unclear.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is expanding its parental control features to teen accounts, giving parents more options to manage how their children use the messaging platform. The latest update adds alerts for group activity along with new controls for Channels, Status updates and Meta AI.
WhatsApp first introduced parent-managed accounts for pre-teens earlier this year. These controls help parents manage their children’s experience on the platform without giving them access to private conversations.
WhatsApp Adds New Parental Controls For Teen Accounts and Meta AI
The initial features allowed parents to decide who could contact a child’s account and which groups the child could join. Parents could also review message requests from unknown contacts and manage privacy settings. A parent-set PIN protects these changes.
WhatsApp later made the controls easier to access on iPhone by adding a dedicated Parental Controls section in the Settings menu. The company has now extended the system to teenagers, while adding more options that are specifically for group activity and content access.
Parents Can Receive Group Activity Alerts
Under the new controls, parents can receive notifications when their teen joins or leaves a WhatsApp group. They can also be notified when a group their teen already belongs to grows significantly in size.
These alerts will give parents more information about changes in their teen’s group activity without allowing them to monitor private conversations inside those groups.
Parents can also manage how their teen interacts with WhatsApp Channels. They can choose how Channels can be used, and control which Status updates their teen can view. They can also manage who is allowed to see their teen’s own Status updates.
See Also: WhatsApp to Move Channels to Chats Tab on Android
More Restrictions for Meta AI
The update also introduces additional parental controls for Meta AI. Parents can choose between the standard Meta AI experience available to users aged 13 and above and a stricter Limited Content option.
The Limited Content setting places additional restrictions on the subjects a teen can discuss with Meta AI. WhatsApp says some Meta AI features that depend on Private Processing are also unavailable after enabling this setting.
This gives parents an additional way to limit their teen’s interaction with AI features while still allowing access to the broader messaging service.
Private Messages Remain Protected
WhatsApp says the new parental controls do not allow parents to read their teen’s private messages or listen to their calls. These communications remain protected by end-to-end encryption.
The company says the expanded controls will provide parents with greater visibility and management options while maintaining the privacy of teens’ personal conversations.
With the latest update, WhatsApp is gradually expanding its parental control system from pre-teen accounts to teenagers, covering areas such as group participation, Channels, Status updates, and AI interactions.

items.content:
Timnas Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) Indonesia gagal meraih medali emas di Asian Games 2026. Berhadapan dengan Myanmar, skuad Merah Putih harus takluk dari Negara Seribu Pagoda ini dengan skor 0-4 tanpa balas.
Bertanding dalam format best of 7 (Bo7), partai final yang digelar di Aichi Sky Expo Hall D hari ini, Kamis (1/10/2026), berjalan berat sebelah sejak game pertama berlangsung untuk timnas MLBB Indonesia.
Baca Juga: Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Series Andalkan Performa Produktivitas dengan Dua Opsi Layar Besar
Terlihat Syauki “Nino” Fauzan Sumarno, Muhammad “Yazukee” Affan Wahyudi, Dalvin “Hijumee” Ramadhana Putra, Arifudin “Arfy” Dingarai Putra, dan Alexander “alekk” Owen Marcetami Buhe mengalami kesulitan bermain lepas.
Timnas Indonesia kerap berada dalam situasi dan kondisi tertekan, di mana para pemain lawan mampu menjelajah seluruh area map land of dawn dengan lebih bebas.
Tak hanya itu, draft pick hero pilihan Garuda Muda juga beberapa kali mampu di counter dengan sempurna lawan. Di sisi lain, Myanmar pun tampil lebih konsisten sejak gim pertama.
Walau sempat memberikan perlawanan, timnas Indonesia tidak mampu memanfaatkan momentum hingga Myanmar akhirnya mengamankan kemenangan 4-0 sekaligus merebut medali emas Asian Games 2026.
Meski gagal naik ke podium tertinggi, raihan medali perak menunjukkan Indonesia masih menjadi salah satu kekuatan utama Mobile Legends di tingkat internasional. Sepanjang turnamen, timnas memperlihatkan performa kompetitif saat menghadapi sejumlah tim unggulan Asia.
Timnas MLBB Indonesia Tambah Koleksi Medali dari Cabang Esports
Jadwal MLBB Asian Games 2026
Medali perak dari nomor MLBB menambah kontribusi esports untuk kontingen Indonesia di Asian Games 2026. Cabang esports kembali menjadi salah satu penyumbang prestasi setelah beberapa nomor pertandingan berlangsung sepanjang pekan terakhir.
Bagi komunitas MLBB Indonesia, hasil ini tentu meninggalkan rasa campur aduk. Di satu sisi, peluang timnas MLBB Indonesia meraih emas harus pupus di partai final. Namun di sisi lain, keberhasilan mencapai final dan membawa pulang medali perak tetap menjadi pencapaian yang layak diapresiasi.
Perjalanan timnas MLBB Indonesia juga menunjukkan regenerasi pemain Indonesia masih berjalan dengan baik. Dengan persaingan yang semakin ketat di level Asia, pengalaman tampil di panggung Asian Games dapat menjadi modal penting untuk menghadapi turnamen internasional berikutnya.
Timnas MLBB ke Asian Games 2026, Nino dkk Bidik Emas
Syauki “Nino” Sumarno saat wawancara tentang persiapan timnas MLBB menuju Asian Games 2026. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson
Syauki “Nino” Sumarno menyatakan dengan tegas dia dan rekan satu timnas MLBB Indonesia siap bertanding di Asian Games 2026 di Aichi-Nagoya, Jepang.
Pemain yang saat ini masih tergabung di tim esports Alter Ego tersebut menyebut, latihan fisik dan latih tanding bersama pelatih timnas MLBB membantu tim mempersiapkan diri untuk mengejar medali emas.
“Latihan dari Coach Eki bisa dibilang lumayan keras. Dari coach Mobile Legends juga sudah bagus banget. Jadi, kita sudah siap banget,” kata Nino dalam wawancara di Jakarta, Selasa (15/9/2026).
Asian Games 2026 berlangsung pada 19 September hingga 4 Oktober 2026. Rentang tersebut merupakan jadwal keseluruhan pesta olahraga, bukan jadwal khusus pertandingan MLBB.
Bagi Nino, persiapan selama pelatnas terasa langsung dalam aktivitas sehari-hari. Ia mengaku lebih bugar dan tidak mudah lelah setelah mengikuti rutinitas latihan.
Nino: Timnas MLBB Percaya Diri Kejar Emas Asian Games 2026
Perubahan selama latihan turut memperkuat keyakinan Nino menghadapi persaingan. Ia menilai performa timnas MLBB Indonesia berkembang dan ingin membawa ke posisi pertama.
Pelatnas Timnas Esports Indonesia disiapkan hingga Mei 2027. Simak agenda menuju Asian Games 2026, Global Esports Games, dan kompetisi berikutnya. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson)
“Jujur, aku yakin banget karena dari latihan kita, aku melihat ada perubahan yang besar, terutama dari performa kita,” ujar Nino.
Ia mengaku ingin mengubah keadaan ketika timnas MLBB Indonesia, dalam penilaian Nino, lebih sering berada di posisi kedua atau ketiga.
“Jujur, aku merasa percaya diri banget bisa mendapatkan emas. Amin,” kata Nino.
Ambisi itu lebih tinggi daripada sasaran resmi yang dijelaskan Manajer Tim Nasional Esports Indonesia, Glorya Famiela Ralahalo. Menurut Glorya, pemerintah menargetkan satu emas melalui eFootball, sementara atlet dari nomor lain tetap ingin melampaui sasaran tersebut.
Adaptasi Albert untuk Maju Tampil di Timnas MLBB
Klasemen MPL ID S18 setelah seluruh pertandingan Week 4 berakhir pada 6 September 2026. (Doc: MPL ID)
Selain latihan, Nino membahas proses adaptasi Albert di timnas MLBB Indonesia. Ia menilai Albert perlu menyesuaikan diri dengan kelompok pemain yang sudah terbentuk. Pada saat yang sama, tim perlu membantu Albert agar mereka bisa bergerak bersama.
“Dia yang harus menyesuaikan ke kita, karena enggak mungkin lima orang ini menyesuaikan ke Albert. Yang pasti, kita harus menarik Albert supaya timnas ini maju bareng-bareng, enggak cuma membawa nama klub,” ujar Nino.
Menurut Nino, proses tersebut sejauh ini berjalan baik. Para pemain tetap memiliki porsi latihan bersama klub dan tim nasional. Kepentingan membawa nama Indonesia menjadi hal ia tekankan. Nino ingin timnas MLBB melangkah bersama meski para pemain juga memiliki tanggung jawab di klub.

To recap, the Samsung Galaxy Glasses are powered by the Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 chipset from Qualcomm. The wearable sports a built-in camera, allowing the smart glasses to provide answers to user queries based on visual context. The company says that the smart glasses will deliver up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge. Meanwhile, the wireless charging case will provide up to seven additional full charges.

items.content:
Beijing calls the Uyghur region a ‘national energy and resource strategic security base’
Originally published on Global Voices
The Karamay Cloud Computing Industrial Park of the Uyghur Region. Screenshot from Xinjiang Radio and Television Station. Fair use.
This post is part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” In this Spotlight, we explore how Big Tech facilitates and hinders authoritarian governments and practices, and how these choices influence the Global South. You can support this coverage by donating here.
On September 14, ministers and senior officials gathered behind closed doors in Urumqi, the capital of China’s Uyghur region, on the eve of the 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Digital Economy Forum. The meeting was presented as a technical and developmental exercise in which participants discussed digital infrastructure, industrial transformation, artificial intelligence, data governance, and the economic value of data. The wider forum was held under the theme “Promoting SCO Data Connectivity, Shaping the Future with AI.”
The choice of Urumqi as the meeting spot was not incidental. Chinese officials are positioning the Uyghur region as a land-based gateway through which China’s digital infrastructure, computing capacity, data systems and technical standards can extend into Central Asia and the wider Eurasian market. At the same time, holding the forum in Urumqi helps Beijing recast a region internationally associated with mass surveillance and severe human rights violations as a showcase of innovation, openness and prosperity.
That strategy also rests on energy. Long treated by Beijing as a source of oil, gas, coal and electricity for the rest of China, the Uyghur region is now being repackaged as a source of the vast computing power needed for artificial intelligence (AI). The new digital economy is being built on top of an older extractive economy.
For Uyghurs, the costs of this transformation are economic, political, social and physical. Their homeland supplies the land, coal, gas, electricity and increasingly computing power, while they have little control over the projects, profits or use of their data. What Beijing presents as technological development may deepen both extraction and control, including state-directed labor transfers, the loss of land-based livelihoods, industrial pollution and pervasive digital surveillance.
Digital technology in the Uyghur homeland has already been used to monitor movement, communications, religious practice and ordinary social behavior. That history — and the suffering it has caused — was absent from the forum’s public language. Instead, officials presented the region’s digital transformation as a promise of modernization.
From declarations to permanent machinery
According to China’s National Data Administration, the September 14 closed-door meeting brought together officials from SCO member states and other partner countries. Nine SCO members — Belarus, China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan — reached agreement on a 2026 SCO Digital Economy Ministerial Statement.
The participants also produced a List of Priority Cooperation Items and Intentions in the SCO Digital Economy, 2026–2027 (上合组织数字经济领域重点合作事项和意向清单 (2026—2027)), which contains nearly 20 cooperation intentions across more than 10 sectors, including digital infrastructure, agriculture, manufacturing, energy, transport and logistics, disaster prevention, education, healthcare and capacity building.
The institutional structure behind the event is more consequential than a single declaration; after the first SCO Digital Economy Forum in Tianjin in 2025, it includes a cooperative platform that monitors developments monthly, reviews projects quarterly, and conducts bilateral or multilateral exchanges every six months. In other words, the system proactively matches Chinese technology, standards and services with the policies and infrastructure needs of SCO states.
The call for submissions for the 2026 collection sought cooperation cases involving 5G, cloud computing, data centers, cross-border cables, artificial intelligence, digital identity, smart cities and digital government, cross-border data flows and data-security technologies. In a press briefing in August, the authorities revealed the 2025 collection of successful cases included a China–Uzbekistan “digital and intelligent port,” a China–Russia trusted data space for trade, a China–Pakistan automotive-finance data platform, and Chinese support for a data exchange in Astana, Kazakhstan. Chinese and Kazakh railway institutions are also connecting data and pre-screening freight documents for the trans-Caspian route.
Why Urumqi?
Chinese officials, during the August press briefing, described the Uyghur region as having 19 ports of entry, three regional international telecommunications gateways and 28 cross-border fiber-optic cables leading toward Central Asia. They also say they are seeking a national internet backbone direct-connection point and a full-service international communications gateway in the region.
The ambitions extend far beyond connectivity. Regional officials have announced plans to build large computing clusters in and around Urumqi, including clusters with tens of thousands — and eventually hundreds of thousands — of accelerator cards. Their stated goal is to turn the city into a computing hub serving Central Asian and wider Eurasian markets and to promote the export of computing power and AI tokens.
They also revealed a plan to build a regional alliance to promote digital standards, with regular technical training and alignment with certification systems so Chinese standards serve as a “priority reference” for Central Asian infrastructure. Such standards can determine who controls data, how systems communicate and what forms of state access are built into data centers, digital identity systems, smart cities and government databases.
Researchers have long identified the SCO as a venue through which China and Russia promote state-centered ideas of “internet sovereignty.” One academic study of China’s cyber-norm strategy describes it as a staging ground for norms that prioritize state control, information security and regime stability, often at the expense of transparency, accountability and human rights. Aligning digital rules and standards is therefore both economic coordination and an attempt to shape the region’s digital governance architecture.
The energy base beneath the AI hub
Artificial intelligence may appear weightless, but its infrastructure is intensely physical. Models are trained and operated in data centers filled with power-hungry processors, connected to electricity grids and cooling systems. The International Energy Agency puts the point plainly: “there is no AI without energy.” It estimates that a typical AI-focused data center consumes as much electricity as 100,000 households, while the largest facilities under construction may consume 20 times as much. Global data-center electricity demand is projected to more than double between 2024 and 2030, driven largely by AI.
China’s digital strategy follows an older geography of extraction. For decades, west–east gas transmission, west–east electricity transmission and west-to-east coal transport have moved energy from inland resource frontiers toward eastern industrial centers. To pave the way for the data economy, China Mobile chairman Yang Jie has publicly called for expanding the storage, processing, training and rendering of eastern data in western China since 2023.
“East Data, West Computing” shifts some computing work to western regions, where land and electricity support demand elsewhere in China. In the Uyghur region, in addition to gas pipelines, coal and electricity exports, data centers and AI clusters are now added to the list of natural resource extraction.
Beijing calls the Uyghur region a “national energy and resource strategic security base.” Official figures put its primary energy production in 2025 at 510 million metric tons of standard coal and its installed new-energy capacity at more than 170 million kilowatts. Electricity is transmitted from the region to more than 20 provincial-level areas; roughly one-third of this outbound electricity is described as green power. Local officials also expect the region to become a base for “green computing” and plan to export computing power and AI tokens — the units processed by language models — toward Central Asia.
Politically, designating the Uyghur homeland as a national “strategic security base” places its resources within Beijing’s security agenda. Decisions about land, mining, electricity transmission and computing infrastructure are and will likely be made through a top-down system dominated by the state and large enterprises. Uyghurs — already denied meaningful political participation — have little independent space to contest land use, environmental harm or the distribution of revenue. Energy extraction and digital governance thus reinforce each other: one supplies material power, while the other expands the state’s capacity to monitor and administer the land and the population.
Mines, industrial parks, transmission corridors and wind and solar bases require land and, in an arid region, scarce water. Where agricultural or pastoral livelihoods are reorganized around state projects, more Uyghurs may face the loss of land-based independence, family separation, forced labor transfers, or work placements directed by officials.
While public data have not revealed how many Uyghurs have been displaced specifically by energy and computing construction, UN human-rights experts warned in January 2026 that state-mandated labor-transfer programs affecting Uyghurs contain indicators of coercion and can lead to displacement. A Sheffield Hallam University investigation traced state-imposed Uyghur labor through the solar supply chain, from quartz mining and coal-powered polysilicon production to solar-module manufacturing.
The “green” label attached to an AI data center does not by itself make its supply chain clean or its labor free. A study of heavy-industrial cities in the region documented serious particulate pollution, although it did not assess the effects of AI data centers or establish Uyghur-specific health outcomes.
A digital showcase built over a surveillance state
There is a profound contradiction in presenting Urumqi as the center of a benign and inclusive digital future.
The Uyghur region is where Chinese authorities built one of the world’s most intrusive systems of technologically enabled population control. According to Human Rights Watch’s investigation, the Integrated Joint Operations Platform aggregated information about individuals and flagged people for investigation based on everyday activities ranging from religious behavior and family relationships to phone use and social contact. Lawful conduct could be treated as an indicator of suspicion.
The UN Human Rights Office’s 2022 assessment also documented extensive surveillance and severe restrictions on privacy, movement and expression in the region. It concluded that the scale of arbitrary and discriminatory detention and related violations against Uyghurs may constitute international crimes, particularly crimes against humanity.
The SCO forum did not address the significant issues concerning privacy rights, independent oversight, algorithmic discrimination, remedies for misuse, civil society participation, or safeguards against state surveillance. “Data governance” was discussed principally as a matter of unlocking value, connecting markets, aligning standards and facilitating cross-border flows.
The complete project list has not been published, so the human-rights implications of individual projects cannot yet be fully assessed. The cooperation categories include smart cities, digital government, digital identity, AI datasets and public-service platforms — systems capable of expanding both public services and state power. The available evidence does not establish that the forum’s projects export the surveillance systems used against Uyghurs.
The question is not whether digital infrastructure can bring economic benefits. It can. The question is whose rules will govern it, who will be able to access the data, and what protections will exist when technology is used against the people it claims to serve. Transparency matters, but is lacking.
The forum as political theatre
Chinese officials have been unusually candid about the political purpose of staging the forum in the Uyghur region. In the August press conference, a senior regional official called it a “major political task” serving national strategy and said it would present an image of social stability, economic development, unity and public happiness.
The forum therefore served two parallel goals: materially, to connect China’s computing infrastructure, data systems and technical standards with neighboring states; narratively, to replace attention to repression with a managed story of technology and prosperity. Urumqi was both the venue and the message. Beijing presented the region where digital tools have been used to categorize, monitor and punish Uyghurs as evidence that its model of digital development should be trusted abroad.
The transformation of the Uyghur region into a Eurasian digital hub is also an outward extension of political power: over infrastructure and data, and over the international narrative about what has happened to Uyghurs.
Without transparency and human-rights assessment, governments and the public cannot meaningfully assess the participating companies, technologies, data-sharing arrangements, or human-rights risks. Without such scrutiny, digital cooperation may bridge a technological divide, as the forum’s organizers promise; however, it may also carry an older extractive hierarchy into the AI era, making an authoritarian model of digital governance more deeply embedded — and harder to challenge — across borders.
Written by Asiye Uyghur

items.title: FBR Establishes National Faceless Centre for Digital Tax Audits and Assessments
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has established a National Faceless Centre (NFC) in Islamabad to introduce a new digital system for tax audits and assessments. The initiative aims to reduce direct interaction between taxpayers and tax officers while making the tax process more transparent and technology-driven.
Under the new system, tax cases will be selected through a computerised, risk-based mechanism instead of being chosen at the discretion of individual officers. Once a case is selected, it will be automatically assigned to an officer anywhere in Pakistan.
Taxpayers will not be informed about the identity of the officer handling their case. Similarly, the assigned officer will have no role in selecting the case, reducing the possibility of direct influence during the selection process.

Taxpayers will not be informed about the identity of the officer handling their case. Similarly, the assigned officer will have no role in selecting the case, reducing the possibility of direct influence during the selection process.
FBR Establishes National Faceless Centre for Digital Tax Audits and Assessments
The new procedure will also divide the handling of each case into three separate stages. One officer will conduct the audit, another will handle the assessment, while a third officer will review the case for quality and procedural compliance before the final order is issued.
This separation is designed to ensure that no single officer has complete control over a case from beginning to end. The FBR says the arrangement will help improve oversight and promote greater consistency in tax proceedings.
All notices, responses and hearings under the new system will be conducted electronically through the FBR’s IRIS system. However, physical verification and recovery activities that are required under the law will continue to be carried out separately by field teams.
See Also: FBR Clarifies Procedure to Seal Businesses Not Linked to Electronic Monitoring System
The National Faceless Centre has been established under the legal framework provided by the Finance Act 2026. It includes separate divisions responsible for faceless audits, faceless assessments, quality control and field operations.
According to the FBR, the reforms are aimed at promoting data-driven decision-making, uniform procedures, and greater transparency in tax administration. By reducing direct contact between taxpayers and tax officials, the new system is also intended to make tax proceedings more structured and less dependent on individual discretion.
The establishment of the National Faceless Centre marks another step toward the digital transformation of Pakistan’s tax administration. The FBR expects the system to improve the way tax cases are selected, processed, and reviewed while creating a more standardised process for taxpayers across the country.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Higher Education Commission (HEC), Pakistan and The National Cyber, Emergency Response Team (National CERT) of Pakistan have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance cybersecurity cooperation, coordination, and resilience across Pakistan’s higher education sector. The MoU marks a significant step towards strengthening the sector’s capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to emerging cyber threats.
A key outcome of the collaboration is the establishment of the Pakistan Education & Research Network (PERN)/Higher Education Commission (HEC) as the Education Sector Computer Emergency Response Team (EduCERT). The initiative will provide a dedicated cybersecurity coordination mechanism for universities and higher education institutions across Pakistan, enabling coordinated efforts to strengthen cyber preparedness, information sharing, and response to emerging threats.
The MoU was signed by Dr. Zia Ul Haq, Executive Director HEC, and Dr. Mehreen Afzal, Director Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC), National CERT, in the presence of Chairman HEC Prof. Dr. Niaz Ahmad Akhtar, Director General National CERT Dr. Haider Abbas, TI, Advisor IT Engr. Nazeer Hussain, Engr. Naeem Ahmed Director IT, and senior representatives of both organisations.
Chairman HEC Prof. Dr. Niaz Ahmad Akhtar said that strengthening cybersecurity across higher education institutions is essential to safeguarding digital infrastructure, academic systems, and institutional data. He emphasised the importance of coordinated efforts, timely information sharing, and enhanced institutional capacity to effectively address evolving cyber threats, adding that EduCERT will provide a structured mechanism for universities to collaborate and strengthen their cybersecurity preparedness.
EduCERT thru PERN will serve as a coordinated cybersecurity platform for Pakistan’s higher education sector, supporting cyber threat monitoring, incident coordination, information sharing, security awareness, and institutional cyber resilience. It will facilitate collaboration among universities by enabling the exchange of threat intelligence, cybersecurity knowledge, and best practices, thereby contributing to a stronger and more coordinated national cybersecurity framework.
The partnership reflects the shared commitment of HEC and National CERT to fostering a coordinated, resilient, and cybersecurity-conscious higher education ecosystem. It will also contribute to strengthening Pakistan’s sectoral CERT framework and enhancing the higher education sector’s capacity to address evolving cyber threats.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Amid ongoing debate over the future of UPI post the introduction of MDR, UPI transaction volumes for the month of September fell marginally, NPCI data reveals.
While volume of transactions processed declined nearly 1.8% month-on-month (MoM) to 24.07 Bn in September from a record 24.51 Bn in August, the value of these transactions also fell 1.5% to ₹29.37 Lakh Cr from ₹29.82 Lakh Cr.
The volume of monthly transactions for the month of September increased 23% YoY while transaction value grew 18%. This is slightly higher than the 22% YoY jump recorded in the month of August.
UPI processed an average of 802 Mn transactions per day in September, up from 791 Mn in August. The average daily transaction value also increased to ₹97,913 Cr from ₹96,205 Cr during the previous month.
UPI’s Monetisation Question
Headlines around UPI over the past month were centred around the Centre’s notification of the new UPI Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework, which is to be implemented from October 15.
Under the framework, eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions above ₹2,000 will attract an MDR of 0.4%, capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above. Person-to-person payments will continue to remain free of MDR.
The proposed charges have sparked concerns among merchants and retailers. Retailer groups have warned that the MDR could discourage businesses from accepting UPI, particularly during the festive season when transaction values are often higher than ₹2,000.
Earlier this week, The All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA) and the All India Consumer Products Distributors Federation (AICPDF) also announced a “No UPI Day” protest for October 2.
However, the protest was called off after representatives of 20 trade associations met finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman to raise concerns regarding MDR.
On the other hand, businesses across the UPI ecosystem, including banks, payment companies and TPAPs, have welcomed the move, as the framework is expected to open up a new revenue stream for players in the payments ecosystem.
Under the standard 0.4% MDR structure, the merchant pays the acquiring bank, which passes 0.28% to the issuing bank as an interchange. Of the remaining 0.12%, the issuing bank pays 0.08% to the payer-side payment service provider, which then shares it with the UPI app provider.
This has long been a demand of the players operating in the UPI ecosystem as it brings more clarity on the sustainability of their business models. For instance, Inc42 learnt that UPI leader, PhonePe, is mulling the revival of its IPO plans post clarity on UPI MDR.
The fintech startup, which handles almost 45% share of UPI merchant payments, will now be targeting a public listing between February-March 2027. It will look to file its updated IPO papers by the end of this year, seeking a valuation of $10 Bn.

items.author: Muhammad Saleem Jhandeer
items.content:
The Sindh Cabinet on Thursday approved extending the term of the inquiry commission investigating the death of Mir Raza Ali until October 15, allowing Justice Omar Sial to continue the proceedings if more time was required.
The Sindh Home Department on August 24 notified the formation of a judicial commission to probe the death of 25-year-old Mir Raza Ali, with Justice Sial appointed as its head following his nomination by the Sindh High Court (SHC) chief justice through a letter dated the same day. The first hearing of the commission took place on September 1.
The decision was taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah at the CM House. The cabinet was briefed that the commission had conducted extensive proceedings and recorded statements from dozens of witnesses as part of its investigation.
The commission required additional time to complete its inquiry and finalise its findings and recommendations, the meeting was told. The cabinet subsequently approved extending the commission’s term until October 15.
KARACHI (October 1, 2026): Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah presides over a cabinet meeting at CM House. pic.twitter.com/eBWicHn8PO
— Sindh Chief Minister House (@SindhCMHouse) October 1, 2026
It also decided that Justice Sial could continue the inquiry beyond the extended deadline if further time was required.
The commission’s term had expired on September 28, according to a written order issued by the commission. The commission had requested the Sindh government to extend its tenure until October 15.
The provincial government’s focal person, Javed Ahmed Abro, had informed the commission that the summary seeking an extension had been approved by the chief minister and forwarded to the Sindh Cabinet for a decision.
The commission had subsequently adjourned its proceedings until October 2, pending the cabinet’s decision.
The written order had stated that if the cabinet did not approve an extension, no further witnesses would be summoned and the commission would prepare and submit its report based on the statements recorded so far.
If the tenure was extended, fresh notices would be issued to witnesses, the order had added.
During an earlier hearing, Investigation Officer Siraj Lashari and a representative of the Citizens-Police Liaison Committee (CPLC) had appeared before the commission to record their statements. However, their statements had not been recorded because the commission’s term had expired.
The case so far
Mir Raza Ali, the 25-year-old owner of dessert brand Wafflix, went missing from Karachi’s PECHS area on July 28, 2026. His body was found the following day in bushes near a wedding hall in Gulistan-e-Johar. Police initially treated the death as a possible suicide, but a second post-mortem conducted after his exhumation found a firearm entry wound, multiple ante-mortem injuries and signs of internal bleeding, leading investigators to treat the case as murder.
The initial post-mortem had faced several objections, with the Karachi police surgeon identifying 14 deficiencies, including the absence of an X-ray, failure to collect hand swabs for gunshot-residue analysis and the lack of chemical examination of gunpowder marks around the bullet wound.
The investigation subsequently came under scrutiny from Raza’s family, who alleged serious lapses in the handling of evidence and CCTV footage and sought the formation of a joint investigation team. The Sindh High Court later rejected the family’s plea for a JIT but directed the relevant authorities to conduct the investigation impartially, fairly and expeditiously.
Read More: Mir Raza commission rejects family's plea to summon top cops
Police told a Senate committee in September that they had recorded statements from 78 people but had not found evidence linking anyone to Raza’s alleged murder. Investigators nevertheless continued to treat the case as murder, while reviewing medical, chemical, forensic and digital evidence.
The Sindh government had meanwhile established a judicial commission headed by Sindh High Court Justice Umar Sial to examine the circumstances surrounding Raza’s death, the conduct of the investigation and any possible negligence or concealment of evidence by police or other officials.
The judicial commission had so far examined police records, witness statements and the circumstances surrounding Mir Raza Ali’s death, with its proceedings raising discrepancies in witness accounts, the handling of evidence and the initial post-mortem. The commission also questioned senior police and health officials over the investigation, including the handling of CCTV footage, Raza’s phone and smartwatch, and the initial focus on a possible suicide.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Former senator Mushahid Hussain Sayed called for a multi-pronged regional diplomatic approach to tackle terrorism emanating from Afghan soil, saying the issue was not merely bilateral between Pakistan and Afghanistan but a wider regional security challenge requiring a collective response from Afghanistan’s neighbours.
He made the remarks during his keynote concluding session at the two-day “International Conference on Afghan Predicament and Trajectory to Peace”, organised by the International Parliamentarians Congress (IPC) in Islamabad.
Sayed said Pakistan and Afghanistan could no longer afford further conflict, confrontation and instability in the region.
He described the conference as a productive, “first-of-its-kind” initiative focusing on Afghanistan’s relations with Pakistan and other neighbours to explore possible ways forward.
Sayed noted that Senator Sitara Ayaz, Secretary General of the IPC and host of the conference, had accompanied him twice to participate in a Track 1.5 Dialogue in Istanbul with Afghan counterparts, organised with the facilitation of Turkish friends.
“Both sides, including the Afghan side, accepted that the core issue dividing Pakistan and Afghanistan is the issue of terrorism emanating from Afghan soil, which is destabilising not only Pakistan but other neighbours of Afghanistan as well,” he said.
Sayed said the central conclusion of the Islamabad conference reflected the vision and philosophy of Allama Muhammad Iqbal, who, in his poems 100 years ago, linked peace in Afghanistan with peace in the region and Asia, while instability in Afghanistan inevitably produced instability and volatility across the region.
“Peace, security and stability are indivisible and inextricably intertwined with the region, especially Pakistan and Afghanistan,” he observed.
The former senator emphasised that despite differences with the regime in Kabul, Pakistan’s relationship with the people of Afghanistan should remain paramount.
Referring to the declaration adopted at the dialogue, he said a people-centric approach should ensure that links involving businessmen, traders, medical tourism and students from Afghanistan were not undermined.
Sayed recalled that Pakistan had been a generous host to Afghan refugees for four decades, hosting the largest number of refugees for the longest duration, adding that the historical and people-to-people bonds, particularly trade and education, between the two countries should not be allowed to suffer because of political differences.
He also referred to recent remarks by Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi describing Pakistan and Afghanistan as “inseparable brothers,” saying a similar sentiment had been conveyed by Turkish interlocutors during the Istanbul dialogue.
Sayed said there were indications of a possible opening from Kabul.
Referring to Pakistani journalists who had recently returned from Kabul, he said they had informed him about a meeting with Afghan Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani.
“According to these journalists, there is a glimmer of hope from the regime in Kabul. The regime is keen to find some way forward. They recognise the problem of terrorism and want to establish some mechanism with Pakistan to take this issue forward through dialogue and resolve it,” he said.
Sayed stressed that Afghanistan’s security situation had implications extending well beyond Pakistan.
“This is not simply an issue between Pakistan and Afghanistan. It is a regional security issue,” he said, noting that terrorism and violent extremism emanating from Afghanistan would impact Pakistan, Iran, China, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Russia, as there were Kabul-based militant groups targeting these countries as well.
He pointed to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) and its Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) as an existing institutional mechanism that could contribute to addressing regional security challenges emanating from Afghanistan.
Sayed also referred to a proposal from Russian Professor Vladimir Sotnikov for a Peace Board comprising Russia and all six neighbours of Afghanistan to work out a collective counter-terrorism strategy against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan.
He cautioned against allowing the region to become embroiled in another cycle of conflict, especially after what he described as the failed wars of aggression by India against Pakistan and by the US and Israel against Iran.
Sayed argued that Pakistan and the wider region had been affected by geopolitical competition since 9/11 and urged regional countries to learn from the consequences of the post-9/11 period.
Referring to the US intervention in Afghanistan, he said that, according to a Brown University research study, the United States had spent approximately $2.2 trillion in Afghanistan between October 7, 2001, and August 15, 2021 — a cost of $100 million a day for 20 years — while leaving behind large quantities of weapons and ammunition worth more than $7 billion, which he said were being used against Pakistan by Afghan-based terrorists.
He said the experience demonstrated the need for regional countries to avoid becoming trapped in another prolonged conflict.
The former senator maintained that the peoples of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran were all victims of geopolitics and that it was now time for Afghanistan to be part of the solution rather than remaining part of the problem.
Sayed called for Pakistan, Iran, China, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Russia to collectively explore practical mechanisms for addressing the Afghan security challenge.
He said sustainable peace in Afghanistan was also essential for Pakistan’s vision of emerging as a hub of regional connectivity.
Sayed said Pakistan was seeking to expand regional linkages through trade, economy, energy, ports, pipelines, roads and railways, connecting Pakistan with Central Asia, Iran, Turkiye and Afghanistan.
He also highlighted the role of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) in Pakistan’s broader regional connectivity vision.
“The main stumbling block is the situation in Afghanistan,” he said, stressing that peace and stability in Afghanistan were prerequisites for unlocking the full potential of regional economic connectivity.
He appreciated the organisers and participants for holding what he described as a frank and democratic discussion on Afghanistan.
Sayed particularly congratulated Senator Sitara Ayaz for facilitating the initiative and said Parliament and parliamentarians should increasingly use their institutional and political space to contribute to resolving challenges affecting Pakistan and the wider region.
According to the statement, the two-day dialogue brought together Pakistani and foreign parliamentarians, diplomats, academics and experts to deliberate on Afghanistan’s security situation, Pakistan-Afghanistan relations, regional stability, connectivity, reconciliation and possible pathways towards peace.
Delegates from China, Russia, Tajikistan, Pakistan and Afghanistan’s diaspora participated in the conference, which was well attended.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a schoolmate three decades ago, survived Tennessee's effort to execute her by means of lethal ​injection late on Wednesday, prison officials said, foiling the state's first attempt to put a woman to death in two centuries.
Pike's condition following the ordeal was ‌not immediately known, and it was not clear what legal avenues her lawyers or the state might pursue next after she was taken for medical treatment from the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.
The Tennessee Department of Correction defended its handling of the high-profile execution, which had been opposed by her lawyers and human rights experts due to Pike's age at the time of the crime, her history as the victim of ​childhood sexual abuse, and untreated mental illness.
"The Tennessee Department of Correction followed every step of the state’s lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General’s Office," the ​agency said in a statement.
"The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures ⁠beyond what was carried out this evening. Christa Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility," the statement concluded.
Pike's lawyers filed a federal court motion during the process seeking ​to halt her execution, citing witnesses' accounts that "executioners had injected both syringes of lethal injection chemicals and Pike is still alive and snoring," NBC News reported.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, who denied Pike's ​clemency petition on Monday, issued a statement after the botched execution, suspending all executions this year and calling for a "comprehensive, third-party review" of Pike's execution attempt, according to the Nashville Tennessean.
The failed execution is the second in Tennessee this year, after prison officials in May aborted attempts to execute a man convicted of murders after failing to find a suitable vein for his lethal injection.
The botched attempt on Wednesday came hours after the ​US Supreme Court lifted an 11th-hour lower-court stay of the execution, clearing the way for Pike, 50, to be put to death for her role in the 1995 torture and beating ​death of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville.
Pike was 18 in January 1995 when she, 17-year-old boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and a third companion lured Slemmer, a classmate at their Knoxville Job Corps vocational center, into a ‌wooded area where ⁠they tortured and killed her.
The grisly nature of the slaying, which involved the perpetrators carving the shape of a pentagram in the victim's chest and taking a chunk of her skull as a souvenir of the carnage, drew intense media coverage at the time.
Pike and Shipp confessed to the killing, and both were convicted of first-degree murder.
Slemmer's mother, May Martinez, has spoken out in support of the execution.
Ambulance called
Journalists who witnessed the attempted execution described snoring, loud exhales, gasps, and complaints from Pike about discomfort in her arm. At times, the curtain was closed, and ​journalists could only hear sounds.
Clergy were called into ​the chamber twice, they said, before an ⁠ambulance was seen arriving at the prison and then leaving.
Aside from being the first woman the state of Tennessee has tried to execute in more than 200 years, Pike was also poised to became the only person in the modern era of US capital punishment to be ​executed in Tennessee for a crime committed as a teenager.
In a 226-page petition asking the governor to commute Pike's death penalty to ​a life sentence without the ⁠possibility of parole, her lawyers earlier this week documented her history as the childhood victim of violence, neglect and sexual abuse, including two rapes at ages 11 and 17. They also cited diagnoses she received in prison for bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder.
Moreover, her lawyers pointed to evidence that Pike's mother drank heavily during pregnancy, contributing to faulty brain development that made it difficult for their ⁠client to control ​her impulses as a young person.
Pike was also convicted in August 2001 of attempted first-degree murder in an ​assault on another inmate, according to the Correction Department.
Executions of female prison inmates are exceedingly rare in the US, with women accounting for just 18 of the 1,683 people put to death since the Supreme Court allowed capital punishment to ​resume in 1976, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. Before Wednesday, Tennessee had executed 17 people.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has told the Islamabad High Court that there is currently no specific law in Pakistan prohibiting children under 16 from using social media, arguing that the regulator cannot create an age-verification system beyond the powers granted to it by law.
The response was submitted in a case seeking restrictions on social media use by children under 16 and the introduction of stronger online-safety safeguards. The Islamabad High Court had earlier sought replies from the federal government, PTA, and other authorities on the petition.
According to PTA’s detailed reply, protecting children from online harms would require a new legal and policy framework, rather than regulatory action by PTA alone. The authority said its existing powers to block unlawful online content are limited in scope and transitional in nature.
PTA also referred to the Prevention of Electronic Crimes (Amendment) Act, 2025, under which the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority is to be established to regulate social media platforms and online content. The amended law provides for a dedicated authority with powers relating to online safety, unlawful content, and regulation of social media platforms.
The regulator said that responsibility for cybercrime investigations and action against certain forms of harmful or obscene online content now falls within the mandate of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency.
PTA told the court it had reviewed more than 1.789 million online links and URLs for alleged violations and had blocked over 1.577 million, representing an overall blocking rate of about 88.20%.
According to the figures submitted by the authority, the blocking rate was 88.68% for TikTok, 87.34% for YouTube and 78.57% for Facebook. PTA said action had also been taken against 79.52% of reported Instagram links and 48.42% of links on X, formerly Twitter.
The authority further said more than 1.066 million websites and links related to obscene content had been blocked. It also reported blocking more than 203,000 links involving content deemed against Islam and over 46,000 links related to national security concerns.
PTA said technical limitations also complicate enforcement. According to its response, widespread use of HTTPS encryption can make it difficult to block individual pieces of content on some websites, leaving regulators with the option of blocking an entire website in certain cases.
The authority also said major social-media platforms are not locally registered in Pakistan and do not always operate under direct local compliance arrangements. PTA said requests for companies to appoint local compliance and grievance officers had not produced the desired response.
At the same time, the regulator said it is working with organizations including UNICEF, TikTok, Meta and GSMA on child online-safety awareness initiatives. It also cited the activation of the 1121 toll-free helpline for reports involving online abuse and exploitation of children, as well as the rollout of Instagram’s safety features for younger users in Pakistan.
The petition before the IHC seeks legislation and an effective age-verification mechanism for social-media accounts used by children under 16. The case was filed through advocates Muhammad Jalal Haider and Yahya Farid Khawaja. Dawn
PTA has asked the court to dismiss the petition to the extent that it seeks relief beyond the regulator’s legal jurisdiction. The ministries of information and broadcasting and interior, along with the National Commission on the Rights of Child, have also submitted responses in the case.

The government is also working to expand the coverage of the Employees’ Old-Age Benefits Institution (EOBI). The move is intended to extend social security benefits to a larger number of eligible workers and older citizens.

The government has also included the implementation of the United Nations’ Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing (MIPAA) among its priorities. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also called on young people to respect and support senior citizens. He stressed the importance of caring for older family members and ensuring that they receive the assistance they need.
The prime minister further urged federal and provincial governments, civil society organisations and the private sector to work together on initiatives aimed at improving the quality of life of senior citizens.

items.title: Call of Duty Gets Its Own Counter-Strike-Style Mode as Modern Warfare 4 Adds Collateral
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Modern Warfare 4 Collateral mode is Activision’s most direct answer yet to Counter-Strike and Valorant. Players start each round with a pistol and some cash and spend what they earn on everything else.
It is a clear change of philosophy for a series built on fast respawns and custom loadouts. In Collateral, a bad round can leave a team with nothing but pistols.
How Collateral works
The structure will be familiar to Call of Duty’s Search and Destroy fans. Teams take turns attacking and defending two bomb sites, and every player begins a round with the same pistol and the same starting amount of money.
Cash comes from eliminating opponents and completing objectives. Between rounds, players spend it on armor, perks, equipment, and weapons.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Modern Warfare 4 Collateral mode is Activision’s most direct answer yet to Counter-Strike and Valorant. Players start each round with a pistol and some cash and spend what they earn on everything else.
It is a clear change of philosophy for a series built on fast respawns and custom loadouts. In Collateral, a bad round can leave a team with nothing but pistols.
How Collateral works
The structure will be familiar to Call of Duty’s Search and Destroy fans. Teams take turns attacking and defending two bomb sites, and every player begins a round with the same pistol and the same starting amount of money.
Cash comes from eliminating opponents and completing objectives. Between rounds, players spend it on armor, perks, equipment, and weapons.
The rule that shapes everything is simple. Purchased gear is lost on death, but the money stays. A player who dies can keep a full wallet and rebuild next round, which makes every purchase a bet.
What Activision removed
Collateral is defined as much by what is missing as by what is added. According to the source report, the mode has no respawns, no automatic health regeneration, no custom classes, and almost no killstreaks.
The one exception is the Recon UAV, which the whole team must buy together. Other reports describe this as a team-buy option for pooling cash.
Perks stay, but in a smaller set, and each one must be bought with in-game money. The shop covers five areas.
Category
Available items
Armor and perks
Armor Vest, Battle Hardened, Lethal Reach, Fast Hands, Ghost
Equipment
Flash Grenade, Molotov Cocktail, Fragmentation Grenade, Stim, Smoke Wall, Riot Shield
Pistols
Silenced Pistol, Revolver, Akimbo Pistols, Power Pistol
Primary weapons
Shotgun, Light Machine Gun, Marksman Rifle, Silenced SMG, Agile SMG
Tier One weapons
Semi-Automatic Rifle, High Damage Rifle, Burst Fire Weapon, Silenced Rifle, Sniper Rifle
Team purchase
Recon UAV
Not Call of Duty’s first attempt
This is not the first time the series has borrowed from the genre. Treyarch’s Heist mode in 2018’s Black Ops 4 also put a cash-based spin on competitive play, and Modern Warfare 4 will include a second cash-based mode, Inflation, a Team Deathmatch-style mode from last month’s beta.
Two economy modes in one game suggest Activision sees money management as a feature to build on, not a one-off experiment. Collateral is the stricter of the two.
What is still unclear
Several questions are open. Modern Warfare 4 launches on October 23 for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC, but a report from Insider Gaming says Activision described Collateral as PC-only, so console availability is not confirmed.
Activision has also not said whether Collateral will appear in Call of Duty esports. The mode is aimed at Search and Destroy players and the more competitive part of the community, but there is no confirmation of an esports role. The starting cash amounts and earning rates have not been published either.
Adding a buy menu is the easy part. Counter-Strike and Valorant have spent years tuning their economies so that a losing team can still compete without being locked out entirely.
Collateral has to get that balance right with Call of Duty’s own weapons and pacing, and with no way to see the numbers before launch. The mode’s success will depend on how much cash a lost round leaves a team and how fast one strong round can snowball.
It also tests a bigger idea. Call of Duty is taking the best-known structure from its competitors and removing its own signature features to fit it. If players embrace that, the series may keep building modes that look less like Call of Duty and more like its rivals.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Two weeks from now, every new passport applicant in Pakistan will get an e-passport. There will be no machine-readable option, whether the application is filed in Lahore or at the consulate in New York.
The government says the change will curb fraud. Whether it also makes getting a passport easier is a separate question, and the answer depends on work that has little to do with the chip.
What changes on October 15
Pakistan will stop issuing machine-readable passports nationwide from October 15, 2026, according to a public notice from the Consulate General of Pakistan in New York. Reports say passport offices have been told to stop processing new machine-readable applications from that date, which makes October 14 the last day to apply for one.
Passports already issued are not affected right away. They stay valid until their expiry dates, but they will not be renewed in the same format. Holders will apply for an e-passport when the time comes.
A short runway for a large change
The decision itself is only a few months old. On June 19, a meeting chaired by the interior minister at the Passport and Immigration Headquarters in Islamabad decided in principle to move fully to e-passports. That was 118 days before the cutoff.
The timeline was not settled for much of that period. An August report said no cutoff date had been set. A circular to passport offices followed in September, and the New York consulate published the date on September 25.
A change that touches every future passport holder at home and abroad arrived with about four months of notice. That is quick, and it puts pressure on the offices and missions that must apply it.
Two reasons for one decision
The government has given two reasons, and they point in different directions.
The interior minister said at the June meeting that a complete move to e-passports would eliminate fraud and forgery in passport issuance. The chip supports that aim. According to the passport directorate, it stores a facial image, personal details, a unique identification number, and a digital signature, following ICAO standards. Pakistan’s e-passports also carry laser engraving and infrared and ultraviolet security features.
The New York notice makes a different promise. It says the transition should make immigration processing faster and more efficient.
A harder-to-forge document answers the first goal. It does not answer the second. Speed depends on queues, payments, processing times, and delivery, and the notice gives no figures for any of them.
The rest of the plan
Those operational pieces were part of the same June meeting. The government decided to run all passport offices on a cashless system from the first of the following month and to shift online applications to the PakID app. Officials also said preparatory work for home delivery of passports, inside Pakistan and abroad, was complete.
This is why the October 15 date matters beyond the format of one document. Applying for, paying for, and receiving a passport are all moving to digital channels at once. If any link in that chain fails, applicants will feel it before they notice the chip.
What overseas Pakistanis should do
The rule applies at missions abroad, where renewals often happen close to travel dates, visa deadlines, and school terms. Anyone with a passport that expires soon should check requirements with their nearest mission before applying.
The notice does not list e-passport fees or processing times. Those details will decide whether the change is a minor adjustment or a real hurdle for people who have to renew on a deadline.
The test comes after October 15
A cutoff is easy to announce and easy to measure. A smooth passport office is harder to build and harder to judge from the outside.
Pakistan has set a firm date for the chip. The less visible work will decide how citizens experience the change: the payment systems, the application platform, and the delivery network. The clearest way to judge the reform would be for the passport directorate to publish processing and delivery times in the weeks after the switch.
Until then, the date shows that the government is serious. It does not yet show that the system is ready.

items.content:
UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi on Thursday ordered the formation of a team to investigate an incident involving a Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv a day earlier.
The UAE’s official WAM news agency said Al Shamsi ordered the formation of an investigation team comprising specialised public prosecutors.
The team will investigate the incident involving Flydubai flight FZ1073, which was travelling from Dubai International Airport to Tel Aviv before being diverted and landing safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, WAM reported.
Al Shamsi directed the team to gather information and evidence and establish the facts, circumstances and motives surrounding the incident, including determining whether it was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose or involved prior planning or direction, according to WAM.
UAE judicial authorities have jurisdiction to investigate the incident under applicable legislation because the aircraft is registered in the UAE and flies under its flag, WAM reported.
Accordingly, UAE law applies to crimes committed aboard the aircraft even when they occur outside the country’s territory, it added.
On Wednesday, FZ1073, carrying 174 passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv, made an emergency landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in the northwestern Saudi city of Tabuk after an altercation was reported in the cockpit.
Flydubai said “an altercation occurred in the flight deck,” adding that crew members aboard the aircraft secured the plane and diverted it safely to Saudi Arabia.
Airport officials said both the captain and first officer were injured and taken to a hospital following the incident. All passengers and crew were reported safe and accounted for.
Saudi Arabia’s National Transport Safety Centre later said its safety investigation team had begun work on the incident and was coordinating with relevant authorities to determine the circumstances, examine aviation safety aspects and collect related information and evidence.
The airport said the passengers later departed Tabuk aboard an alternative aircraft provided by Flydubai.
