items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The Ministry of Information on Wednesday rejected the Afghan Taliban minister’s allegations against Pakistan as “self-rhetorical lies”, saying the statements aimed at externalising the regime’s internal problems reflected its “despair and frustration” in dealing with its own issues.
Fighting between the Afghanistan Freedom Front and the Taliban resumed on Tuesday morning, Sept 29, in Nuristan’s Kamdesh district, Afghanistan International reported citing informed sources, adding that the clashes began with a Taliban attack.
Meanwhile, the Taliban Defence Ministry said its operation against armed opponents in Kamdesh had ended, claiming that 41 people were killed and 62 others detained.
In a statement posted on X, the ministry’s fact-checking account described the latest allegations by the Taliban’s “so-called Minister for Borders” and other “mouthpieces” as “self-rhetorical lies” aimed at diverting attention from what it called serious internal oppression, dissent and instability.
Calling the Afghan Taliban a “non-inclusive and non-representative regime”, the ministry said it had imposed itself on the Afghan people through “force and oppression”.
𝐅𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐂𝐡𝐞𝐜𝐤 | 𝐌𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 & 𝐁𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐝𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠
◼️ The latest allegations by so called Minister for Borders and other mouthpieces of the Taliban regime seeking to attribute the fighting in Nuristan to Pakistan are self rhetorical… pic.twitter.com/S4z5EYre5K
— Fact Checker MoIB (@FactCheckerMoIB) September 30, 2026
“These comical statements to externalise their internal issues and follow-up rhetoric directed towards Pakistan actually reflect the despair and frustration in handling their own issues,” it said.
The ministry further said the Taliban remained “willingly oblivious” to what it described as their “un-Islamic abetment of terror”, adding that the group was acting as a proxy for a “Hindutva design” for the sake of the interests of some of its leaders.
“This rentier approach of destabilising the region for money as a proxy of agencies is leading the Taliban only towards a self-destructive path, devoid of dignity and honour,” the statement said.
Read: Pakistan rubbishes Afghan Taliban claim of captured post as 'false and fabricated'
The statement came after Taliban Borders, Tribes and Tribal Affairs Minister Noorullah Noori warned Pakistan, saying Islamabad should learn from Afghanistan’s history and that Taliban opponents would be “defeated” if they chose war.
Speaking on Wednesday at a meeting with Kuchi elders from six provinces, Noori said those seeking to destabilise Afghanistan would face “serious consequences”.
Referring to the tensions, Noori said: “Pakistan’s army and intelligence services should understand the people of Afghanistan from a historical, ideological, political and practical perspective.”
Taliban opponents, including the Afghanistan Freedom Front, National Resistance Front and United Front of Afghanistan, have stepped up attacks against the Taliban in recent months.
Criticising the group’s political and military opponents, including the National Resistance Front, the minister said Taliban opponents had stood alongside what he called “occupiers” during the presence of US and Nato forces in Afghanistan but now spoke of fighting for freedom.
This is not the first time the Afghan Taliban regime has levelled allegations against Pakistan. In the past, it has accused Pakistan of facilitating infiltration, carrying out airstrikes and smuggling weapons into Afghanistan, allegations that Islamabad has repeatedly rejected.
According to security officials, the Afghan Taliban regime has been providing sanctuary, support and patronage to terrorist groups. They said documented evidence contradicted Kabul’s repeated denials and pointed to an entrenched terrorist network operating from Afghan soil.
Also Read: 'Frivolous and baseless': Pakistan rejects Taliban claims of involvement in Nuristan violence
Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.
Security officials estimate that up to 70 per cent of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.
In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.
The United Nations estimated the strength of TTP in Afghanistan at around 6,000 to 6,500 terrorists. UN reporting had also documented more than 600 terrorist attacks against Pakistan during 2025, including attacks launched from Afghan territory.
According to Pakistani security officials, the TTP had established training facilities in Afghanistan’s Kunar, Nangarhar, Khost and Paktika provinces.
The government has maintained that the issue was fundamentally one of Pakistan's national security and that continued attacks from Afghan soil cannot be addressed through denials alone.
Pakistan says it expected the Taliban regime to fulfil its commitments by taking verifiable action against terrorist groups operating from its territory rather than defending or denying their presence.

items.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) on Wednesday extended the deadline for filing income tax returns for 2026 to October 15, in consideration of "requests from various trade bodies and tax bar associations".
In a notification posted on X, FBR said that "the Federal Board of Revenue is pleased to communicate that the date of filing of income tax return for Tax Year 2026, for the persons who are required to file their returns by September 30, 2026, is hereby extended up to October 15, 2026 in view of the requests from various trade bodies and tax bar associations.”
Read: FBR extends tax return deadline till Oct 31
pic.twitter.com/BNK9aSTcV5
— FBR (@FBRSpokesperson) September 30, 2026
The FBR has been under pressure to broaden Pakistan's narrow tax base and meet ambitious revenue targets set under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund, making digitisation and taxpayer facilitation central to its stated reform agenda in recent years.
Read More: FBR achieves Rs1.71tr tax target
For the current fiscal year, the government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have agreed on the annual tax target of Rs15.263 trillion. This requires a 17.4% increase over last year's receipts. Unlike in the past, the IMF has made it binding to meet tax targets and the approval of its sixth loan tranche hinges on achieving the H1 target.
Provinces have promised to give a little over Rs1 trillion in grants to the federal government for defence and water projects, subject to the condition that the FBR collects Rs15.263 trillion in revenues. The government has also taken revenue and enforcement measures of over Rs1 trillion in the budget to enable the FBR reach the target.
According to provisional statistics, the tax authority got over Rs685 billion in income tax, falling short of the two-month target by a wide margin of Rs74 billion. The income tax collection was also Rs29 billion less than the last fiscal year, marking negative growth of 4%.
For the second consecutive month, the sales tax collection remained higher than the target. The FBR received Rs719 billion worth of sales tax, exceeding the target by Rs85 billion. The sales tax collection was also 14%, or Rs86 billion, higher than last year.
Of the total, Rs496 billion, or 69%, of sales tax was generated at the import stage. In the budget, the government has changed the law in order to collect sales tax at market prices of goods, instead of factory-gate prices, for numerous items. This has reduced chances of tax evasion but has broken the value-added chain.
The collection of federal excise duty stood at Rs118 billion, which was almost equal to the target and Rs3 billion higher than the last year. Customs duty collection hit Rs198 billion, which was slightly lower than the target and equal to the previous year's receipts.

items.author: Ankush Das
items.content:
Today’s brief: does voice help Meesho sell?The challenge of taking AI products to millions of Indian users is making them work across budget smartphones, multiple languages, and patchy networks while keeping costs in check. At Inc42’s inaugural ‘The CTO Summit 2026’ in Bengaluru, executives discussed how they are tackling these barriers to wider adoption.
Speaking during the session, “Building AI Systems For Indian Scale”, executives from ShareChat and Moj, Meesho, Rapido, and Shadowfax outlined their approaches, from voice-led shopping assistants to tools that help delivery workers locate customers.
Rapid changes in AI models add another challenge: companies need infrastructure that allows them to switch providers without rebuilding their applications.
Nitin Jain, CTO at ShareChat and Moj, said companies should avoid becoming tied to a single model or approach. “If we get married to one particular kind of model or approach, that’s not going to work,” he said.
ShareChat focuses on infrastructure that lets teams replace models, reuse contextual information, and assess performance when switching providers, he added.
Jain also outlined how India-specific constraints have shaped the company’s technology. Its users often rely on mid-range phones and limited bandwidth, while the business needs to support multiple languages and deliver a competitive experience despite lower monetisation levels. These requirements have driven investments in data processing and recommendation systems designed to serve a large user base while keeping costs in check.
Making Product Discovery More Accessible
At Meesho, adapting to users’ needs has included developing Vaani, a voice-led shopping assistant that helps shoppers express what they want to find.
Anand Jain, head of engineering at Meesho, said the feature was designed to help users, particularly those with limited digital experience, navigate product discovery.
Meesho reported 22% higher conversions among Vaani users than non-users in some Tier III and IV cohorts. The feature was activated by 1.5 Mn users in its first month, he said.
Notably, the focus on understanding shoppers’ intent also featured in Flipkart’s session at the summit earlier in the day, with CPTO Balaji Thiagarajan outlining how the company is combining search, conversational interactions, voice, and visual inputs to personalise product discovery.
Meesho is also exploring open-weight models and testing on-device AI to manage the cost of serving a large user base. Jain said the company is testing how processing AI requests on phones affects memory, battery life, and the user experience, particularly on lower-end devices.
Keeping AI Costs In Check
Rishikesh SR, cofounder of Rapido, said the company has built software layers that allow teams to work with different models and established rules for their use, while giving employees access to advanced AI models.
He put the combined model acquisition and people costs at less than four paise per ride, stressing that experimentation needs accountability as usage grows.
At Shadowfax, AI is being used to address a longstanding logistics problem: matching incomplete or inaccurately written addresses to precise locations.
Vaibhav Khandelwal, cofounder and CTO of Shadowfax, said the company uses historical delivery data and AI-based address matching to improve location identification. Incorrect pincodes and unclear addresses can delay deliveries and increase logistics costs, he said, putting the impact at around 1% of the company’s margins.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
AI is helping PhonePe reduce operating costs and speed up internal workflows, with specific audit processes shortened from four days to three minutes and about 22 person-days saved per app release, according to its CTO Srijon Biswas.
Speaking to Inc42 CEO and cofounder Vaibhav Vardhan at the inaugural ‘The CTO Summit 2026’, Biswas detailed the gains across operations and software development, alongside the fintech’s more cautious approach to consumer-facing AI.
During the session, “How PhonePe Is Combining DPI And AI For 720 Mn+ Users”, Biswas said the company now has more than 200 AI agents, used by around 1,600 employees daily.
In operations, PhonePe has deployed AI in specific workflows to reduce costs and manual work. Biswas said voice agent costs have fallen to about one-sixth of their previous level.
In certain KYC and onboarding workflows, the company has also removed the need for human agents. “We have been able to reduce 20 agents to zero,” he said, clarifying that the employees were moved to other functions.
Some audit processes have seen substantial time savings, with Biswas saying the time required has fallen from four days to three minutes.
Speeding Up Software Development
The savings extend to software development, where PhonePe has reduced the work required for each app release by about 22 person-days. Biswas said the frequency of releases makes the cumulative saving significant.
In one development workflow, a change that passed from a product manager to a designer and then a developer previously took two to three days. Automated code generation has reduced this to around 10 minutes, he said.
Unit testing on the app has similarly fallen from three days to about half a day.
Biswas said the company broadly evaluates its AI efforts across three areas: operational efficiency, developer efficiency, and consumer-facing applications.
While operational efficiency focuses on reducing costs, developer efficiency is about becoming faster “without losing my quality bar”, he said.
A More Cautious Consumer AI Approach
PhonePe is taking a more cautious approach to consumer-facing AI, where applications require greater engineering effort and careful consideration of the user experience.
One example Biswas cited allows users to ask questions about their transaction history in plain English, instead of navigating multiple filters.
For a regulated fintech, AI agents also need to operate within existing access controls. Biswas said PhonePe took time to build a layer that ensures models and automated systems follow the same role-based access rules.
“We decided to go slow a little bit and made sure that we have a layer which even when a model or any automation wants to access these systems, they have to go through the same roles,” he said.
The emphasis on access controls also featured in a separate discussion at the CTO Summit, where PhonePe and OceanBase executives highlighted fresh data and clear access rules as foundations for reliable AI applications.
Looking ahead, Biswas expects AI to change the composition of engineering teams, with greater emphasis on senior judgement and decision-making.
“You need more people who can make stronger decisions and get them correct more often,” he said.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by 14 paisas and Rs1.89 per litre, respectively, for October 1.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs387.40 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs400.35 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol and HSD by Rs1.49 and Rs2.73 per litre, respectively, for September 30.
Read: Govt decreases petrol by Rs1.49, diesel by Rs2.73 for Sept 30
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
Earlier this month, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices ‌rose on Wednesday and were on track for significant monthly gains on stalled US-Iran peace talks and tightening US fuel markets.
The Brent November futures contract, which expires on Wednesday, was up $1.12, or 1%, at $103.71 a barrel at 10:50 am EDT. The more active December contract was up $2.65, or 2.8%, at $98.81. US West Texas Intermediate crude was ​up $1.98, or 2.2%, at $91.98.
Qatar said on Tuesday it hopes that shuttle diplomacy between Tehran and Washington can ⁠lead to a breakthrough.
Goldman Sachs estimates Gulf oil exports have recovered to 23.3 million barrels per day over the last week, in line with their 2025 average, as exports doubled in September, it said in a note on Tuesday.
"Recovering crude flows should temper supply-driven ‌price pressures, ⁠although persistent product shortages and elevated freight costs are likely to keep the broader energy market tight," analysts at Japanese bank MUFG said.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) received 7,546 complaints from telecom consumers against various telecom and cellular operators during August 2026, with 7,159 complaints, or 94.87 percent, successfully resolved.
According to official data, the complaints were filed against different segments of the telecom sector, including cellular mobile operators (CMOs), Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL), long-distance international (LDI) operators, wireless local loop (WLL) operators, and internet service providers (ISPs).
PTA Receives Over 7,500 Telecom Complaints in August, Resolves 94.87pc
Cellular mobile operators accounted for the largest share of complaints, reflecting their significant subscriber base. A total of 6,774 complaints were lodged against CMOs during the month, of which 6,488, or 95.8 percent, were resolved.
Among individual cellular operators, Jazz received the highest number of complaints at 3,592, with 3,463 complaints (96.41 percent) resolved.
Telenor received 1,099 complaints, of which 1,043 (95 percent) were addressed. Meanwhile, 1,183 complaints were registered against Zong, with 1,148 (97.04 percent) resolved.
See Also: PTA Seeks Power to Reopen Telecom Merger Approvals Under Proposed Competition Rules 2026
Ufone received 869 complaints during August, of which 806, or 92.75 percent, were resolved.
The PTA also received 105 complaints related to basic telephony services, resolving 97 cases, representing a resolution rate of 92.4 percent.
Meanwhile, internet service providers (ISPs) received 667 complaints, of which 574, or 86.1 percent, were addressed during the month.
The data highlights the volume of consumer complaints across Pakistan’s telecommunications sector and the rate at which these complaints were addressed by the concerned operators during August 2026.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday hailed China's “extremely important” role in promoting global peace, stability and development and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its all-weather strategic cooperative partnership with Beijing.
Addressing a ceremony marking the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China, the prime minister said it was a pleasure for him to attend the National Day event and extended his “heartfelt congratulations” to Chinese President Xi Jinping and the people of China.
He described the occasion as a day to pay tribute to the perseverance, unity and indomitable spirit of the Chinese nation.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its all-weather strategic cooperative partnership with China, describing the enduring bilateral friendship as a bond built on mutual trust, unwavering support and deep affinity… pic.twitter.com/r9DnITtx0U
— Prime Minister's Office (@PakPMO) September 30, 2026
“China has an extremely important role in global peace, stability and development,” he said.
Under the “far-sighted leadership” of President Xi, China had made unprecedented progress in human development, science, technology and innovation, the prime minister said.
He said 2026 held “special significance” in the shared journey of Pakistan and China, as the two countries were celebrating the 75th anniversary of the establishment of their diplomatic relations.
2/2
The ambassador also highlighted the expansion of practical economic cooperation, saying bilateral trade reached $16.44 billion from January to July, up 13.4 percent year-on-year.
He said bilateral agricultural trade stood at around $830 million during January-August, an… pic.twitter.com/LMniVk2A0y
— Prime Minister's Office (@PakPMO) September 30, 2026
“Our hearts are connected and beat together,” he said, adding that the friendship between the two countries had withstood every test of time, whether earthquakes, storms or floods.
The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), he said, was a manifestation of the two countries’ longstanding friendship and their shared commitment to a more prosperous and developed future for their people.
“We are now entering the next phase of CPEC, CPEC 2.0,” he said.
Read More: Can China help Pakistan? myth and reality
The new phase would focus particularly on industrialisation, special economic zones, information technology and artificial intelligence, agriculture, mining and minerals, he added.
The prime minister described progress in the agriculture sector as “extremely welcome” and said the first group of 1,000 Pakistani agricultural graduates had completed their training in China.
“Another group of 1,000 people is ready to go to China,” he said, describing the programme as a valuable investment in the capabilities and future of Pakistan’s youth.
PM Shehbaz said Pakistan-China relations were a cornerstone of the country’s foreign policy.
Recalling his conversation with President Xi in May, he said that it had represented a strong reaffirmation of the countries’ longstanding friendship.
“We are fully committed to implementing the important understandings reached between the leadership of the two countries,” he said.
“A sincere friend living in a distant land makes a distant land close,” the prime minister said while quoting a Chinese saying, adding that the words best reflected the friendship and closeness between the two countries.
Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong also addressed the ceremony, describing China and Pakistan as “all-weather strategic cooperative partners”.
He said Pakistan was playing an increasingly important role internationally because of its principled position, broad global vision and high level of diplomatic insight.
Pakistan had supported multilateralism and international cooperation and played an important role in safeguarding peace and security in the region and beyond, the ambassador said.
Also Read: Pakistan, China agree on BJC framework
He said PM Shehbaz had “firmly defended Pakistan’s national interests” during his address to the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
Pakistan’s position on international and regional issues was presented at the UN General Assembly and appreciated by the international community, he added.
“The remarkable journey of the past 75 years proves that China and Pakistan are friends who have stood by each other in times of joy and sorrow,” Jiang said.
He said the two countries had always stood by each other like brothers.
The ambassador said PM Shehbaz had always attached great importance to practical cooperation between China and Pakistan in various fields.

items.author: Rana Yasif
items.content:
The Punjab Assembly's Standing Committee on Human Rights and Minorities Affairs on Wednesday unanimously approved the Christian Marriage Bill 2026, proposing to repeal the century-old Christian Marriage Act 1872 and introduce a modern legal framework governing marriages among the Christian community.
The bill was earlier presented in the Punjab Assembly on April 27, but drew widespread criticism from Christian religious leaders and legal experts, who argued that wider reforms covering divorce, annulment, inheritance, child custody, and separation were also needed, along with proper consultation with the Church during the drafting process.
The meeting, chaired by Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz MPA Raheela Khadim Hussain, evaluated the bill moved by MPA Philebos Christopher.
Christopher told the committee that the proposed legislation was meant to consolidate and modernise the existing legal framework for Christian marriages, strengthen protection of consent and ensure greater legal clarity in matters relating to matrimonial law.
He said a key proposal in the bill was to fix the minimum marriageable age at 18 years for both men and women in the Christian community.
Read: Christian marriage bill faces opposition
According to the MPA, the minimum age for a Christian marriage is 16 years for a boy and 13 years for a girl under the existing law.
“The proposed law would also require both parties to a Christian marriage to identify as Christians,” he highlighted during the meeting.
As per details outlined by the minority lawmaker, the bill proposes a formal procedure for marriage, including written notice before the marriage and a public announcement of the intended marriage. It further seeks to make the registration of Christian marriages with the Union Council and the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) mandatory.
He lamented that registration of Christian marriages with the Union Council and NADRA was not possible under the existing law.
Under the proposed legislation that is now up for approval of the Punjab Assembly, marriages would be allowed to take place in all churches registered with the government of Punjab, according to Christian rites and procedures. It also proposes authorising religiously educated pastors of government-registered churches to solemnise Christian marriages.
“Designated pastors or marriage registrars appointed by the government would also be empowered to conduct marriages,” Christopher explained further.
“A Christian marriage would have to be solemnised in the presence of at least two witnesses, while a formal record of marriages would be maintained through marriage registers and prescribed forms.”
He also emphasised that unlike the existing legal framework, the proposed law would impose no restriction on the day or time for holding a marriage ceremony.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has proposed expanding its regulatory powers by seeking the authority to review and reconsider approvals granted for major telecom sector transactions, including mergers, acquisitions, and other arrangements, at any time if market conditions change.
The proposal has been included in the draft Telecommunication Competition Rules 2026 prepared by the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication (MoITT). Under the existing draft framework, PTA would be allowed to revisit decisions related to telecom transactions where new facts, regulatory concerns, or changes in market conditions emerge.
According to the proposed amendments, PTA has suggested removing the one-year limitation period currently mentioned for reviewing a transaction approval. The regulator has proposed new wording under which it may reconsider, modify, or withdraw its determination or approval whenever deemed necessary in light of changed market circumstances, material facts, regulatory considerations, or any subsequently available information.
The proposed changes would apply to telecom sector transactions that could affect competition, market concentration, infrastructure access, consumer welfare, or continuity of telecom services.
PTA may examine several factors while reviewing such transactions, including spectrum concentration, infrastructure sharing and access, interconnection arrangements, barriers to market entry, national roaming obligations, consumer impact and service continuity.
The framework covers transactions involving changes in company control, spectrum consolidation, mergers, acquisitions and joint ventures within the telecom sector.
Under the proposed rules, PTA may issue a no-objection certificate (NOC), impose transaction-specific conditions, require operational safeguards or make recommendations to relevant authorities after completing its review.
The draft also proposes that PTA may monitor compliance with competition rules and require telecom licensees to provide necessary information, reports or data.
The move comes as regulators worldwide continue to focus on maintaining competition in telecom markets, particularly as consolidation, infrastructure sharing, and spectrum management become increasingly important with the expansion of advanced connectivity services.
If approved, the amendment would significantly change the timeline for regulatory oversight of telecom transactions by allowing PTA to revisit previously approved deals beyond the current one-year review window.

PTA Proposes Tougher Competition Rules for Telecom Operators With Significant Market Power

items.content:
Electric two-wheeler (E2W) manufacturer Simple Energy has raised $180 Mn (₹1,750 Cr) in its Series C funding round. The round was led by Dr. Arokiaswamy Velumani Family Office and saw participation from the Haran Family Office, and angel investor Amit Mishra. Simple Energy’s founder and CEO Suhas Rajkumar and cofounder and CFO Ankit Gupta also participated in the equity funding round.
The Bengaluru-based startup intends to utilise the fresh capital to support its next phase of growth by fueling key functions like marketing, supply chain, R&D and hiring.
The Series C round materialised three months after the EV startup closed its ₹250 Cr Series B funding round. The round was also led by the family office of Dr. Arokiaswamy Velumani. With Simple’s largest funding haul till date, its total equity raise now stands at $264 Mn (₹ 2,530 Cr).
“Our priorities are a new manufacturing facility, higher production, an expanded distribution and service network, and the next generation of products. The continued support of our early investors reinforces our progress as we work to make Simple Energy one of India’s leading full-stack E2W companies,” CEO Rajkumar said.
Founded in 2019 by Rajkumar, Simple Energy was later joined by Shreshth Mishra and Gupta. The EV startup currently sells three electric scooters — Simple One, Simple OneS and Simple Ultra.
In a bid to expand beyond its high-performance Simple One model, the startup recently launched the Simple Wave, an affordable family scooter series starting at ₹1.10 Lakh (ex-showroom). However, on the sales front, the EV maker’s monthly sales for August stood at 1,508, contracting 9.5% from 1,666 E2W scooters sold in July.
The startup currently operates 80 sales outlets across 60 Indian cities, including Delhi, Patna, Hyderabad, and Chennai. It claims to be commanding a production capacity of 10,000 units per month.
It is also looking to expand its dealer-operated store network to 160–170 outlets by March 2027.
The startup reported revenue of around ₹171 Cr in FY26, as the founder claimed, up sharply from roughly ₹44 Cr in FY25. Rajkumar attributed the growth largely to the underlying demand for its products rather than any single growth lever.

items.author: Ankush Das
items.content:
AI applications need up-to-date information and clear rules on what they can access to work reliably at scale, according to executives speaking at the inaugural edition of Inc42’s ‘The CTO Summit 2026’ in Bengaluru.
The challenge is to make information spread across databases, data warehouses, and documents available to these applications while preserving its quality and controlling its use.
The panel, ‘Building The Data Foundation For AI At Scale’, featured PhonePe’s head of engineering, merchant payments, Kisalay Ranjan; OceanBase’s GM, India business, Bhanu Jamwal; and Fibe’s CTO Anil Sinha. Digio EIR Kshitij Shah moderated the discussion.
Ranjan said PhonePe tracks where data comes from and sets rules for its use at the level of individual data elements, across both transactional databases and data warehouses. Adding these controls later through individual applications becomes increasingly difficult as companies automate more tasks, he said.
“The power is first ensuring that whatever data we are consuming is of high quality,” Ranjan said.
Teams must also know where information is stored, whether it is sensitive, whether its use meets compliance requirements, and which applications can access it. PhonePe uses shared platforms to maintain a single authoritative source of sensitive customer data instead of duplicating it across systems, he added.
Jamwal said organisations’ data is spread across separate systems used to process transactions, run analytics, and support AI searches, alongside data lakes. Companies deploying AI agents need to connect these sources so their applications can retrieve current information quickly and accurately, he said.
“There would be a time when you need high accuracy for your agents,” Jamwal said. “You need one single solution which can give you data sitting at one point, but more importantly, give you that fresh data with low latency.”
The OceanBase executive advocated a unified data layer to make information across these systems available to agents and other AI applications with minimal delay.
At IPO-bound lending tech startup Fibe, the focus includes extracting useful information from documents that vary in format, such as records from hospitals, clinics, and educational institutions.
Sinha said Fibe uses generative AI to extract signals from these documents and feeds the signals into its existing credit model, rather than asking GenAI to make lending decisions. He said the model has expanded from 8,000 to 23,000 variables as the company incorporates more information.
Beyond data quality and access, companies also have to balance AI model performance against cost and response times.
Ranjan said smaller models running within PhonePe’s own technology environment can suit tasks that involve large volumes and require quick responses. More advanced models may be useful for tasks requiring stronger reasoning, with the choice depending on the use case, model availability, and cost.
The emphasis on underlying systems also featured in a separate session at the CTO Summit, where Razorpay’s SVP of engineering Prabhu Ram cautioned that AI cannot compensate for weak engineering foundations, including inadequate systems for monitoring performance and detecting problems.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
India’s startup ecosystem entered a more selective funding environment in Q3 2026, with investors deploying capital more cautiously amid macroeconomic pressures, elevated valuations and a sharper focus on high-conviction bets.
According to Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026’, homegrown new-age tech ventures raised $2.2 Bn between July and September, up 5% from the $2.1 Bn raised in the year-ago quarter. However, the number of deals fell 13% from 240 in Q3 2025 to 210 in the just-concluded quarter.
The median ticket size remained flat year-on-year (YoY) at $3 Mn. The funding momentum was largely driven by four mega deals (rounds of at least $100 Mn) versus just one such transaction in Q3 2025. The quarter also saw two startups, Emergent and Astrotalk, enter the coveted unicorn club against zilch in the year-ago period.
It must be noted that Q3 2025 was the weakest third quarter for the Indian startup ecosystem since 2023, when startups managed to raise just $1.7 Bn across 205 deals.
At $2.2 Bn, funding in Q3 2026 was well below $3.4 Bn in Q3 2024 and the eight-quarter historical average of approximately $2.7 Bn. The number of active unique investors also fell 24% YoY to 511 in Q3 2026 from 676 in Q3 2025.
In terms of venture capital (VC) activity, 3one4 Capital recorded the highest deal volume with 19 transactions, followed by Rainmatter, Zerodha’s corporate investment arm, with 16 deals and IvyCap Ventures with 15.
That said, macroeconomic pressures, including higher inflation, softer household spending, high fuel prices, and weak equity market performance, continued to impact capital deployment across the ecosystem this year.
Nevertheless, cumulative startup funding since 2014 has crossed $176 Bn across more than 12,600 deals.
Now, let’s take a look at some of the trends that dominated startup funding activity last quarter.
Access Free Report
Growth Stage Startups Lead Q3 Funding Trend
A defining structural shift during the quarter was the distribution of venture capital between growth and late stage startups. Growth stage funding (Series A and Series B) emerged as the primary driver of quarterly funding growth. Capital deployed at this stage rose 38% YoY to $1.1 Bn across 90 deals. This is despite a meagre 4% YoY uptick in median ticket size for investments at this stage to $8.3 Mn.
Late stage funding (Series C and above) declined 10% YoY to $994 Mn across 27 deals. Even though the quarter recorded more mega deals, the median late stage ticket size fell 18% to $18 Mn, pointing to more cautious deployment at the top end of the funding cycle.
Early stage funding also weakened, falling 18% YoY to $164 Mn across 93 deals, a 15% decline in deal volume. However, the median ticket size increased 20% YoY to $1.2 Mn, suggesting that investors were writing larger cheques for a smaller set of early stage companies.
Aina, Dextr AI, DeHaat Honest Farms and BCT Ventures each raised seed rounds exceeding $3 Mn during the quarter, highlighting continued investor appetite for startups with strong early traction or a differentiated proposition.
Access Free Report
AI Dominates Sectoral Charts
Big ticket deals made a comeback in Q3 2026. Four mega deals materialised during the quarter compared with just one in the year-ago period. Here’s a sneak peek:
Emergent ($130 Mn): The AI startup raised $130 Mn from Creaegis, Khosla Ventures, SoftBank, Lightspeed and Y Combinator, entering the unicorn club
River ($120 Mn): The electric vehicle (EV) maker secured $120 Mn from Elev8 Venture Partners, Claypond Capital, Anicut Capital, Alteria Capital, InnoVen Capital and Stride Ventures
Navi ($100 Mn): The IPO-bound fintech startup raised $100 Mn from Prosus in its first institutional funding round
Pixxel ($100 Mn): The spacetech company raised $100 Mn from Temasek, 360 ONE Asset, IMM Investment, Radical Ventures and growX ventures
The distribution of these rounds across AI, mobility, fintech and spacetech suggests that high ticket investor conviction is broadening beyond consumer internet businesses.
On the sectoral front, AI attracted the most capital in Q3 2026, raising $438 Mn across 35 deals. Funding surged 265% YoY, while deal volume rose 35% YoY. Emergent’s $130 Mn round and Ema’s $77 Mn Series B were two of the largest AI funding rounds during the quarter.
However, concerns over high entry valuations are tempering investor enthusiasm for AI startups.
According to Inc42’s survey of 85+ institutional investors, 63% said Indian AI valuations had risen beyond comfortable levels. While 32% expected a meaningful correction over the next 18 months, 31% described valuations as mildly elevated but supported by actual revenue.
Only 12% considered current valuations fully justified, while 25% said it was too early to assess.
Notably, capital deployment across the AI segment in Q3 2026 was largely concentrated around startups building in the application layer of AI.
So, it was no surprise that 39% of the surveyed investors favour vertical AI applications over base infrastructure. While 23% of investors see greater opportunities in AI hardware startups, only 14% believe sovereign AI models offer meaningful investment opportunities.
Access Free Report
Beyond AI, cleantech attracted $433 Mn across 23 deals, more than three times the year-ago figure. EV startups accounted for 57% of cleantech deals, led by River, Yulu and Ultraviolette.
Deeptech startups raised $290 Mn, up 176% YoY, even though deal volume remained flat at 28. Spacetech companies accounted for 21% of overall deeptech funding.
Conversely, traditional capital magnets (fintech and ecommerce) saw a more muted response from investors this quarter. Although the highest number of funding deals (44) materialised in the ecommerce segment, total funding in the sector tanked 31% YoY to $245 Mn. Meanwhile, fintech funding fell 11% YoY to $249 Mn across 13 deals.
Bengaluru Leads The Startup Squad
Bengaluru widened its lead as India’s primary startup hub in Q3 2026. Startups based in the city raised $1.4 Bn+ across 80 deals during the quarter, up 157% YoY. The city also accounted for 64% of the total startup funding.
Delhi NCR ranked second with $301 Mn (down 27% YoY) across 53 deals, followed by Mumbai with $223 Mn (down 64% YoY) across 34 deals.
Bengaluru’s funding total was driven by large rounds raised by Emergent, River, Pixxel, Navi, Yulu, Ultraviolette, and Ultrahuman. Bengaluru also accounted for 65% ($189 Mn) of the $290 Mn raised by Indian deeptech startups, buoyed by big-ticket rounds of Pixxel, Airbound and QNuLabs.
Bengaluru has long maintained a dominance in venture capital activity in the world’s third largest startup ecosystem and, per investors, will continue to be the favoured spot for their capital deployment.
Given the underlying deeptech shift within the ecosystem, more than half of the investors surveyed by Inc42 identified Bengaluru as the startup hub best positioned to lead India’s deeptech ecosystem by 2030. Meanwhile, 25% backed Chennai and Hyderabad followed at 20%.
Access Free Report
A Quarter Of Investor Exits
The quarter remained especially favourable for early investors, as consolidation and IPO activity remained rampant. The Indian startup ecosystem recorded 22 M&A deals during the quarter under review, up 69% YoY from 13 in Q3 2025.
Prominent completed transactions included upGrad’s Unacademy acquisition for $200 Mn, Imarticus Learning’s BELLS buyout for $84 Mn, and Housing.com’s acquisition of Aurum PropTech for $48 Mn.
With this, total quarterly startup M&As remained above 20 for three consecutive quarters in 2026, with 24 in Q1 and 28 in Q2.
Meanwhile, the likes of ESDS Software Solution, Klassroom, Shiprocket and Rentomojo made their public market debuts during the quarter. All in all, six (nearly 50%) new-age tech stocks listed on the Indian bourses in Q3, giving investors many lucrative exits.
Here are some of the notable investor exits of this season:
KKR-managed Vertical Holdings, which commanded a 73.78% stake in LEAP India, sold its stake worth ₹1,998.6 Cr via the IPO.
Accel India, RentoMojo’s largest institutional shareholder, sold 78.47 Lakh shares for ₹317 Cr, registering a gross return multiple of 8.6X.
Shiprocket’s early investor 500 Global generated 77.6X returns, while Tribe Capital sold shares worth ₹120 Cr at a return multiple of 7.6X.
The Beginning Of A New Startup Exit Cycle?
Of the 85+ investors surveyed by Inc42, 72% said they held late stage portfolio companies with some degree of IPO readiness. Of this group, 57% described their companies as “moderately ready” but waiting for a more favourable market window, while 15% said that their portfolio companies were actively preparing to file their respective draft red herring prospectuses (DRHPs).
Despite the expanding IPO pipeline, only 32% of investors expect domestic IPOs to generate the largest share of their portfolio liquidity over the next 24 months. Secondary buyouts emerged as the preferred route, with 38% of investors expecting them to deliver the highest liquidity volume.
Meanwhile, listed new-age technology companies delivered mixed but broadly positive returns. Between July 1 and September 25, Inc42’s New Age Tech Index gained 3.38%, outperforming the Nifty 50 by nearly seven percentage points.
As of September 25, 2026, Inc42’s New Age Tech Index included 65 of the 72 new-age tech stocks listed on India’s mainboards that had traded for more than a month during the quarter.
Excluding Nasdaq-listed MakeMyTrip and Freshworks, the combined market capitalisation of the remaining India-listed new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage touched $177 Bn, or ₹16.47 Lakh Cr, during the quarter.
India’s startup ecosystem ended Q3 2026 on a cautiously resilient note. While funding grew 5% YoY, fewer deals and a decline in active investors pointed to a more selective market.
Capital increasingly favoured growth stage ventures, AI, deeptech and cleantech, while fintech and ecommerce saw muted investor interest. At the same time, rising M&A activity and a growing IPO pipeline signalled improving exit opportunities. However, secondary buyouts remain the preferred liquidity route among investors, suggesting that public markets alone may not drive the next phase of exits.
Edited by Shishir Parasher
Creatives by Abhyam Gusai

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Generative AI is compressing the traditional travel-booking journey, with travellers combining questions about flights, transit visas, and card offers in a single conversation, according to MakeMyTrip Group CTO Sanjay Mohan.
Speaking at Inc42’s inaugural ‘The CTO Summit 2026’, Mohan said this behaviour requires travel platforms to rethink both their search experience and the technology connecting different parts of a booking.
His session, “What Lakhs Of AI Conversations Are Teaching MakeMyTrip About How India Travels”, explored how conversational AI is changing the way users express their travel needs.
A conventional travel app takes users through a sequence: browsing listings, reviewing a selection, entering passenger details, paying, and receiving confirmation. In a conversation, however, users can bring up requirements associated with several of these stages at once.
Mohan cited the example of a traveller asking for a flight with limits on layover duration, no transit visa requirement, and deals on specific bank cards — all within the same request.
For the platform, answering that request means bringing together information that users would otherwise find across separate screens.
Moving Beyond Keywords And Filters
MakeMyTrip is adapting its data systems to handle these overlapping requirements, Mohan said. This includes using knowledge graphs, which connect related information, and search technology that interprets meaning rather than relying solely on exact keyword matches.
For instance, a traveller asking for a “serene getaway” should be able to find suitable properties even if their listings do not contain that phrase.
“If you tell me, ‘I want a vacation in a very serene getaway’. If no one has put that text, then you will not be able to find it,” Mohan said. “I have to understand what you really mean by ‘serene’.”
The shift towards interpreting intent also featured in Flipkart’s session at the Summit, where CPTO Balaji Thiagarajan discussed moving beyond keyword-led search to combine conversational interactions, voice, visual inputs, and content feeds.
For MakeMyTrip, voice is another part of this shift. Mohan said the platform is expanding speech-to-text and text-to-speech capabilities to serve users in smaller cities where typing can be a barrier. Voice interactions already account for a significant activity in Tier III and IV regions, he added.
How Myra Handles Travel Queries
MakeMyTrip uses its in-house AI assistant Myra to handle conversational interactions across customer touchpoints. Mohan argued that the company’s travel expertise helps it address the detailed questions involved in choosing a trip.
“Travel is a very experiential buying thing. You don’t want to look at a toothpaste from five different angles. But if you’re booking a hotel room, you want to know what the view from the window looks like,” he said.
Myra comprises around 10-12 specialist AI agents covering different travel needs, including flights and accommodation. A central coordinating system routes tasks to these agents and brings their responses together.
Balancing Quality, Speed & Cost
Mohan said using the largest AI models for every task increases both costs and response times. MakeMyTrip instead combines frontier models with open-source and open-weight alternatives, depending on the task.
He also emphasised the need for detailed evaluation sets to test whether each specialist agent produces relevant answers.
“A vertical applied AI can be only as good as your eval set. And therefore, for every expert, flights and hotels and holidays, there has to be a very rich set of evals. Otherwise, you will not know whether the answers are relevant,” Mohan said.
These checks cover live prices and availability, the relevance of responses, and whether the system retains details shared earlier in a conversation.

A day earlier, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif approved the procurement of 45 against the demanded 65 bulletproof vehicles for the security of SCO leaders, according to the cabinet division, which also claimed the move was endorsed by the deputy PM and the ministries of foreign affairs and interior. The approval sparked outcry on social media.

items.content:
The federal government on Wednesday defended its procurement of 45 bulletproof vehicles for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Council of Heads of State (CHS) Summit scheduled during August-September 2027 in Islamabad, saying the vehicles were essential to meet security requirements for the high-profile international gathering.
A day earlier, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif approved the procurement of 45 against the demanded 65 bulletproof vehicles for the security of SCO leaders, according to the cabinet division, which also claimed the move was endorsed by the deputy PM and the ministries of foreign affairs and interior. The approval sparked outcry on social media.
The Cabinet Division, in a statement shared by Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on X, rejected what it described as “sceptical and unwarranted” criticism in the press and on social media over the purchase.
Pakistan is currently chairing the SCO Council of Heads of State, and the government said the upcoming summit would be among the country’s most significant international events.
GOVERNMENT OF PAKISTAN
CABINET SECRETARIAT
CABINET DIVISION
PRESS RELEASE
Purchase of Bulletproof Vehicles for SCO’s CHS Summit, Islamabad 2027
Certain sceptical and unwarranted comments have appeared in the press and social media
on the purchase of 45 bulletproof vehicles by…
— Khawaja M. Asif (@KhawajaMAsif) September 30, 2026
“The summit, scheduled to be held in Islamabad during August-September 2027, will be the most high-profile gathering, second only to the 1973 OIC Summit. This will give Pakistan an opportunity to further raise its stature and honour amongst the comity of nations,” the press release stated.
According to the statement, the summit would bring together heads of state and government as well as senior representatives of international organisations, making secure and reliable transport arrangements a critical requirement.
The government said security considerations were particularly important given Pakistan’s prevailing security environment and what it described as threats from hostile external elements.
“At present, the latest model bulletproof vehicles available with the Cabinet Division are a few 2016 models, which are far below the standards required for the summit,” the statement said.
Read: Relaxation from ban on new vehicles sought
The decision to procure 45 bulletproof vehicles was considered at several forums, according to the Cabinet Division, which said the number had been determined on the basis of the “bare minimum requirement”.
The government clarified that the bulletproof vehicles would only form part of the overall transport arrangements for the summit. Around 300 other non-bulletproof vehicles would be rented for logistical requirements, it added.
The Cabinet Division said the summit represented an important opportunity for Pakistan to enhance its international standing and showcase its capacity to host major diplomatic events.
Describing the SCO summit as a prestigious international gathering, the government said its significance should not be “underestimated, trivialised or politicised”.
It also urged citizens to view the hosting of the summit as an honour for Pakistan and support efforts to organise the event according to international standards.
The SCO, which includes major regional countries, holds its Council of Heads of State meeting annually to discuss cooperation and key regional and international issues.
Yesterday, the Cabinet Division told the meeting that in compliance with the premier’s directive, 15 BMW 760i xDrive (VR9) bulletproof sedans, costing Rs3billion, would be procured in addition to the 30 bulletproof Mercedes-Benz Maybach S680 Guard (VR10) sedans, for which the Economic Coordination Committee had already approved a supplementary grant of Rs6.60 billion.
Read more: Dar chairs SCO council meeting, calls to turn shared vision into tangible outcomes
Appalled by the approval, former senator Mushahid Hussain Sayed took the government to task.
In a post on X, the former upper house representative said, “Government of Pakistan plans to buy 45 bulletproof luxury limousines for Rs 9.6 billion for 9 leaders of SCO for Summit in 2027 for ‘security’ reasons, but security problem has worsened with Pakistan on top of World Terrorism Index as worst-hit country in world! Where’s the CT (counter terrorism) strategy?”

Former Sindh governor Mohammad Zubair Umar also assailed the purchase on social media.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has clarified the procedure for taking action against registered businesses that fail to connect with the required electronic monitoring systems. Under the new mechanism, business premises that do not comply with the prescribed monitoring, video surveillance, or Digital Eye systems may be sealed after completion of the legal process.
According to the FBR, the process will begin with a written report from an Assistant Commissioner or an officer of a higher rank. The report will lead to an inquiry by the Commissioner Inland Revenue. After completing the inquiry, the Commissioner will submit the findings to the Chief Commissioner.
FBR Clarifies Procedure to Seal Businesses Not Linked to Electronic Monitoring System
The Chief Commissioner will then issue a written order on whether the business premises should be sealed. The authorities can seal the entire premises or a specific portion, depending on the circumstances of the case.
Before sealing the premises, the concerned business owner or person must receive a copy of the sealing order. The FBR may also seek assistance from the police if required during the enforcement process.
A sealed business will remain closed until its required monitoring system is successfully connected with the FBR’s system. To reopen the premises, the business will have to pay the prescribed penalty and install the required monitoring system.
The FBR will also ensure technical support during the installation process. Its technical team will be present when the monitoring system is installed and integrated with the tax authority’s system.
Once the installation and integration process is completed, the Commissioner Inland Revenue will issue a certificate within three days confirming compliance. This certificate will allow the business to proceed with the process of reopening its premises, subject to the applicable requirements.
See Also: FBR Simplifies Income Tax Return Filing for Tax Year 2026
The FBR has already introduced electronic production monitoring, video analytics and Digital Eye systems in several sectors. These include tiles, sugar, bottled water, packaged milk and other specified industries.
The tax authority has been expanding the use of digital monitoring tools to improve oversight of production and business activities. The latest procedure provides a formal enforcement mechanism for businesses that fail to comply with the monitoring requirements.
The FBR has also indicated that the electronic monitoring framework could be extended to more businesses and manufacturers in the future. This means additional sectors may be brought under the monitoring system as the tax authority expands its digital oversight mechanisms.

items.summary: OEMs raised the prices of their smartphones by 16 percent on average in India in the first half of 2026, according to Counterpoint Research. On the other hand, OnePlus raised the prices of its phones by 8 percent on average, which is half the industry average. The report highlights that the sub-Rs. 10,000 price segment increased by 29 percent on average. This budget segment was the most affected by the price hikes in India in H1 2026. Meanwhile, the below-Rs. 45,000 price segment was the least affected, recording a 9 percent price rise on average in the given period.

The federal government’s e-Office platform has reportedly faced operational issues, causing delays in official work across several ministries and affecting routine administrative activities.
According to sources, complaints regarding disruptions and slow performance in the e-Office system have been emerging since yesterday, with multiple federal ministries experiencing difficulties in processing official files and completing day-to-day tasks.
The slowdown has affected digital workflows, resulting in delays in government correspondence, file movement, and other administrative procedures that are carried out through the electronic system.
Citizens visiting government offices have also faced difficulties as some services and routine matters could not be processed due to the disruption.
The e-Office system operates through the government’s intranet network and is widely used by ministries and departments for digital file management and official communication.
The platform falls under the domain of the National Information Technology Board (NITB), a subsidiary organization of the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication responsible for implementing and supporting digital solutions for government institutions.
The reported disruption has also raised concerns regarding the reliability of government digital infrastructure as Pakistan continues to expand digital transformation initiatives across public-sector departments.
Officials using the system have reportedly expressed frustration over the slowdown, as delays in the platform have affected routine administrative operations.
The cause of the technical issue and the timeline for complete restoration of normal services were not immediately available.
The incident highlights the growing importance of ensuring stable and resilient digital systems as government departments increasingly shift from traditional paperwork to technology-driven administrative processes.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
Update | September 30, 15:53 IST
Home interior materials platform Gravity has raised around $15 Mn (around ₹142.7 Cr) in a mix of equity and debt funding in a round co-led by 3one4 Capital and Info Edge Ventures.
The round saw participation from Alteria Capital, Genesia Ventures and a group of angel investors. However, the startup did not disclose the bifurcation of equity and debt in the total amount
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen Gravity’s technology, distribution and key-account infrastructure, expand into new categories, build its brand and support working capital requirements as it scales.
Gravity aims to streamline sourcing for designers, studios and other interior businesses. It is a full-stack platform for interior materials, bringing together businesses across categories such as kitchens and wardrobes with shared technology, distribution and operating infrastructure.
Going forward, Gravity plans to expand into categories such as doors and windows, lighting, wall surfaces and home automation. It aims to use the same customer relationships and operating infrastructure across these categories.
Original | July 10, 15:43 IST
Former Livspace cofounder and India CEO Saurabh Jain has teamed up with former Livspace CBO Lalit Mittal to launch a new venture, Gravity, sources told Inc42.
The startup, which is expected to come out of stealth mode in four to five months, aims to solve material procurement and supply chain challenges faced by the broader interior design industry, enabling independent designers, design studios and interior platforms, the sources said.
It is building a house of brands for premium homes and aims to position itself as a full-stack platform for home interior materials. The startup does not intend to operate as a marketplace or a supplier, they added.
Gravity has also held early talks with investors like 3one4 Capital and InfoEdge to raise funding. It is looking to raise $15 Mn (about ₹143 Cr) in a mix of equity and debt, the sources said.
Questions sent to Jain and Mittal didn’t elicit any response till the time of publication.
Before starting Livspace, Jain cofounded DezignUp, which was acquired in 2014. An IIT Delhi alumnus, he was a management consultant in the early years of his career.
Mittal, who is also an IIT Delhi alumnus, was the AVP at Meesho before joining the home interior unicorn in 2019.
Both Mittal and Jain quit Livspace in February this year. Their exit came a few days after the unicorn laid off 1,000 employees, or 12% of its workforce, amid its AI push.
Currently, India’s home interior materials market is estimated to be worth $20 Bn. Gravity will compete with AllHome, which was founded by PharmEasy cofounders and recently raised ₹200 Cr from Bessemer Venture Partners.
The development also comes at a time when a growing number of founders are starting new ventures. Earlier this week, Inc42 reported exclusively that BharatPe cofounder Shashvat Nakrani is set to join Dubai-based luxury ecommerce platform Luxury For You as its cofounder and CEO.
Earlier this week, former Dream11 CTO Amit Sharma announced the launch of a new AI startup. Dunzo cofounder Mukund Jha launched Emergent last year and the vibe coding startup is currently in talks to become a unicorn.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
Engineering education needs to move beyond writing code and equip students to understand how entire software systems work, according to speakers at Inc42’s inaugural ‘The CTO Summit 2026’.
Speaking during the panel ‘The Great Engineering Reset: Teams, Talent & Leadership After AI’, the participants called for greater emphasis on logical thinking, philosophy, and systems design to prepare engineers for work increasingly shaped by AI.
Moderated by Accel VP Anagh Prasad, the panel featured Naukri.com CTO Arvind Heda, Acko cofounder and CPTO Vishwanath Ramarao, and IDfy CEO Ashok Hariharan. The discussion examined how AI is changing engineering roles and team structures, with automation taking over more routine coding and quality assurance work.
Hariharan said this shift raises a longer-term question: how will engineers develop the expertise to design and manage complex systems if they spend less time building them?
Drawing on his “old-school engineering background”, he recalled how earlier generations of engineers had to grapple with problems such as memory management. Over time, tools and software layers made those underlying processes less visible to developers.
“There’s a lot of crap code that gets written,” he said, warning that AI-assisted development could amplify existing quality problems if engineers assume the tools can do everything for them.
The concern extends beyond the code being produced today to the capabilities engineers will develop over the coming years. Hariharan joked that engineers can advance into leadership roles before fully understanding the responsibilities of a lead or manager, eventually becoming VPs.
“I think we are in danger of the same kind of thing now,” he said.
Hariharan said engineering teams have fewer mid-level engineers, leaving a skills gap between senior architects and junior developers. This raises a question about how junior engineers will learn to design systems.
“How do you teach systems design when they don’t necessarily code on a daily basis?” he asked.
The growing demands of testing also surfaced in a separate discussion at the CTO Summit on how AI is changing coding and review. Cashfree Payments CTO Ramkumar Venkatesan said the company’s spending on virtual environments for testing now exceeds its spending on AI tools.
For Hariharan, the shift towards AI-generated code increases the need for architects who understand deployment, security, and scaling. Automating routine implementation work does not remove the responsibility to ensure that the resulting systems are reliable and secure.
“I think there’s a huge number of security flaws that are going to be exposed. I am pretty sure that’s a fear every CTO has,” he said.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Human rights lawyer and activist Jalila Haider on Wednesday received the 2026 Right Livelihood Award, which has also been dubbed the “Alternative Nobel Prize”.
The Right Livelihood Award was established in 1980, when Swedish-German stamp collector Jakob von Uexkull sold part of his collection to fund it, after the foundation behind the Nobel Prizes refused to create new awards in the fields of environmental protection and international development.
According to a press release from the Sweden-based Right Livelihood Foundation, Jalila received the award “for breaking barriers, as the first female lawyer from her Hazara community, to challenge ethnic, state and patriarchal persecution, guided by the conviction that no human being is illegal”.
Read: The travails of the Hazara community
The press release noted that the award goes to "women and women-led organisations confronting the world’s most entrenched power structures: authoritarian rule, patriarchal violence, and unchecked AI development".
The 2026 @RightLivelihood Award goes to women and women-led organisations challenging entrenched power structures:
🏆 Jalila Haider @Advjalila
🏆 Rural Women's Assembly @womensassembly
🏆 Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association @GYLA_CSO
🏆 Timnit Gebru @timnitGebru pic.twitter.com/4v29s5Y5au
— Right Livelihood (@rightlivelihood) September 30, 2026
The foundation's website noted that Jalila was a Hazara human rights lawyer and activist protecting Pakistan’s most vulnerable communities against state repression, patriarchal norms and ethnic violence, adding that in 2018, she led a seven-day hunger strike against the targeted killing of Hazaras that forced the army chief to negotiate directly with Hazara women, resulting in a sustained decrease in attacks against the community.
Right Livelihood Foundation said that Jalila was a founding member of the Women’s Democratic Front (WDF) and helped pioneer Balochistan’s first Women’s March, a street mobilisation that sparked discussions on feminism across the deeply patriarchal region, further adding that her organisation “We the Humans” had also helped over 400 widows of terrorism victims gain financial independence.
Read More: Feminism in the context of digital media
🧵 She's the first female Hazara lawyer in her community's history — and for over a decade she's defended the people her country tries hardest to erase.
Meet @Advjalila, a 2026 @RightLivelihood Laureate from Pakistan. pic.twitter.com/dfDrVuvUBw
— Right Livelihood (@rightlivelihood) September 30, 2026
It added that by "combining legal work with street activism and community empowerment", Jalila had "secured justice for thousands targeted or ignored by those in power, specifically ethnic, gender and religious minorities, as well as refugees", further noting that her law firm had also helped restore freedom of movement for more than 600 political activists and human rights defenders.
According to the press release, "for over 45 years, the Right Livelihood Award has honoured and supported courageous people leading the way to a just, peaceful and sustainable world for all".
A prominent US artificial intelligence researcher and two women-led rights groups were also recognised.
The jury said in a statement it had chosen US artificial intelligence researcher Timnit Gebru “for challenging concentrated power in artificial intelligence and pioneering digital technology rooted in justice, lived experience and human agency”.
Gebru is known for her work examining how biases influence AI, and in 2017, Gebru co-founded Black in AI.
The foundation also gave the nod to the Rural Women’s Assembly — a grassroots movement of more than 178,000 small-scale farmers across 11 Southern African nations.
The Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association, which the jury described as “Georgia’s oldest and most prominent human rights organisation”, was also honoured.

items.author: Staff
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Some of the most valuable skills in Pakistan have traditionally been practiced behind closed doors.
A woman embroiders a dress for a wedding. Another makes pickles from a recipe passed down through generations. Someone turns clay into beautiful pottery, teaches children after school or creates products by hand that would easily find buyers if they could reach the right market. The talent is there. So is the hard work. What has often been missing is a way to take that talent beyond the home and connect it with opportunity.
For millions of women, especially those living in underserved communities, entering the formal marketplace has never been easy. Physical distance, limited mobility, lack of market access and unfamiliarity with digital tools can turn a valuable skill into something that remains largely invisible beyond the immediate community.
Technology is changing that. PTCL’s Ba-Ikhtiar initiative was built around the belief that connectivity can do more than bring people online. It can help people take their skills, ideas and ambitions further.
The journey began in Haripur, where 100 women were given an opportunity to build on the skills they already possessed. In partnership with the Pakistan Poverty Alleviation Fund (PPAF), PTCL trained the participants in areas such as digital marketing, financial literacy and entrepreneurship.
The objective was not to change who these women were or what they knew. It was to give them the means to turn what they knew into something more. And the results began to speak for themselves.
Women who had once relied primarily on local networks started exploring digital marketplaces, building online businesses and presenting their products to customers beyond their immediate surroundings. Some went even further. Farhat ul Ain and Marrium Hussain took their embroidery to GITEX 2024 in Dubai, giving international audiences an opportunity to see the skill and craftsmanship that had originated in Haripur.
It was a small but significant shift: from making something for someone they knew to creating something that could reach someone they had never met. That is the promise of digital inclusion.
It is also why Ba-Ikhtiar has continued to evolve. What began with a focused cohort in Haripur has expanded to women in underserved communities across Pakistan. The programme now covers a broader range of livelihoods, from stitching, pottery and handicrafts to food preservation, online tutoring and organic cosmetics.
The digital component has evolved alongside it. Women are being introduced to practical skills that can help them navigate the online world with greater confidence, from communicating online to accessing essential digital services and understanding online safety.
Because having a product is only one part of running a business. Knowing how to photograph it, promote it, communicate with a customer, manage a transaction and protect oneself online can be just as important.
This is where PTCL’s vision for connectivity comes into focus. A connected Pakistan is not simply one where more people have access to a network. It is one where connectivity creates possibilities. Through Ba-Ikhtiar, PTCL is working to make that possibility more tangible for women.

items.author: Ankush Das
items.content:
AI coding tools are generating code faster, shifting more of engineers’ attention towards designing systems, reviewing output, and testing whether software works reliably.
During a discussion titled ‘How Engineering Changes When AI Writes The Code’ at Inc42’s inaugural ‘The CTO Summit 2026’ in Bengaluru, panellists described how AI is changing engineering work beyond code generation, from the time spent on design and review to investment in testing infrastructure. This shift is also prompting teams to rethink productivity: more code does not necessarily mean better products or faster releases.
The panel discussion was moderated by Kshitij Shah, EIR at Digio.
Jitendra Agrawal, executive VP of engineering at JioHotstar, said engineers are spending more time on design and review, with greater emphasis on brainstorming before implementation.
He said AI allows teams to attempt features they had previously set aside but cautioned against claiming large productivity gains without evidence.
Pankaj Goel, CTO of LeadSquared, said AI can quickly inflate conventional measures such as pull requests per developer and lines of code without establishing whether teams are performing better.
“Some of these metrics get diluted with AI use and get inflated very, very fast,” he said. Speed to production, stability, availability, and customer impact, he added, are better indicators of engineering performance.
Testing Takes A Larger Role
At Cashfree Payments, spending on virtual environments for testing now exceeds spending on AI tools, according to CTO Ramkumar Venkatesan. The company keeps token spending constrained and ties it to returns, he said.
Cashfree has automated 97% of its test cases, he added, allowing its testing team to focus more on performance and security testing.
The emphasis on validation echoed a point raised by Razorpay’s SVP of engineering Prabhu Ram in another session at the summit: AI cannot make up for weak engineering foundations, including inadequate systems for monitoring performance and detecting problems.
Rethinking Access To AI Tools
Beyond measuring output and validating code, companies are also adjusting how employees access AI tools.
Thiyagaraj T, director of engineering at Eightfold, said the company moved from fixed AI budgets for employees to automatic top-ups after its initial approach resulted in high underutilisation.
“The common theme is that we want to democratise usage,” he said.
HR and operations teams now use higher plans than some engineers, he added, reflecting adoption beyond product and engineering.
The discussion highlighted why code generation alone offers an incomplete picture of AI’s value. Assessing the gains also requires accounting for design, review, testing, and the time it takes to deliver software that works reliably for customers.
