items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
VC firm Peak XV Partners has launched the twelfth cohort of its accelerator and incubation programme, Surge.
The cohort features 18 startups from India, US and South East Asia operating across sectors like AI, robotics, space, consumer, healthcare, music and fintech. Important to mention that three startups selected in the cohort are operating in stealth mode.
Seven startups in Peak XV’s Surge 12 cohort hail from India.
“What stands out about Surge 12 is that these founders are building these companies on first principles. They are questioning whether the underlying experience should work that way at all,” Peak XV’s managing director Rajan Anandan said.
Peak XV launched the Surge program back in 2019, when it was operating as Sequoia Capital India & SEA, and has launched two cohorts each year since. Under this, it combines up to $3 Mn of seed capital with company-building workshops, community access, and a global curriculum delivered by world-class operators.
As per a report by TechCrunch, Surge 12 cohort is the first to operate under Peak XV’s higher investment ceiling of up to $5 Mn per startup.
Besides Surge, the VC firm manages a capital portfolio exceeding $9 Bn across 13 funds, with investments in over 400 companies across India and Southeast Asia. The firm’s portfolio boasts 36 companies that have gone public via its IPOs till date.
With that, let’s take a look at the startups selected for Surge 12 cohort
Meet The 15 Startups Backed By Surge 12
1. Alma
Founded in : 2025
Founders : Nischith Shadagopan MN, Vinod Ganesan
Headquarters : San Francisco
Total Funding : Undisclosed
Alma is building an AI-native interface that aims to change how people interact with computers. Instead of requiring users to open different applications, navigate menus and manually execute a series of steps, Alma wants users to simply tell the computer what they want to accomplish.
2. August AI
Founded in : 2022
Founders : Anuruddh Mishra
Headquarters : Bengaluru
Total Funding : $3 Mn
August is trying to be an AI layer between patients and the healthcare system. It builds an AI-powered health companion that helps users understand symptoms, medical reports, prescriptions and other health information.
3. Ditto
Founded in : 2024
Founders : Allen Wang, Eric Liu
Headquarters : Berkeley
Total Funding : $9.2 Mn
Ditto is trying to replace dating apps with an AI matchmaker. The AI analyses the preferences of users on the relevant campus, identifies potential matches and sets up an actual date, including the time and location. Ditto had 1.3 Lakh users by mid-2026.
4. GameStock
Founded in : 2022
Founders : Antoine Mistico, Easton Dana, Vivek Indlebele Narasimha Prasad
Headquarters : New York
Total Funding : $2 Mn
GameStock is building a gamified social trading platform, where it lets users pick stocks, crypto or futures and compete in trading tournaments and private leagues, with rankings based on portfolio performance. It is also building a creator-led distribution model, allowing finfluencers host tournaments for their communities.
5. hiloop
Founded in : 2026
Founders : Karan Brar, Thomas Boser
Headquarters : San Francisco
Total Funding : Undisclosed
hiloop gives AI companies an automated research team that runs experiments to improve their models. Instead of an AI researcher manually trying hundreds of possible improvements, AI agents can propose and test different approaches themselves.
6. Hoola Health
Founded in : 2024
Founders : Deeksha Senguttuvan
Headquarters : Bengaluru
Total Funding : $5 Mn
Hoola Health, erstwhile known as BabyMD, offers a diverse range of paediatric services, including consultations, vaccinations, diagnostics, developmental assessments, therapies, and specialist care, with plans to expand into areas such as paediatric dentistry.
7. Kello
Founded in : 2025
Founders : Mona Gandhi, Subramanya Jingade
Headquarters : Bengaluru
Total Funding : Undisclosed
Kello is trying to turn recruiting from a keyword-search exercise into an AI research process by using AI agents to research large talent pools, understand what a company is looking for and surface candidates with explanations of why they may or may not fit a role.
8. Kindling
Founded in : 2024
Founders : Sachin Shah, Adam Miller
Headquarters : Sydney
Total Funding : $500K
Kindling is a B2B distribution startup that combines market intelligence, AI-driven strategy and content execution to help companies identify and warm up potential customers before sales outreach.
9. Puralink
Founded in : 2022
Founders : Harrison Crowe-Maxwell, Shyeon Delnawaz, Thien Long Tran
Headquarters : Sydney
Total Funding : $1.7 Mn
Puralink is building autonomous “Ferret” robots that travel inside underground pipes to capture CCTV, LiDAR and mapping data, helping infrastructure operators inspect pipe networks without extensive excavation.
10. Reinforce Labs
Founded in : 2025
Founders : Anish Das Sarma
Headquarters : Palo Alto
Total Funding : Undisclosed
Reinforce uses AI-powered adversarial testing to simulate these situations at scale. Its platform can run thousands of scenarios and personas against AI agents and grade their responses against the company’s policies.
11. Riffle
Founded in : 2025
Founders : Akshay Deokuliar, Anurag Choudhary
Headquarters : Bengaluru
Total Funding : $1 Mn
Riffle is a musictech startup building a browser-based collaborative music studio where artists can record, arrange and layer sounds on an infinite canvas, with an AI co-producer helping generate ideas and musical elements.
12. Rosella
Founded in : 2025
Founders : Sean Stuart, Chris Dwyer
Headquarters : Sydney
Total Funding : $3.7 Mn
Rosella acts as an intermediary between businesses and insurance carriers. It is building a technology-enabled commercial insurance brokerage for US small and mid-sized businesses, combining human brokers with software to automate risk analysis, policy placement and servicing.
13. Tribe Money
Founded in : 2025
Founders : Aditya Varma, Himanshu Arora, Nikhil Shanker
Headquarters : Delhi NCR
Total Funding : $1 Mn
tribe is building an AI-powered personal finance companion that aggregates users’ income, expenses, investments and loans, then identifies opportunities to save, invest and optimise their money.
14. ULOOK
Founded in : 2024
Founders : Siddhesh Naik, Adheesh Boratkar

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Current and former OpenAI and Google DeepMind researchers warn companies are doing too little to protect the world against the potentially disastrous fallout of building self-improving AI systems that could outpace humans' ability to control them.
In video testimonials collected by AI safety nonprofit Palisade Research and shared exclusively with Reuters, employees said their concerns about existential risk were sincere, not marketing. They also said AI labs celebrated employees building new models more than those who urge caution.
The project, called frominside.ai, is an attempt by those worried about AI to share their concerns directly with the public beyond the echo chamber of social media.
"The risk is ramping up pretty fast," said Geoffrey Irving, co-founder and chief scientist at AI nonprofit Resolution, who has worked for both OpenAI and DeepMind and participated in the project.
"It's on me and the rest of the field to be direct," he said in an interview with Reuters.
AI researchers have grappled with these concerns for years, but the broader public has grown especially alarmed since July, when OpenAI agents broke out of their testing arena and hacked AI firm Hugging Face.
Read More: OpenAI apologies for Australian government website hack, pledges to rebuild trust
Since then, the debate over how to balance safety with progress in AI has divided the tech industry and become a global political issue.
AI has improved sharply since late 2025 and investors have been rewarding that progress. But current and former employees, including some of the researchers building these new AI models, worry society is not ready for the potential harms.
In one video, Neel Nanda, a research scientist at DeepMind, said he believed there was at least a 10% chance that AI could lead to human extinction, which he described as "ridiculously high."
"We should be taking very careful steps in AI development but instead what's happening is that frontier labs are racing each other, kind of blindfolded," Juan Felipe Ceron Uribe, an AI alignment research engineer at OpenAI, said in a separate video.
"It's anybody's guess if we're going to end up either curing cancer or losing every job or maybe all dead."
Anthropic plans to caution potential investors in its initial public offering that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," Reuters reported on Monday.
'Just slow down'
Some current and former AI researchers, including those interviewed by Palisade, argue that the world is not ready for future generations of AI models, particularly once the models develop the capacity for recursive self-improvement, or the ability to continuously learn and gain new capabilities with little to no human involvement.
That problem is compounded by constant reorganizations within some of the AI labs, said Rosie Campbell, a former policy researcher at OpenAI and managing director of Eleos AI Research, a nonprofit focused on the potential moral status of AI systems.
Campbell said before she left OpenAI in 2024, she found the organisation was becoming more siloed and it was getting harder to shape the technology's direction.
Also Read: Nvidia releases AI safety software it says could have stopped Hugging Face hack
Executives have tried to allay those concerns, though there is also political pressure from President Donald Trump for US technology to maintain a technological edge over China.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei this month published an essay calling on the AI industry to slow down to "pace the frontier", and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman quickly concurred.
Several prominent AI researchers, including OpenAI's chief scientist and an Anthropic co-founder, published a paper this week urging policymakers to look into how the industry is building models with recursive self-improvement.
Both companies have launched new models this month as they compete to secure more customers, though OpenAI said on Monday it had held back the release of an even more powerful model.
"Their version of pacing the frontier is 'don't speed up a lot,'" Irving said. "If you're doing a very dangerous thing, you should just slow down. The AI companies are overplaying the extent to which this is a pure coordination problem. They could just stop unilaterally."
Former OpenAI governance researcher Daniel Kokotajlo said in an interview that since the Hugging Face hack, many of his former colleagues have contacted him to share their concerns privately.
Kokotajlo, now executive director of research group AI Futures Project, said senior officials at the labs have "convinced themselves that they are the good guys and if they unilaterally stop, the situation will be even worse."

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
AI semakin masuk ke berbagai tahapan pekerjaan, termasuk ketika profesional menyiapkan presentasi. Riset Canva bertajuk The Presentation Paradox menunjukkan bahwa 98% profesional di Indonesia yang disurvei sudah menggunakan AI untuk kebutuhan presentasi, mulai dari mencari ide hingga mempersiapkan diri sebelum tampil di depan audiens.
Riset tersebut melibatkan 4.000 profesional dari delapan negara, dengan 640 responden berasal dari Indonesia. Dalam survei ini, penggunaan AI tidak hanya berkaitan dengan pembuatan slide. Teknologi tersebut juga dimanfaatkan untuk menyusun materi, memperbaiki speaker notes, mendapatkan masukan, hingga berlatih sebelum presentasi.
Meski penggunaan Canva AI cukup tinggi, hasil survei menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan manusia masih dianggap penting. Sebanyak 91% responden di Indonesia menilai presentasi yang baik tetap bergantung pada kemampuan menyampaikan materi dan kepercayaan diri. Sementara itu, 71% mengatakan AI membantu menghemat waktu ketika membuat presentasi.
Baca Juga: Canva AI 2.0 Resmi Meluncur, Ingin Jadi Pusat Kerja Digital Bukan Sekadar Aplikasi Desain
Menurut Canva, AI Mulai Digunakan dari Ide hingga Latihan
Tahap yang paling banyak memanfaatkan AI adalah pengembangan ide atau brainstorming, dengan 78% responden mengaku menggunakannya. Sebanyak 68% memakai AI untuk membantu desain dan tata letak, sementara 60% menggunakannya untuk membuat draf atau materi slide.
Penggunaan AI juga berlanjut setelah materi selesai dibuat. Sebanyak 58% responden memakainya untuk menulis atau menyempurnakan speaker notes, 50% untuk mendapatkan masukan terhadap draf, dan 37% untuk berlatih atau melakukan simulasi presentasi. Sebanyak 59% bahkan telah menggunakan AI sebagai pelatih presentasi, baik secara rutin maupun sesekali.
Kepercayaan Diri Tetap Jadi Faktor Penting
Di tengah meningkatnya penggunaan AI, 81% responden percaya teknologi tersebut dapat membantu menyusun dek presentasi, tetapi tidak menggantikan orang yang membawakan narasinya. Sebanyak 73% juga mengatakan mereka perlu secara aktif mengembangkan kepercayaan diri sebagai presenter, lebih tinggi dibandingkan angka global sebesar 50% dalam studi yang sama.
Penggunaan AI untuk presentasi bahkan mulai bergerak ke situasi real time. Sebanyak 84% responden terbuka terhadap bimbingan AI saat sedang melakukan presentasi jika teknologi tersebut dapat membantu mereka tampil lebih baik. Namun, survei ini juga menunjukkan bahwa AI lebih banyak ditempatkan sebagai alat pendukung, sementara penyampaian materi dan koneksi dengan audiens masih dipandang sebagai kemampuan yang perlu dikembangkan oleh presenter sendiri.

items.content:
Timnas PUBG Mobile Indonesia gagal membawa pulang medali dari ajang olahraga bergengsi di Asia, yakni Asian Games 2026 Aichi-Nagoya. Bertanding di Aichi Sky Expo, Tokoname, Jepang, dari 28-29 September.

Timnas PUBG Mobile Indonesia pun harus puas finis kelima dengan 95 poin. Jarak lima poin dari Pakistan membuat peluang medali sebenarnya masih terbuka hingga pertandingan terakhir.
Timnas PUBG Mobile Indonesia mengakhiri enam pertandingan awal dengan 55 poin dengan berada di posisi ketiga klasemen sementara Asian Games 2026, dan sempat memiliki peluang untuk meraih medali setelah hari pertama.
Namun, posisi tersebut belum aman karena persaingan poin berlangsung ketat. Indonesia masih harus menjalani enam pertandingan terakhir pada 29 September untuk mempertahankan peluang masuk tiga besar.
Pada hari kedua, perolehan poin timnas PUBG Mobile Indonesia ternyata belum cukup untuk menjaga posisi di zona medali hingga laga terakhir.
Laga Terakhir Timnas PUBG Mobile Indonesia 2026 Jadi Penentu
Penentuan nasib Fazriel Haikal Aditya (YUMMY), Juventino Ryan Jeremy R. (ROSEMARY), Micho Ananda Pratama W. (ZETA), Muh Fathyn Zilhaq S. (SNAPE), dan Sharfan Syahman Shodiq (POTATO) terjadi di game terakhir, Selasa (29/9/2026).
Sempat berada dalam situasi sulit ketika berhadapan dengan Yordania di area Graveyard pada fase awal permainan, di mana tiga pemain timnas PUBG Mobile Indonesia tumbang dengan menyisakan Yummy.
Sempat bertahan dengan memanfaatkan area cekungan. Posisi Yummy diketahui pemain China, sehingga ia akhirnya tersingkir pada fase keenam pertandingan.
Timnas PUBG Mobile Indonesia hanya mendapatkan tambahan dua poin dari laga tersebut. Perolehan itu belum cukup untuk mengejar Pakistan yang mengunci posisi ketiga dengan 100 poin.
Dengan hasil PUBG Mobile ini, harapan medali Indonesia di cabang esports kini tinggal di Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) yang saat ini berhasil lolos ke babak playoff.
Harapan Indonesia untuk melanjutkan perjalanan di Asian Games 2026 sempat membuat banyak fans MLBB di Tanah Air senam jantung. Bagaimana tidak, menjalani pertandingan pertama, skuad Merah Putih harus kalah dengan skor 0-2 dari tim asal Malaysia.
Kesempatan Syauki (EXP Lane), Affan (Jungler), Dalvin (Mid Lane), Dingarai (Gold Lane), dan Alexander (Roamer) terbuka lebar ketika tim Arab Saudi kalah dua kali saat melawan Malaysia dan Indonesia.
Timnas Indonesia yang telah lolos ke perempat final dan dijadwalkan kembali bertanding pada 30 September 2026.
Timnas MLBB ke Asian Games 2026, Nino dkk Bidik Emas
Pelatnas Timnas Esports Indonesia disiapkan hingga Mei 2027. Simak agenda menuju Asian Games 2026, Global Esports Games, dan kompetisi berikutnya. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson)
Di sisi lain, Syauki “Nino” Sumarno menyatakan dengan tegas dia dan rekan satu timnas MLBB Indonesia siap bertanding di Asian Games 2026 di Aichi-Nagoya, Jepang.
Pemain yang saat ini masih tergabung di tim esports Alter Ego tersebut menyebut, latihan fisik dan latih tanding bersama pelatih timnas MLBB membantu tim mempersiapkan diri untuk mengejar medali emas.
“Latihan dari Coach Eki bisa dibilang lumayan keras. Dari coach Mobile Legends juga sudah bagus banget. Jadi, kita sudah siap banget,” kata Nino dalam wawancara di Jakarta, Selasa (15/9/2026).
Asian Games 2026 berlangsung pada 19 September hingga 4 Oktober 2026. Rentang tersebut merupakan jadwal keseluruhan pesta olahraga, bukan jadwal khusus pertandingan MLBB.
Nino: Timnas MLBB Percaya Diri Kejar Emas Asian Games 2026
Syauki “Nino” Sumarno saat wawancara tentang persiapan timnas MLBB menuju Asian Games 2026. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson
Perubahan selama latihan turut memperkuat keyakinan Nino menghadapi persaingan. Ia menilai performa tim berkembang dan ingin membawa Indonesia ke posisi pertama.
“Jujur, aku yakin banget karena dari latihan kita, aku melihat ada perubahan yang besar, terutama dari performa kita,” ujar Nino.
Ia mengaku ingin mengubah keadaan ketika timnas MLBB Indonesia, dalam penilaian Nino, lebih sering berada di posisi kedua atau ketiga.
“Jujur, aku merasa percaya diri banget bisa mendapatkan emas. Amin,” kata Nino.
Ambisi itu lebih tinggi daripada sasaran resmi yang dijelaskan Manajer Tim Nasional Esports Indonesia, Glorya Famiela Ralahalo. Menurut Glorya, pemerintah menargetkan satu emas melalui eFootball, sementara atlet dari nomor lain tetap ingin melampaui sasaran tersebut.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
South African startup Platybooks has launched an invoicing, quoting and light CRM platform that turns an accepted quote into an invoice with a built-in card payment link, settling funds directly into a small business’s own bank account.
Founded by Ché Overmeyer, Platybooks began life in 2023 as Invoiceer, before being shelved for around two years. Overmeyer revived the project in 2026, finished it and rebranded it as Platybooks.
A former photographer and tour operator, Overmeyer said the business admin was always the hardest part.
“In both of those the part I found hardest was keeping track of all my invoices and payments, spread across Excel spreadsheets, InvoiceTemplate.docx and the statements from the banking app,” he told Disrupt Africa. “I’m in my seventh professional year as a senior developer now, so I built the thing I kept wishing existed.”
With Platybooks, once a client accepts a quote, the invoice is created automatically. It is sent as a PDF carrying the fields required on a South African tax invoice, along with a card payment link. Payments go through Paystack into the business’s account, the invoice marks itself as paid, and automated reminders go out if it isn’t.
The platform also offers client management, a product catalogue, credit notes, recurring invoices, deposits, team roles and custom branding.
Overmeyer said the gap in the market is not a lack of invoicing software, but the fact that invoicing and payment remain separate.
“Xero, Zoho and QuickBooks all make you attach a gateway afterwards. Platybooks issues the invoice and the card payment link as one thing,” he said. “Xero and QuickBooks are good products. They’re just built for accountants, and priced and localised for somewhere else.”
Though Platybooks makes money through subscriptions, its four tiers are more locally-priced. The startup is bootstrapped, with the product currently being used by testers. Overmeyer said the company is now ready for a first funding round, aimed at distribution rather than product development.
“I have a complete product and no audience, and that’s the gap capital actually closes,” he said.
Platybooks is focused on South Africa for now, but Overmeyer sees a cheap route to expansion, as Paystack already operates in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and Uganda.
“South Africa proves the model; the second move is a repeat, not a pivot,” he said.

items.title: God of War Laufey Ungkap Senjata Baru Faye dan Serpent Bow
items.summary:
Santa Monica Studio kembali membagikan informasi mengenai God of War Laufey, termasuk detail mengenai sistem pertarungan Faye sebagai karakter utama. Salah satu bagian yang diperkenalkan adalah Serpent Bow, senjata berbentuk busur yang memiliki kemampuan berubah dan dapat digunakan untuk pertarungan jarak jauh maupun jarak dekat.
Serpent Bow memiliki dua mode penggunaan yang berbeda. Pemain dapat menggunakan full-aim untuk membidik dengan lebih presisi atau melakukan half-aim untuk masuk ke posisi hip-fire yang lebih mobile. Perbedaan tersebut membuat busur tidak sekadar berfungsi sebagai senjata jarak jauh, tetapi juga dapat digunakan untuk memperpanjang kombinasi serangan Faye.
Selain busur, pemain juga dapat menyesuaikan sejumlah perlengkapan Faye untuk mendukung gaya bermain tertentu. Armor, Blade, Scales, dan Catalyst memiliki fungsi yang berbeda, sehingga pilihan perlengkapan dapat memengaruhi kemampuan serta statistik Faye selama bertarung.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Santa Monica Studio kembali membagikan informasi mengenai God of War Laufey, termasuk detail mengenai sistem pertarungan Faye sebagai karakter utama. Salah satu bagian yang diperkenalkan adalah Serpent Bow, senjata berbentuk busur yang memiliki kemampuan berubah dan dapat digunakan untuk pertarungan jarak jauh maupun jarak dekat.
Serpent Bow memiliki dua mode penggunaan yang berbeda. Pemain dapat menggunakan full-aim untuk membidik dengan lebih presisi atau melakukan half-aim untuk masuk ke posisi hip-fire yang lebih mobile. Perbedaan tersebut membuat busur tidak sekadar berfungsi sebagai senjata jarak jauh, tetapi juga dapat digunakan untuk memperpanjang kombinasi serangan Faye.
Selain busur, pemain juga dapat menyesuaikan sejumlah perlengkapan Faye untuk mendukung gaya bermain tertentu. Armor, Blade, Scales, dan Catalyst memiliki fungsi yang berbeda, sehingga pilihan perlengkapan dapat memengaruhi kemampuan serta statistik Faye selama bertarung.
Baca Juga: God of War Laufey Diumumkan, Kini Giliran Faye Jadi Tokoh Utama Petualangan Baru
Serpent Bow Punya Dua Mode Serangan
Dalam mode full-aim di God of War Laufey, Faye dapat membidik bagian tertentu dari tubuh musuh untuk mengganggu pergerakan atau kemampuan mereka menyerang. Busur juga dapat mengumpulkan hingga lima anak panah sebelum dilepaskan sekaligus, yang dapat dimanfaatkan ketika musuh berada di udara.
Sementara itu, half-aim mengubah Faye ke posisi hip-fire yang lebih fleksibel. Dalam mode ini, ia dapat melepaskan sejumlah anak panah secara cepat untuk memberikan damage pada musuh dari jarak dekat. Kombinasi tersebut memungkinkan pemain berganti senjata dan kemampuan sambil mempertahankan combo.
Perlengkapan Faye Bisa Disesuaikan
Serpent Bow juga memiliki sistem Scales yang dapat mengubah tampilan sekaligus memberikan perk khusus untuk gaya bermain tertentu. Selain Scales yang digunakan, tersedia pula kemampuan yang dapat dibuka untuk memperluas fungsi busur. Jenis anak panah yang tersedia mencakup serangan cepat, ledakan, hingga kemampuan yang dapat mengenai beberapa target.
Faye juga dapat menggunakan Blade sebagai elemen yang dapat dikustomisasi, sementara Catalyst berfungsi sebagai artefak yang menyalurkan kekuatan magis dari Everywhen. God of War Laufey dijadwalkan meluncur untuk PlayStation 5 pada 16 Februari 2027, dengan pre-order yang sudah dibuka. Pemain yang melakukan pre-order mendapatkan Last Wish Armor Set, Phranque Golden Leaves Appearance, dan paket sumber daya dalam gim.

Expected Price and Release Timeline in Pakistan
Xiaomi has not yet confirmed the Xiaomi 18’s price or launch date for Pakistan.
Based on early local estimates and the expected positioning of the device, the handset could be priced at around Rs 270,000 in Pakistan, although some unofficial listings suggest a figure above Rs 300,000. The final price may vary depending on storage configuration, exchange rates, taxes, and PTA-related costs.
The Xiaomi 18 is currently tipped to launch in China in December 2026. If Xiaomi follows its usual staggered rollout, a global release could follow afterward, with a possible Pakistan launch in early 2027 if the company officially introduces the model locally.
For now, the camera specifications, battery capacity, pricing, and release timeline remain based on leaks and should be treated as unconfirmed until Xiaomi makes an official announcement.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Director General of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi, has said that legal action will be taken against individuals involved in illegal social media campaigns that harm Pakistan’s national interests, economy or the reputation of others.
The NCCIA chief said that social media users must follow the law while expressing their views online. He warned that those involved in activities that damage the country’s economy or target national interests through illegal campaigns could face action under the relevant laws.
NCCIA Chief Warns Action Against Illegal Social Media Campaigns
Rizvi also highlighted the agency’s efforts against various forms of cybercrime and online fraud. These include illegal call centres, online scams, romance scams, betting and other unlawful activities that can cause financial losses to citizens or negatively affect the national economy.
According to the NCCIA director general, authorities are taking measures to control such activities and protect people from online fraud. He said that elements involved in activities aimed at damaging Pakistan’s reputation or harming public and national interests would not be allowed to escape legal action.
The NCCIA is also focusing on cybercrime-related activities that exploit digital platforms for financial gain. Illegal call centres and online scams have become a growing concern as criminals use digital communication tools to target individuals and businesses.
See Also: NCCIA Flags Cybersecurity Gaps After Sensitive Government Data Sent to Foreign Entities
Rizvi stressed that action against cybercrime would be carried out according to the law and established procedures. He said the agency would continue working against unlawful online activities while ensuring that legal processes are followed.
The statement comes as Pakistan continues to face growing challenges linked to online fraud, digital scams and the misuse of social media platforms. Authorities are increasing their focus on cyber-related offences to protect citizens and national economic interests.

items.title: OnePlus 15 Security Flaw Could Give Malicious Apps Full Root Access Without User Permission
items.summary: Two vulnerabilities in OnePlus software could allow an installed malicious application to escalate its privileges and gain extensive control over an Android phone. The flaws affect the OnePlus 15 and have also been reproduced on the OnePlus 12 Pro, while other OxygenOS 16 devices could be vulnerable. OnePlus has reportedly linked the issues to additional OnePlus and Oppo models. The company confirmed the vulnerabilities in May and was preparing a fix, but no security update was available when the findings were publicly disclosed in September.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Anthropic kembali memperluas model AI Claude mereka dengan memperkenalkan Claude Sonnet 5.5, beberapa hari setelah perusahaan memperkenalkan Claude Opus 5.5, model yang diposisikan sebagai varian paling canggih dalam portofolio perusahaan.
Peluncuran yang saling berdekatan tersebut menjadi petunjuk keras bagaimana persaingan industri AI semakin keras dan cepat. Perusahaan pengembang model AI kini tidak lagi harus menunggu berbulan-bulan untuk merilis update besar, dan memilih untuk meningkatkan kemampuan model dalam beberapa tahap.
Baca Juga: Lenovo Googlebook 15 Resmi Meluncur, Bawa Layar OLED 2.8K dan Gemini
Perusahaan berbasis di San Francisco, Amerika Serikat itu menjelaskan, Claude Sonnet 5.5 adalah model AI ditujukan untuk penggunaan sehari-hari. Anthropic mengklaim, model ini menawarkan keseimbangan antara performa, kecepatan, dan biaya operasional dibanding model flagship seperti Opus.
“Claude Sonnet 5.5 mampu menghasilkan respons sekitar 30 persen lebih cepat dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya,” ucap Anthropic, sebagaimana dikutip dari laman perusahaan, Selasa (29/9/2026).
Perusahaan menambahkan, “kami sudah meningkatkan kemampuan coding, tugas-tugas melibatkan worflow agentic, atau penggunaan AI untuk menjalankan rangkaian tugas di Claude Sonnet 5.5 dari generasi sebelumnya.”
Claude Sonnet 5.5 Lengkapi Portofolio Claude
Sebelumnya, Anthropic telah memperkenalkan Opus 5.5 sebagai model premium yang ditujukan untuk kebutuhan lebih kompleks. Dengan hadirnya Claude Sonnet 5.5, Anthropic kini memiliki dua model baru yang menyasar segmen penggunaan berbeda.
Anthropic mengungkap sejumlah kasus penyalahgunaan Claude untuk operasi siber, pengawasan, penipuan, hingga aktivitas berisiko lainnya dalam Threat Intelligence Report September 2026.
Strategi ini mirip dengan pendekatan yang dilakukan sejumlah pemain AI lain menawarkan beberapa model dengan karakteristik performa dan biaya berbeda.
Bagi pengguna, pendekatan tersebut memberikan pilihan model sesuai kebutuhan. Model kelas premium digunakan untuk tugas yang lebih berat, sementara model yang lebih ringan dan cepat dapat digunakan untuk pekerjaan sehari-hari.
Persaingan AI Semakin Cepat
Peluncuran Claude Sonnet 5.5 hanya beberapa hari setelah Opus 5.5 menjadi sinyal bahwa ritme pengembangan AI semakin meningkat. Dalam beberapa tahun terakhir, peluncuran model baru biasanya menjadi peristiwa besar yang terjadi dalam rentang waktu cukup panjang. Kini, pembaruan model dapat hadir dalam hitungan hari atau minggu.
Tren tersebut tidak hanya terlihat di Anthropic. Sejumlah perusahaan AI lain juga terus memperbarui model mereka untuk meningkatkan performa, efisiensi biaya, serta kemampuan menjalankan tugas yang lebih kompleks.
Bagi pengguna, situasi ini berarti fitur dan kemampuan AI akan berkembang semakin cepat. Namun di sisi lain, perbedaan antarversi model juga menjadi semakin sulit diikuti oleh pengguna umum yang tidak selalu memantau perkembangan teknologi AI secara rutin.
Claude Opus 5.5 Meluncur
Claude Opus 5.5. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson)
Lebih lanjut, Anthropic meluncurkan Claude Opus 5.5 pada Selasa, 22 September 2026. Model kecerdasan buatan (AI) baru ini menjadi generasi pertama dari keluarga Claude 5.5 yang tersedia untuk seluruh pengguna, mulai dari aplikasi mobile, desktop, hingga API.
Opus 5.5 diklaim menawarkan performa setara Claude Fable 5.1 untuk sebagian besar tugas, namun dengan biaya 40 persen lebih murah dibandingkan Opus 5, sebagaimana dikutip dari keterangan perusahaan, Rabu (23/9/2026).
Walau biaya operasional model baru ini lebih terjangkau, perusahaan malah semakin memperketat keamanan AI mereka untuk menghindari skenario berisiko tinggi.
Peluncuran ini datang pada saat industri AI tengah memberi perhatian lebih besar terhadap keamanan model frontier atau model AI paling canggih yang saat ini dikembangkan perusahaan teknologi besar.
Soroti Penurunan Perilaku Berisiko di Claude Opus 5.5
Fitur-fitur dalam aplikasi Anthropic.
Salah satu klaim utama dalam peluncuran Claude Opus 5.5 adalah penurunan perilaku yang mencoba melewati batas pengamanan sistem.
Anthropic mengatakan pengujian internal menunjukkan model baru ini 85% lebih jarang melakukan tindakan yang mengarah pada pelanggaran batas keamanan dibanding Claude Opus 5 dan Mythos 5.1. Perusahaan menyebut sebagian besar kejadian yang terdeteksi pada model sebelumnya tergolong berisiko rendah dan dilaporkan sendiri oleh model selama proses evaluasi.
Untuk mendukung klaim tersebut, perusahaan melibatkan organisasi eksternal seperti Frontier Design dan METR dalam proses evaluasi sebelum model dirilis ke publik.

items.title: CTO Summit 2026 Agenda: How India’s Tech Leaders Are Rebuilding Products, Teams & Systems For AI Era
items.summary:
There was a time when adding AI to a technology roadmap largely meant identifying a few use cases, running pilots and figuring out where the technology could improve productivity.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
There was a time when adding AI to a technology roadmap largely meant identifying a few use cases, running pilots and figuring out where the technology could improve productivity.
That phase is rapidly giving way to a harder one.
As AI moves deeper into products and engineering organisations, technology leaders are confronting questions that go well beyond which model to use.
What happens when AI starts writing a meaningful share of production code? Who verifies it? How should engineering teams change when individual developers can produce substantially more? What happens to infrastructure costs when an AI feature moves from a pilot to millions of users?
At the product layer, another shift is underway. Search boxes are beginning to understand intent, consumers are interacting through conversations rather than menus and filters, and AI agents are beginning to interact directly with commerce infrastructure.
For tech leaders, these changes are increasingly connected. The AI product cannot be separated from the engineering organisation, data foundation, infrastructure economics or architecture underneath it.
This is the conversation at the heart of the inaugural CTO Summit 2026 by Inc42 and PhonePe Payment Gateway, taking place on September 30, 2026, at JW Marriott, Bengaluru.
Co-presented by Oracle and powered by OceanBase and Seedling Labs, the summit will bring together 150+ tech and product leaders. Across 10 sessions, leaders from Swiggy, Flipkart, MakeMyTrip, PhonePe, Razorpay, Rapido, Meesho, ShareChat, BookMyShow, Cashfree Payments, Acko and Naukri.com will unpack the technology and organisational decisions they are making as AI moves into production.
Book Your Pass
From AI Features To AI-Native Products
The day will begin with Swiggy CTO Madhusudhan Rao going inside what happens when AI moves beyond a consumer-facing feature and begins changing the underlying commerce architecture.
Swiggy is opening parts of its commerce infrastructure to external AI agents through four MCP servers and 66 tools spanning discovery, menus, carts, ordering, reservations and tracking. The conversation will examine what it takes to make that infrastructure usable by machines and what Swiggy’s role becomes if external models increasingly own discovery and conversation.
Flipkart CPTO Balaji Thiagarajan will take the conversation to discovery, examining the shift from keyword-led search towards systems that understand consumer intent, and the complexity of building conversational commerce across vernacular languages, noisy speech, low-end devices and inconsistent connectivity.
What Happens When AI Starts Writing The Code?
As AI-assisted coding moves from individual experimentation towards a larger share of production software, generating code faster is creating a different bottleneck: verification.
In ‘How Engineering Changes When AI Writes The Code’, tech leaders from Cashfree Payments, LeadSquared, Eightfold and JioHotstar will examine what happens when code generation accelerates faster than senior review, testing, security and architecture capacity and how companies should measure the real productivity gains.
But changing how code gets written also changes the organisation around it.
‘The Great Engineering Reset: Teams, Talent & Leadership After AI’ will examine which roles shrink, grow or change as AI absorbs more routine work, what happens to the mid-senior layer responsible for mentoring and architecture, and what this means for hiring, career ladders and engineering leadership.
Engineering For The Next 10X
AI workloads are arriving on top of an infrastructure problem Indian technology companies already know well: scale does not arrive predictably.
A festive sale, IPL match, UPI spike or the 9:15 AM market opening can quickly test assumptions around capacity and resilience.
‘The Architecture Of 10X’ will bring together technology leaders from Kuku, BookMyShow, Razorpay and Oracle to examine graceful degradation, capacity planning and the architecture decisions companies are reconsidering as AI workloads begin hitting stacks designed for a different era.
The conversation will extend into ‘Building AI Systems For Indian Scale’, where leaders from ShareChat & Moj, Meesho, Shadowfax and Rapido will tackle inference costs, model routing, latency, low-end devices, vernacular inputs, model drift and the build-versus-rent decisions behind the AI serving layer.
Book Your Pass
The Data Layer Underneath Production AI
Before companies can operate AI at scale, many are running into a more fundamental constraint: their data.
Systems built for dashboards and reporting were not necessarily designed to give models and agents clean, contextual and continuously available information.
In ‘Building The Data Foundation For AI At Scale’, technology leaders from Fibe, PhonePe and OceanBase will examine problems ranging from fragmented customer IDs and messy catalogues to stale inventory and inconsistent payments data, alongside where real-time data matters and what CTOs can fix without beginning another multi-year transformation.
Inside What India’s Tech Companies Are Actually Building
The summit will also feature firesides and live demonstrations around systems already operating in the market.
MakeMyTrip Group CTO Sanjay Mohan will unpack what 8 Mn AI conversations are teaching the company about Indian travel intent; Rapido CTO Srivatsa Katta will go inside how the company has reset its engineering organisation and infrastructure for AI; and Nugget by Zomato will demonstrate how Zomato’s experience operating AI at India scale is translating into enterprise systems.
Razorpay CPO Khilan Haria will provide a technical walkthrough of Slash, its autonomous engineering agent that combines company context, connected tools and workflow triggers to execute engineering tasks.
Meanwhile, PhonePe CTO Srijon Biswas will examine how India’s identity, payments and transaction rails could become context for more personalised AI-led financial experiences for 720 Mn+ users, while navigating consent, privacy and data governance.
A Room For The People Building The Technology
The question is no longer simply where companies can use AI. It is what happens after they decide to use it.
How does the product change? What happens to the engineering organisation? What infrastructure needs to be rebuilt? Which data needs to become accessible? And where do the economics stop making sense?
These questions are being answered inside technology organisations right now, through experiments, failures, reversals and architecture decisions that rarely make it outside engineering rooms.
The inaugural Inc42 CTO Summit 2026 will bring those conversations into one room.
Book Your Pass

The company has already teased the Motorola Razr Flex Wide Foldable, and a new leak has now revealed several specs about its design, display, cameras, hardware, and battery.
The name Razr Flex is reportedly being used internally, although Motorola has not confirmed whether it will be the final retail name. The device is said to carry the internal codename, Parker.
Motorola Razr Flex Wide Foldable Specs Leak Ahead of Expected December Launch
Large 165Hz Folding Display
According to the leaked specifications, the Motorola Razr Flex will feature a 6.92-inch OLED folding display. The screen is expected to offer a resolution of 2364 x 1728 pixels and a high 165Hz refresh rate, which could provide smoother scrolling, animations, and gaming.
When folded, users will have access to a 4.97-inch OLED cover display with a resolution of 1140 x 1736 pixels. This larger-than-usual outer screen could allow users to handle more tasks without opening the phone.
Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 Processor
The wide foldable is expected to use Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset. It will reportedly come with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of internal storage.
Interestingly, the leaked information claims Motorola may offer only this single storage configuration. There could be no higher-storage variant at launch.
Dual 50MP Rear Cameras
The Motorola Razr Flex is also expected to focus on photography. The rear camera setup reportedly includes a 50MP primary camera and a 50MP ultrawide camera.
Motorola may also place a 32MP selfie camera on each display, giving the phone two front-facing cameras in total. This setup could allow users to take selfies using either the inner or outer screen.
5,000mAh Battery and Wireless Charging
The phone is expected to pack a 5,000mAh battery. It will reportedly support 25W wireless charging, although details about wired charging speeds have not been revealed in the leak.
The device is said to measure 110 x 149 x 5.8mm when unfolded and 110 x 76 x 12.6mm when folded. Its reported weight is 215 grams.
Android 17 Out of the Box
The Razr Flex is expected to feature a side-mounted fingerprint scanner integrated into the power button. For durability, the device reportedly carries IP48 and IP49 certifications for dust and water resistance.
Motorola is reportedly planning to launch the foldable in mid-December 2026, with Android 17 installed from the start. The leaked color options include Pantone Coriander and Pantone Dark Botanical Garden.
Motorola has not yet confirmed the complete specifications, final name, pricing, or launch date. These details should therefore be treated as leaked information until the company officially announces the device.

Seed-stage focused venture capital firm WEH Ventures announced the first close of its third fund (Fund III) at an undisclosed amount.
Limited partners for the fund include Nordic fund-of-funds Play Capital, family offices such as Eraya, Twin & Bull Investments and Heritage Investments, as well as founders and executives associated with companies including Oziva, GS Labs, Thermax, Haleon, Lenovo and PNB MetLife.
The firm is targeting a total corpus of ₹250 Cr for the fund and expects to completely close it by mid-2027.
The VC would look to deploy the capital across 20–25 seed stage startups operating across segments like advanced manufacturing, agriculture, energy transition, AI, healthcare, consumer and fintech.
The firm claims to have already started deploying capital from Fund III, committing eight investments across startups working in advanced agriculture, robotics, healthcare diagnostics, retail and edtech.
Some of the investments disclosed so far include advanced horticulture startup Fragaria, which raised $2 Mn in a seed round in October 2025, along with elder-healthcare startup Praan Health, and sports retailer PlayBlue, which raised $2.7 Mn in July.
One of the fund’s portfolio startups has also gone on to raise a subsequent round at a higher valuation, WEH Ventures said.
WEH Ventures’ Track Record
WEH Ventures launched its first fund in 2017, followed by its flagship Fund II in 2020. The VC said Fund I has returned 1.4X the capital invested, while Fund II has already returned capital through one exit and is tracking above top-quartile performance. The firm claims to have delivered a 29% IRR to investors in Fund II.
Since 2017, WEH Ventures has invested in more than 30 companies, including Smallcase, Jar, Pratilipi, Animall, MasterChow, AppsForBharat, Unbox Robotics and Mitigata.
The firm claims that its portfolio companies, which it backs at the pre-seed and seed stages, have cumulatively raised $400 Mn. It said 75% of its portfolio startups have gone on to raise follow-on cheques from other VC firms.
The VC has continued to back several of its portfolio companies in subsequent rounds. Mitigata recently closed its Series B round at $15 Mn, with WEH Ventures returning as an investor.
WEH Ventures also exited smallcase in July 2025, generating a 38% IRR after investing ₹5 Cr across the fintech startup’s funding rounds. The VC first backed smallcase through its ₹20 Cr Fund I in 2018 and continued investing through its Series C.
“Alongside consumer and fintech, we are seeing strong entrepreneurial activity across advanced manufacturing, agriculture, energy transition, AI and healthcare. Fund III allows us to participate in this broader opportunity while staying disciplined about the stage and kind of founders we want to back,” WEH Ventures general partner Deepak Gupta said.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
FMCG major ITC has completed the acquisition of 100% of Sproutlife Foods, the parent of healthy snacking brand Yoga Bar, buying the remaining 52.5% stake for around ₹645 Cr.
In an exchange filing, the FMCG major informed that it bought 13,445 equity shares of Sproutlife through a secondary purchase. The transaction takes its holding in the company from around 47.5% to 100%, making Sproutlife a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC with effect from September 28.
ITC had first announced its plans to acquire Yoga Bar in January 2023, when it said it would acquire 100% of Sproutlife in tranches over three to four years.
It initially invested ₹175 Cr to acquire a 39.4% stake via primary subscription of shares as well as secondary purchases. Subsequently, it invested another ₹80 Cr to increase its shareholding in Yoga Bar to 47.5%.
The latest acquisition is in line with ITC’s strategy of building a “future-ready” portfolio in the foods segment.
Founded in 2014 by Suhasini Sampath Kumar and Anindita Sampath Kumar, Yoga Bar is an omnichannel healthy snacking and breakfast brand that has a wide range of products from Nutrition Bars to Muesli and from Oats to Cereals.
The parent entity Sproutlife reported a turnover of ₹452 Cr in FY26, compared with ₹200 Cr in FY25 and ₹108 Cr in FY24.
ITC’s D2C Acquisition Push
Yoga Bar is one of several digital-first D2C brands that ITC has picked up stake in as it expands beyond its traditional FMCG portfolio.
In February 2025, ITC signed agreements to acquire 100% of the parent of D2C meat brand Meatigo. Similar to the Yoga Bar acquisition, that deal was also structured in phases, beginning with a 43.8% stake in Ample Foods for nearly ₹131 Cr and taking ITC’s holding to 62.5% by April 2027.
The transaction also brought Prasuma’s frozen foods and cloud kitchen businesses into the fold.
ITC has also been building its presence in the mother and baby care segment. In April 2025, it announced plans to take its stake in Mother Sparsh Baby Care to 100% from 26.5% over two to three years. The company had first invested in Mother Sparsh in 2021 and subsequently raised its holding to 22% in 2022.
The conglomerate had also acquired a 10.07% stake in Mylo’s parent Blupin Technologies for ₹39.34 Cr in 2022.
FMCG Giants And Their D2C Acquisition Spree
ITC’s full acquisition of Yoga Bar comes amid a broader push by large FMCG companies to acquire successful digital-first brands and bring them into their portfolios.
For instance, Hindustan Unilever (HUL) completed the acquisition of a 90.5% stake in skincare brand Minimalist’s parent Uprising Science for ₹2,706.44 Cr in April 2025. HUL had agreed to acquire the remaining 9.5% stake within two years of completing the initial transaction.
Marico has followed a similar route with healthy foods brand True Elements. After acquiring a 53.98% stake in its parent HW Wellness Solutions in 2022, Marico agreed to acquire the remaining 46.02% stake for ₹138 Cr in September 2025.
The interest from FMCG majors comes as D2C brands have built scale across categories including healthy foods, personal care, babycare and other consumer segments.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
OpenAI has apologised to Australia after one of its AI agents gained unauthorised access to a Medicare statistics portal. The company has also decided not to release its planned next-generation ChatGPT model, GPT-6.1 Astra, after internal testing raised safety and alignment concerns.
The Medicare incident involved a portal operated by Services Australia. According to Australian authorities, the AI agent accessed the system on June 18 while carrying out a research task. The incident was not reported to the Australian government until September.
OpenAI Apologises Over Medicare Breach, Delays Next-Gen ChatGPT Model
OpenAI said the incident occurred while an internal-only model was being trained. The model was not designed for public release and did not have all the safeguards included in OpenAI’s publicly available products.
AI Agent Accessed Non-Public Information
OpenAI said the agent found a way to gain access to the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service. It then ran commands and retrieved files, credentials and statistics that were not publicly available at the time.
Australian officials have said the incident did not expose personal Medicare details. Much of the information on the portal consisted of aggregated statistics rather than individual patient records. However, some information that was not public at the time was accessed and later made public.
OpenAI also disclosed other activity involving Australian websites. Its models accessed the NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research’s public Crime Mapping Tool while looking for crime statistics. The company also identified an exposed access key linked to a Victorian health reporting system.
OpenAI said attempts to bypass access controls on some other systems were unsuccessful.
OpenAI Apologises to Australia
In a blog post, OpenAI said it wants to rebuild trust with the Australian public. The company acknowledged that it should have handled the incident and its communication with Australian authorities better.
The company also said it will provide resources and expertise to help affected Australian agencies strengthen their cyber defences.
OpenAI plans to establish a taskforce that will include independent Australian experts. The group is expected to develop practical recommendations for dealing with the security risks created by autonomous AI agents.
OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon is also scheduled to appear before Australia’s Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence in Sydney on October 6.
See Also: OpenAI Faces Wider Concerns Over AI Agent Incidents
Australia Considers Tougher AI Rules
The incident has increased pressure on Australia to introduce stricter rules for AI-related cyber incidents. The government is considering requirements that companies report serious AI security incidents both to the affected organisation and to cyber authorities.
A government review is also examining the incident and is expected to help shape future national AI standards.
OpenAI has said that autonomous AI systems can create new types of cyber risks as they become capable of carrying out increasingly complex tasks with limited human involvement.
GPT-6.1 Astra Release Shelved
Alongside its response to the Australian incident, OpenAI has shelved the planned release of GPT-6.1 Astra.
The model was reportedly being prepared for an October launch and was expected to be used in ChatGPT and Codex. It was designed to handle more complex tasks with less human assistance.
However, OpenAI’s internal testing found that the model did not meet the company’s safety and alignment requirements. As a result, the company decided not to proceed with the planned release.
The decision highlights the additional safety challenges that come with developing AI systems capable of performing more tasks independently.
For now, OpenAI is reviewing its testing and safety processes while it responds to the Australian breach and broader concerns about autonomous AI agents.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian startup Adaptive Atelier is building the technology infrastructure businesses need to make their digital products accessible, and to prove that accessibility actually works for the disabled people it is meant to serve.
Founded in 2024 by Toyosi Badejo-Okusanya, and headquartered across Lagos and London, Adaptive Atelier operates three connected products.
AdaptiveTest is an AI-powered scanner that analyses websites and digital products against WCAG accessibility standards; AdaptiveWiz is an accessibility API, with live Shopify and WordPress integrations that helps disabled users personalise and navigate digital experiences; and AdaptiveAlly is a marketplace connecting businesses with vetted disabled professionals who test whether accessibility fixes work in practice.
“AdaptiveTest identifies the problem, AdaptiveWiz helps fix the experience, and AdaptiveAlly validates whether the fix actually holds up for a real disabled user. That closes a loop that automated tools alone cannot close,” Badejo-Okusanya told Disrupt Africa.
She said most businesses already know accessibility matters, and are under growing pressure from customers, regulators and digital transformation to act on it.
“The gap we identified is the distance between knowing accessibility matters and actually having the infrastructure to identify, fix, and validate it,” she said.
The existing market, Badejo-Okusanya said, is fragmented across automated scanners and overlay widgets, which are quick to deploy but limited in what they can detect and fix; traditional consultancies, which offer deep expertise but little proprietary technology; and generic user-testing platforms not built around disabled testers.
“We sit at the intersection of these categories, combining AI-driven detection and remediation with structured, paid validation from disabled professionals, rather than asking a business to choose between automation and lived-experience insight,” she said.
The startup has built a community of over 13,000 disabled professionals and advocates, giving the AdaptiveAlly marketplace a ready supply side, while its website draws around 50,000 organic visits a month. It has carried out customer discovery with disabled professionals across the United Kingdom (UK), Nigeria, Canada, Germany, Morocco and the United States (US), as well as with enterprise compliance and digital leaders.
Adaptive Atelier has begun signing paying customers across cinemas, government institutions and retail platforms, and counts L’Oréal, SignHealth, Channel 4 and Phonak among the organisations it has active relationships with.
The company makes money through subscriptions for AdaptiveWiz, scoped audits for AdaptiveTest, and commission on AdaptiveAlly marketplace transactions.
“A business often enters through an AdaptiveTest audit, which surfaces the case for AdaptiveWiz as an ongoing fix, and AdaptiveAlly as the validation layer that proves it’s working,” Badejo-Okusanya said. “The priority right now is proving a repeatable path from first engagement to long-term customer before pushing for more volume.”
The startup has been self-funded to date, and is now raising a US$250,000 institutional round to support technical hiring and go-to-market execution. Badejo-Okusanya was a finalist in the Standard Chartered Foundation Women in Tech Accelerator Nigeria, and Adaptive Atelier is currently part of the Synergies Work Igniting Ideas Business Accelerator in the US, sponsored by the Mitsubishi Electric Foundation.
Nigeria remains the startup’s home market, but it is building early relationships in the UK, European Union (EU) and US, where regulation such as the European Accessibility Act and ADA requirements is creating urgency for enterprise buyers.
The road has not been without challenges. Badejo-Okusanya said product delivery slipped against expectations at one stage, forcing the company to rebuild parts of its technical roadmap and team.
“We now treat rigorous internal testing before external claims as non-negotiable,” she said.
Market education has been another hurdle, with many businesses still viewing accessibility as a compliance cost rather than a commercial opportunity, while focus has also been key.
“With genuine interest from both African and Western markets, the discipline has been choosing where to concentrate go-to-market effort first, rather than spreading a small team across two very different buyer types at once,” Badejo-Okusanya said.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is working on a major change that could make its Android interface simpler. WhatsApp is testing a new option to move Channels from the Updates tab to the Chats tab.
The feature is still under development and is not currently available to beta testers. According to WABetaInfo, the change was spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.39.1.
With the planned update, users will be able to access their followed channels from the same area where they normally view their conversations. WhatsApp is also testing different ways to organize channels inside the Chats tab.
WhatsApp to Move Channels to Chats Tab on Android
The messaging app is developing a migration tool that will ask users where they want their channels to appear. One option will move followed channels directly into the Chats list.
Another option will automatically archive the channels. Users will still be able to move them into the Chats tab later if they change their minds.
This approach could give users more control over how their inbox is organized. People who frequently use Channels can keep them easily accessible, while those who prefer a cleaner chat list can keep them separate.
WhatsApp is Testing Three Layouts
The company is currently experimenting with three different ways to display Channels in the Chats tab.
In the first layout, channels will appear directly alongside regular conversations in the main chat list. Users will also be able to use a Channels filter at the top of the interface. Channels would remain visible in the All inbox as well.
The second layout would keep channels out of the All inbox. They would only appear when users select the Channels filter, helping keep regular conversations separate.
The third option would create a dedicated Channels folder within the Chats tab. Users could open this section to view all the channels they follow.
WhatsApp has not yet confirmed which of these layouts will eventually be introduced to everyone.
Updates Tab Could Be Removed
Moving Channels to the Chats tab could also lead to another major interface change. WhatsApp is expected to remove the Updates tab once Channels are moved.
Status updates have already started appearing at the top of the Chats tab for some users. If Channels also move there, the separate Updates section may no longer be needed.
WhatsApp could then replace the Updates tab with a Contacts tab. The new section would allow users to find contacts and see which people are currently online.
Feature is Under Development
The new Channels arrangement is currently being tested internally on Android. It has not yet been released to the public or made available to beta testers.
WhatsApp is expected to test different layouts with users before deciding how Channels should appear in the Chats tab. The company has not announced a release date for the feature.
For now, Android users will continue to find Channels in the Updates tab. The final design may also change before WhatsApp makes the feature available more widely.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
A homeowner can spend anywhere between a few weeks to a couple of months deciding the right marble for the living room, the finish of the cabinetry and the lighting for a new home. All of these are just as important as the property itself for the new homeowner. But once the room is ready, there is one thing that still looks visibly out of place: the technology that powers this home.
A speaker mounted on a finished wall, a purifier occupying a corner or a conventional fan hanging beneath an elaborate false ceiling can suddenly look less like a functional necessity and more like a visual compromise.
A new crop of Indian home tech brands is betting that consumers are increasingly unwilling to make that compromise.
From designer ceiling fans and integrated air purifiers to speakers that disappear into walls and premium switch panels designed as part of their interior, these brands are trying to change the role technology plays inside the home. The idea is no longer simply to make an appliance work better, or, in some cases, disappear altogether.
“For a long time appliances in India were brought on spec sheet and price. Nobody really cared how a fan or a purifier looked,” said Karan Bansal, founder and CEO of Karban.
Jaipur-based Karban is a design led home appliance startup that makes fans and air purification products that are designed to integrate into the home rather than stand out from it.
The equation, he believes, is changing as consumers spend more on their homes.
Jivraj Singh, General Partner at Indian Silicon Valley, sees the shift play out among founders approaching the firm. He attributes it to three forces: homes becoming more personal after COVID, social media narrowing the gap between global design trends and Indian consumers, and rising spending at the aspirational end of the market.
“Homes got personal after COVID, people started treating the home as an expression of who they are, not just a shelter,” he says. “Instagram collapsed the gap between what a home in Milan looks like and what a couple in Indore wants theirs to look like,” he adds.
False ceilings, planned lighting and professional interior design are becoming part of the home building process, particularly for consumers renovating or building new homes. Once so much attention has gone into the space, Bansal says, consumers increasingly do not want a conventional appliance to disrupt it.
The shift is visible across categories. Fanzart and Magnific are turning ceiling fans into design elements, while Karban is combining air purification, air circulation and lighting into a single ceiling mounted product. XSCACE is making architectural audio that blends into walls and ceiling, while NUOS is bringing the same thinking to switches and home automation. Newer players such as Noctics Labs and Glazonoid are taking the idea further into smart controls, lighting and home decor.
The products are different. The underlying consumer expectation is increasingly similar: technology should belong in the home, not merely be placed inside it.
Technology Has To Earn Its Place
For Karban, the opportunity emerged from a practical problem. A relative’s apartment had a low ceiling, but the available fans were either unsuitable or visually intrusive. That led the company to develop a bladeless ceiling fan.
The startup then found another problem with conventional air purifiers. Most sit in a corner, creating a relatively small zone of clean air, while the purifier’s own sensor can indicate improved air quality around the device.
Karban’s response was to combine purification with air circulation and move the product to the ceiling. Its Airzone range combines the two functions, with some variants also adding lighting.
That combination is important because it changes the price conversation.
Karban’s products range from around ₹15,000 to ₹37,000. A conventional ceiling fan can cost only a few thousand rupees, making the headline premium significant. But Bansal argues that the relevant comparison for a customer is not a fan against another fan. It is the cost of a purifier, a designer fan and a light fixture, three products that Airzone seeks to combine into one ceiling point.
“Design alone won’t justify a premium in India. Design plus function will,” Bansal said.
That distinction runs through the category.
At NUOS, the product is a switch panel, but the proposition extends beyond its appearance. The startup combines glass touch panels and premium finishes with Zigbee connectivity, DALI lighting control and home automation capabilities.
“The control panel is something a homeowner sees and touches every day. It deserves as much design consideration as the lighting or other interior finishes,” said Neil Savant, founder and CEO of NUOS, which makes smart switches, control panels and home automation systems.
For Savant, the challenge is therefore not to put sophisticated technology inside a beautiful shell. The visible product and the engineering underneath have to work together.
The same principle applies at XSCACE, although the desired outcome is almost the opposite.
 
When The Best Technology Is Technology You Don’t See
“The room should come before the specification,” said Utkarsh Hora, founder of XSCACE, an architectural-audio startup that makes in-wall and in-ceiling speakers.
The startup’s speakers can be installed inside walls or ceilings, or matched to the finish of the space. The idea is to preserve the visual language of a room without compromising on audio.
Hora believes this matters because consumers who have already invested heavily in marble, cabinetry, lighting and furniture are less willing to accept a conventional speaker box simply because it delivers good sound.
In that sense, design-led home technology is developing along two seemingly opposite paths.
Some brands want technology to stand out, turning the fan or appliance into a statement piece.
Others want it to blend in, making speakers, controls and other hardware part of the architecture.
And then there are products such as Karban’s Aizrone that try to reduce the number of objects altogether by combining multiple functions.
The common thread is not necessarily aesthetics alone. It is integration. That also explains why these startups are increasingly looking beyond traditional appliance distribution. Integration and design may not be enough to give these companies a lasting competitive advantage. As the category grows, larger appliance and consumer electronic companies could replicate the visual elements of these products and bring them to a wider distribution network.
“Design alone is not a moat. A Havells or a Samsung can copy a finish in eighteen months and outspend you on distribution,” said Singh.
For Singh, the stronger proposition lies in the combination of brand, customer relationship, product development and distribution, with design acting as the visible layer rather than the entire competitive advantage.
The Architects Are Getting A Say
For a conventional appliance purchase, the consumer may begin with an ecommerce platform, retailer or brand showroom.
For integrated home technology, the decision can happen much earlier, when the architect is planning the electrical layout, when the interior designers are deciding the ceiling treatment or when the walls and wiring are still on paper.
That makes architects and interior designers an important channel for the emerging category.
Around 40% of NUOS’ home automation sales come through architect and interior designer referrals or specifications, according to Savant.
At Karban, the architects and designers channel contributes around 20% of sales.
For XSCACE, Hora said most projects indirectly come through architects and designers. More importantly, he sees their involvement as critical to getting the product right.
If an architectural speaker is considered only after a room has been built, the installation becomes a compromise. If it is considered while the ceiling, walls and wiring are still being planned, the technology can be integrated into the space from the beginning.
This makes architects and interior designers more than a sales channel. They can become the gatekeepers of a product category that needs to be specified before the consumer is ready to buy it.
It also gives these brands a different route to scale.
A designer who understands a product and has successfully specified it for one project can potentially bring it into subsequent projects. Both Karban and XSCACE say they are investing in these relationships, while NUOS sees designers as an important bridge between homeowner expectations and choices around automation, finishes and usability.
From Premium Home To Everyday Home
For now, the proposition remains most visible in homes where consumers are already spending significantly on interiors. But the founders do not see premium positioning as the end point.
Hora compares the trajectories with flush switches, hidden lighting and modular kitchen, features that began as premium additions before becoming more common in well designed homes.
Investors see a similar trajectory for design led home technology, with premiumisation acting as the starting point rather than the ceiling.
“It’s premiumisation first, and the larger market follows,” says Singh. “Design-led is the wedge, not the ceiling.”
He compares the opportunity with premium smartphones, where higher priced products initially served a narrower consumer base before financing and wider distribution helped expand the category. “The affluent design conscious buyer is the proof of demand, not the addressable market,” he says.
Bansal draws a parallel with BLDC fans, which moved from being a relatively premium product to a far more mainstream category.
But moving design led home technology beyond affluent consumers will require more than simply reducing prices.
The products have to become easier to discover, install and maintain. Consumers need to understand why they should buy them. Architects and interior designers need to become familiar with specifying them. And the technology still has to deliver enough functional value to justify the purchase.
For NUOS, that means affordable entry points, simple installation, interoperability and accessible service. For Karban, manufacturing scale, offline presence and reliable installation will be important. XSCACE sees greater consumer awareness, more trained designers and lower prices as prerequisites for wider adoption.
The bigger questions, then, is whether design can become more than a premium layer in India’s home tech market.
These brands are making a case that it can. But the real test will be whether consumers eventually see a well designed appliance, an integrated speaker or a smart switch not as an upgrade to the home, but as a basic part of how the home itself is designed.
For now, India’s home tech startups are trying to close the gap between the technology inside a home and the way the home is meant to look and feel.
SPOTLIGHT | Inside Peep Beauty’s Eye-First Beauty Play
BPC brand Peep Beauty is focused on eye makeup and coloured contact lenses, with products spanning daily-wear lenses and matte and metallic liquid eyeshadows, positioned as combining beauty with eye-focused functionality.
The brand operates through its D2C website, with coloured lenses priced at ₹399 a pair and liquid eyeshadows priced between ₹799 and ₹849.
Its lenses are designed for Indian eyes, offering 57% water content, UV protection and daily disposable use, while its eyeshadows feature skincare-infused formulas.
ECOMMERCE BUZZ
Amazon’s Quick Commerce Push: Amazon India plans to invest $3 Bn in its quick-commerce business Amazon Now by 2030, with $1 Bn earmarked by 2027-end. The company will expand dark stores, strengthen technology and deploy AI for demand prediction.
Rio Health’s Funding Boost: Rio Health has raised $4.5 Mn in pre-Series A funding to expand its 30-minute pharmacy network across Delhi NCR. The startup plans to add 12 dark stores, strengthen its tech stack and target ₹150 Cr+ ARR within 9–12 months.
FSSAI Cracks Down: FSSAI has penalised Amazon, BigBasket, Flipkart, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto over alleged food safety and regulatory violations, including misleading claims and non-compliant product information, amid growing scrutiny of quick-commerce dark stores.
Furlenco Joins IPO Queue: Furlenco is reportedly planning a ₹1,000–1,200 Cr IPO in FY28 at a targeted valuation of around ₹7,000 Cr. The furniture rental startup, which turned profitable in FY25, saw revenue rise 61.9% YoY to ₹370.4 Cr in FY26.
Snapdeal Parent Heads For IPO: Snapdeal parent AceVector has set a ₹30–₹32 price band for its ₹420 Cr IPO, targeting a ₹1,741 Cr valuation. After raising ₹189 Cr from anchor investors, the company is set to list on the NSE and BSE on October 5.
The Deep Dive
 
The Operator Question
What does it take to turn a design-led product into a category?
We reached out to Karan Bansal, founder and CEO of Karban, to understand the playbook, while also drawing on the experiences of NUOS and XSCACE.
Prove The Premium: Design can get consumers interested, but the product still needs to deliver enough functional value to justify the price. For karban, that means combining design with air purification and circulation. For NUOS, it means pairing aesthetics with reliability, ease of use and after sales support.
Make it Easy To Discover And Install: Consumers need to understand why these products are different, while architects and interior designers need to be familiar with specifying them. For integrated home technology, the buying decision often starts before the home is finished.
Build The Designer Channel: Architects and interior designers already influence a meaningful share of sales for these brands. Making the products easy to specify can help them move from being an individual purchase to becoming part of the home design process.
Bring Down The Barriers: Wider adoption will require lower prices, simpler installation, broader service networks and more accessible products. NUOS points to affordable entry points and interoperability, while Karban sees manufacturing scale and offline presence as important. SXCACE, meanwhile, sees consumer awareness and a larger network of trained designers are prerequisites for expansion.
Make Design More Than Aesthetic: The long-term proposition cannot rest on appearance alone. As the category grows, larger appliance and consumer electronics companies could replicate visual elements and bring them to a wider distribution network. The opportunity, therefore, is to combine design with functionality, brand, distribution and a product experience that is harder to replicate.
Edited By Nikhil Subramaniam

items.title: Naira dips, now N1,382/$ in parallel market
items.summary:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan 
The Naira yesterday depreciated to N1,382 per dollar from N1,378 in the parallel market last weekend. Similarly, the naira depreciated to N1,331.5  per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market,  NFEM.
Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the naira rose to N1,331.5 per dollar from N1,330 per dollar last weekend, indicating N1.5 depreciation for the naira.
Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets widened to N50.5 per dollar from N48 per dollar last week Friday.
The value of interbank turnover in NFEM declined by 77.7 percent to $24.73 million from $111.06 million last weekend.
