items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
It was a busy month for India’s fintech ecosystem. On the public markets, SEBI issued final observations on the proposed IPO of Social Worth Technologies, the parent company of lending tech startup Fibe (formerly EarlySalary), while digital lending unicorn Moneyview completed its stock market debut. Meanwhile, Zerodha received the regulator’s nod to operate as a merchant banker, and Upstox launched US stock investing on its platform.
Beyond these developments, two themes dominated the fintech conversation in September: the growing use of AI in payments and the changing economics of fintech businesses.
With a flurry of AI-centric products, the Global Fintech Fest 2026 (GFF) in Mumbai was a major showcase this month. BharatPe launched an agentic AI platform for merchants, Pine Labs unveiled an agent-led commerce feature on L&T Finance’s PLANET app, while several banks and NBFCs partnered with new-age startups to bring AI capabilities to their platforms.
While UPI operator NPCI also launched enterprise-focused AI tools, its expected launch of a framework for agentic payments on UPI did not materialise.
Meanwhile, the rapid advancement of AI has raised concerns about the potential risks that frontier models could pose to the security and stability of the financial system.
At GFF, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra both stressed the need for fintech companies to strengthen consumer trust. NPCI MD and CEO Dilip Asbe also said banks and payments companies would need to invest in AI to combat cyber threats, while explaining the rationale behind introducing merchant discount rate (MDR) charges on UPI.
This brings us to the second major theme of the month: fintech economics. After months of speculation, the new UPI MDR regime has finally been notified. From October 15, UPI payments above ₹2,000 will attract a 0.4% fee, with exemptions for smaller merchants, critical sectors and peer-to-peer (P2P) transfers. The new framework has sparked a debate over who will ultimately bear the cost and whether, or to what extent, it could be passed on to consumers.
The insurance sector is facing a similar inflexion point. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has proposed bringing back product- and channel-specific commission caps for insurance distributors. The move could directly affect commission-dependent listed insurtech companies like PB Fintech and Turtlemint.
The common thread running through these developments is the challenge of balancing consumer protection with the commercial interests of fintech and financial services companies.
Against this backdrop, we are back with the sixth edition of the “Five Fintech Startups To Watch”. This monthly series spotlights startups operating in some of the most promising and fast-evolving segments of India’s fintech ecosystem.
With that said, here are some of the interesting ventures that caught our attention in September.
Editor’s Note: The list below is not a ranking of any kind. Startups have been listed alphabetically.
72 Street | AI-Powered Investment Advisory
As India’s capital markets broaden and deepen, retail investors often struggle to make sense of the language of the markets. A savvy investor today has to sift through multiple sources, decode technical information and turn it into actionable insights. Mumbai-based 72 Street is looking to shorten this learning curve, particularly for Gen Z and first-time investors.
The wealthtech startup is building a research-led investment platform for retail investors, combining stock screening with human analyst oversight to make market research easier to understand and act on.
Founded in 2025 by Rohit Agarwal and Fal Ghancha, 72 Street has raised ₹4 Cr from angel investors and ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) to date as it seeks a slice of India’s booming investment tech market, which now exceeds $14 Bn.
The startup’s platform has two key components: the 72 Street app and its AI researcher, Venty. The app offers research-backed stock ideas, live market data, watchlists and investment tools, bringing a range of market information onto a single platform. Venty, meanwhile, helps users make sense of this data.
The AI researcher analyses more than 3,800 NSE- and BSE-listed stocks across fundamental, technical and sentiment indicators. It also detects chart patterns to generate AI-powered insights, which SEBI-registered research analysts then review before presenting them to users.
Cruise Money | Agentic AI Assistant For Your Wealth
Managing personal finances across multiple accounts and investment products can be overwhelming. Figuring out how to deploy your money to meet specific goals, how much to save, where to invest and how much to spend can be just as complicated.
Cruise Money is looking to simplify this using AI agents that aggregate financial data, decode spending patterns and offer actionable advice.
Founded by Vinay Bharathwaj, Ganesh KV and Vikrant Mudaliar in 2025, Cruise Money operates in India’s robo-advisory market, which is projected to reach $7 Bn by 2034.. Its app brings together users’ financial information, including mutual fund holdings and cash flows, and uses chat to help them understand their spending, savings and investment goals.
On the regulatory front, Cruise accesses users’ accounts through the RBI’s Account Aggregator framework on a read-only basis and provides investment guidance under the SEBI-registered Investment Adviser framework.
The startup plans to launch its first agentic card around Diwali 2026. Users can describe a purchase or financial goal to the chatbot, after which the AI-powered platform will suggest ways to achieve it based on their financial profile. For instance, someone looking to buy a new smartphone could receive a recommendation for an EMI plan suited to their spending capacity. Users can then complete the transaction directly through the platform.
Cruise’s USP is proactively guiding users based on their financial priorities. Its AI agents can nudge users to increase their savings to stay on track for retirement goals or recommend direct mutual fund plans instead of regular plans.
Drona Pay | Helping Banks And Insurers Combat Fraud
As technology advances, financial fraud and money laundering are becoming not just more frequent, but more sophisticated. Financial institutions need to identify suspicious accounts and transactions faster while keeping false positives to a minimum, so legitimate customers are not unnecessarily flagged.
With India’s fraud detection and prevention market growing rapidly at over 20% CAGR to cross $7.2 Bn by 2033, Drona Pay is seeking to help financial institutions detect risk earlier and respond faster.
Founded in 2021 by Satish Kashyap, Pallavi Narvekar and Sukhdev Sinh Zala, Drona Pay is building risk and compliance software for banks, fintechs, payment processors and insurers. The platform analyses transactions and user behaviour in real time using machine learning, alternative data and behavioural biometrics. Signals such as device information, IP addresses, location and keystroke patterns can help identify account takeovers, mule accounts, social engineering scams, merchant fraud and suspicious lending activity.
Its product suite includes transaction monitoring, anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing tools, case management, data integration, early-warning alerts and decisioning for offers, delinquency and insurance claims. The company’s analytics platform also combines banking, lending and card data to build customer profiles and help financial institutions assess risk.
LendingIQ | Automating Lending Workflows
Founded by Ashish Kaushik, Ankit Singh and Sai Koundinya in 2025, LendingIQ builds and operates AI agents for banks, fintechs and NBFCs. The startup operates in the market for AI in lending, which was pegged at $835 Mn in 2024 and projected to grow at over 36% to reach $5.4 Bn by 2029.
It targets a common challenge in credit operations: manually extracting information, chasing missing documents, and interpreting lending policies. Together, these slow down decisions and create inconsistencies in assessments.
LendingIQ’s AI agents support functions across loan origination, underwriting, collections and servicing. They can also continuously update their workflows to stay aligned with a lender’s rulebook as policies change.
The platform first connects with a lender’s existing systems and audits its processes to identify areas where AI agents could deliver the highest return on investment. It then tests the agents on a sandboxed sample of the lender’s data to validate their performance before deployment. Once deployed, the agents integrate into existing workflows, with LendingIQ monitoring metrics such as accuracy, latency, exceptions, and policy changes to ensure they continue to perform as expected.
LendingIQ primarily serves lenders across retail and SME lending, home loans, gold loans, auto finance and commercial lending. The startup works with clients across India, the US, Europe, the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand. It claims that most clients see measurable results within two weeks of deploying their first AI agent.
WeCredit | Transforming Traditional Borrowing Landscape
Founded by Mukul Devpura, Brijesh Chokhra, Laksh Dua, Sumit Chokhra and Piyush Beli in 2022, WeCredit is a digital credit marketplace that helps individuals and small businesses compare loan products from multiple lenders. The startup is targeting the fragmented $491 Bn Indian lending market. It aims to help borrowers navigate different providers to find suitable products, compare terms and understand their options.
WeCredit lists personal, business, car, home and gold loans from more than 25 lending partners, including Moneyview, KreditBee, L&T Finance and Olyv. Users can compare offers and apply for loans through the platform, although interest rates, eligibility, approval and disbursal remain subject to individual lenders’ criteria and verification processes.
The startup also offers personal loan and EMI calculators, along with free credit-score and credit-report checks powered by Equifax.
By bringing multiple lenders onto a single platform, WeCredit aims to reduce the time borrowers spend searching for loans and help them compare options before applying. The platform also says this can reduce the need for borrowers to make multiple applications and, in turn, limit hard credit enquiries that could affect their credit scores.
According to its website, WeCredit has more than 5 Lakh users and has facilitated over ₹2,500 Cr in loan disbursals since inception.
Edited by Shishir Parasher
With inputs from Akshit Pushkarna
Creative by Abhyam Gusai
The post Fintech Startups To Watch: Startups That Caught Our Eye In September appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max Runs GTA V Better Than You Might Expect
items.summary:
The PC version of GTA V has been demonstrated running at up to 80 FPS on an iPhone 18 Pro Max using Vapor, an experimental project designed to run PC and Mac games on Apple devices.
Vapor developer StephenDev0 published the full benchmark on September 27. The game averaged 66 FPS during the city-driving section of GTA V’s built-in benchmark, while other scenes averaged around 80 FPS.
GTA V Runs at 1080p
The test ran at 1080p using DirectX 11. Texture quality was set to High, while FXAA and 16x anisotropic filtering were enabled. Population density was set to 75%, distance scaling to 50%, and sharp shadows were enabled.
MSAA was turned off, while the remaining graphics settings were set to Normal.
Here's the full GTA V benchmark running in Vapor on an iPhone 18 Pro Max
City drive: 66 FPS average
Other scenes: 80 FPS average
• 1080p, DirectX 11
• High textures
• FXAA, 16x AF
• 75% population density
• 50% distance scaling
• Sharp shadows, MSAA off
• Everything else… pic.twitter.com/Dv8mE
items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
The PC version of GTA V has been demonstrated running at up to 80 FPS on an iPhone 18 Pro Max using Vapor, an experimental project designed to run PC and Mac games on Apple devices.
Vapor developer StephenDev0 published the full benchmark on September 27. The game averaged 66 FPS during the city-driving section of GTA V’s built-in benchmark, while other scenes averaged around 80 FPS.
GTA V Runs at 1080p
The test ran at 1080p using DirectX 11. Texture quality was set to High, while FXAA and 16x anisotropic filtering were enabled. Population density was set to 75%, distance scaling to 50%, and sharp shadows were enabled.
MSAA was turned off, while the remaining graphics settings were set to Normal.
Here's the full GTA V benchmark running in Vapor on an iPhone 18 Pro Max
City drive: 66 FPS average
Other scenes: 80 FPS average
• 1080p, DirectX 11
• High textures
• FXAA, 16x AF
• 75% population density
• 50% distance scaling
• Sharp shadows, MSAA off
• Everything else… pic.twitter.com/Dv8mEdEIod
— Vapor (@play_vapor) September 27, 2026
GTA V does not have a native iPhone version. Vapor instead works to run software originally built for PC and Mac on Apple hardware, using translation technologies including JIT to handle software that was not originally designed for iOS.
That adds extra processing overhead compared with running a game built natively for the device.
Powered by Apple’s A20 Pro
The iPhone 18 Pro Max uses Apple’s A20 Pro chip. Reports covering the benchmark have compared its GTA V performance with Nvidia’s GeForce GTX 1650, an entry-level desktop graphics card released in 2019.
However, this comparison should be treated cautiously because the benchmark does not provide a controlled side-by-side test using identical hardware conditions, power measurements, and frame-time data.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max also uses an upgraded cooling design intended to improve sustained performance under demanding workloads.
Vapor remains a work in progress. The developer said there are still minor issues that need to be fixed, meaning the current results should not be treated as final performance figures.
The benchmark nevertheless shows that the PC version of GTA V can currently run above 60 FPS on the iPhone 18 Pro Max at 1080p through Vapor, despite the additional translation required to run the game on iOS.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Update | September 28, 17:44 IST
AceVector’s ₹420 Cr IPO ended the second day of bidding with full subscription. TIll now, investors have placed bids for 8.56 Cr shares against the 7.42 Cr shares on offer, translating to an oversubscription of 1.15X.
Retail investors have shown the highest interest till date, oversubscribing their quota 1.36X. These investors have placed bids for 1.87 Cr shares against 1.37 Cr shares reserved for them.
Following them, non-institutional investors (NIIs) oversubscribed their quota 1.25X, placing bids for 2.57 Cr shares against 2.06 Cr shares on offer.
Within the NII category, the portion reserved for bids of more than ₹2 Lakh and up to ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 1.43X, while the portion reserved for bids above ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 1.16X.
The qualified institutional buyer (QIB) portion also oversubscribed their quota by 1.03X. These investors placed bids for 4.12 Cr shares against 3.99 Cr shares reserved for the category.
Original | September 28, 14:56 IST
Snapdeal parent AceVector’s ₹420 Cr IPO has been subscribed 96% as of 14:33 IST on the second day of bidding, with investors placing bids for 7.16 Cr shares against the 7.42 Cr shares on offer.
Till now, retail investors have been most bullish on the public float, oversubscribing their quota 1.11X. These investors have placed bids for 1.53 Cr shares till now against 1.37 Cr shares reserved for them.
Following them, the qualified institutional buyer (QIB) portion has been completely subscribed, with these investors placing bids for 4.03 Cr shares against 3.99 Cr shares reserved for the category. This translates to an oversubscription of 1.01X.
Non-institutional investors (NIIs) subscribed their quota by 78%, placing bids for 1.61 Cr shares against 2.06 Cr shares on offer.
Within the NII category, investors bidding for lots in the range of ₹2-10 Lakh oversubscribed their quota by 1.20X, while the portion for bids above ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 78%.
On the first day of bidding on Friday (September 25), the IPO was subscribed just 23%, with investors placing bids for 1.72 Cr shares against 7.42 Cr shares on offer.
The IPO is set to close tomorrow (September 29). AceVector set a price band of ₹30-₹32 per share, valuing the company at up to ₹1,741.4 Cr.
Its shares are expected to list on the BSE and NSE on October 5. As per grey market price (GMP) price for AceVector today, the company’s shares are expected to make a flat listing.
Ahead of opening the IPO, AceVector raised ₹189 Cr from anchor investors by allotting 5.91 Cr shares at ₹32 apiece. Helios Mutual Fund and Taurus Ethical Fund were the only domestic mutual funds to participate. Together, they picked up 93.75 Lakh shares, or 15.87% of the anchor allocation.
The issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹287 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 4.16 Cr shares, worth ₹133 Cr at the upper end of the price band.
AceVector plans to use ₹132 Cr of the fresh issue proceeds for Snapdeal’s marketing and business promotion and another ₹50 Cr for its technology infrastructure. The remaining funds will be used for acquisitions and general corporate purposes. On the other hand, investors like SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners, among others will be paring their stake in the company via the IPO.
Founded in 2010 by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, AceVector owns ecommerce platform Snapdeal, ecommerce enablement platform Unicommerce and consumer brands business Stellaro Brands. The group adopted the AceVector name in 2022.
The company’s restated net loss for the fiscal year FY26 narrowed nearly 64% to ₹45.5 Cr in from ₹126.3 Cr in FY25. Its operating revenue, meanwhile, rose 29.2% to ₹510.3 Cr from ₹395 Cr.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Asian Games 2026 akan menjadi edisi terakhir yang menampilkan ajang esports dalam program resmi pesta olahraga terbesar di Asia tersebut. Sebagai gantinya, Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) tengah menyiapkan ajang tersendiri bernama Asian Esports and Mind Sports Games di 2027.
Langkah tersebut menandai perubahan besar dalam posisi esports di ekosistem olahraga Asia. OCA pun sudah menandatangani dengan Kuwait sebagai tuan rumah edisi perdana kompetisi tersebut tahun depan, sebagaimana dikutip dari DotEsports, Senin (28/9/2026).
Baca Juga: Aksesori vivo Selfie Monitor Bikin Vlogging Pakai vivo X500 Jauh Lebih Mudah
Keputusan ini sebenarnya bukan hal baru. Dalam Rapat Executive Board ke-90 yang digelar pada November 2024, OCA telah menyetujui proposal dari Esports, Martial Arts and Mind Sports Committee untuk menghapus esports setelah Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026.
Mengapa Asian Games 2026 Jadi Edisi Terakhir Esports?
Berdasarkan keputusan tersebut, esports tidak lagi akan menjadi bagian setelah Asian Games 2026 di Jepang berakhir.
Pada saat sama, OCA juga menyetujui pembentukan Asian Mind Sports Federation serta penyelenggaraan kompetisi khusus untuk esports dan cabang olahraga pikiran (mind sports). Langkah ini menjadi fondasi bagi penyelenggaraan Asian Esports and Mind Sports Games.
Asian Games 2026: Timnas Pokemon Unite Indonesia Raih Perak. (Doc: NOC Indonesia)
Kuwait kini telah dikonfirmasi sebagai tuan rumah pertama. OCA memperkirakan ajang tersebut akan melibatkan sekitar 4.000 atlet, menunjukkan skala kompetisi yang cukup besar untuk edisi perdananya.
Presiden OCA, HE Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al-Thani, mengatakan penyelenggaraan Asian Esports and Mind Sports Games sejalan dengan visi organisasi untuk memperluas kesempatan kompetisi bagi atlet di seluruh Asia.
“Kami senang menandatangani kontrak tuan rumah dengan Kuwait untuk menggelar edisi pertama Asian Esports and Mind Sports Games,” ujarnya dalam pengumuman resmi OCA.
Esports Masih Tampil di Asian Games 2026
Meski demikian, esports belum sepenuhnya meninggalkan Asian Games.Asian Games 2026 Aichi-Nagoya tetap akan menjadi edisi terakhir Asian Games memasukkan esports dalam skema saat ini. Setelah itu, kompetisi esports akan beralih ke ajang baru yang berdiri terpisah dari pesta olahraga terbesar di Asia tersebut.
Timnas Indonesia MLBB memulai perjuangan di Asian Games 2026 pada 29 September dengan menghadapi Malaysia dan Arab Saudi di fase grup.
Sebelumnya, esports telah mencatat sejarah sebagai cabang peraih medali resmi di Asian Games Hangzhou 2022. Kehadirannya saat itu dianggap sebagai salah satu tonggak penting dalam upaya integrasi esports ke dalam kompetisi olahraga multievent.
Karena itu, keputusan OCA untuk memindahkan esports ke kompetisi tersendiri menandai babak baru bagi perkembangan esports tingkat kontinental.
OCA Belum Ungkap Daftar Game yang Dipertandingkan
Meski tuan rumah dan kerangka besar kompetisi sudah diumumkan, banyak aspek penting yang masih belum diketahui.
OCA belum mengungkap daftar game yang akan dipertandingkan, format kompetisi, sistem kualifikasi, maupun mekanisme partisipasi negara-negara anggota.
Ilustrasi
Belum jelas pula apakah Asian Esports and Mind Sports Games akan menggunakan struktur yang serupa dengan Asian Games, termasuk keterlibatan komite olimpiade nasional (NOC) dan federasi esports masing-masing negara.
Selain itu, OCA juga sedang membahas kemungkinan Filipina menjadi tuan rumah edisi kedua pada 2029. Keputusan terkait hal tersebut diperkirakan akan dibahas dalam General Assembly OCA 2027 di Doha.
Bagi atlet, federasi, dan program esports nasional di Asia, pertanyaan terbesar saat ini bukan lagi soal lokasi penyelenggaraan. Yang lebih penting adalah bagaimana bentuk kompetisi baru tersebut, serta posisi yang akan ditempati esports setelah tidak lagi menjadi bagian dari Asian Games mulai 2027.
Asian Games 2026: Indonesia Gagal Menembus Empat Besar Honor of Kings
Lebih lanjut, perjalanan timnas Honor of Kings (HoK) Indonesia di Asian Games 2026 Aichi-Nagoya harus berakhir lebih cepat dari prediksi. Skuad Garuda tersingkir pada babak perempat final setelah kalah dengan skor 0-2 dari tim asal China.
Hasli tersebut sekaligus mengubur harapan Indonesia untuk meraih medali dari cabang Honor of Kings, karena hanya empat tim terbaik saja yang berhak melanjutkan perjuangan ke semifinal dan perebutan podium.
Berhadapan dengan tim asal China bukan tugas mudah bagi Indonesia, kerana Negeri Tirai Bambu merupakan pasar terbesar sekaligus rumah untuk ekosistem kompetitif HoK paling berkembang dan kuat selama bertahun-tahun.
Dalam pertandingan perempat final, timnas yang diperkuat oleh Iqbal Khan Drensen, Emanuel Hendo Paska, Agung Budi Prasetyo, Neville Garrick, dan Muh Naufal Aushaf Mahfuzh menghadapi masalah untuk mengimbangi tempo permainan lawan. Alhasil, China mampu mengamankan dua game langsung dan menutup seri dengan skor 2-0.
Kekalahan tersebut membuat langkah Indonesia di nomor Honor of Kings resmi terhenti di babak delapan besar Asian Games 2026. Sementara itu, China melanjutkan perjalanan ke semifinal untuk menjaga peluang meraih medali.

items.summary:
Pakistan chaired the first meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's (SCO) Council of National Coordinators (CNC) in Islamabad on Monday, which saw participation from the Indian side as well, despite the freeze in bilateral relations between the two countries.
According to a statement issued by the Foreign Office on X, the meeting discussed a wide range of matters related to SCO activities and cooperation among member states.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Pakistan chaired the first meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's (SCO) Council of National Coordinators (CNC) in Islamabad on Monday, which saw participation from the Indian side as well, despite the freeze in bilateral relations between the two countries.
According to a statement issued by the Foreign Office on X, the meeting discussed a wide range of matters related to SCO activities and cooperation among member states.
The participants also deliberated on the programme of events planned to be held during Pakistan’s chairmanship of the organisation, the ministry said.
Pakistan assumed the chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for the 2026-27 period, during which it is scheduled to host and oversee a series of meetings and activities under the regional grouping.
Under Pakistan’s chairmanship of the SCO CHS (2026-27), first meeting of the Council of National Coordinators was held in Islamabad today. The participants discussed a wide range of issues pertaining to SCO activities and coopetation, including the programme of events to be held… pic.twitter.com/MOKTfRRlCC
— Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) September 28, 2026
India's SCO national coordinator Alok Dimri leads the Indian delegation to Islamabad, which is expected to stay in the country till the end of the month.
Dr Mohammad Faisal, a senior Pakistani diplomat who served as Pakistan's high commissioner to the United Kingdom, is representing Pakistan in the meeting.
The CNC is responsible for coordinating and managing the SCO's regular activities, including the necessary preparations for the meetings of the Council of Heads of State, the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) and the Council of Ministers for Foreign Affairs. National focal points are appointed by each Member State in accordance with its internal rules and procedures. It is provisioned to meet at least three times a year.
The FO said a day earlier that the meeting would mark an "important initial engagement" under Pakistan's chairmanship and would contribute to preparations for "various high-level engagements and activities" to be undertaken during the chairmanship, including the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting to be hosted by Pakistan in August 2027.
Pakistan, which holds the chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for 2026-27, would seek to advance the organisation's objectives under the theme "Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity", according to the FO.
"In this regard, Pakistan's Chairmanship would focus on promoting greater connectivity, fostering innovation, enhancing economic cooperation, and strengthening people-to-people contacts," it had said.
The FO said the aim would be to "translate the shared vision of Member States into practical and mutually beneficial initiatives".
"Pakistan would work closely with all Member States and the SCO Secretariat to advance these priorities and further strengthen cooperation within the SCO," it had said.
The CNC meeting would therefore provide an early forum for coordination among member states as Pakistan began its programme of activities as chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State, the FO said.
According to the statement, the meeting would contribute to preparations for various high-level engagements and activities during Pakistan's chairmanship, including the August 2027 meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State.

items.title: Tirah valley IDPs’ return to begin from October 10
items.summary:
Khyber Deputy Commissioner (DC) Shahid Ali announced during a grand jirga in Tirah Maidan on Monday that the return of internally displaced persons (IDPs) from Tirah Valley would formally begin on October 10.
Thousands of families displaced from Tirah Valley in Khyber district continue to endure severe hardships, with slow disbursement of financial assistance and uncertainty surrounding their return to their native areas compounding their difficulties.
DC Shahid Ali visited Tirah Maidan and participated in a grand jirga attended by a 24-member committee, local elders and security forces. Discussions focused on the return of IDPs, rehabilitation, provision of basic facilities and the resettlement of Bagh Bazaar.
Addressing the jirga, DC Ali said the return process would start on October 10 and that the administration and relevant departments would address problems arising during the process. He clarified that the return was not limited to transporting people back to their ancestral area

Addressing the jirga, DC Ali said the return process would start on October 10 and that the administration and relevant departments would address problems arising during the process. He clarified that the return was not limited to transporting people back to their ancestral areas, but restoration of basic needs and facilities also remained a priority.
Read: Tirah families await return after 255 days
The jirga was attended by the head of the 24-member committee, Maulana Hazrat Khan, Zahir Shah, Kamaluddin and other local elders, along with district administration officials. Participants placed issues related to the return process, the current situation in the area and the restoration of basic facilities before the deputy commissioner.
Elders demanded the rehabilitation of roads, bridges, health and education facilities, water supply, electricity, communication systems and other essential services so that returning families did not face shortages of necessities.
Detailed discussions were also held on administrative measures for a dignified, organised and phased return of the IDPs and on the plan of action. DC Ali listened to the concerns raised by the elders and the committee and directed relevant officers to take practical steps to resolve public problems.
Bara Assistant Commissioner (AC) Talha Rafiq, Tirah Maidan AC Muhammad Anwar, Tirah Maidan Tehsildar Shabab, Bara Tehsildar Daud Afridi and other officials accompanied the deputy commissioner.
Former federal minister Hamidullah Jan Afridi welcomed the development, saying “better late than never”, but stressed that mere return was not enough. He urged the authorities to fulfil all promises made to the affected families at the time of their displacement and clear outstanding dues.
“The people of Tirah have endured hardships for a long time. Along with their return, peace and security in the valley, reconstruction of homes, roads and basic infrastructure must also be ensured,” he said while talking to The Express Tribune.
Read More: Tirah victims demand return, compensation
DC Ali said steps would be taken in collaboration with relevant departments to restore public facilities and advance development activities in Tirah Maidan. Problems would be resolved phase-wise with the cooperation of local elders, the 24-member committee and concerned institutions.
During the visit, DC Ali also inspected Bagh centre and met local elders who briefed him on problems and public needs in Bagh Bazaar and other areas. He assured them that the issues would be raised at relevant forums and that he would make every effort at his level for their resolution.
Spokesman for the Tirah Affectees Movement, Sohbat Khan Afridi, said a jirga without practical steps was meaningless and that no concrete progress had so far been made on resolving the IDPs’ problems. He demanded that an official schedule for the return be issued immediately so that the affected families receive clear information about the procedure, dates and administrative arrangements.
Jamaat Ulema-e-Islam leader Izzatullah Hamkhayal said the IDPs of Tirah Valley had been suffering for a long time and their return was inevitable. He urged relevant institutions to play a priority role in establishing and maintaining sustainable peace in Tirah Maidan, and said all promises made to the affected people should be fulfilled and outstanding dues cleared before October 10.
He added that the government must ensure the provision of basic facilities, infrastructure and other necessities after the return so that the families do not face difficulties again.
Following the announcement of the return, the attention of the IDPs and local elders has now focused on the formal schedule, financial payments, reconstruction of homes and infrastructure, provision of basic facilities and practical steps for lasting peace in the area.

items.title: Nvidia Open Agent Safety Platform Launched for In-Silicon AI Agent Security With OpenShell and Sentry
items.summary: Nvidia Open Agent Safety Platform has been introduced as an open stack for isolation, monitoring, and behavior detection of AI agents. After several incidents of AI agents going off course to execute tasks that they are neither instructed nor intended to take, the new platform aims to help frontier labs to keep them contained in sandboxed environments. Nvidia is referring to such actions as “Drift”. Nvidia’s new Open Agent Safety Platform focuses on providing in-silicon agent security with the help of Nvidia OpenShell and Sentry. OpenShell aims to offer a secure runtime boundary that governs and mediates all actions taken by the AI agent, while also enforcing the policy at runtime.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Shares of insurtech companies Turtlemint and PB Fintech continued to spiral today, losing over ₹35,705 Cr in cumulative market capitalisation over the past three trading sessions. While Turtlemint hit a new loss of ₹81.45 during intraday trade today, PB Fintech’s shares lost over ₹30 apiece during early hours of today’s trade.
While Turtlemint’s stock closed today’s trading session 4.07% lower at ₹83.75, PB Fintech’s stock ended 1.17% lower at ₹1,151.90. With this, PB Fintech’s stock has seen an erosion of ₹34,155.78 Cr since Wednesday while Turtlemint’s stock has seen an erosion of ₹1,548.96 Cr.
The bearish momentum of the stocks comes as investors continue to react to the IRDAI’s proposed overhaul of insurance distribution economics.
On Wednesday, post market hours, IRDAI’s consultation paper, ‘Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution’, proposed bringing back capping product-level commission caps about three years after the regulator removed such limits and shifted to an expense of management (EoM) framework.
While the underlying reasoning for the regulatory body to propose the revision is to curb mis-selling and make distribution costs more reasonable for customers, it could potentially have a consequential impact for insurance distributors.
For companies like Turtlemint and PB Fintech, commissions play a key part in the overall business model, with these earnings contributing to the revenue earned on policies as well as influencing customer acquisition spending and sales incentives.
The proposal, as per PB Fintech cofounder Yashish Dahiya, could lead to these companies rethink their economics across products and channels. During an investor call, Dahiyan mentioned that the company could potentially explore insurance manufacturing, although it would wait for greater regulatory clarity before taking a decision.
However, the proposals are not final. IRDAI has invited comments from stakeholders until October 25, after which the regulator will decide on the final framework.
Understanding The Selling Pressure For Insurtech Stocks
The proposed framework would set different commission ceilings based on the insurance product, distribution channel and effort involved in selling and servicing a policy.
Open-architecture insurance distribution entities, which include insurance brokers like Turtlemint’s insurance broking arm and Policybazaar, could face lower caps than individual agents and other distributors.
For digital insurance distributors, the proposed changes could put pressure on commissions from health, motor and life insurance policies. This could also affect customer acquisition costs, sales incentives and the economics of partnerships with insurers.
Jefferies has flagged the proposed commission cuts as a risk for both Turtlemint and PB Fintech. The brokerage estimates that a 10% reduction in new-business commission rates could translate into a 10-12% decline in earnings.
The proposed caps vary across insurance categories. For instance, IRDAI has proposed a 15% commission ceiling for insurance distribution entities on new individual health policies and 5% on renewals and portability. For agents, the proposed limits are 20% and 10%, respectively.
Motor insurance could also see a significant reset.
The proposed framework includes zero commission for insurance distribution entities selling third-party cover on new vehicles, while own-damage, personal accident and legal liability insurance would have a 5% ceiling for such entities.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The federal government has begun work on establishing a dedicated Federal Cyber Emergency Response Team (Federal CERT) to strengthen cybersecurity across ministries, divisions, and other public-sector institutions, according to information available on the initiative.
The new body will operate within Pakistan’s existing national cybersecurity structure and will report through the government CERT mechanism to the National CERT, as set out under the country’s CERT Rules 2023. Those rules define the Federal CERT as a sectoral CERT responsible for federal government entities and other public-sector bodies.
Federal CERT to Monitor Threats and Respond to Cyber Incidents
The Federal CERT is expected to monitor cyber threats, detect attacks, and coordinate rapid response to incidents affecting federal institutions. It will also provide cybersecurity support to government departments and help improve information-sharing and coordination across the public sector.
Under the CERT Rules, sectoral CERTs are tasked with functions including collecting information on emerging threats, conducting advanced threat analysis, issuing alerts and warnings, managing vulnerabilities, and carrying out security assessments.
The move comes as the government expands its broader cybersecurity framework for public institutions. The National CERT is already responsible for incident management, security audits, forensic and malware analysis, capacity building, and other cyber defense functions.
The National CERT has also introduced the Pakistan Information Security Framework 2026 and recently launched a cybersecurity handbook for federal, provincial, and public-sector organizations, reflecting a wider push to standardize government cyber resilience and incident response.
As part of the Federal CERT rollout, the recruitment process for a director and cybersecurity specialists has also been initiated. National CERT has separately been recruiting technical staff under its broader “Cyber Security for Digital Pakistan” program, including experts in incident management, penetration testing, threat intelligence, audit, and compliance.
Once operational, the Federal CERT is expected to act as a dedicated cybersecurity coordination point for federal organizations, helping protect government digital infrastructure while improving detection, information sharing, and response to cyber incidents.
The initiative builds on Pakistan’s National Cyber Security Policy 2021, CERT Rules 2023, and the government’s evolving information-security framework for federal institutions.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has proposed tougher competition rules for telecom operators found to hold Significant Market Power (SMP), expanding both the criteria used to assess market dominance and the regulatory obligations that may follow.
The proposed changes form part of the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication’s Competition Rules 2026 and are intended to give the regulator a broader framework for assessing how much influence a telecom operator holds in a relevant market.
Under the proposed amendment, a licensee may be presumed to have significant market power if its share exceeds 25 percent of the relevant telecommunications market.
However, PTA would not rely on market share alone. Instead, the regulator may examine a wider set of market, financial, and competitive factors before reaching a final determination.
Broader Test for Significant Market Power
The proposed framework would allow PTA to consider market share based on sectoral revenues, overall market concentration, control over essential infrastructure, spectrum holdings, economies of scale, vertical integration, and barriers faced by new or expanding competitors.
Other factors may include an operator’s financial and technical resources, access to subscribers and distribution channels, network effects, buyer power, demand elasticity, excess profitability, and competition on non-price factors.
PTA may also consider the possibility of coordinated behavior between operators where relevant to competition in the market.
The broader approach means that crossing the 25 percent threshold would not automatically determine an operator’s status. Instead, the Authority would assess the overall structure and competitive conditions of the relevant market.
Additional Obligations for SMP Operators
Telecom operators determined to possess Significant Market Power could face a wider range of regulatory requirements.
These may include controls relating to tariffs and pricing, non-discrimination, transparency, interconnection and access services, reference offers, infrastructure access, accounting separation, and cost accounting.
Operators may also be required to provide fair and reasonable access to essential facilities where such infrastructure is considered critical for effective competition.
The proposed rules would further allow PTA to conduct periodic market reviews and revise an operator’s SMP status where competitive conditions, market structure, or technology change.
The amendment is designed to strengthen competition oversight in Pakistan’s telecom sector by moving beyond a simple market-share test and allowing the regulator to apply remedies based on a broader assessment of market influence.
If adopted, the Competition Rules 2026 could result in closer regulatory scrutiny for operators with substantial market presence while giving PTA greater flexibility to respond to changes in the telecom market.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Ms. Shaza Fatima Khawaja visited Huawei’s Global Service Center (GSC) in Islamabad, where she was given a briefing on its operations, toured the centre and interacted with young Pakistani engineers and technology professionals supporting global ICT operations. The Minister was received by Mr. Ethan Sun, CEO Huawei Pakistan, Mr. Ahmed Bilal Masud, CEO AI & Cloud, Huawei Pakistan, and senior management of GSC.
Speaking on the occasion, Minister Shaza Fatima stated that Huawei GSC demonstrated Pakistan’s growing potential as a global hub for technology and IT-enabled services. Describing the model as “exports without shipping containers,” she said Pakistani professionals were increasingly delivering high-value digital services to international markets from within the country. She highlighted Pakistan’s young workforce, noting that around 68 percent of the population is under the age of 30, and emphasized the need to translate this demographic strength into skilled human capital and global economic opportunities.
Recalling Huawei-Pakistan training partnership agreed during the Prime Minister’s visit to China, Ms. Shaza Fatima appreciated Huawei’s commitment to train 300,000 young Pakistanis in ICT skills. She stressed stronger collaboration among government, industry and academia to build a sustainable technology talent pipeline and connect young Pakistanis with international opportunities. The Minister appreciated Huawei’s contribution to technical capacity building through its ICT Academies and encouraged the company to further expand investment, knowledge transfer, mentoring and explore opportunities for establishing an R&D centre in Pakistan.
Interacting with women engineers at the Centre, the Minister appreciated their contribution to Pakistan’s digital economy and underscored the importance of creating greater opportunities for women in the technology sector.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Ethan Sun said Huawei was proud to contribute to Pakistan’s digital development by strengthening local technical expertise and creating opportunities for Pakistani professionals to participate in the global digital economy.
The Huawei Global Service Center in Islamabad serves as a hub for global technology operations, providing remote technical support, network operations, service assurance and other advanced ICT services to international customers. The Centre provides Pakistani engineers and technical professionals with opportunities to contribute to global technology operations from within Pakistan.

items.title: Resident Evil Requiem Diperkirakan Sudah Terjual 8,5 Juta Kopi
items.summary:
Resident Evil Requiem kembali mencatat angka penjualan besar setelah sebelumnya Capcom mengumumkan game tersebut telah terjual lebih dari 6 juta kopi hanya dalam dua minggu sejak peluncuran. Pencapaian itu menjadikannya salah satu game dengan pertumbuhan penjualan tercepat dalam sejarah seri Resident Evil.
Kini, Alinea Analytics memperkirakan penjualan Resident Evil Requiem telah mencapai sekitar 8,5 juta kopi. Estimasi tersebut mencakup versi PlayStation 5, PC, dan Xbox Series X|S. Berbeda dari angka 6 juta yang sebelumnya diumumkan Capcom, angka 8,5 juta ini merupakan perkiraan dari perusahaan analitik dan bukan angka penjualan resmi terbaru dari Capcom.
Menariknya, distribusi penjualan berdasarkan platform menunjukkan perbedaan yang cukup besar. Alinea Analytics memperkirakan PlayStation 5 menyumbang 48,1 persen dari total penjualan, sementara Steam berada di angka 43,4 persen. Xbox Series X|S menjadi platform dengan kontribusi paling kecil, yakni sekitar 8,6 persen dari keseluruhan
items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Resident Evil Requiem kembali mencatat angka penjualan besar setelah sebelumnya Capcom mengumumkan game tersebut telah terjual lebih dari 6 juta kopi hanya dalam dua minggu sejak peluncuran. Pencapaian itu menjadikannya salah satu game dengan pertumbuhan penjualan tercepat dalam sejarah seri Resident Evil.
Kini, Alinea Analytics memperkirakan penjualan Resident Evil Requiem telah mencapai sekitar 8,5 juta kopi. Estimasi tersebut mencakup versi PlayStation 5, PC, dan Xbox Series X|S. Berbeda dari angka 6 juta yang sebelumnya diumumkan Capcom, angka 8,5 juta ini merupakan perkiraan dari perusahaan analitik dan bukan angka penjualan resmi terbaru dari Capcom.
Menariknya, distribusi penjualan berdasarkan platform menunjukkan perbedaan yang cukup besar. Alinea Analytics memperkirakan PlayStation 5 menyumbang 48,1 persen dari total penjualan, sementara Steam berada di angka 43,4 persen. Xbox Series X|S menjadi platform dengan kontribusi paling kecil, yakni sekitar 8,6 persen dari keseluruhan penjualan yang diperkirakan.

PlayStation 5 dan Steam Jadi Kontributor Utama
Data dari Alinea Analytics
Jika estimasi tersebut akurat, PlayStation 5 dan PC melalui Steam menjadi sumber utama penjualan Resident Evil Requiem. Selisih antara keduanya juga relatif tipis, dengan PS5 berada sedikit di atas Steam berdasarkan perhitungan Alinea Analytics.
Data tersebut sekaligus menunjukkan bahwa Xbox Series X|S memiliki porsi yang jauh lebih kecil dibandingkan dua platform lainnya. Namun, angka ini sebaiknya tidak langsung dianggap sebagai gambaran keseluruhan minat pemain terhadap seri Resident Evil, karena data yang digunakan merupakan estimasi penjualan dan tidak menjelaskan seluruh faktor di balik perbedaan antarplatform.
Penjualan Fisik Masih Punya Peran
Alinea Analytics juga mencatat bahwa penjualan fisik masih memiliki kontribusi yang cukup besar di PS5. Berdasarkan estimasinya, sekitar 30,8 persen penjualan Resident Evil Requiem di platform tersebut berasal dari salinan fisik.
Selain penjualan unit, perusahaan analitik tersebut memperkirakan Resident Evil Requiem telah menghasilkan lebih dari US$500 juta pendapatan dari seluruh platform yang dianalisis. Namun, angka pendapatan ini juga merupakan estimasi, bukan laporan keuangan resmi Capcom. Dengan demikian, performa komersial Requiem memang terlihat kuat berdasarkan data yang tersedia, tetapi angka 8,5 juta kopi dan US$500 juta tetap perlu dipisahkan dari angka resmi yang telah dikonfirmasi Capcom.

items.title: SC Refuses To Stay UPI MDR, Seeks Centre’s Response On ₹2,000 Threshold
items.summary:
The Supreme Court today refused to stay the Centre’s decision to introduce merchant discount rate (MDR) charges on select UPI payments above ₹2,000, while seeking responses on the legal basis and nature of the levy.
According to a Bar and Bench report, the SC bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, was hearing a PIL filed by advocate Anjan Datta challenging the framework, which is scheduled to take effect from October 15.
The SC directed the Centre, the RBI, and the NPCI to file their responses within four weeks.
The petition argued that the levy could squeeze merchants’ working capital, encourage traders to refuse UPI payments or split transactions to avoid charges, and eventually be reflected in consumer prices.

According to a Bar and Bench report, the SC bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, was hearing a PIL filed by advocate Anjan Datta challenging the framework, which is scheduled to take effect from October 15.
The SC directed the Centre, the RBI, and the NPCI to file their responses within four weeks.
The petition argued that the levy could squeeze merchants’ working capital, encourage traders to refuse UPI payments or split transactions to avoid charges, and eventually be reflected in consumer prices.
It questioned the ₹2,000 transaction threshold and the ₹1 Lakh monthly receipt limit for merchant exemptions, alleging that the government had not disclosed the data or methodology used to determine them. The plea also contrasted these restrictions with the continued zero-charge protection for RuPay debit card payments, which has no monetary ceiling.
For instance, a ₹2,001 transaction would attract MDR while a ₹2,000 payment would remain exempt, creating an abrupt increase in costs that could influence merchant behaviour, the petitioner argued.
During the hearing, Additional Solicitor General N Venkataraman told the court that P2P UPI transfers would remain free and around 96% of merchant transactions would be unaffected.
Under the framework, P2P transfers and P2M payments up to ₹2,000 will remain free. Eligible P2M transactions above ₹2,000 will attract 0.4% MDR, subject to a ₹300 cap, which is reached at a transaction value of ₹75,000.
Specified sectors, including railways, telecom, insurance, and fuel, will attract a flat ₹5 charge, while capital-market payments will carry a 0.02% levy, capped at ₹300. Small merchants receiving up to ₹1 Lakh a month through UPI QR codes will remain exempt.
MDR is charged to merchants for processing payments. The framework prohibits passing the charge on to consumers, although the petition raises concerns about merchants recovering the cost through higher prices.
How Centre Cleared Way For UPI MDR
The framework follows amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act (PSSA), 2007.
In a September 14 gazette notification, the finance ministry specified RuPay-powered debit cards and UPI transactions up to ₹2,000 as electronic payment modes on which banks and system providers cannot impose charges.
The notification followed Parliament’s passage of the Taxation And Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which amended Section 10A of the PSSA.
The earlier provision barred banks and system providers from imposing charges on UPI transactions. The amendment, however, allowed the Centre to specify the electronic payment modes and transaction thresholds that would remain exempt from MDR.
The government subsequently fixed the UPI exemption at ₹2,000, paving the way for charges on higher-value merchant payments.
The move comes as UPI has grown rapidly over the past few years under the zero-MDR regime. UPI processed 2,451 Cr transactions worth ₹29.82 Lakh Cr in August.
NPCI MD and CEO Dilip Asbe said last week that a market-driven model is needed to fund the rising cybersecurity, infrastructure and scalability costs of the payments network. He said the ecosystem would need to keep investing in AI and other technologies to protect UPI infrastructure.
“The ability and the tools with the hackers are really very powerful compared to what we could actually use inside. And somewhere AI is fairly expensive to use, and we’ll have to continue to invest, use AI to make our systems fully protected… (so that) the trust in the payment system is fully maintained,” he said.
Asbe estimated that the new MDR framework could generate ₹13,000 Cr to ₹15,000 Cr in its first year. He also said the cost of maintaining and expanding the payments infrastructure has risen sharply, including the cost of server hardware.
The post SC Refuses To Stay UPI MDR, Seeks Centre’s Response On ₹2,000 Threshold appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Guest Post
items.content:
I have watched hundreds of founder-investor conversations. Across boardrooms in Johannesburg, accelerator stages in Lagos, pitch nights in Nairobi and Zoom calls that could have been emails. And after all of that, I want to offer you something most pitch coaches will not say out loud, writes Steven Dossou, venture strategist and founder at AETHER by IRIS Vision Capital.
The biggest mistake founders make is not their deck. It is not their numbers. It is not their story.
It is walking into the room thinking the pitch is one-directional.
A fundraising pitch is not a performance. It is an interview. And the most important shift a founder can make is realising they are not the only one being evaluated.
You are also evaluating the investor.
You are choosing a partner, not collecting a cheque
Let me say that more plainly. Raising capital from the wrong investor is one of the most expensive decisions a founder can make. I have seen it kill companies that the market actually wanted. Not because the money ran out, but because the relationship broke down. Misaligned expectations. Wrong timelines. An investor who did not understand the sector applying pressure from a playbook that never fit.
This is part of the problem AETHER is built to solve. Not just connecting founders with investors, but connecting founders with the right investors based on genuine compatibility across sector, stage, geography and working style. The infrastructure for intelligent matching in private capital simply does not exist at scale yet. Most founders are still walking into rooms with whoever said yes.
That has to change. And it starts with how founders approach the pitch itself.
Know who is sitting across the table before you open your mouth
Oren Klaff opens Pitch Anything with a framework that most people read and then immediately ignore. He argues that the brain processes a pitch through a hierarchy of frames, and the person who controls the frame controls the outcome. But before you can control anything, you need to understand the cognitive landscape of the person you are pitching to.
Investors are not a single audience. They never were.
Some are numbers-driven. They want revenue, margins, churn, CAC, LTV, burn rate, runway, and a credible path to a return. If you cannot walk them through a unit economics model without flinching, you have already lost them. For this investor, your story is decoration. Your numbers are the pitch.
Others are founder-driven. They are making a bet on you before they make a bet on the business. They want to understand why you are the person who has to solve this problem. What have you lived through that qualifies you to build this? Can you attract a team? Can you navigate the hard months? For this investor, the numbers are supporting evidence. The founder is the thesis.
And then there are investors who are moved by neither numbers nor narrative alone. They are looking for a signal that you understand your market at a depth that they cannot access without you. They want proprietary insight. They want to feel that you know something they do not.
The mistake is not having the wrong pitch. The mistake is giving the same pitch to all three.
Before every conversation, I ask three questions: What does this investor care most about? What has their portfolio told me about their thesis? And what would make them say no before I even finish the first slide?
Research the investor the way you expect them to research you.
Story is not biography
One of Klaff’s sharpest observations in Pitch Anything is about what he calls the STRONG method: Setting the frame, Telling the story, Revealing the intrigue, Offering the prize, Nailing the hookpoint, Getting the deal. The order matters. Most founders invert it. They tell the story first, in exhaustive detail, and by the time they get to the intrigue, the investor has already decided.
Storytelling in a pitch is not about saying everything. It is about making the right person care about the right thing at the right moment.
I learned this the hard way. Early in my career, I sat across from a fund manager in Accra and spent eleven minutes explaining the origin of the idea I was presenting. By the time I got to the market opportunity, he had checked his phone twice. I had not lost him because the opportunity was weak. I lost him because I made him wait too long to understand why it mattered.
The lesson: do not make the investor do the work of finding the insight. Create the context, establish the stakes, generate the curiosity, then give them the opportunity. In that order.
Numbers need a narrative. Narrative needs numbers.
The two failure modes sit on opposite ends of the same spectrum.
On one end, the founder who shows up with a pitch deck full of emotion, vision and energy but cannot answer basic questions about their cost of acquisition or how they calculated their market size. When an investor asks a financial question and the founder stumbles, what the investor hears is not “I am not a finance person.” What they hear is “I do not understand my own business well enough to protect your capital.”
On the other end, the founder who hides behind the spreadsheet. Slide after slide of charts and projections, delivered with the confidence of someone who believes that if the model is right, the deal closes itself. It does not. Numbers without context are just numbers. If you grew 200% last quarter, I need to know from what base. If your TAM is $15 billion, I need to understand how you reach 1% of it. If you are raising $3 million, I need to know what that capital specifically unlocks and why that milestone changes the trajectory of the company.
The strongest founders I have worked with do not choose between story and numbers. They move between the two fluently. They know which number to lead with for which investor, and they know which moment of the story makes that number land harder.
The psychology of the room
Klaff spends considerable time in Pitch Anything on what he calls “status frames” and the croc brain, the primitive part of the mind that filters for threat, novelty and social hierarchy before anything else gets processed. His point is that if you walk into a pitch presenting yourself as lower-status than the investor, your brilliant idea will still be filtered through that lens.
This does not mean manufactured arrogance. It means earned confidence.
There is a psychological difference between:
“I really need this investment to work out.”
and:
“We are looking for the right partners to help us reach the next stage.”
The underlying need for capital may be identical. The frame is entirely different. One communicates desperation. The other communicates selectivity. And selectivity, even in early-stage fundraising, signals that something worth having is on the table.
I have watched founders with imperfect businesses create genuine investor interest through the quality of their conviction and the clarity of their thinking. I have also watched founders with genuinely strong businesses undermine themselves because they communicated from a place of anxiety. The investor reads the body language, the hesitation, the over-explanation, and they price it in.
Acknowledge what you do not know. A founder who says “here is what we know, here is what we have not yet proven, and here is how we intend to prove it” demonstrates more credibility than one who claims certainty across the board. Investors have been lied to. They are not looking for perfection. They are looking for honesty, clarity and a credible path.
Interview the investor
This is where most founders leave significant value on the table.
During the pitch, ask questions. Real ones, not performative ones.
How do you typically engage with portfolio companies after investment? What does your follow-on strategy look like? What has gone wrong in similar investments, and how did you respond? What would make you uncomfortable about backing this? Who else in your portfolio might become a strategic partner or a competitor to us?
These questions serve two purposes. First, they give you genuinely useful information about whether this is the right partner for the next three to seven years of your life. Second, they shift the dynamic of the conversation. The founder who asks sharp questions about the investor’s portfolio and working style is not a supplicant. They are a peer evaluating a potential business relationship.
This takes confidence. It also takes preparation. But it is the difference between a pitch and a conversation. And conversations close deals.
The pitch starts long before the deck
Fundraising is not a ten-minute presentation. It is a process that demands four distinct skills operating simultaneously: public speaking to hold attention and communicate credibility; deal-making to understand what the other party needs and structure an offer accordingly; financial fluency to speak the language of return and risk; and psychological awareness to read the room, control the frame and know when to press and when to pause.
Most founders develop one or two of these and neglect the rest. The ones who raise capital well have done the work on all four.
Disrupt Africa covers this ecosystem every day. You know that African founders are navigating harder markets, longer cycles and more skeptical capital than their counterparts in Silicon Valley. The margin for a weak pitch is thinner here. The need to be sharp, credible and genuinely prepared is higher.
The founders who raise are not always the ones with the best ideas. They are the ones who understand what they are asking for, who they are asking, why it matters, and what the other person needs to hear to say yes.
Next time you walk into that room, do not ask yourself how to convince the investor to write a cheque.
Ask yourself whether you are talking to the right investor in the first place, and whether you are ready to find out.
Steven Dossou is a venture strategist, TEDx speaker and founder of AETHER , an AI-powered capital matchmaking platform connecting founders, investors, LPs and fund managers across the US, Europe, Middle East and Africa. He is the founder of IRIS Vision Capital and operates across US, Europe and Africa.

items.title: Aksesori vivo Selfie Monitor Bikin Vlogging Pakai vivo X500 Jauh Lebih Mudah
items.summary:
Dalam memperkenalkan lini flagship terbarunya yakni vivo X500 Series awal pekan ini, vivo juga turut menghadirkan sejumlah aksesori khusus, dirancang agar mampu meningkatkan pengalaman pengguna dalam menikmati kualitas dan kemampuan kamera smartphone vivo terbaru. Selain lensa telefoto, vivo Selfie Monitor juga tidak kalah menarik perhatian. Menjadi layar kedua yang dapat dilepas-pasang secara nirkabel.
Ya, ini memang bukanlah solusi yang benar-benar baru. Sebelumnya, aksesori layar kedua yang bisa ditempel ke bodi belakang smartphone memang sudah banyak dijual, namun umumnya tidak memiliki tampilan layar yang oke, atau kurang responsif. Sementara OPPO sempat merilis solusi serupa lewat OPPO Bubble, dirancang untuk Reno16 Series.
Namun berbeda dengan solusi OPPO, vivo Selfie Monitor dirancang dalam dimensi jauh lebih besar, walaupun sejatinya masih relatif kompak sebagai aksesori layar sekunder. Fungsinya juga lebih banyak, dan bisa menjadi solusi praktis selain menyematkan layar kedua
items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
Dalam memperkenalkan lini flagship terbarunya yakni vivo X500 Series awal pekan ini, vivo juga turut menghadirkan sejumlah aksesori khusus, dirancang agar mampu meningkatkan pengalaman pengguna dalam menikmati kualitas dan kemampuan kamera smartphone vivo terbaru. Selain lensa telefoto, vivo Selfie Monitor juga tidak kalah menarik perhatian. Menjadi layar kedua yang dapat dilepas-pasang secara nirkabel.
Ya, ini memang bukanlah solusi yang benar-benar baru. Sebelumnya, aksesori layar kedua yang bisa ditempel ke bodi belakang smartphone memang sudah banyak dijual, namun umumnya tidak memiliki tampilan layar yang oke, atau kurang responsif. Sementara OPPO sempat merilis solusi serupa lewat OPPO Bubble, dirancang untuk Reno16 Series.
Namun berbeda dengan solusi OPPO, vivo Selfie Monitor dirancang dalam dimensi jauh lebih besar, walaupun sejatinya masih relatif kompak sebagai aksesori layar sekunder. Fungsinya juga lebih banyak, dan bisa menjadi solusi praktis selain menyematkan layar kedua secara permanen seperti apa yang dilakukan oleh Xiaomi dengan flagship terbarunya yang juga rilis pekan ini.
Baca juga: Unboxing vivo X500 Pro Max Photographer Kit, Edisi Khusus dengan Aksesori Kamera Komplit
Tawarkan Layar Luas dan Mekanisme Magnetik
Spesifikasi vivo Selfie Monitor terbilang cukup menarik untuk fungsi yang ditawarkan. Dari tampilannya, perangkat ini dibuat terlihat seperti aksesori MagSafe, berbentuk persegi, dengan bagian utama didominasi oleh layar. Dimensi layar vivo Selfie Monitor tergolong luas, mencapai 3,92 inci. Dan dengan rasio lebih normal dibandingkan penawaran OPPO, maka menjadikannya lebih fungsional.
Panel yang digunakan juga berkualitas, sudah berjenis AMOLED dengan kerapatan piksel tinggi 419ppi. Semua dikemas ke dalam sebuah bodi yang tergolong ramping, hanya 5,65mm, dengan bobot kisaran 68 gram saja. Layar aksesori vivo satu ini juga mendukung input sentuh, memungkinkan pengguna untuk ganti mode foto, video dan lainnya.
Di balik sisi layar, ada permukaan yang dilengkapi oleh magnet, supaya bisa menempel ke bodi belakang vivo X500 Series yang sudah terpasang case khusus. Sementara di sisi perangkat, vivo Selfie Monitor juga dilengkapi sejumlah tombol untuk menambah fungsi sekaligus pintasan.
Tersambung secara nirkabel, vivo Selfie Monitor dapat tetap digunakan hingga jarak 10 meter dari perangkat. Dengan kata lain, tidak hanya difungsikan ketika sedang menempel di sisi belakang bodi saja. Sehingga menambah fungsi perangkat, termasuk sebagai remote shutter.
Harga vivo Selfie Monitor Rp1,6 Jutaan
Dalam presentasinya, vivo Selfie Monitor diunggulkan dengan tampilan antarmuka yang dirancang versatile—tidak hanya bisa digunakan untuk ubah antara mode foto dan video, namun juga mendukung tampilan perekaman video profesional dengan sejumlah informasi parameter manual. Pas untuk kreator yang ingin hasilkan visual lebih presisi sesuai keinginan.
Dan ketika sedang tidak digunakan, dimensi aksesori vivo X500 Series satu ini juga dirancang mudah untuk dibawa ke mana saja, termasuk mudah masuk ke kantong atau saku celana. Belum diketahui apakah aksesori satu ini juga akan dibuat kompatibel ke smartphone vivo lainnya.
Harga vivo Selfie Monitor dibanderol sekitar CNY599 (Rp1,6 jutaan). Sayangnya, aksesori ini baru tersedia untuk pasar China saja. Menurut Gizmo friends, apakah menarik untuk dibuat tersedia resmi kelak vivo X500 Series dijual di Indonesia?

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority has issued around 300 district-level Class Licenses to telecom and internet service providers as part of an expanding effort to improve broadband access, fiber deployment, and digital connectivity across the country.
PTA officials said most of the new licenses have been issued in districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where the regulator is seeking to encourage smaller operators to expand internet access beyond major urban centers.
The district-level licensing framework allows companies to provide internet services within a specific district rather than requiring broader regional or nationwide licenses. PTA introduced the framework from January 1, 2026, with the stated aim of promoting local investment and improving broadband penetration in underserved areas.
District-Level Licenses Target Fiber Expansion
According to PTA officials, the issuance of 300 licenses over the past several months is expected to support fiberization and last-mile connectivity, particularly in areas where fixed broadband infrastructure remains limited.
Each class license is valid for 10 years. The initial license fee is Rs 300,000, while the annual license fee for the first year is Rs 100,000. Earlier details of the framework also show an application processing fee of Rs 20,000 and annual license fees that rise by 10% in subsequent years.
License holders are required to begin providing services within one year of receiving the license. Previous PTA licensing details also require operators to meet rollout obligations after obtaining their commencement certificate.
The regulator has said the district-based model is designed to lower entry barriers for smaller and regional internet providers while increasing competition in Pakistan’s broadband market.
Earlier this year, PTA had issued dozens of such licenses in districts including Lahore, Sargodha, Faisalabad, Islamabad, Attock, South Waziristan, and Lower Chitral, showing that the framework was already extending into both urban and underserved areas.
PTA officials now expect the larger licensing drive to help accelerate fiber deployment in remote districts, improve internet availability, and widen access to digital services. The initiative forms part of a broader push to expand Pakistan’s telecom infrastructure, with authorities also pursuing measures to reduce right-of-way costs and encourage investment in fiber networks.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Anyone bringing telecom equipment into Pakistan will now need PTA’s sign-off first. The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has made compliance with prescribed technical standards mandatory, and the rules explicitly cover 5G devices and network equipment.
Under the framework, a certificate from PTA must be obtained before relevant equipment is imported, installed, or used. PTA 5G equipment compliance is now a legal condition, not a voluntary benchmark.
What the framework requires
The rules bring international standards for 5G user equipment into Pakistani regulation. The requirements cover radio performance, spectrum access, and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). EMC means a device works properly around other electronics without causing or suffering interference.
Separate radio conformance testing requirements have been set for 5G New Radio (NR) base stations. NR is the air interface that 5G networks use, and base stations are the towers and radio units that connect devices to the network.
Testing for 5G equipment also draws on the relevant 3GPP and ETSI conformance standards. For 5G user equipment, the requirements cover radio transmission, reception, performance, and protocol testing.
Legal basis and who is covered
The framework is enforced under the Telecommunication Equipment Standard Regulations 2024. It was notified in the Gazette through S.R.O. 1110(I)/2026 after federal government approval.
It applies to PTA licensees, telecom equipment manufacturers, and importers. That puts operators and the supply chain under the same obligation.
Element
What the rules say
Requirement
PTA certificate before import, installation, or use
Standards
5G user equipment: radio performance, spectrum access, EMC
Base stations
Separate radio conformance testing for 5G NR
Test references
3GPP and ETSI conformance standards
Legal basis
Telecommunication Equipment Standard Regulations 2024; S.R.O. 1110(I)/2026
Applies to
PTA licensees, manufacturers, importers
What PTA says it wants
PTA says the step should improve compatibility, interoperability, safety, and service quality. It also expects the framework to support technical progress in the telecom ecosystem and to encourage local manufacturing.
Interoperability means equipment from different makers can work together on the same network. For a country that imports most of its telecom hardware, that is a practical concern.
Why the timing matters
Pakistan sold 480 MHz of spectrum in its March 2026 auction, raising about $507 million from Jazz, Zong, and Ufone. Operators are now expected to build out 5G. A standards regime that arrives once the network build begins puts a clear checkpoint on the equipment they order.
For importers, this adds a compliance step before goods clear. Firms that already test to 3GPP and ETSI standards may find the transition simple. Smaller importers, who often rely on suppliers’ paperwork, may find it harder.
The value of this framework will show in execution. Clear timelines, published test procedures, and a fast, predictable certification process would make it an asset to serious importers and manufacturers. If the process is slow or opaque, it will add cost and delay without the quality gains PTA is aiming for.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Agritech startup Balwaan Krishi has raised ₹100 Cr (around $10 Mn) in its Series B funding round led by First Bridge India Growth Fund Private Equity, with participation from other institutional investors whose names were not disclosed.
The Jaipur-based startup will use the capital to expand domestic manufacturing capacity, strengthen its dealer and service network in southern India, and develop new farm equipment.
Balwaan said a significant portion of the funding will go towards manufacturing in India to reduce its dependence on imported machinery and components, while giving it greater control over product quality and availability.
Its product development plans include power weeders, battery sprayers, and other farm equipment, with connected features to monitor machines and identify maintenance needs before a breakdown.
Founded in 2016 by brothers duo Rohit and Shubham Bajaj, Balwaan makes agricultural equipment for Indian farming conditions. Its products are priced between ₹10,000 and ₹1 Lakh, targeting small and marginal farmers for whom larger machinery may be too expensive or unsuitable.
The startup claims that more than 4 Lakh farmers use its equipment. It sells through a network of more than 800 dealers across northern India, alongside ecommerce channels.
The latest funding will support the expansion of its distribution and after-sales service network in southern India.
“This funding allows us to strengthen manufacturing, broaden our reach and continue building products specifically for Indian farming conditions,” said cofounder Rohit.
The Series B round follows Balwaan’s ₹40 Cr Series A investment from JM Financial Private Equity in June 2024. That funding was also earmarked for product development and distribution expansion, including in southern India.
Balwaan’s fundraise adds to investments across agricultural machinery, supply chains, and financing this year. In March, WayCool raised ₹210 Cr from Lightrock India.
Meanwhile, Arya.ag raised $80 Mn in a Series D round from GEF Capital Partners in January. Around 70% of that round comprised primary capital, with the remainder coming from secondary share sales. Arya.ag said it planned to use the fresh capital to expand its reach among farmer communities and accelerate product development.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Defence tech startup Tonbo Imaging has received SEBI approval for its proposed IPO, which comprises an OFS of up to 1.81 Cr equity shares.
The Bengaluru-based startup had initially filed its DRHP in December 2025 and secured SEBI’s approval in July. It subsequently filed fresh draft papers in August, keeping the offer size largely unchanged.
According to SEBI’s latest processing status update, the regulator issued its observations on Tonbo’s IPO papers on September 21.
All three cofounders — Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar, Ankit Kumar, and Cecilia D’Souza — are looking to sell part of their holdings through the IPO, alongside a promoter group shareholder and existing investors.
The startup’s backers include Qualcomm Ventures, Artiman, Celesta, Edelweiss Value and Growth Fund, HBL Engineering, Tenacity Ventures, Export-Import Bank of India, and Florintree.
Founded in 2003, Tonbo Imaging transitioned into a defence-focused product manufacturing company in 2012 following the buyout of its erstwhile parent by its promoters, which include cofounders Kondangi, Ankit Kumar, and D’Souza.
In April last year, the startup raised ₹175 Cr in its Series D funding round from Florintee Advisors and EXIM Bank at a valuation of ₹1,500 Cr.
According to the Frost & Sullivan report cited in the company’s DRHP, Tonbo was the largest manufacturer by sales value of thermal imaging systems supplied to government and defence agencies in India during FY24-FY26. It accounted for 94.3% of India’s thermal imaging exports by units during the same period.
As of March 31, 2026, Tonbo had deployed more than 28,000 systems across 24 countries. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging cores, weapon sights, thermal binoculars, targeting systems, missile seekers, fire-control systems and missile-guidance systems.
The startup said it owns 100% of its intellectual property since FY24, spanning optics, embedded software and electronics.
Tonbo follows an asset-light manufacturing model, outsourcing production to certified electronics manufacturing services partners such as Kaynes Technology and Avalon Technology. Prototype development, system integration and qualification testing are undertaken in-house.
On the financial front, Tonbo Imaging reported a net profit of ₹362.6 Cr in FY26, a 30% decrease from ₹469.1 Cr in the previous year. The startup also reported a 22.7% decline in its operating revenue to ₹299.9 Cr from ₹374.3 Cr in FY25.
