items.author: Rilwan Muhammad
items.content:
The Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has intensified its sensitisation campaign in Kano state on the Dangote Refinery Initial Public Offering (IPO), encouraging more northerners to participate in the investment.
According to the forum, the campaign, held in Kano on Saturday, was aimed at helping prospective investors understand the share purchase process and avoid falling victim to misinformation or exploitation.
‎Some prospective investors had expressed concerns about the IPO, with claims circulating on social media that the refinery was yet to make profits and that the offer could expose ordinary Nigerians to losses.
‎But the President of the ACF Kano State chapter and leader of the Shareholders Association, Dr Goni Umar Farouk, dismissed the claims as unfounded, saying the refinery’s financial records showed significant revenue and profit.
2027: ADC, NDC going nowhere, Atiku&#8217;s LGA still voted APC last week &#8211; Nentawe
Inmates die as cholera hits Kano prison
‎Farouk said the refinery generated $1.82 billion in the first six months of the year, while its revenue rose from N9.38 trillion in 2024 to N18.74 trillion in 2025.
‎He also said the refinery recorded N2.5 trillion in profit after tax during the half-year period.
‎“So, anyone saying the refinery is running at a loss is simply spreading falsehood,” he said.
‎Farouk said the ACF intervention was intended to ensure that northern Nigerians were adequately informed about the IPO and could make investment decisions based on available financial information rather than rumours circulating online.
‎The ACF said its campaign would continue to educate residents on the IPO process and encourage prospective investors to use legitimate channels when seeking to participate.
‎Farouk also said investors should consider the refinery’s financial performance and future prospects when assessing the offer, rather than relying on unverified claims on social media.
Sa’a Umar, one of those who purchased shares through the ACF arrangement, said she initially had reservations about the investment but decided to participate after receiving information about the process.
‎“I came to register here at the ACF office and we pray to benefit. Investment is important, and we encourage others to come here instead of trying elsewhere and making mistakes,” she said.
‎Another investor, Iliya Ado, said the sensitisation programme had helped address some of his earlier concerns about participating in the offer.
‎“People may not know where to go, or they may be discouraged, but the system is working. I appreciate the early work of the forum. It is a very good initiative for the development of people through investments,” he said.
‎The sensitisation drive came amid growing interest in the Dangote Refinery IPO, which is being presented as an opportunity for Nigerians to participate directly in the ownership of one of the country’s major industrial assets.

items.title: Spain beat England in Nations League to extend unbeaten run
items.summary:
World champions Spain came from behind to beat England 3-2 in an entertaining Nations League encounter at Wembley on Saturday, denying the hosts a cathartic win after their painful World Cup exit.
Victory for Luis de la Fuente’s men extends Spain’s astonishing unbeaten run to 39 matches — a record for a European team.
Thomas Tuchel’s men got off to a nightmare start when Lamine Yamal pounced on a gaffe by defender Marc Guehi, and they could easily have been three goals down as silky Spain created multiple chances.
But England, criticised for their ultra-defensive tactics in their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina, showed adventure of their own and got their reward in the 36th minute when Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon finished a fine team move.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
World champions Spain came from behind to beat England 3-2 in an entertaining Nations League encounter at Wembley on Saturday, denying the hosts a cathartic win after their painful World Cup exit.
Victory for Luis de la Fuente’s men extends Spain’s astonishing unbeaten run to 39 matches — a record for a European team.
Thomas Tuchel’s men got off to a nightmare start when Lamine Yamal pounced on a gaffe by defender Marc Guehi, and they could easily have been three goals down as silky Spain created multiple chances.
But England, criticised for their ultra-defensive tactics in their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina, showed adventure of their own and got their reward in the 36th minute when Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon finished a fine team move.
Four minutes later the home side were ahead after Kane headed home Nico O’Reilly’s cross via a Marc Cucurella deflection.
Kane had a golden chance to give England a two-goal cushion from the penalty spot 10 minutes into the second half but slipped slightly, crashing his shot against the bar.
Spain, who beat England in the Euro 2024 final, took full advantage, with substitutes Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal putting their side ahead, taking advantage of more sloppy defensive play from the home side.
– Shaky start –
England boss Thomas Tuchel was adamant ahead of the match that it did not signal a new start but will have been dismayed his team’s nervy start.
Manchester City’s Guehi, with a chance to clear in the second minute, inexplicably turned back towards goalkeeper James Trafford, apparently unaware that Yamal was just behind him.
The teenager collected the ball and curled a left-footed effort off the inside of the post.
Ferran Torres was in the thick of the action, with an effort ruled out for offside and another shot saved by Trafford, in for long-time number one Jordan Pickford.
He also squandered a golden opportunity with just the goalkeeper to beat.
Yamal then set up Dani Olmo, who flashed wide as Spain rued yet another miss.
England, who had showed plenty of promise down the wings, made the visitors pay with an incisive counter-attacking goal after winning the ball back deep in their own half.
Gordon was involved early in the move and surged forward, collecting Jude Bellingham’s pass to steer the ball decisively past goalkeeper Unai Simon.
And, with the atmosphere now totally changed, England were in front when Kane rose to head home.
Tuchel’s men started the second half brightly and had a chance to extend their lead from the spot when they were awarded a penalty for a Rodri foul on Bellingham following a VAR check.
But Kane crashed his shot against the bar and England paid the price when Baena steered home on the hour mark after O’Reilly had given the ball away to Olmo.
Worse was to come for the home side when Baena turned provider for Oyarzabal, who dinked the ball over Trafford.

The National Working Committee (NWC) of the All Progressives Congress (APC) says it has reviewed the party’s structures nationwide and declared it ready for the 2027 general elections.
The APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, made this known at a news conference on Saturday at the end of the committee’s three-day retreat in Maiduguri.
Yilwatda said the review covered the party’s structures from the national, state, local government and ward levels to polling units.
He added that the assessment gave the party what he described as “clean bill of health”, noting that the NWC considered the APC strong and prepared for the 2027 elections.
The chairman said the NWC also passed a vote of confidence on President Bola Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and other candidates who emerged from the party’s primary elections.
According to him, the committee will intensify reconciliation efforts at the state, local government and ward levels to address internal differences and strengthen the party.
He urged state chapters that had yet to establish reconciliation committees to do so, saying the initiative would help to consolidate the party ahead of the elections.
Yilwatda said the NWC would take active role in engagements and campaign activities aimed at communicating the policies and programmes of the Tinubu administration to Nigerians.
On recent elections, he said the committee reviewed the outcomes of off-cycle and by-elections and was satisfied with APC’s performance.
He cited Ogun and Delta as states where the party had previously not won elections but recorded victories in recent contests.
The chairman said the APC won four of five elections conducted the previous week, while losing one, describing its performance in the lost election as strong.
He commended the Borno Government for hosting the retreat and thanked newsmen for the coverage.
He also condoled with the government and people of Niger over the death of 37 miners.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Former Deputy President of the Senate, Sen. Ovie Omo-Agege, says Thursday’s Supreme Court judgment on the Electoral Act did not disqualify him from contesting the 2027 Delta Central Senatorial election.
This is contained in a statement by his Special Adviser on Strategy and Communications, Mr Godwin Anaighe, on Saturday in Asaba.
Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central, said the judgment did not make any order against him or pronounce him ineligible to contest the 2027 election.
According to him, the Supreme Court only restored Sections 77(5), 77(6), 77(7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, which concern party membership registers and candidate nomination.
He described as misplaced the celebration by supporters of Sen. Ede Dafinone, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, who, according to him, were congratulating their candidate over the judgment.
Omo-Agege said his name was contained in the NDC membership register submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) before May 10 and appeared on the commission’s published final list of candidates.
“The distinction is straightforward: The Court ruled on the relevant provisions of the Electoral Act; it did not issue a candidate-specific ruling against Omo-Agege,” he said.
Omo-Agege said turning the judgment into an announcement that he was out of the race amounted to political propaganda rather than an accurate representation of the court’s decision.
He said he remained focused on the 2027 contest in Delta Central, urging his political opponents to campaign on their records and programmes.
“If Dafinone wants the Senate seat, he should come to the field with his record, his programme and his arguments for another term,” he said.
Omo-Agege said the people of Delta Central would make their choice at the appropriate time, adding that political celebrations could not replace the electoral contest.
(NAN)

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Ireland’s football team voted on Saturday to fulfil a Nations League tie with Israel despite goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu pulling out of the match due to unease over the war in Gaza.
“We carried out a vote amongst the squad to establish their sentiment on fulfilling the fixtures,” Football Association of Ireland (FAI) head David Courell told reporters in Debrecen, Hungary, where the game will take place on Sunday.
“It was a significant majority that was returned with the intention to continue.
“Based on that, the association took the decision on behalf of Irish football, that this fixture would continue as we have always intended to fulfil the fixtures,” he added.
Ireland are scheduled to play two Nations League ties against Israel, with the first — officially Israel’s home fixture – at the neutral venue in Hungary.
Ireland’s designated home match on October 4 has been moved from Dublin’s Aviva Stadium to Backa Topola, Serbia, following concerns over disruption and security.
“I have reached a decision that I have not taken lightly,” Bolton’s Bazunu said on Instagram.
“I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel. My decision is based purely upon my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong,” the 24-year-old added.
Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause, with sympathy often linked to the country’s own history of British rule.
Dublin, alongside Spain and Norway, formally recognised a Palestinian state in 2024, and has repeatedly criticised Israel over the Gaza conflict.
Israel strongly rejects allegations its conduct in Gaza amounts to genocide.
“Football has won, the separation between football and politics must be maintained,” said a statement by the Israeli FA later Saturday hailing the Irish decision.
“The ones who have certainly lost today are those who wanted to intimidate, to separate and to turn the football pitch into a political arena,” it added.
Since Ireland were drawn in the same Nations League group as Israel, prominent Irish figures including sportspeople, fan groups and pro-Palestinian campaigners have protested against the ties going ahead.
Bazunu’s decision triggered the delay of a scheduled press conference on Saturday, followed by a vote among the squad on whether to fulfil the fixture or not.
“Nobody is comfortable playing these games for many reasons,” said Ireland’s Icelandic manager Heimir Hallgrimsson.
“We are trying to tackle it in the best way we can at the moment,” he added.
Ireland players will not fulfil any media duties tomorrow, or against Austria in Dublin on October 1, or around the game against Israel in Serbia three days later, said Courell.
The players will wear black armbands “for all lives lost in the conflict” during Sunday’s match, with profits from the Austria game to be donated to charity, he said.
Sunday’s match comes days after national broadcaster RTE confirmed Ireland would again boycott the Eurovision Song Contest next year because of Israel’s participation.
In a rare move for a state broadcaster, RTE said earlier it will show the Israel game without Irish commentary or pundits.

items.content:
National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has dismissed the threat posed by opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Briefing journalists at the conclusion of a three-day retreat in Maiduguri, Borno State capital, on Saturday, he said parties like the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) would merely be participating in the polls rather than mounting a serious contest against the ruling party.
The event brought together members of the National Working Committee (NWC), elected National Executive Committee (NEC) members, and state chairmen of the ruling party.
According to the APC chairman, the party’s electoral prospects remain formidable, citing recent outcomes from five by-elections held across the country.
Inmates die as cholera hits Kano prison
Hardship: Apologise, then leave the stage, Atiku tells Tinubu
He said the ruling party secured victory in four of the contests, losing only one to the APM—not to the major opposition parties “often touted” in the media.
“We went to Ekiti and came first; the party that came second was the PDP, not the so-called opposition (ADC and NDC). We went to Osun and we became second, none of those political parties you claimed won even a councillorship.
“So if they can’t even win a councillorship, are we contesting against them? As far as I am concerned, they are participants in this election, not contesting with us. We are very confident that our party can win this election; we are prepared to win the 2027 election.”
Highlighting further electoral data, Yilwatda referenced off-cycle polls in Osun and legislative contests in the North, including Kano, Bauchi, and Gombe, where the APC recorded strong showings.
He argued that media narratives regarding opposition momentum do not align with realities on the ground.
“Even last week, we had a by-election in Adamawa, in Ganye local government, where Atiku comes from, and we won the election. We are very grounded, and I doubt if any party can challenge us,” he said.
Retreat Resolutions and Votes of Confidence
Detailing the resolutions reached during the three-day retreat, Yilwatda announced that the party leadership observed a moment of mourning, extending condolences to the government and people of Niger State over the tragic loss of 37 miners.
He also noted that the NWC conducted a comprehensive review of the party’s structures from the national level down to the polling units, giving the APC a “clean bill of health” as a strong, healthy, and well-oiled machine heading into 2027.
Crucially, the gathering passed a vote of confidence in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima, and all party candidates emerging from primary elections.
“We strongly believe that we produce some of the most credible candidates, most acceptable, and most prepared to serve the people of Nigeria,” Yilwatda remarked.
The party also resolved to intensify grassroots reconciliation efforts, urging state chapters to establish committees to consolidate unity and preserve past electoral gains. The NWC pledged to lead campaigns from the front, highlighting the administration’s achievements.
Pointing to recent electoral breakthroughs in areas traditionally considered opposition strongholds—such as winning senatorial seats in states where the party previously struggled—Yilwatda expressed optimism about the APC’s widening national appeal.
Concluding the briefing, the APC Chairman expressed gratitude to Nigerians for their support over the past three years and called on citizens and party faithful to turn out en masse to re-elect President Tinubu and other APC candidates in 2027.

By Edwin Phillip, Lafia
The People Democratic Party, PDP, has urged it supporters to vote and stay behind to protect their votes during the 2027 general elections, stating that they shoud not give in to intimidation and the antics of people who are in to scuttle their chances.
The PDP national deputy chairman north, Mr Yusuf Nya Agirikwe, said this during the party’s Nasarawa State gubernatorial candidate’s campaign flag off ceremony, which took place at party secretariat in Lafia the Nasarawa State capital on Saturday.
He said: “I have come to establish it myself today, that PDP has the mandate of the people to rule them in this state.
“We can only actualize this if you will be able to vote and defend your votes, are you going to do it?
​”Are we going to do it?”
He commended the members and leaders of the party in the state for coming in their numbers to support the party, adding that they should ensure that their numbers translate to victory for their governorship candidate in Nasarawa, Dr. David Emmanuel Ombugadu.
“But what I have seen with my eyes, and many of my colleagues who are here, we will go and testify that the Nasarawa people are truly behind him. And whatever he is doing, he has your endorsement, he has your support.
“The only thing I am going to tell you is that from today, go and tell your friends, go and tell your friends that PDP is the winning party. Go out and bring your votes,” he added.
He, however, apologised on the absence of the national chairman of the party and it national leader, Nyesom Wike.
Speaking during the event, the governorship candidate of the party in theState, David Ombugadu said that he is dedicating the opportunity given to him to to be party flag bearer to the women, youths and leaders of Nasarawa State. 
​”I want to sincerely thank God for your commitment and your sacrifice; everything you have done. You stood firm.
“We must protect our votes so that we can have a government that will represent the people.
“We can have a government that will enable our farmers to go to farms. So that we can have a government that will allow us to take advantage of the mineral resources that we have,” he said.
According to him, Nasarawa citizens should not be complaining of poverty; having been blessed with abundant agricultural resources and huge mineral deposits.
He promised that if given the mandate, he will ensure that the healthcare needs of poor and vulnerable would be his priority,
“But through my leadership, we will make sure that all pregnant women will go to the hospital and there will be drugs. All farm owners, you will go to farms and you will sleep in your farms.
​”I want to assure you that under my watch, everybody in Nasarawa State will matter.”
He added that his team has unveiled a 5-year manifesto for Nasarawa State, where issues of security as well as women capital developmentwill take a centre stage.
He appreciated the national leadership of the party for their support and pledged his total support, adding that he worked in tandem with the dictate of the party’s leadership.
“Thank you, our national leader. We want to affirm today, and now, that we — the entire Nasarawa State – stands for Rainbow Coalition.
“We are all united in support of our national leader. We are waiting for our national leader to give us direction. Wherever he goes, we will go.”

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
By Udeme Akpan & Mariam Eko
Oil marketers have begun cutting the pump price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), also known as petrol, with MRS reducing its price in Lagos and environs by N20 per litre to N1,350 from N1,370.
Checks by Vanguard showed that some independent oil marketers also reduced their retail prices to N1,360 from more than N1,380 per litre.
The reduction comes as depot prices continue to soften, with PMS falling to as low as N1,303 per litre in Port Harcourt, according to the latest Daily Depot Price Intelligence Report for Friday, September 25, 2026.
The downward movement in the domestic market also coincided with a sharp decline in international crude oil prices.
Brent crude fell by $2.28, or 2.14 per cent, to $104.30 per barrel from $106.58, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) declined by $1.79, or 1.89 per cent, to $92.82 from $94.61 per barrel.
The decline extended to refined products, with gasoline falling 4.31 per cent to $3.411, while natural gas dropped 3.46 per cent to $3.183.
The latest depot data showed that Bulk Strategic, Masters, Sigmund and T.S.L depots in Port Harcourt were selling PMS at N1,303 per litre, the lowest price recorded across the markets monitored.
In Lagos, A.A Rano, AIPEC, Bovas, Dangote, Emadeb, Sahara and Wosbab depots were listed at N1,325 per litre.
Petrol prices averaged N1,326 per litre in Lagos, N1,318 in Calabar, N1,315 in Warri and N1,303 in Port Harcourt.
At N1,350 per litre, MRS’s new Lagos pump price is N25 above the N1,325 per litre depot price recorded by the monitored Lagos suppliers.
The gap between MRS’s Lagos retail price and the lowest depot price in Port Harcourt is N47 per litre.
However, the depot report also showed wide regional variations in Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel.
Diesel prices ranged from N1,790 per litre in Lagos to N1,900 per litre in Port Harcourt.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
By Luminous Jannamike
ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain why Nigeria’s public debt has risen to ₦166.79 trillion despite increased government revenues, saying Nigerians are yet to see the promised gains from the administration’s economic reforms.
Read Also:
After more than three years of higher food, transport, fuel, electricity and other living costs, Atiku said Nigerians were entitled to know why government revenues had risen while borrowing continued.
In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said Nigeria’s public debt rose from ₦49.85 trillion in March 2023 to ₦166.79 trillion by June 2026.
“A government that says more money is coming in must explain why it keeps borrowing and why the people paying for its policies cannot see the promised gains,” Atiku said.
He urged Tinubu to provide a full reconciliation of the debt, including old obligations newly captured, exchange-rate effects on foreign debt, fresh loans contracted since 2023, repayments and outstanding balances.
“I expect President Tinubu to put the full account before Nigerians,” he said.
Atiku also questioned the gap between official economic indicators and the rising cost of living, arguing that improved government revenues and other macroeconomic indicators had yet to translate into affordable living conditions for many Nigerians.
“The true test of economic policy is whether Nigerians can afford food, transportation, housing, education, healthcare and electricity,” he said.
IMF assessment
The criticism comes against the backdrop of a June 2026 IMF assessment which, while acknowledging improved macroeconomic outcomes from Nigeria’s reforms, said conditions remained difficult for many Nigerians.
The Fund estimated poverty at 63 per cent and said 27 million Nigerians had faced food insecurity in late 2025.
Atiku further cited BudgIT figures showing ₦12.52 trillion spent on debt service against ₦18.63 trillion in revenue by the third quarter of 2025, while the 2026 fiscal framework projects a deficit of about ₦31.45 trillion.
“If President Tinubu understands abroad what debt payments are taking away from Nigeria, then he must explain at home why the borrowing bill continues to grow,” Atiku said.
He also demanded explanations for $39.25 million listed as ‘other charges’ in the DMO’s second-quarter 2026 external debt-service schedule, including a $22.5 million charge linked to a First Abu Dhabi Bank Total Return Swap.
“What exactly was the $22.5 million charge for? Which agreement authorised it? What was the original facility? How much was drawn? What obligations remain outstanding?” he asked.
Atiku called for a reconciliation of the ₦19.48 trillion Treasury Bills outstanding as at June 30, saying Nigerians needed to know what was redeemed, rolled over and genuinely borrowed.
He also demanded an apology from Tinubu and the APC over the hardship caused by the reforms.
“Nigerians were asked to sacrifice. Fuel subsidy was removed. The naira was allowed to depreciate sharply. Electricity and transportation costs rose. Government revenues increased, yet borrowing continued. After all of this, the Nigerian people are entitled to ask one simple question: what exactly did our sacrifice buy?” Atiku said.
“The real test of this economy is not whether the numbers look good in government presentations. It is whether ordinary Nigerians can afford to live,” he added.
Vanguard News

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
By Chinedu Adonu
The Chairman of the National Democratic Congress, NDC, in Enugu State, Dr John Paul Ani, has commended the peaceful conduct of the ongoing local government election in his area, while alleging irregularities and denial of access to party officials in some other council areas.
Ani, who spoke with journalists after casting his ballot in Ward 2, Unit 001, Town Hall, Nkanu West Local Government Area, said the exercise was peaceful, transparent and credible in his polling area.
He commended the Enugu State Independent Electoral Commission, ENSIEC, for conducting what he described as a largely hitch-free exercise.
“My assessment of the process is that the process was peaceful, transparent and credible, the way I voted. I want to commend the commission, ENSIEC, for conducting such a hitch-free exercise,” Ani said.
However, he said the party had received reports from its chairmen and other officials in some local government areas alleging conduct by some ENSIEC officials that, according to him, was inconsistent with democratic principles.
He specifically mentioned Nri, Oji River and Ezeagu Local Government Areas, alleging that some NDC chairmen and party officials were denied access to local government council headquarters where election materials were being distributed.
“By law, every political party must be at the headquarters where materials will be distributed to various wards and polling units.
“But in these local governments that I have mentioned, the reports we are getting from there was that our people were not allowed access,” he said.
Ani called on ENSIEC to investigate the allegations and take appropriate action if the claims were established.
“We are calling on ENSIEC to do more to investigate this situation and then bring the perpetrators of this act to book,” he said.
He urged the commission to demonstrate its independence and impartiality in the conduct of the election.
“ENSIEC, as a commission, should prove itself, once again, as the people’s commission and not an arm of the ruling APC,” Ani said.
On the expected outcome of the election, the NDC chairman expressed confidence that his party would perform strongly, citing its campaign and the quality of candidates it fielded.
“For us in NDC, we are confident that we will win this election at the end of the day because we have done a campaign. We have fielded credible candidates; we fielded people that understand what the masses want,” he said.
Ani said the NDC had deployed agents to polling units where it fielded candidates and that the party was monitoring the collation process at ward and local government levels.
He, however, said the party would await the official declaration of results by ENSIEC.
“We have voted, we have monitored the exercise, and we have moved to coalition centres, ward coalition centres.
“So, after this exercise, we will go to the local government where the result will be officially announced by the commission. And then when we get to the bridge, we will cross it,” he said.
Ani acknowledged that ENSIEC was leading in some areas, adding that no party could expect to win every constituency.
“As it is right now, ENSIEC is leading in some areas. Of course, we can’t win all. But we know where we have fielded candidates that we are confident that we will win at the end of the day,” he said.
He further alleged that election materials had not reached some polling areas as of the time of his briefing, particularly in Oji River, Aninri and Ezeagu.
“From the reports we got, there are some places that materials did not even reach, even at this point, especially in Oji River, Aninri and Ezeagu.
“But in Nkanu West, where I am and where I voted, materials got into every polling unit in the local government,” Ani said.
Vanguard News

items.content:
Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, has commended President Bola Tinubu for resisting pressure to reach a conclusion before the investigation into the purported Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC) was completed.
Gbajabiamila appeared before the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) in July 2026 as part of the probe. The commission subsequently reported that it found no evidence connecting him or his office to the purported organisation or the appointment of its alleged director-general.
He said on Saturday at the 2026 Gbaja Mega Empowerment programme in Lagos that the Nigerian Police, Department of State Services (DSS) and ICPC cleared him of the allegations linked to his office.
The former Speaker of the House of Representatives said the experience had tested him personally, while expressing gratitude to those who stood by him.
“The past few months have tested me in ways I never expected. Stories were written, strange accusations were made, lies were told, and my integrity was questioned,” he said.
“At the end of all the investigations, the Nigerian Police, the DSS, the ICPC cleared me of any wrongdoing, and the investigative reports are in the public domain,” he added.
Commending Tinubu, he said, “I must thank my principal, President Bola Tinubu. Many people wanted him to rush to judgment and give a verdict before the investigation. He refused and insisted on due process.”
Gbajabiamila urged young Nigerians aspiring to public office not to be discouraged by the challenges that could accompany political leadership.
“For those who seek high office, especially our young ones, sometimes this is the high price you have to pay and sacrifice you have to make. Do not be discouraged,” he said.
Gbajabiamila insisted that the allegations would not distract him from his official responsibilities.
“No amount of money, no amount of blackmail or lies, whether sponsored from within or outside, will detract me from my work and the work Mr. President has given me to do,” he said.
Gbajabiamila also warned individuals allegedly using his name to deceive members of the public, saying they would face legal consequences.
“And to anyone using my name to defraud people or misrepresent me, know that the law will always catch up with you,” he said.
His remarks came as he presided over an empowerment initiative valued at approximately ₦1.15bn, targeting about 5,000 beneficiaries in Surulere.
The programme featured cash grants, vehicles, business equipment and other forms of assistance intended to support small businesses, improve livelihoods and create economic opportunities for residents.
Gbajabiamila said the event, originally scheduled for June, was postponed to allow organisers to verify submissions from wards, trade associations and community-based groups.
According to the former lawmaker, 3,905 beneficiaries received ₦250,000 each, while another 348 people were given ₦500,000 apiece.
The distribution also covered 61 electric vehicles, 50 electric tricycles, 60 minibuses and 100 laptops.
Other items provided included four Toyota HiAce 18-seater buses, two security patrol vehicles, a medical ambulance and two additional vehicles.
He said the inclusion of electric cars, tricycles and bikes was part of efforts to promote cleaner transportation and expand business opportunities through e-hailing services.
Gbajabiamila said the expansion of electric and compressed natural gas-powered vehicles could help lower transport costs, improve air quality and generate employment.
Speaking at the event, Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat said the All Progressives Congress (APC) remained committed to connecting with Nigerians and addressing their needs at the grassroots.
Hamzat attributed the party’s growing strength to the efforts of its elected representatives to maintain close relationships with residents and their communities.
He said sustained engagement with citizens was central to the APC’s identity and extended beyond election campaigns.
“That is why our party is the party of the people,” he said.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan's real estate investment trust (REIT) sector is gaining traction, with 18 funds established and projects worth more than Rs2 trillion under development, according to Arif Habib Dolmen REIT Management Company CEO Muhammad Ijaz.
Speaking on a Tribune podcast, Ijaz said REITs could help formalise Pakistan's largely informal real estate sector while allowing investors with relatively modest capital to participate in property-related businesses.
He said the REIT framework addressed two major challenges associated with real estate investment – the need for substantial capital and the illiquidity of property assets.
Under the model, real estate assets are divided into units that can be purchased by investors, making participation possible for both small and large investors.
Ijaz said Dolmen City REIT, Pakistan's first REIT, had an asset value of around Rs22 billion when it was launched, with 2.2 billion units issued at Rs10 each. "Those who want to invest Rs5,000 can do so, and those who want to invest Rs5 billion can also do so," he said.
Explaining the regulatory framework, he said the title of REIT assets remained with the trustee, while investors held REIT units that effectively represented their ownership interest. Trustees are licensed entities, including the Central Depository Company (CDC) and Digital Custodian Company, while REIT management companies are responsible for managing the underlying business.
Ijaz said five REITs were currently listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange, with additional listings expected soon. Rental REITs are required to be listed within their first year, while developmental and hybrid REITs are required to be listed within three years, he said.
He distinguished between rental and developmental REITs, saying rental REITs generally acquire built-up properties and generate income by leasing them, while developmental REITs develop land or projects for sale or lease.
According to Ijaz, REITs are required to distribute 90% of distributable income to unit holders. He said Dolmen City REIT had initially offered a yield of around 10%, while its yield for investors who bought units at around Rs11 had subsequently risen substantially as the unit price increased.
He also highlighted the emergence of property-share schemes aimed at people who could not afford to purchase an entire apartment.
Under the model, investors can purchase a fractional share of a property. For example, a 1,800-square-foot apartment valued at Rs30 million could be divided into 100-square-foot shares worth Rs1.8 million each.
Ijaz said investors could accumulate additional shares over time and potentially sell them later. The model is being developed initially in Naya Nazimabad, with the ownership and rental arrangements managed through institutional and contractual structures.
He said the REIT sector was no longer confined to Karachi. Of the 18 REIT funds, 10 were in Karachi while eight were in Lahore and Islamabad. Projects include developments associated with Naya Nazimabad, Surjani Town, Lahore's Central Business District, Ravi Urban Development Authority and Rifah Medical City.
Ijaz said a 150-acre project in Surjani Town had been divided into two REIT funds, focusing on horizontal and vertical development, with emphasis on environmentally friendly urban development.
He argued that construction and real estate development could play a significant role in Pakistan's economic growth because the sector relied heavily on local labour and locally available raw materials.
However, he cautioned against speculative trading in property files, saying the sector needed greater professionalism, institutional participation and regulatory clarity.
Ijaz also called for greater availability of mortgage finance and institutional funding for professionally managed housing projects. He said "build-to-rent" could emerge as an important business model, allowing people to access professionally managed rental housing rather than bearing the financial and administrative burden of constructing their own homes.
He said Pakistan's real estate sector had significant potential if supported by better taxation policies, institutional investment and professional project management.
"Construction and real estate development should be kept in priority," Ijaz said, stressing that the sector could generate employment and stimulate economic activity across multiple industries.

Tuesday saw further consolidation amid falling oil prices. The index gained 250 points (+0.15%) at 171,402. The market further extended its advance on Wednesday, when it closed higher by 830 points (+0.48%) at 172,233.
However, geopolitical uncertainty dampened PSX sentiment on the second last day of the trading week, Thursday. The index declined 1,734 points (-1.01%) to close at 170,499. Friday was a range-bound day with the KSE-100 gaining 266 points (+0.16%) and settled at 170,765.
"Overall, geopolitical developments kept the market flat," observed Arif Habib Limited (AHL) in its commentary. The KSE-100 closed at 170,765 points, down 0.1% from 170,885 points in the previous week, as hopes of progress in US-Iran talks and softer oil prices supported the market early in the week before geopolitical concerns resurfaced and crude prices rose.
Power generation rose 5.1% year-on-year to 14,943 gigawatt hours (GWh) in Aug'26, the third-highest August generation on record, supported by higher hydel, coal, gas and wind output. Generation cost increased 38% YoY to Rs10.01/kWh due to higher RLNG and furnace oil mix and elevated oil prices, prompting power distribution companies to seek a positive fuel cost adjustment of Rs1.73/kWh, mentioned AHL.
Oil production improved 1.4% WoW to 68.5k barrels per day, mainly due to higher flows from Makori East, Maramzai and Mardankhel, while gas production decreased 2.5% WoW to 2,934 million cubic feet per day, driven by lower production from Mari, Uch, Kandhkot and Shewa.
Pakistan's oil and gas reserves reached 3,720 million barrels of oil equivalent in Jun'26, with oil reserves up 15% YoY to 276 million barrels and gas reserves up 9% to 20,664 billion cubic feet. Newly discovered fields added 53.5 million barrels of oil and 773 billion cubic feet of gas, while the country's estimated reserve life stood at around 19 years.
Pakistan's total liquid foreign exchange reserves rose 0.07% WoW to $26.8 billion, while the State Bank reserves increased 0.05% to $21.4 billion and banks' reserves grew 0.15% to $5.41 billion. Import cover remained unchanged at 3.03 months.
Attock Refinery, Pakistan Refinery, National Refinery and Cnergyico signed upgrade agreements with Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS) under the Pakistan Oil Refining Policy for Upgradation of Existing/Brownfield Refineries 2023, as amended in Feb'24 and Aug'26.
Petroleum prices were mixed in the latest revision under the daily pricing mechanism, with high-speed diesel falling to Rs412.12/litre during the week, while motor spirit reached Rs389.28/litre, added AHL.
Local and geopolitical uncertainty drove caution, noted Wadee Zaman of JS Global, stating that the KSE-100 remained broadly flat during the week, closing at 170,765 (-119 points), as geopolitical uncertainty and domestic political developments continued to weigh on investor sentiment.
Brent crude averaged $103.1/barrel, down 2.2% WoW, while domestic MS and HSD prices declined by Rs1.51/litre and Rs12.80/litre to Rs389.28/ltr and Rs412.12/ltr, respectively, following five consecutive weekly increases. On the external front, Pakistan and the IMF commenced talks for the fourth review of the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility, potentially paving the way for the release of the fifth tranche of $1 billion, mentioned Zaman.
Meanwhile, the ADB revised down Pakistan's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 3.7% from 4.5% previously. Pakistan secured $4.7 billion in foreign loans during 2MFY27, while profit and dividend repatriation declined 13.4% YoY to $557 million.
In a key development, four of Pakistan's five local refineries signed formal upgrade agreements with the government, paving the way for an estimated $6 billion investment over the next five years. In the latest Pakistan Investment Bond auction, the government raised Rs181 billion, with yields increasing by 20-75 basis points across different tenors. The State Bank's foreign exchange reserves remained stable at $21.4 billion, he said.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
India has ordered more than 100 captive coal-fired power plants to operate at maximum capacity from October 1 through year-end to meet what it expects will be a rise in electricity demand.
The federal power ministry's order, invoked under emergency provisions of the Electricity Act, applies to plants with installed capacity of at least 50 megawatts. The aim is to meet an "expected rise in electricity demand in the coming months," showed the order dated September 25 and seen by Reuters. Nearly 40% of coal-fired plants are operating with critically low fuel stock due to a surge in power demand as the El Nino climate phenomenon raises temperatures more than usual.
The plants primarily serve industrial facilities such as aluminium smelters, steel manufacturers, cement factories and oil refineries. The power ministry has directed generators to sell surplus electricity through power exchanges.
The order covers 112 plants belonging to companies including Vedanta, Tata Steel, Hindalco Industries, JSW Steel, UltraTech Cement, Reliance Industries, Indian Oil, Bharat Aluminium, Hindustan Zinc and Nayara Energy.
The ministry has ordered plants to report weekly to the Central Electricity Authority detailing generation, captive consumption, power sales, available capacity and coal stocks.
Separately, the ministry has extended an earlier emergency order requiring Tata Power's imported coal-fired plant in Mundra, Gujarat to operate at full capacity until December 31, citing the demand situation.
Section 11 of the Electricity Act allows the government, under extraordinary circumstances, to direct generators to operate power stations in accordance with its instructions.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Defenders Ime Okon and Samukele Kabini scored their first goals for South Africa in a tense 2-1 win over Guinea on Saturday in 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.
Centre-back Okon, who plays for German second-tier club Hannover, hammered a loose ball into the net from close range to give the hosts a 30th-minute lead in Soweto.
Norway-based full-back Kabini, a second-half substitute for Aubrey Modiba, claimed the 77th-minute match-winner, racing through to beat goalkeeper Soumaila Sylla at his near post.
Guinea had equalised after 69 minutes when a free kick was not cleared and Seydouba Cisse reacted quickest to fire past captain Ronwen Williams.
The match marked the start of a second permanent spell in charge of South Africa for Pitso Mosimane, a three-time CAF Champions League-winning coach with Mamelodi Sundowns and Al Ahly.
He has inherited from retired Belgian tactician Hugo Broos a team good at retaining possession, but lacking clinical finishing.
Much of the pre-match focus was on Guinea striker Serhou Guirassy, a prolific scorer for Borussia Dortmund, but winger Aliou Balde posed a greater threat with his pace and footwork.
South Africa were the fifth of 10 African participants at the 2026 World Cup after Algeria, Democratic Republic of Congo, Ivory Coast and Morocco to begin AFCON qualifying with a win.
Egypt, Senegal and Tunisia drew and Cape Verde and Ghana lost.
Victory lifted South Africa to the top of Group D, ahead of Eritrea and Kenya, who drew 1-1 in Nairobi.
Nahom Girmai scored for the visitors in the first half and Ryan Ogam levelled on 87 minutes for Kenya, who will co-host the 2027 AFCON with Tanzania and Uganda.
Automatic qualifiers Kenya are in Group D to gain competitive match practice. Their presence leaves the other three teams competing for one place at the finals.
AFP

items.summary:

Speaking to the media, Dr. Kashif said the facility has begun performing angiography procedures, while stents are also being implanted in heart patients.
He added that procedures involving angiography and the insertion of assist devices have also commenced at the Cath Lab.
According to Dr. Kashif, patients are receiving treatment for cardiac diseases without any charges at DHQ Hospital Bahawalnagar.
Medical Superintendent DHQ Hospital Dr. Amir Raza said the facility is a gift from Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz for the people of Bahawalnagar.
He noted that heart patients from the district previously had to travel to Lahore, Bahawalpur, and Multan for treatment. With the new Cath Lab now operational, they can access these cardiac services locally and free of cost.

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Maryam Nawaz Sharif has directed authorities to install a new CT scan machine in every district of the province as part of measures to improve public healthcare services.
The directive was issued during a video-link meeting chaired by the chief minister, where the progress of healthcare initiatives, hospital staffing, digital monitoring, and medical facilities across Punjab was reviewed.
CM Maryam Nawaz also ordered the establishment of telemedicine centers for seasonal and common diseases. Patients will be able to consult doctors through video calls and, where necessary, be referred to the relevant hospital or ward.
The centers will also facilitate appointments with concerned hospital wards, laboratories, and other healthcare facilities.
During the meeting, it was also decided to upgrade 300 Maryam Nawaz Hospitals, formerly Rural Health Centers, into fully fledged hospitals.
The chief minister directed the recruitment of 40,000 doctors and allied health professionals across Punjab. Officials informed the meeting that 2,524 doctors, 2,482 women medical officers, 408 consultants, and 32 cardiologists had already been recruited, while 7,572 lady health visitors and 5,048 support staff had been posted at hospitals across the province.
The meeting also approved the introduction of digital medical boxes for Clinics on Wheels for the first time in Punjab. The system will allow ultrasound, blood sugar, complete blood count (CBC), and ECG tests to be carried out through a single setup.
The boxes will also support cameras for teleconferencing, while mobile-linked smart ultrasound devices will be introduced as part of the initiative.
Officials said 911 Clinics on Wheels had provided medical care to 30 million patients within a short period.
CM Maryam Nawaz also announced a monthly “Hospital of the Month” award for hospitals demonstrating outstanding performance across the province.
She ordered the immediate replacement of medical superintendents at four hospitals over poor performance and negligence of duties and directed authorities to create a pool of doctors and medical superintendents for emergency situations.
The chief minister also called for improved cleanliness and parking facilities at district and tehsil headquarters hospitals.
Clinic Quality Control Officers will be appointed for the first time in Punjab to assess the quality of treatment provided to patients.
Meanwhile, a Directorate of Monitoring and Surveillance has been established in Primary Healthcare to ensure round-the-clock digital monitoring of hospitals. The system will cover district and tehsil headquarters hospitals, Maryam Nawaz Hospitals, Maryam Nawaz Health Clinics, Field Hospitals, and Clinics on Wheels.
The meeting was informed that Community Health Monitoring Health Inspectors had completed registration and data collection for more than 119.8 million people across Punjab.
Officials also said medicines had been delivered to the homes of 3,444 Type 1 diabetes patients, 14,286 hepatitis patients, and 13,864 tuberculosis patients.
The meeting further agreed to introduce legislation linking private clinics with the Health Information Management System (HIMS).
Provincial Secretary for Primary and Secondary Healthcare and Population Nadia Saqib briefed the meeting on the progress of the healthcare initiatives.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
New-age tech stocks saw a bearish week, with a sharp sell-off in PB Fintech and Turtlemint following IRDAI’s proposed commission caps overshadowing gains in Capillary Technologies and Zelio E-Mobility.
Turtlemint plunged 34.97%, while Policybazaar parent PB Fintech lost 33.02% during the week. The declines came as investors assessed the potential impact of lower insurance commissions on the companies’ revenue and profitability.
SaaS company Capillary Technologies led the gainers, rising 24.59% to ₹603.15. Zelio E-Mobility followed with a 23.96% jump to ₹1,056.90.
Zelio, ESDS, Shadowfax, Nazara, and BlueStone touched fresh 52-week highs during the week. Meanwhile, Shiprocket, IndiaMART, Menhood, Turtlemint, and PB Fintech hit fresh lows. Lenskart, Paytm, and Swiggy also ended the week in the red.
Overall, of the 65 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 28 gained between 0.26% and 24.59% this week, while 37 fell between 0.01% and 34.97%. The combined market capitalisation of the 65 companies declined by $3.6 Bn, or about 2.1%, to $166.6 Bn from $170.2 Bn the previous week.
The weakness coincided with a seventh consecutive weekly decline in the benchmark indices. However, activity in the primary market continued, with Moneyview and AceVector opening their IPOs for subscription and Spinny confidentially filing its IPO papers.
Now, let’s take a look at some of the key developments at new-age tech companies this week:
Moneyview, AceVector Open IPOs: Moneyview’s ₹1,092 Cr IPO was subscribed 6.01X at the end of its second day of bidding yesterday. Snapdeal parent AceVector’s ₹420 Cr IPO closed its first day with 23% subscription. Meanwhile, used-car marketplace Spinny confidentially filed its IPO papers with SEBI, targeting an issue of ₹2,500–₹3,000 Cr.
Investors Pare Stakes Across Listed Tech Companies: TPG exited FirstCry through a ₹202 Cr bulk deal, while Mastercard sold its Pine Labs holding for ₹934 Cr. A91 Partners and Xponentia reduced their holdings in SEDEMAC, Accel and 360 ONE sold BlueStone shares worth ₹513 Cr, and ADIA offloaded 3.5 Cr Lenskart shares for ₹2,390.6 Cr.
ESDS Reports Mixed Q1 Performance: The cloud and AI company’s net profit rose 14% YoY to ₹29.3 Cr in Q1 FY27 but declined 57% QoQ. Operating revenue increased 7.3% YoY to ₹133.7 Cr, although it fell 20% sequentially.
Aequs Approves ₹650 Cr Fundraise: The contract manufacturer’s board approved a preferential issue of warrants worth up to ₹650 Cr to promoter group entity Mellwood Trustee Services. The proceeds will support capacity expansion across its aerospace and consumer businesses.
Nykaa, L’Oréal To Back Beauty Brands: Nykaa partnered with BOLD, L’Oréal’s corporate VC fund, to acquire minority stakes in emerging Indian beauty and wellness brands. The brands’ founders will retain operational control of their businesses
ED Chargesheets EaseMyTrip’s Nishant Pitti: The ED chargesheeted EaseMyTrip cofounder and chairman Nishant Pitti in the Mahadev betting app money laundering case, alleging that he facilitated the entry of illegal betting proceeds into Indian equities through FPIs. The agency has provisionally attached shares belonging to Pitti worth ₹59.6 Cr. Responding to Inc42, Pitti said he was unaware of any chargesheet, had not been summoned by the court, and maintained that his transactions complied with applicable laws.
Purple Style Labs Narrows Q1 Loss: Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop parent Purple Style Labs trimmed its net loss by 12% to ₹88.1 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹100.3 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Operating revenue increased 13% to ₹119.4 Cr from ₹105.7 Cr.
Lenskart Raises Le Petit Lunetier Stake: Lenskart’s Singapore subsidiary NESO Brands invested €0.248 Mn (₹2.71 Cr) for an additional 2.52% stake in French eyewear brand Le Petit Lunetier. The transaction increased NESO’s holding to 34.34% from 31.82%.
Ola Electric Eyes Rights Issue: Ola Electric’s board will consider a rights issue on September 28 (Monday). The fundraising proposal comes as the company invests in EVs, battery cells, and energy storage, while its Q1 FY27 revenue declined 45% YoY to ₹455 Cr.
Veefin Gets In-Principle Mainboard Nod: Fintech SaaS company Veefin Solutions received BSE’s in-principle approval to migrate from its SME platform to the mainboard. The approval carries a 45-day validity window for completing the prescribed formalities, including submitting a listing application and an updated information memorandum.
Markets Extend Losing Streak To Seven Weeks
The Sensex and Nifty declined 0.54% and 0.88%, respectively, during the week to close at 73,895.74 and 23,140.50, extending their losing streak to seven weeks.
Higher crude oil prices, renewed Middle East tensions, and rising US bond yields weighed on sentiment. For India, elevated crude prices raised concerns over the import bill, inflation, and the rupee.
Foreign investor selling added to the pressure. Provisional exchange data showed net foreign equity selling of ₹11,490 Cr during September 21-25.
In the coming week, investors will track developments involving the US and Iran, Brent crude prices, US bond yields, and the rupee, alongside domestic economic releases.
“On the domestic front, industrial production data for August, government budget data, the external debt position and the HSBC Manufacturing PMI reading will be released during the week,” said Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research at Religare Broking.
Now, let’s take a detailed look at the performance of PB Fintech, Turtlemint, and Zelio this week.
PB Fintech, Turtlemint Reel Under Proposed Commission Caps
PB Fintech and Turtlemint bore the brunt of the week’s selling after IRDAI proposed product- and channel-specific commission caps and tighter expenses of management (EoM) limits.
PB Fintech fell 33.02% during the week to ₹1,165.50 on the BSE, taking its market capitalisation to ₹53,933.83 Cr ($5.6 Bn). Turtlemint declined 34.97% to ₹87.30.
The proposals would reintroduce product-level commission ceilings more than three years after IRDAI removed such limits in April 2023 and gave insurers greater flexibility within an overall EoM framework.
Under the consultation paper, insurance distribution entities would receive no commission on third-party insurance for new vehicles, while commissions on new-vehicle own-damage, personal accident, and legal liability covers would be capped at 5%.
For individual health insurance, commissions for these entities would be capped at 15% on new policies and 5% on renewals and portability.
IRDAI has also proposed reducing life insurers’ EoM limits to 15% of premiums within two years and 12.5% within five years. General insurers would face limits of 25% and 20%, respectively.
For digital insurance distributors, lower payouts would reduce revenue earned from policy sales and renewals, putting pressure on margins unless they can offset the impact through higher volumes, lower acquisition costs, or other income streams.
Jefferies estimated that a 10% reduction in new business commission rates could lower PB Fintech’s earnings by 10%-12%. It retained its ‘Buy’ rating but cut its price target to ₹1,540 from ₹2,050.
The proposals have also prompted PB Fintech to consider a broader change in strategy. Cofounder and group chairman Yashish Dahiya said on an investor call on Thursday (September 24) that the company was considering entering insurance manufacturing, which would allow it to design and underwrite policies, although it would await greater regulatory clarity.
The selling extended to insurers, with HDFC Life declining 6.13% and ICICI Prudential Life falling 4.23% during the week.
The proposals remain under consultation, with stakeholder comments invited until October 25. The final commission ceilings and implementation timelines will determine the extent of the impact on distributors and insurers.
Zelio Rallies 24% Amid ₹168 Cr Fundraising Plan
Zelio E-Mobility gained 23.96% during the week to close at ₹1,056.90 on the BSE SME platform, with the rally coinciding with its proposed ₹167.95 Cr fundraise.
The EV manufacturer’s board approved a preferential issue of up to 9.73 Lakh equity shares at ₹853 apiece to four non-promoter investors, targeting nearly ₹83 Cr.
Motilal Oswal Financial Services will invest ₹40.1 Cr, followed by Calliope Capital Advisors at ₹31.4 Cr, Param Value Investments at ₹8.5 Cr, and Hem Growth Opportunities Fund at nearly ₹3 Cr.
Zelio also plans to issue over 9.96 Lakh convertible warrants at the same price to promoters Niraj Arya, Deepak Arya, and Kunal Arya, raising nearly ₹85 Cr. The promoters will pay 25% of the warrant value upfront, with the balance payable upon conversion within 18 months.
Following the equity allotment and full warrant conversion, promoter shareholding is expected to decline to 70.9% from 72.8%, while public shareholding would increase to 29.1% from 27.2%.
Zelio plans to deploy the proceeds towards growth initiatives as it expands manufacturing capacity and distribution. Following the addition of its Coimbatore facility, the company is targeting annual production capacity of 2.4 Lakh units in Q2 FY27, up from 1.8 Lakh units.
It also plans to expand its dealership network to 550 by the end of FY27 from 400 at the end of FY26.
Founded in 2021, the Hisar-based company primarily manufactures low-speed escooters. It listed on the BSE SME platform in 2025 after raising ₹78.34 Cr.
Zelio’s standalone profit rose 75.4% to ₹28 Cr in FY26 from nearly ₹16 Cr in FY25. Including its auto-components subsidiary, consolidated operating revenue stood at ₹310.7 Cr in FY26.

Pakistan’s tourism and hospitality sector is entering a transformative era driven by innovation, intelligent technology, and the evolving expectations of global travelers. From the majestic northern peaks to the rich cultural heritage and coastal landscapes of the south, Pakistan offers extraordinary experiences that bridge communities and cultures.
As we celebrate World Tourism Day 2026 under the theme “Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism”, we recognize technology’s powerful role in reshaping the future of travel. Digital platforms, predictive analytics, and artificial intelligence are revolutionizing how guests discover destinations, tailor their journeys, and experience hospitality.
At Hashoo Group and the PC Hospitality Division, innovation is central to our expansion across our businesses. Operating an integrated ecosystem of nearly 40 hotels and over 50 dining venues, and scaling toward 60 properties, we are embedding tech-enabled solutions at every stage of the journey. From launching Pakistan’s first 24/7 multi-branded central reservation structure to leveraging data insights for yield and operational efficiency, we ensure every stay is seamless and personalized. Yet, through every digital advance, our focus remains absolute : utilizing technology to elevate, rather than replace, the authentic warmth and genuine human connection that define true hospitality.
Smart systems also empower us to advance our environmental stewardship. As we expand into pristine regions, marked by benchmark developments like Pearl-Continental Attabad Lake, Hunza, AI-driven resource management and data analytics allow us to protect local ecosystems while delivering luxury standards.
Our vision remains firmly anchored in People, Planet, and Prosperity. Through the Hashoo School of Hospitality Management, we are equipping the next generation with digital skillsets and leadership capabilities, enabling young professionals to compete on world stages. Simultaneously, through the Hashoo Foundation, we continue to drive community empowerment, capacity building, and inclusive growth, ensuring that technology serves as a bridge to opportunity across the nation.
Technology is not altering the soul of hospitality as much as it is empowering us to deliver more responsive, sustainable, and memorable experiences. On World Tourism Day, let us commit to a digitally driven, responsible future for Pakistani tourism, strengthening our national hospitality ecosystem and inspiring travelers worldwide.
Happy World Tourism Day !

items.content:
From the sounds that shaped generations to the voices ready to shape what comes next, VELO’s Make Yourself Heard brings Pakistan’s musical past and present into one experience.
Pakistan is full of musical talent, but talent alone does not guarantee an audience. Singers and instrumentalists can share a performance in minutes, only to see it disappear among countless uploads. For emerging artists, the challenge is finding a way for the right people to hear them.
VELO’s Make Yourself Heard gives those undiscovered artists a platform to reach beyond their existing circles. Bringing emerging performers into the same conversation as established artists, it welcomes music across languages, genres and cultural styles. Whether someone sings or plays an instrument, the platform gives their sound a chance to be discovered on its own terms.
The Next Chapter of VELO’s Music Journey
Make Yourself Heard builds on an established connection between VELO and Pakistani music. Across three seasons, VELO Sound Station has produced performances and remakes featuring veteran and new artists. This campaign extends that journey by inviting eligible performers outside its established lineup to share their talent for a chance to be considered for the platform.
This initiative has been a popular topic of conversation in the music community. Established artists have shared their perspectives on discovering talent and the difficulty of reaching an audience. The entries give that conversation a focus: performances by singers and instrumentalists whose names audiences may not know yet.
A Visual History of Pakistani Music
Make Yourself Heard also draws on the music that preceded today’s emerging artists. They have introduced Six Limited-Edition Can designs which reference different eras of Pakistan’s musical history, from early pop and folk influences to disco-pop, pop-rock, hip-hop and contemporary independent music.
The cans serve as visual tributes to those styles, while the submitted performances give audiences new music to discover. For eligible singers and instrumentalists, the invitation is simple: share an original performance and give your sound the chance to reach a wider audience.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Xiaomi’s HyperOS 4, based on Android 17, brings several system-wide upgrades and new features. Among them, five changes stand out for making the biggest difference to everyday use.
1. Soft Light Glass Brings a Major UI Redesign
HyperOS 4 introduces a new Soft Light Glass effect, bringing dynamic glass refraction, layered cards, and translucent blur effects across the interface.
The design extends to the lock screen, home screen, app icons, Control Centre, folders, and widgets.
Most eligible Xiaomi devices should receive the new effect, but deeper integration will be limited to select devices due to hardware requirements. These include models powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite, Dimensity 9500, Xring O1, or newer flagship chipsets.
2. Super XiaoAi 2.0 Adds Deeper AI Features
The new Super XiaoAi 2.0 assistant runs on Xiaomi’s MiMo V2.5 large language model.
It adds improved long-term memory, cross-app actions, and context-aware screen recognition. A new Expert Mode can handle multi-step commands, including checking calendars to plan trips.
It can also generate research reports, PowerPoint presentations, websites and videos from a single prompt.
HyperOS 4 also adds the Inspiration Ball, which analyzes on-screen content and suggests actions such as opening maps, creating calendar entries or finding shopping links.
Apps including Recorder and AI Voice Notes also gain AI-powered summaries, key-point extraction and task generation.
3. Faster Performance
Xiaomi says HyperOS 4 uses AI-based memory preloading to improve performance.
The company claims 27.2% more available memory and 17% faster app launches after extended use.
The updated HyperCore engine also reduces redundant CPU instructions by around 14.4% compared with HyperOS 3.
Gallery scrolling is claimed to be up to 90% smoother, while Camera startup is 200ms faster. HDR photo processing has also dropped from 310ms to 240ms.
4. Redesigned Lock Screen
HyperOS 4 adds more flexible clock customization, allowing users to resize, stretch, and reposition clock layouts.
Notifications now appear in vertically stacked groups instead of separate cards.
The lock screen also supports spatial depth effects that can place subjects in front of clocks, dates and other interface elements.
5. Dual-Phone Syncing
The new Dual-Phone Syncing feature lets two Xiaomi, Redmi or POCO phones share incoming calls and SMS verification codes in real time.
The devices do not need to share Bluetooth or Wi-Fi because syncing works over the internet.
Both devices must use the same Xiaomi account. The receiving phone must run HyperOS 4, while the sending phone can remain on HyperOS 3.
Dual-Phone Syncing is currently available only in China, although it could expand to other regions later.
